entries.title: 2FA
entries.summaryMd: An authentication system that requires more than one distinct authentication factor for successful authentication. Multifactor authentication can be performed using a multifactor authenticator or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. The three authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are.

senses.definitionMd: An authentication system that requires more than one distinct authentication factor for successful authentication. Multifactor authentication can be performed using a multifactor authenticator or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. The three authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are.

entries.title: ABAC
entries.summaryMd: An access control approach in which access is mediated based on attributes associated with subjects (requesters) and the objects to be accessed. Each object and subject has a set of associated attributes, such as location, time of creation, access rights, etc. Access to an object is authorized or denied depending upon whether the required (e.g., policy-defined) correlation can be made between the attributes of that object and of the requesting subject.

senses.definitionMd: An access control approach in which access is mediated based on attributes associated with subjects (requesters) and the objects to be accessed. Each object and subject has a set of associated attributes, such as location, time of creation, access rights, etc. Access to an object is authorized or denied depending upon whether the required (e.g., policy-defined) correlation can be made between the attributes of that object and of the requesting subject.

entries.title: APDU
entries.summaryMd: A part of the application layer in the Open Systems Interconnection Reference model that is used for communication between two separate device's applications. In the context of smart cards, an APDU is the communication unit between a smart card reader and a smart card. The structure of the APDU is defined by [ISO 7816-4].

entries.title: APT
entries.summaryMd: An adversary with sophisticated levels of expertise and significant resources, allowing it through the use of multiple different attack vectors (e.g., cyber, physical, and deception), to generate opportunities to achieve its objectives which are typically to establish and extend its presence within the information technology infrastructure of organizations for purposes of continually exfiltrating information and/or to undermine or impede critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization, or place itself in a position to do so in the future; moreover, the advanced persistent threat pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time, adapting to a defender’s efforts to resist it, and with determination to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.

senses.definitionMd: An adversary with sophisticated levels of expertise and significant resources, allowing it through the use of multiple different attack vectors (e.g., cyber, physical, and deception), to generate opportunities to achieve its objectives which are typically to establish and extend its presence within the information technology infrastructure of organizations for purposes of continually exfiltrating information and/or to undermine or impede critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization, or place itself in a position to do so in the future; moreover, the advanced persistent threat pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time, adapting to a defender’s efforts to resist it, and with determination to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.

entries.title: AUC
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the ability of a classifier to distinguish between classes in machine learning. A higher AUC means that a model performs better when dis­tinguishing between the two classes. AUC measures the entire two-dimensional area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve.

entries.title: CAPI
entries.summaryMd: An application programming interface included with Microsoft Windows operating systems that provides services to enable developers to secure Windows-based applications using cryptography. While providing a consistent API for applications, API allows for specialized cryptographic modules (cryptographic service providers) to be provided by third parties, such as hardware security module (HSM) manufacturers. This enables applications to leverage the additional security of HSMs while using the same APIs they use to access built-in Windows cryptographic service providers. (Also known variously as CryptoAPI, Microsoft Cryptography API, MS-CAPI or simply CAPI)

senses.definitionMd: An application programming interface included with Microsoft Windows operating systems that provides services to enable developers to secure Windows-based applications using cryptography. This enables applications to leverage the additional security of HSMs while using the same APIs they use to access built-in Windows cryptographic service providers. (Also known variously as CryptoAPI, Microsoft Cryptography API, MS-CAPI or simply CAPI)

Industrial control systems include supervisory control and data acquisition systems used to control geographically dispersed assets, as well as distributed control systems and smaller control systems using programmable logic controllers to control localized processes.

senses.definitionMd: An information system used to control industrial processes such as manufacturing, product handling, production, and distribution. Industrial control systems include supervisory control and data acquisition systems used to control geographically dispersed assets, as well as distributed control systems and smaller control systems using programmable logic controllers to control localized processes.

entries.title: ICT
entries.summaryMd: Encompasses the capture, storage, retrieval, processing, display, representation, presentation, organization, management, security, transfer, and interchange of data and information.

senses.definitionMd: Encompasses the capture, storage, retrieval, processing, display, representation, presentation, organization, management, security, transfer, and interchange of data and information.

entries.title: ICV
entries.summaryMd: A fixed string that is prepended to the plaintext within the authenticated-encryption function of a key-wrap algorithm, in order to enable the verification of the integrity of the plaintext within the authenticated-decryption function.

senses.definitionMd: A fixed string that is prepended to the plaintext within the authenticated-encryption function of a key-wrap algorithm, in order to enable the verification of the integrity of the plaintext within the authenticated-decryption function.

entries.title: ICV1
entries.summaryMd: The 64-bit default ICV for KW:0xA6A6A6A6A6A6A6A6.

senses.definitionMd: The 64-bit default ICV for KW:0xA6A6A6A6A6A6A6A6.

entries.title: ICV2
entries.summaryMd: The 32-bit default ICV for KWP:0xA65959A6.

senses.definitionMd: The 32-bit default ICV for KWP:0xA65959A6.

entries.title: ICV3
entries.summaryMd: The 32-bit default ICV for TKW:0xA6A6A6A6.

senses.definitionMd: The 32-bit default ICV for TKW:0xA6A6A6A6.

entries.title: ID
entries.summaryMd: Unique data used to represent a person’s identity and associated attributes. A name or a card number are examples of identifiers.

senses.definitionMd: Unique data used to represent a person’s identity and associated attributes. A name or a card number are examples of identifiers.

entries.title: iDEN
entries.summaryMd: a proprietary mobile communications technology developed by Motorola that combine the capabilities of a digital cellular telephone with two-way radio.

senses.definitionMd: a proprietary mobile communications technology developed by Motorola that combine the capabilities of a digital cellular telephone with two-way radio.

entries.title: IDS
entries.summaryMd: Software that looks for suspicious activity and alerts administrators.

senses.definitionMd: Software that looks for suspicious activity and alerts administrators.

entries.title: IED
entries.summaryMd: Any device incorporating one or more processors with the capability to receive or send data/control from or to an external source (e.g., electronic multifunction meters, digital relays, controllers).

senses.definitionMd: Any device incorporating one or more processors with the capability to receive or send data/control from or to an external source (e.g., electronic multifunction meters, digital relays, controllers).

entries.title: IETF
entries.summaryMd: The internet standards organization made up of network designers, operators, vendors, and researchers that defines protocol standards (e.g., IP, TCP, DNS) through process of collaboration and consensus.

senses.definitionMd: The internet standards organization made up of network designers, operators, vendors, and researchers that defines protocol standards (e.g., IP, TCP, DNS) through process of collaboration and consensus.

entries.title: IM
entries.summaryMd: a facility for exchanging messages in real-time with other people over the Internet and tracking the progress of the conversation.

senses.definitionMd: a facility for exchanging messages in real-time with other people over the Internet and tracking the progress of the conversation.

entries.title: IMAP
aliases: Internet Message Access Protocol Mail Delivery Agent
entries.summaryMd: a method of communication used to read electronic mail stored in a remote server.

senses.definitionMd: a method of communication used to read electronic mail stored in a remote server.

entries.title: IMEI
entries.summaryMd: a unique number programmed into GSM and UMTS mobile phones.

senses.definitionMd: a unique number programmed into GSM and UMTS mobile phones.

entries.title: IMSI
entries.summaryMd: a unique number associated with every GSM mobile phone user.

senses.definitionMd: a unique number associated with every GSM mobile phone user.

entries.title: INFOSEC
entries.summaryMd: The protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

senses.definitionMd: The protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

entries.title: IO
entries.summaryMd: A general term for the equipment that is used to communicate with a computer as well as the data involved in the communications.

senses.definitionMd: A general term for the equipment that is used to communicate with a computer as well as the data involved in the communications.

entries.title: IoT
entries.summaryMd: The network of devices that contain the hardware, software, firmware, and actuators which allow the devices to connect, interact, and freely exchange data and information.

senses.definitionMd: The network of devices that contain the hardware, software, firmware, and actuators which allow the devices to connect, interact, and freely exchange data and information.

entries.title: IP
entries.summaryMd: The Internet Protocol, as defined in IETF RFC 6864, which is the principal communications protocol in the IETF Internet protocol suite for specifying system address information when relaying datagrams across network boundaries.

senses.definitionMd: The Internet Protocol, as defined in IETF RFC 6864, which is the principal communications protocol in the IETF Internet protocol suite for specifying system address information when relaying datagrams across network boundaries.

entries.title: IPS
entries.summaryMd: System which can detect an intrusive activity and can also attempt to stop the activity, ideally before it reaches its targets.

senses.definitionMd: System which can detect an intrusive activity and can also attempt to stop the activity, ideally before it reaches its targets.

entries.title: IR
entries.summaryMd: See incident handling.

senses.definitionMd: See incident handling.

entries.title: IREX
entries.summaryMd: Iris Exchange – the NIST program supporting iris-based biometrics

senses.definitionMd: Iris Exchange – the NIST program supporting iris-based biometrics

entries.title: IRP
entries.summaryMd: The documentation of a predetermined set of instructions or procedures to detect, respond to, and limit consequences of a malicious cyber attacks against an organization’s information systems(s).

senses.definitionMd: The documentation of a predetermined set of instructions or procedures to detect, respond to, and limit consequences of a malicious cyber attacks against an organization’s information systems(s).

entries.title: IS
entries.summaryMd: The protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

senses.definitionMd: The protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

entries.title: ISA
entries.summaryMd: Individual who implements approved secure baseline configurations, incorporates secure configuration settings for IT products, and conducts/assists with configuration monitoring activities as needed.

senses.definitionMd: Individual who implements approved secure baseline configurations, incorporates secure configuration settings for IT products, and conducts/assists with configuration monitoring activities as needed.

entries.title: ISAO
entries.summaryMd: An ISAO is any entity or collaboration created or employed by public- or private sector organizations, for purposes of gathering and analyzing critical cyber and related information in order to better understand security problems and interdependencies related to cyber systems, so as to ensure their availability, integrity, and reliability.

senses.definitionMd: An ISAO is any entity or collaboration created or employed by public- or private sector organizations, for purposes of gathering and analyzing critical cyber and related information in order to better understand security problems and interdependencies related to cyber systems, so as to ensure their availability, integrity, and reliability.

entries.title: ISC
entries.summaryMd: A discrete identifiable IT asset that represents a building block of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: A discrete identifiable IT asset that represents a building block of an information system.

entries.title: ISO
entries.summaryMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions. [Note: The terms “continuous” and “ongoing” in this context mean that security controls and organizational risks are assessed and analyzed at a frequency sufficient to support risk-based security decisions to adequately protect organization information.]

senses.definitionMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions. [Note: The terms “continuous” and “ongoing” in this context mean that security controls and organizational risks are assessed and analyzed at a frequency sufficient to support risk-based security decisions to adequately protect organization information.]

entries.title: ISSO
entries.summaryMd: See system security officer (SSO).

senses.definitionMd: See system security officer (SSO).

entries.title: ISU
entries.summaryMd: Individual, or (system) process acting on behalf of an individual, authorized to access an information system. [Note: With respect to SecCM, an information system user is an individual who uses the information system functions, initiates change requests, and assists with functional testing.]

senses.definitionMd: Individual, or (system) process acting on behalf of an individual, authorized to access an information system. [Note: With respect to SecCM, an information system user is an individual who uses the information system functions, initiates change requests, and assists with functional testing.]

entries.title: IT
entries.summaryMd: (A) with respect to an executive agency means any equipment or interconnected system or subsystem of equipment, used in the automatic acquisition, storage, analysis, evaluation, manipulation, management, movement, control, display, switching, interchange, transmission, or reception of data or information by the executive agency, if the equipment is used by the executive agency directly or is used by a contractor under a contract with the executive agency that requires the use— (i) of that equipment; or (ii) of that equipment to a significant extent in the performance of a service or the furnishing of a product; (B) includes computers, ancillary equipment (including imaging peripherals, input, output, and storage devices necessary for security and surveillance), peripheral equipment designed to be controlled by the central processing unit of a computer, software, firmware and similar procedures, services (including support services), and related resources; but (C) does not include any equipment acquired by a federal contractor incidental to a federal contract.

senses.definitionMd: (A) with respect to an executive agency means any equipment or interconnected system or subsystem of equipment, used in the automatic acquisition, storage, analysis, evaluation, manipulation, management, movement, control, display, switching, interchange, transmission, or reception of data or information by the executive agency, if the equipment is used by the executive agency directly or is used by a contractor under a contract with the executive agency that requires the use— (i) of that equipment; or (ii) of that equipment to a significant extent in the performance of a service or the furnishing of a product; (B) includes computers, ancillary equipment (including imaging peripherals, input, output, and storage devices necessary for security and surveillance), peripheral equipment designed to be controlled by the central processing unit of a computer, software, firmware and similar procedures, services (including support services), and related resources; but (C) does not include any equipment acquired by a federal contractor incidental to a federal contract.

entries.title: IUT
entries.summaryMd: Implementation Under Test

senses.definitionMd: Implementation Under Test

entries.title: IV
entries.summaryMd: A binary vector used as the input to initialize the algorithm for the encryption of a plaintext block sequence to increase security by introducing additional cryptographic variance and to synchronize cryptographic equipment. The initialization vector need not be secret. Some of the Triple Data Encryption Algorithm Modes of Operation require 3 initialization vectors.

senses.definitionMd: A binary vector used as the input to initialize the algorithm for the encryption of a plaintext block sequence to increase security by introducing additional cryptographic variance and to synchronize cryptographic equipment. The initialization vector need not be secret. Some of the Triple Data Encryption Algorithm Modes of Operation require 3 initialization vectors.

entries.title: JWT
entries.summaryMd: A data exchange format made of a header, payload, and signature where the header and the payload take the form of JSON objects. They are encoded and concatenated with the aggregate being signed to generate a signature.

senses.definitionMd: A data exchange format made of a header, payload, and signature where the header and the payload take the form of JSON objects. They are encoded and concatenated with the aggregate being signed to generate a signature.

entries.title: K1
entries.summaryMd: The first subkey.

senses.definitionMd: The first subkey.

entries.title: K2
entries.summaryMd: The second subkey.

senses.definitionMd: The second subkey.

senses.definitionMd: A procedure that provides assurance to one party (i.e., key-confirmation recipient) that another party (i.e., key-confirmation provider) possesses the correct secret keying material and/or shared secret from which that secret keying material is derived.

entries.title: KDK
entries.summaryMd: As used in this Recommendation, a function used to derive secret keying material from a shared secret (or a key) and other information.

senses.definitionMd: As used in this Recommendation, a function used to derive secret keying material from a shared secret (or a key) and other information.

senses.definitionMd: A method used to derive keying material from initial shared secrets and possibly other information.

entries.title: KECCAK
entries.summaryMd: The family of all sponge functions with a KECCAK-f permutation as the underlyinng function and multi-rate padding as the padding rule. KECCAK was originally specified in [G. Bertoni, J. Daemen, M. Peeters, and G. Van Assche, The KECCAK reference, version 3.0], and standardized in FIPS 202.

senses.definitionMd: The family of all sponge functions with a KECCAK-f permutation as the underlyinng function and multi-rate padding as the padding rule. KECCAK was originally specified in [G. Bertoni, J. Daemen, M. Peeters, and G. Van Assche, The KECCAK reference, version 3.0], and standardized in FIPS 202.

entries.summaryMd: The key for the underlying block cipher of KW, KWP, or TKW. May be called a key-wrapping key in other documents.

senses.definitionMd: The key for the underlying block cipher of KW, KWP, or TKW. May be called a key-wrapping key in other documents.

entries.title: KEM

senses.definitionMd: A set of three cryptographic algorithms (KeyGen, Encaps, and Decaps) that can be used by two parties to establish a shared secret key over a public channel.

entries.title: KEYn
entries.summaryMd: Block of data representing KEY n

senses.definitionMd: Block of data representing KEY n

entries.title: KiB

senses.definitionMd: Kibi Byte, Measuring Unit 210 Bytes = 1024 Bytes

entries.title: KMAC

senses.definitionMd: KECCAK Message Authentication Code.

senses.definitionMd: The activities involving the handling of cryptographic keys and other related security parameters (e.g., initialization vectors) during the entire lifecycle of the keys, including their generation, storage, establishment, entry and output, use and destruction.

senses.definitionMd: Documents how key management for current and/or planned cryptographic products and services will be implemented to ensure lifecycle key management support for cryptographic processes.

entries.title: KMPS

senses.definitionMd: A document or set of documentation that describes (in detail) the organizational structure, responsible roles, and organization rules for the functions identified in the associated cryptographic Key Management Policy (see [IETF RFC 3647]).

entries.title: KOUT

senses.definitionMd: A means of restricting access to system resources based on the sensitivity (as represented by a label) of the information contained in the system resource and the formal authorization (i.e., clearance) of users to access information of such sensitivity.

senses.definitionMd: a byte string.

entries.title: MATLAB

MATLAB includes functions for data analysis and visu alization; numeric and symbolic computation; engineering and scientific graphics; modeling, simulation and prototyping; and programming, application development and a GUI design.

senses.definitionMd: An integrated, technical computer environment that combines numeric computation, advanced graphics and visualization, and a high level programming language. entries.title: MF
entries.summaryMd: A characteristic of an authentication system or an authenticator that requires more than one distinct authentication factor for successful authentication. MFA can be performed using a single authenticator that provides more than one factor or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. The three authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are.

senses.definitionMd: A characteristic of an authentication system or an authenticator that requires more than one distinct authentication factor for successful authentication. MFA can be performed using a single authenticator that provides more than one factor or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. entries.title: MFA
entries.summaryMd: An authentication system that requires more than one distinct authentication factor for successful authentication. Multifactor authentication can be performed using a multifactor authenticator or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. The three authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are.

senses.definitionMd: Any information system (including any telecommunications system) used or operated by an agency or by a contractor of an agency, or other organization on behalf of an agency—(i) the function, operation, or use of which involves intelligence activities; involves cryptologic activities related to national security; involves command and control of military forces; involves equipment that is an integral part of a weapon or weapons system; or is critical to the direct fulfillment of military or intelligence missions (excluding a system that is to be used for routine administrative and business applications, for example, payroll, finance, logistics, and personnel management applications); or (ii) is protected at all times by procedures established for information that have been specifically authorized under criteria established by an Executive Order or an Act of Congress to be kept classified in the interest of national defense or foreign policy.

entries.title: SoD
entries.summaryMd: refers to the principle that no user should be given enough privileges to misuse the system on their own. For example, the person authorizing a paycheck should not also be the one who can prepare them. Separation of duties can be enforced either statically (by defining conflicting roles, i.e., roles which cannot be executed by the same user) or dynamically (by enforcing the control at access time). An example of dynamic separation of duty is the two-person rule. The first user to execute a two-person operation can be any authorized user, whereas the second user can be any authorized user different from the first [R.S. Sandhu., and P Samarati, “Access Control: Principles and Practice,” IEEE Communications Magazine 32(9), September 1994, pp. 40-48.]. There are various types of SOD, an important one is history-based SOD that regulate for example, the same subject (role) cannot access the same object for variable number of times.

entries.title: access control list
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism that implements access control for a system resource by enumerating the identities of the system entities that are permitted to access the resources.

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism that implements access control for a system resource by enumerating the identities of the system entities that are permitted to access the resources.

entries.title: Access Control Matrix
entries.summaryMd: A table in which each row represents a subject, each column represents an object, and each entry is the set of access rights for that subject to that object.

senses.definitionMd: A table in which each row represents a subject, each column represents an object, and each entry is the set of access rights for that subject to that object.

entries.title: access control mechanism
entries.summaryMd: Implementations of formal AC policy such as AC model. Access control mechanisms can be designed to adhere to the properties of the model by machine implementation using protocols, architecture, or formal languages such as program code.

senses.definitionMd: Implementations of formal AC policy such as AC model. Access control mechanisms can be designed to adhere to the properties of the model by machine implementation using protocols, architecture, or formal languages such as program code.

entries.title: Access Control Model
entries.summaryMd: Formal presentations of the security policies enforced by AC systems, and are useful for proving theoretical limitations of systems. AC models bridge the gap in abstraction between policy and mechanism.

senses.definitionMd: Formal presentations of the security policies enforced by AC systems, and are useful for proving theoretical limitations of systems. AC models bridge the gap in abstraction between policy and mechanism.

entries.title: Access Control Policy
entries.summaryMd: an access control paradigm whereby access rights are granted to users through the use of policies which combine attributes together. The policies can use any type of attributes (user attributes, resource attributes, environment attribute etc.

senses.definitionMd: an access control paradigm whereby access rights are granted to users through the use of policies which combine attributes together. The policies can use any type of attributes (user attributes, resource attributes, environment attribute etc.

entries.title: Access control system
entries.summaryMd: A set of procedures and/or processes, normally automated, which allows access to a controlled area or to information to be controlled, in accordance with pre-established policies and rules.

senses.definitionMd: A set of procedures and/or processes, normally automated, which allows access to a controlled area or to information to be controlled, in accordance with pre-established policies and rules.

entries.title: access cross domain solution
entries.summaryMd: A type of transfer cross domain solution (CDS) that provides access to a computing platform, application, or data residing in different security domains without transfer of user data between the domains.

senses.definitionMd: A type of transfer cross domain solution (CDS) that provides access to a computing platform, application, or data residing in different security domains without transfer of user data between the domains.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "access cross domain solution"

entries.title: access level
entries.summaryMd: A category within a given security classification limiting entry or system connectivity to only authorized persons.

senses.definitionMd: A category within a given security classification limiting entry or system connectivity to only authorized persons.

entries.title: access list
entries.summaryMd: Roster of individuals authorized admittance to a controlled area.

senses.definitionMd: Roster of individuals authorized admittance to a controlled area.

entries.title: Access Management
entries.summaryMd: Access Management is the set of practices that enables only those permitted the ability to perform an action on a particular resource. The three most common Access Management services you encounter every day perhaps without realizing it are: Policy Administration, Authentication, and Authorization.

senses.definitionMd: Access Management is the set of practices that enables only those permitted the ability to perform an action on a particular resource. The three most common Access Management services you encounter every day perhaps without realizing it are: Policy Administration, Authentication, and Authorization.

entries.title: Access Point (AP)
entries.summaryMd: A device that logically connects wireless client devices operating in infrastructure to one another and provides access to a distribution system, if connected, which is typically an organization’s enterprise wired network.

senses.definitionMd: A device that logically connects wireless client devices operating in infrastructure to one another and provides access to a distribution system, if connected, which is typically an organization’s enterprise wired network.

entries.title: access profile
entries.summaryMd: Association of a user with a list of protected objects the user may access.

senses.definitionMd: Association of a user with a list of protected objects the user may access.

entries.title: access program (SAP)
entries.summaryMd: A program established for a specific class of classified information that imposes safeguarding and access requirements that exceed those normally required for information at the same classification level.

senses.definitionMd: A program established for a specific class of classified information that imposes safeguarding and access requirements that exceed those normally required for information at the same classification level.

entries.title: access type
entries.summaryMd: Privilege to perform action on an object. Read, write, execute, append, modify, delete, and create are examples of access types.

senses.definitionMd: Privilege to perform action on an object. Read, write, execute, append, modify, delete, and create are examples of access types.

entries.title: Access Vector
entries.summaryMd: reflects the access required to exploit the vulnerability.

senses.definitionMd: reflects the access required to exploit the vulnerability.

entries.title: Account
entries.summaryMd: An entity in a blockchain that is identified with an address and can send transactions to the blockchain.

senses.definitionMd: An entity in a blockchain that is identified with an address and can send transactions to the blockchain.

entries.title: account linking
entries.summaryMd: The association of multiple federated identifiers with a single RP subscriber account or the management of those associations.

senses.definitionMd: The association of multiple federated identifiers with a single RP subscriber account or the management of those associations.

entries.title: account recovery
entries.summaryMd: The ability to regain ownership of a subscriber account and its associated information and privileges.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to regain ownership of a subscriber account and its associated information and privileges.

entries.title: account resolution
entries.summaryMd: The association of an RP subscriber account with information that is already held by the RP prior to the federation transaction and outside of a trust agreement.

senses.definitionMd: The association of an RP subscriber account with information that is already held by the RP prior to the federation transaction and outside of a trust agreement.

entries.title: accountability
entries.summaryMd: The principle that an individual is entrusted to safeguard and control equipment, keying material, and information and is answerable to proper authority for the loss or misuse of that equipment or information.

senses.definitionMd: The principle that an individual is entrusted to safeguard and control equipment, keying material, and information and is answerable to proper authority for the loss or misuse of that equipment or information.

entries.title: accounting legend code
entries.summaryMd: A numeric code used to indicate the minimum accounting controls required for items of accountable COMSEC material within the COMSEC material control system (CMCS).

senses.definitionMd: A numeric code used to indicate the minimum accounting controls required for items of accountable COMSEC material within the COMSEC material control system (CMCS).

entries.title: accounting number
entries.summaryMd: A number assigned to an individual item of COMSEC material at its point of origin to facilitate its handling and accounting.

senses.definitionMd: A number assigned to an individual item of COMSEC material at its point of origin to facilitate its handling and accounting.

entries.title: accreditation
entries.summaryMd: The official management decision given by a senior agency official to authorize operation of an information system and to explicitly accept the risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, or individuals, based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of security controls.

senses.definitionMd: The official management decision given by a senior agency official to authorize operation of an information system and to explicitly accept the risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, or individuals, based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of security controls.

entries.title: accreditation boundary
entries.summaryMd: All components of an information system to be accredited by an authorizing official and excludes separately accredited systems to which the information system is connected. Synonymous with the term security perimeter defined in CNSS Instruction 4009 and DCID 6/3.

senses.definitionMd: All components of an information system to be accredited by an authorizing official and excludes separately accredited systems to which the information system is connected. Synonymous with the term security perimeter defined in CNSS Instruction 4009 and DCID 6/3.

entries.title: accrediting authority
entries.summaryMd: A senior (federal) official or executive with the authority to formally assume responsibility for operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.

senses.definitionMd: A senior (federal) official or executive with the authority to formally assume responsibility for operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.

entries.title: accuracy
entries.summaryMd: Closeness of computations or estimates to the exact or true values that the statistics were intended to measure.

senses.definitionMd: Closeness of computations or estimates to the exact or true values that the statistics were intended to measure.

entries.title: accuracy (absolute)
entries.summaryMd: The degree of conformity of a measured or calculated value to the true value, typically based on a global reference system. For time, the global reference can be based on the following time scales: UTC, International Atomic Time (TAI), or GPS. For position, the global reference can be WGS 84.

senses.definitionMd: The degree of conformity of a measured or calculated value to the true value, typically based on a global reference system. For time, the global reference can be based on the following time scales: UTC, International Atomic Time (TAI), or GPS. For position, the global reference can be WGS 84.

entries.title: accuracy (relative)
entries.summaryMd: The degree of agreement between measured or calculated values among the devices and applications dependent on the position, navigation, or time data at an instant in time.

senses.definitionMd: The degree of agreement between measured or calculated values among the devices and applications dependent on the position, navigation, or time data at an instant in time.

entries.title: acquirer
entries.summaryMd: Stakeholder that acquires or procures a product or service.

senses.definitionMd: Stakeholder that acquires or procures a product or service.

entries.title: acquisition
entries.summaryMd: Process of obtaining a system, product, or service.

senses.definitionMd: Process of obtaining a system, product, or service.

entries.title: activation
entries.summaryMd: The process of inputting an activation factor into a multi-factor authenticator to enable its use for authentication.

senses.definitionMd: The process of inputting an activation factor into a multi-factor authenticator to enable its use for authentication.

entries.title: activation data
entries.summaryMd: A pass-phrase, personal identification number (PIN), biometric data, or other mechanisms of equivalent authentication robustness used to protect access to any use of a private key, except for private keys associated with System or Device certificates.

senses.definitionMd: A pass-phrase, personal identification number (PIN), biometric data, or other mechanisms of equivalent authentication robustness used to protect access to any use of a private key, except for private keys associated with System or Device certificates.

entries.title: activation factor
entries.summaryMd: An additional authentication factor that is used to enable successful authentication with a multi-factor authenticator.

senses.definitionMd: An additional authentication factor that is used to enable successful authentication with a multi-factor authenticator.

entries.title: Activation/Issuance
entries.summaryMd: A process that includes the procurement of FIPS-approved blank PIV Cards or hardware/software tokens (for Derived PIV Credential), initializing them using appropriate software and data elements, personalization of these cards/tokens with the identity credentials of authorized subjects, and pick-up/delivery of the personalized cards/tokens to the authorized subjects, along with appropriate instructions for protection and use.

senses.definitionMd: A process that includes the procurement of FIPS-approved blank PIV Cards or hardware/software tokens (for Derived PIV Credential), initializing them using appropriate software and data elements, personalization of these cards/tokens with the identity credentials of authorized subjects, and pick-up/delivery of the personalized cards/tokens to the authorized subjects, along with appropriate instructions for protection and use.

entries.title: activation secret
entries.summaryMd: A password that is used locally as an activation factor for a multi-factor authenticator.

senses.definitionMd: A password that is used locally as an activation factor for a multi-factor authenticator.

entries.title: active attack
entries.summaryMd: An attack on a secure communication protocol where the attacker transmits data to the claimant, Credential Service Provider (CSP), verifier, or Relying Party (RP). Examples of active attacks include man-in- the middle (MitM), impersonation, and session hijacking.

senses.definitionMd: An attack on a secure communication protocol where the attacker transmits data to the claimant, Credential Service Provider (CSP), verifier, or Relying Party (RP). Examples of active attacks include man-in- the middle (MitM), impersonation, and session hijacking.

entries.title: active content
entries.summaryMd: Electronic documents that can carry out or trigger actions automatically on a computer platform without the intervention of a user.

senses.definitionMd: Electronic documents that can carry out or trigger actions automatically on a computer platform without the intervention of a user.

entries.title: active cyber defense
entries.summaryMd: Synchronized, real-time capability to discover, detect, analyze, and mitigate threats and vulnerabilities.

senses.definitionMd: Synchronized, real-time capability to discover, detect, analyze, and mitigate threats and vulnerabilities.

entries.title: Active Directory
entries.summaryMd: A Microsoft directory service for the management of identities in Windows domain networks.

senses.definitionMd: A Microsoft directory service for the management of identities in Windows domain networks.

entries.title: Active Security Testing
entries.summaryMd: Security testing that involves direct interaction with a target, such as sending packets to a target.

senses.definitionMd: Security testing that involves direct interaction with a target, such as sending packets to a target.

entries.title: Active state
entries.summaryMd: A lifecycle state for a key in which the key may be used to cryptographically protect information (e.g., encrypt plaintext or generate a digital signature), to cryptographically process previously protected information (e.g., decrypt ciphertext or verify a digital signature) or both.

senses.definitionMd: A lifecycle state for a key in which the key may be used to cryptographically protect information (e.g., encrypt plaintext or generate a digital signature), to cryptographically process previously protected information (e.g., decrypt ciphertext or verify a digital signature) or both.

entries.title: Active Tag
entries.summaryMd: A tag that relies on a battery for power.

senses.definitionMd: A tag that relies on a battery for power.

entries.title: Activities
entries.summaryMd: An assessment object that includes specific protection-related pursuits or actions supporting an information system that involve people (e.g., conducting system backup operations, monitoring network traffic).

senses.definitionMd: An assessment object that includes specific protection-related pursuits or actions supporting an information system that involve people (e.g., conducting system backup operations, monitoring network traffic).

entries.title: activity
entries.summaryMd: Set of cohesive tasks of a process.

senses.definitionMd: Set of cohesive tasks of a process.

entries.title: Actor
entries.summaryMd: See threat actor.

senses.definitionMd: See threat actor.

entries.title: Actual Residual Risk
entries.summaryMd: The risk remaining after management has taken action to alter its severity.

senses.definitionMd: The risk remaining after management has taken action to alter its severity.

entries.title: Actual State
entries.summaryMd: The observable state or behavior of an assessment object (device, software, person, credential, account, etc.) at the point in time when the collector generates security-related information. In particular, the actual state includes the states or behaviors that might indicate the presence of security defects.

senses.definitionMd: The observable state or behavior of an assessment object (device, software, person, credential, account, etc.) at the point in time when the collector generates security-related information. In particular, the actual state includes the states or behaviors that might indicate the presence of security defects.

entries.title: Actuating Capability
entries.summaryMd: The ability to change something in the physical world.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to change something in the physical world.

entries.title: actuator
entries.summaryMd: A device for moving or controlling a mechanism or system. It is operated by a source of energy, typically electric current, hydraulic fluid pressure, or pneumatic pressure, and converts that energy into motion. An actuator is the mechanism by which a control system acts upon an environment. The control system can be simple (a fixed mechanical or electronic system), software-based (e.g., a printer driver, robot control system), or a human or other agent.

senses.definitionMd: A device for moving or controlling a mechanism or system. It is operated by a source of energy, typically electric current, hydraulic fluid pressure, or pneumatic pressure, and converts that energy into motion. An actuator is the mechanism by which a control system acts upon an environment. The control system can be simple (a fixed mechanical or electronic system), software-based (e.g., a printer driver, robot control system), or a human or other agent.

entries.title: Ad Hoc HIEs
entries.summaryMd: An Ad Hoc HIE occurs when two healthcare organizations exchange health information, usually under the precondition of familiarity and trust, using existing and usual office infrastructure such as mail, fax, e-mail and phone calls.

senses.definitionMd: An Ad Hoc HIE occurs when two healthcare organizations exchange health information, usually under the precondition of familiarity and trust, using existing and usual office infrastructure such as mail, fax, e-mail and phone calls.

entries.title: Ad Hoc Network
entries.summaryMd: A wireless network that allows easy connection establishment between wireless client devices in the same physical area without the use of an infrastructure device, such as an access point or a base station.

senses.definitionMd: A wireless network that allows easy connection establishment between wireless client devices in the same physical area without the use of an infrastructure device, such as an access point or a base station.

entries.title: adaptability
entries.summaryMd: The property of an architecture, design, and implementation that can accommodate changes to the threat model, mission or business functions, systems, and technologies without major programmatic impacts.

senses.definitionMd: The property of an architecture, design, and implementation that can accommodate changes to the threat model, mission or business functions, systems, and technologies without major programmatic impacts.

entries.title: add-on security
entries.summaryMd: Incorporation of new or additional hardware, software, or firmware safeguards in an operational information system.

senses.definitionMd: Incorporation of new or additional hardware, software, or firmware safeguards in an operational information system.

entries.title: Additional Authenticated Data
entries.summaryMd: The input data to the authenticated encryption function that is authenticated but not encrypted.

senses.definitionMd: The input data to the authenticated encryption function that is authenticated but not encrypted.

entries.title: Additional input
entries.summaryMd: Information known by two parties that is cryptographically bound to the secret keying material being protected using the encryption operation.

senses.definitionMd: Information known by two parties that is cryptographically bound to the secret keying material being protected using the encryption operation.

entries.title: Address
entries.summaryMd: The associated data string.

senses.definitionMd: The associated data string.

entries.title: Address Resolution Protocol (ARP)
entries.summaryMd: A protocol used to obtain a node’s physical address. A client station broadcasts an ARP request onto the network with the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the target node with which it wishes to communicate, and with that address the node responds by sending back its physical address so that packets can be transmitted to it.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol used to obtain a node’s physical address. A client station broadcasts an ARP request onto the network with the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the target node with which it wishes to communicate, and with that address the node responds by sending back its physical address so that packets can be transmitted to it.

entries.title: addressable
entries.summaryMd: To meet the addressable implementation specifications, a covered entity or business associate must (i) assess whether each implementation specification is a reasonable and appropriate safeguard in its environment, when analyzed with reference to the likely contribution to protecting the electronic protected health information; and (ii) as applicable to the covered entity or business associate - (A) Implement the implementation specification if reasonable and appropriate; or (B) if implementing the implementation specification is not reasonable and appropriate—(1) document why it would not be reasonable and appropriate to implement the implementation specification; and (2) implement an equivalent alternative measure if reasonable and appropriate.

senses.definitionMd: To meet the addressable implementation specifications, a covered entity or business associate must (i) assess whether each implementation specification is a reasonable and appropriate safeguard in its environment, when analyzed with reference to the likely contribution to protecting the electronic protected health information; and (ii) as applicable to the covered entity or business associate - (A) Implement the implementation specification if reasonable and appropriate; or (B) if implementing the implementation specification is not reasonable and appropriate—(1) document why it would not be reasonable and appropriate to implement the implementation specification; and (2) implement an equivalent alternative measure if reasonable and appropriate.

entries.title: adequate security
entries.summaryMd: Security commensurate with the risk and the magnitude of harm resulting from the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of information.

senses.definitionMd: Security commensurate with the risk and the magnitude of harm resulting from the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of information.

entries.title: adj-RIB-In
entries.summaryMd: Routes learned from inbound update messages from BGP peers.

senses.definitionMd: Routes learned from inbound update messages from BGP peers.

entries.title: adj-RIB-Out
entries.summaryMd: Routes that the BGP router will advertise, based on its local policy, to its peers.

senses.definitionMd: Routes that the BGP router will advertise, based on its local policy, to its peers.

entries.title: Adjudicative Entity
entries.summaryMd: An agency authorized by law, Executive Order, designation by the Security Executive Agent, or delegation by the Suitability & Credentialing Executive Agent to make an adjudication. Adjudication has the meaning provided in [Executive Order 13764], “(a) ‘Adjudication’ means the evaluation of pertinent data in a background investigation, as well as any other available information that is relevant and reliable, to determine whether a covered individual is: (i) suitable for Government employment; (ii) eligible for logical and physical access; (iii) eligible for access to classified information; (iv) eligible to hold a sensitive position; or (v) fit to perform work for or on behalf of the Government as a Federal employee, contractor, or non-appropriated fund employee.”

senses.definitionMd: An agency authorized by law, Executive Order, designation by the Security Executive Agent, or delegation by the Suitability & Credentialing Executive Agent to make an adjudication. Adjudication has the meaning provided in [Executive Order 13764], “(a) ‘Adjudication’ means the evaluation of pertinent data in a background investigation, as well as any other available information that is relevant and reliable, to determine whether a covered individual is: (i) suitable for Government employment; (ii) eligible for logical and physical access; (iii) eligible for access to classified information; (iv) eligible to hold a sensitive position; or (v) fit to perform work for or on behalf of the Government as a Federal employee, contractor, or non-appropriated fund employee.”

entries.title: Administrative domain
entries.summaryMd: A logical collection of hosts and network resources (e.g., department, building, company, organization) governed by common policies.

senses.definitionMd: A logical collection of hosts and network resources (e.g., department, building, company, organization) governed by common policies.

entries.title: administrative incident (COMSEC)
entries.summaryMd: A violation of procedures or practices dangerous to security that is not serious enough to jeopardize the integrity of a controlled cryptographic item (CCI), but requires corrective action to ensure the violation does not recur or possibly lead to a reportable COMSEC incident.

senses.definitionMd: A violation of procedures or practices dangerous to security that is not serious enough to jeopardize the integrity of a controlled cryptographic item (CCI), but requires corrective action to ensure the violation does not recur or possibly lead to a reportable COMSEC incident.

entries.title: advanced cyber threat
entries.summaryMd: See advanced persistent threat.

senses.definitionMd: See advanced persistent threat.

entries.title: Advanced Encryption Standard
entries.summaryMd: A U.S. Government-approved cryptographic algorithm that can be used to protect electronic data. The AES algorithm is a symmetric block cipher that can encrypt (encipher) and decrypt (decipher) information.

senses.definitionMd: A U.S. Government-approved cryptographic algorithm that can be used to protect electronic data. The AES algorithm is a symmetric block cipher that can encrypt (encipher) and decrypt (decipher) information.

entries.title: advanced key processor
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic device that performs all cryptographic functions for a management client node and contains the interfaces to 1) exchange information with a client platform, 2) interact with fill devices, and 3) connect a client platform securely to the primary services node (PRSN).

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic device that performs all cryptographic functions for a management client node and contains the interfaces to 1) exchange information with a client platform, 2) interact with fill devices, and 3) connect a client platform securely to the primary services node (PRSN).

entries.title: advanced persistent threat
entries.summaryMd: An adversary with sophisticated levels of expertise and significant resources, allowing it through the use of multiple different attack vectors (e.g., cyber, physical, and deception), to generate opportunities to achieve its objectives which are typically to establish and extend its presence within the information technology infrastructure of organizations for purposes of continually exfiltrating information and/or to undermine or impede critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization, or place itself in a position to do so in the future; moreover, the advanced persistent threat pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time, adapting to a defender’s efforts to resist it, and with determination to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.

senses.definitionMd: An adversary with sophisticated levels of expertise and significant resources, allowing it through the use of multiple different attack vectors (e.g., cyber, physical, and deception), to generate opportunities to achieve its objectives which are typically to establish and extend its presence within the information technology infrastructure of organizations for purposes of continually exfiltrating information and/or to undermine or impede critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization, or place itself in a position to do so in the future; moreover, the advanced persistent threat pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time, adapting to a defender’s efforts to resist it, and with determination to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.

entries.title: Advanced Persistent Threats
entries.summaryMd: An adversary with sophisticated levels of expertise and significant resources, allowing it through the use of multiple different attack vectors (e.g., cyber, physical, and deception) to generate opportunities to achieve its objectives, which are typically to establish and extend footholds within the information technology infrastructure of organizations for purposes of continually exfiltrating information and/or to undermine or impede critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization, or place itself in a position to do so in the future; moreover, the advanced persistent threat pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time, adapting to a defender’s efforts to resist it, and with determination to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.

senses.definitionMd: An adversary with sophisticated levels of expertise and significant resources, allowing it through the use of multiple different attack vectors (e.g., cyber, physical, and deception) to generate opportunities to achieve its objectives, which are typically to establish and extend footholds within the information technology infrastructure of organizations for purposes of continually exfiltrating information and/or to undermine or impede critical aspects of a mission, program, or organization, or place itself in a position to do so in the future; moreover, the advanced persistent threat pursues its objectives repeatedly over an extended period of time, adapting to a defender’s efforts to resist it, and with determination to maintain the level of interaction needed to execute its objectives.

entries.title: adversarial example
entries.summaryMd: A modified testing sample that induces misclassification or misbehav­ior of a machine learning model at deployment time.

senses.definitionMd: A modified testing sample that induces misclassification or misbehav­ior of a machine learning model at deployment time.

entries.title: Adversarial Machine Learning
entries.summaryMd: Attacks that exploit the statistical, data-based nature of ma­chine learning systems.

senses.definitionMd: Attacks that exploit the statistical, data-based nature of ma­chine learning systems.

entries.title: adversary
entries.summaryMd: Person, group, organization, or government that conducts or has the intent to conduct detrimental activities.

senses.definitionMd: Person, group, organization, or government that conducts or has the intent to conduct detrimental activities.

entries.title: adverse consequence
entries.summaryMd: An undesirable consequence associated with a loss.

senses.definitionMd: An undesirable consequence associated with a loss.

entries.title: adverse cybersecurity event
entries.summaryMd: Any event with a potentially negative impact on cybersecurity.

senses.definitionMd: Any event with a potentially negative impact on cybersecurity.

entries.title: adversity
entries.summaryMd: Adverse conditions, stresses, attacks, or compromises.

senses.definitionMd: Adverse conditions, stresses, attacks, or compromises.

entries.title: advisory
entries.summaryMd: Notification of significant new trends or developments regarding the threat to the information systems of an organization. This notification may include analytical insights into trends, intentions, technologies, or tactics of an adversary targeting information systems. Rationale: General definition of a commonly understood term.

senses.definitionMd: Notification of significant new trends or developments regarding the threat to the information systems of an organization. This notification may include analytical insights into trends, intentions, technologies, or tactics of an adversary targeting information systems. Rationale: General definition of a commonly understood term.

entries.title: AES(k, input)
entries.summaryMd: A single AES encryption operation as specified in [FIPS 197] with k and input being the AES encryption key and one 128-bit block of plaintext/data, respectively.

senses.definitionMd: A single AES encryption operation as specified in [FIPS 197] with k and input being the AES encryption key and one 128-bit block of plaintext/data, respectively.

entries.title: Affine Transformation
entries.summaryMd: A transformation consisting of multiplication by a matrix followed by the addition of a vector.

senses.definitionMd: A transformation consisting of multiplication by a matrix followed by the addition of a vector.

entries.title: After Action Report
entries.summaryMd: A document containing findings and recommendations from an exercise or a test.

senses.definitionMd: A document containing findings and recommendations from an exercise or a test.

entries.title: agency
entries.summaryMd: Any executive department, military department, government corporation, government controlled corporation, or other establishment in the executive branch of the government (including the Executive Office of the President), or any independent regulatory agency, but does not include: (i) the Government Accountability Office; (ii) the Federal Election Commission; (iii) the governments of the District of Columbia and of the territories and possessions of the United States, and their various subdivisions; or (iv) government-owned contractor-operated facilities, including laboratories engaged in national defense research and production activities.

senses.definitionMd: Any executive department, military department, government corporation, government controlled corporation, or other establishment in the executive branch of the government (including the Executive Office of the President), or any independent regulatory agency, but does not include: (i) the Government Accountability Office; (ii) the Federal Election Commission; (iii) the governments of the District of Columbia and of the territories and possessions of the United States, and their various subdivisions; or (iv) government-owned contractor-operated facilities, including laboratories engaged in national defense research and production activities.

entries.title: Agency Dashboard
entries.summaryMd: An organizational-level dashboard that: a) collects data from a collection system; and b) shows detailed assessment object-level data and assessment object-level defects to organizationally authorized personnel.

senses.definitionMd: An organizational-level dashboard that: a) collects data from a collection system; and b) shows detailed assessment object-level data and assessment object-level defects to organizationally authorized personnel.

entries.title: Agent
entries.summaryMd: A program acting on behalf of a person or organization.

senses.definitionMd: A program acting on behalf of a person or organization.

entries.title: Aggregate
entries.summaryMd: To combine several more-specific prefixes into a less-specific prefix.

senses.definitionMd: To combine several more-specific prefixes into a less-specific prefix.

entries.title: Aggregated Information
entries.summaryMd: Information elements collated on a number of individuals, typically used for the purposes of making comparisons or identifying patterns.

senses.definitionMd: Information elements collated on a number of individuals, typically used for the purposes of making comparisons or identifying patterns.

entries.title: ambiguity rule

In some [National Statistical Organizations] the values of p and q are confidential.

entries.title: artificial intelligence system
entries.summaryMd: Any data system, software, hardware, application, tool, or utility that operates in whole or in part using AI.

senses.definitionMd: Any data system, software, hardware, application, tool, or utility that operates in whole or in part using AI.

entries.title: Asia-Pacific Network Information Centre
entries.summaryMd: The Regional Internet Registry for the Asia Pacific region that allocates and registers Internet resources in its region.

senses.definitionMd: The Regional Internet Registry for the Asia Pacific region that allocates and registers Internet resources in its region.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Asia-Pacific Network Information Centre"

entries.title: aspect
entries.summaryMd: The subject or topic of an assessment element that is associated with a portion of the ISCM program under assessment.

senses.definitionMd: The subject or topic of an assessment element that is associated with a portion of the ISCM program under assessment.

entries.title: assembly
entries.summaryMd: An item forming a portion of an equipment, that can be provisioned and replaced as an entity and which normally incorporates replaceable parts and groups of parts.

senses.definitionMd: An item forming a portion of an equipment, that can be provisioned and replaced as an entity and which normally incorporates replaceable parts and groups of parts.

entries.title: assertion
entries.summaryMd: A verifiable statement from an IdP to an RP that contains information about an end user. Assertions may also contain information about the end user’s authentication event at the IdP.

senses.definitionMd: A verifiable statement from an IdP to an RP that contains information about an end user. Assertions may also contain information about the end user’s authentication event at the IdP.

entries.title: assertion injection attack
entries.summaryMd: In the context of a federated protocol, consists of an attacker attempting to force an RP to accept or process an assertion or assertion reference in order to gain access to the RP or deny a legitimate subscriber access to the RP. The attacker does this by taking an assertion or assertion reference and injecting it into a vulnerable RP.

senses.definitionMd: In the context of a federated protocol, consists of an attacker attempting to force an RP to accept or process an assertion or assertion reference in order to gain access to the RP or deny a legitimate subscriber access to the RP. The attacker does this by taking an assertion or assertion reference and injecting it into a vulnerable RP.

entries.title: assertion presentation
entries.summaryMd: The method by which an assertion is transmitted to the RP.

senses.definitionMd: The method by which an assertion is transmitted to the RP.

entries.title: assessment
entries.summaryMd: The process of identifying risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, resulting from the operation of an information system. Part of risk management, incorporates threat and vulnerability analyses, and considers mitigations provided by security controls planned or in place. Synonymous with risk analysis.

senses.definitionMd: The process of identifying risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, resulting from the operation of an information system. Part of risk management, incorporates threat and vulnerability analyses, and considers mitigations provided by security controls planned or in place. Synonymous with risk analysis.

entries.title: assessment approach
entries.summaryMd: The approach used to assess risk and its contributing risk factors, including quantitatively, qualitatively, or semi-quantitatively.

senses.definitionMd: The approach used to assess risk and its contributing risk factors, including quantitatively, qualitatively, or semi-quantitatively.

entries.title: Assessment Boundary
entries.summaryMd: The scope of (assessment objects included in) an organization’s ISCM implementation to which assessment of objects is applied. Typically, assessment boundary includes an entire network to its outside perimeter.

senses.definitionMd: The scope of (assessment objects included in) an organization’s ISCM implementation to which assessment of objects is applied. Typically, assessment boundary includes an entire network to its outside perimeter.

entries.title: Assessment Completeness
entries.summaryMd: The degree to which the continuous monitoring-generated, security-related information is collected on all assessment objects for all applicable defect checks within a defined period of time.

senses.definitionMd: The degree to which the continuous monitoring-generated, security-related information is collected on all assessment objects for all applicable defect checks within a defined period of time.

entries.title: Assessment Criterion/Criteria
entries.summaryMd: A rule (or rules) of logic to allow the automated or manual detection of defects. Typically, the assessment criterion in ISCM defines what in the desired state specification is compared to what in the actual state and the conditions that indicate a defect.

senses.definitionMd: A rule (or rules) of logic to allow the automated or manual detection of defects. Typically, the assessment criterion in ISCM defines what in the desired state specification is compared to what in the actual state and the conditions that indicate a defect.

entries.title: assessment element
entries.summaryMd: A specific ISCM concept to be evaluated in the context of a specific ISCM Process Step.

senses.definitionMd: A specific ISCM concept to be evaluated in the context of a specific ISCM Process Step.

entries.title: assessment element attribute
entries.summaryMd: An item of information that is specifically applicable to an assessment element, such as the source for the assessment element or risk management level to which the element applies.

senses.definitionMd: An item of information that is specifically applicable to an assessment element, such as the source for the assessment element or risk management level to which the element applies.

entries.title: assessment element text
entries.summaryMd: A statement that should be true for a well-implemented ISCM program. This statement is the evaluation criteria part of an assessment element.

senses.definitionMd: A statement that should be true for a well-implemented ISCM program. This statement is the evaluation criteria part of an assessment element.

entries.title: assessment findings
entries.summaryMd: Assessment results produced by the application of an assessment procedure to a security control or control enhancement to achieve an assessment objective; the execution of a determination statement within an assessment procedure by an assessor that results in either a satisfied or other than satisfied condition.

senses.definitionMd: Assessment results produced by the application of an assessment procedure to a security control or control enhancement to achieve an assessment objective; the execution of a determination statement within an assessment procedure by an assessor that results in either a satisfied or other than satisfied condition.

entries.title: assessment method
entries.summaryMd: One of three types of actions (i.e., examine, interview, test) taken by assessors in obtaining evidence during an assessment.

senses.definitionMd: One of three types of actions (i.e., examine, interview, test) taken by assessors in obtaining evidence during an assessment.

entries.title: assessment object
entries.summaryMd: The item (i.e., specifications, mechanisms, activities, individuals) upon which an assessment method is applied during an assessment.

senses.definitionMd: The item (i.e., specifications, mechanisms, activities, individuals) upon which an assessment method is applied during an assessment.

entries.title: assessment objective
entries.summaryMd: A set of determination statements that expresses the desired outcome for the assessment of a security control or control enhancement.

senses.definitionMd: A set of determination statements that expresses the desired outcome for the assessment of a security control or control enhancement.

entries.title: assessment plan
entries.summaryMd: The objectives for the control assessments and a detailed roadmap of how to conduct such assessments.

senses.definitionMd: The objectives for the control assessments and a detailed roadmap of how to conduct such assessments.

entries.title: assessment procedure
entries.summaryMd: A set of assessment objectives and an associated set of assessment methods and assessment objects.

senses.definitionMd: A set of assessment objectives and an associated set of assessment methods and assessment objects.

entries.title: assessment results
entries.summaryMd: The output or outcome of an assessment.

senses.definitionMd: The output or outcome of an assessment.

entries.title: Assessment Timeliness
entries.summaryMd: The degree to which the continuous monitoring-generated, security-related information is collected within the specified period of time (or frequency).

senses.definitionMd: The degree to which the continuous monitoring-generated, security-related information is collected within the specified period of time (or frequency).

entries.title: assessor
entries.summaryMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a risk assessment.

senses.definitionMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a risk assessment.

entries.title: asset
entries.summaryMd: A major application, general support system, high impact program, physical plant, mission critical system, personnel, equipment, or a logically related group of systems.

senses.definitionMd: A major application, general support system, high impact program, physical plant, mission critical system, personnel, equipment, or a logically related group of systems.

entries.title: asset identification
entries.summaryMd: SCAP constructs to uniquely identify assets (components) based on known identifiers and/or known information about the assets.

senses.definitionMd: SCAP constructs to uniquely identify assets (components) based on known identifiers and/or known information about the assets.

entries.title: Asset Identification Element
entries.summaryMd: A complete, bound expression of an asset identification using the constructs defined in this specification.

senses.definitionMd: A complete, bound expression of an asset identification using the constructs defined in this specification.

entries.title: Asset Report
entries.summaryMd: A collection of content (or link to content) about an asset.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of content (or link to content) about an asset.

entries.title: Asset Report Request
entries.summaryMd: A collection of structured information used as input to generate an asset report. An asset report request may be of any format and may have different contexts depending on the nature of the request. For instance, the request may be written in a control language that dictates how the request is to be propagated and executed. The request may also be written as a formal definition without reference to how the request is to be executed. The request may also be a prose description that must be interpreted and executed by a person. These examples are not exhaustive.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of structured information used as input to generate an asset report. An asset report request may be of any format and may have different contexts depending on the nature of the request. For instance, the request may be written in a control language that dictates how the request is to be propagated and executed. The request may also be written as a formal definition without reference to how the request is to be executed. The request may also be a prose description that must be interpreted and executed by a person. These examples are not exhaustive.

entries.title: asset reporting format
entries.summaryMd: A format for expressing the transport format of information about assets and the relationships between assets and reports.

senses.definitionMd: A format for expressing the transport format of information about assets and the relationships between assets and reports.

entries.title: Asset Reporting Format Report
entries.summaryMd: The collection of all assets, report requests, reports, and relationships for a given instance of ARF.

senses.definitionMd: The collection of all assets, report requests, reports, and relationships for a given instance of ARF.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Asset Reporting Format Report"

entries.title: Asset Tag
entries.summaryMd: Simple key value attributes that are associated with a platform (e.g., location, company name, division, or department).

senses.definitionMd: Simple key value attributes that are associated with a platform (e.g., location, company name, division, or department).

entries.title: assignment operation
entries.summaryMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to assign a specific, organization-defined value to the control or control enhancement (e.g., assigning a list of roles to be notified or a value for the frequency of testing).
