senses.definitionMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to assign a specific, organization-defined value to the control or control enhancement (e.g., assigning a list of roles to be notified or a value for the frequency of testing).

entries.title: assignment statement
entries.summaryMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to assign a specific, organization-defined value to the control or control enhancement (e.g., assigning a list of roles to be notified or a value for the frequency of testing). See organization-defined control parameters and selection statement.

senses.definitionMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to assign a specific, organization-defined value to the control or control enhancement (e.g., assigning a list of roles to be notified or a value for the frequency of testing). See organization-defined control parameters and selection statement.

entries.title: Associated Data
entries.summaryMd: Input data to the CCM generation-encryption process that is authenticated but not encrypted.

senses.definitionMd: Input data to the CCM generation-encryption process that is authenticated but not encrypted.

entries.title: Association
entries.summaryMd: A relationship for a particular purpose; for example, a key is associated with the application or process for which it will be used.

senses.definitionMd: A relationship for a particular purpose; for example, a key is associated with the application or process for which it will be used.

entries.title: Assumption
entries.summaryMd: Used to indicate the conditions that are required to be true when an approved key-establishment scheme is executed in accordance with this Recommendation.

senses.definitionMd: Used to indicate the conditions that are required to be true when an approved key-establishment scheme is executed in accordance with this Recommendation.

entries.title: assurance
entries.summaryMd: Measure of confidence that the security features, practices, procedures, and architecture of an information system accurately mediates and enforces the security policy.

senses.definitionMd: Measure of confidence that the security features, practices, procedures, and architecture of an information system accurately mediates and enforces the security policy.

entries.title: assurance case
entries.summaryMd: A reasoned, auditable artifact created that supports the contention that its top-level claim (or set of claims), is satisfied, including systematic argumentation and its underlying evidence and explicit assumptions that support the claim(s).

senses.definitionMd: A reasoned, auditable artifact created that supports the contention that its top-level claim (or set of claims), is satisfied, including systematic argumentation and its underlying evidence and explicit assumptions that support the claim(s).

entries.title: assurance evidence
entries.summaryMd: The information upon which decisions regarding assurance, trustworthiness, and risk of the solution are substantiated.

senses.definitionMd: The information upon which decisions regarding assurance, trustworthiness, and risk of the solution are substantiated.

entries.title: assurance_level
entries.summaryMd: The level of assurance (e.g., HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW) that a claimed signatory possesses the private signature key.

senses.definitionMd: The level of assurance (e.g., HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW) that a claimed signatory possesses the private signature key.

entries.title: Assurance message
entries.summaryMd: See private-key-possession assurance message.

senses.definitionMd: See private-key-possession assurance message.

entries.title: Assurance of domain parameter validity
entries.summaryMd: Confidence that the domain parameters are arithmetically correct.

senses.definitionMd: Confidence that the domain parameters are arithmetically correct.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Assurance of domain parameter validity"

entries.title: assurance of integrity
entries.summaryMd: Guarding against improper information modification or destruction, and includes ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity.

senses.definitionMd: Guarding against improper information modification or destruction, and includes ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity.

entries.title: Assurance of possession
entries.summaryMd: Confidence that an entity possesses a private key and any associated keying material.

senses.definitionMd: Confidence that an entity possesses a private key and any associated keying material.

entries.title: Assurance of public key validity
entries.summaryMd: Confidence that the public key is arithmetically correct.

senses.definitionMd: Confidence that the public key is arithmetically correct.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Assurance of public key validity"

entries.title: Assurance of validity
entries.summaryMd: Confidence that a public key or domain parameter is arithmetically correct.

senses.definitionMd: Confidence that a public key or domain parameter is arithmetically correct.

entries.title: Assurance- signature
entries.summaryMd: A digital signature on a private-key-possession assurance message.

senses.definitionMd: A digital signature on a private-key-possession assurance message.

entries.title: assurance_time
entries.summaryMd: The time at which assurance of possession is obtained.

senses.definitionMd: The time at which assurance of possession is obtained.

entries.title: assured information sharing
entries.summaryMd: The ability to confidently share information with those who need it, when and where they need it, as determined by operational need and an acceptable level of security risk.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to confidently share information with those who need it, when and where they need it, as determined by operational need and an acceptable level of security risk.

entries.title: assured software
entries.summaryMd: Computer application that has been designed, developed, analyzed and tested using processes, tools, and techniques that establish a level of confidence in it.

senses.definitionMd: Computer application that has been designed, developed, analyzed and tested using processes, tools, and techniques that establish a level of confidence in it.

entries.title: asymmetric cryptography
entries.summaryMd: Cryptography that uses two separate keys to exchange data — one to encrypt or digitally sign the data and one to decrypt the data or verify the digital signature. Also known as public-key cryptography.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptography that uses two separate keys to exchange data — one to encrypt or digitally sign the data and one to decrypt the data or verify the digital signature. Also known as public-key cryptography.

entries.title: Asymmetric-key cryptography
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic system where users have a private key that is kept secret and used to generate a public key (which is freely provided to others). Users can digitally sign data with their private key and the resulting signature can be verified by anyone using the corresponding public key. Also known as a Public-key cryptography.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic system where users have a private key that is kept secret and used to generate a public key (which is freely provided to others). Users can digitally sign data with their private key and the resulting signature can be verified by anyone using the corresponding public key. Also known as a Public-key cryptography.

entries.title: Asymptotic Analysis
entries.summaryMd: A statistical technique that derives limiting approximations for functions of interest.

senses.definitionMd: A statistical technique that derives limiting approximations for functions of interest.

entries.title: Asymptotic Distribution
entries.summaryMd: The limiting distribution of a test statistic arising when n approaches infinity.

senses.definitionMd: The limiting distribution of a test statistic arising when n approaches infinity.

entries.title: atomic clock
entries.summaryMd: A clock referenced to an atomic oscillator. Only clocks with an internal atomic oscillator qualify as atomic clocks.

senses.definitionMd: A clock referenced to an atomic oscillator. Only clocks with an internal atomic oscillator qualify as atomic clocks.

entries.title: atomic operation
entries.summaryMd: An atomic operation is effectively executed as a single step, no other process can read or modify the internal state while the atomic operation is executed.

senses.definitionMd: An atomic operation is effectively executed as a single step, no other process can read or modify the internal state while the atomic operation is executed.

entries.title: atomic oscillator
entries.summaryMd: An oscillator that uses the quantized energy levels in atoms or molecules as the source of its resonance. The laws of quantum mechanics dictate that the energies of a bound system, such as an atom, have certain discrete values. An electromagnetic field at a particular frequency can boost an atom from one energy level to a higher one, or an atom at a high energy level can drop to a lower level by emitting energy. The resonance frequency, fo, of an atomic oscillator is the difference between the two energy levels divided by Planck’s constant, h. The principle underlying the atomic oscillator is that since all atoms of a specific element are identical, they should produce exactly the same frequency when they absorb or release energy. In theory, the atom is a perfect “pendulum” whose oscillations are counted to measure a time interval. The national frequency standards developed by NIST and other laboratories derive their resonance frequency from the cesium atom and typically use cesium fountain technology. Rubidium oscillators are the lowest priced and most common atomic oscillators, but cesium beam and hydrogen maser atomic oscillators are also sold commercially in much smaller quantities.

senses.definitionMd: An oscillator that uses the quantized energy levels in atoms or molecules as the source of its resonance. The laws of quantum mechanics dictate that the energies of a bound system, such as an atom, have certain discrete values. An electromagnetic field at a particular frequency can boost an atom from one energy level to a higher one, or an atom at a high energy level can drop to a lower level by emitting energy. The resonance frequency, fo, of an atomic oscillator is the difference between the two energy levels divided by Planck’s constant, h. The principle underlying the atomic oscillator is that since all atoms of a specific element are identical, they should produce exactly the same frequency when they absorb or release energy. In theory, the atom is a perfect “pendulum” whose oscillations are counted to measure a time interval. The national frequency standards developed by NIST and other laboratories derive their resonance frequency from the cesium atom and typically use cesium fountain technology. Rubidium oscillators are the lowest priced and most common atomic oscillators, but cesium beam and hydrogen maser atomic oscillators are also sold commercially in much smaller quantities.

entries.title: Atomic Swap
entries.summaryMd: An exchange of tokens that does not involve the intervention of any trusted intermediary and automatically reverts if all of the provisions are not met.

senses.definitionMd: An exchange of tokens that does not involve the intervention of any trusted intermediary and automatically reverts if all of the provisions are not met.

entries.title: attack
entries.summaryMd: Any kind of malicious activity that attempts to collect, disrupt, deny, degrade, or destroy information system resources or the information itself.

senses.definitionMd: Any kind of malicious activity that attempts to collect, disrupt, deny, degrade, or destroy information system resources or the information itself.

entries.title: attack sensing and warning
entries.summaryMd: Detection, correlation, identification, and characterization of intentional unauthorized activity with notification to decision makers so that an appropriate response can be developed.

senses.definitionMd: Detection, correlation, identification, and characterization of intentional unauthorized activity with notification to decision makers so that an appropriate response can be developed.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "attack sensing and warning"

entries.title: attack signature
entries.summaryMd: A specific sequence of events indicative of an unauthorized access attempt.

senses.definitionMd: A specific sequence of events indicative of an unauthorized access attempt.

entries.title: attack surface
entries.summaryMd: The set of points on the boundary of a system, a system component, or an environment where an attacker can try to enter, cause an effect on, or extract data from, that system, component, or environment.

senses.definitionMd: The set of points on the boundary of a system, a system component, or an environment where an attacker can try to enter, cause an effect on, or extract data from, that system, component, or environment.

entries.title: attack tree
entries.summaryMd: A branching, hierarchical data structure that represents a set of potential approaches to achieving an event in which system security is penetrated or compromised in a specified way.

senses.definitionMd: A branching, hierarchical data structure that represents a set of potential approaches to achieving an event in which system security is penetrated or compromised in a specified way.

entries.title: attacker
entries.summaryMd: A person who seeks to exploit potential vulnerabilities of a system.

senses.definitionMd: A person who seeks to exploit potential vulnerabilities of a system.

entries.title: attended
entries.summaryMd: Under continuous positive control of personnel authorized for access or use.

senses.definitionMd: Under continuous positive control of personnel authorized for access or use.

entries.title: attestation
entries.summaryMd: The process of providing a digital signature for a set of measurements securely stored in hardware, and then having the requester validate the signature and the set of measurements.

senses.definitionMd: The process of providing a digital signature for a set of measurements securely stored in hardware, and then having the requester validate the signature and the set of measurements.

entries.title: attribute
entries.summaryMd: An attribute is any distinctive feature, characteristic, or property of an object that can be identified or isolated quantitatively or qualitatively by either human or automated means.

senses.definitionMd: An attribute is any distinctive feature, characteristic, or property of an object that can be identified or isolated quantitatively or qualitatively by either human or automated means.

entries.title: attribute-based access control (ABAC)
entries.summaryMd: An access control approach in which access is mediated based on attributes associated with subjects (requesters) and the objects to be accessed. Each object and subject has a set of associated attributes, such as location, time of creation, access rights, etc. Access to an object is authorized or denied depending upon whether the required (e.g., policy-defined) correlation can be made between the attributes of that object and of the requesting subject.

senses.definitionMd: An access control approach in which access is mediated based on attributes associated with subjects (requesters) and the objects to be accessed. Each object and subject has a set of associated attributes, such as location, time of creation, access rights, etc. Access to an object is authorized or denied depending upon whether the required (e.g., policy-defined) correlation can be made between the attributes of that object and of the requesting subject.

entries.title: attribute-based authorization
entries.summaryMd: A structured process that determines when a user is authorized to access information, systems, or services based on attributes of the user and of the information, system, or service.

senses.definitionMd: A structured process that determines when a user is authorized to access information, systems, or services based on attributes of the user and of the information, system, or service.

entries.title: attribute disclosure
entries.summaryMd: Re-identification event in which an entity learns confidential information about a data principal, without necessarily identifying the data principal.

senses.definitionMd: Re-identification event in which an entity learns confidential information about a data principal, without necessarily identifying the data principal.

entries.title: attribute inference attacks
entries.summaryMd: An attack against machine learning models that infers sensitive attributes of a training data record, given partial knowledge about the record.

senses.definitionMd: An attack against machine learning models that infers sensitive attributes of a training data record, given partial knowledge about the record.

entries.title: attribute provider
entries.summaryMd: The provider of an identity API that provides access to a subscriber’s attributes without necessarily asserting that the subscriber is present to the RP.

senses.definitionMd: The provider of an identity API that provides access to a subscriber’s attributes without necessarily asserting that the subscriber is present to the RP.

entries.title: Attribute Reference
entries.summaryMd: A statement asserting a property of a subscriber without necessarily containing identity information, independent of format. For example, for the attribute “birthday,” a reference could be “older than 18” or “born in December.”

senses.definitionMd: A statement asserting a property of a subscriber without necessarily containing identity information, independent of format. For example, for the attribute “birthday,” a reference could be “older than 18” or “born in December.”

entries.title: attribute validation
entries.summaryMd: Confirmation (through the provision of strong, sound, objective evidence) that requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled (e.g., a trustworthy credential has been presented, or data or information has been formatted in accordance with a defined set of rules, or a specific process has demonstrated that an entity under consideration meets, in all respects, its defined attributes or requirements).

senses.definitionMd: Confirmation (through the provision of strong, sound, objective evidence) that requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled (e.g., a trustworthy credential has been presented, or data or information has been formatted in accordance with a defined set of rules, or a specific process has demonstrated that an entity under consideration meets, in all respects, its defined attributes or requirements).

entries.title: Attribute Value
entries.summaryMd: A complete statement that asserts an identity attribute of a subscriber, independent of format. For example, for the attribute “birthday,” a value could be “12/1/1980” or “December 1, 1980.”

senses.definitionMd: A complete statement that asserts an identity attribute of a subscriber, independent of format. For example, for the attribute “birthday,” a value could be “12/1/1980” or “December 1, 1980.”

entries.title: Attribute-Value Pair
entries.summaryMd: A tuple a=v in which a (the attribute) is an alphanumeric label representing a property or state, and v (the value) is the value assigned to the attribute.

senses.definitionMd: A tuple a=v in which a (the attribute) is an alphanumeric label representing a property or state, and v (the value) is the value assigned to the attribute.

entries.title: Audience
entries.summaryMd: The intended audience that should be able to install, test, and use the checklist, including suggested minimum skills and knowledge required to correctly use the checklist.

senses.definitionMd: The intended audience that should be able to install, test, and use the checklist, including suggested minimum skills and knowledge required to correctly use the checklist.

entries.title: audience restriction
entries.summaryMd: The restriction of a message to a specific target audience to prevent a receiver from unknowingly processing a message that is intended for another recipient. In federation protocols, assertions are audience-restricted to specific RPs to prevent an RP from accepting an assertion that was generated for a different RP.

senses.definitionMd: The restriction of a message to a specific target audience to prevent a receiver from unknowingly processing a message that is intended for another recipient. In federation protocols, assertions are audience-restricted to specific RPs to prevent an RP from accepting an assertion that was generated for a different RP.

entries.title: audit
entries.summaryMd: Independent review and examination of records and activities to assess the adequacy of system controls, to ensure compliance with established policies and operational procedures.

senses.definitionMd: Independent review and examination of records and activities to assess the adequacy of system controls, to ensure compliance with established policies and operational procedures.

entries.title: Audit administrator
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for establishing and reviewing an audit log, assuring that the log is reviewed periodically and after any security-compromise-relevant event, and providing audit reports to FCKMS managers.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for establishing and reviewing an audit log, assuring that the log is reviewed periodically and after any security-compromise-relevant event, and providing audit reports to FCKMS managers.

entries.title: audit log
entries.summaryMd: A chronological record of system activities. Includes records of system accesses and operations performed in a given period.

senses.definitionMd: A chronological record of system activities. Includes records of system accesses and operations performed in a given period.

entries.title: audit record
entries.summaryMd: An individual entry in an audit log related to an audited event.

senses.definitionMd: An individual entry in an audit log related to an audited event.

entries.title: audit record reduction
entries.summaryMd: A process that manipulates collected audit information and organizes it into a summary format that is more meaningful to analysts.

senses.definitionMd: A process that manipulates collected audit information and organizes it into a summary format that is more meaningful to analysts.

entries.title: audit reduction tools
entries.summaryMd: Preprocessors designed to reduce the volume of audit records to facilitate manual review. Before a security review, these tools can remove many audit records known to have little security significance. These tools generally remove records generated by specific classes of events, such as records generated by nightly backups.

senses.definitionMd: Preprocessors designed to reduce the volume of audit records to facilitate manual review. Before a security review, these tools can remove many audit records known to have little security significance. These tools generally remove records generated by specific classes of events, such as records generated by nightly backups.

entries.title: audit trail
entries.summaryMd: A record showing who has accessed an information technology (IT) system and what operations the user has performed during a given period.

senses.definitionMd: A record showing who has accessed an information technology (IT) system and what operations the user has performed during a given period.

entries.title: Auditor
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for establishing and reviewing an audit log, assuring that the log is reviewed periodically and after any security-compromise-relevant event, and providing audit reports to FCKMS managers.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for establishing and reviewing an audit log, assuring that the log is reviewed periodically and after any security-compromise-relevant event, and providing audit reports to FCKMS managers.

entries.title: authenticable entity
entries.summaryMd: An entity that can successfully participate in an authentication protocol with a card application.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that can successfully participate in an authentication protocol with a card application.

entries.title: authenticate
entries.summaryMd: The process of establishing confidence of authenticity; in this case, the validity of a person’s identity and an authenticator (e.g., PIV Card or derived PIV credential).

senses.definitionMd: The process of establishing confidence of authenticity; in this case, the validity of a person’s identity and an authenticator (e.g., PIV Card or derived PIV credential).

entries.title: Authenticated Configuration Scanner
entries.summaryMd: A product that runs with administrative or root privileges on a target system to conduct its assessment.

senses.definitionMd: A product that runs with administrative or root privileges on a target system to conduct its assessment.

entries.title: Authenticated Decryption
entries.summaryMd: The function of GCM in which the ciphertext is decrypted into the plaintext, and the authenticity of the ciphertext and the AAD is verified.

senses.definitionMd: The function of GCM in which the ciphertext is decrypted into the plaintext, and the authenticity of the ciphertext and the AAD is verified.

entries.title: authenticated-decryption function
entries.summaryMd: A function that decrypts purported ciphertext into corresponding plaintext and verifies the authenticity and, therefore, the integrity of the data. The output is either the plaintext or an indication that the plaintext is not authentic.

senses.definitionMd: A function that decrypts purported ciphertext into corresponding plaintext and verifies the authenticity and, therefore, the integrity of the data. The output is either the plaintext or an indication that the plaintext is not authentic.

entries.title: Authenticated Encryption
entries.summaryMd: The function of GCM in which the plaintext is encrypted into the ciphertext, and an authentication tag is generated on the AAD and the ciphertext.

senses.definitionMd: The function of GCM in which the plaintext is encrypted into the ciphertext, and an authentication tag is generated on the AAD and the ciphertext.

entries.title: authenticated- encryption function
entries.summaryMd: A function that encrypts plaintext into ciphertext and provides a means for the associated authenticated-decryption function to verify the authenticity and, therefore, the integrity of the data.

senses.definitionMd: A function that encrypts plaintext into ciphertext and provides a means for the associated authenticated-decryption function to verify the authenticity and, therefore, the integrity of the data.

entries.title: authenticated protected channel
entries.summaryMd: An encrypted channel that uses approved cryptography where the connection initiator (client) has authenticated the recipient (server).

senses.definitionMd: An encrypted channel that uses approved cryptography where the connection initiator (client) has authenticated the recipient (server).

entries.title: Authenticated RFID
entries.summaryMd: The use of digital signature technology to provide evidence of the authenticity of a tag and possibly chain of custody events.

senses.definitionMd: The use of digital signature technology to provide evidence of the authenticity of a tag and possibly chain of custody events.

entries.title: authenticated session
entries.summaryMd: A session in which messages between two participants are encrypted and integrity is protected using a set of shared secrets called “session keys.” A protected session is said to be authenticated if one participant proves possession of one or more authenticators in addition to the session keys and if the other party can verify the identity associated with the authenticators during the session. If both participants are authenticated, the protected session is said to be mutually authenticated.

senses.definitionMd: A session in which messages between two participants are encrypted and integrity is protected using a set of shared secrets called “session keys.” A protected session is said to be authenticated if one participant proves possession of one or more authenticators in addition to the session keys and if the other party can verify the identity associated with the authenticators during the session. If both participants are authenticated, the protected session is said to be mutually authenticated.

entries.title: authentication
entries.summaryMd: Verifying the identity of a user, process, or device, often as a prerequisite to allowing access to resources in an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Verifying the identity of a user, process, or device, often as a prerequisite to allowing access to resources in an information system.

entries.title: authentication assurance level
entries.summaryMd: A category that describes the strength of the authentication process.

senses.definitionMd: A category that describes the strength of the authentication process.

entries.title: Authentication code
entries.summaryMd: A keyed cryptographic checksum based on an approved security function; also known as a Message Authentication Code.

senses.definitionMd: A keyed cryptographic checksum based on an approved security function; also known as a Message Authentication Code.

entries.title: authentication event
entries.summaryMd: An attempt by a user to authenticate to an online service that ends in overall success or failure.

senses.definitionMd: An attempt by a user to authenticate to an online service that ends in overall success or failure.

entries.title: Authentication Factor
entries.summaryMd: The three types of authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are. Every authenticator has one or more authentication factors.

senses.definitionMd: The three types of authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are. Every authenticator has one or more authentication factors.

entries.title: Authentication Header (AH)
entries.summaryMd: A deprecated IPsec security protocol that provides integrity protection (but not confidentiality) for packet headers and data.

senses.definitionMd: A deprecated IPsec security protocol that provides integrity protection (but not confidentiality) for packet headers and data.

entries.title: Authentication Information
entries.summaryMd: Information used to establish the validity of a claimed identity.

senses.definitionMd: Information used to establish the validity of a claimed identity.

entries.title: Authentication Key
entries.summaryMd: A private or symmetric key used by an authenticator to generate the authenticator output.

senses.definitionMd: A private or symmetric key used by an authenticator to generate the authenticator output.

entries.title: authentication mechanism
entries.summaryMd: Hardware or software-based mechanisms that force users to prove their identity before accessing data on a device.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware or software-based mechanisms that force users to prove their identity before accessing data on a device.

entries.title: authentication period
entries.summaryMd: The period between any initial authentication process and subsequent re-authentication processes during a single terminal session or during the period data is being accessed.

senses.definitionMd: The period between any initial authentication process and subsequent re-authentication processes during a single terminal session or during the period data is being accessed.

entries.title: authentication protocol
entries.summaryMd: 2. A defined sequence of messages between a Claimant and a Verifier that demonstrates that the Claimant has possession and control of a valid token to establish his/her identity, and optionally, demonstrates to the Claimant that he or she is communicating with the intended Verifier.

senses.definitionMd: 2. A defined sequence of messages between a Claimant and a Verifier that demonstrates that the Claimant has possession and control of a valid token to establish his/her identity, and optionally, demonstrates to the Claimant that he or she is communicating with the intended Verifier.

entries.title: Authentication Tag
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic checksum on data that is designed to reveal both accidental errors and the intentional modification of the data.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic checksum on data that is designed to reveal both accidental errors and the intentional modification of the data.

entries.title: authenticator
entries.summaryMd: Something the cardholder possesses and controls (e.g., PIV Card or derived PIV credential) that is used to authenticate the cardholder’s identity.

senses.definitionMd: Something the cardholder possesses and controls (e.g., PIV Card or derived PIV credential) that is used to authenticate the cardholder’s identity.

entries.title: Authenticator Assurance Level (AAL)
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the strength of an authentication mechanism and, therefore, the confidence in it, as defined in [NIST SP 800-63-3] in terms of three levels: AAL1 (Some confidence), AAL2 (High confidence), AAL3 (Very high confidence).

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the strength of an authentication mechanism and, therefore, the confidence in it, as defined in [NIST SP 800-63-3] in terms of three levels: AAL1 (Some confidence), AAL2 (High confidence), AAL3 (Very high confidence).

entries.title: authenticator binding
entries.summaryMd: The establishment of an association between a specific authenticator and a subscriber account that allows the authenticator to authenticate the subscriber associated with the account, possibly in conjunction with other authenticators.

senses.definitionMd: The establishment of an association between a specific authenticator and a subscriber account that allows the authenticator to authenticate the subscriber associated with the account, possibly in conjunction with other authenticators.

entries.title: authenticity
entries.summaryMd: The property that data originated from its purported source.

senses.definitionMd: The property that data originated from its purported source.

entries.title: Author
entries.summaryMd: The organization responsible for creating the checklist in its current format. In most cases an organization will represent both the author and authority of a checklist, but this is not always true. For example, if an organization produces validated SCAP content for a NIST publication, the organization that created the SCAP content will be listed as the Author, but NIST will remain the Authority.

senses.definitionMd: The organization responsible for creating the checklist in its current format. In most cases an organization will represent both the author and authority of a checklist, but this is not always true. For example, if an organization produces validated SCAP content for a NIST publication, the organization that created the SCAP content will be listed as the Author, but NIST will remain the Authority.

entries.title: authority
entries.summaryMd: The organization responsible for producing the original security configuration guidance represented by the checklist.

senses.definitionMd: The organization responsible for producing the original security configuration guidance represented by the checklist.

entries.title: Authority to Operate
entries.summaryMd: Authorization to Operate; One of three possible decisions concerning an issuer made by a Designated Authorizing Official after all assessment activities have been performed stating that the issuer is authorized to perform specific PIV Card and/or Derived Credential issuance services.

senses.definitionMd: Authorization to Operate; One of three possible decisions concerning an issuer made by a Designated Authorizing Official after all assessment activities have been performed stating that the issuer is authorized to perform specific PIV Card and/or Derived Credential issuance services.

entries.title: Authority Type
entries.summaryMd: The type of organization that is the authority for the checklist. The three types are Governmental Authority, Software Vendor, and Third Party (e.g., security organizations).

senses.definitionMd: The type of organization that is the authority for the checklist. The three types are Governmental Authority, Software Vendor, and Third Party (e.g., security organizations).

entries.title: authorization
entries.summaryMd: The right or a permission that is granted to a system entity to access a system resource.

senses.definitionMd: The right or a permission that is granted to a system entity to access a system resource.

entries.title: authorization boundary
entries.summaryMd: All components of an information system to be authorized for operation by an authorizing official and excludes separately authorized systems, to which the information system is connected.

senses.definitionMd: All components of an information system to be authorized for operation by an authorizing official and excludes separately authorized systems, to which the information system is connected.

entries.title: authorization package
entries.summaryMd: Documents the results of the security control assessment and provides the authorizing official with essential information needed to make a risk-based decision on whether to authorize operation of an information system or a designated set of common controls. Contains: (i) the security plan; (ii) the security assessment report (SAR); and (iii) the plan of action and milestones (POA&M). Note: Many departments and agencies may choose to include the risk assessment report (RAR) as part of the security authorization package. Also, many organizations use system security plan in place of the security plan.

senses.definitionMd: Documents the results of the security control assessment and provides the authorizing official with essential information needed to make a risk-based decision on whether to authorize operation of an information system or a designated set of common controls. Contains: (i) the security plan; (ii) the security assessment report (SAR); and (iii) the plan of action and milestones (POA&M). Note: Many departments and agencies may choose to include the risk assessment report (RAR) as part of the security authorization package. Also, many organizations use system security plan in place of the security plan.

entries.title: authorization to operate
entries.summaryMd: See authorization to operate (ATO).

senses.definitionMd: See authorization to operate (ATO).

entries.title: authorization to use
entries.summaryMd: The official management decision given by an authorizing official to authorize the use of an information system, service, or application based on the information in an existing authorization package generated by another organization, and to explicitly accept the risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of controls in the system, service, or application.

senses.definitionMd: The official management decision given by an authorizing official to authorize the use of an information system, service, or application based on the information in an existing authorization package generated by another organization, and to explicitly accept the risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of controls in the system, service, or application.

entries.title: authorize processing
entries.summaryMd: The official management decision given by a senior agency official to authorize operation of an information system and to explicitly accept the risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, or individuals, based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of security controls.

senses.definitionMd: The official management decision given by a senior agency official to authorize operation of an information system and to explicitly accept the risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, or individuals, based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of security controls.

entries.title: Authorized
entries.summaryMd: Entitled to a specific mode of access.

senses.definitionMd: Entitled to a specific mode of access.

entries.title: Authorized Entity
entries.summaryMd: An entity that has implicitly or explicitly been granted approval to interact with a particular IoT device. The device cybersecurity capabilities in the core baseline do not specify how authorization is implemented for distinguishing authorized and unauthorized entities, but can include identity management and authentication to establish the authorization of entities. It is left to the organization to decide how each device will implement authorization. Also, an entity authorized to interact with an IoT device in one way might not be authorized to interact with the same device in another way.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that has implicitly or explicitly been granted approval to interact with a particular IoT device. The device cybersecurity capabilities in the core baseline do not specify how authorization is implemented for distinguishing authorized and unauthorized entities, but can include identity management and authentication to establish the authorization of entities. It is left to the organization to decide how each device will implement authorization. Also, an entity authorized to interact with an IoT device in one way might not be authorized to interact with the same device in another way.

entries.title: authorized ID
entries.summaryMd: The key management entity (KME) authorized to order against a traditional short title.

senses.definitionMd: The key management entity (KME) authorized to order against a traditional short title.

entries.title: Authorized individuals, services, and other IoT product components
entries.summaryMd: An entity (i.e., a person, device, service, network, domain, developer, or other party who might interact with an IoT device) that has implicitly or explicitly been granted approval to interact with a particular IoT device.

senses.definitionMd: An entity (i.e., a person, device, service, network, domain, developer, or other party who might interact with an IoT device) that has implicitly or explicitly been granted approval to interact with a particular IoT device.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Authorized individuals, services, and other IoT product components"

entries.title: Authorized Key
entries.summaryMd: A public key that has been configured as authorizing access to an account by anyone capable of using the corresponding private key (identity key) in the SSH protocol. An authorized key may be configured with certain restrictions, most notably a forced command and a source restriction.

senses.definitionMd: A public key that has been configured as authorizing access to an account by anyone capable of using the corresponding private key (identity key) in the SSH protocol. An authorized key may be configured with certain restrictions, most notably a forced command and a source restriction.

entries.title: Authorized Keys File
entries.summaryMd: The file associated with a specific account where one or more authorized keys and optional restrictions are stored. Each account for which public key authentication is allowed on an SSH server has a unique authorized keys file.

senses.definitionMd: The file associated with a specific account where one or more authorized keys and optional restrictions are stored. Each account for which public key authentication is allowed on an SSH server has a unique authorized keys file.

entries.title: authorized party
entries.summaryMd: In federation, the organization, person, or entity that is responsible for making decisions regarding the release of information within the federation transaction, most notably subscriber attributes. This is often the subscriber (when runtime decisions are used) or the party operating the IdP (when allowlists are used).

senses.definitionMd: In federation, the organization, person, or entity that is responsible for making decisions regarding the release of information within the federation transaction, most notably subscriber attributes. This is often the subscriber (when runtime decisions are used) or the party operating the IdP (when allowlists are used).

entries.title: authorized user
entries.summaryMd: Any appropriately cleared individual with a requirement to access an information system (IS) for performing or assisting in a lawful and authorized government function.

senses.definitionMd: Any appropriately cleared individual with a requirement to access an information system (IS) for performing or assisting in a lawful and authorized government function.

entries.title: authorized vendor
entries.summaryMd: Manufacturer of information security (INFOSEC) equipment authorized to produce quantities in excess of contractual requirements for direct sale to eligible buyers. Eligible buyers are typically U.S. Government organizations or U.S. Government contractors.

senses.definitionMd: Manufacturer of information security (INFOSEC) equipment authorized to produce quantities in excess of contractual requirements for direct sale to eligible buyers. Eligible buyers are typically U.S. Government organizations or U.S. Government contractors.

entries.title: authorizing official
entries.summaryMd: Official with the authority to formally assume responsibility for operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, or individuals. Synonymous with Accreditation Authority.

senses.definitionMd: Official with the authority to formally assume responsibility for operating an information system at an acceptable level of risk to agency operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), agency assets, or individuals. Synonymous with Accreditation Authority.

entries.title: authorizing official designated representative
entries.summaryMd: An organizational official acting on behalf of an authorizing official in carrying out and coordinating the required activities associated with security authorization.

senses.definitionMd: An organizational official acting on behalf of an authorizing official in carrying out and coordinating the required activities associated with security authorization.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "authorizing official designated representative"

entries.title: Automated Access
entries.summaryMd: Access to a computer by an automated process without an interactive user, generally machine-to-machine access. Automated access is often triggered from scripts or schedulers, e.g., by executing an SSH client or a file transfer application. Many programs may also use automated access using SSH internally, including many privileged access management systems and systems management tools.

senses.definitionMd: Access to a computer by an automated process without an interactive user, generally machine-to-machine access. Automated access is often triggered from scripts or schedulers, e.g., by executing an SSH client or a file transfer application. Many programs may also use automated access using SSH internally, including many privileged access management systems and systems management tools.

entries.title: Automated Certificate
entries.summaryMd: A protocol defined in IETF RFC 8555 that provides for the automated enrollment of certificates.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol defined in IETF RFC 8555 that provides for the automated enrollment of certificates.

entries.title: Automated Certificate Management Environment
entries.summaryMd: A protocol defined in IETF RFC 8555 that provides for the automated enrollment of certificates.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol defined in IETF RFC 8555 that provides for the automated enrollment of certificates.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Automated Certificate Management Environment"

entries.title: Automated Checklist
entries.summaryMd: A checklist that is used through one or more tools that automatically alter or verify settings based on the contents of the checklist. Automated checklists document their security settings in a machine-readable format, either standard or proprietary.

senses.definitionMd: A checklist that is used through one or more tools that automatically alter or verify settings based on the contents of the checklist. Automated checklists document their security settings in a machine-readable format, either standard or proprietary.

entries.title: Automated Process
entries.summaryMd: An application, script, or management system that leverages SSH to execute commands or transfer data to/from another system.

senses.definitionMd: An application, script, or management system that leverages SSH to execute commands or transfer data to/from another system.

entries.title: automated security monitoring
entries.summaryMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness to support organizational risk decisions. See information security continuous monitoring, risk monitoring, and status monitoring

senses.definitionMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness to support organizational risk decisions. See information security continuous monitoring, risk monitoring, and status monitoring

entries.title: automatic remote rekeying
entries.summaryMd: Procedure to rekey distant cryptographic equipment electronically without specific actions by the receiving terminal operator.

senses.definitionMd: Procedure to rekey distant cryptographic equipment electronically without specific actions by the receiving terminal operator.

entries.title: Autonomous System (AS)
entries.summaryMd: One or more routers under a single administration operating the same routing policy.

senses.definitionMd: One or more routers under a single administration operating the same routing policy.

entries.title: Autonomous System Number (ASN)
entries.summaryMd: A two-byte number that identifies an AS.

senses.definitionMd: A two-byte number that identifies an AS.

entries.title: availability
entries.summaryMd: Ensuring timely and reliable access to and use of information.

senses.definitionMd: Ensuring timely and reliable access to and use of information.

entries.title: availability breakdown
entries.summaryMd: In the AML context, a disruption of the ability of other users or processes to obtain timely and reliable access to an AI system’s outputs or func­tionality.

senses.definitionMd: In the AML context, a disruption of the ability of other users or processes to obtain timely and reliable access to an AI system’s outputs or func­tionality.

entries.title: Availability Impact
entries.summaryMd: measures the potential impact to availability of a successfully exploited misuse vulnerability. Availability refers to the accessibility of information resources.

senses.definitionMd: measures the potential impact to availability of a successfully exploited misuse vulnerability. Availability refers to the accessibility of information resources.

entries.title: availability (PNT)
entries.summaryMd: The availability of a PNT system is the percentage of time that the services of the system are usable. Availability is an indication of the ability of the system to provide usable service within the specified coverage area. Signal availability is the percentage of time that PNT signals transmitted from external sources are available for use. Availability is a function of both the physical characteristics of the environment and the technical capabilities of the PNT service provider.

senses.definitionMd: The availability of a PNT system is the percentage of time that the services of the system are usable. Availability is an indication of the ability of the system to provide usable service within the specified coverage area. Signal availability is the percentage of time that PNT signals transmitted from external sources are available for use. Availability is a function of both the physical characteristics of the environment and the technical capabilities of the PNT service provider.

entries.title: average query
entries.summaryMd: A query that determines the mean of some set of values.

senses.definitionMd: A query that determines the mean of some set of values.

entries.title: Awareness
entries.summaryMd: Awareness is not training. The purpose of awareness presentations is simply to focus attention on security. Awareness presentations are intended to allow individuals to recognize IT security concerns and respond accordingly. In awareness activities, the learner is the recipient of information, whereas the learner in a training environment has a more active role. Awareness relies on reaching broad audiences with attractive packaging techniques. Training is more formal, having a goal of building knowledge and skills to facilitate the job performance.

senses.definitionMd: Awareness is not training. The purpose of awareness presentations is simply to focus attention on security. Awareness presentations are intended to allow individuals to recognize IT security concerns and respond accordingly. In awareness activities, the learner is the recipient of information, whereas the learner in a training environment has a more active role. Awareness relies on reaching broad audiences with attractive packaging techniques. Training is more formal, having a goal of building knowledge and skills to facilitate the job performance.

entries.title: awareness content
entries.summaryMd: Content that is designed and implemented to help employees understand how their actions may impact or influence vulnerabilities and threats. Organizations provide various types of awareness materials (e.g., posters, newsletters, websites) so that employees can realize their roles in protecting cyber assets.

senses.definitionMd: Content that is designed and implemented to help employees understand how their actions may impact or influence vulnerabilities and threats. Organizations provide various types of awareness materials (e.g., posters, newsletters, websites) so that employees can realize their roles in protecting cyber assets.

entries.title: awareness training
entries.summaryMd: The foundational cybersecurity or privacy training program for all personnel. It is designed to help learners understand the roles that they play in protecting information, cybersecurity, and privacy-related assets. It often consists of instructor-led and online courses, exercises, or other methods that inform learners of the acceptable uses of and risks to the organization’s systems.

senses.definitionMd: The foundational cybersecurity or privacy training program for all personnel. It is designed to help learners understand the roles that they play in protecting information, cybersecurity, and privacy-related assets. It often consists of instructor-led and online courses, exercises, or other methods that inform learners of the acceptable uses of and risks to the organization’s systems.

entries.title: b
entries.summaryMd: The block size, in bits.

senses.definitionMd: The block size, in bits.

entries.title: backdoor
entries.summaryMd: An undocumented way of gaining access to computer system. A backdoor is a potential security risk.

senses.definitionMd: An undocumented way of gaining access to computer system. A backdoor is a potential security risk.

entries.title: backdoor pattern
entries.summaryMd: A transformation or insertion applied to a data sample that triggers an adversary-specified behaviour in a model that has been subject to a backdoor poi­soning attack. For example, in computer vision, an adversary could poison a model such that the insertion of a square of white pixels induces a desired target label.

senses.definitionMd: A transformation or insertion applied to a data sample that triggers an adversary-specified behaviour in a model that has been subject to a backdoor poi­soning attack. For example, in computer vision, an adversary could poison a model such that the insertion of a square of white pixels induces a desired target label.

entries.title: backdoor poisoning attack
entries.summaryMd: A poisoning attack that causes a model to perform an adversary-selected behaviour in response to inputs that follow a particular backdoor pattern.

senses.definitionMd: A poisoning attack that causes a model to perform an adversary-selected behaviour in response to inputs that follow a particular backdoor pattern.

entries.title: Backscatter Channel
entries.summaryMd: The type of back channel used by passive tags. Since passive tags do not have a local power source, they communicate by reflecting or backscattering electromagnetic signals received from a reader.

senses.definitionMd: The type of back channel used by passive tags. Since passive tags do not have a local power source, they communicate by reflecting or backscattering electromagnetic signals received from a reader.

entries.title: Backtracking Resistance
entries.summaryMd: An RBG provides backtracking resistance relative to time T if it provides assurance that an adversary that has knowledge of the state of the RBG at some time(s) subsequent to time T (but incapable of performing work that matches the claimed security strength of the RBG) would be unable to distinguish between observations of ideal random bitstrings and (previously unseen) bitstrings that are output by the RBG at or prior to time T. In particular, an RBG whose design allows the adversary to "backtrack" from the initially-compromised RBG state(s) to obtain knowledge of prior RBG states and the corresponding outputs (including the RBG state and output at time T) would not provide backtracking resistance relative to time T. (Contrast with prediction resistance.)

senses.definitionMd: An RBG provides backtracking resistance relative to time T if it provides assurance that an adversary that has knowledge of the state of the RBG at some time(s) subsequent to time T (but incapable of performing work that matches the claimed security strength of the RBG) would be unable to distinguish between observations of ideal random bitstrings and (previously unseen) bitstrings that are output by the RBG at or prior to time T. In particular, an RBG whose design allows the adversary to "backtrack" from the initially-compromised RBG state(s) to obtain knowledge of prior RBG states and the corresponding outputs (including the RBG state and output at time T) would not provide backtracking resistance relative to time T. (Contrast with prediction resistance.)

entries.title: backup
entries.summaryMd: A copy of files and programs made to facilitate recovery if necessary.

senses.definitionMd: A copy of files and programs made to facilitate recovery if necessary.

entries.title: Backup facility
entries.summaryMd: A redundant system or service that is kept available for use in case of a failure of a primary facility.

senses.definitionMd: A redundant system or service that is kept available for use in case of a failure of a primary facility.

entries.title: Backup (key and/or metadata)
entries.summaryMd: To copy a key and/or metadata to a medium that is separate from that used for operational storage and from which the key and/or metadata can be recovered if the original values in operational storage are lost or modified.

senses.definitionMd: To copy a key and/or metadata to a medium that is separate from that used for operational storage and from which the key and/or metadata can be recovered if the original values in operational storage are lost or modified.

entries.title: Backup (system)
entries.summaryMd: The process of copying information or processing status to a redundant system, service, device or medium that can provide the needed processing capability when needed.

senses.definitionMd: The process of copying information or processing status to a redundant system, service, device or medium that can provide the needed processing capability when needed.

entries.title: banner
entries.summaryMd: Display on an information system that sets parameters for system or data use.

senses.definitionMd: Display on an information system that sets parameters for system or data use.

entries.title: Banner Grabbing
entries.summaryMd: The process of capturing banner information—such as application type and version— that is transmitted by a remote port when a connection is initiated.

senses.definitionMd: The process of capturing banner information—such as application type and version— that is transmitted by a remote port when a connection is initiated.

entries.title: base assessment
entries.summaryMd: The ISCMAx assessment file from which a merge is initiated.

senses.definitionMd: The ISCMAx assessment file from which a merge is initiated.

entries.title: Base layer
entries.summaryMd: The underlying layer of an image upon which all other components are added.

senses.definitionMd: The underlying layer of an image upon which all other components are added.

entries.title: base point
entries.summaryMd: A fixed elliptic curve point that generates the group used for elliptic curve cryptography.

senses.definitionMd: A fixed elliptic curve point that generates the group used for elliptic curve cryptography.

entries.title: Base Standards
entries.summaryMd: define fundamentals and generalized procedures. They provide an infrastructure that can be used by a variety of applications, each of which can make its own selection from the options offered by them.

senses.definitionMd: define fundamentals and generalized procedures. They provide an infrastructure that can be used by a variety of applications, each of which can make its own selection from the options offered by them.

entries.title: baseline
entries.summaryMd: Hardware, software, and relevant documentation for an information system at a given point in time.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware, software, and relevant documentation for an information system at a given point in time.

entries.title: baseline configuration
entries.summaryMd: A documented set of specifications for an information system, or a configuration item within a system, that has been formally reviewed and agreed on at a given point in time, and which can be changed only through change control procedures.

senses.definitionMd: A documented set of specifications for an information system, or a configuration item within a system, that has been formally reviewed and agreed on at a given point in time, and which can be changed only through change control procedures.

entries.title: basic assessment
entries.summaryMd: An assessment that includes only critical elements.

senses.definitionMd: An assessment that includes only critical elements.

entries.title: Basic Input/Output System (BIOS)
entries.summaryMd: In this publication, refers collectively to boot firmware based on the conventional BIOS, Extensible Firmware Interface (EFI), and the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI).

senses.definitionMd: In this publication, refers collectively to boot firmware based on the conventional BIOS, Extensible Firmware Interface (EFI), and the Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI).

entries.title: basic testing
entries.summaryMd: A test methodology that assumes no knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as black box testing.

senses.definitionMd: A test methodology that assumes no knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as black box testing.

entries.title: Basis vector
entries.summaryMd: A vector consisting of a ―1‖ in the ithposition and ―0‖ in all of the other positions.

senses.definitionMd: A vector consisting of a ―1‖ in the ithposition and ―0‖ in all of the other positions.

entries.title: bastion host
entries.summaryMd: A special purpose computer on a network where the computer is specifically designed and configured to withstand attacks.

senses.definitionMd: A special purpose computer on a network where the computer is specifically designed and configured to withstand attacks.

entries.title: Bayesian methodology
entries.summaryMd: Statistical approach to data analysis based on Bayes’ theorem where uncertainty is quantified by combining existing information with new information to create forecast models.

senses.definitionMd: Statistical approach to data analysis based on Bayes’ theorem where uncertainty is quantified by combining existing information with new information to create forecast models.

entries.title: beacon
entries.summaryMd: Initial signal by satellite conducted when first put into mission operation in order to establish communications with command and control and report initial operating status.

senses.definitionMd: Initial signal by satellite conducted when first put into mission operation in order to establish communications with command and control and report initial operating status.

entries.title: behavior
entries.summaryMd: The way that an entity functions as an action, reaction, or interaction.

senses.definitionMd: The way that an entity functions as an action, reaction, or interaction.

entries.title: behavior analysis
entries.summaryMd: The act of examining malware interactions within its operating environment including file systems, the registry (if on Windows), the network, as well as other processes and Operating System components.

senses.definitionMd: The act of examining malware interactions within its operating environment including file systems, the registry (if on Windows), the network, as well as other processes and Operating System components.

entries.title: Behavior Management
entries.summaryMd: See Capability, Behavior Management.

senses.definitionMd: See Capability, Behavior Management.

entries.title: Behavioral Anomaly Detection
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism providing a multifaceted approach to detecting cybersecurity attacks.

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism providing a multifaceted approach to detecting cybersecurity attacks.

entries.title: Benchmark
entries.summaryMd: The root node of an XCCDF benchmark document; may also be the root node of an XCCDF results document (the results of evaluating the XCCDF benchmark document).

senses.definitionMd: The root node of an XCCDF benchmark document; may also be the root node of an XCCDF results document (the results of evaluating the XCCDF benchmark document).

entries.title: Benchmark Consumer
entries.summaryMd: A product that accepts an existing XCCDF benchmark document, processes it, and produces an XCCDF results document.

senses.definitionMd: A product that accepts an existing XCCDF benchmark document, processes it, and produces an XCCDF results document.

entries.title: Benchmark Producer
entries.summaryMd: A product that generates XCCDF benchmark documents.

senses.definitionMd: A product that generates XCCDF benchmark documents.

entries.title: bend
entries.summaryMd: The use of a mechanical process to alter the physical shape of the storage media and make reading the media difficult or infeasible using state-of-the-art laboratory techniques.

senses.definitionMd: The use of a mechanical process to alter the physical shape of the storage media and make reading the media difficult or infeasible using state-of-the-art laboratory techniques.

entries.title: benign environment
entries.summaryMd: A non-hostile location protected from external hostile elements by physical, personnel, and procedural security countermeasures.

senses.definitionMd: A non-hostile location protected from external hostile elements by physical, personnel, and procedural security countermeasures.

entries.title: BER-TLV data object
entries.summaryMd: A data object coded according to ISO/IEC 8824-2:2021.

senses.definitionMd: A data object coded according to ISO/IEC 8824-2:2021.

entries.title: Bernoulli Random Variable
entries.summaryMd: A random variable that takes on the value of one with probability p and the value of zero with probability 1-p.

senses.definitionMd: A random variable that takes on the value of one with probability p and the value of zero with probability 1-p.

entries.title: Best Practice
entries.summaryMd: A procedure that has been shown by research and experience to produce optimal results and that is established or proposed as a standard suitable for widespread adoption.

senses.definitionMd: A procedure that has been shown by research and experience to produce optimal results and that is established or proposed as a standard suitable for widespread adoption.

entries.title: BGP Origin Validation
entries.summaryMd: BGP Origin Validation specifies a mechanism described in RFC 6811 where a BGP router can verify if a particular prefix was allowed to be announced by the route's originator.

senses.definitionMd: BGP Origin Validation specifies a mechanism described in RFC 6811 where a BGP router can verify if a particular prefix was allowed to be announced by the route's originator.

entries.title: BGP Path Validation
entries.summaryMd: BGP Path Validation specifies a mechanism described in RFC 8205 that allows verifying a path an UPDATE traversed by verifying the validity of the signatures over the relevant data.

senses.definitionMd: BGP Path Validation specifies a mechanism described in RFC 8205 that allows verifying a path an UPDATE traversed by verifying the validity of the signatures over the relevant data.

entries.title: BGP Peer
entries.summaryMd: A router running the BGP protocol that has an established BGP session active.

senses.definitionMd: A router running the BGP protocol that has an established BGP session active.

entries.title: BGP Secure Routing Extension
entries.summaryMd: BGP Secure Routing Extension consisting of multiple software modules that implement Route Origin Validation as well as BGPsec Path Validation.

senses.definitionMd: BGP Secure Routing Extension consisting of multiple software modules that implement Route Origin Validation as well as BGPsec Path Validation.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "BGP Secure Routing Extension"

entries.title: BGP security extension
entries.summaryMd: Security extension to the BGP protocol. It allows to digitally sign path information that can be independently verified and therefore eliminate the possibility to alter path information without notice.

senses.definitionMd: Security extension to the BGP protocol. It allows to digitally sign path information that can be independently verified and therefore eliminate the possibility to alter path information without notice.

entries.title: BGP Session
entries.summaryMd: A TCP session in which both ends are operating BGP and have successfully processed an OPEN message from the other end.

senses.definitionMd: A TCP session in which both ends are operating BGP and have successfully processed an OPEN message from the other end.

entries.title: BGP Speaker
entries.summaryMd: Any router running the BGP protocol.

senses.definitionMd: Any router running the BGP protocol.

entries.title: BGPsec
aliases: Border Gateway Protocol with Security Extensions
entries.summaryMd: Security extension to the BGP protocol. It allows to digitally sign path information that can be independently verified and therefore eliminate the possibility to alter path information without notice.

senses.definitionMd: Security extension to the BGP protocol. It allows to digitally sign path information that can be independently verified and therefore eliminate the possibility to alter path information without notice.

entries.title: BGPsec Input-Output
entries.summaryMd: BGPsec Input-Output (BIO) enables the generation and storage of precomputed reproducible BGPsec traffic for testing purposes.

senses.definitionMd: BGPsec Input-Output (BIO) enables the generation and storage of precomputed reproducible BGPsec traffic for testing purposes.

entries.title: Bi
entries.summaryMd: The ith block of the formatted input.

senses.definitionMd: The ith block of the formatted input.

entries.title: bi-directional (CDS)
entries.summaryMd: A cross domain device or system with the capability to provide both the transmission and reception of information or data between two or more different security domains (e.g., between TS/SCI and Secret or Secret and Unclassified).

senses.definitionMd: A cross domain device or system with the capability to provide both the transmission and reception of information or data between two or more different security domains (e.g., between TS/SCI and Secret or Secret and Unclassified).

entries.title: Bias
entries.summaryMd: With respect to the uniform distribution on \([0,n-1]\)

senses.definitionMd: With respect to the uniform distribution on \([0,n-1]\)

entries.title: Biased
entries.summaryMd: A value that is chosen from a sample space is said to be biased if one value is more likely to be chosen than another value. Contrast with unbiased.

senses.definitionMd: A value that is chosen from a sample space is said to be biased if one value is more likely to be chosen than another value. Contrast with unbiased.

entries.title: bidirectional authentication
entries.summaryMd: The process of both entities involved in a transaction verifying each other.

senses.definitionMd: The process of both entities involved in a transaction verifying each other.

entries.title: Big-endian
entries.summaryMd: The property of a byte string having its bytes positioned in order of decreasing significance. In particular, the leftmost (first) byte is the most significant, and the rightmost (last) byte is the least significant. The term “big-endian” may also be applied in the same manner to bit strings.

senses.definitionMd: The property of a byte string having its bytes positioned in order of decreasing significance. In particular, the leftmost (first) byte is the most significant, and the rightmost (last) byte is the least significant. The term “big-endian” may also be applied in the same manner to bit strings.

entries.title: Binary data (from a noise source)
entries.summaryMd: Digitized output from a noise source that consists of a single bit; that is, each sampled output value is represented as either 0 or 1.

senses.definitionMd: Digitized output from a noise source that consists of a single bit; that is, each sampled output value is represented as either 0 or 1.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Binary data (from a noise source)"

entries.title: binary label
entries.summaryMd: A single label indicating a product has met a baseline standard.

senses.definitionMd: A single label indicating a product has met a baseline standard.

entries.title: Binary Sequence
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of zeroes and ones.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of zeroes and ones.

entries.title: Bind
entries.summaryMd: To deterministically transform a logical construct into a machine-readable representation suitable for machine interchange and processing. The result of this transformation is called a binding. A binding may also be referred to as the “bound form” of its associated logical construct.

senses.definitionMd: To deterministically transform a logical construct into a machine-readable representation suitable for machine interchange and processing. The result of this transformation is called a binding. A binding may also be referred to as the “bound form” of its associated logical construct.

entries.title: binding
entries.summaryMd: Process of associating two related elements of information.

senses.definitionMd: Process of associating two related elements of information.

entries.title: Binomial Distribution
entries.summaryMd: A random variable is binomially distributed if there is an integer n and a probability p such that the random variable is the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli experiments, where the probability of success in a single experiment is p. In a Bernoulli experiment, there are only two possible outcomes.

senses.definitionMd: A random variable is binomially distributed if there is an integer n and a probability p such that the random variable is the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli experiments, where the probability of success in a single experiment is p. In a Bernoulli experiment, there are only two possible outcomes.

entries.title: biometric
entries.summaryMd: 1. Measurable physical characteristics or personal behavioral traits used to identify, or verify the claimed identity of, an individual. Facial images, fingerprints, and handwriting samples are all examples of biometrics.

senses.definitionMd: 1. Measurable physical characteristics or personal behavioral traits used to identify, or verify the claimed identity of, an individual. Facial images, fingerprints, and handwriting samples are all examples of biometrics.

entries.title: Biometric Authentication (BIO, BIO-A)
entries.summaryMd: A form of authentication in which authenticity is established by biometric verification of a new biometric sample from a cardholder to a biometric data record read from the cardholder’s activated PIV Card. In BIO, the biometric sample may be captured from the cardholder in isolation, while in BIO-A, an attendant must oversee the process of biometric capture.

senses.definitionMd: A form of authentication in which authenticity is established by biometric verification of a new biometric sample from a cardholder to a biometric data record read from the cardholder’s activated PIV Card. In BIO, the biometric sample may be captured from the cardholder in isolation, while in BIO-A, an attendant must oversee the process of biometric capture.

entries.title: Biometric Capture Device
entries.summaryMd: Device that collects a signal from a biometric characteristic and converts it to a captured biometric sample.

senses.definitionMd: Device that collects a signal from a biometric characteristic and converts it to a captured biometric sample.

entries.title: Biometric Characteristic
entries.summaryMd: Biological attribute of an individual from which distinctive and repeatable values can be extracted for the purpose of automated recognition. Fingerprint ridge structure and face topography are examples of biometric characteristics.

senses.definitionMd: Biological attribute of an individual from which distinctive and repeatable values can be extracted for the purpose of automated recognition. Fingerprint ridge structure and face topography are examples of biometric characteristics.

entries.title: Biometric Data
entries.summaryMd: Biological attribute of an individual from which distinctive and repeatable values can be extracted for the purpose of automated recognition. Fingerprint ridge structure and face topography are examples of biometric characteristics.

senses.definitionMd: Biological attribute of an individual from which distinctive and repeatable values can be extracted for the purpose of automated recognition. Fingerprint ridge structure and face topography are examples of biometric characteristics.

entries.title: Biometric Data Record
entries.summaryMd: Biometric sample or aggregation of biometric samples at any stage of processing.
