senses.definitionMd: Biometric sample or aggregation of biometric samples at any stage of processing.

entries.title: Biometric Information Template
entries.summaryMd: Biometric Information Template – a [CARD-BIO] data structure indicating Card capability

senses.definitionMd: Biometric Information Template – a [CARD-BIO] data structure indicating Card capability

entries.title: Biometric On-Card Comparison Authentication (OCC-AUTH)
entries.summaryMd: An authentication mechanism where biometric on-card comparison (OCC) is used instead of a PIN to activate a PIV Card for authentication.

senses.definitionMd: An authentication mechanism where biometric on-card comparison (OCC) is used instead of a PIN to activate a PIV Card for authentication.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Biometric On-Card Comparison Authentication (OCC-AUTH)"

entries.title: Biometric On-Card Comparison (OCC)
entries.summaryMd: A one-to-one comparison of fingerprint biometric data records transmitted to the PIV Card with a biometric reference previously stored on the PIV Card. In this Standard, OCC is used as a means of performing card activation and as part of Biometric On- Card Comparison Authentication (OCC-AUTH).

senses.definitionMd: A one-to-one comparison of fingerprint biometric data records transmitted to the PIV Card with a biometric reference previously stored on the PIV Card. In this Standard, OCC is used as a means of performing card activation and as part of Biometric On- Card Comparison Authentication (OCC-AUTH).

entries.title: biometric reference
entries.summaryMd: One or more stored biometric samples, templates, or models attributed to an individual and used as the object of biometric comparison in a database, such as a facial image stored digitally on a passport, fingerprint minutiae template on a National ID card, or Gaussian Mixture Model for speaker recognition.

senses.definitionMd: One or more stored biometric samples, templates, or models attributed to an individual and used as the object of biometric comparison in a database, such as a facial image stored digitally on a passport, fingerprint minutiae template on a National ID card, or Gaussian Mixture Model for speaker recognition.

entries.title: biometric sample
entries.summaryMd: An analog or digital representation of biometric characteristics prior to biometric feature extraction, such as a record that contains a fingerprint image.

senses.definitionMd: An analog or digital representation of biometric characteristics prior to biometric feature extraction, such as a record that contains a fingerprint image.

entries.title: Biometric Verification
entries.summaryMd: Automated process of confirming a biometric claim through biometric comparison.

senses.definitionMd: Automated process of confirming a biometric claim through biometric comparison.

entries.title: Biometric Verification Decision
entries.summaryMd: A determination of whether biometric probe(s) and biometric reference(s) have the same biometric source based on comparison score(s) during a biometric verification transaction.

senses.definitionMd: A determination of whether biometric probe(s) and biometric reference(s) have the same biometric source based on comparison score(s) during a biometric verification transaction.

entries.title: Biometrics
entries.summaryMd: A measurable physical characteristic or personal behavioral trait used to recognize the identity, or verify the claimed identity, of an applicant. Facial images, fingerprints, and iris scan samples are all examples of biometrics.

senses.definitionMd: A measurable physical characteristic or personal behavioral trait used to recognize the identity, or verify the claimed identity, of an applicant. Facial images, fingerprints, and iris scan samples are all examples of biometrics.

entries.title: bit
entries.summaryMd: A binary digit: 0 or 1.

senses.definitionMd: A binary digit: 0 or 1.

entries.title: Bit Error
entries.summaryMd: The substitution of a ‘0’ bit for a ‘1’ bit, or vice versa.

senses.definitionMd: The substitution of a ‘0’ bit for a ‘1’ bit, or vice versa.

entries.title: bit error rate
entries.summaryMd: Ratio between the number of bits incorrectly received and the total number of bits transmitted through a communications channel. Also applies to storage.

senses.definitionMd: Ratio between the number of bits incorrectly received and the total number of bits transmitted through a communications channel. Also applies to storage.

entries.title: Bit Length
entries.summaryMd: The number of bits in a bit string.

senses.definitionMd: The number of bits in a bit string.

entries.title: Bit Stream Imaging
entries.summaryMd: A bit-for-bit copy of the original media, including free space and slack space. Also known as disk imaging.

senses.definitionMd: A bit-for-bit copy of the original media, including free space and slack space. Also known as disk imaging.

entries.title: bit string
entries.summaryMd: An ordered sequence of zeros and ones. The leftmost bit is the most significant bit of the string. The rightmost bit is the least significant bit of the string.

senses.definitionMd: An ordered sequence of zeros and ones. The leftmost bit is the most significant bit of the string. The rightmost bit is the least significant bit of the string.

entries.title: Bitstring
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of bits.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of bits.

entries.title: Bitwise Exclusive-Or
entries.summaryMd: An operation on two bitstrings of equal length that combines corresponding bits of each bitstring using an exclusive-or operation.

senses.definitionMd: An operation on two bitstrings of equal length that combines corresponding bits of each bitstring using an exclusive-or operation.

entries.title: black box testing
entries.summaryMd: A test methodology that assumes no knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as black box testing.

senses.definitionMd: A test methodology that assumes no knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as black box testing.

entries.title: black core
entries.summaryMd: A communication network architecture in which user data traversing a global internet protocol (IP) network is end-to-end encrypted at the IP layer. Related to striped core.

senses.definitionMd: A communication network architecture in which user data traversing a global internet protocol (IP) network is end-to-end encrypted at the IP layer. Related to striped core.

entries.title: BLACK data
entries.summaryMd: Data that is protected by encryption so that it can be transported or stored without fear of compromise. Also known as encrypted data.

senses.definitionMd: Data that is protected by encryption so that it can be transported or stored without fear of compromise. Also known as encrypted data.

entries.title: blacklist
entries.summaryMd: A list of discrete entities, such as hosts, email addresses, network port numbers, runtime processes, or applications, that have been previously determined to be associated with malicious activity.

senses.definitionMd: A list of discrete entities, such as hosts, email addresses, network port numbers, runtime processes, or applications, that have been previously determined to be associated with malicious activity.

entries.title: blacklisting
entries.summaryMd: The process used to identify: (i) software programs that are not authorized to execute on an information system; or (ii) prohibited universal resource locators (URL)/websites.

senses.definitionMd: The process used to identify: (i) software programs that are not authorized to execute on an information system; or (ii) prohibited universal resource locators (URL)/websites.

entries.title: bLen
entries.summaryMd: The length of the bit string B in bits

senses.definitionMd: The length of the bit string B in bits

entries.title: blended attack
entries.summaryMd: A type of attack that combines multiple attack methods against one or more vulnerabilities.

senses.definitionMd: A type of attack that combines multiple attack methods against one or more vulnerabilities.

entries.title: block
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of bits of a given fixed length. In this Standard, blocks consist of 128 bits, sometimes represented as arrays of bytes or words.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of bits of a given fixed length. In this Standard, blocks consist of 128 bits, sometimes represented as arrays of bytes or words.

entries.title: block cipher
entries.summaryMd: A family of permutations of blocks that is parameterized by the key.

senses.definitionMd: A family of permutations of blocks that is parameterized by the key.

entries.title: Block Cipher Algorithm
entries.summaryMd: A family of functions and their inverse functions that is parameterized by cryptographic keys; the functions map bit strings of a fixed length to bit strings of the same length.

senses.definitionMd: A family of functions and their inverse functions that is parameterized by cryptographic keys; the functions map bit strings of a fixed length to bit strings of the same length.

entries.title: block cipher mode of operation
entries.summaryMd: An algorithm for the cryptographic transformation of data that is based on a block cipher.

senses.definitionMd: An algorithm for the cryptographic transformation of data that is based on a block cipher.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "block cipher mode of operation"

entries.title: Block data
entries.summaryMd: The portion of a block that contains a set of validated transactions and ledger events.

senses.definitionMd: The portion of a block that contains a set of validated transactions and ledger events.

entries.title: Block Frequency Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of the block frequency test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in each of M non-overlapping blocks created from a sequence appear to have a random distribution.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of the block frequency test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in each of M non-overlapping blocks created from a sequence appear to have a random distribution.

entries.title: Block header
entries.summaryMd: The portion of a block that contains information about the block itself (block metadata), typically including a timestamp, a hash representation of the block data, the hash of the previous block’s header, and a cryptographic nonce (if needed).

senses.definitionMd: The portion of a block that contains information about the block itself (block metadata), typically including a timestamp, a hash representation of the block data, the hash of the previous block’s header, and a cryptographic nonce (if needed).

entries.title: Block reward
entries.summaryMd: A reward (typically cryptocurrency) awarded to publishing nodes for successfully adding a block to the blockchain.

senses.definitionMd: A reward (typically cryptocurrency) awarded to publishing nodes for successfully adding a block to the blockchain.

entries.title: block size
entries.summaryMd: The number of bits in an input (or output) block of the block cipher.

senses.definitionMd: The number of bits in an input (or output) block of the block cipher.

entries.title: blockchain
entries.summaryMd: A distributed digital ledger of cryptographically-signed transactions that are grouped into blocks. Each block is cryptographically linked to the previous one (making it tamper evident) after validation and undergoing a consensus decision. As new blocks are added, older blocks become more difficult to modify (creating tamper resistance). New blocks are replicated across copies of the ledger within the network, and any conflicts are resolved automatically using established rules.

senses.definitionMd: A distributed digital ledger of cryptographically-signed transactions that are grouped into blocks. Each block is cryptographically linked to the previous one (making it tamper evident) after validation and undergoing a consensus decision. As new blocks are added, older blocks become more difficult to modify (creating tamper resistance). New blocks are replicated across copies of the ledger within the network, and any conflicts are resolved automatically using established rules.

entries.title: Blockchain Explorer
entries.summaryMd: A software for visualizing blocks, transactions, and blockchain network metrics (e.g., average transaction fees, hashrates, block size, block difficulty).

senses.definitionMd: A software for visualizing blocks, transactions, and blockchain network metrics (e.g., average transaction fees, hashrates, block size, block difficulty).

entries.title: Blockchain implementation
entries.summaryMd: a specific blockchain.

senses.definitionMd: a specific blockchain.

entries.title: Blockchain network
entries.summaryMd: the network in which a blockchain is being used.

senses.definitionMd: the network in which a blockchain is being used.

entries.title: Blockchain network user
entries.summaryMd: Any single person, group, business, or organization which is using or operating a blockchain node.

senses.definitionMd: Any single person, group, business, or organization which is using or operating a blockchain node.

entries.title: Blockchain Subnetwork
entries.summaryMd: A blockchain network that is tightly coupled with one or more other blockchain networks, as found in sharding.

senses.definitionMd: A blockchain network that is tightly coupled with one or more other blockchain networks, as found in sharding.

entries.title: Blockchain technology
entries.summaryMd: a term to describe the technology in the most generic form.

senses.definitionMd: a term to describe the technology in the most generic form.

entries.title: blocklist
entries.summaryMd: A documented list of specific elements that are blocked, per policy decision. This concept has historically been known as a “blacklist.”

senses.definitionMd: A documented list of specific elements that are blocked, per policy decision. This concept has historically been known as a “blacklist.”

entries.title: blue team
entries.summaryMd: The group responsible for defending an enterprise's use of information systems by maintaining its security posture against a group of mock attackers (i.e., the Red Team). Typically the Blue Team and its supporters must defend against real or simulated attacks 1) over a significant period of time, 2) in a representative operational context (e.g., as part of an operational exercise), and 3) according to rules established and monitored with the help of a neutral group refereeing the simulation or exercise (i.e., the White Team).

senses.definitionMd: The group responsible for defending an enterprise's use of information systems by maintaining its security posture against a group of mock attackers (i.e., the Red Team). Typically the Blue Team and its supporters must defend against real or simulated attacks 1) over a significant period of time, 2) in a representative operational context (e.g., as part of an operational exercise), and 3) according to rules established and monitored with the help of a neutral group refereeing the simulation or exercise (i.e., the White Team).

entries.title: Bluetooth
entries.summaryMd: A wireless protocol that allows two similarly equipped devices to communicate with each other within a short distance (e.g., 30 ft.).

senses.definitionMd: A wireless protocol that allows two similarly equipped devices to communicate with each other within a short distance (e.g., 30 ft.).

entries.title: Body
entries.summaryMd: The section of an email message that contains the actual content of the message.

senses.definitionMd: The section of an email message that contains the actual content of the message.

entries.title: body of evidence
entries.summaryMd: The totality of evidence used to substantiate trust, trustworthiness, and risk relative to the system.

senses.definitionMd: The totality of evidence used to substantiate trust, trustworthiness, and risk relative to the system.

entries.title: bootstrapping
entries.summaryMd: A subprocess of network-layer onboarding. It introduces just enough information to a device and a network onboarding component to enable them to trust one another and establish a secure channel. The trust established between the device and the network onboarding component through bootstrapping may be either mutual or one-way. The introduction within bootstrapping may be performed as an out-of-band (OOB) process requiring human interaction.

senses.definitionMd: A subprocess of network-layer onboarding. It introduces just enough information to a device and a network onboarding component to enable them to trust one another and establish a secure channel. The trust established between the device and the network onboarding component through bootstrapping may be either mutual or one-way. The introduction within bootstrapping may be performed as an out-of-band (OOB) process requiring human interaction.

entries.title: Border Gateway Protocol
entries.summaryMd: The Border Gateway Protocol is a protocol designed by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) to exchange routing information between autonomous systems.

senses.definitionMd: The Border Gateway Protocol is a protocol designed by the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) to exchange routing information between autonomous systems.

entries.title: Botnet
entries.summaryMd: The word “botnet” is formed from the words “robot” and ”network.” Cyber criminals use special Trojan viruses to breach the security of several users’ computers, take control of each computer, and organize all the infected machines into a network of “bots” that the criminal can remotely manage.

senses.definitionMd: The word “botnet” is formed from the words “robot” and ”network.” Cyber criminals use special Trojan viruses to breach the security of several users’ computers, take control of each computer, and organize all the infected machines into a network of “bots” that the criminal can remotely manage.

entries.title: bound authenticator
entries.summaryMd: An authenticator verified by the RP in addition to an assertion at FAL3. The bound authenticator is bound to the RP subscriber account.

senses.definitionMd: An authenticator verified by the RP in addition to an assertion at FAL3. The bound authenticator is bound to the RP subscriber account.

entries.title: boundary
entries.summaryMd: Physical or logical perimeter of a system.

senses.definitionMd: Physical or logical perimeter of a system.

entries.title: boundary protection
entries.summaryMd: Monitoring and control of communications at the external boundary of an information system to prevent and detect malicious and other unauthorized communications, through the use of boundary protection devices (e.g. gateways, routers, firewalls, guards, encrypted tunnels).

senses.definitionMd: Monitoring and control of communications at the external boundary of an information system to prevent and detect malicious and other unauthorized communications, through the use of boundary protection devices (e.g. gateways, routers, firewalls, guards, encrypted tunnels).

entries.title: boundary protection device
entries.summaryMd: A device with appropriate mechanisms that: (i) facilitates the adjudication of different interconnected system security policies (e.g., controlling the flow of information into or out of an interconnected system); and/or (ii) provides information system boundary protection.

senses.definitionMd: A device with appropriate mechanisms that: (i) facilitates the adjudication of different interconnected system security policies (e.g., controlling the flow of information into or out of an interconnected system); and/or (ii) provides information system boundary protection.

entries.title: bounded differential privacy
entries.summaryMd: A unit of privacy variant that calls two datasets D1 and D2 neighbors if it is possible to construct D2 from D1 by changing one person’s data. Under bounded differential privacy, neighboring datasets have the same size. Bounded differential privacy allows for mechanisms that release the total size of the dataset with no noise.

senses.definitionMd: The loss of control, compromise, unauthorized disclosure, unauthorized acquisition, or any similar occurrence where: a person other than an authorized user accesses or potentially accesses personally identifiable information; or an authorized user accesses personally identifiable information for another than authorized purpose.

entries.title: Brokered Trust

entries.title: calibration
entries.summaryMd: A comparison between a device under test and an established standard, such as UTC(NIST). When the calibration is finished, it should be possible to state the estimated time offset and/or frequency offset of the device under test with respect to the standard, as well as the measurement uncertainty. Calibrations can be absolute or relative. Absolute calibrations are not biased by the calibration reference and would, therefore, be more reproducible. However, absolute calibrations can be more complex to determine. The bias in relative calibrations would be consistent if all the devices in the system are calibrated against the same calibration reference. Calibrations may also be performed relative to other devices without reference to an absolute standard. Relative calibrations are generally simpler to perform than absolute calibrations.

senses.definitionMd: A comparison between a device under test and an established standard, such as UTC(NIST). entries.title: CCE ID

entries.title: Cellular Network Isolation Card (CNIC)

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Cellular Network Isolation Card (CNIC)"

entries.title: Central Limit Theorem
entries.summaryMd: For a random sample of size n from a population with meanm and variance s2, the distribution of the sample means is approximately normal with mean m and variance s2/n as the sample size increases.

senses.definitionMd: For a random sample of size n from a population with meanm and variance s2, the distribution of the sample means is approximately normal with mean m and variance s2/n as the sample size increases.

entries.title: central management
entries.summaryMd: The organization-wide management and implementation of selected security and privacy controls and related processes. Central management includes planning, implementing, assessing, authorizing, and monitoring the organization-defined, centrally managed security and privacy controls and processes.

senses.definitionMd: The organization-wide management and implementation of selected security and privacy controls and related processes. Central management includes planning, implementing, assessing, authorizing, and monitoring the organization-defined, centrally managed security and privacy controls and processes.

entries.title: central office of record
entries.summaryMd: The entity that keeps records of accountable COMSEC material held by COMSEC accounts subject to its oversight.

senses.definitionMd: The entity that keeps records of accountable COMSEC material held by COMSEC accounts subject to its oversight.

entries.title: Central Oversight Authority
entries.summaryMd: The cryptographic key management system (CKMS) entity that provides overall CKMS data synchronization and system security oversight for an organization or set of organizations.

senses.definitionMd: The cryptographic key management system (CKMS) entity that provides overall CKMS data synchronization and system security oversight for an organization or set of organizations.

entries.title: central services node
entries.summaryMd: The Key Management Infrastructure core node that provides central security management and data management services.

senses.definitionMd: The Key Management Infrastructure core node that provides central security management and data management services.

entries.title: Central Verification System
entries.summaryMd: A system operated by the Office of Personnel Management that contains information on security clearances, investigations, suitability, fitness determinations, [HSPD-12] decisions, PIV credentials, and polygraph data.

senses.definitionMd: A system operated by the Office of Personnel Management that contains information on security clearances, investigations, suitability, fitness determinations, [HSPD-12] decisions, PIV credentials, and polygraph data.

entries.title: Centralized network
entries.summaryMd: A network configuration where participants must communicate with a central authority to communicate with one another. Since all participants must go through a single centralized source, the loss of that source would prevent all participants from communicating.

senses.definitionMd: A network configuration where participants must communicate with a central authority to communicate with one another. Since all participants must go through a single centralized source, the loss of that source would prevent all participants from communicating.

entries.title: centric architecture
entries.summaryMd: A complex system of systems composed of subsystems and services that are part of a continuously evolving, complex community of people, devices, information and services interconnected by a network that enhances information sharing and collaboration. Subsystems and services may or may not be developed or owned by the same entity, and, in general, will not be continually present during the full life cycle of the system of systems. Examples of this architecture include service-oriented architectures and cloud computing architectures.

senses.definitionMd: A complex system of systems composed of subsystems and services that are part of a continuously evolving, complex community of people, devices, information and services interconnected by a network that enhances information sharing and collaboration. Subsystems and services may or may not be developed or owned by the same entity, and, in general, will not be continually present during the full life cycle of the system of systems. Examples of this architecture include service-oriented architectures and cloud computing architectures.

entries.title: certificate
entries.summaryMd: A set of data that uniquely identifies a public key (which has a corresponding private key) and an owner that is authorized to use the key pair. The certificate contains the owner’s public key and possibly other information and is digitally signed by a Certification Authority (i.e., a trusted party), thereby binding the public key to the owner.

senses.definitionMd: A set of data that uniquely identifies a public key (which has a corresponding private key) and an owner that is authorized to use the key pair. The certificate contains the owner’s public key and possibly other information and is digitally signed by a Certification Authority (i.e., a trusted party), thereby binding the public key to the owner.

entries.title: Certificate Authority Authorization
entries.summaryMd: A record associated with a Domain Name Server (DNS) entry that specifies the CAs that are authorized to issue certificates for that domain.

senses.definitionMd: A record associated with a Domain Name Server (DNS) entry that specifies the CAs that are authorized to issue certificates for that domain.

entries.title: Certificate Authority (CA)
entries.summaryMd: A trusted entity that issues and revokes public key certificates.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted entity that issues and revokes public key certificates.

entries.title: certificate authority workstation (CAW)
entries.summaryMd: The computer system or systems that process certification authority (CA) software and/or have access to the CA private keys, end entity keys, or end entity public keys prior to certification.

senses.definitionMd: The computer system or systems that process certification authority (CA) software and/or have access to the CA private keys, end entity keys, or end entity public keys prior to certification.

entries.title: Certificate Chain
entries.summaryMd: An ordered list of certificates that starts with an end-entity certificate, includes one or more certificate authority (CA) certificates, and ends with the end-entity certificate’s root CA certificate, where each certificate in the chain is the certificate of the CA that issued the previous certificate. By checking to see if each certificate in the chain was issued by a trusted CA, the receiver of an end-user certificate can determine whether or not it should trust the end-entity certificate by verifying the signatures in the chain of certificates.

senses.definitionMd: An ordered list of certificates that starts with an end-entity certificate, includes one or more certificate authority (CA) certificates, and ends with the end-entity certificate’s root CA certificate, where each certificate in the chain is the certificate of the CA that issued the previous certificate. By checking to see if each certificate in the chain was issued by a trusted CA, the receiver of an end-user certificate can determine whether or not it should trust the end-entity certificate by verifying the signatures in the chain of certificates.

entries.title: Certificate class
entries.summaryMd: A CA-designation (e.g., "class 0" or "class 1") indicating how thoroughly the CA checked the validity of the certificate. Per X.509 rules, the "class" should be encoded in the certificate as a CP extension: the CA can insert an object identifier (OID) that designates the set of procedures applied for the issuance of the certificate. These OIDs are CA-specific and can be understood only by referring to the CA's Certification Practice Statement.

senses.definitionMd: A CA-designation (e.g., "class 0" or "class 1") indicating how thoroughly the CA checked the validity of the certificate. Per X.509 rules, the "class" should be encoded in the certificate as a CP extension: the CA can insert an object identifier (OID) that designates the set of procedures applied for the issuance of the certificate. These OIDs are CA-specific and can be understood only by referring to the CA's Certification Practice Statement.

entries.title: Certificate-inventory management
entries.summaryMd: See Key-inventory management.

senses.definitionMd: See Key-inventory management.

entries.title: certificate management
entries.summaryMd: Process whereby certificates (as defined above) are generated, stored, protected, transferred, loaded, used, and destroyed.

senses.definitionMd: Process whereby certificates (as defined above) are generated, stored, protected, transferred, loaded, used, and destroyed.

entries.title: Certificate owner
entries.summaryMd: The human(s) responsible for the management of a given certificate.

senses.definitionMd: The human(s) responsible for the management of a given certificate.

entries.title: certificate-related information
entries.summaryMd: Information, such as subscriber’s postal address, that is not included in a certificate. May be used by a certification authority (CA) managing certificates.

senses.definitionMd: Information, such as subscriber’s postal address, that is not included in a certificate. May be used by a certification authority (CA) managing certificates.

entries.title: certificate revocation list (CRL)
entries.summaryMd: A list of revoked public key certificates created and digitally signed by a certification authority.

senses.definitionMd: A list of revoked public key certificates created and digitally signed by a certification authority.

entries.title: Certificate Signing Request
entries.summaryMd: A request sent from a certificate requester to a certificate authority to apply for a digital identity certificate. The certificate signing request contains the public key as well as other information to be included in the certificate and is signed by the private key corresponding to the public key.

senses.definitionMd: A request sent from a certificate requester to a certificate authority to apply for a digital identity certificate. The certificate signing request contains the public key as well as other information to be included in the certificate and is signed by the private key corresponding to the public key.

entries.title: certificate status server
entries.summaryMd: An authority that provides status information about certificates on behalf of the CA through online transactions (e.g., an online certificate status protocol (OCSP) responder).

senses.definitionMd: An authority that provides status information about certificates on behalf of the CA through online transactions (e.g., an online certificate status protocol (OCSP) responder).

entries.title: Certificate Transparency
entries.summaryMd: A framework for publicly logging the existence of Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificates as they are issued or observed in a manner that allows anyone to audit CA activity and notice the issuance of suspect certificates as well as to audit the certificate logs themselves. (Experimental RFC 6962)

senses.definitionMd: A framework for publicly logging the existence of Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificates as they are issued or observed in a manner that allows anyone to audit CA activity and notice the issuance of suspect certificates as well as to audit the certificate logs themselves. (Experimental RFC 6962)

entries.title: certification
entries.summaryMd: A comprehensive assessment of the management, operational, and technical security controls in an information system, made in support of security accreditation, to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security requirements for the system.

senses.definitionMd: A comprehensive assessment of the management, operational, and technical security controls in an information system, made in support of security accreditation, to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security requirements for the system.

entries.title: certification analyst
entries.summaryMd: The independent technical liaison for all stakeholders involved in the certification and accreditation (C&A) process responsible for objectively and independently evaluating a system as part of the risk management process. Based on the security requirements documented in the security plan, performs a technical and non-technical review of potential vulnerabilities in the system and determines if the security controls (management, operational, and technical) are correctly implemented and effective.

senses.definitionMd: The independent technical liaison for all stakeholders involved in the certification and accreditation (C&A) process responsible for objectively and independently evaluating a system as part of the risk management process. Based on the security requirements documented in the security plan, performs a technical and non-technical review of potential vulnerabilities in the system and determines if the security controls (management, operational, and technical) are correctly implemented and effective.

entries.title: certification authority
entries.summaryMd: A trusted entity that issues and revokes public key certificates.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted entity that issues and revokes public key certificates.

entries.title: Certification Authority Workstation
entries.summaryMd: Commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) workstation with a trusted operating system and special purpose application software that is used to issue certificates. Rationale: Term has been replaced by the term “certificate authority workstation (CAW)”.

senses.definitionMd: Commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) workstation with a trusted operating system and special purpose application software that is used to issue certificates. Rationale: Term has been replaced by the term “certificate authority workstation (CAW)”.

entries.title: certification package
entries.summaryMd: Product of the certification effort documenting the detailed results of the certification activities. Rationale: The Risk Management Framework uses a new term to refer to this concept, and it is called security assessment report (SAR).

senses.definitionMd: Product of the certification effort documenting the detailed results of the certification activities. Rationale: The Risk Management Framework uses a new term to refer to this concept, and it is called security assessment report (SAR).

entries.title: certification practice statement (CPS)
entries.summaryMd: A statement of the practices that a certification authority (CA) employs in issuing, suspending, revoking, and renewing certificates and providing access to them, in accordance with specific requirements (i.e., requirements specified in this Certificate Policy, or requirements specified in a contract for services).

senses.definitionMd: A statement of the practices that a certification authority (CA) employs in issuing, suspending, revoking, and renewing certificates and providing access to them, in accordance with specific requirements (i.e., requirements specified in this Certificate Policy, or requirements specified in a contract for services).

entries.title: certification test and evaluation
entries.summaryMd: Software, hardware, and firmware security tests conducted during development of an information system component.

entries.title: certified TEMPEST technical authority

entries.title: certifier
entries.summaryMd: Individual responsible for making a technical judgment of the system’s compliance with stated requirements, identifying and assessing the risks associated with operating the system, coordinating the certification activities, and consolidating the final certification and accreditation packages. Rationale: Term has been replaced by the term “security control assessor”.

senses.definitionMd: Individual responsible for making a technical judgment of the system’s compliance with stated requirements, identifying and assessing the risks associated with operating the system, coordinating the certification activities, and consolidating the final certification and accreditation packages. entries.title: chain

entries.title: chain of custody

senses.definitionMd: A process that tracks the movement of evidence through its collection, safeguarding, and analysis lifecycle by documenting each person who handled the evidence, the date/time it was collected or transferred, and the purpose for the transfer.

entries.title: chain of evidence
entries.summaryMd: A process and record that shows who obtained the evidence; where and when the evidence was obtained; who secured the evidence; and who had control or possession of the evidence. The “sequencing” of the chain of evidence follows this order: collection and identification; analysis; storage; preservation; presentation in court; return to owner. Rationale: Sufficiently covered under chain of custody.

senses.definitionMd: A process and record that shows who obtained the evidence; where and when the evidence was obtained; who secured the evidence; and who had control or possession of the evidence. entries.title: Challenge-Response Protocol
entries.summaryMd: An authentication protocol where the verifier sends the claimant a challenge (usually a random value or a nonce) that the claimant combines with a secret (often by hashing the challenge and a shared secret together, or by applying a private key operation to the challenge) to generate a response that is sent to the verifier. The verifier can independently verify the response generated by the Claimant (such as by re-computing the hash of the challenge and the shared secret and comparing to the response, or performing a public key operation on the response) and establish that the Claimant possesses and controls the secret.

senses.definitionMd: An authentication protocol where the verifier sends the claimant a challenge (usually a random value or a nonce) that the claimant combines with a secret (often by hashing the challenge and a shared secret together, or by applying a private key operation to the challenge) to generate a response that is sent to the verifier. The verifier can independently verify the response generated by the Claimant (such as by re-computing the hash of the challenge and the shared secret and comparing to the response, or performing a public key operation on the response) and establish that the Claimant possesses and controls the secret.

entries.title: characterization
entries.summaryMd: An extended test of the performance characteristics of a clock or oscillator. A characterization involves more work than a typical calibration. The device under test is usually measured for a long period of time (days or weeks), and sometimes, a series of measurements is made under different environmental conditions. A characterization is often used to determine the types of noise that limit the uncertainty of the measurement and the sensitivity of the device to environmental changes.

A new checklist revision would be created to accommodate this change, while still maintaining the Prose checklist revision for interested parties.

entries.summaryMd: An implementation of a CKMS design produced by a vendor that conforms to the requirements of [NIST SP 800-130], provides a set of key-management services and cryptographic functions, and operates in accordance with the CKMS designer’s CKMS Security Policy.

senses.definitionMd: An implementation of a CKMS design produced by a vendor that conforms to the requirements of [NIST SP 800-130], provides a set of key-management services and cryptographic functions, and operates in accordance with the CKMS designer’s CKMS Security Policy.

entries.title: CKMS Security Policy
entries.summaryMd: A security policy specific to a CKMS

senses.definitionMd: A security policy specific to a CKMS

entries.title: CKMS vendor
entries.summaryMd: The entity that markets the CKMS to CKMS service providers.

senses.definitionMd: The entity that markets the CKMS to CKMS service providers.

entries.title: claim
entries.summaryMd: A true-false statement about the limitations on the values of an unambiguously defined property called the claim’s property; and limitations on the uncertainty of the property’s values falling within these limitations during the claim’s duration of applicability under stated conditions.

senses.definitionMd: A true-false statement about the limitations on the values of an unambiguously defined property called the claim’s property; and limitations on the uncertainty of the property’s values falling within these limitations during the claim’s duration of applicability under stated conditions.

entries.title: claimant
entries.summaryMd: A subject whose identity is to be verified using one or more authentication protocols.

senses.definitionMd: A subject whose identity is to be verified using one or more authentication protocols.

entries.title: Claimed signatory
entries.summaryMd: From the verifier’s perspective, the claimed signatory is the entity that purportedly generated a digital signature.

senses.definitionMd: From the verifier’s perspective, the claimed signatory is the entity that purportedly generated a digital signature.

entries.title: classical data analysis
entries.summaryMd: A data analysis technique where data collection is followed by the imposition of a model, and the analysis, estimation, and testing that follow focus on the parameters of that model.

senses.definitionMd: A data analysis technique where data collection is followed by the imposition of a model, and the analysis, estimation, and testing that follow focus on the parameters of that model.

entries.title: classification
entries.summaryMd: The task of predicting which of a set of discrete categories an input belongs to.

senses.definitionMd: The task of predicting which of a set of discrete categories an input belongs to.

entries.title: classified information
entries.summaryMd: Classified information or classified national security information means information that has been determined pursuant to E. O. 12958 as amended by E.O. 13292 or any predecessor order to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and is marked to indicate its classified status when in documentary form.

senses.definitionMd: Classified information or classified national security information means information that has been determined pursuant to E. O. 12958 as amended by E.O. 13292 or any predecessor order to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and is marked to indicate its classified status when in documentary form.

entries.title: classified national security information
entries.summaryMd: Information that has been determined pursuant to Executive Order 13526 or any predecessor order to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and is marked to indicate its classified status when in documentary form.

senses.definitionMd: Information that has been determined pursuant to Executive Order 13526 or any predecessor order to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and is marked to indicate its classified status when in documentary form.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "classified national security information"

entries.title: clean host
entries.summaryMd: A host with an operating system installation that has never been accessed by end users, such as a host freshly built from a fully-patched security baseline image.

senses.definitionMd: A host with an operating system installation that has never been accessed by end users, such as a host freshly built from a fully-patched security baseline image.

entries.title: clean word list
entries.summaryMd: List of words that are acceptable, but would normally be rejected because they contain a word on the dirty word list (e.g., secret within secretary).

senses.definitionMd: List of words that are acceptable, but would normally be rejected because they contain a word on the dirty word list (e.g., secret within secretary).

entries.title: clear
entries.summaryMd: A method of sanitization that applies logical techniques to sanitize data in all user-addressable storage locations for protection against simple non-invasive data recovery techniques; typically applied through the standard Read and Write commands to the storage device, such as by rewriting with a new value or using a menu option to reset the device to the factory state (where rewriting is not supported).

senses.definitionMd: A method of sanitization that applies logical techniques to sanitize data in all user-addressable storage locations for protection against simple non-invasive data recovery techniques; typically applied through the standard Read and Write commands to the storage device, such as by rewriting with a new value or using a menu option to reset the device to the factory state (where rewriting is not supported).

entries.title: clearance
entries.summaryMd: A formal security determination by an authorized adjudicative office that an individual is authorized access, on a need to know basis, to a specific level of classified information (TOP SECRET, SECRET, or CONFIDENTIAL).

senses.definitionMd: A formal security determination by an authorized adjudicative office that an individual is authorized access, on a need to know basis, to a specific level of classified information (TOP SECRET, SECRET, or CONFIDENTIAL).

entries.title: cleartext
entries.summaryMd: Data that is input to an encryption process.

senses.definitionMd: Data that is input to an encryption process.

entries.title: Clen
entries.summaryMd: The bit length of the ciphertext.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the ciphertext.

entries.title: client
entries.summaryMd: a machine or software application that accesses a cloud over a network connection, perhaps on behalf of a consumer; and

senses.definitionMd: a machine or software application that accesses a cloud over a network connection, perhaps on behalf of a consumer; and

entries.title: client application
entries.summaryMd: A program running on a computer in communication with a card interface device.

senses.definitionMd: A program running on a computer in communication with a card interface device.

entries.title: client node
entries.summaryMd: Enables customers to access primary services nodes (PRSNs) to obtain key management infrastructure (KMI) products and services and to generate, produce, and distribute traditional (symmetric) key products. The management client (MGC) configuration of the client node allows customers to operate locally, independent of a PRSN.

senses.definitionMd: Enables customers to access primary services nodes (PRSNs) to obtain key management infrastructure (KMI) products and services and to generate, produce, and distribute traditional (symmetric) key products. The management client (MGC) configuration of the client node allows customers to operate locally, independent of a PRSN.

entries.title: clipping
entries.summaryMd: The general name for any algorithm that enforces a bound on the impact of one user’s data on an aggregate statistic. A common example is enforcing lower and upper bounds on values being summed in order to bound the global sensitivity of the sum.

senses.definitionMd: The general name for any algorithm that enforces a bound on the impact of one user’s data on an aggregate statistic. A common example is enforcing lower and upper bounds on values being summed in order to bound the global sensitivity of the sum.

entries.title: clipping parameter
entries.summaryMd: The specific choice of lower and upper bounds that are used when an algorithm performs clipping. The utility of a differentially private algorithm is often dependent on choosing good clipping parameters. One must be careful not to compute the clipping parameter directly from the data, as doing so may lead to a violation of privacy.

senses.definitionMd: The specific choice of lower and upper bounds that are used when an algorithm performs clipping. The utility of a differentially private algorithm is often dependent on choosing good clipping parameters. One must be careful not to compute the clipping parameter directly from the data, as doing so may lead to a violation of privacy.

entries.title: clock
entries.summaryMd: A device that generates periodic, accurately spaced signals for timekeeping applications. A clock consists of at least three parts: an oscillator, a device that counts the oscillations and converts them to units of time interval (such as seconds, minutes, hours, and days), and a means of displaying or recording the results.

senses.definitionMd: A device that generates periodic, accurately spaced signals for timekeeping applications. A clock consists of at least three parts: an oscillator, a device that counts the oscillations and converts them to units of time interval (such as seconds, minutes, hours, and days), and a means of displaying or recording the results.

entries.title: Cloned Tag
entries.summaryMd: A tag that is made to be a duplicate of a legitimate tag. A cloned tag can be created by reading data such as an identifier from a legitimate tag and writing that data to a different tag.

senses.definitionMd: A tag that is made to be a duplicate of a legitimate tag. A cloned tag can be created by reading data such as an identifier from a legitimate tag and writing that data to a different tag.

entries.title: closed security environment
entries.summaryMd: Environment providing sufficient assurance that applications and equipment are protected against the introduction of malicious logic during an information system life cycle. Closed security is based upon a system's developers, operators, and maintenance personnel having sufficient clearances, authorization, and configuration control.

senses.definitionMd: Environment providing sufficient assurance that applications and equipment are protected against the introduction of malicious logic during an information system life cycle. Closed security is based upon a system's developers, operators, and maintenance personnel having sufficient clearances, authorization, and configuration control.

entries.title: Closed Source Operating System
entries.summaryMd: Source code for an operating system is not publically available.

senses.definitionMd: Source code for an operating system is not publically available.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Closed Source Operating System"

entries.title: closed storage
entries.summaryMd: The storage of classified information in properly secured General Services Administration-approved security containers.

senses.definitionMd: The storage of classified information in properly secured General Services Administration-approved security containers.

entries.title: Closed System
entries.summaryMd: A system that is self-contained within an enterprise. Closed systems do not have an inter-enterprise subsystem.

senses.definitionMd: A system that is self-contained within an enterprise. Closed systems do not have an inter-enterprise subsystem.

entries.title: Cloud Auditor
entries.summaryMd: A party that can conduct an independent assessment of cloud services, information system operations, performance, and security of the cloud implementation

senses.definitionMd: A party that can conduct an independent assessment of cloud services, information system operations, performance, and security of the cloud implementation

entries.title: Cloud Broker
entries.summaryMd: An entity that manages the use, performance, and delivery of cloud services and negotiates relationships between Cloud Providers and Cloud Consumers

senses.definitionMd: An entity that manages the use, performance, and delivery of cloud services and negotiates relationships between Cloud Providers and Cloud Consumers

entries.title: Cloud Carrier
entries.summaryMd: An intermediary that provides connectivity and transport of cloud services from Cloud Providers to Cloud Consumers

senses.definitionMd: An intermediary that provides connectivity and transport of cloud services from Cloud Providers to Cloud Consumers

entries.title: cloud computing
entries.summaryMd: A model for enabling ubiquitous, convenient, on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g., networks, servers, storage, applications, and services) that can be rapidly provisioned and released with minimal management effort or service provider interaction.

senses.definitionMd: A model for enabling ubiquitous, convenient, on-demand network access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g., networks, servers, storage, applications, and services) that can be rapidly provisioned and released with minimal management effort or service provider interaction.

entries.title: Cloud Consumer
entries.summaryMd: A person or organization that maintains a business relationship with and uses service from Cloud Providers

senses.definitionMd: A person or organization that maintains a business relationship with and uses service from Cloud Providers

entries.title: cloud consumer or customer
entries.summaryMd: a person or organization that is a customer of a cloud; note that a cloud customer may itself be a cloud and that clouds may offer services to one another;

senses.definitionMd: a person or organization that is a customer of a cloud; note that a cloud customer may itself be a cloud and that clouds may offer services to one another;

entries.title: cloud infrastructure
entries.summaryMd: the collection of hardware and software that enables the five essential characteristics of cloud computing. The cloud infrastructure can be viewed as containing both a physical layer and an abstraction layer. The physical layer consists of the hardware resources that are necessary to support the cloud services being provided, and typically includes server, storage and network components. The abstraction layer consists of the software deployed across the physical layer, which manifests the essential cloud characteristics. Conceptually the abstraction layer sits above the physical layer.

senses.definitionMd: the collection of hardware and software that enables the five essential characteristics of cloud computing. The cloud infrastructure can be viewed as containing both a physical layer and an abstraction layer. The physical layer consists of the hardware resources that are necessary to support the cloud services being provided, and typically includes server, storage and network components. The abstraction layer consists of the software deployed across the physical layer, which manifests the essential cloud characteristics. Conceptually the abstraction layer sits above the physical layer.

entries.title: Cloud Provider
entries.summaryMd: The entity (a person or an organization) responsible for making a service available to interested parties

senses.definitionMd: The entity (a person or an organization) responsible for making a service available to interested parties

entries.title: cloud provider or provider
entries.summaryMd: an organization that provides cloud services.

senses.definitionMd: an organization that provides cloud services.

entries.title: Cloud workload
entries.summaryMd: A logical bundle of software and data that is present in, and processed by, a cloud computing technology.

senses.definitionMd: A logical bundle of software and data that is present in, and processed by, a cloud computing technology.

entries.title: Cluster
entries.summaryMd: A group of contiguous sectors.

senses.definitionMd: A group of contiguous sectors.

entries.title: Cn
entries.summaryMd: Block of data representing the Ciphertext n

senses.definitionMd: Block of data representing the Ciphertext n

entries.title: coalition partner

senses.definitionMd: A nation in an ad hoc defense arrangement with the United States.

entries.title: code
entries.summaryMd: System of communication in which arbitrary groups of letters, numbers, or symbols represent units of plain text of varying length.

senses.definitionMd: System of communication in which arbitrary groups of letters, numbers, or symbols represent units of plain text of varying length.

entries.title: code analysis
entries.summaryMd: The act of reverse-engineering the malicious program to understand the code that implements the software behavior. For example, when looking at compiled programs, the process involves using a disassembler, a debugger, and perhaps a decompiler to examine the program’s low-level assembly or byte-code instructions. A disassembler converts the instructions from their binary form into the human-readable assembly form. A decompiler attempts to recreate the original source code of the program. A debugger allows the analyst to step through the code, interacting with it, and observing the effects of its instructions to understand its purpose.

senses.definitionMd: The act of reverse-engineering the malicious program to understand the code that implements the software behavior. For example, when looking at compiled programs, the process involves using a disassembler, a debugger, and perhaps a decompiler to examine the program’s low-level assembly or byte-code instructions. A disassembler converts the instructions from their binary form into the human-readable assembly form. A decompiler attempts to recreate the original source code of the program. A debugger allows the analyst to step through the code, interacting with it, and observing the effects of its instructions to understand its purpose.

entries.title: Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA)
entries.summaryMd: A spread spectrum technology for cellular networks based on the Interim Standard-95 (IS-95) from the Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA).

senses.definitionMd: A spread spectrum technology for cellular networks based on the Interim Standard-95 (IS-95) from the Telecommunications Industry Association (TIA).

entries.title: code group
entries.summaryMd: Group of letters, numbers, or both in a code system used to represent a plain text word, phrase, or sentence.

senses.definitionMd: Group of letters, numbers, or both in a code system used to represent a plain text word, phrase, or sentence.

entries.title: code vocabulary
entries.summaryMd: Set of plain text words, numerals, phrases, or sentences for which code equivalents are assigned in a code system.

senses.definitionMd: Set of plain text words, numerals, phrases, or sentences for which code equivalents are assigned in a code system.

entries.title: codebook
entries.summaryMd: Document containing plain text and code equivalents in a systematic arrangement, or a technique of machine encryption using a word substitution technique or algorithm that encrypts data in blocks of a specified length.

senses.definitionMd: Document containing plain text and code equivalents in a systematic arrangement, or a technique of machine encryption using a word substitution technique or algorithm that encrypts data in blocks of a specified length.

entries.title: Codec
entries.summaryMd: coder/decoder, which converts analog voice into digital data and back again, and may also compress and decompress the data for more efficient transmission.

senses.definitionMd: coder/decoder, which converts analog voice into digital data and back again, and may also compress and decompress the data for more efficient transmission.

entries.title: coded
entries.summaryMd: Identifying information (such as name or social security number) that would enable the investigator to readily ascertain the identity of the individual to whom the private information or specimens pertain has been replaced with a number, letter, symbol, or combination thereof (i.e., the code).

senses.definitionMd: Identifying information (such as name or social security number) that would enable the investigator to readily ascertain the identity of the individual to whom the private information or specimens pertain has been replaced with a number, letter, symbol, or combination thereof (i.e., the code).

entries.title: Coder-Decoder
entries.summaryMd: coder/decoder, which converts analog voice into digital data and back again, and may also compress and decompress the data for more efficient transmission.

entries.title: coercivity
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the ability of a ferromagnetic material to withstand an external magnetic field without becoming demagnetized.

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the ability of a ferromagnetic material to withstand an external magnetic field without becoming demagnetized.

entries.title: cognizant security officer/authority
entries.summaryMd: An entity charged with responsibility for physical, technical, personnel, and information security affecting that organization.

senses.definitionMd: An entity charged with responsibility for physical, technical, personnel, and information security affecting that organization.

entries.title: cold site
entries.summaryMd: A backup facility that has the necessary electrical and physical components of a computer facility, but does not have the computer equipment in place. The site is ready to receive the necessary replacement computer equipment in the event that the user has to move from their main computing location to an alternate site.

entries.title: Collateral Damage Potential
entries.summaryMd: measures the potential for loss of life or physical assets through damage or theft of property or equipment.

senses.definitionMd: measures the potential for loss of life or physical assets through damage or theft of property or equipment.

entries.title: collateral information
entries.summaryMd: National security information (including intelligence information) classified Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential that is not in the Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) or Special Access Program (SAP) category.

senses.definitionMd: National security information (including intelligence information) classified Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential that is not in the Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) or Special Access Program (SAP) category.

entries.title: Collecting and Communicating Audit Trails
entries.summaryMd: To define and identify security-relevant events and the data to be collected and communicated as determined by policy, regulation, or risk analysis to support identification of those security-relevant events.

senses.definitionMd: To define and identify security-relevant events and the data to be collected and communicated as determined by policy, regulation, or risk analysis to support identification of those security-relevant events.

entries.title: Collection
entries.summaryMd: The first phase of the computer and network forensics process, which involves identifying, labeling, recording, and acquiring data from the possible sources of relevant data, while following guidelines and procedures that preserve the integrity of the data.

senses.definitionMd: The first phase of the computer and network forensics process, which involves identifying, labeling, recording, and acquiring data from the possible sources of relevant data, while following guidelines and procedures that preserve the integrity of the data.

entries.title: Collection System

senses.definitionMd: A system that collects actual state data and compares the collected actual state data to the desired state specification to find security defects.

entries.title: Collector
entries.summaryMd: Typically, an automated sensor that gathers actual state data. Part of the collection system.

senses.definitionMd: Typically, an automated sensor that gathers actual state data. Part of the collection system.

entries.title: collision
entries.summaryMd: An event in which two different messages have the same message digest.

senses.definitionMd: An event in which two different messages have the same message digest.

entries.title: Collision resistance

entries.title: Command and Control
entries.summaryMd: Command and Control' is the exercise of authority and direction by a properly designated commander over assigned and attached forces in the accomplishment of the mission. senses.definitionMd: Command and Control' is the exercise of authority and direction by a properly designated commander over assigned and attached forces in the accomplishment of the mission. entries.title: Command Authority
entries.summaryMd: The command authority is responsible for the appointment of user representatives for a department, agency, or organization and their key and granting of modern (electronic) key ordering privileges for those User Representatives.

senses.definitionMd: The command authority is responsible for the appointment of user representatives for a department, agency, or organization and their key and granting of modern (electronic) key ordering privileges for those User Representatives.

entries.title: commercial COMSEC evaluation program (CCEP)

Products developed under the CCEP may include modules, subsystems, equipment, systems, and ancillary devices.

entries.title: commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS)
entries.summaryMd: A software and/or hardware product that is commercially ready-made and available for sale, lease, or license to the general public.

senses.definitionMd: A software and/or hardware product that is commercially ready-made and available for sale, lease, or license to the general public.

entries.title: commercial solutions for classified (CSfC)
entries.summaryMd: A COTS end-to-end strategy and process in which two or more COTS products can be combined into a solution to protect classified information.

entries.title: Commit-Chain
entries.summaryMd: A scheme that enables the off-chain processing of transactions by one or more operators with on-chain state update commitments that do not contain per-transaction data.

senses.definitionMd: A scheme that enables the off-chain processing of transactions by one or more operators with on-chain state update commitments that do not contain per-transaction data.

entries.title: commodity service

entries.title: common access card (CAC)

entries.title: common carrier

entries.title: common configuration enumeration (CCE)
entries.summaryMd: A nomenclature and dictionary of software security configurations.

senses.definitionMd: A nomenclature and dictionary of software security configurations.

entries.title: common configuration scoring system (CCSS)
entries.summaryMd: A SCAP specification for measuring the severity of software security configuration issues.

senses.definitionMd: A SCAP specification for measuring the severity of software security configuration issues.

entries.title: common control
entries.summaryMd: A security control that is inherited by one or more organizational information systems.

entries.title: common control provider

entries.title: common criteria

entries.title: Common Name

entries.title: common platform enumeration (CPE)

senses.definitionMd: A nomenclature and dictionary of hardware, operating systems, and applications.

entries.title: common secure configuration
entries.summaryMd: A recognized standardized and established benchmark (e.g., National Checklist Program, DISA STIGs, CIS Benchmarks, etc.) that stipulates specific secure configuration settings for a given IT platform.

entries.title: common services provider (CSP)

entries.title: common user application software (CUAS)

entries.title: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifiers
entries.summaryMd: An identifier for a specific software flaw defined within the official CVE Dictionary and that conforms to the CVE specification.
