entries.summaryMd: A taxonomy for identifying the common sources of software flaws (e.g., buffer overflows, failure to check input data).

senses.definitionMd: A taxonomy for identifying the common sources of software flaws (e.g., buffer overflows, failure to check input data).

entries.title: Communicate-P (Function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop and implement appropriate activities to enable organizations and individuals to have a reliable understanding and engage in a dialogue about how data are processed and associated privacy risks.

senses.definitionMd: Develop and implement appropriate activities to enable organizations and individuals to have a reliable understanding and engage in a dialogue about how data are processed and associated privacy risks.

entries.title: Communicating group
entries.summaryMd: A set of communicating entities that employ cryptographic services and need cryptographic keying relationships to enable cryptographically protected communications.

senses.definitionMd: A set of communicating entities that employ cryptographic services and need cryptographic keying relationships to enable cryptographically protected communications.

entries.title: Communications
entries.summaryMd: The actions and associated activities that are used to exchange information, provide instructions, give details, etc. In the context of this paper, communications refers to the full range of activities involved with providing information to support the secure use of IoT devices. Communications include using such tools as phone calls, emails, user guides, in-person classes, instruction manuals, webinars, written instructions, videos, quizzes, frequently asked questions (FAQ) documents, and any other type of tool for such information exchanges.

senses.definitionMd: The actions and associated activities that are used to exchange information, provide instructions, give details, etc. In the context of this paper, communications refers to the full range of activities involved with providing information to support the secure use of IoT devices. Communications include using such tools as phone calls, emails, user guides, in-person classes, instruction manuals, webinars, written instructions, videos, quizzes, frequently asked questions (FAQ) documents, and any other type of tool for such information exchanges.

entries.title: communications cover
entries.summaryMd: Result of measures used to obfuscate message externals to resist traffic analysis.

senses.definitionMd: Result of measures used to obfuscate message externals to resist traffic analysis.

entries.title: communications deception
entries.summaryMd: Deliberate transmission, retransmission, or alteration of communications to mislead an adversary's interpretation of the communications.

senses.definitionMd: Deliberate transmission, retransmission, or alteration of communications to mislead an adversary's interpretation of the communications.

entries.title: Communications Module
entries.summaryMd: The sub-component of a Smart Meter responsible for AMI communications between Smart Meters in the field and the Network Management System. The Communications Module may or may not be a separate electronic element, and/or may include the HAN Interface.

senses.definitionMd: The sub-component of a Smart Meter responsible for AMI communications between Smart Meters in the field and the Network Management System. The Communications Module may or may not be a separate electronic element, and/or may include the HAN Interface.

entries.title: Communications Router
entries.summaryMd: A communications device that transfers messages between two networks. Common uses for routers include connecting a LAN to a WAN, and connecting MTUs and RTUs to a long-distance network medium for SCADA communication.

senses.definitionMd: A communications device that transfers messages between two networks. Common uses for routers include connecting a LAN to a WAN, and connecting MTUs and RTUs to a long-distance network medium for SCADA communication.

entries.title: communications security
entries.summaryMd: A component of CS that deals with measures and controls taken to deny unauthorized persons information derived from telecommunications and to ensure the authenticity of such telecommunications. COMSEC includes cryptographic security, transmission security, emissions security, and physical security of COMSEC material and information.

senses.definitionMd: A component of CS that deals with measures and controls taken to deny unauthorized persons information derived from telecommunications and to ensure the authenticity of such telecommunications. COMSEC includes cryptographic security, transmission security, emissions security, and physical security of COMSEC material and information.

entries.title: Community cloud
entries.summaryMd: The cloud infrastructure is provisioned for exclusive use by a specific community of consumers from organizations that have shared concerns (e.g., mission, security requirements, policy, and compliance considerations). It may be owned, managed, and operated by one or more of the organizations in the community, a third party, or some combination of them, and it may exist on or off premises.

senses.definitionMd: The cloud infrastructure is provisioned for exclusive use by a specific community of consumers from organizations that have shared concerns (e.g., mission, security requirements, policy, and compliance considerations). It may be owned, managed, and operated by one or more of the organizations in the community, a third party, or some combination of them, and it may exist on or off premises.

entries.title: community of interest (COI)
entries.summaryMd: A collaborative group of users (working at the appropriate security level or levels) who exchange information in pursuit of their shared goals, interests, missions, or business processes, and must have a shared vocabulary for the information exchanged. The group exchanges information within and between systems.

senses.definitionMd: A collaborative group of users (working at the appropriate security level or levels) who exchange information in pursuit of their shared goals, interests, missions, or business processes, and must have a shared vocabulary for the information exchanged. The group exchanges information within and between systems.

entries.title: community risk
entries.summaryMd: Probability that a particular vulnerability will be exploited within an interacting population and adversely impact some members of that population.

senses.definitionMd: Probability that a particular vulnerability will be exploited within an interacting population and adversely impact some members of that population.

entries.title: Compact Disc
entries.summaryMd: A class of media from which data are read by optical means.

senses.definitionMd: A class of media from which data are read by optical means.

entries.title: Comparison
entries.summaryMd: Estimation, calculation, or measurement of similarity or dissimilarity between biometric probe(s) and biometric reference(s).

senses.definitionMd: Estimation, calculation, or measurement of similarity or dissimilarity between biometric probe(s) and biometric reference(s).

entries.title: compartmentalization
entries.summaryMd: A nonhierarchical grouping of information used to control access to data more finely than with hierarchical security classification alone.

senses.definitionMd: A nonhierarchical grouping of information used to control access to data more finely than with hierarchical security classification alone.

entries.title: Compatible security domains
entries.summaryMd: Two Security Domains are compatible if they can exchange a key and its metadata without violating (or altering) either domain’s FCKMS security policy.

senses.definitionMd: Two Security Domains are compatible if they can exchange a key and its metadata without violating (or altering) either domain’s FCKMS security policy.

entries.title: compensating controls
entries.summaryMd: The security and privacy controls implemented in lieu of the controls in the baselines described in NIST Special Publication 800-53 that provide equivalent or comparable protection for a system or organization.

senses.definitionMd: The security and privacy controls implemented in lieu of the controls in the baselines described in NIST Special Publication 800-53 that provide equivalent or comparable protection for a system or organization.

entries.title: compensating security control
entries.summaryMd: A management, operational, and/or technical control (i.e., safeguard or countermeasure) employed by an organization in lieu of a recommended security control in the low, moderate, or high baselines that provides equivalent or comparable protection for an information system.

senses.definitionMd: A management, operational, and/or technical control (i.e., safeguard or countermeasure) employed by an organization in lieu of a recommended security control in the low, moderate, or high baselines that provides equivalent or comparable protection for an information system.

entries.title: Competency
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism for organizations to assess learners.

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism for organizations to assess learners.

entries.title: competency area
entries.summaryMd: A cluster of related Knowledge and Skill statements that correlates with one’s capability to perform Tasks in a particular domain. Competency Areas can help learners discover areas of interest, inform career planning and development, identify gaps for knowledge and skills development, and provide a means of assessing or demonstrating a learner’s capabilities in the domain.

senses.definitionMd: A cluster of related Knowledge and Skill statements that correlates with one’s capability to perform Tasks in a particular domain. Competency Areas can help learners discover areas of interest, inform career planning and development, identify gaps for knowledge and skills development, and provide a means of assessing or demonstrating a learner’s capabilities in the domain.

entries.title: competent security official
entries.summaryMd: Any cognizant security authority or person designated by the cognizant security authority.

senses.definitionMd: Any cognizant security authority or person designated by the cognizant security authority.

entries.title: Complementary Error Function
entries.summaryMd: See Erfc.

senses.definitionMd: See Erfc.

entries.title: complex system
entries.summaryMd: A system in which there are non-trivial relationships between cause and effect: each effect may be due to multiple causes; each cause may contribute to multiple effects; causes and effects may be related as feedback loops, both positive and negative; and cause-effect chains are cyclic and highly entangled rather than linear and separable.

senses.definitionMd: A system in which there are non-trivial relationships between cause and effect: each effect may be due to multiple causes; each cause may contribute to multiple effects; causes and effects may be related as feedback loops, both positive and negative; and cause-effect chains are cyclic and highly entangled rather than linear and separable.

entries.title: Compliance audit
entries.summaryMd: A comprehensive review of an organization's adherence to governing documents such as whether a Certification Practice Statement satisfies the requirements of a Certificate Policy and whether an organization adheres to its Certification Practice Statement.

senses.definitionMd: A comprehensive review of an organization's adherence to governing documents such as whether a Certification Practice Statement satisfies the requirements of a Certificate Policy and whether an organization adheres to its Certification Practice Statement.

entries.title: Compliance Mapping
entries.summaryMd: The process of correlating CCE settings defined in a source data stream with the security control identifiers defined in [NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4].

senses.definitionMd: The process of correlating CCE settings defined in a source data stream with the security control identifiers defined in [NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4].

entries.title: component
entries.summaryMd: An element of a large system—such as an identity card, issuer, card reader, or identity verification support—within the PIV system.

senses.definitionMd: An element of a large system—such as an identity card, issuer, card reader, or identity verification support—within the PIV system.

entries.title: Component schema
entries.summaryMd: The schema for an SCAP component specification (e.g. XCCDF, CPE, CVSS). Within this document, this term is distinct from “OVAL component schema”, which is defined by the OVAL specification.

senses.definitionMd: The schema for an SCAP component specification (e.g. XCCDF, CPE, CVSS). Within this document, this term is distinct from “OVAL component schema”, which is defined by the OVAL specification.

entries.title: Component specification
entries.summaryMd: One of the individual specifications that comprises SCAP.

senses.definitionMd: One of the individual specifications that comprises SCAP.

entries.title: Component Test
entries.summaryMd: A test of individual hardware and software components or groups of related components.

senses.definitionMd: A test of individual hardware and software components or groups of related components.

entries.title: composed commercial solution
entries.summaryMd: Two or more commercial Information Assurance (IA) products layered together to address the security requirements of an operational use case according to National Security Agency (NSA) guidance. A composed solution, once approved by NSA, may take the place of a single certified Government-off-the-Shelf (GOTS) IA product to provide the confidentiality and/or other security services necessary to protect National Security Systems.

senses.definitionMd: Two or more commercial Information Assurance (IA) products layered together to address the security requirements of an operational use case according to National Security Agency (NSA) guidance. A composed solution, once approved by NSA, may take the place of a single certified Government-off-the-Shelf (GOTS) IA product to provide the confidentiality and/or other security services necessary to protect National Security Systems.

entries.title: Comprehensive Test
entries.summaryMd: A test of all systems and components that support a particular IT plan, such as a contingency plan or computer security incident response plan.

senses.definitionMd: A test of all systems and components that support a particular IT plan, such as a contingency plan or computer security incident response plan.

entries.title: comprehensive testing
entries.summaryMd: A test methodology that assumes explicit and substantial knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as white box testing.

senses.definitionMd: A test methodology that assumes explicit and substantial knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as white box testing.

entries.title: Compressed File
entries.summaryMd: A file reduced in size through the application of a compression algorithm, commonly performed to save disk space. The act of compressing a file makes it unreadable to most programs until the file is uncompressed.

senses.definitionMd: A file reduced in size through the application of a compression algorithm, commonly performed to save disk space. The act of compressing a file makes it unreadable to most programs until the file is uncompressed.

entries.title: compromise
entries.summaryMd: A judgment, based on the preponderance of the evidence, that a disclosure of information to unauthorized persons or a violation of the security policy for a system in which unauthorized, intentional or unintentional disclosure, modification, destruction, or loss of an object has occurred.

senses.definitionMd: A judgment, based on the preponderance of the evidence, that a disclosure of information to unauthorized persons or a violation of the security policy for a system in which unauthorized, intentional or unintentional disclosure, modification, destruction, or loss of an object has occurred.

entries.title: Compromise recovery
entries.summaryMd: The procedures and processes of restoring a system, device or process that has been compromised back to a secure or trusted state, including destroying compromised keys, replacing compromised keys (as needed), and verifying the secure state of the recovered system.

senses.definitionMd: The procedures and processes of restoring a system, device or process that has been compromised back to a secure or trusted state, including destroying compromised keys, replacing compromised keys (as needed), and verifying the secure state of the recovered system.

entries.title: compromised key list (CKL)
entries.summaryMd: The set of Key Material Identification Numbers (KMIDs) of all keys in a universal that have been reported compromised. Cryptographic devices will not establish a secure connection with equipment whose KMID is on the CKL.

senses.definitionMd: The set of Key Material Identification Numbers (KMIDs) of all keys in a universal that have been reported compromised. Cryptographic devices will not establish a secure connection with equipment whose KMID is on the CKL.

entries.title: Compromised state
entries.summaryMd: A lifecycle state for a key that is known or suspected of being known by an unauthorized entity.

senses.definitionMd: A lifecycle state for a key that is known or suspected of being known by an unauthorized entity.

entries.title: compromising emanations
entries.summaryMd: Unintentional signals that, if intercepted and analyzed, would disclose the information transmitted, received, handled, or otherwise processed by telecommunications or information systems equipment.

senses.definitionMd: Unintentional signals that, if intercepted and analyzed, would disclose the information transmitted, received, handled, or otherwise processed by telecommunications or information systems equipment.

entries.title: computationally bounded adversary
entries.summaryMd: An adversarial algorithm that is constrained in running time and memory, and is thus unlikely to break a cryptosystem under consideration. The nature of the constraints depends on the context, including the desired security strength of the cryptosystem.

senses.definitionMd: An adversarial algorithm that is constrained in running time and memory, and is thus unlikely to break a cryptosystem under consideration. The nature of the constraints depends on the context, including the desired security strength of the cryptosystem.

entries.title: Computer
entries.summaryMd: A device that accepts digital data and manipulates the information based on a program or sequence of instructions for how data is to be processed.

senses.definitionMd: A device that accepts digital data and manipulates the information based on a program or sequence of instructions for how data is to be processed.

entries.title: computer abuse
entries.summaryMd: Intentional or reckless misuse, alteration, disruption, or destruction of information processing resources.

senses.definitionMd: Intentional or reckless misuse, alteration, disruption, or destruction of information processing resources.

entries.title: computer cryptography
entries.summaryMd: Use of a crypto-algorithm program by a computer to authenticate or encrypt/decrypt information.

senses.definitionMd: Use of a crypto-algorithm program by a computer to authenticate or encrypt/decrypt information.

entries.title: computer forensics
entries.summaryMd: In its strictest connotation, the application of computer science and investigative procedures involving the examination of digital evidence - following proper search authority, chain of custody, validation with mathematics, use of validated tools, repeatability, reporting, and possibly expert testimony.

senses.definitionMd: In its strictest connotation, the application of computer science and investigative procedures involving the examination of digital evidence - following proper search authority, chain of custody, validation with mathematics, use of validated tools, repeatability, reporting, and possibly expert testimony.

entries.title: computer incident response team (CIRT)
entries.summaryMd: Group of individuals usually consisting of Security Analysts organized to develop, recommend, and coordinate immediate mitigation actions for containment, eradication, and recovery resulting from computer security incidents. Also called a Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) or a CIRC (Computer Incident Response Center, Computer Incident Response Capability, or Cyber Incident Response Team).

senses.definitionMd: Group of individuals usually consisting of Security Analysts organized to develop, recommend, and coordinate immediate mitigation actions for containment, eradication, and recovery resulting from computer security incidents. Also called a Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) or a CIRC (Computer Incident Response Center, Computer Incident Response Capability, or Cyber Incident Response Team).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "computer incident response team (CIRT)"

entries.title: computer network attack (CNA)
entries.summaryMd: An attack, via cyberspace, targeting an enterprise’s use of cyberspace for the purpose of disrupting, disabling, destroying, or maliciously controlling a computing environment/infrastructure; or destroying the integrity of the data or stealing controlled information.

senses.definitionMd: An attack, via cyberspace, targeting an enterprise’s use of cyberspace for the purpose of disrupting, disabling, destroying, or maliciously controlling a computing environment/infrastructure; or destroying the integrity of the data or stealing controlled information.

entries.title: computer network defense (CND)
entries.summaryMd: Actions taken within protected cyberspace to defeat specific threats that have breached or are threatening to breach cyberspace security measures and include actions to detect, characterize, counter, and mitigate threats, including malware or the unauthorized activities of users, and to restore the system to a secure configuration.

senses.definitionMd: Actions taken within protected cyberspace to defeat specific threats that have breached or are threatening to breach cyberspace security measures and include actions to detect, characterize, counter, and mitigate threats, including malware or the unauthorized activities of users, and to restore the system to a secure configuration.

entries.title: computer network exploitation (CNE)
entries.summaryMd: Enabling operations and intelligence collection capabilities conducted through the use of computer networks to gather data from target or adversary information systems or networks. Note: Within the Department of Defense (DoD), term was approved for deletion from JP 1-02 (DoD Dictionary). Original source of term was JP 1-02 (DoD Dictionary). The military no longer uses this term to describe these operations, but it is still used outside of military operations.

senses.definitionMd: Enabling operations and intelligence collection capabilities conducted through the use of computer networks to gather data from target or adversary information systems or networks. Note: Within the Department of Defense (DoD), term was approved for deletion from JP 1-02 (DoD Dictionary). Original source of term was JP 1-02 (DoD Dictionary). The military no longer uses this term to describe these operations, but it is still used outside of military operations.

entries.title: computer network operations (CNO)
entries.summaryMd: The employment of cyberspace capabilities where the primary purpose is to achieve objectives in or through cyberspace.

senses.definitionMd: The employment of cyberspace capabilities where the primary purpose is to achieve objectives in or through cyberspace.

entries.title: Computer Security Incident
entries.summaryMd: An occurrence that actually or imminently jeopardizes, without lawful authority, the integrity, confidentiality, or availability of information or an information system; or constitutes a violation or imminent threat of violation of law, security policies, security procedures, or acceptable use policies.

senses.definitionMd: An occurrence that actually or imminently jeopardizes, without lawful authority, the integrity, confidentiality, or availability of information or an information system; or constitutes a violation or imminent threat of violation of law, security policies, security procedures, or acceptable use policies.

entries.title: Computer Security Log Management
entries.summaryMd: Log management for computer security log data only.

senses.definitionMd: Log management for computer security log data only.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Computer Security Log Management"

entries.title: computer security object
entries.summaryMd: A resource, tool, or mechanism used to maintain a condition of security in a computerized environment. These objects are defined in terms of attributes they possess, operations they perform or are performed on them, and their relationship with other objects.

senses.definitionMd: A resource, tool, or mechanism used to maintain a condition of security in a computerized environment. These objects are defined in terms of attributes they possess, operations they perform or are performed on them, and their relationship with other objects.

entries.title: computer security subsystem
entries.summaryMd: Hardware/software designed to provide computer security features in a larger system environment.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware/software designed to provide computer security features in a larger system environment.

entries.title: computerized telephone system (CTS)
entries.summaryMd: A generic term used to describe any telephone system that uses centralized stored program computer technology to provide switched telephone networking features and services. CTSs are referred to commercially, by such terms, as: computerized private branch exchange (CPBX); private branch exchange (PBX); private automatic branch exchange (PABX); electronic private automatic branch exchange (EABX); computerized branch exchange (CBX); computerized key telephone systems (CKTS); hybrid key systems; business communications systems; and office communications systems.

senses.definitionMd: A generic term used to describe any telephone system that uses centralized stored program computer technology to provide switched telephone networking features and services. CTSs are referred to commercially, by such terms, as: computerized private branch exchange (CPBX); private branch exchange (PBX); private automatic branch exchange (PABX); electronic private automatic branch exchange (EABX); computerized branch exchange (CBX); computerized key telephone systems (CKTS); hybrid key systems; business communications systems; and office communications systems.

entries.title: Computing Device
entries.summaryMd: A functional unit that can perform substantial computations, including numerous arithmetic operations and logic operations without human intervention. A computing device can consist of a standalone unit or several interconnected units. It can also be a device that provides a specific set of functions, such as a phone or a personal organizer, or more general functions such as a laptop or desktop computer.

senses.definitionMd: A functional unit that can perform substantial computations, including numerous arithmetic operations and logic operations without human intervention. A computing device can consist of a standalone unit or several interconnected units. It can also be a device that provides a specific set of functions, such as a phone or a personal organizer, or more general functions such as a laptop or desktop computer.

entries.title: computing environment
entries.summaryMd: Workstation or server (host) and its operating system, peripherals, and applications.

senses.definitionMd: Workstation or server (host) and its operating system, peripherals, and applications.

entries.title: COMSEC account
entries.summaryMd: An administrative entity identified by an account number, used to maintain accountability, custody and control of COMSEC material.

senses.definitionMd: An administrative entity identified by an account number, used to maintain accountability, custody and control of COMSEC material.

entries.title: COMSEC account audit
entries.summaryMd: Inventory and reconciliation of the holdings, records, and procedures of a COMSEC account ensuring all accountable COMSEC material is properly handled and safeguarded. An audit must include an administrative review of procedures, a 100% sighting of all TOP SECRET keying material marked CRYPTO (both physical and electronic) to include hand receipt holders, and a random sampling of all other applicable material (including other keying material, classified and unclassified COMSEC equipment on hand in the account, and on hand receipt).

senses.definitionMd: Inventory and reconciliation of the holdings, records, and procedures of a COMSEC account ensuring all accountable COMSEC material is properly handled and safeguarded. An audit must include an administrative review of procedures, a 100% sighting of all TOP SECRET keying material marked CRYPTO (both physical and electronic) to include hand receipt holders, and a random sampling of all other applicable material (including other keying material, classified and unclassified COMSEC equipment on hand in the account, and on hand receipt).

entries.title: COMSEC account manager
entries.summaryMd: An individual designated by proper authority to be responsible for the receipt, transfer, accountability, safeguarding, and destruction of COMSEC material assigned to a COMSEC account. This applies to both primary accounts and subaccounts. The equivalent key management infrastructure (KMI) position is the KMI operating account (KOA) manager.

senses.definitionMd: An individual designated by proper authority to be responsible for the receipt, transfer, accountability, safeguarding, and destruction of COMSEC material assigned to a COMSEC account. This applies to both primary accounts and subaccounts. The equivalent key management infrastructure (KMI) position is the KMI operating account (KOA) manager.

entries.title: COMSEC aids
entries.summaryMd: All COMSEC material other than equipment or devices, which assist in securing telecommunications and is required in the production, operation, and maintenance of COMSEC systems and their components. Some examples are: COMSEC keying material, and supporting documentation, such as operating and maintenance manuals.

senses.definitionMd: All COMSEC material other than equipment or devices, which assist in securing telecommunications and is required in the production, operation, and maintenance of COMSEC systems and their components. Some examples are: COMSEC keying material, and supporting documentation, such as operating and maintenance manuals.

entries.title: COMSEC assembly
entries.summaryMd: Group of parts, elements, subassemblies, or circuits that are removable items of COMSEC equipment. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

senses.definitionMd: Group of parts, elements, subassemblies, or circuits that are removable items of COMSEC equipment. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

entries.title: COMSEC boundary
entries.summaryMd: Definable perimeter encompassing all hardware, firmware, and software components performing critical COMSEC functions, such as key generation, handling, and storage. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

senses.definitionMd: Definable perimeter encompassing all hardware, firmware, and software components performing critical COMSEC functions, such as key generation, handling, and storage. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

entries.title: COMSEC chip set
entries.summaryMd: Collection of NSA approved microchips. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

senses.definitionMd: Collection of NSA approved microchips. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

entries.title: COMSEC control program
entries.summaryMd: Computer instructions or routines controlling or affecting the externally performed functions of key generation, key distribution, message encryption/decryption, or authentication. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

senses.definitionMd: Computer instructions or routines controlling or affecting the externally performed functions of key generation, key distribution, message encryption/decryption, or authentication. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

entries.title: COMSEC custodian
entries.summaryMd: An individual designated by proper authority to be responsible for the receipt, transfer, accountability, safeguarding, and destruction of COMSEC material assigned to a COMSEC account. This applies to both primary accounts and subaccounts. The equivalent key management infrastructure (KMI) position is the KMI operating account (KOA) manager.

senses.definitionMd: An individual designated by proper authority to be responsible for the receipt, transfer, accountability, safeguarding, and destruction of COMSEC material assigned to a COMSEC account. This applies to both primary accounts and subaccounts. The equivalent key management infrastructure (KMI) position is the KMI operating account (KOA) manager.

entries.title: COMSEC demilitarization
entries.summaryMd: The process of preparing National Security System equipment for disposal by extracting all CCI, classified, or CRYPTO-marked components for their secure destruction, as well as defacing and disposing of the remaining equipment hulk.

senses.definitionMd: The process of preparing National Security System equipment for disposal by extracting all CCI, classified, or CRYPTO-marked components for their secure destruction, as well as defacing and disposing of the remaining equipment hulk.

entries.title: COMSEC element
entries.summaryMd: Removable item of COMSEC equipment, assembly, or subassembly; normally consisting of a single piece or group of replaceable parts. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

senses.definitionMd: Removable item of COMSEC equipment, assembly, or subassembly; normally consisting of a single piece or group of replaceable parts. Rationale: The term falls under the broader term “COMSEC material”.

entries.title: COMSEC emergency
entries.summaryMd: A tactical operational situation, as perceived by the responsible person/officer in charge, in which the alternative to strict compliance with procedural restrictions affecting use of a COMSEC equipment would be plain text communication.

senses.definitionMd: A tactical operational situation, as perceived by the responsible person/officer in charge, in which the alternative to strict compliance with procedural restrictions affecting use of a COMSEC equipment would be plain text communication.

entries.title: COMSEC end-item
entries.summaryMd: Equipment or combination of components ready for use in a COMSEC application.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment or combination of components ready for use in a COMSEC application.

entries.title: COMSEC equipment
entries.summaryMd: Equipment designed to provide security to telecommunications by converting information to a form unintelligible to an unauthorized interceptor and, subsequently, by reconverting such information to its original form for authorized recipients; also, equipment designed specifically to aid in, or as an essential element of, the conversion process. COMSEC equipment includes cryptographic-equipment, crypto-ancillary equipment, cryptographic production equipment, and authentication equipment.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment designed to provide security to telecommunications by converting information to a form unintelligible to an unauthorized interceptor and, subsequently, by reconverting such information to its original form for authorized recipients; also, equipment designed specifically to aid in, or as an essential element of, the conversion process. COMSEC equipment includes cryptographic-equipment, crypto-ancillary equipment, cryptographic production equipment, and authentication equipment.

entries.title: COMSEC facility
entries.summaryMd: The space used for generating, storing, repairing, or using COMSEC material. The COMSEC material may be in either physical or electronic form. Unless otherwise noted, the term "COMSEC facility" refers to all types of COMSEC facilities, including telecommunications facilities, and includes platforms such as ships, aircraft, and vehicles.

senses.definitionMd: The space used for generating, storing, repairing, or using COMSEC material. The COMSEC material may be in either physical or electronic form. Unless otherwise noted, the term "COMSEC facility" refers to all types of COMSEC facilities, including telecommunications facilities, and includes platforms such as ships, aircraft, and vehicles.

entries.title: COMSEC incident
entries.summaryMd: Any occurrence that potentially jeopardizes the security of COMSEC material or the secure transmission of national security information. COMSEC Incident includes Cryptographic Incident, Personnel Incident, Physical Incident, and Protective Technology/Package Incident.

senses.definitionMd: Any occurrence that potentially jeopardizes the security of COMSEC material or the secure transmission of national security information. COMSEC Incident includes Cryptographic Incident, Personnel Incident, Physical Incident, and Protective Technology/Package Incident.

entries.title: COMSEC Incident Monitoring Activity
entries.summaryMd: The office within a department or agency maintaining a record of COMSEC incidents caused by elements of that department or agency, and ensuring all actions required of those elements are completed.

senses.definitionMd: The office within a department or agency maintaining a record of COMSEC incidents caused by elements of that department or agency, and ensuring all actions required of those elements are completed.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "COMSEC Incident Monitoring Activity"

entries.title: COMSEC insecurity
entries.summaryMd: A COMSEC incident that has been investigated, evaluated, and determined to jeopardize the security of COMSEC material or the secure transmission of information.

senses.definitionMd: A COMSEC incident that has been investigated, evaluated, and determined to jeopardize the security of COMSEC material or the secure transmission of information.

entries.title: COMSEC manager
entries.summaryMd: An individual designated by proper authority to be responsible for the receipt, transfer, accountability, safeguarding, and destruction of COMSEC material assigned to a COMSEC account. This applies to both primary accounts and subaccounts. The equivalent key management infrastructure (KMI) position is the KMI operating account (KOA) manager.

entries.title: COMSEC material

This includes Controlled Cryptographic Item (CCI) equipment, Cryptographic High Value Products (CHVP) and other Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) equipment, etc.

entries.title: COMSEC material control system

entries.title: Condition coverage
entries.summaryMd: The percentage of conditions within decision expressions that have been evaluated to both true and false. Note that 100% condition coverage does not guarantee 100% decision coverage. For example, “if (A || B) {do something} else {do something else}” is tested with [0 1], [1 0], then A and B will both have been evaluated to 0 and 1, but the else branch will not be taken because neither test leaves both A and B false.

Any transactions “lost” by the state not chosen are added back into the pending transaction pool.
