entries.title: control assessor
entries.summaryMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a control assessment. See assessor.

senses.definitionMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a control assessment. See assessor.

entries.title: control baseline
entries.summaryMd: Hardware, software, and relevant documentation for an information system at a given point in time.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware, software, and relevant documentation for an information system at a given point in time.

entries.title: Control Cell
entries.summaryMd: A central location for exercise coordination, typically in a separate area from the exercise participants.

senses.definitionMd: A central location for exercise coordination, typically in a separate area from the exercise participants.

entries.title: Control Center
entries.summaryMd: An equipment structure or group of structures from which a process is measured, controlled, and/or monitored.

senses.definitionMd: An equipment structure or group of structures from which a process is measured, controlled, and/or monitored.

entries.title: control correlation identifier (CCI)
entries.summaryMd: Decomposition of a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) control into a single, actionable, measurable statement.

senses.definitionMd: Decomposition of a National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) control into a single, actionable, measurable statement.

entries.title: control designation
entries.summaryMd: The process of assigning a control to one of three control types: common, hybrid, or system-specific.

senses.definitionMd: The process of assigning a control to one of three control types: common, hybrid, or system-specific.

entries.title: control effectiveness
entries.summaryMd: A measure of whether a given control is contributing to the reduction of information security or privacy risk.

senses.definitionMd: A measure of whether a given control is contributing to the reduction of information security or privacy risk.

entries.title: control enhancement
entries.summaryMd: Augmentation of a control to build in additional, but related, functionality to the control; increase the strength of the control; or add assurance to the control.

senses.definitionMd: Augmentation of a control to build in additional, but related, functionality to the control; increase the strength of the control; or add assurance to the control.

entries.title: control inheritance
entries.summaryMd: A situation in which a system or application receives protection from controls (or portions of controls) that are developed, implemented, assessed, authorized, and monitored by entities other than those responsible for the system or application; entities either internal or external to the organization where the system or application resides.

senses.definitionMd: A situation in which a system or application receives protection from controls (or portions of controls) that are developed, implemented, assessed, authorized, and monitored by entities other than those responsible for the system or application; entities either internal or external to the organization where the system or application resides.

entries.title: Control Item
entries.summaryMd: See Security Control Item.

senses.definitionMd: See Security Control Item.

entries.title: Control Loop
entries.summaryMd: A control loop consists of sensors for measurement, controller hardware (e.g., PLCs), actuators (e.g., control valves, breakers, switches, and motors), and the communication of variables. Controlled variables are transmitted to the controller from the sensors. The controller interprets the signals and generates corresponding manipulated variables based on set points, which it transmits to the actuators. Process changes from disturbances result in new sensor signals, identifying the state of the process, to again be transmitted to the controller.

senses.definitionMd: A control loop consists of sensors for measurement, controller hardware (e.g., PLCs), actuators (e.g., control valves, breakers, switches, and motors), and the communication of variables. Controlled variables are transmitted to the controller from the sensors. The controller interprets the signals and generates corresponding manipulated variables based on set points, which it transmits to the actuators. Process changes from disturbances result in new sensor signals, identifying the state of the process, to again be transmitted to the controller.

entries.title: Control Network
entries.summaryMd: Those networks of an enterprise typically connected to equipment that controls physical processes and that is time or safety critical. The control network can be subdivided into zones, and there can be multiple separate control networks within one enterprise and site.

senses.definitionMd: Those networks of an enterprise typically connected to equipment that controls physical processes and that is time or safety critical. The control network can be subdivided into zones, and there can be multiple separate control networks within one enterprise and site.

entries.title: Control-P (Function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop and implement appropriate activities to enable organizations or individuals to manage data with sufficient granularity to manage privacy risks.

senses.definitionMd: Develop and implement appropriate activities to enable organizations or individuals to manage data with sufficient granularity to manage privacy risks.

entries.title: control parameter
entries.summaryMd: See organization-defined control parameter.

senses.definitionMd: See organization-defined control parameter.

entries.title: Control Server
entries.summaryMd: A term that is used to imply that the output of a controller or computer program is used as input to other controllers.

senses.definitionMd: A term that is used to imply that the output of a controller or computer program is used as input to other controllers.

entries.title: Control System
entries.summaryMd: A system in which deliberate guidance or manipulation is used to achieve a prescribed value for a variable. Control systems include SCADA, DCS, PLCs, BAS, and other types of OT measurement and control systems.

senses.definitionMd: A system in which deliberate guidance or manipulation is used to achieve a prescribed value for a variable. Control systems include SCADA, DCS, PLCs, BAS, and other types of OT measurement and control systems.

entries.title: controlled
entries.summaryMd: The online repository of information and policy regarding how authorized holders of CUI should handle such information. Note: The Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Registry: (i) identifies all categories and subcategories of information that require safeguarding or dissemination controls consistent with law, regulation and Government-wide policies; (ii) provides descriptions for each category and subcategory; (iii) identifies the basis for safeguarding and dissemination controls;(iv) contains associated markings and applicable safeguarding, disseminating, and (v) specifies CUI that may be originated only by certain executive branch agencies and organizations. The CUI Executive Agent is the approval authority for all categories/subcategories of information identified as CUI in the CUI Registry and only those categories/subcategories listed are considered CUI.

senses.definitionMd: The online repository of information and policy regarding how authorized holders of CUI should handle such information. Note: The Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Registry: (i) identifies all categories and subcategories of information that require safeguarding or dissemination controls consistent with law, regulation and Government-wide policies; (ii) provides descriptions for each category and subcategory; (iii) identifies the basis for safeguarding and dissemination controls;(iv) contains associated markings and applicable safeguarding, disseminating, and (v) specifies CUI that may be originated only by certain executive branch agencies and organizations. The CUI Executive Agent is the approval authority for all categories/subcategories of information identified as CUI in the CUI Registry and only those categories/subcategories listed are considered CUI.

entries.title: controlled access area
entries.summaryMd: The complete building or facility area under direct physical control within which unauthorized persons are denied unrestricted access and are either escorted by authorized personnel or are under continuous physical or electronic surveillance.

senses.definitionMd: The complete building or facility area under direct physical control within which unauthorized persons are denied unrestricted access and are either escorted by authorized personnel or are under continuous physical or electronic surveillance.

entries.title: controlled access protection
entries.summaryMd: Minimum set of security functionality that enforces access control on individual users and makes them accountable for their actions through login procedures, auditing of security-relevant events, and resource isolation.

senses.definitionMd: Minimum set of security functionality that enforces access control on individual users and makes them accountable for their actions through login procedures, auditing of security-relevant events, and resource isolation.

entries.title: controlled area
entries.summaryMd: Any area or space for which the organization has confidence that the physical and procedural protections provided are sufficient to meet the requirements established for protecting the information and/or information system.

senses.definitionMd: Any area or space for which the organization has confidence that the physical and procedural protections provided are sufficient to meet the requirements established for protecting the information and/or information system.

entries.title: controlled cryptographic item (CCI)
entries.summaryMd: Secure telecommunications or information system, or associated cryptographic component, that is unclassified and handled through the COMSEC material control system (CMCS), an equivalent material control system, or a combination of the two that provides accountability and visibility. Such items are marked “Controlled Cryptographic Item”, or, where space is limited, “CCI”.

senses.definitionMd: Secure telecommunications or information system, or associated cryptographic component, that is unclassified and handled through the COMSEC material control system (CMCS), an equivalent material control system, or a combination of the two that provides accountability and visibility. Such items are marked “Controlled Cryptographic Item”, or, where space is limited, “CCI”.

entries.title: controlled cryptographic item (CCI) assembly
entries.summaryMd: A device approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) as a controlled cryptographic item, that embodies a cryptographic logic or other cryptographic design, and performs the entire COMSEC function, but is dependent upon the host equipment to operate.

senses.definitionMd: A device approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) as a controlled cryptographic item, that embodies a cryptographic logic or other cryptographic design, and performs the entire COMSEC function, but is dependent upon the host equipment to operate.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "controlled cryptographic item (CCI) assembly"

entries.title: controlled cryptographic item (CCI) component
entries.summaryMd: A device approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) as a controlled cryptographic item, that embodies a cryptographic logic or other cryptographic design, and performs the entire COMSEC function, but is dependent upon the host equipment to operate.

senses.definitionMd: A device approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) as a controlled cryptographic item, that embodies a cryptographic logic or other cryptographic design, and performs the entire COMSEC function, but is dependent upon the host equipment to operate.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "controlled cryptographic item (CCI) component"

entries.title: controlled cryptographic item (CCI) equipment
entries.summaryMd: A telecommunications or information handling equipment that embodies a CCI component or CCI assembly and performs the entire COMSEC function without dependence on host equipment to operate.

senses.definitionMd: A telecommunications or information handling equipment that embodies a CCI component or CCI assembly and performs the entire COMSEC function without dependence on host equipment to operate.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "controlled cryptographic item (CCI) equipment"

entries.title: controlled interface
entries.summaryMd: A boundary with a set of mechanisms that enforces the security policies and controls the flow of information between interconnected information systems.

senses.definitionMd: A boundary with a set of mechanisms that enforces the security policies and controls the flow of information between interconnected information systems.

entries.title: controlled space
entries.summaryMd: Three-dimensional space surrounding information system equipment, within which unauthorized individuals are denied unrestricted access and are either escorted by authorized individuals or are under continuous physical or electronic surveillance.

senses.definitionMd: Three-dimensional space surrounding information system equipment, within which unauthorized individuals are denied unrestricted access and are either escorted by authorized individuals or are under continuous physical or electronic surveillance.

entries.title: controlled unclassified information (CUI)
entries.summaryMd: Information that law, regulation, or governmentwide policy requires to have safeguarding or disseminating controls, excluding information that is classified under Executive Order 13526, Classified National Security Information, December 29, 2009, or any predecessor or successor order, or the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended.

senses.definitionMd: Information that law, regulation, or governmentwide policy requires to have safeguarding or disseminating controls, excluding information that is classified under Executive Order 13526, Classified National Security Information, December 29, 2009, or any predecessor or successor order, or the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended.

entries.title: Controlled Variable
entries.summaryMd: The variable that the control system attempts to keep at the set point value. The set point may be constant or variable.

senses.definitionMd: The variable that the control system attempts to keep at the set point value. The set point may be constant or variable.

entries.title: Controller
entries.summaryMd: A device or program that operates automatically to regulate a controlled variable.

senses.definitionMd: A device or program that operates automatically to regulate a controlled variable.

entries.title: controlling authority (CONAUTH)
entries.summaryMd: The official responsible for directing the operation of a cryptonet using traditional key and for managing the operational use and control of keying material assigned to the cryptonet.

senses.definitionMd: The official responsible for directing the operation of a cryptonet using traditional key and for managing the operational use and control of keying material assigned to the cryptonet.

entries.title: controlling domain
entries.summaryMd: The domain that assumes the greater risk and thus enforces the most restrictive policy.

senses.definitionMd: The domain that assumes the greater risk and thus enforces the most restrictive policy.

entries.title: controls
entries.summaryMd: Policies, procedures, guidelines, practices, or organizational structures that manage security, privacy, and other risks.

senses.definitionMd: Policies, procedures, guidelines, practices, or organizational structures that manage security, privacy, and other risks.

entries.title: Conventional BIOS
entries.summaryMd: Legacy boot firmware used in many x86-compatible computer systems. Also known as the legacy BIOS.

senses.definitionMd: Legacy boot firmware used in many x86-compatible computer systems. Also known as the legacy BIOS.

entries.title: Conversation
entries.summaryMd: Where Web services maintain some state during an interaction that involves multiple messages or participants.

senses.definitionMd: Where Web services maintain some state during an interaction that involves multiple messages or participants.

entries.title: convolutional neural networks
entries.summaryMd: A class of feed-forward neural networks that include at least one convolutional layer, referred to as CNNs. In convolutional layers, feature detectors (known as kernels or filters) detect specific features across the input data. CNNs are primarily used for processing grid-like data, such as images, and are particularly effective for tasks like image classification, object detection, and image segmentation.

senses.definitionMd: A class of feed-forward neural networks that include at least one convolutional layer, referred to as CNNs. In convolutional layers, feature detectors (known as kernels or filters) detect specific features across the input data. CNNs are primarily used for processing grid-like data, such as images, and are particularly effective for tasks like image classification, object detection, and image segmentation.

entries.title: cookie
entries.summaryMd: A piece of state information supplied by a Web server to a browser, in a response for a requested resource, for the browser to store temporarily and return to the server on any subsequent visits or requests.

senses.definitionMd: A piece of state information supplied by a Web server to a browser, in a response for a requested resource, for the browser to store temporarily and return to the server on any subsequent visits or requests.

entries.title: cooperative key generation (CKG)
entries.summaryMd: Electronically exchanging functions of locally generated, random components, from which both terminals of a secure circuit construct traffic encryption key or key encryption key for use on that circuit. See per-call key.

senses.definitionMd: Electronically exchanging functions of locally generated, random components, from which both terminals of a secure circuit construct traffic encryption key or key encryption key for use on that circuit. See per-call key.

entries.title: cooperative remote rekeying
entries.summaryMd: Synonymous with manual remote rekeying.

senses.definitionMd: Synonymous with manual remote rekeying.

entries.title: Coordination
entries.summaryMd: Refers to the building, from a set of Web services, of something at a higher level, typically itself exposed as a larger Web service. Also referred to as “Composability.” Choreography and orchestration are two approaches to coordination.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to the building, from a set of Web services, of something at a higher level, typically itself exposed as a larger Web service. Also referred to as “Composability.” Choreography and orchestration are two approaches to coordination.

entries.title: Copy (data)
entries.summaryMd: To replicate data in another location while maintaining it in its original location.

senses.definitionMd: To replicate data in another location while maintaining it in its original location.

entries.title: Core
entries.summaryMd: A set of privacy protection activities and outcomes. The Framework Core comprises three elements: Functions, Categories, and Subcategories.

senses.definitionMd: A set of privacy protection activities and outcomes. The Framework Core comprises three elements: Functions, Categories, and Subcategories.

entries.title: core attributes
entries.summaryMd: The set of identity attributes that the CSP has determined and documented to be required for identity proofing and to provide services.

senses.definitionMd: The set of identity attributes that the CSP has determined and documented to be required for identity proofing and to provide services.

entries.title: Core Baseline
entries.summaryMd: A set of technical device capabilities needed to support common cybersecurity controls that protect the customer’s devices and device data, systems, and ecosystems.

senses.definitionMd: A set of technical device capabilities needed to support common cybersecurity controls that protect the customer’s devices and device data, systems, and ecosystems.

entries.title: Core Root of Trust for Measurement (CRTM)
entries.summaryMd: The first piece of BIOS code that executes on the main processor during the boot process. On a system with a Trusted Platform Module the CRTM is implicitly trusted to bootstrap the process of building a measurement chain for subsequent attestation of other firmware and software that is executed on the computer system.

senses.definitionMd: The first piece of BIOS code that executes on the main processor during the boot process. On a system with a Trusted Platform Module the CRTM is implicitly trusted to bootstrap the process of building a measurement chain for subsequent attestation of other firmware and software that is executed on the computer system.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Core Root of Trust for Measurement (CRTM)"

entries.title: Core Software
entries.summaryMd: An organizationally defined set of software that, at a minimum, includes firmware and root operating system elements used to boot the system. Core software merits specialized monitoring as it may be difficult for commonly used whitelisting software to check.

senses.definitionMd: An organizationally defined set of software that, at a minimum, includes firmware and root operating system elements used to boot the system. Core software merits specialized monitoring as it may be difficult for commonly used whitelisting software to check.

entries.title: Corporate-Owned Personally-Enabled (COPE)
entries.summaryMd: A device owned by an enterprise and issued to an employee. Both the enterprise and the employee can install applications onto the device.

senses.definitionMd: A device owned by an enterprise and issued to an employee. Both the enterprise and the employee can install applications onto the device.

entries.title: correct re-identifications
entries.summaryMd: Putative re-identifications that correctly infer an individual's identity and associated data.

senses.definitionMd: Putative re-identifications that correctly infer an individual's identity and associated data.

entries.title: correctness proof
entries.summaryMd: Formal technique used to prove mathematically that a computer program satisfies its specified requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Formal technique used to prove mathematically that a computer program satisfies its specified requirements.

entries.title: Correlation
entries.summaryMd: See “Event Correlation”.

senses.definitionMd: See “Event Correlation”.

entries.title: counterfeit
entries.summaryMd: An unauthorized copy or substitute that has been identified, marked, and/or altered by a source other than the item's legally authorized source and has been misrepresented to be an authorized item of the legally authorized source.

senses.definitionMd: An unauthorized copy or substitute that has been identified, marked, and/or altered by a source other than the item's legally authorized source and has been misrepresented to be an authorized item of the legally authorized source.

entries.title: counterintelligence
entries.summaryMd: Information gathered and activities conducted to identify, deceive, exploit, disrupt, or protect against espionage, other intelligence activities, sabotage, or assassinations conducted for or on behalf of foreign powers, organizations, or persons, or their agents, or international terrorist organizations or activities.

senses.definitionMd: Information gathered and activities conducted to identify, deceive, exploit, disrupt, or protect against espionage, other intelligence activities, sabotage, or assassinations conducted for or on behalf of foreign powers, organizations, or persons, or their agents, or international terrorist organizations or activities.

entries.title: countermeasures
entries.summaryMd: Actions, devices, procedures, techniques, or other measures that reduce the vulnerability of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Actions, devices, procedures, techniques, or other measures that reduce the vulnerability of an information system.

entries.title: counting query
entries.summaryMd: A query that counts the number of rows in a dataset with a particular property.

senses.definitionMd: A query that counts the number of rows in a dataset with a particular property.

entries.title: courier
entries.summaryMd: A duly authorized and trustworthy individual who has been officially designated to transport/carry material, and if the material is classified, is cleared to the level of material being transported.

senses.definitionMd: A duly authorized and trustworthy individual who has been officially designated to transport/carry material, and if the material is classified, is cleared to the level of material being transported.

entries.title: Course of Action
entries.summaryMd: A time-phased or situation-dependent combination of risk response measures.

senses.definitionMd: A time-phased or situation-dependent combination of risk response measures.

entries.title: Cover-Coding
entries.summaryMd: A technique to reduce the risks of eavesdropping by obscuring the information that is transmitted. The EPCglobal Class- 1 Generation-2 and ISO/IEC 18000-6C standards use cover-coding to obscure certain transmissions from readers to tags. A more detailed description of how cover-coding is used in these two standards can be found in Section 5.3.2.1 on cover-coding.

senses.definitionMd: A technique to reduce the risks of eavesdropping by obscuring the information that is transmitted. The EPCglobal Class- 1 Generation-2 and ISO/IEC 18000-6C standards use cover-coding to obscure certain transmissions from readers to tags. A more detailed description of how cover-coding is used in these two standards can be found in Section 5.3.2.1 on cover-coding.

entries.title: cover (TRANSEC)
entries.summaryMd: Result of measures used to obfuscate message externals to resist traffic analysis.

senses.definitionMd: Result of measures used to obfuscate message externals to resist traffic analysis.

entries.title: coverage
entries.summaryMd: An attribute associated with an assessment method that addresses the scope or breadth of the assessment objects included in the assessment (e.g., types of objects to be assessed and the number of objects to be assessed by type). The values for the coverage attribute, hierarchically from less coverage to more coverage, are basic, focused, and comprehensive.

senses.definitionMd: An attribute associated with an assessment method that addresses the scope or breadth of the assessment objects included in the assessment (e.g., types of objects to be assessed and the number of objects to be assessed by type). The values for the coverage attribute, hierarchically from less coverage to more coverage, are basic, focused, and comprehensive.

entries.title: covered entity
entries.summaryMd: Under HIPAA, a health plan, a health care clearinghouse, or a health care provider that conducts certain health care transactions electronically (e.g., billing).

senses.definitionMd: Under HIPAA, a health plan, a health care clearinghouse, or a health care provider that conducts certain health care transactions electronically (e.g., billing).

entries.title: covert channel
entries.summaryMd: An unintended or unauthorized intra-system channel that enables two cooperating entities to transfer information in a way that violates the system's security policy but does not exceed the entities' access authorizations.

senses.definitionMd: An unintended or unauthorized intra-system channel that enables two cooperating entities to transfer information in a way that violates the system's security policy but does not exceed the entities' access authorizations.

entries.title: covert channel analysis
entries.summaryMd: Determination of the extent to which the security policy model and subsequent lower-level program descriptions may allow unauthorized access to information.

senses.definitionMd: Determination of the extent to which the security policy model and subsequent lower-level program descriptions may allow unauthorized access to information.

entries.title: covert storage channel
entries.summaryMd: A system feature that enables one system entity to signal information to another entity by directly or indirectly writing a storage location that is later directly or indirectly read by the second entity.

senses.definitionMd: A system feature that enables one system entity to signal information to another entity by directly or indirectly writing a storage location that is later directly or indirectly read by the second entity.

entries.title: Covert Testing
entries.summaryMd: Testing performed using covert methods and without the knowledge of the organization’s IT staff, but with full knowledge and permission of upper management.

senses.definitionMd: Testing performed using covert methods and without the knowledge of the organization’s IT staff, but with full knowledge and permission of upper management.

entries.title: covert timing channel
entries.summaryMd: A system feature that enables one system entity to signal information to another by modulating its own use of a system resource in such a way as to affect system response time observed by the second entity. See: covert channel.

senses.definitionMd: A system feature that enables one system entity to signal information to another by modulating its own use of a system resource in such a way as to affect system response time observed by the second entity. See: covert channel.

entries.title: CPE Attribute Comparison
entries.summaryMd: The first phase of CPE name matching, where a matching engine compares each of the A-V pairs of a source CPE name to the corresponding A-V pair of a target name in order to specify one of four possible logical attribute comparison relations for each attribute in a CPE name.

senses.definitionMd: The first phase of CPE name matching, where a matching engine compares each of the A-V pairs of a source CPE name to the corresponding A-V pair of a target name in order to specify one of four possible logical attribute comparison relations for each attribute in a CPE name.

entries.title: CPE Dictionary
entries.summaryMd: A repository of identifier CPE names (WFNs in bound form) and associated metadata.

senses.definitionMd: A repository of identifier CPE names (WFNs in bound form) and associated metadata.

entries.title: CPE Name
entries.summaryMd: An identifier for a unique uniform resource identifier (URI) assigned to a specific platform type that conforms to the CPE specification.

senses.definitionMd: An identifier for a unique uniform resource identifier (URI) assigned to a specific platform type that conforms to the CPE specification.

entries.title: CPE Name Comparison
entries.summaryMd: The second phase of CPE name matching, where the individual attribute comparison results from the first phase are analyzed as a collection to determine an overall comparison result for the two names. The result of a name comparison is the identification of the relationship between a source CPE name and target CPE name.

senses.definitionMd: The second phase of CPE name matching, where the individual attribute comparison results from the first phase are analyzed as a collection to determine an overall comparison result for the two names. The result of a name comparison is the identification of the relationship between a source CPE name and target CPE name.

entries.title: CPE Name Matching
entries.summaryMd: A one-to-one source-to-target comparison of CPE names. CPE name matching has two phases

senses.definitionMd: A one-to-one source-to-target comparison of CPE names. CPE name matching has two phases

entries.title: Cradle
entries.summaryMd: A docking station, which creates an interface between a user’s PC and PDA and enables communication and battery recharging.

senses.definitionMd: A docking station, which creates an interface between a user’s PC and PDA and enables communication and battery recharging.

entries.title: credential
entries.summaryMd: Evidence attesting to one’s right to credit or authority. In this Standard, it is the PIV Card or derived PIV credential associated with an individual that authoritatively binds an identity (and, optionally, additional attributes) to that individual.

senses.definitionMd: Evidence attesting to one’s right to credit or authority. In this Standard, it is the PIV Card or derived PIV credential associated with an individual that authoritatively binds an identity (and, optionally, additional attributes) to that individual.

entries.title: Credential Management
entries.summaryMd: To manage the life cycle of entity credentials used for authentication.

senses.definitionMd: To manage the life cycle of entity credentials used for authentication.

entries.title: credential service provider (CSP)
entries.summaryMd: A trusted entity that issues or registers subscriber tokens and issues electronic credentials to subscribers. The CSP may encompass registration authorities (RAs) and verifiers that it operates. A CSP may be an independent third party, or may issue credentials for its own use.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted entity that issues or registers subscriber tokens and issues electronic credentials to subscribers. The CSP may encompass registration authorities (RAs) and verifiers that it operates. A CSP may be an independent third party, or may issue credentials for its own use.

entries.title: credible source
entries.summaryMd: An entity that can provide or validate the accuracy of identity evidence and attribute information. A credible source has access to attribute information that was validated through an identity proofing process or that can be traced to an authoritative source, or it maintains identity attribute information obtained from multiple sources that is checked for data correlation for accuracy, consistency, and currency.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that can provide or validate the accuracy of identity evidence and attribute information. A credible source has access to attribute information that was validated through an identity proofing process or that can be traced to an authoritative source, or it maintains identity attribute information obtained from multiple sources that is checked for data correlation for accuracy, consistency, and currency.

entries.title: critical AI system
entries.summaryMd: Any system incorporating critical software and in which failure can cause substantial harm to the public.

senses.definitionMd: Any system incorporating critical software and in which failure can cause substantial harm to the public.

entries.title: critical component
entries.summaryMd: A component which is or contains information and communications technology (ICT), including hardware, software, and firmware, whether custom, commercial, or otherwise developed, and which delivers or protects mission critical functionality of a system or which, because of the system’s design, may introduce vulnerability to the mission critical functions of an applicable system.

senses.definitionMd: A component which is or contains information and communications technology (ICT), including hardware, software, and firmware, whether custom, commercial, or otherwise developed, and which delivers or protects mission critical functionality of a system or which, because of the system’s design, may introduce vulnerability to the mission critical functions of an applicable system.

entries.title: critical infrastructure
entries.summaryMd: System and assets, whether physical or virtual, so vital to the U.S. that the incapacity or destruction of such systems and assets would have a debilitating impact on security, national economic security, national public health or safety, or any combination of those matters.

senses.definitionMd: System and assets, whether physical or virtual, so vital to the U.S. that the incapacity or destruction of such systems and assets would have a debilitating impact on security, national economic security, national public health or safety, or any combination of those matters.

entries.title: critical infrastructure sectors
entries.summaryMd: The 16 sectors designated by PPD-21 as vital to the United States, namely: chemical; commercial facilities; communications; critical manufacturing; dams; the defense industrial base; emergency services; energy; financial services; food and agriculture; government facilities; healthcare and public health; information technology; nuclear reactors, materials, and waste; transportation systems; and water and wastewater systems.

senses.definitionMd: The 16 sectors designated by PPD-21 as vital to the United States, namely: chemical; commercial facilities; communications; critical manufacturing; dams; the defense industrial base; emergency services; energy; financial services; food and agriculture; government facilities; healthcare and public health; information technology; nuclear reactors, materials, and waste; transportation systems; and water and wastewater systems.

entries.title: critical program (or technology)
entries.summaryMd: A program which significantly increases capability, mission effectiveness, or extends the expected effective life of an essential system/capability.

senses.definitionMd: A program which significantly increases capability, mission effectiveness, or extends the expected effective life of an essential system/capability.

entries.title: Critical Services
entries.summaryMd: The subset of mission essential services required to conduct manufacturing operations. Function or capability that is required to maintain health, safety, the environment and availability for the equipment under control.

senses.definitionMd: The subset of mission essential services required to conduct manufacturing operations. Function or capability that is required to maintain health, safety, the environment and availability for the equipment under control.

entries.title: critical software
entries.summaryMd: Any software that has, or has direct software dependencies upon, one or more components with at least one of these attributes: · is designed to run with elevated privilege or manage privileges; · has direct or privileged access to networking or computing resources; · is designed to control access to data or operational technology; · performs a function critical to trust; or, · operates outside of normal trust boundaries with privileged access.

senses.definitionMd: Any software that has, or has direct software dependencies upon, one or more components with at least one of these attributes: · is designed to run with elevated privilege or manage privileges; · has direct or privileged access to networking or computing resources; · is designed to control access to data or operational technology; · performs a function critical to trust; or, · operates outside of normal trust boundaries with privileged access.

entries.title: Critical Value
entries.summaryMd: The value that is exceeded by the test statistic with a small probability (significance level). A "look-up" or calculated value of a test statistic (i.e., a test statistic value) that, by construction, has a small probability of

senses.definitionMd: The value that is exceeded by the test statistic with a small probability (significance level). A "look-up" or calculated value of a test statistic (i.e., a test statistic value) that, by construction, has a small probability of

entries.title: criticality
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the degree to which an organization depends on the information or information system for the success of a mission or of a business function.

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the degree to which an organization depends on the information or information system for the success of a mission or of a business function.

entries.title: criticality analysis
entries.summaryMd: An end-to-end functional decomposition performed by systems engineers to identify mission critical functions and components. Includes identification of system missions, decomposition into the functions to perform those missions, and traceability to the hardware, software, and firmware components that implement those functions. Criticality is assessed in terms of the impact of function or component failure on the ability of the component to complete the system missions(s).

senses.definitionMd: An end-to-end functional decomposition performed by systems engineers to identify mission critical functions and components. Includes identification of system missions, decomposition into the functions to perform those missions, and traceability to the hardware, software, and firmware components that implement those functions. Criticality is assessed in terms of the impact of function or component failure on the ability of the component to complete the system missions(s).

entries.title: criticality level
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the degree to which an organization depends on the information or information system for the success of a mission or of a business function.

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the degree to which an organization depends on the information or information system for the success of a mission or of a business function.

entries.title: Criticality Reviews
entries.summaryMd: A determination of the ranking and priority of manufacturing system components, services, processes, and inputs in order to establish operational thresholds and recovery objectives.

senses.definitionMd: A determination of the ranking and priority of manufacturing system components, services, processes, and inputs in order to establish operational thresholds and recovery objectives.

entries.title: cross certificate
entries.summaryMd: A certificate issued from a certificate authority (CA) that signs the public key of another CA not within its trust hierarchy that establishes a trust relationship between the two CAs.

senses.definitionMd: A certificate issued from a certificate authority (CA) that signs the public key of another CA not within its trust hierarchy that establishes a trust relationship between the two CAs.

entries.title: Cross-certification
entries.summaryMd: A process whereby two CAs establish a trust relationship between them by each CA signing a certificate containing the public key of the other CA.

senses.definitionMd: A process whereby two CAs establish a trust relationship between them by each CA signing a certificate containing the public key of the other CA.

entries.title: Cross-certify
entries.summaryMd: The establishment of a trust relationship between two Certification Authorities (CAs) through the signing of each other's public key in certificates; referred to as a “cross-certificate.”

senses.definitionMd: The establishment of a trust relationship between two Certification Authorities (CAs) through the signing of each other's public key in certificates; referred to as a “cross-certificate.”

entries.title: cross domain
entries.summaryMd: The act of manually and/or automatically accessing and/or transferring information between different security domains.

senses.definitionMd: The act of manually and/or automatically accessing and/or transferring information between different security domains.

entries.title: cross domain baseline list
entries.summaryMd: A list managed by the unified cross domain services management office (UCDSMO) that identifies CDSs that are available for deployment within the Department of Defense (DoD) and intelligence community (IC).

senses.definitionMd: A list managed by the unified cross domain services management office (UCDSMO) that identifies CDSs that are available for deployment within the Department of Defense (DoD) and intelligence community (IC).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "cross domain baseline list"

entries.title: cross domain capabilities
entries.summaryMd: The set of functions that enable the transfer of information between security domains in accordance with the policies of the security domains involved.

senses.definitionMd: The set of functions that enable the transfer of information between security domains in accordance with the policies of the security domains involved.

entries.title: cross domain enabled
entries.summaryMd: Applications/services that exist on and are capable of interacting across two or more different security domains.

senses.definitionMd: Applications/services that exist on and are capable of interacting across two or more different security domains.

entries.title: cross domain portal
entries.summaryMd: A single web-site providing access to cross domain services.

senses.definitionMd: A single web-site providing access to cross domain services.

entries.title: cross domain service
entries.summaryMd: An IT service that provides that provides access or transfer of information solutions between different security domains.

senses.definitionMd: An IT service that provides that provides access or transfer of information solutions between different security domains.

entries.title: cross domain solution (CDS)
entries.summaryMd: A form of controlled interface that provides the ability to manually and/or automatically access and transfer information between different security domains. A CDS may consist of one or more devices.

senses.definitionMd: A form of controlled interface that provides the ability to manually and/or automatically access and transfer information between different security domains. A CDS may consist of one or more devices.

entries.title: cross domain solution (CDS) filtering
entries.summaryMd: The process of inspecting data as it traverses a cross domain solution and determines if the data meets pre-defined policy.

senses.definitionMd: The process of inspecting data as it traverses a cross domain solution and determines if the data meets pre-defined policy.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "cross domain solution (CDS) filtering"

entries.title: cross domain sunset list
entries.summaryMd: A list managed by the unified cross domain services management office (UCDSMO) that identifies cross domain solutions (CDSs) that are or have been in operation, but are no longer available for additional deployment and need to be replaced within a specified period of time.

senses.definitionMd: A list managed by the unified cross domain services management office (UCDSMO) that identifies cross domain solutions (CDSs) that are or have been in operation, but are no longer available for additional deployment and need to be replaced within a specified period of time.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "cross domain sunset list"

entries.title: crosslinks
entries.summaryMd: Communication between satellites.

senses.definitionMd: Communication between satellites.

entries.title: cryptanalysis
entries.summaryMd: 2. The study of mathematical techniques for attempting to defeat cryptographic techniques and/or information systems security. This includes the process of looking for errors or weaknesses in the implementation of an algorithm or of the algorithm itself.

senses.definitionMd: 2. The study of mathematical techniques for attempting to defeat cryptographic techniques and/or information systems security. This includes the process of looking for errors or weaknesses in the implementation of an algorithm or of the algorithm itself.

entries.title: cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer
entries.summaryMd: A device capable of using quantum algorithms to break a cryptosystem that is secure against classical (i.e., non-quantum) computers.

senses.definitionMd: A device capable of using quantum algorithms to break a cryptosystem that is secure against classical (i.e., non-quantum) computers.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer"

entries.title: crypto agility
entries.summaryMd: The capabilities needed to replace and adapt cryptographic algorithms in protocols, applications, software, hardware, firmware, and infrastructures while preserving security and ongoing operations.

senses.definitionMd: The capabilities needed to replace and adapt cryptographic algorithms in protocols, applications, software, hardware, firmware, and infrastructures while preserving security and ongoing operations.

entries.title: crypto agility for a communication protocol
entries.summaryMd: The ability to maintain interoperability when introducing new cryptographic algorithms and preventing the use of vulnerable algorithms.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to maintain interoperability when introducing new cryptographic algorithms and preventing the use of vulnerable algorithms.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "crypto agility for a communication protocol"

entries.title: crypto agility for a computing system
entries.summaryMd: The ability to adopt new cryptographic algorithms and stop the use of vulnerable algorithms in applications without disrupting the running system.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to adopt new cryptographic algorithms and stop the use of vulnerable algorithms in applications without disrupting the running system.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "crypto agility for a computing system"

entries.title: crypto agility for an enterprise
entries.summaryMd: A capacity to seamlessly and rapidly transition away from vulnerable cryptographic algorithms and adopt new, stronger ones without incurring significant changes to their infrastructure or experiencing unnecessary disruptions.

senses.definitionMd: A capacity to seamlessly and rapidly transition away from vulnerable cryptographic algorithms and adopt new, stronger ones without incurring significant changes to their infrastructure or experiencing unnecessary disruptions.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "crypto agility for an enterprise"

entries.title: Cryptocurrency
entries.summaryMd: A digital asset/credit/unit within the system, which is cryptographically sent from one blockchain network user to another. In the case of cryptocurrency creation (such as the reward for mining), the publishing node includes a transaction sending the newly created cryptocurrency to one or more blockchain network users. These assets are transferred from one user to another by using digital signatures with asymmetric-key pairs.

senses.definitionMd: A digital asset/credit/unit within the system, which is cryptographically sent from one blockchain network user to another. In the case of cryptocurrency creation (such as the reward for mining), the publishing node includes a transaction sending the newly created cryptocurrency to one or more blockchain network users. These assets are transferred from one user to another by using digital signatures with asymmetric-key pairs.

entries.title: cryptographic
entries.summaryMd: Pertaining to, or concerned with, cryptography.

senses.definitionMd: Pertaining to, or concerned with, cryptography.

entries.title: Cryptographic Accelerator
entries.summaryMd: A specialized separate coprocessor chip from the main processing unit where cryptographic tasks are offloaded to for performance benefits.

senses.definitionMd: A specialized separate coprocessor chip from the main processing unit where cryptographic tasks are offloaded to for performance benefits.

entries.title: cryptographic alarm
entries.summaryMd: Circuit or device that detects failures or aberrations in the logic or operation of cryptographic equipment. Crypto-alarm may inhibit transmission or may provide a visible and/or audible alarm.

senses.definitionMd: Circuit or device that detects failures or aberrations in the logic or operation of cryptographic equipment. Crypto-alarm may inhibit transmission or may provide a visible and/or audible alarm.

entries.title: Cryptographic algorithm
entries.summaryMd: 1. A well-defined computational procedure that takes variable inputs, including a cryptographic key, and produces an output.

senses.definitionMd: 1. A well-defined computational procedure that takes variable inputs, including a cryptographic key, and produces an output.

entries.title: cryptographic ancillary equipment (crypto-ancillary equipment)
entries.summaryMd: Equipment designed specifically to facilitate efficient or reliable operation of cryptographic equipment, but which does not itself perform cryptographic functions.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment designed specifically to facilitate efficient or reliable operation of cryptographic equipment, but which does not itself perform cryptographic functions.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "cryptographic ancillary equipment (crypto-ancillary equipment)"

entries.title: Cryptographic API: Next Generation
entries.summaryMd: The long-term replacement for the Cryptographic Application Programming Interface (CAPI).

senses.definitionMd: The long-term replacement for the Cryptographic Application Programming Interface (CAPI).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Cryptographic API: Next Generation"

entries.title: Cryptographic application
entries.summaryMd: An application that performs a cryptographic function.

senses.definitionMd: An application that performs a cryptographic function.

entries.title: Cryptographic Application Programming Interface
entries.summaryMd: An application programming interface included with Microsoft Windows operating systems that provides services to enable developers to secure Windows-based applications using cryptography. While providing a consistent API for applications, API allows for specialized cryptographic modules (cryptographic service providers) to be provided by third parties, such as hardware security module (HSM) manufacturers. This enables applications to leverage the additional security of HSMs while using the same APIs they use to access built-in Windows cryptographic service providers. (Also known variously as CryptoAPI, Microsoft Cryptography API, MS-CAPI or simply CAPI)

senses.definitionMd: An application programming interface included with Microsoft Windows operating systems that provides services to enable developers to secure Windows-based applications using cryptography. While providing a consistent API for applications, API allows for specialized cryptographic modules (cryptographic service providers) to be provided by third parties, such as hardware security module (HSM) manufacturers. This enables applications to leverage the additional security of HSMs while using the same APIs they use to access built-in Windows cryptographic service providers. (Also known variously as CryptoAPI, Microsoft Cryptography API, MS-CAPI or simply CAPI)

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Cryptographic Application Programming Interface"

entries.title: cryptographic binding
entries.summaryMd: Associating two or more related elements of information using cryptographic techniques.

senses.definitionMd: Associating two or more related elements of information using cryptographic techniques.

entries.title: cryptographic boundary
entries.summaryMd: Explicitly defined continuous perimeter that establishes the physical and/or logical bounds of a cryptographic module and contains all the hardware, software, and/or firmware components of a cryptographic module.

senses.definitionMd: Explicitly defined continuous perimeter that establishes the physical and/or logical bounds of a cryptographic module and contains all the hardware, software, and/or firmware components of a cryptographic module.

entries.title: Cryptographic checksum
entries.summaryMd: A mathematical value created using a cryptographic algorithm that is assigned to data and later used to test the data to verify that the data has not changed.

senses.definitionMd: A mathematical value created using a cryptographic algorithm that is assigned to data and later used to test the data to verify that the data has not changed.

entries.title: cryptographic component
entries.summaryMd: The hardware or firmware embodiment of the cryptographic logic in a secure telecommunications or automated information processing system. A cryptographic component may be a modular assembly, a printed wiring assembly (PWA), a microcircuit, or a combination of these items.

senses.definitionMd: The hardware or firmware embodiment of the cryptographic logic in a secure telecommunications or automated information processing system. A cryptographic component may be a modular assembly, a printed wiring assembly (PWA), a microcircuit, or a combination of these items.

entries.title: Cryptographic device
entries.summaryMd: A physical device that performs a cryptographic function (e.g., random number generation, message authentication, digital signature generation, encryption, or key establishment). A cryptographic device must employ one or more cryptographic modules for cryptographic operations. The device may also be composed from other applications and components in addition to the cryptographic module(s). A cryptographic device may be a stand-alone cryptographic mechanism or a CKMS component.

senses.definitionMd: A physical device that performs a cryptographic function (e.g., random number generation, message authentication, digital signature generation, encryption, or key establishment). A cryptographic device must employ one or more cryptographic modules for cryptographic operations. The device may also be composed from other applications and components in addition to the cryptographic module(s). A cryptographic device may be a stand-alone cryptographic mechanism or a CKMS component.

entries.title: cryptographic equipment (cryptoequipment)
entries.summaryMd: Equipment that embodies a cryptographic logic.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment that embodies a cryptographic logic.

entries.title: cryptographic erase
entries.summaryMd: A method of sanitization in which the media encryption key (MEK) for the encrypted Target Data is sanitized, making recovery of the decrypted Target Data infeasible.

senses.definitionMd: A method of sanitization in which the media encryption key (MEK) for the encrypted Target Data is sanitized, making recovery of the decrypted Target Data infeasible.

entries.title: Cryptographic function
entries.summaryMd: Cryptographic algorithms, together with modes of operation (if appropriate); for example, block ciphers, digital signature algorithms, asymmetric key-establishment algorithms, message authentication codes, hash functions, or random bit generators.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptographic algorithms, together with modes of operation (if appropriate); for example, block ciphers, digital signature algorithms, asymmetric key-establishment algorithms, message authentication codes, hash functions, or random bit generators.

entries.title: Cryptographic hash function
entries.summaryMd: A function on bit strings in which the length of the output is fixed. Approved hash functions (such as those specified in FIPS 180 and FIPS 202) are designed to satisfy the following properties:1. (One-way) It is computationally infeasible to find any input that maps to any new pre-specified output2. (Collision-resistant) It is computationally infeasible to find any two distinct inputs that map to the same output.

senses.definitionMd: A function on bit strings in which the length of the output is fixed. Approved hash functions (such as those specified in FIPS 180 and FIPS 202) are designed to satisfy the following properties:1. (One-way) It is computationally infeasible to find any input that maps to any new pre-specified output2. (Collision-resistant) It is computationally infeasible to find any two distinct inputs that map to the same output.

entries.title: Cryptographic Hash Value
entries.summaryMd: The result of applying a cryptographic hash function to data (e.g., a message).

senses.definitionMd: The result of applying a cryptographic hash function to data (e.g., a message).

entries.title: cryptographic high value product (CHVP)
entries.summaryMd: NSA-approved products incorporating only UNCLASSIFIED components and UNCLASSIFIED cryptographic algorithms. This includes COTS products approved by NSA, but does not include Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) or their components, unless an individual component has been approved as a CHVP. Unkeyed CHVPs are not classified or designated as Controlled Cryptographic Items (CCI).

senses.definitionMd: NSA-approved products incorporating only UNCLASSIFIED components and UNCLASSIFIED cryptographic algorithms. This includes COTS products approved by NSA, but does not include Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) or their components, unless an individual component has been approved as a CHVP. Unkeyed CHVPs are not classified or designated as Controlled Cryptographic Items (CCI).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "cryptographic high value product (CHVP)"

entries.title: Cryptographic Ignition Key
entries.summaryMd: Device or electronic key used to unlock the secure mode of cryptographic equipment.

senses.definitionMd: Device or electronic key used to unlock the secure mode of cryptographic equipment.

entries.title: cryptographic incident
entries.summaryMd: Any uninvestigated or unevaluated equipment malfunction or operator or COMSEC Account Manager error that has the potential to jeopardize the cryptographic security of a machine, off-line manual cryptosystem OR any investigated or evaluated occurrence that has been determined as not jeopardizing the cryptographic security of a cryptosystem.

senses.definitionMd: Any uninvestigated or unevaluated equipment malfunction or operator or COMSEC Account Manager error that has the potential to jeopardize the cryptographic security of a machine, off-line manual cryptosystem OR any investigated or evaluated occurrence that has been determined as not jeopardizing the cryptographic security of a cryptosystem.

entries.title: cryptographic initialization
entries.summaryMd: Function used to set the state of a cryptographic logic prior to key generation, encryption, or other operating mode.

senses.definitionMd: Function used to set the state of a cryptographic logic prior to key generation, encryption, or other operating mode.

entries.title: cryptographic key
entries.summaryMd: A parameter used in conjunction with a cryptographic algorithm that determines its operation. Examples applicable to this Standard include: 1. The computation of a digital signature from data, and 2. The verification of a digital signature.

senses.definitionMd: A parameter used in conjunction with a cryptographic algorithm that determines its operation. Examples applicable to this Standard include: 1. The computation of a digital signature from data, and 2. The verification of a digital signature.

entries.title: Cryptographic key component
entries.summaryMd: One of at least two parameters that have the same security properties (e.g., randomness) as a cryptographic key; parameters are combined using an approved cryptographic function to form a plaintext cryptographic key before use.

senses.definitionMd: One of at least two parameters that have the same security properties (e.g., randomness) as a cryptographic key; parameters are combined using an approved cryptographic function to form a plaintext cryptographic key before use.

entries.title: Cryptographic keying relationship
entries.summaryMd: Two or more entities share the same symmetric key.

senses.definitionMd: Two or more entities share the same symmetric key.

entries.title: cryptographic logic
entries.summaryMd: A comprehensive and precisely defined sequence of steps or procedural rules used to produce cipher text from plain text and vice versa.

senses.definitionMd: A comprehensive and precisely defined sequence of steps or procedural rules used to produce cipher text from plain text and vice versa.

entries.title: cryptographic material (cryptomaterial)
entries.summaryMd: All material, including documents, devices, or equipment that contains cryptographic information and is essential to the encryption, decryption, or authentication of telecommunications.

senses.definitionMd: All material, including documents, devices, or equipment that contains cryptographic information and is essential to the encryption, decryption, or authentication of telecommunications.

entries.title: Cryptographic mechanism
entries.summaryMd: An element of a cryptographic application, process, module or device that provides a cryptographic service, such as confidentiality, integrity, source authentication, and access control (e.g., encryption and decryption, and digital signature generation and verification).

senses.definitionMd: An element of a cryptographic application, process, module or device that provides a cryptographic service, such as confidentiality, integrity, source authentication, and access control (e.g., encryption and decryption, and digital signature generation and verification).

entries.title: Cryptographic module
entries.summaryMd: See Cryptographic module.

senses.definitionMd: See Cryptographic module.

entries.title: Cryptographic Module Security Policy
entries.summaryMd: A specification of the security rules under which a cryptographic module is designed to operate.

senses.definitionMd: A specification of the security rules under which a cryptographic module is designed to operate.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Cryptographic Module Security Policy"

entries.title: cryptographic net (cryptonet)
entries.summaryMd: Stations that hold a common key. This may include multiple communications networks.

senses.definitionMd: Stations that hold a common key. This may include multiple communications networks.

entries.title: Cryptographic officer
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for and authorized to initialize and manage all cryptographic services, functions, and keys of the FCKMS.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for and authorized to initialize and manage all cryptographic services, functions, and keys of the FCKMS.

entries.title: Cryptographic operation
entries.summaryMd: The execution of a cryptographic algorithm. Cryptographic operations are performed in cryptographic modules.

senses.definitionMd: The execution of a cryptographic algorithm. Cryptographic operations are performed in cryptographic modules.

entries.title: cryptographic period (cryptoperiod)
entries.summaryMd: Time span during which each key setting remains in effect.

senses.definitionMd: Time span during which each key setting remains in effect.

entries.title: Cryptographic primitive
entries.summaryMd: A low-level cryptographic algorithm used as a basic building block for higher-level cryptographic algorithms.

senses.definitionMd: A low-level cryptographic algorithm used as a basic building block for higher-level cryptographic algorithms.

entries.title: cryptographic product
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key (public, private, or shared) or public key certificate, used for encryption, decryption, digital signature, or signature verification; and other items, such as compromised key lists (CKL) and certificate revocation lists (CRL), obtained by trusted means from the same source which validate the authenticity of keys or certificates. Protected software which generates or regenerates keys or certificates may also be considered a cryptographic product.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key (public, private, or shared) or public key certificate, used for encryption, decryption, digital signature, or signature verification; and other items, such as compromised key lists (CKL) and certificate revocation lists (CRL), obtained by trusted means from the same source which validate the authenticity of keys or certificates. Protected software which generates or regenerates keys or certificates may also be considered a cryptographic product.

entries.title: cryptographic randomization
entries.summaryMd: Function that randomly determines the transmit state of a cryptographic logic.

senses.definitionMd: Function that randomly determines the transmit state of a cryptographic logic.

entries.title: cryptographic security (cryptosecurity)
entries.summaryMd: The security or protection resulting from the proper use of technically sound cryptosystems.

senses.definitionMd: The security or protection resulting from the proper use of technically sound cryptosystems.

entries.title: Cryptographic service
entries.summaryMd: A service that provides confidentiality, integrity, source authentication, entity authentication, non-repudiation support, access control and availability (e.g., encryption and decryption, and digital signature generation and verification).

senses.definitionMd: A service that provides confidentiality, integrity, source authentication, entity authentication, non-repudiation support, access control and availability (e.g., encryption and decryption, and digital signature generation and verification).

entries.title: cryptographic solution
entries.summaryMd: The generic term for a cryptographic device, COMSEC equipment, or combination of such devices/equipment containing either a classified algorithm or an unclassified algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: The generic term for a cryptographic device, COMSEC equipment, or combination of such devices/equipment containing either a classified algorithm or an unclassified algorithm.

entries.title: cryptographic synchronization
entries.summaryMd: Process by which a receiving decrypting cryptographic logic attains the same internal state as the transmitting encrypting logic.

senses.definitionMd: Process by which a receiving decrypting cryptographic logic attains the same internal state as the transmitting encrypting logic.

entries.title: cryptographic system analysis
entries.summaryMd: Process of establishing the exploitability of a cryptographic system, normally by reviewing transmitted traffic protected or secured by the system under study.

senses.definitionMd: Process of establishing the exploitability of a cryptographic system, normally by reviewing transmitted traffic protected or secured by the system under study.

entries.title: cryptographic system (cryptosystem)
entries.summaryMd: Associated CS items interacting to provide a single means of encryption or decryption.

senses.definitionMd: Associated CS items interacting to provide a single means of encryption or decryption.

entries.title: cryptographic system evaluation
entries.summaryMd: Process of determining vulnerabilities of a cryptographic system and recommending countermeasures.

senses.definitionMd: Process of determining vulnerabilities of a cryptographic system and recommending countermeasures.

entries.title: cryptographic system review
entries.summaryMd: Examination of a cryptographic system by the controlling authority ensuring its adequacy of design and content, continued need, and proper distribution.

senses.definitionMd: Examination of a cryptographic system by the controlling authority ensuring its adequacy of design and content, continued need, and proper distribution.

entries.title: cryptographic system survey
entries.summaryMd: Management technique in which actual holders of a cryptographic system express opinions on the system's suitability and provide usage information for technical evaluations.

senses.definitionMd: Management technique in which actual holders of a cryptographic system express opinions on the system's suitability and provide usage information for technical evaluations.

entries.title: cryptographic token
entries.summaryMd: 2. A token where the secret is a cryptographic key.

senses.definitionMd: 2. A token where the secret is a cryptographic key.

entries.title: cryptography
entries.summaryMd: The discipline that embodies the principles, means, and methods for the transformation of data in order to hide their semantic content, prevent their unauthorized use, or prevent their undetected modification.

senses.definitionMd: The discipline that embodies the principles, means, and methods for the transformation of data in order to hide their semantic content, prevent their unauthorized use, or prevent their undetected modification.

entries.title: cryptologic
entries.summaryMd: The term 'cryptologic' means of or pertaining to cryptology.

senses.definitionMd: The term 'cryptologic' means of or pertaining to cryptology.

entries.title: cryptology
entries.summaryMd: Originally the field encompassing both cryptography and cryptanalysis. Today, cryptology in the U.S. Government is the collection and/or exploitation of foreign communications and non- communications emitters, known as SIGINT; and solutions, products, and services, to ensure the availability, integrity, authentication, confidentiality, and non-repudiation of national security telecommunications and information systems, known as IA.

senses.definitionMd: Originally the field encompassing both cryptography and cryptanalysis. Today, cryptology in the U.S. Government is the collection and/or exploitation of foreign communications and non- communications emitters, known as SIGINT; and solutions, products, and services, to ensure the availability, integrity, authentication, confidentiality, and non-repudiation of national security telecommunications and information systems, known as IA.

entries.title: cryptonet evaluation report
entries.summaryMd: A free form message from the electronic key management system (EKMS) Tier 1 that includes the Controlling Authority’s ID and Name, Keying Material Information, Description/Cryptonet Name, Remarks, and Authorized User Information.

senses.definitionMd: A free form message from the electronic key management system (EKMS) Tier 1 that includes the Controlling Authority’s ID and Name, Keying Material Information, Description/Cryptonet Name, Remarks, and Authorized User Information.

entries.title: Cryptoperiod
entries.summaryMd: The time span during which a specific key is authorized for use or in which the keys for a given system or application may remain in effect.

senses.definitionMd: The time span during which a specific key is authorized for use or in which the keys for a given system or application may remain in effect.

entries.title: CSF Category
entries.summaryMd: A group of related cybersecurity outcomes that collectively comprise a CSF Function.

senses.definitionMd: A group of related cybersecurity outcomes that collectively comprise a CSF Function.

entries.title: CSF Community Profile
entries.summaryMd: A baseline of CSF outcomes that is created and published to address shared interests and goals among a number of organizations. A Community Profile is typically developed for a particular sector, subsector, technology, threat type, or other use case. An organization can use a Community Profile as the basis for its own Target Profile.

senses.definitionMd: A baseline of CSF outcomes that is created and published to address shared interests and goals among a number of organizations. A Community Profile is typically developed for a particular sector, subsector, technology, threat type, or other use case. An organization can use a Community Profile as the basis for its own Target Profile.

entries.title: CSF Core
entries.summaryMd: A taxonomy of high-level cybersecurity outcomes that can help any organization manage its cybersecurity risks. Its components are a hierarchy of Functions, Categories, and Subcategories that detail each outcome.

senses.definitionMd: A taxonomy of high-level cybersecurity outcomes that can help any organization manage its cybersecurity risks. Its components are a hierarchy of Functions, Categories, and Subcategories that detail each outcome.

entries.title: CSF Current Profile
entries.summaryMd: A part of an Organizational Profile that specifies the Core outcomes that an organization is currently achieving (or attempting to achieve) and characterizes how or to what extent each outcome is being achieved.

senses.definitionMd: A part of an Organizational Profile that specifies the Core outcomes that an organization is currently achieving (or attempting to achieve) and characterizes how or to what extent each outcome is being achieved.

entries.title: CSF Function

entries.title: cyberspace

entries.title: data asset
entries.summaryMd: 1. Any entity that is comprised of data. For example, a database is a data asset that is comprised of data records. A data asset may be a system or application output file, database, document, or web page. A data asset also includes a service that may be provided to access data from an application. For example, a service that returns individual records from a database would be a data asset. Similarly, a web site that returns data in response to specific queries (e.g., www.weather.com) would be a data asset.

senses.definitionMd: 1. Any entity that is comprised of data. For example, a database is a data asset that is comprised of data records. For example, a service that returns individual records from a database would be a data asset. entries.title: delay (path delay)
entries.summaryMd: The [signal] delay between a transmitter and a receiver. Path delay is often the largest contributor to time transfer uncertainty. For example, consider a radio signal broadcast over a 1000 km path. Since radio signals travel at the speed of light (with a delay of about 3.3 µs/km), we can calibrate the 1000 km path by estimating the path delay as 3.3 ms and applying a 3.3 ms correction to our measurement. Sophisticated time transfer systems, such as GPS, automatically correct for path delay. The absolute path delay is not important to frequency transfer systems because on-time pulses are not required, but variations in path delay still limit the frequency uncertainty.

entries.summaryMd: An attribute associated with an assessment method that addresses the rigor and level of detail associated with the application of the method. The values for the depth attribute, hierarchically from less depth to more depth, are basic, focused, and comprehensive.

senses.definitionMd: An attribute associated with an assessment method that addresses the rigor and level of detail associated with the application of the method. The values for the depth attribute, hierarchically from less depth to more depth, are basic, focused, and comprehensive.

entries.title: derived attribute value
entries.summaryMd: A statement that asserts a limited identity attribute of a subscriber without containing the attribute value from which it is derived, independent of format. For example, instead of requesting the attribute “birthday,” a derived value could be “older than 18.” Instead of requesting the attribute for “physical address,” a derived value could be “currently residing in this district.” Previous versions of these guidelines referred to this construct as an “attribute reference.”
