entries.title: derived credential
entries.summaryMd: A credential issued based on proof of possession and control of a token associated with a previously issued credential, so as not to duplicate the identity proofing process.

senses.definitionMd: A credential issued based on proof of possession and control of a token associated with a previously issued credential, so as not to duplicate the identity proofing process.

entries.title: Derived Personal Identity Verification (PIV)
entries.summaryMd: A credential issued based on proof of possession and control of the PIV Card, so as not to duplicate the identity proofing process as defined in [SP 800-63-2]. A Derived PIV Credential token is a hardware or software-based token that contains the Derived PIV Credential.

senses.definitionMd: A credential issued based on proof of possession and control of the PIV Card, so as not to duplicate the identity proofing process as defined in [SP 800-63-2]. A Derived PIV Credential token is a hardware or software-based token that contains the Derived PIV Credential.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Derived Personal Identity Verification (PIV)"

entries.title: Derived PIV Application
entries.summaryMd: A standardized application residing on a removable, hardware cryptographic token that hosts a Derived PIV Credential and associated mandatory and optional elements.

senses.definitionMd: A standardized application residing on a removable, hardware cryptographic token that hosts a Derived PIV Credential and associated mandatory and optional elements.

entries.title: Derived PIV Credential
entries.summaryMd: A credential issued based on proof of possession and control of a PIV Card. Derived PIV credentials are typically used in situations that do not easily accommodate a PIV Card, such as in conjunction with mobile devices.

senses.definitionMd: A credential issued based on proof of possession and control of a PIV Card. Derived PIV credentials are typically used in situations that do not easily accommodate a PIV Card, such as in conjunction with mobile devices.

entries.title: Derived PIV Credential Issuer
entries.summaryMd: Derived PIV Credential (and associated token) Issuer; an issuer of Derived PIV Credentials as defined in [NIST SP 800-63-2]and [NIST SP 800-157].

senses.definitionMd: Derived PIV Credential (and associated token) Issuer; an issuer of Derived PIV Credentials as defined in [NIST SP 800-63-2]and [NIST SP 800-157].

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Derived PIV Credential Issuer"

entries.title: Derived Relationship Mapping
entries.summaryMd: A potential mapping between Reference Document Elements identified by finding elements from two or more Reference Documents that map to the same Focal Document Element.

senses.definitionMd: A potential mapping between Reference Document Elements identified by finding elements from two or more Reference Documents that map to the same Focal Document Element.

entries.title: derived requirement
entries.summaryMd: A requirement that is implied or transformed from a higher-level requirement. Note 1: Implied requirements cannot be assessed since they are not contained in any requirement baseline. The decomposition of requirements throughout the engineering process makes the implicit requirements explicit, allowing them to be stated and captured in appropriate baselines and allowing associated assessment criteria to be stated. Note 2: A derived requirement must trace back to at least one higher-level requirement.

entries.title: Derived Test Requirement
entries.summaryMd: A statement of requirement, needed information, and associated test procedures necessary to test a specific SCAP feature.

senses.definitionMd: A statement of requirement, needed information, and associated test procedures necessary to test a specific SCAP feature.

entries.title: descriptive label
entries.summaryMd: Provides facts about properties or features of a product without any grading or evaluation. Information may be displayed in a variety of ways, such as in tabular format or with icons or text.

senses.definitionMd: Provides facts about properties or features of a product without any grading or evaluation. Information may be displayed in a variety of ways, such as in tabular format or with icons or text.

entries.title: design
entries.summaryMd: Process to define the architecture, system elements, interfaces, and other characteristics of a system or system element.

senses.definitionMd: Process to define the architecture, system elements, interfaces, and other characteristics of a system or system element.

entries.title: design characteristics
entries.summaryMd: Design attributes or distinguishing features that pertain to a measurable description of a product or service.

senses.definitionMd: Design attributes or distinguishing features that pertain to a measurable description of a product or service.

entries.title: design margin
entries.summaryMd: The margin allocated during design based on assessments of uncertainty and unknowns. This margin is often consumed as the design matures.

senses.definitionMd: The margin allocated during design based on assessments of uncertainty and unknowns. This margin is often consumed as the design matures.

entries.title: design principle
entries.summaryMd: A distillation of experience designing, implementing, integrating, and upgrading systems that systems engineers and architects can use to guide design decisions and analysis. A design principle typically takes the form of a terse statement or a phrase identifying a key concept, accompanied by one or more statements that describe how that concept applies to system design (where “system” is construed broadly to include operational processes and procedures, and may also include development and maintenance environments).

entries.title: Designated Accrediting Authority
entries.summaryMd: Synonymous with designated accrediting authority (DAA).

senses.definitionMd: Synonymous with designated accrediting authority (DAA).

entries.title: designated approval authority (DAA)
entries.summaryMd: Official with the authority to formally assume responsibility for operating a system at an acceptable level of risk. This term is synonymous with authorizing official, designated accrediting authority, and delegated accrediting authority. Rationale: Term has been replaced by the term “authorizing official”.

entries.title: designated cipher function
entries.summaryMd: As part of the choice of the underlying block cipher with a KEK, either the forward transformation or the inverse transformation.

senses.definitionMd: As part of the choice of the underlying block cipher with a KEK, either the forward transformation or the inverse transformation.

entries.title: Desired State

senses.definitionMd: See Desired State Specification.

entries.title: Desired State Specification
entries.summaryMd: See Desired State Specification.

entries.title: destroy
entries.summaryMd: An action applied to a key or a piece of secret data. After a key or a piece of secret data is destroyed, no information about its value can be recovered.

senses.definitionMd: An action applied to a key or a piece of secret data. After a key or a piece of secret data is destroyed, no information about its value can be recovered.

entries.title: Destroyed state
entries.summaryMd: A lifecycle state of a key whereby the key is no longer available and cannot be reconstructed.

senses.definitionMd: A lifecycle state of a key whereby the key is no longer available and cannot be reconstructed.

entries.title: Destruction
entries.summaryMd: The process of overwriting, erasing, or physically destroying information (e.g., a cryptographic key) so that it cannot be recovered. See NIST SP 800-88.

senses.definitionMd: The process of overwriting, erasing, or physically destroying information (e.g., a cryptographic key) so that it cannot be recovered. See NIST SP 800-88.

entries.title: detailed assessment
entries.summaryMd: An assessment that contains all the elements (critical and non-critical) for a given breadth.

senses.definitionMd: An assessment that contains all the elements (critical and non-critical) for a given breadth.

entries.title: detect (CSF function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop and implement the appropriate activities to identify the occurrence of a cybersecurity event.

senses.definitionMd: Develop and implement the appropriate activities to identify the occurrence of a cybersecurity event.

entries.title: Deterministic Algorithm
entries.summaryMd: An algorithm that, given the same inputs, always produces the same outputs.

senses.definitionMd: An algorithm that, given the same inputs, always produces the same outputs.

entries.title: developer
entries.summaryMd: A general term that includes: (i) developers or manufacturers of information systems, system components, or information system services; (ii) systems integrators; (iii) vendors; (iv) and product resellers. Development of systems, components, or services can occur internally within organizations (i.e., in-house development) or through external entities.

entries.title: Development Operations (DevOps)
entries.summaryMd: A set of practices for automating the processes between software development and information technology operations teams so that they can build, test, and release software faster and more reliably. The goal is to shorten the systems development life cycle and improve reliability while delivering features, fixes, and updates frequently in close alignment with business objectives.

entries.title: Device
entries.summaryMd: A combination of components that function together to serve a specific purpose.

senses.definitionMd: A combination of components that function together to serve a specific purpose.

entries.title: device birth certificate
entries.summaryMd: Credentials that a device needs in order to establish communications with and be authenticated by the network onboarding component. Device bootstrapping credentials are typically installed on the device during manufacturing, and they must already be on the device before it initiates the network-layer onboarding process. The device bootstrapping credentials are authoritative credentials that are unique to the device and independent of context; they are sometimes referred to as the device birth certificate. The device bootstrapping credentials always include some sort of secret (e.g., a private or secret pre-shared key), which the device will use to authenticate itself to the network onboarding component and to establish a secure communications channel with the network onboarding component.

entries.title: device bootstrapping credentials
entries.summaryMd: Credentials that a device needs in order to establish communications with and be authenticated by the network onboarding component. entries.title: Device Cybersecurity Capability
entries.summaryMd: Cybersecurity features or functions that computing devices provide through their own technical means (i.e., device hardware and software).

senses.definitionMd: Cybersecurity features or functions that computing devices provide through their own technical means (i.e., device hardware and software).

entries.summaryMd: See core baseline.

senses.definitionMd: See core baseline.

entries.title: device distribution profile
entries.summaryMd: An approval-based access control list (ACL) for a specific product that 1) names the user devices in a specific KMI operating account (KOA) to which primary services nodes (PRSNs) distribute the product and 2) states conditions of distribution for each device.

entries.title: Device Identifier
entries.summaryMd: A context-unique value—a value unique within a specific context—that is associated with a device (for example, a string consisting of a network address).

senses.definitionMd: A context-unique value—a value unique within a specific context—that is associated with a device (for example, a string consisting of a network address).

entries.title: device information declaration
entries.summaryMd: A trusted digital assertion with information about the IoT device, such as the identity or certificate of the device owner and possibly the identities or certificates of any other entities that the device owner has authorized to onboard the device on its behalf.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted digital assertion with information about the IoT device, such as the identity or certificate of the device owner and possibly the identities or certificates of any other entities that the device owner has authorized to onboard the device on its behalf.

entries.title: device onboarder
entries.summaryMd: The person or a proxy that is performing onboarding.

senses.definitionMd: The person or a proxy that is performing onboarding.

entries.title: device registration manager
entries.summaryMd: The management role that is responsible for performing activities related to registering users that are devices.

senses.definitionMd: The management role that is responsible for performing activities related to registering users that are devices.

entries.title: Device Role
entries.summaryMd: A device role is a group of devices with the same rules. For example, the list of white-listed software for a server is likely different from that for a workstation. This would cause servers and devices to have separate device roles.

senses.definitionMd: A device role is a group of devices with the same rules. For example, the list of white-listed software for a server is likely different from that for a workstation. This would cause servers and devices to have separate device roles.

entries.title: Diagnostics
entries.summaryMd: Information concerning known failure modes and their characteristics. Such information can be used in troubleshooting and failure analysis to help pinpoint the cause of a failure and help define suitable corrective measures.

senses.definitionMd: Information concerning known failure modes and their characteristics. Such information can be used in troubleshooting and failure analysis to help pinpoint the cause of a failure and help define suitable corrective measures.

entries.title: Dictionary
entries.summaryMd: A dynamic-length data structure that stores a collection of elements or values, where a unique label identifies each element. The label can be any data type.

senses.definitionMd: A dynamic-length data structure that stores a collection of elements or values, where a unique label identifies each element. The label can be any data type.

entries.title: Dictionary Contributor
entries.summaryMd: An organization or person that submits new identifier CPE names to a dictionary for inclusion.

senses.definitionMd: An organization or person that submits new identifier CPE names to a dictionary for inclusion.

entries.title: Dictionary Creator
entries.summaryMd: An organization that instantiates a CPE dictionary that conforms to the guidance within this specification. A dictionary creator is the organization that is ultimately responsible for the dictionary.

senses.definitionMd: An organization that instantiates a CPE dictionary that conforms to the guidance within this specification. A dictionary creator is the organization that is ultimately responsible for the dictionary.

entries.title: Dictionary Maintainer
entries.summaryMd: An organization that manages a CPE dictionary and all processes relating to that CPE dictionary. In the majority of cases, the organization that serves as the dictionary creator for a specific CPE dictionary will also serve as the dictionary maintainer. Otherwise, generally the dictionary maintainer is supporting the dictionary on behalf of the dictionary creator.

senses.definitionMd: An organization that manages a CPE dictionary and all processes relating to that CPE dictionary. In the majority of cases, the organization that serves as the dictionary creator for a specific CPE dictionary will also serve as the dictionary maintainer. entries.title: Dictionary Management Documents
entries.summaryMd: A set of documentation that captures the rules and processes specific to a CPE dictionary.

senses.definitionMd: A set of documentation that captures the rules and processes specific to a CPE dictionary.

entries.title: Dictionary Search
entries.summaryMd: The process of determining which identifier names within a CPE dictionary are members of a source name that represents a set of products.

senses.definitionMd: The process of determining which identifier names within a CPE dictionary are members of a source name that represents a set of products.

entries.title: Dictionary User
entries.summaryMd: An organization, individual, product, or service that consumes a CPE dictionary for any purpose.

senses.definitionMd: An organization, individual, product, or service that consumes a CPE dictionary for any purpose.

entries.title: differential privacy
entries.summaryMd: A rigorous mathematical definition of disclosure that considers the risk that an individual's confidential data may be learned as a result of a mathematical analysis based on that data being made publicly available.

senses.definitionMd: A rigorous mathematical definition of disclosure that considers the risk that an individual's confidential data may be learned as a result of a mathematical analysis based on that data being made publicly available.

entries.title: differentially private synthetic dataset
entries.summaryMd: A synthetic dataset that is produced by mechanisms that satisfy differential privacy.

senses.definitionMd: A synthetic dataset that is produced by mechanisms that satisfy differential privacy.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "differentially private synthetic dataset"

entries.title: Diffie-Hellman
entries.summaryMd: A method used to securely exchange or establish secret keys across an insecure network. Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman is used to create temporary or single-use secret keys.

senses.definitionMd: A method used to securely exchange or establish secret keys across an insecure network. Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman is used to create temporary or single-use secret keys.

entries.title: diffusion models
entries.summaryMd: A class of latent variable generative models consisting of three major components: a forward process, a reverse process, and a sampling procedure. The goal of the diffusion model is to learn a diffusion process that generates the probability distribution of a given dataset. It is widely used in computer vision on a variety of tasks, including image denoising, inpainting, super-resolution, and image generation.

senses.definitionMd: A class of latent variable generative models consisting of three major components: a forward process, a reverse process, and a sampling procedure. entries.title: Digest
entries.summaryMd: Output of a hash function or XOF.

senses.definitionMd: Output of a hash function or XOF.

entries.title: Digital asset
entries.summaryMd: Any asset that is purely digital, or is a digital representation of a physical asset.

senses.definitionMd: Any asset that is purely digital, or is a digital representation of a physical asset.

entries.title: Digital Certificate
entries.summaryMd: Certificate (as defined above).

senses.definitionMd: Certificate (as defined above).

entries.title: Digital Evidence
entries.summaryMd: Electronic information stored or transmitted in binary form.

senses.definitionMd: Electronic information stored or transmitted in binary form.

entries.title: Digital Fingerprint
entries.summaryMd: A hash that uniquely identifies data. Changing a single bit in the data stream used to generate the message digest will yield a completely different message digest.

senses.definitionMd: A hash that uniquely identifies data. Changing a single bit in the data stream used to generate the message digest will yield a completely different message digest.

entries.title: digital forensics
entries.summaryMd: In its strictest connotation, the application of computer science and investigative procedures involving the examination of digital evidence - following proper search authority, chain of custody, validation with mathematics, use of validated tools, repeatability, reporting, and possibly expert testimony.

senses.definitionMd: In its strictest connotation, the application of computer science and investigative procedures involving the examination of digital evidence - following proper search authority, chain of custody, validation with mathematics, use of validated tools, repeatability, reporting, and possibly expert testimony.

entries.title: digital identity
entries.summaryMd: The set of physical and behavioral characteristics by which an individual is uniquely recognizable. Note: This also encompasses non-person entities (NPEs).

senses.definitionMd: The set of physical and behavioral characteristics by which an individual is uniquely recognizable. Note: This also encompasses non-person entities (NPEs).

entries.title: Digital Identity Acceptance Statement
entries.summaryMd: Documents the results of the digital identity risk management process. This includes the impact assessment, initial assurance level selection, and tailoring process.

senses.definitionMd: Documents the results of the digital identity risk management process. This includes the impact assessment, initial assurance level selection, and tailoring process.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Digital Identity Acceptance Statement"

entries.title: digital infrastructure
entries.summaryMd: The ability to store and exchange data through a centralized communication system. Data communication and exchange are all simplified with the right software and hardware equipment.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to store and exchange data through a centralized communication system. Data communication and exchange are all simplified with the right software and hardware equipment.

entries.title: digital media
entries.summaryMd: A form of electronic media where data are stored in digital (as opposed to analog) form.

senses.definitionMd: A form of electronic media where data are stored in digital (as opposed to analog) form.

entries.title: digital policy
entries.summaryMd: Access control rules that compile directly into machine executable codes or signals. Subject/object attributes, operations, and environment conditions are the fundamental elements of digital policy, the building blocks of digital policy rules, which are enforced by an access control mechanism.

senses.definitionMd: Access control rules that compile directly into machine executable codes or signals. entries.title: digital signature
entries.summaryMd: The result of a cryptographic transformation of data that, when properly implemented, provides a mechanism for verifying origin authentication, data integrity, and signatory non-repudiation.

senses.definitionMd: The result of a cryptographic transformation of data that, when properly implemented, provides a mechanism for verifying origin authentication, data integrity, and signatory non-repudiation.

entries.title: Digital Signature Algorithm
entries.summaryMd: A Federal Information Processing Standard for digital signatures, based on the mathematical concept of modular exponentiations and the discrete logarithm problem.

senses.definitionMd: A Federal Information Processing Standard for digital signatures, based on the mathematical concept of modular exponentiations and the discrete logarithm problem.

entries.title: digital transaction
entries.summaryMd: A discrete event between a user and a system that supports a business or programmatic purpose. A government digital system may have multiple categories or types of transactions, which may require separate analysis within the overall digital identity risk assessment.

senses.definitionMd: A discrete event between a user and a system that supports a business or programmatic purpose. A government digital system may have multiple categories or types of transactions, which may require separate analysis within the overall digital identity risk assessment.

entries.title: digital twin
entries.summaryMd: The virtual (i.e., digital) representation of a physical or perceived real-world entity, concept, or notion.

senses.definitionMd: The virtual (i.e., digital) representation of a physical or perceived real-world entity, concept, or notion.

entries.title: digital twin application software
entries.summaryMd: A software application that comprehends, manipulates, reads, writes, or modifies digital twin definitions and instances according to the digital twin standard.

senses.definitionMd: A software application that comprehends, manipulates, reads, writes, or modifies digital twin definitions and instances according to the digital twin standard.

entries.title: digital twin definition
entries.summaryMd: A machine-readable specification that describes features that may be modeled for a particular type of real-world entity.

senses.definitionMd: A machine-readable specification that describes features that may be modeled for a particular type of real-world entity.

entries.title: digital twin instance
entries.summaryMd: A digital data structure, object, or entity in a computer software environment that represents a specific physical instance of a real-world object whose type or class is given by an associated digital twin definition.

senses.definitionMd: A digital data structure, object, or entity in a computer software environment that represents a specific physical instance of a real-world object whose type or class is given by an associated digital twin definition.

entries.title: Digital Video Disc
entries.summaryMd: Has the same shape and size as a CD, but with a higher density that gives the option for data to be double-sided and/or double-layered.

senses.definitionMd: Has the same shape and size as a CD, but with a higher density that gives the option for data to be double-sided and/or double-layered.

entries.title: Digitization
entries.summaryMd: The process of generating bits from the noise source.

senses.definitionMd: The process of generating bits from the noise source.

entries.title: direct BLACK wireline
entries.summaryMd: A BLACK metallic wireline that directly leaves the inspectable space in a continuous electrical path with no signal interruption or isolation. Continuous wirelines may be patched or spliced. Examples of wirelines that directly leave the inspectable space are analog telephone lines, commercial television cables, and alarm lines. Wirelines that do not leave the inspectable space are wirelines that pass through a digital switch or converter that reestablishes the signal level or reformats the signaling. Examples of BLACK wirelines that do not directly leave the inspectable space are telephone lines that connect to digital telephone switches, Ethernet lines that connect to digital network routers and alarm lines that connect to an alarm panel.

senses.definitionMd: A BLACK metallic wireline that directly leaves the inspectable space in a continuous electrical path with no signal interruption or isolation.
