entries.title: Direct Digital Manufacturing
entries.summaryMd: fabricating physical objects from a data file using computer-controlled processes with little to no human intervention. It includes Additive Manufacturing (AM), 3D printing, and rapid prototyping.

senses.definitionMd: fabricating physical objects from a data file using computer-controlled processes with little to no human intervention. It includes Additive Manufacturing (AM), 3D printing, and rapid prototyping.

entries.title: direct identifier
entries.summaryMd: An attribute that alone enables unique identification of a data principal within a specific operational context.

senses.definitionMd: An attribute that alone enables unique identification of a data principal within a specific operational context.

entries.title: direct identifying data
entries.summaryMd: Data that directly identify a single individual.

senses.definitionMd: Data that directly identify a single individual.

entries.title: direct prompt injection
entries.summaryMd: A direct prompting attack in which the attacker exploits prompt injection.

senses.definitionMd: A direct prompting attack in which the attacker exploits prompt injection.

entries.title: direct prompting attack
entries.summaryMd: In the generative AI context, an attack conducted by the primary user of the system through query access (e.g., as opposed to through resource control).

senses.definitionMd: In the generative AI context, an attack conducted by the primary user of the system through query access (e.g., as opposed to through resource control).

entries.title: Direct Random String
entries.summaryMd: In the RBG-based construction of IVs, an output string of an RBG that is used as the random field for an IV.

senses.definitionMd: In the RBG-based construction of IVs, an output string of an RBG that is used as the random field for an IV.

entries.title: directly identifying variables
entries.summaryMd: a category of data that contains direct identifiers

senses.definitionMd: a category of data that contains direct identifiers

entries.title: Directory
entries.summaryMd: Organizational structures that are used to group files together.

senses.definitionMd: Organizational structures that are used to group files together.

entries.title: dirty word list
entries.summaryMd: A list of discrete entities, such as hosts, email addresses, network port numbers, runtime processes, or applications, that have been previously determined to be associated with malicious activity.

senses.definitionMd: A list of discrete entities, such as hosts, email addresses, network port numbers, runtime processes, or applications, that have been previously determined to be associated with malicious activity.

entries.title: disallowed
entries.summaryMd: The algorithm or key length is no longer allowed for applying cryptographic protection.

senses.definitionMd: The algorithm or key length is no longer allowed for applying cryptographic protection.

entries.title: disassociability
entries.summaryMd: Enabling the processing of PII or events without association to individuals or devices beyond the operational requirements of the system.

senses.definitionMd: Enabling the processing of PII or events without association to individuals or devices beyond the operational requirements of the system.

entries.title: disaster recovery plan (DRP)
entries.summaryMd: A predetermined set of instructions or procedures that describe how an organization’s mission-essential functions will be sustained within 12 hours and for up to 30 days as a result of a disaster event before returning to normal operations.

senses.definitionMd: A predetermined set of instructions or procedures that describe how an organization’s mission-essential functions will be sustained within 12 hours and for up to 30 days as a result of a disaster event before returning to normal operations.

entries.title: disciplined oscillator
entries.summaryMd: An oscillator whose output frequency is continuously adjusted (often through the use of a phase locked loop) to agree with an external reference. For example, a GPS disciplined oscillator (GPSDO) usually consists of a quartz or rubidium oscillator whose output frequency is continuously adjusted to agree with signals broadcast by the GPS satellites.

senses.definitionMd: An oscillator whose output frequency is continuously adjusted (often through the use of a phase locked loop) to agree with an external reference. For example, a GPS disciplined oscillator (GPSDO) usually consists of a quartz or rubidium oscillator whose output frequency is continuously adjusted to agree with signals broadcast by the GPS satellites.

entries.title: disclosure
entries.summaryMd: Divulging of, or provision of access to, data.

senses.definitionMd: Divulging of, or provision of access to, data.

entries.title: disclosure limitation
entries.summaryMd: Statistical methods used to hinder anyone from identifying an individual respondent or establishment by analyzing published data, especially by manipulating mathematical and arithmetical relationships among the data.

senses.definitionMd: Statistical methods used to hinder anyone from identifying an individual respondent or establishment by analyzing published data, especially by manipulating mathematical and arithmetical relationships among the data.

entries.title: Discovery
entries.summaryMd: The act of locating a machine-processable description of a Web service-related resource that may have been previously unknown and that meets certain functional criteria. It involves matching a set of functional and other criteria with a set of resource descriptions. The goal is to find an appropriate Web service-related resource.

senses.definitionMd: The act of locating a machine-processable description of a Web service-related resource that may have been previously unknown and that meets certain functional criteria. It involves matching a set of functional and other criteria with a set of resource descriptions. The goal is to find an appropriate Web service-related resource.

entries.title: Discovery Service
entries.summaryMd: A service that enables agents to retrieve Web services-related resource description.

senses.definitionMd: A service that enables agents to retrieve Web services-related resource description.

entries.title: Discrete Fourier Transform Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to detect periodic features (i.e., repetitive patterns that are near each other) in the tested sequence that would indicate a deviation from the assumption of randomness.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to detect periodic features (i.e., repetitive patterns that are near each other) in the tested sequence that would indicate a deviation from the assumption of randomness.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Discrete Fourier Transform Test"

entries.title: Discrete Process
entries.summaryMd: A type of process where a specified quantity of material moves as a unit (part or group of parts) between work stations and each unit maintains its unique identity.

senses.definitionMd: A type of process where a specified quantity of material moves as a unit (part or group of parts) between work stations and each unit maintains its unique identity.

entries.title: discretionary access control (DAC)
entries.summaryMd: An access control policy that is enforced over all subjects and objects in an information system where the policy specifies that a subject that has been granted access to information can do one or more of the following: (i) pass the information to other subjects or objects; (ii) grant its privileges to other subjects; (iii) change security attributes on subjects, objects, information systems, or system components; (iv) choose the security attributes to be associated with newly-created or revised objects; or (v) change the rules governing access control. Mandatory access controls restrict this capability.

senses.definitionMd: An access control policy that is enforced over all subjects and objects in an information system where the policy specifies that a subject that has been granted access to information can do one or more of the following: (i) pass the information to other subjects or objects; (ii) grant its privileges to other subjects; (iii) change security attributes on subjects, objects, information systems, or system components; (iv) choose the security attributes to be associated with newly-created or revised objects; or (v) change the rules governing access control. Mandatory access controls restrict this capability.

entries.title: discriminative
entries.summaryMd: A type of machine learning method that learns to discriminate between classes.

senses.definitionMd: A type of machine learning method that learns to discriminate between classes.

entries.title: discussion
entries.summaryMd: Statements used to provide additional explanatory information for controls, control enhancements, security requirements, or enhanced security requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Statements used to provide additional explanatory information for controls, control enhancements, security requirements, or enhanced security requirements.

entries.title: Disinfecting
entries.summaryMd: Removing malware from within a file.

senses.definitionMd: Removing malware from within a file.

entries.title: disinformation
entries.summaryMd: The process of providing deliberately deceptive information to adversaries to mislead or confuse them regarding the security posture of the system or organization or the state of cyber preparedness.

senses.definitionMd: The process of providing deliberately deceptive information to adversaries to mislead or confuse them regarding the security posture of the system or organization or the state of cyber preparedness.

entries.title: Disk image
entries.summaryMd: A virtual representation of a real disk drive.

senses.definitionMd: A virtual representation of a real disk drive.

entries.title: Disk Imaging
entries.summaryMd: Generating a bit-for-bit copy of the original media, including free space and slack space. Also known as a bit stream image.

senses.definitionMd: Generating a bit-for-bit copy of the original media, including free space and slack space. Also known as a bit stream image.

entries.title: Disk-to-Disk Copy
entries.summaryMd: Copying the contents of media directly to another media.

senses.definitionMd: Copying the contents of media directly to another media.

entries.title: Disk-to-File Copy
entries.summaryMd: Copying the contents of media to a single logical data file.

senses.definitionMd: Copying the contents of media to a single logical data file.

entries.title: disruption
entries.summaryMd: An unplanned event that causes the general system or major application to be inoperable for an unacceptable length of time (e.g., minor or extended power outage, extended unavailable network, or equipment or facility damage or destruction).

senses.definitionMd: An unplanned event that causes the general system or major application to be inoperable for an unacceptable length of time (e.g., minor or extended power outage, extended unavailable network, or equipment or facility damage or destruction).

entries.title: distinguishable information
entries.summaryMd: Information that can be used to identify an individual.

senses.definitionMd: Information that can be used to identify an individual.

entries.title: distinguished name (DN)
entries.summaryMd: An identifier that uniquely represents an object in the X.500 directory information tree.

senses.definitionMd: An identifier that uniquely represents an object in the X.500 directory information tree.

entries.title: distinguishing identifier
entries.summaryMd: Information which unambiguously distinguishes an entity in the authentication process.

senses.definitionMd: Information which unambiguously distinguishes an entity in the authentication process.

entries.title: distributed denial of service (DDoS)
entries.summaryMd: A denial of service technique that uses numerous hosts to perform the attack.

senses.definitionMd: A denial of service technique that uses numerous hosts to perform the attack.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "distributed denial of service (DDoS)"

entries.title: Distributed network
entries.summaryMd: A network configuration where every participant can communicate with one another without going through a centralized point. Since there are multiple pathways for communication, the loss of any participant will not prevent communication. This is also known as peer-to-peer network.

senses.definitionMd: A network configuration where every participant can communicate with one another without going through a centralized point. Since there are multiple pathways for communication, the loss of any participant will not prevent communication. This is also known as peer-to-peer network.

entries.title: distributed self-assessment
entries.summaryMd: The least formal type of assessment; the element judgments are based on the evaluations by small groups that work in parallel.

senses.definitionMd: The least formal type of assessment; the element judgments are based on the evaluations by small groups that work in parallel.

entries.title: Distribution
entries.summaryMd: The transport of a key and other keying material from an entity that either owns or generates the key to another entity that is intended to use the key.

senses.definitionMd: The transport of a key and other keying material from an entity that either owns or generates the key to another entity that is intended to use the key.

entries.title: Disturbance
entries.summaryMd: An undesired change in a variable being applied to a system that tends to adversely affect the value of a controlled variable.

senses.definitionMd: An undesired change in a variable being applied to a system that tends to adversely affect the value of a controlled variable.

entries.title: Document Type Definition (DTD)
entries.summaryMd: A document defining the format of the contents present between the tags in an XML or SGML document, and the way they should be interpreted by the application reading the XML or SGML document.

senses.definitionMd: A document defining the format of the contents present between the tags in an XML or SGML document, and the way they should be interpreted by the application reading the XML or SGML document.

entries.title: DoD information
entries.summaryMd: Any information that has not been cleared for public release in accordance with Department of Defense (DoD) Directive 5230.09, “Clearance of DoD Information for Public Release”, and that has been collected, developed, received, transmitted, used, or stored by DoD, or by a non-DoD entity in support of an official DoD activity.

senses.definitionMd: Any information that has not been cleared for public release in accordance with Department of Defense (DoD) Directive 5230.09, “Clearance of DoD Information for Public Release”, and that has been collected, developed, received, transmitted, used, or stored by DoD, or by a non-DoD entity in support of an official DoD activity.

entries.title: domain
entries.summaryMd: A domain operating at a single security level (which includes a unique combination of classification, releasabilities, and dissemination controls) that implements a security policy and is administered by a single authority.

senses.definitionMd: A domain operating at a single security level (which includes a unique combination of classification, releasabilities, and dissemination controls) that implements a security policy and is administered by a single authority.

entries.title: Domain authority
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for determining whether another domain’s FCKMS Security Policy is equivalent to or compatible with its own domain policy. The FCKMS system authority often performs this role.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for determining whether another domain’s FCKMS Security Policy is equivalent to or compatible with its own domain policy. The FCKMS system authority often performs this role.

entries.title: Domain Name
entries.summaryMd: A label that identifies a network domain using the Domain Naming System.

senses.definitionMd: A label that identifies a network domain using the Domain Naming System.

entries.title: Domain Name Server
entries.summaryMd: The internet's equivalent of a phone book. It maintains a directory of domain names, as defined by the Domain Name System, and translates them to Internet Protocol addresses.

senses.definitionMd: The internet's equivalent of a phone book. It maintains a directory of domain names, as defined by the Domain Name System, and translates them to Internet Protocol addresses.

entries.title: Domain Name System (DNS)
entries.summaryMd: The system by which Internet domain names and addresses are tracked and regulated as defined by IETF RFC 1034 and other related RFCs.

senses.definitionMd: The system by which Internet domain names and addresses are tracked and regulated as defined by IETF RFC 1034 and other related RFCs.

entries.title: Domain of Use
entries.summaryMd: The intended usage of a format

senses.definitionMd: The intended usage of a format

entries.title: Domain parameter
entries.summaryMd: Parameters used with cryptographic algorithms that are usually common to a domain of users. An ECDSA or EdDSA cryptographic key pair is associated with a specific set of domain parameters.

senses.definitionMd: Parameters used with cryptographic algorithms that are usually common to a domain of users. An ECDSA or EdDSA cryptographic key pair is associated with a specific set of domain parameters.

entries.title: Domain parameter seed
entries.summaryMd: A string of bits that is used as input for a domain parameter generation or validation process.

senses.definitionMd: A string of bits that is used as input for a domain parameter generation or validation process.

entries.title: Domain Separation
entries.summaryMd: For a function, a partitioning of the inputs to different application domains so that no input is assigned to more than one domain.

senses.definitionMd: For a function, a partitioning of the inputs to different application domains so that no input is assigned to more than one domain.

entries.title: dominance rule
entries.summaryMd: A cell is regarded as confidential, if the n largest units contribute more than k % to the cell total, e.g., n=2 and k=85 means that a cell is defined as risky if the two largest units contribute more than 85 % to the cell total. The n and k are given by the statistical authority. In some NSOs [national statistical office] the values of n and k are confidential.

senses.definitionMd: A cell is regarded as confidential, if the n largest units contribute more than k % to the cell total, e.g., n=2 and k=85 means that a cell is defined as risky if the two largest units contribute more than 85 % to the cell total. The n and k are given by the statistical authority. In some NSOs [national statistical office] the values of n and k are confidential.

entries.title: Double spend (attack)
entries.summaryMd: An attack where a blockchain network user attempts to explicitly double spend a digital asset.

senses.definitionMd: An attack where a blockchain network user attempts to explicitly double spend a digital asset.

entries.title: Double spend (problem)
entries.summaryMd: Transacting with the same set of digital assets more than once. This is a problem which has plagued many digital money systems, and a problem that most blockchain networks are designed to prevent.

senses.definitionMd: Transacting with the same set of digital assets more than once. This is a problem which has plagued many digital money systems, and a problem that most blockchain networks are designed to prevent.

entries.title: Downgrading
entries.summaryMd: An authorized reduction in the level of protection to be provided to specified information, e.g., from a Moderate impact-level down to a Low impact-level.

senses.definitionMd: An authorized reduction in the level of protection to be provided to specified information, e.g., from a Moderate impact-level down to a Low impact-level.

entries.title: downlink
entries.summaryMd: Communication that originates from the satellite to the ground.

senses.definitionMd: Communication that originates from the satellite to the ground.

entries.title: dP
entries.summaryMd: RSA private exponent for the prime factor p in the CRT format, i.e., d mod (p - 1); an integer.

senses.definitionMd: RSA private exponent for the prime factor p in the CRT format, i.e., d mod (p - 1); an integer.

entries.title: dQ
entries.summaryMd: RSA private exponent for the prime factor q in the CRT format, i.e., d mod (q - 1); an integer.

senses.definitionMd: RSA private exponent for the prime factor q in the CRT format, i.e., d mod (q - 1); an integer.

entries.title: DRBG mechanism
entries.summaryMd: The portion of an RBG that includes the functions necessary to instantiate and uninstantiate the RBG, generate pseudorandom bits, (optionally) reseed the RBG and test the health of the the DRBG mechanism.

senses.definitionMd: The portion of an RBG that includes the functions necessary to instantiate and uninstantiate the RBG, generate pseudorandom bits, (optionally) reseed the RBG and test the health of the the DRBG mechanism.

entries.title: DRBG Mechanism Boundary
entries.summaryMd: A conceptual boundary that is used to explain the operations of a DRBG mechanism and its interaction with and relation to other processes. (See min-entropy.)

senses.definitionMd: A conceptual boundary that is used to explain the operations of a DRBG mechanism and its interaction with and relation to other processes. (See min-entropy.)

entries.title: dual authorization
entries.summaryMd: A system of storage and handling that is designed to prohibit individual access to certain resources by requiring the presence and actions of at least two authorized persons, each capable of detecting incorrect or unauthorized security procedures with respect to the task being performed.

senses.definitionMd: A system of storage and handling that is designed to prohibit individual access to certain resources by requiring the presence and actions of at least two authorized persons, each capable of detecting incorrect or unauthorized security procedures with respect to the task being performed.

entries.title: Dual_EC_DRBG
entries.summaryMd: A DRBG originally specified in SP 800-90A that has been withdrawn.

senses.definitionMd: A DRBG originally specified in SP 800-90A that has been withdrawn.

entries.title: dual-use foundation model
entries.summaryMd: An AI model that is trained on broad data; generally uses self-supervision; contains at least tens of billions of parameters; is applicable across a wide range of contexts; and that exhibits, or could be easily modified to exhibit, high levels of performance at tasks that pose a serious risk to security, national economic security, national public health or safety, or any combination of those matters, such as by:(i) substantially lowering the barrier of entry for non-experts to design, synthesize, acquire, or use chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) weapons;(ii) enabling powerful offensive cyber operations through automated vulnerability discovery and exploitation against a wide range of potential targets of cyber attacks; or(iii) permitting the evasion of human control or oversight through means of deception or obfuscation.Models meet this definition even if they are provided to end users with technical safeguards that attempt to prevent users from taking advantage of the relevant unsafe capabilities.

senses.definitionMd: An AI model that is trained on broad data; generally uses self-supervision; contains at least tens of billions of parameters; is applicable across a wide range of contexts; and that exhibits, or could be easily modified to exhibit, high levels of performance at tasks that pose a serious risk to security, national economic security, national public health or safety, or any combination of those matters, such as by:(i) substantially lowering the barrier of entry for non-experts to design, synthesize, acquire, or use chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear (CBRN) weapons;(ii) enabling powerful offensive cyber operations through automated vulnerability discovery and exploitation against a wide range of potential targets of cyber attacks; or(iii) permitting the evasion of human control or oversight through means of deception or obfuscation.Models meet this definition even if they are provided to end users with technical safeguards that attempt to prevent users from taking advantage of the relevant unsafe capabilities.

entries.title: Duplicate Digital Evidence
entries.summaryMd: A duplicate is an accurate digital reproduction of all data objects contained on the original physical item and associated media (e.g., flash memory, RAM, ROM).

senses.definitionMd: A duplicate is an accurate digital reproduction of all data objects contained on the original physical item and associated media (e.g., flash memory, RAM, ROM).

entries.title: Duty Cycle
entries.summaryMd: The percentage of time that a device is operating over a specified period. For example, a reader that is emitting energy to communicate with tags for 15 seconds every minute has a duty cycle of 25%.

senses.definitionMd: The percentage of time that a device is operating over a specified period. For example, a reader that is emitting energy to communicate with tags for 15 seconds every minute has a duty cycle of 25%.

entries.title: dynamic code analyzer
entries.summaryMd: A tool that analyzes computer software by executing programs built from the software being analyzed on a real or virtual processor and observing its behavior, probing the application and analyzing application responses.

senses.definitionMd: A tool that analyzes computer software by executing programs built from the software being analyzed on a real or virtual processor and observing its behavior, probing the application and analyzing application responses.

entries.title: dynamic subsystem
entries.summaryMd: A subsystem that is not continually present during the execution phase of an information system. Service-oriented architectures and cloud computing architectures are examples of architectures that employ dynamic subsystems.

senses.definitionMd: A subsystem that is not continually present during the execution phase of an information system. Service-oriented architectures and cloud computing architectures are examples of architectures that employ dynamic subsystems.

entries.title: e
entries.summaryMd: The original input string of zero and one bits to be tested.

senses.definitionMd: The original input string of zero and one bits to be tested.

entries.title: e-authentication assurance level
entries.summaryMd: A measure of trust or confidence in an authentication mechanism defined in publications Office of Management and Budget (OMB)-04-04 and NIST SP 800-63 in terms of four levels: 1: LITTLE OR NO confidence 2: SOME confidence 3: HIGH confidence 4: VERY HIGH confidence.

senses.definitionMd: A measure of trust or confidence in an authentication mechanism defined in publications Office of Management and Budget (OMB)-04-04 and NIST SP 800-63 in terms of four levels: 1: LITTLE OR NO confidence 2: SOME confidence 3: HIGH confidence 4: VERY HIGH confidence.

entries.title: e-government (e-gov)
entries.summaryMd: The use by the U.S. Government of web-based Internet applications and other information technology. Rationale: General definition of a commonly understood term

senses.definitionMd: The use by the U.S. Government of web-based Internet applications and other information technology. Rationale: General definition of a commonly understood term

entries.title: Ease-of-use
entries.summaryMd: A metric of satisfaction in using a product as established by one or more individuals using the product.

senses.definitionMd: A metric of satisfaction in using a product as established by one or more individuals using the product.

entries.title: Eavesdropper
entries.summaryMd: A party that secretly receives communications intended for others.

senses.definitionMd: A party that secretly receives communications intended for others.

entries.title: eBits
entries.summaryMd: The bit length of the RSA exponent e.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the RSA exponent e.

entries.title: Education
entries.summaryMd: The ‘Education’ level integrates all of the security skills and competencies of the various functional specialties into a common body of knowledge, adds a multidisciplinary study of concepts, issues, and principles (technological and social), and strives to produce IT security specialists and professionals capable of vision and pro-active response.

senses.definitionMd: The ‘Education’ level integrates all of the security skills and competencies of the various functional specialties into a common body of knowledge, adds a multidisciplinary study of concepts, issues, and principles (technological and social), and strives to produce IT security specialists and professionals capable of vision and pro-active response.

entries.title: effective period
entries.summaryMd: Time span during which each COMSEC key edition (i.e., multiple key segments) remains in effect.

senses.definitionMd: Time span during which each COMSEC key edition (i.e., multiple key segments) remains in effect.

entries.title: effectiveness
entries.summaryMd: The extent to which planned activities are realized and planned results achieved.

senses.definitionMd: The extent to which planned activities are realized and planned results achieved.

entries.title: efficient (cryptographic) algorithm
entries.summaryMd: An algorithm whose running time is practical for the relevant security strength.

senses.definitionMd: An algorithm whose running time is practical for the relevant security strength.

entries.title: Egress Filtering
entries.summaryMd: Filtering of outgoing network traffic.

senses.definitionMd: Filtering of outgoing network traffic.

entries.title: ei
entries.summaryMd: The ith bit in the original sequencee.

senses.definitionMd: The ith bit in the original sequencee.

entries.title: Electromagnetic Interference
entries.summaryMd: An electromagnetic disturbance that interrupts, obstructs, or otherwise degrades or limits the effective performance of electronics/electrical equipment.

senses.definitionMd: An electromagnetic disturbance that interrupts, obstructs, or otherwise degrades or limits the effective performance of electronics/electrical equipment.

entries.title: electronic business (e-business)
entries.summaryMd: Doing business online. Rationale: Term is general and not specific to IA.

senses.definitionMd: Doing business online. Rationale: Term is general and not specific to IA.

entries.title: Electronic Business XML (ebXML)
entries.summaryMd: Sponsored by UN/CEFACT and OASIS, a modular suite of specifications that enable enterprises of any size and in any geographical location to perform business-to-business transactions using XML.

senses.definitionMd: Sponsored by UN/CEFACT and OASIS, a modular suite of specifications that enable enterprises of any size and in any geographical location to perform business-to-business transactions using XML.

entries.title: electronic credentials
entries.summaryMd: Digital documents used in authentication that bind an identity or an attribute to a subscriber's authenticator.

senses.definitionMd: Digital documents used in authentication that bind an identity or an attribute to a subscriber's authenticator.

entries.title: electronic/digital file transfer
entries.summaryMd: Transmission of a file (information) between two systems via a file transfer (communications) protocol.

senses.definitionMd: Transmission of a file (information) between two systems via a file transfer (communications) protocol.

entries.title: Electronic Evidence
entries.summaryMd: Information and data of investigative value that is stored on or transmitted by an electronic device.

senses.definitionMd: Information and data of investigative value that is stored on or transmitted by an electronic device.

entries.title: electronic fill device (EFD)
entries.summaryMd: A COMSEC item used to transfer or store key in electronic form or to insert key into cryptographic equipment.

senses.definitionMd: A COMSEC item used to transfer or store key in electronic form or to insert key into cryptographic equipment.

entries.title: electronic key management system (EKMS)
entries.summaryMd: An interoperable collection of systems that automate the planning, ordering, generating, distributing, storing, filling, using, and destroying of electronic key and management of other types of COMSEC material.

senses.definitionMd: An interoperable collection of systems that automate the planning, ordering, generating, distributing, storing, filling, using, and destroying of electronic key and management of other types of COMSEC material.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "electronic key management system (EKMS)"

entries.title: electronic messaging services
entries.summaryMd: Services providing interpersonal messaging capability; meeting specific functional, management, and technical requirements; and yielding a business- quality electronic mail service suitable for the conduct of official government business.

senses.definitionMd: Services providing interpersonal messaging capability; meeting specific functional, management, and technical requirements; and yielding a business- quality electronic mail service suitable for the conduct of official government business.

entries.title: Electronic Product Code (EPC) Identifier
entries.summaryMd: One of the available formats for encoding identifiers on RFID tags. The EPC is a globally unique number that identifies a specific item in the supply chain. This number may be used to identify a container, pallet, case or individual unit.

senses.definitionMd: One of the available formats for encoding identifiers on RFID tags. The EPC is a globally unique number that identifies a specific item in the supply chain. This number may be used to identify a container, pallet, case or individual unit.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Electronic Product Code (EPC) Identifier"

entries.title: Electronic Product Code Information Services (EPCIS)
entries.summaryMd: An inter-enterprise subsystem that facilitates information sharing using the EPCglobal network. EPCISs provide information services necessary for the storage, communication and dissemination of EPC data in a secure environment.

senses.definitionMd: An inter-enterprise subsystem that facilitates information sharing using the EPCglobal network. EPCISs provide information services necessary for the storage, communication and dissemination of EPC data in a secure environment.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Electronic Product Code Information Services (EPCIS)"

entries.title: Electronic Protected Health Information
entries.summaryMd: Information that comes within paragraphs (1)(i) or (1)(ii) of the definition of protected health information as specified in this section (see “protected health information”).

senses.definitionMd: Information that comes within paragraphs (1)(i) or (1)(ii) of the definition of protected health information as specified in this section (see “protected health information”).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Electronic Protected Health Information"

entries.title: Electronic Serial Number (ESN)
entries.summaryMd: A unique 32-bit number programmed into CDMA phones when they are manufactured.

senses.definitionMd: A unique 32-bit number programmed into CDMA phones when they are manufactured.

entries.title: electronic signature
entries.summaryMd: A method of signing an electronic message that- (A) identifies and authenticates a particular person as the source of the electronic message; and (B) indicates such person's approval of the information contained in the electronic message.

senses.definitionMd: A method of signing an electronic message that- (A) identifies and authenticates a particular person as the source of the electronic message; and (B) indicates such person's approval of the information contained in the electronic message.

entries.title: electronically generated key
entries.summaryMd: Key generated in a COMSEC device by introducing (either mechanically or electronically) a seed key into the device and then using the seed, together with a software algorithm stored in the device, to produce the desired key.

senses.definitionMd: Key generated in a COMSEC device by introducing (either mechanically or electronically) a seed key into the device and then using the seed, together with a software algorithm stored in the device, to produce the desired key.

entries.title: element
entries.summaryMd: A statement about an ISCM concept that is true for a well-implemented ISCM program.

senses.definitionMd: A statement about an ISCM concept that is true for a well-implemented ISCM program.

entries.title: Element Processes
entries.summaryMd: A series of operations performed in the making or treatment of an element; performing operations on elements/data.

senses.definitionMd: A series of operations performed in the making or treatment of an element; performing operations on elements/data.

entries.title: elephant diffuser
entries.summaryMd: A (now deprecated) component in BitLocker Drive Encryption to increase resistance against ciphertext modification.

senses.definitionMd: A (now deprecated) component in BitLocker Drive Encryption to increase resistance against ciphertext modification.

entries.title: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm
entries.summaryMd: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm specified in ANSI X9.62 and approved in FIPS 186.

senses.definitionMd: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm specified in ANSI X9.62 and approved in FIPS 186.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm"

entries.title: embedded computer
entries.summaryMd: Computer system that is an integral part of a larger system. Rationale: Listed for deletion in 2010 version of CNSS 4009.

senses.definitionMd: Computer system that is an integral part of a larger system. Rationale: Listed for deletion in 2010 version of CNSS 4009.

entries.title: emergence
entries.summaryMd: The behaviors and outcomes that result from how individual system elements compose to form the system as a whole.

senses.definitionMd: The behaviors and outcomes that result from how individual system elements compose to form the system as a whole.

entries.title: emergency action plan (EAP)
entries.summaryMd: A plan developed to prevent loss of national intelligence; protect personnel, facilities, and communications; and recover operations damaged by terrorist attack, natural disaster, or similar events.

senses.definitionMd: A plan developed to prevent loss of national intelligence; protect personnel, facilities, and communications; and recover operations damaged by terrorist attack, natural disaster, or similar events.

entries.title: Emergency revocation
entries.summaryMd: A revocation of keying material that is effected in response to an actual or suspected compromise of a key.

senses.definitionMd: A revocation of keying material that is effected in response to an actual or suspected compromise of a key.

entries.title: emission security (EMSEC)
entries.summaryMd: The component of communications security that results from all measures taken to deny unauthorized persons information of value that might be derived from intercept and analysis of compromising emanations from cryptoequipment and information systems. See TEMPEST.

senses.definitionMd: The component of communications security that results from all measures taken to deny unauthorized persons information of value that might be derived from intercept and analysis of compromising emanations from cryptoequipment and information systems. See TEMPEST.

entries.title: enabling system
entries.summaryMd: A system that provides support to the life cycle activities associated with the system of interest. Enabling systems are not necessarily delivered with the system of interest and do not necessarily exist in the operational environment of the system of interest.

senses.definitionMd: A system that provides support to the life cycle activities associated with the system of interest. Enabling systems are not necessarily delivered with the system of interest and do not necessarily exist in the operational environment of the system of interest.

entries.title: enc8(i)
entries.summaryMd: For an integer i ranging from 0 to 255, enc8(i) is the byte encoding of i, with bit 0 being the low-order bit of the byte.

senses.definitionMd: For an integer i ranging from 0 to 255, enc8(i) is the byte encoding of i, with bit 0 being the low-order bit of the byte.

entries.title: Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP)
entries.summaryMd: The core IPsec security protocol; can provide integrity protection and (optionally) encryption protection for packet headers and data.

senses.definitionMd: The core IPsec security protocol; can provide integrity protection and (optionally) encryption protection for packet headers and data.

entries.title: encapsulation
entries.summaryMd: The process of applying the Encaps algorithm of a KEM. This algorithm accepts the encapsulation key as input, requires private randomness, and produces a shared secret key and an associated ciphertext as output.

senses.definitionMd: The process of applying the Encaps algorithm of a KEM. This algorithm accepts the encapsulation key as input, requires private randomness, and produces a shared secret key and an associated ciphertext as output.

entries.title: encapsulation key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key produced by a KEM during key generation and used during the encapsulation process. The encapsulation key can be made public.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key produced by a KEM during key generation and used during the encapsulation process. The encapsulation key can be made public.

entries.title: encipher
entries.summaryMd: Cryptographically transform data to produce cipher text.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptographically transform data to produce cipher text.

entries.title: enclave
entries.summaryMd: A set of system resources that operate in the same security domain and that share the protection of a single, common, continuous security perimeter.

senses.definitionMd: A set of system resources that operate in the same security domain and that share the protection of a single, common, continuous security perimeter.

entries.title: enclave boundary
entries.summaryMd: Point at which an enclave’s internal network service layer connects to an external network’s service layer, i.e., to another enclave or to a wide area network (WAN).

senses.definitionMd: Point at which an enclave’s internal network service layer connects to an external network’s service layer, i.e., to another enclave or to a wide area network (WAN).

entries.title: encode
entries.summaryMd: Use a system of symbols to represent information, which might originally have some other representation. Example: Morse code.

senses.definitionMd: Use a system of symbols to represent information, which might originally have some other representation. Example: Morse code.

entries.title: encrypt
entries.summaryMd: Cryptographically transform data to produce cipher text.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptographically transform data to produce cipher text.

entries.title: encrypted key
entries.summaryMd: Key that has been encrypted in a system approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) for key encryption.

senses.definitionMd: Key that has been encrypted in a system approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) for key encryption.

entries.title: encryption
entries.summaryMd: The cryptographic transformation of data to produce ciphertext.

senses.definitionMd: The cryptographic transformation of data to produce ciphertext.

entries.title: encryption algorithm
entries.summaryMd: Set of mathematically expressed rules for rendering data unintelligible by executing a series of conversions controlled by a key.

senses.definitionMd: Set of mathematically expressed rules for rendering data unintelligible by executing a series of conversions controlled by a key.

entries.title: encryption certificate
entries.summaryMd: A certificate containing a public key that can encrypt or decrypt electronic messages, files, documents, or data transmissions, or establish or exchange a session key for these same purposes. Key management sometimes refers to the process of storing protecting and escrowing the private component of the key pair associated with the encryption certificate.

senses.definitionMd: A certificate containing a public key that can encrypt or decrypt electronic messages, files, documents, or data transmissions, or establish or exchange a session key for these same purposes. Key management sometimes refers to the process of storing protecting and escrowing the private component of the key pair associated with the encryption certificate.

entries.title: encryption key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key that is used with a PKE in order to encrypt plaintexts into ciphertexts. The encryption key can be made public.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key that is used with a PKE in order to encrypt plaintexts into ciphertexts. The encryption key can be made public.

entries.title: end cryptographic unit (ECU)
entries.summaryMd: Device that 1) performs cryptographic functions, 2) typically is part of a larger system for which the device provides security services, and 3) from the viewpoint of a supporting security infrastructure (e.g., a key management system) is the lowest level of identifiable component with which a management transaction can be conducted.

senses.definitionMd: Device that 1) performs cryptographic functions, 2) typically is part of a larger system for which the device provides security services, and 3) from the viewpoint of a supporting security infrastructure (e.g., a key management system) is the lowest level of identifiable component with which a management transaction can be conducted.

entries.title: end-point protection platform
entries.summaryMd: Safeguards implemented through software to protect end-user machines such as workstations and laptops against attack (e.g., antivirus, antispyware, anti-adware, personal firewalls, host-based intrusion detection and prevention systems, etc.).

senses.definitionMd: Safeguards implemented through software to protect end-user machines such as workstations and laptops against attack (e.g., antivirus, antispyware, anti-adware, personal firewalls, host-based intrusion detection and prevention systems, etc.).

entries.title: end-to-end encryption
entries.summaryMd: Communications encryption in which data is encrypted when being passed through a network, but routing information remains visible.

senses.definitionMd: Communications encryption in which data is encrypted when being passed through a network, but routing information remains visible.

entries.title: end-to-end security
entries.summaryMd: Safeguarding information in an information system from point of origin to point of destination.

senses.definitionMd: Safeguarding information in an information system from point of origin to point of destination.

entries.title: endpoint
entries.summaryMd: Any device that is used to access a digital identity on a network, such as laptops, desktops, mobile phones, tablets, servers, Internet of Things devices, and virtual environments.

senses.definitionMd: Any device that is used to access a digital identity on a network, such as laptops, desktops, mobile phones, tablets, servers, Internet of Things devices, and virtual environments.

entries.title: Endpoint Protection Platform
entries.summaryMd: Safeguards implemented through software to protect end-user machines such as workstations and laptops against attack (e.g., antivirus, antispyware, antiadware, personal firewalls, host-based intrusion detection and prevention systems, etc.).

senses.definitionMd: Safeguards implemented through software to protect end-user machines such as workstations and laptops against attack (e.g., antivirus, antispyware, antiadware, personal firewalls, host-based intrusion detection and prevention systems, etc.).

entries.title: energy-latency attack
entries.summaryMd: An attack that exploits the performance dependency on hardware and model optimizations to negate the effects of hardware optimizations, increase computational latency, increase hardware temperature, and massively increase the amount of energy consumed.

senses.definitionMd: An attack that exploits the performance dependency on hardware and model optimizations to negate the effects of hardware optimizations, increase computational latency, increase hardware temperature, and massively increase the amount of energy consumed.

entries.title: engineered system
entries.summaryMd: A system designed or adapted to interact with an anticipated operational environment to achieve one or more intended purposes while complying with applicable constraints.

senses.definitionMd: A system designed or adapted to interact with an anticipated operational environment to achieve one or more intended purposes while complying with applicable constraints.

entries.title: engineered team
entries.summaryMd: The individuals on the systems engineering team with security responsibilities, systems security engineers that are part of the systems engineering team, or a combination thereof.

senses.definitionMd: The individuals on the systems engineering team with security responsibilities, systems security engineers that are part of the systems engineering team, or a combination thereof.

entries.title: Enhanced Data for GSM Evolution (EDGE)
entries.summaryMd: An upgrade to GPRS to provide higher data rates by joining multiple time slots.

senses.definitionMd: An upgrade to GPRS to provide higher data rates by joining multiple time slots.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Enhanced Data for GSM Evolution (EDGE)"

entries.title: Enhanced Messaging Service (EMS)
entries.summaryMd: An improved message system for GSM mobile devices allowing picture, sound, animation and text elements to be conveyed through one or more concatenated SMS messages.

senses.definitionMd: An improved message system for GSM mobile devices allowing picture, sound, animation and text elements to be conveyed through one or more concatenated SMS messages.

entries.title: Enhanced Overlay
entries.summaryMd: Overlay that adds processes, controls, enhancements, and additional implementation guidance specific to the purpose of the overlay.

senses.definitionMd: Overlay that adds processes, controls, enhancements, and additional implementation guidance specific to the purpose of the overlay.

entries.title: enhanced security requirements
entries.summaryMd: Security requirements that can be implemented in addition to the requirements in NIST Special Publication 800-171. The additional security requirements provide the foundation for a defense-in-depth protection strategy that includes three mutually supportive and reinforcing components: (1) penetration-resistant architecture, (2) damage-limiting operations, and (3) cyber resiliency.

senses.definitionMd: Security requirements that can be implemented in addition to the requirements in NIST Special Publication 800-171. The additional security requirements provide the foundation for a defense-in-depth protection strategy that includes three mutually supportive and reinforcing components: (1) penetration-resistant architecture, (2) damage-limiting operations, and (3) cyber resiliency.

entries.title: Enrollment
entries.summaryMd: The process of making a person’s identity known to the PIV system, associating a unique identifier with that identity, and collecting and recording the person’s relevant attributes into the system. In some other NIST documents, such as [NIST SP 800-63A], identity registration is referred to as enrollment.

senses.definitionMd: The process of making a person’s identity known to the PIV system, associating a unique identifier with that identity, and collecting and recording the person’s relevant attributes into the system. In some other NIST documents, such as [NIST SP 800-63A], identity registration is referred to as enrollment.

entries.title: Enrollment Data Set
entries.summaryMd: A record that includes information about a biometric enrollment (i.e., name and role of the acquiring agent, office and organization, time, place, and acquisition method).

senses.definitionMd: A record that includes information about a biometric enrollment (i.e., name and role of the acquiring agent, office and organization, time, place, and acquisition method).

entries.title: enrollment manager
entries.summaryMd: The management role that is responsible for assigning user identities to management and non-management roles.

senses.definitionMd: The management role that is responsible for assigning user identities to management and non-management roles.

entries.title: ensemble learning
entries.summaryMd: A type of a meta machine learning approach that combines the predic­tions of several models to improve performance.

senses.definitionMd: A type of a meta machine learning approach that combines the predic­tions of several models to improve performance.

entries.title: enterprise
entries.summaryMd: An organization that coordinates the operation of one or more processing sites.

senses.definitionMd: An organization that coordinates the operation of one or more processing sites.

entries.title: enterprise architecture (EA)
entries.summaryMd: The description of an enterprise’s entire set of information systems: how they are configured, how they are integrated, how they interface to the external environment at the enterprise’s boundary, how they are operated to support the enterprise mission, and how they contribute to the enterprise’s overall security posture.

senses.definitionMd: The description of an enterprise’s entire set of information systems: how they are configured, how they are integrated, how they interface to the external environment at the enterprise’s boundary, how they are operated to support the enterprise mission, and how they contribute to the enterprise’s overall security posture.

entries.title: enterprise cross domain services (ECDS)
entries.summaryMd: A set of cross domain services implemented by a government agency or an authorized commercial provider that is able to support a wide set of mission customers, provision new data flows via an established and timely process, and meet enterprise-level scalability and availability requirements, including support for connections to multiple security domains.

senses.definitionMd: A set of cross domain services implemented by a government agency or an authorized commercial provider that is able to support a wide set of mission customers, provision new data flows via an established and timely process, and meet enterprise-level scalability and availability requirements, including support for connections to multiple security domains.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "enterprise cross domain services (ECDS)"

entries.title: enterprise cross domain services (ECDS) provider
entries.summaryMd: An organization that establishes, manages and maintains the overall infrastructure and security posture offering automated capabilities to users and applications within an enterprise environment for information sharing across and among security domains.

senses.definitionMd: An organization that establishes, manages and maintains the overall infrastructure and security posture offering automated capabilities to users and applications within an enterprise environment for information sharing across and among security domains.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "enterprise cross domain services (ECDS) provider"

entries.title: enterprise-hosted cross domain solution
entries.summaryMd: A cross domain solution (CDS) that is managed by an enterprise cross domain service provider (ECDSP), but provides cross domain service to a dedicated customer. Enterprise-hosted CDS are frequently former point-to-point CDSs that have been moved from a customer site to an ECDSP.

senses.definitionMd: A cross domain solution (CDS) that is managed by an enterprise cross domain service provider (ECDSP), but provides cross domain service to a dedicated customer. Enterprise-hosted CDS are frequently former point-to-point CDSs that have been moved from a customer site to an ECDSP.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "enterprise-hosted cross domain solution"

entries.title: enterprise information technology
entries.summaryMd: The application of computers and telecommunications equipment to store, retrieve, transmit, and manipulate data, in the context of a business or other enterprise.

senses.definitionMd: The application of computers and telecommunications equipment to store, retrieve, transmit, and manipulate data, in the context of a business or other enterprise.

entries.title: Enterprise Mobility Management
entries.summaryMd: Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) systems are a common way of managing mobile devices in the enterprise. Although not a security technology by itself, EMMs can help to deploy policies to an enterprise’s device pool and to monitor device state.

senses.definitionMd: Enterprise Mobility Management (EMM) systems are a common way of managing mobile devices in the enterprise. Although not a security technology by itself, EMMs can help to deploy policies to an enterprise’s device pool and to monitor device state.

entries.title: enterprise patch management
entries.summaryMd: The process of identifying, prioritizing, acquiring, installing, and verifying the installation of patches, updates, and upgrades throughout an organization.

senses.definitionMd: The process of identifying, prioritizing, acquiring, installing, and verifying the installation of patches, updates, and upgrades throughout an organization.

entries.title: Enterprise Risk
entries.summaryMd: The effect of uncertainty on enterprise mission and objectives.

senses.definitionMd: The effect of uncertainty on enterprise mission and objectives.

entries.title: enterprise risk management
entries.summaryMd: The methods and processes used by an enterprise to manage risks to its mission and to establish the trust necessary for the enterprise to support shared missions. It involves the identification of mission dependencies on enterprise capabilities, the identification and prioritization of risks due to defined threats, the implementation of countermeasures to provide both a static risk posture and an effective dynamic response to active threats; and it assesses enterprise performance against threats and adjusts countermeasures as necessary.

senses.definitionMd: The methods and processes used by an enterprise to manage risks to its mission and to establish the trust necessary for the enterprise to support shared missions. It involves the identification of mission dependencies on enterprise capabilities, the identification and prioritization of risks due to defined threats, the implementation of countermeasures to provide both a static risk posture and an effective dynamic response to active threats; and it assesses enterprise performance against threats and adjusts countermeasures as necessary.

entries.title: Enterprise Risk Register
entries.summaryMd: A risk register at the enterprise level that contains normalized and aggregated inputs from subordinate organizations’ risk registers and profiles.

senses.definitionMd: A risk register at the enterprise level that contains normalized and aggregated inputs from subordinate organizations’ risk registers and profiles.

entries.title: enterprise service
entries.summaryMd: A set of one or more computer applications and middleware systems hosted on computer hardware that provides standard information systems capabilities to end users and hosted mission applications and services.

senses.definitionMd: A set of one or more computer applications and middleware systems hosted on computer hardware that provides standard information systems capabilities to end users and hosted mission applications and services.

entries.title: Enterprise Subsystem
entries.summaryMd: The portion of the RFID system that analyzes, processes, and stores information collected by the RF subsystem. The primary role of the enterprise subsystem is to make the data collected by the RF subsystem useful for a supporting business process. An enterprise subsystem is made up of middleware, analytic systems, and network infrastructure.

senses.definitionMd: The portion of the RFID system that analyzes, processes, and stores information collected by the RF subsystem. The primary role of the enterprise subsystem is to make the data collected by the RF subsystem useful for a supporting business process. An enterprise subsystem is made up of middleware, analytic systems, and network infrastructure.

entries.title: entity
entries.summaryMd: An individual (person), organization, device or process. Used interchangeably with “party.”

senses.definitionMd: An individual (person), organization, device or process. Used interchangeably with “party.”

entries.title: Entity authentication
entries.summaryMd: The process of providing assurance about the identity of an entity interacting with a system (e.g., to access a resource). Also see Source authentication.

senses.definitionMd: The process of providing assurance about the identity of an entity interacting with a system (e.g., to access a resource). Also see Source authentication.

entries.title: Entity registration
entries.summaryMd: A function in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key; a process whereby an entity becomes a member of a security domain.

senses.definitionMd: A function in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key; a process whereby an entity becomes a member of a security domain.

entries.title: Entropy
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the disorder or randomness in a closed system. The entropy of uncertainty of a random variable X with probabilities pi, …, pn is defined to be H(X)=-∑_(i=1)^n 〖p_i log〖 p〗_i 〗

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the disorder or randomness in a closed system. The entropy of uncertainty of a random variable X with probabilities pi, …, pn is defined to be H(X)=-∑_(i=1)^n 〖p_i log〖 p〗_i 〗

entries.title: Entropy Input
entries.summaryMd: An input bitstring that provides an assessed minimum amount of unpredictability for a DRBG mechanism. (See min-entropy.)

senses.definitionMd: An input bitstring that provides an assessed minimum amount of unpredictability for a DRBG mechanism. (See min-entropy.)

entries.title: Entropy rate
entries.summaryMd: The rate at which a digitized noise source (or entropy source) provides entropy; it is computed as the assessed amount of entropy provided by a bitstring output from the source, divided by the total number of bits in the bitstring (yielding the assessed bits of entropy per output bit). This will be a value between zero (no entropy) and one.

senses.definitionMd: The rate at which a digitized noise source (or entropy source) provides entropy; it is computed as the assessed amount of entropy provided by a bitstring output from the source, divided by the total number of bits in the bitstring (yielding the assessed bits of entropy per output bit). This will be a value between zero (no entropy) and one.

entries.title: Entropy Source
entries.summaryMd: A physical source of information whose output either appears to be random in itself or by applying some filtering/distillation process. This output is used as input to either a RNG or PRNG.

senses.definitionMd: A physical source of information whose output either appears to be random in itself or by applying some filtering/distillation process. This output is used as input to either a RNG or PRNG.

entries.title: environment
entries.summaryMd: Aggregate of external procedures, conditions, and objects affecting the development, operation, and maintenance of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Aggregate of external procedures, conditions, and objects affecting the development, operation, and maintenance of an information system.

entries.title: environment conditions
entries.summaryMd: Dynamic factors, independent of subject and object, that may be used as attributes at decision time to influence an access decision.

senses.definitionMd: Dynamic factors, independent of subject and object, that may be used as attributes at decision time to influence an access decision.

entries.title: environment of operation
entries.summaryMd: The physical surroundings in which an information system processes, stores, and transmits information.

senses.definitionMd: The physical surroundings in which an information system processes, stores, and transmits information.

entries.title: Environmental Support
entries.summaryMd: Any environmental factor for which the organization determines that it needs to continue to provide support in a contingency situation, even if in a degraded state. This could include factors such as power, air conditioning, humidity control, fire protection, lighting, etc. For example, while developing the contingency plan, the organization may determine that it is necessary to continue to ensure the appropriate temperature and humidity during a contingency situation so they would plan for the capacity to support that via supplemental/mobile air conditioning units, backup power, etc. and the associated procedures to ensure cutover operations. Such determinations are based on an assessment of risk, system categorization (impact level), and organizational risk tolerance.

senses.definitionMd: Any environmental factor for which the organization determines that it needs to continue to provide support in a contingency situation, even if in a degraded state. This could include factors such as power, air conditioning, humidity control, fire protection, lighting, etc. For example, while developing the contingency plan, the organization may determine that it is necessary to continue to ensure the appropriate temperature and humidity during a contingency situation so they would plan for the capacity to support that via supplemental/mobile air conditioning units, backup power, etc. and the associated procedures to ensure cutover operations. Such determinations are based on an assessment of risk, system categorization (impact level), and organizational risk tolerance.

entries.title: Environmental testing
entries.summaryMd: Evaluating the behavior of a device or system to obtain assurance that it will not be compromised by environmental conditions or fluctuations when operating outside the normal environmental operating range.

senses.definitionMd: Evaluating the behavior of a device or system to obtain assurance that it will not be compromised by environmental conditions or fluctuations when operating outside the normal environmental operating range.

entries.title: EO-critical software
entries.summaryMd: Any software that has, or has direct software dependencies upon, one or more components with at least one of these attributes: · is designed to run with elevated privilege or manage privileges; · has direct or privileged access to networking or computing resources; · is designed to control access to data or operational technology; · performs a function critical to trust; or, · operates outside of normal trust boundaries with privileged access.

senses.definitionMd: Any software that has, or has direct software dependencies upon, one or more components with at least one of these attributes: · is designed to run with elevated privilege or manage privileges; · has direct or privileged access to networking or computing resources; · is designed to control access to data or operational technology; · performs a function critical to trust; or, · operates outside of normal trust boundaries with privileged access.

entries.title: Ephemeral Key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key that is generated for each execution of a key-establishment process and that meets other requirements of the key type (e.g., unique to each message or session).

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key that is generated for each execution of a key-establishment process and that meets other requirements of the key type (e.g., unique to each message or session).

entries.title: Ephemeral key pair
entries.summaryMd: A short-term key pair used with a public-key (asymmetric-key) algorithm that is generated when needed; the public key of an ephemeral key pair is not provided in a public key certificate, unlike static public keys which are often included in a certificate.

senses.definitionMd: A short-term key pair used with a public-key (asymmetric-key) algorithm that is generated when needed; the public key of an ephemeral key pair is not provided in a public key certificate, unlike static public keys which are often included in a certificate.

entries.title: Equivalent inverse cipher
entries.summaryMd: An alternative specification of the inverse of CIPHER() with a structure similar to that of CIPHER() and with a modified key schedule as input.

senses.definitionMd: An alternative specification of the inverse of CIPHER() with a structure similar to that of CIPHER() and with a modified key schedule as input.

entries.title: Equivalent Process
entries.summaryMd: Two processes are equivalent if the same output is produced when the same values are input to each process (either as input parameters, as values made available during the process, or both).

senses.definitionMd: Two processes are equivalent if the same output is produced when the same values are input to each process (either as input parameters, as values made available during the process, or both).

entries.title: Equivalent security domains
entries.summaryMd: Two or more security domains that have FCKMS security policies that have been determined to provide equivalent protection for the information.

senses.definitionMd: Two or more security domains that have FCKMS security policies that have been determined to provide equivalent protection for the information.

entries.title: erasure
entries.summaryMd: Process intended to render magnetically stored information irretrievable by normal means.

senses.definitionMd: Process intended to render magnetically stored information irretrievable by normal means.

entries.title: Erfc
entries.summaryMd: See Erfc.

senses.definitionMd: See Erfc.

entries.title: error
entries.summaryMd: The difference between desired and actual performance or behavior of a system or system element.

senses.definitionMd: The difference between desired and actual performance or behavior of a system or system element.

entries.title: error detection code
entries.summaryMd: A code computed from data and comprised of redundant bits of information designed to detect, but not correct, unintentional changes in the data.

senses.definitionMd: A code computed from data and comprised of redundant bits of information designed to detect, but not correct, unintentional changes in the data.

entries.title: ES(nBits)
entries.summaryMd: The estimated maximum security strength for an RSA modulus of length nBits (see Table 2).

senses.definitionMd: The estimated maximum security strength for an RSA modulus of length nBits (see Table 2).

entries.title: Escape
entries.summaryMd: The act of breaking out of a guest OS to gain access to the hypervisor, other guest OSs, or the underlying host OS.

senses.definitionMd: The act of breaking out of a guest OS to gain access to the hypervisor, other guest OSs, or the underlying host OS.

entries.title: Estimate
entries.summaryMd: The estimated value of a parameter, as computed using an estimator.

senses.definitionMd: The estimated value of a parameter, as computed using an estimator.

entries.title: Estimated maximum security strength
entries.summaryMd: An estimate of the largest security strength that can be attained by a cryptographic mechanism given the explicit and implicit assumptions that are made regarding its implementation and supporting infrastructure (e.g., the algorithms employed, the selection of associated primitives and/or auxiliary functions, the choices for various parameters, the methods of generation and/or protection for any required keys, etc.). The estimated maximum security strengths of various approved cryptographic mechanisms are provided in [SP 800-57].

senses.definitionMd: An estimate of the largest security strength that can be attained by a cryptographic mechanism given the explicit and implicit assumptions that are made regarding its implementation and supporting infrastructure (e.g., the algorithms employed, the selection of associated primitives and/or auxiliary functions, the choices for various parameters, the methods of generation and/or protection for any required keys, etc.). The estimated maximum security strengths of various approved cryptographic mechanisms are provided in [SP 800-57].

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Estimated maximum security strength"

entries.title: Estimator
entries.summaryMd: A technique for estimating the value of a parameter.

senses.definitionMd: A technique for estimating the value of a parameter.

entries.title: Evaluated Products List
entries.summaryMd: List of validated products that have been successfully evaluated under the National Information Assurance Partnership (NIAP) Common Criteria Evaluation and Validation Scheme (CCEVS). Rationale: EPL is no longer used. Product compliant list (PCL) is the replacement term.

senses.definitionMd: List of validated products that have been successfully evaluated under the National Information Assurance Partnership (NIAP) Common Criteria Evaluation and Validation Scheme (CCEVS). Rationale: EPL is no longer used. Product compliant list (PCL) is the replacement term.

entries.title: evaluating authority
entries.summaryMd: The official responsible for evaluating a reported COMSEC incident for the possibility of compromise.

senses.definitionMd: The official responsible for evaluating a reported COMSEC incident for the possibility of compromise.

entries.title: Evaluation Assurance Level
entries.summaryMd: Set of assurance requirements that represent a point on the Common Criteria predefined assurance scale. Rationale: NIAP has switched to a “protection profile” program to secure devices.

senses.definitionMd: Set of assurance requirements that represent a point on the Common Criteria predefined assurance scale. Rationale: NIAP has switched to a “protection profile” program to secure devices.

entries.title: evaluation criteria
entries.summaryMd: The standards by which accomplishments of technical and operational effectiveness or suitability characteristics may be assessed. Evaluation criteria are a benchmark, standard, or factor against which conformance, performance, and suitability of a technical capability, activity, product, or plan is measured.

senses.definitionMd: The standards by which accomplishments of technical and operational effectiveness or suitability characteristics may be assessed. Evaluation criteria are a benchmark, standard, or factor against which conformance, performance, and suitability of a technical capability, activity, product, or plan is measured.

entries.title: event
entries.summaryMd: Occurrence or change of a particular set of circumstances.

senses.definitionMd: Occurrence or change of a particular set of circumstances.

entries.title: Event Aggregation
entries.summaryMd: See “Event Aggregation”.

senses.definitionMd: See “Event Aggregation”.

entries.title: Event Correlation
entries.summaryMd: See “Event Correlation”.

senses.definitionMd: See “Event Correlation”.

entries.title: Event Filtering
entries.summaryMd: The suppression of log entries from analysis, reporting, or long-term storage because their characteristics indicate that they are unlikely to contain information of interest.

senses.definitionMd: The suppression of log entries from analysis, reporting, or long-term storage because their characteristics indicate that they are unlikely to contain information of interest.

entries.title: event‐level privacy

entries.summaryMd: The set of all features associated with a single artifact is its feature set. Each algorithm must include a criteria by which candidate features are selected for inclusion in this set. For example, an algorithm might select all the (byte, offset) pairs produced by reading every 16th byte in the artifact.

entries.title: Features
entries.summaryMd: The basic elements through which artifacts are compared. Comparison of two features always yields a binary {0, 1} outcome indicating a match or non-match; because features are defined as the most basic comparison unit that the algorithm considers, partial matches are not permitted. Generally, a feature can be any value derived from an artifact. Each approximate matching algorithm must define the structure of its features and the method by which they are derived. For example, an algorithm might define a feature as a (byte, offset) pair produced by reading the value of a byte and storing it along with the offset at which it was read.

entries.title: frequency
entries.summaryMd: The rate of a repetitive event. If T is the period of a repetitive event, then the frequency f is its reciprocal, 1/T. Conversely, the period is the reciprocal of the frequency, T = 1 / f. Because the period is a time interval expressed in seconds (s), it is easy to see the close relationship between time interval and frequency. The standard unit for frequency is the hertz (Hz), defined as the number of events or cycles per second. The frequency of electrical signals is often measured in multiples of hertz, including kilohertz (kHz), megahertz (MHz), or gigahertz (GHz).

entries.title: frequency stability

It is important to note the time interval—some devices have good short-term stability while others have good long-term stability. Stability does not determine whether the frequency of a signal is right or wrong. It only indicates whether that frequency stays the same. The Allan deviation is the most common metric used to estimate frequency stability, but several similar statistics are also used.

entries.title: Hash chain
entries.summaryMd: An append-only data structure where data is bundled into data blocks that include a hash of the previous data block’s data within the newest data block. entries.title: hash digest

senses.definitionMd: The result of applying a hash function to data.

entries.title: Hash_DRBG

entries.title: hash function
entries.summaryMd: A function on bit strings in which the length of the output is fixed. Approved hash functions (such as those specified in FIPS 180 and FIPS 202) are designed to satisfy the following properties:1. (One-way) It is computationally infeasible to find any input that maps to any new pre-specified output2. (Collision-resistant) It is computationally infeasible to find any two distinct inputs that map to the same output.

senses.definitionMd: A function on bit strings in which the length of the output is fixed. entries.title: hash value/result

senses.definitionMd: The result of applying a hash function to a message. Also known as a “hash value.”
