entries.summaryMd: The process whereby data (e.g., a message) was input to a cryptographic hash function (see Cryptographic hash function) to produce a hash value (see Hash value).

senses.definitionMd: The process whereby data (e.g., a message) was input to a cryptographic hash function (see Cryptographic hash function) to produce a hash value (see Hash value).

entries.summaryMd: The process of using a mathematical algorithm against data to produce a numeric value that is representative of that data.

entries.title: hidden Markov model
entries.summaryMd: A Markov model in which the system being modeled is assumed to be a Markov process with unobservable states. The model provides an observ­able process whose outcomes are influenced by the outcomes of a Markov model in a known way. An HMM can be used to describe the evolution of observable events that depend on internal factors that are not directly observable. In ma­chine learning, it is assumed that the internal state of a model is hidden but not its hyperparameters.

Host keys are used for authenticating hosts (machines) themselves, not users or accounts, whereas identity keys and authorized keys relate to authenticating users/accounts and authorizing access to accounts on hosts.

entries.title: IA architecture

Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

senses.definitionMd: A description of the structure and behavior for an enterprise’s security processes, information security systems, personnel and organizational sub- units, showing their alignment with the enterprise’s mission and strategic plans. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

entries.title: IA-enabled information technology product
entries.summaryMd: Product or technology whose primary role is not security, but which provides security services as an associated feature of its intended operating capabilities. Examples include such products as security-enabled web browsers, screening routers, trusted operating systems, and security-enabled messaging systems. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms. Rationale: Listed for deletion in 2010 version of CNSS 4009.

entries.title: IA-enabled product
entries.summaryMd: Product whose primary role is not security, but provides security services as an associated feature of its intended operating capabilities. Note: Examples include such products as security-enabled web browsers, screening routers, trusted operating systems, and security enabling messaging systems. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

entries.title: IA infrastructure
entries.summaryMd: The underlying security framework that lies beyond an enterprise’s defined boundary, but supports its information assurance (IA) and IA-enabled products, its security posture and its risk management plan. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

entries.title: IA product
entries.summaryMd: Product whose primary purpose is to provide security services (e.g., confidentiality, authentication, integrity, access control, non-repudiation of data); correct known vulnerabilities; and/or provide layered defense against various categories of non-authorized or malicious penetrations of information systems or networks. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

entries.title: ICT/OT-related service providers
entries.summaryMd: Any organization or individual providing services which may include authorized access to an ICT or OT system.

senses.definitionMd: Any organization or individual providing services which may include authorized access to an ICT or OT system.

entries.title: ICT Supply Chain
entries.summaryMd: Linked set of resources and processes between acquirers, integrators, and suppliers that begins with the design of ICT products and services and extends through development, sourcing, manufacturing, handling, and delivery of ICT products and services to the acquirer.

senses.definitionMd: Linked set of resources and processes between acquirers, integrators, and suppliers that begins with the design of ICT products and services and extends through development, sourcing, manufacturing, handling, and delivery of ICT products and services to the acquirer.

entries.title: ICT Supply Chain Risk
entries.summaryMd: Risks that arise from the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or information systems and reflect the potential adverse impacts to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.

senses.definitionMd: Risks that arise from the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or information systems and reflect the potential adverse impacts to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "ICT Supply Chain Risk"

entries.title: ICT Supply Chain Risk Management
entries.summaryMd: The process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating the risks associated with the global and distributed nature of ICT product and service supply chains.

senses.definitionMd: The process of identifying, assessing, and mitigating the risks associated with the global and distributed nature of ICT product and service supply chains.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "ICT Supply Chain Risk Management"

entries.summaryMd: See Ideal Random Sequence.

entries.title: identifiable person
entries.summaryMd: one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identification number or to one or more factors specific to his physical, physiological, mental, economic, cultural or social identity

senses.definitionMd: one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identification number or to one or more factors specific to his physical, physiological, mental, economic, cultural or social identity

entries.title: identification
entries.summaryMd: The process of discovering the identity (i.e., origin or initial history) of a person or item from the entire collection of similar persons or items.

senses.definitionMd: The process of discovering the identity (i.e., origin or initial history) of a person or item from the entire collection of similar persons or items.

entries.title: Identification and Authentication
entries.summaryMd: The process of establishing the identity of an entity interacting with a system.

senses.definitionMd: The process of establishing the identity of an entity interacting with a system.

entries.title: identified information
entries.summaryMd: information that explicitly identifies an individual

senses.definitionMd: information that explicitly identifies an individual

entries.title: identifier
entries.summaryMd: Unique data used to represent a person’s identity and associated attributes. A name or a card number are examples of identifiers.

senses.definitionMd: Unique data used to represent a person’s identity and associated attributes. A name or a card number are examples of identifiers.

entries.title: Identifier CPE Name
entries.summaryMd: A bound representation of a CPE WFN that uniquely identifies a single product class. Also referred to as an “identifier name”.

senses.definitionMd: A bound representation of a CPE WFN that uniquely identifies a single product class. Also referred to as an “identifier name”.

entries.title: Identifier Lookup
entries.summaryMd: The process of determining if a single identifier name exists in a CPE dictionary.

senses.definitionMd: The process of determining if a single identifier name exists in a CPE dictionary.

entries.title: Identify
entries.summaryMd: The bit string denoting the identifier associated with an entity.

senses.definitionMd: The bit string denoting the identifier associated with an entity.

entries.title: identify (CSF function)
entries.summaryMd: The bit string denoting the identifier associated with an entity.

senses.definitionMd: The bit string denoting the identifier associated with an entity.

entries.title: Identify-P (Function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop the organizational understanding to manage privacy risk for individuals arising from data processing.

senses.definitionMd: Develop the organizational understanding to manage privacy risk for individuals arising from data processing.

entries.title: Identifying Information
entries.summaryMd: Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual.

senses.definitionMd: Information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual's identity, either alone or when combined with other information that is linked or linkable to a specific individual.

entries.title: identity
entries.summaryMd: The set of physical and behavioral characteristics by which an individual is uniquely recognizable.

senses.definitionMd: The set of physical and behavioral characteristics by which an individual is uniquely recognizable.

entries.title: Identity and access management
entries.summaryMd: Broadly refers to the administration of individual identities within a system, such as a company, a network or even a country. In enterprise IT, identity management is about establishing and managing the roles and access privileges of individual network users.

senses.definitionMd: Broadly refers to the administration of individual identities within a system, such as a company, a network or even a country. In enterprise IT, identity management is about establishing and managing the roles and access privileges of individual network users.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Identity and access management"

entries.title: identity API
entries.summaryMd: A protected API that is accessed by an RP to retrieve the attributes of a specific subscriber.

senses.definitionMd: A protected API that is accessed by an RP to retrieve the attributes of a specific subscriber.

entries.title: Identity Assurance Level (IAL)
entries.summaryMd: A category that conveys the degree of confidence that a person’s claimed identity is their real identity, as defined in [NIST SP 800-63-3] in terms of three levels: IAL 1 (Some confidence), IAL 2 (High confidence), IAL 3 (Very high confidence).

senses.definitionMd: A category that conveys the degree of confidence that a person’s claimed identity is their real identity, as defined in [NIST SP 800-63-3] in terms of three levels: IAL 1 (Some confidence), IAL 2 (High confidence), IAL 3 (Very high confidence).

entries.title: Identity authentication
entries.summaryMd: The process of providing assurance about the identity of an entity interacting with a system; also see Source authentication.

senses.definitionMd: The process of providing assurance about the identity of an entity interacting with a system; also see Source authentication.

entries.title: identity-based access control
entries.summaryMd: Access control based on the identity of the user (typically relayed as a characteristic of the process acting on behalf of that user) where access authorizations to specific objects are assigned based on user identity.

senses.definitionMd: Access control based on the identity of the user (typically relayed as a characteristic of the process acting on behalf of that user) where access authorizations to specific objects are assigned based on user identity.

entries.title: Identity-based authentication
entries.summaryMd: A process that provides assurance of an entity’s identity by means of an authentication mechanism that verifies the identity of the entity. Contrast with role-based authentication

senses.definitionMd: A process that provides assurance of an entity’s identity by means of an authentication mechanism that verifies the identity of the entity. Contrast with role-based authentication

entries.title: identity certificate
entries.summaryMd: A certificate that provides authentication of the identity claimed. Within the National Security System (NSS) public key infrastructure (PKI), identity certificates may be used only for authentication or may be used for both authentication and digital signatures.

senses.definitionMd: A certificate that provides authentication of the identity claimed. Within the National Security System (NSS) public key infrastructure (PKI), identity certificates may be used only for authentication or may be used for both authentication and digital signatures.

entries.title: Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM)
entries.summaryMd: Programs, processes, technologies, and personnel used to create trusted digital identity representations of individuals and non-person entities (NPEs), bind those identities to credentials that may serve as a proxy for the individual or NPE in access transactions, and leverage the credentials to provide authorized access to an agency‘s resources. See also attribute-based access control (ABAC).

senses.definitionMd: Programs, processes, technologies, and personnel used to create trusted digital identity representations of individuals and non-person entities (NPEs), bind those identities to credentials that may serve as a proxy for the individual or NPE in access transactions, and leverage the credentials to provide authorized access to an agency‘s resources. See also attribute-based access control (ABAC).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM)"

entries.title: Identity Ecosystem
entries.summaryMd: An online environment where individuals can choose from a variety of credentials to use in lieu of passwords for interactions conducted across the internet.

senses.definitionMd: An online environment where individuals can choose from a variety of credentials to use in lieu of passwords for interactions conducted across the internet.

entries.title: Identity Federation
entries.summaryMd: A group of organizations that agree to follow the rules of a trust framework.

senses.definitionMd: A group of organizations that agree to follow the rules of a trust framework.

entries.title: Identity Fraud and Identity Theft
entries.summaryMd: Identity theft and identity fraud are terms used to refer to all types of crime in which someone wrongfully obtains and uses another personʼs personal data in some way that involves fraud or deception, typically for economic gain.

senses.definitionMd: Identity theft and identity fraud are terms used to refer to all types of crime in which someone wrongfully obtains and uses another personʼs personal data in some way that involves fraud or deception, typically for economic gain.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Identity Fraud and Identity Theft"

entries.title: Identity Key
entries.summaryMd: A private key that is used for authentication in the SSH protocol; grants access to the accounts for which the corresponding public key has been configured as an authorized key.

senses.definitionMd: A private key that is used for authentication in the SSH protocol; grants access to the accounts for which the corresponding public key has been configured as an authorized key.

entries.title: Identity Management System (IDMS)
entries.summaryMd: One or more systems or applications that manage the identity proofing, registration, and issuance processes.

senses.definitionMd: One or more systems or applications that manage the identity proofing, registration, and issuance processes.

entries.title: identity proofing
entries.summaryMd: The process of providing sufficient information (e.g., identity history, credentials, documents) to establish an identity.

senses.definitionMd: The process of providing sufficient information (e.g., identity history, credentials, documents) to establish an identity.

entries.title: Identity Provider (IdP)
entries.summaryMd: A trusted entity that issues or registers subscriber authenticators and issues electronic credentials to subscribers. A CSP may be an independent third party or issue credentials for its own use.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted entity that issues or registers subscriber authenticators and issues electronic credentials to subscribers. A CSP may be an independent third party or issue credentials for its own use.

entries.title: identity registration
entries.summaryMd: The process of making a person’s identity known to the PIV system, associating a unique identifier with that identity, and collecting and recording the person’s relevant attributes into the system. In some other NIST documents, such as [NIST SP 800-63A], identity registration is referred to as enrollment.

senses.definitionMd: The process of making a person’s identity known to the PIV system, associating a unique identifier with that identity, and collecting and recording the person’s relevant attributes into the system. In some other NIST documents, such as [NIST SP 800-63A], identity registration is referred to as enrollment.

entries.title: identity resolution
entries.summaryMd: The process of collecting information about an applicant to uniquely distinguish an individual within the context of the population that the CSP serves.

senses.definitionMd: The process of collecting information about an applicant to uniquely distinguish an individual within the context of the population that the CSP serves.

entries.title: Identity Service Provider (ISP)
entries.summaryMd: A trusted entity that issues or registers subscriber authenticators and issues electronic credentials to subscribers. A CSP may be an independent third party or issue credentials for its own use.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted entity that issues or registers subscriber authenticators and issues electronic credentials to subscribers. A CSP may be an independent third party or issue credentials for its own use.

entries.title: identity token
entries.summaryMd: Smart card, metal key, or other physical object used to authenticate identity.

senses.definitionMd: Smart card, metal key, or other physical object used to authenticate identity.

entries.title: identity verification
entries.summaryMd: The process of confirming or denying that a claimed identity is correct by comparing the credentials of a person requesting access with those previously proven and associated with the PIV Card or a derived PIV credential associated with the identity being claimed.

senses.definitionMd: The process of confirming or denying that a claimed identity is correct by comparing the credentials of a person requesting access with those previously proven and associated with the PIV Card or a derived PIV credential associated with the identity being claimed.

entries.title: IDP, IDR, IDU, IDV
entries.summaryMd: Identifier bit strings for parties P, R, U, and V, respectively.

senses.definitionMd: Identifier bit strings for parties P, R, U, and V, respectively.

entries.title: Ij

senses.definitionMd: The jth input block.

entries.title: Image
entries.summaryMd: An exact bit-stream copy of all electronic data on a device, performed in a manner that ensures the information is not altered.

senses.definitionMd: An exact bit-stream copy of all electronic data on a device, performed in a manner that ensures the information is not altered.

entries.title: Imaging
entries.summaryMd: The process used to obtain a bit by bit copy of data residing on the original electronic media; allows the investigator to review a duplicate of the original evidence while preserving that evidence

entries.title: Immutable
entries.summaryMd: Data that can only be written, not modified or deleted.

senses.definitionMd: Data that can only be written, not modified or deleted.

entries.title: impact
entries.summaryMd: The magnitude of harm that can be expected to result from the consequences of unauthorized disclosure of information, unauthorized modification of information, unauthorized destruction of information, or loss of information or information system availability.

senses.definitionMd: The magnitude of harm that can be expected to result from the consequences of unauthorized disclosure of information, unauthorized modification of information, unauthorized destruction of information, or loss of information or information system availability.

entries.title: impact level
entries.summaryMd: The assessed potential impact resulting from a compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information type, expressed as a value of low, moderate, or high.

senses.definitionMd: The assessed potential impact resulting from a compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information type, expressed as a value of low, moderate, or high.

entries.title: impact value
entries.summaryMd: The assessed potential impact resulting from a compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information type, expressed as a value of low, moderate, or high.

senses.definitionMd: The assessed potential impact resulting from a compromise of the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information type, expressed as a value of low, moderate, or high.

entries.title: implant
entries.summaryMd: Electronic device or electronic equipment modification designed to gain unauthorized interception of information-bearing emanations.

senses.definitionMd: Electronic device or electronic equipment modification designed to gain unauthorized interception of information-bearing emanations.

entries.title: Implementation
entries.summaryMd: An implementation of an RBG is a cryptographic device or portion of a cryptographic device that is the physical embodiment of the RBG design, for example, some code running on a computing platform.

senses.definitionMd: An implementation of an RBG is a cryptographic device or portion of a cryptographic device that is the physical embodiment of the RBG design, for example, some code running on a computing platform.

entries.title: Implementation Testing for Validation
entries.summaryMd: Testing by an independent and accredited party to ensure that an implementation of this Recommendation conforms to the specifications of this Recommendation.

entries.title: Implementation Tier
entries.summaryMd: Provides a point of reference on how an organization views privacy risk and whether it has sufficient processes and resources in place to manage that risk.

entries.summaryMd: Implementation Under Test

entries.title: Import
entries.summaryMd: A process available to end users by which an SCAP source data stream can be loaded into the vendor’s product. During this process, the vendor process may optionally translate this file into a proprietary format.

entries.title: imputation
entries.summaryMd: A procedure for entering a value for a specific data item where the response is missing or unusable.

entries.title: inadvertent disclosure
entries.summaryMd: Type of incident involving accidental exposure of information to an individual not authorized access.

entries.title: Incentive Mechanism
entries.summaryMd: See Incentive Mechanism

senses.definitionMd: See Incentive Mechanism

entries.title: incident
entries.summaryMd: An occurrence that actually or potentially jeopardizes the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system or the information the system processes, stores, or transmits or that constitutes a violation or imminent threat of violation of security policies, security procedures, or acceptable use policies.

senses.definitionMd: An occurrence that actually or potentially jeopardizes the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system or the information the system processes, stores, or transmits or that constitutes a violation or imminent threat of violation of security policies, security procedures, or acceptable use policies.

entries.title: incident handling
entries.summaryMd: The mitigation of violations of security policies and recommended practices.

senses.definitionMd: The mitigation of violations of security policies and recommended practices.

entries.title: incident response
entries.summaryMd: The mitigation of violations of security policies and recommended practices.

senses.definitionMd: The mitigation of violations of security policies and recommended practices.

entries.title: incident response plan
entries.summaryMd: The documentation of a predetermined set of instructions or procedures to detect, respond to, and limit consequences of a malicious cyber attacks against an organization’s information systems(s).

senses.definitionMd: The documentation of a predetermined set of instructions or procedures to detect, respond to, and limit consequences of a malicious cyber attacks against an organization’s information systems(s).

entries.title: Incomplete Gamma Function
entries.summaryMd: The incomplete gamma function Q(a,x) is defined in Section 5.5.3.

senses.definitionMd: The incomplete gamma function Q(a,x) is defined in Section 5.5.3.

entries.title: Incremental testing
entries.summaryMd: Testing a system or device to determine that minor changes have not affected its security and intended functionality.

senses.definitionMd: Testing a system or device to determine that minor changes have not affected its security and intended functionality.

entries.title: incs(X)
entries.summaryMd: The output of incrementing the right-most s bits of the bit string X, regarded as the binary representation of an integer, by 1 modulo 2s.

senses.definitionMd: The output of incrementing the right-most s bits of the bit string X, regarded as the binary representation of an integer, by 1 modulo 2s.

entries.title: Inculpatory Evidence
entries.summaryMd: Evidence that tends to increase the likelihood of fault or guilt.

senses.definitionMd: Evidence that tends to increase the likelihood of fault or guilt.

entries.title: Independent
entries.summaryMd: Two random variables X and Y are independent if they do not convey information about each other. Receiving information about X does not change the assessment of the probability distribution of Y (and vice versa).

senses.definitionMd: Two random variables X and Y are independent if they do not convey information about each other. Receiving information about X does not change the assessment of the probability distribution of Y (and vice versa).

entries.title: Independent and Identically Distributed
entries.summaryMd: A quality of a sequence of random variables for which each element of the sequence has the same probability distribution as the other values, and all values are mutually independent.

senses.definitionMd: A quality of a sequence of random variables for which each element of the sequence has the same probability distribution as the other values, and all values are mutually independent.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Independent and Identically Distributed"

entries.title: Independent Qualified Reviewer
entries.summaryMd: A Reviewer tasked by NIST with making a recommendation to NIST regarding public review or listing of the checklist.

senses.definitionMd: A Reviewer tasked by NIST with making a recommendation to NIST regarding public review or listing of the checklist.

entries.title: Independent Regulatory Agency
entries.summaryMd: The term 'independent regulatory agency' means the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the Consumer Product Safety Commission, the Federal Communications Commission, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, the Federal Housing Finance Board, the Federal Maritime Commission, the Federal Trade Commission, the Interstate Commerce Commission, the Mine Enforcement Safety and Health Review Commission, the National Labor Relations Board, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission, the Postal Rate Commission, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and any other similar agency designated by statute as a Federal independent regulatory agency or commission.

senses.definitionMd: The term 'independent regulatory agency' means the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the Consumer Product Safety Commission, the Federal Communications Commission, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, the Federal Housing Finance Board, the Federal Maritime Commission, the Federal Trade Commission, the Interstate Commerce Commission, the Mine Enforcement Safety and Health Review Commission, the National Labor Relations Board, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission, the Postal Rate Commission, the Securities and Exchange Commission, and any other similar agency designated by statute as a Federal independent regulatory agency or commission.

entries.title: independent validation authority (IVA)
entries.summaryMd: Entity that reviews the soundness of independent tests and system compliance with all stated security controls and risk mitigation actions. IVAs will be designated by the authorizing official as needed.

senses.definitionMd: Entity that reviews the soundness of independent tests and system compliance with all stated security controls and risk mitigation actions. IVAs will be designated by the authorizing official as needed.

entries.title: independent verification & validation (IV&V)
entries.summaryMd: A comprehensive review, analysis, and testing, (software and/or hardware) performed by an objective third party to confirm (i.e., verify) that the requirements are correctly defined, and to confirm (i.e., validate) that the system correctly implements the required functionality and security requirements.

senses.definitionMd: A comprehensive review, analysis, and testing, (software and/or hardware) performed by an objective third party to confirm (i.e., verify) that the requirements are correctly defined, and to confirm (i.e., validate) that the system correctly implements the required functionality and security requirements.

entries.title: indicator
entries.summaryMd: A pattern of relevant observable adversary activity in the operational cyber domain.

senses.definitionMd: A pattern of relevant observable adversary activity in the operational cyber domain.

entries.title: Indicator of Compromise
entries.summaryMd: Technical artifacts or observables that suggest that an attack is imminent or is currently underway or that a compromise may have already occurred.

senses.definitionMd: Technical artifacts or observables that suggest that an attack is imminent or is currently underway or that a compromise may have already occurred.

entries.title: indirect identifier
entries.summaryMd: information that can be used to identify an individual through association with other information

senses.definitionMd: information that can be used to identify an individual through association with other information

entries.title: indirect prompt injection
entries.summaryMd: A type of prompt injection executed through resource control rather than through user-provided input as in a direct prompt injection.

senses.definitionMd: A type of prompt injection executed through resource control rather than through user-provided input as in a direct prompt injection.

entries.title: Individual
entries.summaryMd: A citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence. Agencies may, consistent with individual practice, choose to extend the protections of the Privacy Act and E-Government Act to businesses, sole proprietors, aliens, etc.

senses.definitionMd: A citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence. Agencies may, consistent with individual practice, choose to extend the protections of the Privacy Act and E-Government Act to businesses, sole proprietors, aliens, etc.

entries.title: individual accountability
entries.summaryMd: Ability to associate positively the identity of a user with the time, method, and degree of access to an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Ability to associate positively the identity of a user with the time, method, and degree of access to an information system.

entries.title: individuals
entries.summaryMd: An assessment object that includes people applying specifications, mechanisms, or activities.

senses.definitionMd: An assessment object that includes people applying specifications, mechanisms, or activities.

entries.title: industrial control system (ICS)
entries.summaryMd: An information system used to control industrial processes such as manufacturing, product handling, production, and distribution. Industrial control systems include supervisory control and data acquisition systems used to control geographically dispersed assets, as well as distributed control systems and smaller control systems using programmable logic controllers to control localized processes.

senses.definitionMd: An information system used to control industrial processes such as manufacturing, product handling, production, and distribution. Industrial control systems include supervisory control and data acquisition systems used to control geographically dispersed assets, as well as distributed control systems and smaller control systems using programmable logic controllers to control localized processes.

entries.title: Industrial Security
entries.summaryMd: The portion of internal security that refers to the protection of industrial installations, resources, utilities, materials, and classified information essential to protect from loss or damage.

senses.definitionMd: The portion of internal security that refers to the protection of industrial installations, resources, utilities, materials, and classified information essential to protect from loss or damage.

entries.title: infeasible
entries.summaryMd: Infeasible acknowledges the possibility of data recovery with future, more advanced technology. It simply means that, for a given level of effort and using current "state of the art" techniques, recovery cannot be done.

senses.definitionMd: Infeasible acknowledges the possibility of data recovery with future, more advanced technology. It simply means that, for a given level of effort and using current "state of the art" techniques, recovery cannot be done.

entries.title: inference
entries.summaryMd: Refers to the ability to deduce the identity of a person associated with a set of data through “clues” contained in that information. This analysis permits determination of the individual’s identity based on a combination of facts associated with that person even though specific identifiers have been removed, like name and social security number.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to the ability to deduce the identity of a person associated with a set of data through “clues” contained in that information. entries.title: information
entries.summaryMd: An instance of an information type.

senses.definitionMd: An instance of an information type.

entries.title: information and communications technology (ICT)
entries.summaryMd: Includes all categories of ubiquitous technology used for the gathering, storing, transmitting, retrieving, or processing of information (e.g., microelectronics, printed circuit boards, computing systems, software, signal processors, mobile telephony, satellite communications, and networks).

senses.definitionMd: Includes all categories of ubiquitous technology used for the gathering, storing, transmitting, retrieving, or processing of information (e.g., microelectronics, printed circuit boards, computing systems, software, signal processors, mobile telephony, satellite communications, and networks).

entries.title: information assurance component (IAC)
entries.summaryMd: An application (hardware and/or software) that provides one or more Information Assurance capabilities in support of the overall security and operational objectives of a system. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

senses.definitionMd: An application (hardware and/or software) that provides one or more Information Assurance capabilities in support of the overall security and operational objectives of a system. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

entries.title: information assurance (IA)
entries.summaryMd: Measures that protect and defend information and information systems by ensuring their availability, integrity, authentication, confidentiality, and non-repudiation. These measures include providing for restoration of information systems by incorporating protection, detection, and reaction capabilities.

senses.definitionMd: Measures that protect and defend information and information systems by ensuring their availability, integrity, authentication, confidentiality, and non-repudiation. These measures include providing for restoration of information systems by incorporating protection, detection, and reaction capabilities.

entries.title: information assurance (IA) professional
entries.summaryMd: Individual who works IA issues and has real world experience plus appropriate IA training and education commensurate with their level of IA responsibility. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms. Rationale: Term is self-describing and generic.

senses.definitionMd: Individual who works IA issues and has real world experience plus appropriate IA training and education commensurate with their level of IA responsibility. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms. Rationale: Term is self-describing and generic.

entries.title: Information Assurance Manager
entries.summaryMd: See information systems security manager (ISSM).

senses.definitionMd: See information systems security manager (ISSM).

entries.title: Information Assurance Officer
entries.summaryMd: See information systems security officer (ISSO). Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms. Rationale: Term is deprecated in favor of ISSO.

senses.definitionMd: See information systems security officer (ISSO). Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms. Rationale: Term is deprecated in favor of ISSO.

entries.title: information assurance vulnerability alert (IAVA)
entries.summaryMd: Notification that is generated when an Information Assurance vulnerability may result in an immediate and potentially severe threat to DoD systems and information; this alert requires corrective action because of the severity of the vulnerability risk. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

senses.definitionMd: Notification that is generated when an Information Assurance vulnerability may result in an immediate and potentially severe threat to DoD systems and information; this alert requires corrective action because of the severity of the vulnerability risk. entries.title: information assurance vulnerability bulletin (IAVB)
entries.summaryMd: Addresses new vulnerabilities that do not pose an immediate risk to DoD systems, but are significant enough that noncompliance with the corrective action could escalate the risk. Note: DoDI 8500.01 has transitioned from the term information assurance (IA) to the term cybersecurity. This could potentially impact IA related terms.

senses.definitionMd: Addresses new vulnerabilities that do not pose an immediate risk to DoD systems, but are significant enough that noncompliance with the corrective action could escalate the risk. entries.title: information domain
entries.summaryMd: A three-part concept for information sharing, independent of, and across information systems and security domains that 1) identifies information sharing participants as individual members, 2) contains shared information objects, and 3) provides a security policy that identifies the roles and privileges of the members and the protections required for the information objects.An information domain may contain data that is at different security levels, and not all data in an information domain is releasable or discloseable to all participants. Participants in an information domain must acknowledge the increased risk of the potential for unintended release or disclosure of information.

senses.definitionMd: A three-part concept for information sharing, independent of, and across information systems and security domains that 1) identifies information sharing participants as individual members, 2) contains shared information objects, and 3) provides a security policy that identifies the roles and privileges of the members and the protections required for the information objects.An information domain may contain data that is at different security levels, and not all data in an information domain is releasable or discloseable to all participants. Participants in an information domain must acknowledge the increased risk of the potential for unintended release or disclosure of information.

entries.title: information environment
entries.summaryMd: The aggregate of individuals, organizations, and systems that collect, process, disseminate, or act on information.

senses.definitionMd: The aggregate of individuals, organizations, and systems that collect, process, disseminate, or act on information.

entries.title: information exchange
entries.summaryMd: Access to or the transfer of data outside of system authorization boundaries in order to accomplish a mission or business function.

senses.definitionMd: Access to or the transfer of data outside of system authorization boundaries in order to accomplish a mission or business function.

entries.title: information exchange agreement
entries.summaryMd: A document specifying protection requirements and responsibilities for information being exchanged outside of system authorization boundaries. Similar to the interconnection security agreement but does not include technical details associated with an interconnection.

senses.definitionMd: A document specifying protection requirements and responsibilities for information being exchanged outside of system authorization boundaries. Similar to the interconnection security agreement but does not include technical details associated with an interconnection.

entries.title: information flow control
entries.summaryMd: Procedure to ensure that information transfers within an information system are not made in violation of the security policy.

senses.definitionMd: Procedure to ensure that information transfers within an information system are not made in violation of the security policy.

entries.title: information item
entries.summaryMd: Separately identifiable body of information that is produced, stored, and delivered for human use.

senses.definitionMd: Separately identifiable body of information that is produced, stored, and delivered for human use.

entries.title: information leakage
entries.summaryMd: The intentional or unintentional release of information to an untrusted environment.

senses.definitionMd: The intentional or unintentional release of information to an untrusted environment.

entries.title: information life cycle
entries.summaryMd: The stages through which information passes, typically characterized as creation or collection, processing, dissemination, use, storage, and disposition, to include destruction and deletion.

senses.definitionMd: The stages through which information passes, typically characterized as creation or collection, processing, dissemination, use, storage, and disposition, to include destruction and deletion.

entries.title: information management
entries.summaryMd: The planning, budgeting, manipulating, and controlling of information throughout its life cycle.

senses.definitionMd: The planning, budgeting, manipulating, and controlling of information throughout its life cycle.

entries.title: Information Management Policy
entries.summaryMd: The high-level policy of an organization that specifies what information is to be collected or created, and how it is to be managed.

senses.definitionMd: The high-level policy of an organization that specifies what information is to be collected or created, and how it is to be managed.

entries.title: information object
entries.summaryMd: A well-defined piece of information, definition, or specification that requires a name to identify its use in an instance of communication.

senses.definitionMd: A well-defined piece of information, definition, or specification that requires a name to identify its use in an instance of communication.

entries.title: information operations (IO)
entries.summaryMd: The integrated employment, during military operations, of information-related capabilities in concert with other lines of operation to influence, disrupt, corrupt, or usurp the decision-making of adversaries and potential adversaries while protecting our own.

senses.definitionMd: The integrated employment, during military operations, of information-related capabilities in concert with other lines of operation to influence, disrupt, corrupt, or usurp the decision-making of adversaries and potential adversaries while protecting our own.

entries.title: information owner
entries.summaryMd: Official with statutory or operational authority for specified information and responsibility for establishing the controls for its generation, collection, processing, dissemination, and disposal.

senses.definitionMd: Official with statutory or operational authority for specified information and responsibility for establishing the controls for its generation, collection, processing, dissemination, and disposal.

entries.title: Information Relevant to Cybersecurity
entries.summaryMd: Information describing use of, assumptions, risks, vulnerabilities, assessments, and/or mitigations related to the IoT product, its components, and data.

senses.definitionMd: Information describing use of, assumptions, risks, vulnerabilities, assessments, and/or mitigations related to the IoT product, its components, and data.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Information Relevant to Cybersecurity"

entries.title: information resources
entries.summaryMd: Information and related resources, such as personnel, equipment, funds, and information technology.

senses.definitionMd: Information and related resources, such as personnel, equipment, funds, and information technology.

entries.title: information resources management (IRM)
entries.summaryMd: The process of managing information resources to accomplish agency missions and to improve agency performance, including through the reduction of information collection burdens on the public.

senses.definitionMd: The process of managing information resources to accomplish agency missions and to improve agency performance, including through the reduction of information collection burdens on the public.

entries.title: information security
entries.summaryMd: The protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

senses.definitionMd: The protection of information and information systems from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction in order to provide confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

entries.title: information security architect
entries.summaryMd: Individual, group, or organization responsible for ensuring that the information security requirements necessary to protect the organization’s core missions and business processes are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture including reference models, segment and solution architectures, and the resulting information systems supporting those missions and business processes.

senses.definitionMd: Individual, group, or organization responsible for ensuring that the information security requirements necessary to protect the organization’s core missions and business processes are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture including reference models, segment and solution architectures, and the resulting information systems supporting those missions and business processes.

entries.title: information security architecture
entries.summaryMd: A description of the structure and behavior for an enterprise’s security processes, information security systems, personnel and organizational sub-units, showing their alignment with the enterprise’s mission and strategic plans.

senses.definitionMd: A description of the structure and behavior for an enterprise’s security processes, information security systems, personnel and organizational sub-units, showing their alignment with the enterprise’s mission and strategic plans.

entries.title: information security continuous monitoring (ISCM)
entries.summaryMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions. Note: The terms “continuous” and “ongoing” in this context mean that security controls and organizational risks are assessed and analyzed at a frequency sufficient to support risk-based security decisions to adequately protect organization information. See organizational information security continuous monitoring and automated security monitoring.

senses.definitionMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions. entries.title: information security continuous monitoring (ISCM) process
entries.summaryMd: A process to: • Define an ISCM strategy; • Establish an ISCM program; • Implement an ISCM program; • Analyze data and Report findings; • Respond to findings; and • Review and Update the ISCM strategy and program.

senses.definitionMd: A process to: • Define an ISCM strategy; • Establish an ISCM program; • Implement an ISCM program; • Analyze data and Report findings; • Respond to findings; and • Review and Update the ISCM strategy and program.

entries.title: information security continuous monitoring (ISCM) program
entries.summaryMd: A program established to collect information in accordance with pre-established metrics, utilizing information readily available in part through implemented security controls.

entries.title: information security officer
entries.summaryMd: See Senior Agency Information Security Officer.

senses.definitionMd: See Senior Agency Information Security Officer.

entries.title: information security policy
entries.summaryMd: Aggregate of directives, regulations, rules, and practices that prescribes how an organization manages, protects, and distributes information.

senses.definitionMd: Aggregate of directives, regulations, rules, and practices that prescribes how an organization manages, protects, and distributes information.

entries.title: information security risk
entries.summaryMd: The risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation due to the potential for unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of information and/or information systems. See risk.

senses.definitionMd: The risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation due to the potential for unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of information and/or information systems. entries.title: Information Security Testing
entries.summaryMd: The process of validating the effective implementation of security controls for information systems and networks, based on the organization’s security requirements.

entries.title: Information Sharing and Analysis Organization
entries.summaryMd: An ISAO is any entity or collaboration created or employed by public- or private sector organizations, for purposes of gathering and analyzing critical cyber and related information in order to better understand security problems and interdependencies related to cyber systems, so as to ensure their availability, integrity, and reliability.

entries.title: information sharing environment (ISE)

entries.title: information steward
entries.summaryMd: An agency official with statutory or operational authority for specified information and responsibility for establishing the controls for its generation, collection, processing, dissemination, and disposal.

entries.summaryMd: Individual who implements approved secure baseline configurations, incorporates secure configuration settings for IT products, and conducts/assists with configuration monitoring activities as needed.

entries.title: information system component inventory

entries.summaryMd: See Information System Contingency Plan.

entries.summaryMd: The phases through which an information system passes, typically characterized as initiation, development, operation, and termination (i.e., sanitization, disposal and/or destruction).

entries.title: information system resilience
entries.summaryMd: The ability of an information system to continue to: (i) operate under adverse conditions or stress, even if in a degraded or debilitated state, while maintaining essential operational capabilities; and (ii) recover to an effective operational posture in a time frame consistent with mission needs.

entries.summaryMd: Individual assigned responsibility for conducting information system security engineering activities.

entries.title: Information System Security Engineering
entries.summaryMd: Process that captures and refines information security requirements and ensures that their integration into information technology component products and information systems through purposeful security design or configuration.

entries.title: information system security officer
entries.summaryMd: Individual with assigned responsibility for maintaining the appropriate operational security posture for an information system or program.

entries.summaryMd: See Information System User

senses.definitionMd: See Information System User

entries.title: information systems security (INFOSEC)
entries.summaryMd: The protection of information systems against unauthorized access to or modification of information, whether in storage, processing or transit, and against the denial of service to authorized users, including those measures necessary to detect, document, and counter such threats. See information assurance (IA).

senses.definitionMd: The protection of information systems against unauthorized access to or modification of information, whether in storage, processing or transit, and against the denial of service to authorized users, including those measures necessary to detect, document, and counter such threats. See information assurance (IA).

entries.title: information systems security (INFOSEC) boundary
entries.summaryMd: A definable perimeter encompassing all the critical functions in an INFOSEC product and separating them from all other functions within the product.

entries.summaryMd: Individual responsible for the CS of a program, organization, system, or enclave.

entries.title: information technology product
entries.summaryMd: A discrete, identifiable information technology asset (e.g., hardware, software, firmware) that represents a building block of an information system. Information system components include commercial information technology products.

entries.title: information type
entries.summaryMd: A specific category of information (e.g., privacy, medical, proprietary, financial, investigative, contractor sensitive, security management), defined by an organization or, in some instances, by a specific law, Executive Order, directive, policy, or regulation.

senses.definitionMd: A specific category of information (e.g., privacy, medical, proprietary, financial, investigative, contractor sensitive, security management), defined by an organization or, in some instances, by a specific law, Executive Order, directive, policy, or regulation.

entries.title: information value
entries.summaryMd: A qualitative measure of the importance of the information based upon factors such as the level of robustness of security controls allocated to the protection of information based upon: mission criticality, the sensitivity (e.g., classification and compartmentalization) of the information, releasability or privacy requirements, perishability/longevity of the information (e.g., short life data versus long life intelligence source data), and potential impact of loss of confidentiality and integrity and/or availability of the information.

senses.definitionMd: A qualitative measure of the importance of the information based upon factors such as the level of robustness of security controls allocated to the protection of information based upon: mission criticality, the sensitivity (e.g., classification and compartmentalization) of the information, releasability or privacy requirements, perishability/longevity of the information (e.g., short life data versus long life intelligence source data), and potential impact of loss of confidentiality and integrity and/or availability of the information.

entries.title: informational label
entries.summaryMd: Provides facts about properties or features of a product without any grading or evaluation. Information may be displayed in a variety of ways, such as in tabular format or with icons or text.

entries.title: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
entries.summaryMd: The capability provided to the consumer is to provision processing, storage, networks, and other fundamental computing resources where the consumer is able to deploy and run arbitrary software, which can include operating systems and applications. entries.title: Ingress Filtering

entries.title: inheritance
entries.summaryMd: A situation in which an information system or application receives protection from security controls (or portions of security controls) that are developed, implemented, and assessed, authorized, and monitored by entities other than those responsible for the system or application; entities either internal or external to the organization where the system or application resides. entries.title: Initial Analysis

entries.title: Initialization Vector (IV)
entries.summaryMd: A binary vector used as the input to initialize the algorithm for the encryption of a plaintext block sequence to increase security by introducing additional cryptographic variance and to synchronize cryptographic equipment. senses.definitionMd: A binary vector used as the input to initialize the algorithm for the encryption of a plaintext block sequence to increase security by introducing additional cryptographic variance and to synchronize cryptographic equipment. entries.title: injection attack
entries.summaryMd: An attack in which an attacker supplies untrusted biometric information or media into a program or process. For example, this could include injecting a falsified image of identity evidence, a forged video of a user, or a morphed image to defeat evidence validation technology or biometric and visual comparisons for user verification.

senses.definitionMd: An attack in which an attacker supplies untrusted biometric information or media into a program or process. entries.title: Input Block
entries.summaryMd: A data block that is an input to either the forward cipher function or the inverse cipher function of the block cipher algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: A data block that is an input to either the forward cipher function or the inverse cipher function of the block cipher algorithm.

entries.title: input checking
entries.summaryMd: Examination of a potential input to an algorithm for the purpose of determining whether it conforms to certain requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Examination of a potential input to an algorithm for the purpose of determining whether it conforms to certain requirements.

entries.title: insider
entries.summaryMd: Any person with authorized access to any United States Government resource to include personnel, facilities, information, equipment, networks, or systems.

senses.definitionMd: Any person with authorized access to any United States Government resource to include personnel, facilities, information, equipment, networks, or systems.

entries.title: insider threat
entries.summaryMd: The threat that an insider will use her/his authorized access, wittingly or unwittingly, to do harm to the security of the United States. This threat can include damage to the United States through espionage, terrorism, unauthorized disclosure, or through the loss or degradation of departmental resources or capabilities.

senses.definitionMd: The threat that an insider will use her/his authorized access, wittingly or unwittingly, to do harm to the security of the United States. This threat can include damage to the United States through espionage, terrorism, unauthorized disclosure, or through the loss or degradation of departmental resources or capabilities.

entries.title: insider threat program
entries.summaryMd: A coordinated collection of capabilities authorized by the Department/Agency (D/A) that is organized to deter, detect, and mitigate the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.

senses.definitionMd: A coordinated collection of capabilities authorized by the Department/Agency (D/A) that is organized to deter, detect, and mitigate the unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.

entries.title: inspectable space
entries.summaryMd: Three dimensional space surrounding equipment that processes classified and/or sensitive information within which TEMPEST exploitation is not considered practical or where legal authority to identify and remove a potential TEMPEST exploitation exists. Synonymous with zone of control.

senses.definitionMd: Three dimensional space surrounding equipment that processes classified and/or sensitive information within which TEMPEST exploitation is not considered practical or where legal authority to identify and remove a potential TEMPEST exploitation exists. Synonymous with zone of control.

entries.title: Inspection
entries.summaryMd: Examination of an object of conformity assessment and determination of its conformity with detailed requirements or, on the basis of professional judgement, with general requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Examination of an object of conformity assessment and determination of its conformity with detailed requirements or, on the basis of professional judgement, with general requirements.

entries.title: Installation (as used herein)
entries.summaryMd: Any of the following actions: - Executing an installer to load software. - Listing Software in the operating system software directory. - (Merely) placing executable software on a medium from which it can be executed, even if no installer software is run and there is no listing for it in the operating system software directory. - Any other action that allows an executable software file to be loaded into the CPU (e.g., browsing a website that downloads software; opening an e-mail (or attachment) that downloads software; etc.).

senses.definitionMd: Any of the following actions: - Executing an installer to load software. - Listing Software in the operating system software directory. - (Merely) placing executable software on a medium from which it can be executed, even if no installer software is run and there is no listing for it in the operating system software directory. - Any other action that allows an executable software file to be loaded into the CPU (e.g., browsing a website that downloads software; opening an e-mail (or attachment) that downloads software; etc.).

entries.title: Installation (of keying material)
entries.summaryMd: The process of making keying material available for establishing and maintaining cryptographic relationships.

senses.definitionMd: The process of making keying material available for establishing and maintaining cryptographic relationships.

entries.title: Instant Messaging (IM)
entries.summaryMd: A facility for exchanging messages in real-time with other people over the Internet and tracking the progress of a given conversation.

senses.definitionMd: A facility for exchanging messages in real-time with other people over the Internet and tracking the progress of a given conversation.

entries.title: Instantiation of an RBG
entries.summaryMd: An instantiation of an RBG is a specific, logically independent, initialized RBG. One instantiation is distinguished from another by a “handle” (e.g., an identifying number).

senses.definitionMd: An instantiation of an RBG is a specific, logically independent, initialized RBG. One instantiation is distinguished from another by a “handle” (e.g., an identifying number).

entries.title: int(X)
entries.summaryMd: The integer for which the bit string X is a binary representation. len(X) The bit length of the bit string X.

senses.definitionMd: The integer for which the bit string X is a binary representation. len(X) The bit length of the bit string X.

entries.title: integrated CCI (controlled cryptographic items) component
entries.summaryMd: A CCI component that is designed to be incorporated into an otherwise unclassified communication or information processing equipment or system to form a CCI equipment or CCI system. Note: The integrated CCI component cannot perform any function by itself. It obtains power from the host equipment. An integrated CCI component may take a variety of forms (see paragraph 8 of the basic Instruction regarding the terminology for CCI component).
