entries.title: Integrated Circuit Card ID (ICCID)
entries.summaryMd: The unique serial number assigned to, maintained within, and usually imprinted on the (U)SIM.

senses.definitionMd: The unique serial number assigned to, maintained within, and usually imprinted on the (U)SIM.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Integrated Circuit Card ID (ICCID)"

entries.title: Integrated Circuit Card Identification
entries.summaryMd: a unique and immutable identifier maintained within the SIM.

senses.definitionMd: a unique and immutable identifier maintained within the SIM.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Integrated Circuit Card Identification"

entries.title: Integrated Digital Enhanced Network (iDEN)
entries.summaryMd: A proprietary mobile communications technology developed by Motorola that combines the capabilities of a digital cellular telephone with two-way radio.

senses.definitionMd: A proprietary mobile communications technology developed by Motorola that combines the capabilities of a digital cellular telephone with two-way radio.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Integrated Digital Enhanced Network (iDEN)"

entries.title: Integrator
entries.summaryMd: An organization that customizes (e.g., combines, adds, optimizes) elements, processes, and systems. The integrator function can be performed by acquirer, integrator, or supplier organizations.

senses.definitionMd: An organization that customizes (e.g., combines, adds, optimizes) elements, processes, and systems. The integrator function can be performed by acquirer, integrator, or supplier organizations.

entries.title: integrity
entries.summaryMd: Guarding against improper information modification or destruction, and includes ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity.

senses.definitionMd: Guarding against improper information modification or destruction, and includes ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity.

entries.title: Integrity authentication
entries.summaryMd: A physical or cryptographic means of providing assurance that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted, or stored.

senses.definitionMd: A physical or cryptographic means of providing assurance that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted, or stored.

entries.title: integrity check value
entries.summaryMd: A fixed string that is prepended to the plaintext within the authenticated-encryption function of a key-wrap algorithm, in order to enable the verification of the integrity of the plaintext within the authenticated-decryption function.

senses.definitionMd: A fixed string that is prepended to the plaintext within the authenticated-encryption function of a key-wrap algorithm, in order to enable the verification of the integrity of the plaintext within the authenticated-decryption function.

entries.title: Integrity Impact
entries.summaryMd: measures the potential impact to integrity of a successfully exploited misuse vulnerability. Integrity refers to the trustworthiness and guaranteed veracity of information.

senses.definitionMd: measures the potential impact to integrity of a successfully exploited misuse vulnerability. Integrity refers to the trustworthiness and guaranteed veracity of information.

entries.title: Integrity protection
entries.summaryMd: A physical or cryptographic means of providing assurance that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted, or stored.

senses.definitionMd: A physical or cryptographic means of providing assurance that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted, or stored.

entries.title: Integrity verification
entries.summaryMd: Obtaining assurance that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted or stored.

senses.definitionMd: Obtaining assurance that information has not been altered in an unauthorized manner since it was created, transmitted or stored.

entries.title: integrity violation
entries.summaryMd: In the AML context, an AI system being forced to misperform against its intended objectives, producing outputs or predictions that align with the at­tacker’s objective.

senses.definitionMd: In the AML context, an AI system being forced to misperform against its intended objectives, producing outputs or predictions that align with the at­tacker’s objective.

entries.title: intellectual property
entries.summaryMd: Refers broadly to the creations of the human mind. IP rights protect the interests of innovators and creators by giving them rights over their creations. IP is usually divided into two branches, namely industrial property and copyright. Industrial property takes a range of forms, including patents for inventions, industrial designs, trademarks, service marks, layout-designs of integrated circuits, commercial names and designations, geographical indications and protection against unfair competition. Copyright relates to literary and artistic creations, such as books, music, paintings and sculptures, films and technology-based works (such as computer programs and electronic databases). In certain languages, copyright is referred to as authors' rights.

senses.definitionMd: Refers broadly to the creations of the human mind. IP rights protect the interests of innovators and creators by giving them rights over their creations. IP is usually divided into two branches, namely industrial property and copyright. Industrial property takes a range of forms, including patents for inventions, industrial designs, trademarks, service marks, layout-designs of integrated circuits, commercial names and designations, geographical indications and protection against unfair competition. Copyright relates to literary and artistic creations, such as books, music, paintings and sculptures, films and technology-based works (such as computer programs and electronic databases). In certain languages, copyright is referred to as authors' rights.

entries.title: intelligence
entries.summaryMd: 2. The term 'intelligence' includes foreign intelligence and counterintelligence.

senses.definitionMd: 2. The term 'intelligence' includes foreign intelligence and counterintelligence.

entries.title: intelligence activities
entries.summaryMd: All activities that agencies within the Intelligence Community are authorized to conduct pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 12333, United States Intelligence Activities.

senses.definitionMd: All activities that agencies within the Intelligence Community are authorized to conduct pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 12333, United States Intelligence Activities.

entries.title: intelligence community (IC)
entries.summaryMd: Intelligence Community and elements of the Intelligence Community refers to: (1) The Office of the Director of National Intelligence; (2) The Central Intelligence Agency; (3) The National Security Agency; (4) The Defense Intelligence Agency; (5) The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency; (6) The National Reconnaissance Office; (7) The other offices within the Department of Defense for the collection of specialized national foreign intelligence through reconnaissance programs; (8) The intelligence and counterintelligence elements of the Army, the Navy, the Air Force, and the Marine Corps; (9) The intelligence elements of the Federal Bureau of Investigation; (10) The Office of National Security Intelligence of the Drug Enforcement Administration; (11) The Office of Intelligence and Counterintelligence of the Department of Energy; (12) The Bureau of Intelligence and Research of the Department of State; (13) The Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of the Treasury; (14) The Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security; (15) The intelligence and counterintelligence elements of the Coast Guard; and (16) Such other elements of any department or agency as may be designated by the President, or designated jointly by the Director and the head of the department or agency concerned, as an element of the Intelligence Community.

senses.definitionMd: Intelligence Community and elements of the Intelligence Community refers to: (1) The Office of the Director of National Intelligence; (2) The Central Intelligence Agency; (3) The National Security Agency; (4) The Defense Intelligence Agency; (5) The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency; (6) The National Reconnaissance Office; (7) The other offices within the Department of Defense for the collection of specialized national foreign intelligence through reconnaissance programs; (8) The intelligence and counterintelligence elements of the Army, the Navy, the Air Force, and the Marine Corps; (9) The intelligence elements of the Federal Bureau of Investigation; (10) The Office of National Security Intelligence of the Drug Enforcement Administration; (11) The Office of Intelligence and Counterintelligence of the Department of Energy; (12) The Bureau of Intelligence and Research of the Department of State; (13) The Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of the Treasury; (14) The Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security; (15) The intelligence and counterintelligence elements of the Coast Guard; and (16) Such other elements of any department or agency as may be designated by the President, or designated jointly by the Director and the head of the department or agency concerned, as an element of the Intelligence Community.

entries.title: Intended owner
entries.summaryMd: An entity that intends to act as a signatory but has not yet obtained a private key that will be used to generate digital signatures.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that intends to act as a signatory but has not yet obtained a private key that will be used to generate digital signatures.

entries.title: Intended signatory
entries.summaryMd: An entity that intends to generate digital signatures in the future.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that intends to generate digital signatures in the future.

entries.title: Inter-Enterprise Subsystem
entries.summaryMd: The portion of the RFID system that connects multiple enterprise subsystems together. The inter-enterprise subsystem consists of network infrastructure, a naming service, and possibly a discovery service. Inter-enterprise subsystems are most commonly associated with supply chain applications.

senses.definitionMd: The portion of the RFID system that connects multiple enterprise subsystems together. The inter-enterprise subsystem consists of network infrastructure, a naming service, and possibly a discovery service. Inter-enterprise subsystems are most commonly associated with supply chain applications.

entries.title: Interactive User
entries.summaryMd: A person who uses an SSH client to access one or more SSH servers, typically to perform administrative operations, transfer data, or access applications.

senses.definitionMd: A person who uses an SSH client to access one or more SSH servers, typically to perform administrative operations, transfer data, or access applications.

entries.title: interchangeable
entries.summaryMd: The ability to combine signals from multiple PNT data sources into a single PNT solution, as well as the ability to provide a solution from an alternative source when a primary source is not available.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to combine signals from multiple PNT data sources into a single PNT solution, as well as the ability to provide a solution from an alternative source when a primary source is not available.

entries.title: interconnection
entries.summaryMd: See system interconnection.

senses.definitionMd: See system interconnection.

entries.title: interconnection security agreement (ISA)
entries.summaryMd: A document that regulates security-relevant aspects of an intended connection between an agency and an external system. It regulates the security interface between any two systems operating under two different distinct authorities. It includes a variety of descriptive, technical, procedural, and planning information. It is usually preceded by a formal MOA/MOU that defines high- level roles and responsibilities in management of a cross-domain connection.

senses.definitionMd: A document that regulates security-relevant aspects of an intended connection between an agency and an external system. It regulates the security interface between any two systems operating under two different distinct authorities. It includes a variety of descriptive, technical, procedural, and planning information. It is usually preceded by a formal MOA/MOU that defines high- level roles and responsibilities in management of a cross-domain connection.

entries.title: interface
entries.summaryMd: In a service-oriented architecture, a specification of the operations that a service offers its clients. In WSDL 2.0 an interface component describes sequences of messages that a service sends or receives. In WSDL 1.1 an interface is specified in a portType element.

senses.definitionMd: In a service-oriented architecture, a specification of the operations that a service offers its clients. In WSDL 2.0 an interface component describes sequences of messages that a service sends or receives. In WSDL 1.1 an interface is specified in a portType element.

entries.title: Interface Capabilities
entries.summaryMd: Capabilities which enable interactions involving IoT devices (e.g., device-to-device communications, human-to-device communications). The types of interface capabilities are application, human user, and network.

senses.definitionMd: Capabilities which enable interactions involving IoT devices (e.g., device-to-device communications, human-to-device communications). The types of interface capabilities are application, human user, and network.

entries.title: interface device
entries.summaryMd: An electronic device that connects an integrated circuit card and the card applications therein to a client application.

senses.definitionMd: An electronic device that connects an integrated circuit card and the card applications therein to a client application.

entries.title: Interim Approval to Operate
entries.summaryMd: Temporary authorization granted by principal accrediting authority (PAA) or authorizing official (AO) for an information system to process information based on preliminary results of a security evaluation of the system.

senses.definitionMd: Temporary authorization granted by principal accrediting authority (PAA) or authorizing official (AO) for an information system to process information based on preliminary results of a security evaluation of the system.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Interim Approval to Operate"

entries.title: interim authorization to test (IATT)
entries.summaryMd: Temporary authorization to test an information system in a specified operational information environment within the timeframe and under the conditions or constraints enumerated in the written authorization.

senses.definitionMd: Temporary authorization to test an information system in a specified operational information environment within the timeframe and under the conditions or constraints enumerated in the written authorization.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "interim authorization to test (IATT)"

entries.title: Intermediary Service
entries.summaryMd: A component that lies between the Service Client (subscriber) and the Service Provider (publisher). It intercepts the request from the Service Client, provides the service (functionality), and forwards the request to the Service Provider. Similarly, it intercepts the response from the Service Provider and forwards it to the Service Client.

senses.definitionMd: A component that lies between the Service Client (subscriber) and the Service Provider (publisher). It intercepts the request from the Service Client, provides the service (functionality), and forwards the request to the Service Provider. Similarly, it intercepts the response from the Service Provider and forwards it to the Service Client.

entries.title: Intermediate Certification Authority (CA)
entries.summaryMd: A CA that is signed by a superior CA (e.g., a Root CA or another Intermediate CA) and signs CAs (e.g., another Intermediate or Subordinate CA). The Intermediate CA exists in the middle of a trust chain between the Trust Anchor, or Root, and the subscriber certificate issuing Subordinate CAs.

senses.definitionMd: A CA that is signed by a superior CA (e.g., a Root CA or another Intermediate CA) and signs CAs (e.g., another Intermediate or Subordinate CA). The Intermediate CA exists in the middle of a trust chain between the Trust Anchor, or Root, and the subscriber certificate issuing Subordinate CAs.

entries.title: intermittent ad-hoc connection
entries.summaryMd: A needs-based connection initiated for a specific time or purpose after which the connection is terminated. Intermittent connections are most often made via virtual connection.

senses.definitionMd: A needs-based connection initiated for a specific time or purpose after which the connection is terminated. Intermittent connections are most often made via virtual connection.

entries.title: internal assessment engagement
entries.summaryMd: Formal engagement led by a team within the organization that determines element judgments.

senses.definitionMd: Formal engagement led by a team within the organization that determines element judgments.

entries.title: Internal Border Gateway Protocol
entries.summaryMd: A BGP operation communicating routing information within an AS.

senses.definitionMd: A BGP operation communicating routing information within an AS.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Internal Border Gateway Protocol"

entries.title: Internal Control
entries.summaryMd: An overarching mechanism that an enterprise uses to achieve and monitor enterprise objectives.

senses.definitionMd: An overarching mechanism that an enterprise uses to achieve and monitor enterprise objectives.

entries.title: internal network
entries.summaryMd: A network where: (i) the establishment, maintenance, and provisioning of security controls are under the direct control of organizational employees or contractors; or (ii) cryptographic encapsulation or similar security technology provides the same effect. An internal network is typically organization-owned, yet may be organization-controlled while not being organization-owned.

senses.definitionMd: A network where: (i) the establishment, maintenance, and provisioning of security controls are under the direct control of organizational employees or contractors; or (ii) cryptographic encapsulation or similar security technology provides the same effect. An internal network is typically organization-owned, yet may be organization-controlled while not being organization-owned.

entries.title: internal security controls
entries.summaryMd: Hardware, firmware, or software features within an information system that restrict access to resources to only authorized subjects.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware, firmware, or software features within an information system that restrict access to resources to only authorized subjects.

entries.title: Internal Security Testing
entries.summaryMd: Security testing conducted from inside the organization’s security perimeter.

senses.definitionMd: Security testing conducted from inside the organization’s security perimeter.

entries.title: Internal State
entries.summaryMd: The collection of stored information about a DRBG instantiation. This can include both secret and non-secret information. Compare to working state.

senses.definitionMd: The collection of stored information about a DRBG instantiation. This can include both secret and non-secret information. Compare to working state.

entries.title: International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI)
entries.summaryMd: A unique identification number programmed into GSM and UMTS mobile devices.

senses.definitionMd: A unique identification number programmed into GSM and UMTS mobile devices.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI)"

entries.title: International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI)
entries.summaryMd: A unique number associated with every GSM mobile phone subscriber, which is maintained on a (U)SIM.

senses.definitionMd: A unique number associated with every GSM mobile phone subscriber, which is maintained on a (U)SIM.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI)"

entries.title: internet
entries.summaryMd: The single, interconnected, worldwide system of commercial, governmental, educational, and other computer networks that share (a) the protocol suite specified by the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) and (b) the name and address spaces managed by the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN).

senses.definitionMd: The single, interconnected, worldwide system of commercial, governmental, educational, and other computer networks that share (a) the protocol suite specified by the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) and (b) the name and address spaces managed by the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN).

entries.title: Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)
entries.summaryMd: The internet standards organization made up of network designers, operators, vendors, and researchers that defines protocol standards (e.g., IP, TCP, DNS) through process of collaboration and consensus.

senses.definitionMd: The internet standards organization made up of network designers, operators, vendors, and researchers that defines protocol standards (e.g., IP, TCP, DNS) through process of collaboration and consensus.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)"

entries.title: Internet Key Exchange (IKE)
entries.summaryMd: The Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) protocol (RFC 5996) that is used to set up a security association in the Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) protocol suite.

senses.definitionMd: The Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) protocol (RFC 5996) that is used to set up a security association in the Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) protocol suite.

entries.title: Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP)
entries.summaryMd: A mailbox access protocol defined by IETF RFC 3501. IMAP is one of the most commonly used mailbox access protocols. IMAP offers a much wider command set than POP.

senses.definitionMd: A mailbox access protocol defined by IETF RFC 3501. IMAP is one of the most commonly used mailbox access protocols. IMAP offers a much wider command set than POP.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP)"

entries.title: Internet Protocol
entries.summaryMd: Standard protocol for transmission of data from source to destinations in packet-switched communications networks and interconnected systems of such networks.

senses.definitionMd: Standard protocol for transmission of data from source to destinations in packet-switched communications networks and interconnected systems of such networks.

entries.title: Internet Protocol (IP) addresses
entries.summaryMd: Standard protocol for transmission of data from source to destinations in packet-switched communications networks and interconnected systems of such networks.

senses.definitionMd: Standard protocol for transmission of data from source to destinations in packet-switched communications networks and interconnected systems of such networks.

entries.title: Internet Protocol Security
entries.summaryMd: A protocol that adds security features to the standard IP protocol to provide confidentiality and integrity services.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol that adds security features to the standard IP protocol to provide confidentiality and integrity services.

entries.title: Interoperability
entries.summaryMd: The ability of one entity to communicate with another entity.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of one entity to communicate with another entity.

entries.title: Interoperability Test
entries.summaryMd: Interoperability tests measure the performance associated with the use of standardized biometric data records in a multiple vendor environment. It involves the production of the templates by N enrollment products and authentication of these against images processed by M others.

senses.definitionMd: Interoperability tests measure the performance associated with the use of standardized biometric data records in a multiple vendor environment. It involves the production of the templates by N enrollment products and authentication of these against images processed by M others.

entries.title: interoperating system
entries.summaryMd: System that exchanges information with the system of interest and uses the information that has been exchanged.

senses.definitionMd: System that exchanges information with the system of interest and uses the information that has been exchanged.

entries.title: Interpreter
entries.summaryMd: A program that processes a script or other program expression and carries out the requested action, in accordance with the language definition.

senses.definitionMd: A program that processes a script or other program expression and carries out the requested action, in accordance with the language definition.

entries.title: interval scale
entries.summaryMd: From the Stevens Scale of Measurement, a quantitative measurement scale using variables with equal values and no true zero, such as time and temperature.

senses.definitionMd: From the Stevens Scale of Measurement, a quantitative measurement scale using variables with equal values and no true zero, such as time and temperature.

entries.title: interview
entries.summaryMd: A type of assessment method that is characterized by the process of conducting discussions with individuals or groups within an organization to facilitate understanding, achieve clarification, or lead to the location of evidence, the results of which are used to support the determination of security control effectiveness over time.

senses.definitionMd: A type of assessment method that is characterized by the process of conducting discussions with individuals or groups within an organization to facilitate understanding, achieve clarification, or lead to the location of evidence, the results of which are used to support the determination of security control effectiveness over time.

entries.title: intranet
entries.summaryMd: A computer network, especially one based on Internet technology, that an organization uses for its own internal (and usually private) purposes and that is closed to outsiders.

senses.definitionMd: A computer network, especially one based on Internet technology, that an organization uses for its own internal (and usually private) purposes and that is closed to outsiders.

entries.title: intrusion
entries.summaryMd: A security event, or a combination of multiple security events, that constitutes a security incident in which an intruder gains, or attempts to gain, access to a system or system resource without having authorization to do so.

senses.definitionMd: A security event, or a combination of multiple security events, that constitutes a security incident in which an intruder gains, or attempts to gain, access to a system or system resource without having authorization to do so.

entries.title: intrusion detection
entries.summaryMd: The process of monitoring the events occurring in a computer system or network and analyzing them for signs of possible incidents.

senses.definitionMd: The process of monitoring the events occurring in a computer system or network and analyzing them for signs of possible incidents.

entries.title: intrusion detection system (IDS)
entries.summaryMd: IDSs which detect attacks by capturing and analyzing network packets. Listening on a network segment or switch, one network-based IDS can monitor the network traffic affecting multiple hosts that are connected to the network segment.

senses.definitionMd: IDSs which detect attacks by capturing and analyzing network packets. Listening on a network segment or switch, one network-based IDS can monitor the network traffic affecting multiple hosts that are connected to the network segment.

entries.title: intrusion prevention
entries.summaryMd: The process of monitoring the events occurring in a computer system or network, analyzing them for signs of possible incidents, and attempting to stop detected possible incidents.

senses.definitionMd: The process of monitoring the events occurring in a computer system or network, analyzing them for signs of possible incidents, and attempting to stop detected possible incidents.

entries.title: intrusion prevention system (IPS)
entries.summaryMd: Intrusion Prevention System: Software that has all the capabilities of an intrusion detection system and can also attempt to stop possible incidents.

senses.definitionMd: Intrusion Prevention System: Software that has all the capabilities of an intrusion detection system and can also attempt to stop possible incidents.

entries.title: Invalidate
entries.summaryMd: To render a credential or authenticator incapable of being used for authentication by causing its authenticator output to no longer be accepted by relying parties.

senses.definitionMd: To render a credential or authenticator incapable of being used for authentication by causing its authenticator output to no longer be accepted by relying parties.

entries.title: inventory
entries.summaryMd: The physical or virtual verification of the presence of each item of COMSEC material charged to a COMSEC account.

senses.definitionMd: The physical or virtual verification of the presence of each item of COMSEC material charged to a COMSEC account.

entries.title: Inventory management
entries.summaryMd: As used in this Recommendation, the management of keys and/or certificates to monitor their status (e.g., expiration dates and whether compromised); assign and track their owners or sponsors (who/what they are and where they are located or how to contact them); and report the status to the appropriate official for remedial action, when required.

senses.definitionMd: As used in this Recommendation, the management of keys and/or certificates to monitor their status (e.g., expiration dates and whether compromised); assign and track their owners or sponsors (who/what they are and where they are located or how to contact them); and report the status to the appropriate official for remedial action, when required.

entries.summaryMd: The function that reverses the transformation of the forward cipher function when the same cryptographic key is used.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Inverse Cipher Function (Inverse Cipher Operation)"

entries.title: Inverse Cipher Operation/Inverse Transformation
entries.summaryMd: The block cipher algorithm function that is the inverse of the forward cipher function. The term “inverse cipher operation” is used for TDEA, while the term “inverse transformation” is used for DEA.

senses.definitionMd: The block cipher algorithm function that is the inverse of the forward cipher function. The term “inverse cipher operation” is used for TDEA, while the term “inverse transformation” is used for DEA.

entries.title: inverse transformation
entries.summaryMd: The inverse of the permutation of blocks that is determined by the choice of a block cipher and a key.

senses.definitionMd: The inverse of the permutation of blocks that is determined by the choice of a block cipher and a key.

entries.title: Invocation Field
entries.summaryMd: In the deterministic construction of IVs, the field that identifies the sets of inputs to the authenticated encryption function in a particular device or context.

senses.definitionMd: In the deterministic construction of IVs, the field that identifies the sets of inputs to the authenticated encryption function in a particular device or context.

entries.title: IoT device
entries.summaryMd: Devices that have at least one transducer (sensor or actuator) for interacting directly with the physical world and at least one network interface (e.g., Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) for interfacing with the digital world.

senses.definitionMd: Devices that have at least one transducer (sensor or actuator) for interacting directly with the physical world and at least one network interface (e.g., Ethernet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) for interfacing with the digital world.

entries.title: IoT Platform
entries.summaryMd: An IoT platform is typically a third-party vendor provided/hosted SaaS-based tool that is used to support IoT device and endpoint management, connectivity and network management, data management, processing and analysis, application development, cybersecurity, access control, monitoring, event processing, and interfacing/integration. Documentation about such a third party can provide important information about supply chain cybersecurity practices and vulnerabilities to allow for the IoT user to more accurately determine risks related to the use of an IoT platform.

senses.definitionMd: An IoT platform is typically a third-party vendor provided/hosted SaaS-based tool that is used to support IoT device and endpoint management, connectivity and network management, data management, processing and analysis, application development, cybersecurity, access control, monitoring, event processing, and interfacing/integration. Documentation about such a third party can provide important information about supply chain cybersecurity practices and vulnerabilities to allow for the IoT user to more accurately determine risks related to the use of an IoT platform.

entries.title: IoT Product
entries.summaryMd: An IoT device and any other product components necessary to use the IoT device.

senses.definitionMd: An IoT device and any other product components necessary to use the IoT device.

entries.title: IoT Product Component
entries.summaryMd: Equipment (i.e., hardware and software) other than the primary device that can be hosted remotely, locally, or on other equipment (e.g., a mobile app on the customer’s smartphone) that supports the IoT device in its functionality.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment (i.e., hardware and software) other than the primary device that can be hosted remotely, locally, or on other equipment (e.g., a mobile app on the customer’s smartphone) that supports the IoT device in its functionality.

entries.title: IoT Product Developer
entries.summaryMd: The entity that creates an assembled final IoT product. Some cybersecurity outcomes may be supported by the IoT product developer’s suppliers or other contracted third-parties with support responsibilities related to the IoT product or its components.

senses.definitionMd: The entity that creates an assembled final IoT product. Some cybersecurity outcomes may be supported by the IoT product developer’s suppliers or other contracted third-parties with support responsibilities related to the IoT product or its components.

entries.title: IP Payload Compression Protocol
entries.summaryMd: A protocol used to perform lossless compression for packet payloads.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol used to perform lossless compression for packet payloads.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "IP Payload Compression Protocol"

entries.title: IP Security
entries.summaryMd: Provide(s) interoperable, high quality, cryptographically-based security for IPv4 and IPv6. The set of security services offered includes access control, connectionless integrity, data origin authentication, detection and rejection of replays (a form of partial sequence integrity), confidentiality (via encryption), and limited traffic flow confidentiality.

senses.definitionMd: Provide(s) interoperable, high quality, cryptographically-based security for IPv4 and IPv6. The set of security services offered includes access control, connectionless integrity, data origin authentication, detection and rejection of replays (a form of partial sequence integrity), confidentiality (via encryption), and limited traffic flow confidentiality.

entries.title: IPComp
entries.summaryMd: A protocol used to perform lossless compression for packet payloads.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol used to perform lossless compression for packet payloads.

entries.title: IPsec
entries.summaryMd: Provide(s) interoperable, high quality, cryptographically-based security for IPv4 and IPv6. The set of security services offered includes access control, connectionless integrity, data origin authentication, detection and rejection of replays (a form of partial sequence integrity), confidentiality (via encryption), and limited traffic flow confidentiality.

senses.definitionMd: Provide(s) interoperable, high quality, cryptographically-based security for IPv4 and IPv6. The set of security services offered includes access control, connectionless integrity, data origin authentication, detection and rejection of replays (a form of partial sequence integrity), confidentiality (via encryption), and limited traffic flow confidentiality.

entries.title: Iris segmentation
entries.summaryMd: Segmentation is the automated (and possibly manually reviewed) detection of the iris-sclera and iris-pupil boundaries. This localizes the iris texture that is used for actual recognition.

senses.definitionMd: Segmentation is the automated (and possibly manually reviewed) detection of the iris-sclera and iris-pupil boundaries. This localizes the iris texture that is used for actual recognition.

entries.title: ISCM Capability
entries.summaryMd: See ISCM Capability.

senses.definitionMd: See ISCM Capability.

entries.title: ISCM Dashboard
entries.summaryMd: A hierarchy of dashboards to facilitate reporting of appropriate security-related information at multiple organizational levels.

senses.definitionMd: A hierarchy of dashboards to facilitate reporting of appropriate security-related information at multiple organizational levels.

entries.title: isogeny
entries.summaryMd: A (non-constant) mapping from an elliptic curve to a second elliptic curve, which preserves point addition and fixes the identity point.

senses.definitionMd: A (non-constant) mapping from an elliptic curve to a second elliptic curve, which preserves point addition and fixes the identity point.

entries.title: Isolation
entries.summaryMd: The ability to keep multiple instances of software separated so that each instance only sees and can affect itself.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to keep multiple instances of software separated so that each instance only sees and can affect itself.

entries.title: isomorphism (of elliptic curves)
entries.summaryMd: A bijective mapping from one elliptic curve to another, which maps addition (on the first curve) to addition (on the image curve).

senses.definitionMd: A bijective mapping from one elliptic curve to another, which maps addition (on the first curve) to addition (on the image curve).

entries.title: Issuance
entries.summaryMd: Agreeing on the type of token that will be used for future authentication

senses.definitionMd: Agreeing on the type of token that will be used for future authentication

entries.title: issuer
entries.summaryMd: The organization that is issuing the PIV Card to an applicant. Typically, this is an organization for which the applicant is working.

senses.definitionMd: The organization that is issuing the PIV Card to an applicant. Typically, this is an organization for which the applicant is working.

entries.title: Issuing Facility
entries.summaryMd: A physical site or location—including all equipment, staff, and documentation—that is responsible for carrying out one or more of the following PIV functions: identity proofing and registration; card and token production; activation and issuance; post-issuance binding of derived PIV credentials; and maintenance.

senses.definitionMd: A physical site or location—including all equipment, staff, and documentation—that is responsible for carrying out one or more of the following PIV functions: identity proofing and registration; card and token production; activation and issuance; post-issuance binding of derived PIV credentials; and maintenance.

entries.title: IT security awareness and training program
entries.summaryMd: Explains proper rules of behavior for the use of agency information systems and information. The program communicates information technology (IT) security policies and procedures that need to be followed. (i.e., NSTISSD 501, NIST SP 800-50)

senses.definitionMd: Explains proper rules of behavior for the use of agency information systems and information. The program communicates information technology (IT) security policies and procedures that need to be followed. (i.e., NSTISSD 501, NIST SP 800-50)

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "IT security awareness and training program"

entries.title: IT System
entries.summaryMd: Any organized assembly of resources and procedures united and regulated by interaction or interdependence to accomplish a set of specific functions. Note: Systems also include specialized systems such as industrial/process controls systems, telephone switching and private branch exchange (PBX) systems, and environmental control systems.

senses.definitionMd: Any organized assembly of resources and procedures united and regulated by interaction or interdependence to accomplish a set of specific functions. Note: Systems also include specialized systems such as industrial/process controls systems, telephone switching and private branch exchange (PBX) systems, and environmental control systems.

entries.title: Item
entries.summaryMd: A named constituent of a benchmark. The three types of items are groups, rules, and values.

senses.definitionMd: A named constituent of a benchmark. The three types of items are groups, rules, and values.

entries.title: item accounting
entries.summaryMd: Accounting for all the accountable components of a COMSEC equipment configuration by a single short title.

senses.definitionMd: Accounting for all the accountable components of a COMSEC equipment configuration by a single short title.

entries.title: Ivn
entries.summaryMd: Block of data representing IV n

senses.definitionMd: Block of data representing IV n

entries.title: j
entries.summaryMd: The index to a sequence of data blocks or data segments ordered from left to right.

senses.definitionMd: The index to a sequence of data blocks or data segments ordered from left to right.

entries.title: jailbreak
entries.summaryMd: A direct prompting attack intended to circumvent restrictions placed on model outputs, such as circumventing refusal behaviour to enable misuse.

senses.definitionMd: A direct prompting attack intended to circumvent restrictions placed on model outputs, such as circumventing refusal behaviour to enable misuse.

entries.title: jamming
entries.summaryMd: An attack that attempts to interfere with the reception of broadcast communications.

senses.definitionMd: An attack that attempts to interfere with the reception of broadcast communications.

entries.title: jitter
entries.summaryMd: non-uniform delays that can cause packets to arrive and be processed out of sequence

senses.definitionMd: non-uniform delays that can cause packets to arrive and be processed out of sequence

entries.title: joint authorization
entries.summaryMd: Security authorization involving multiple authorizing officials.

senses.definitionMd: Security authorization involving multiple authorizing officials.

entries.title: JSON Web Token
entries.summaryMd: A data exchange format made of a header, payload, and signature where the header and the payload take the form of JSON objects. They are encoded and concatenated with the aggregate being signed to generate a signature.

senses.definitionMd: A data exchange format made of a header, payload, and signature where the header and the payload take the form of JSON objects. They are encoded and concatenated with the aggregate being signed to generate a signature.

entries.title: judgment
entries.summaryMd: The association of one of the preconfigured evaluation choices with an element from the context of a specific organizational level.

senses.definitionMd: The association of one of the preconfigured evaluation choices with an element from the context of a specific organizational level.

entries.title: judgment value
entries.summaryMd: Predefined values that represent the possible choices that an assessor makes in judging whether or how well the gathered information satisfies an assessment element.

senses.definitionMd: Predefined values that represent the possible choices that an assessor makes in judging whether or how well the gathered information satisfies an assessment element.

entries.title: k-anonymity
entries.summaryMd: A technique “to release person-specific data such that the ability to link to other information using the quasi-identifier is limited.” The k-anonymity technique achieves this through suppression of identifiers and output perturbation, although recent work has shown that the k-anonymity mechanism can be reversed in some instances.

senses.definitionMd: A technique “to release person-specific data such that the ability to link to other information using the quasi-identifier is limited.” The k-anonymity technique achieves this through suppression of identifiers and output perturbation, although recent work has shown that the k-anonymity mechanism can be reversed in some instances.

entries.title: KAS1-basic
entries.summaryMd: The basic form of Key-Agreement Scheme 1.

senses.definitionMd: The basic form of Key-Agreement Scheme 1.

entries.title: KAS1-Party_V-confirmation
entries.summaryMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 1 with confirmation by party V. Previously known as KAS1-responder-confirmation.

senses.definitionMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 1 with confirmation by party V. Previously known as KAS1-responder-confirmation.

entries.title: KAS2-basic
entries.summaryMd: The basic form of Key-Agreement Scheme 2.

senses.definitionMd: The basic form of Key-Agreement Scheme 2.

entries.title: KAS2-bilateral-confirmation
entries.summaryMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 2 with bilateral confirmation.

senses.definitionMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 2 with bilateral confirmation.

entries.title: KAS2-Party_U-confirmation
entries.summaryMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 2 with confirmation by party U. Previously known as KAS2-initiator-confirmation.

senses.definitionMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 2 with confirmation by party U. Previously known as KAS2-initiator-confirmation.

entries.title: KAS2-Party_V-confirmation
entries.summaryMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 2 with confirmation by party V. Previously known as KAS2-responder-confirmation.

senses.definitionMd: Key-Agreement Scheme 2 with confirmation by party V. Previously known as KAS2-responder-confirmation.

entries.title: KBits
entries.summaryMd: The bit length of the secret keying material.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the secret keying material.

entries.title: KECCAK Message Authentication Code
entries.summaryMd: KECCAK Message Authentication Code.

senses.definitionMd: KECCAK Message Authentication Code.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "KECCAK Message Authentication Code"

entries.title: (KEM) ciphertext
entries.summaryMd: A bit string that is produced by encapsulation and used as an input to decapsulation.

senses.definitionMd: A bit string that is produced by encapsulation and used as an input to decapsulation.

entries.title: Kerberos
entries.summaryMd: An authentication system developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Kerberos is designed to enable two parties to exchange private information across a public network.

senses.definitionMd: An authentication system developed at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Kerberos is designed to enable two parties to exchange private information across a public network.

entries.title: key
entries.summaryMd: A parameter used in conjunction with a cryptographic algorithm that determines its operation. Examples applicable to this Standard include: 1. The computation of a digital signature from data, and 2. The verification of a digital signature.

senses.definitionMd: A parameter used in conjunction with a cryptographic algorithm that determines its operation. Examples applicable to this Standard include: 1. The computation of a digital signature from data, and 2. The verification of a digital signature.

entries.title: key administration
entries.summaryMd: Functions of loading, storing, copying, and distributing the keys and producing the necessary audit information to support those functions. (System Unique).

senses.definitionMd: Functions of loading, storing, copying, and distributing the keys and producing the necessary audit information to support those functions. (System Unique).

entries.title: key agreement
entries.summaryMd: A key-establishment procedure where resultant keying material is a function of information contributed by two or more participants, so that no party can predetermine the value of the keying material independently of the other party’s contribution.

senses.definitionMd: A key-establishment procedure where resultant keying material is a function of information contributed by two or more participants, so that no party can predetermine the value of the keying material independently of the other party’s contribution.

entries.title: Key agreement primitive
entries.summaryMd: A DLC primitive specified in [SP 800-56A] or an RSA Secret Value Encapsulation (RSASVE) operation specified in [NIST SP 800-56B].

senses.definitionMd: A DLC primitive specified in [SP 800-56A] or an RSA Secret Value Encapsulation (RSASVE) operation specified in [NIST SP 800-56B].

entries.title: Key-agreement transaction
entries.summaryMd: An execution of a key-agreement scheme.

senses.definitionMd: An execution of a key-agreement scheme.

entries.title: Key and metadata management functions
entries.summaryMd: Functions performed by a CKMS or FCKMS in order to manage keys and metadata.

senses.definitionMd: Functions performed by a CKMS or FCKMS in order to manage keys and metadata.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Key and metadata management functions"

entries.title: Key-Auto-Key (KAK)
entries.summaryMd: Cryptographic logic using previous key to produce key.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptographic logic using previous key to produce key.

entries.title: Key Bundle
entries.summaryMd: The three DEA cryptographic keys (Key1, Key2, Key3) that are used with a TDEA mode.

senses.definitionMd: The three DEA cryptographic keys (Key1, Key2, Key3) that are used with a TDEA mode.

entries.title: Key center
entries.summaryMd: A common central source of the keys or key components that are necessary to support cryptographically protected exchanges within one or more communicating groups.

senses.definitionMd: A common central source of the keys or key components that are necessary to support cryptographically protected exchanges within one or more communicating groups.

entries.title: Key-center environment
entries.summaryMd: As used in this Recommendation, an environment in which the keys or key components needed to support cryptographically protected exchanges within one or more communicating groups are obtained from a common central source.

senses.definitionMd: As used in this Recommendation, an environment in which the keys or key components needed to support cryptographically protected exchanges within one or more communicating groups are obtained from a common central source.

entries.title: Key certification
entries.summaryMd: In a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), a process that permits keys or key components to be unambiguously associated with their certificate sources (e.g., using digital signatures to associate public-key certificates with the certification authorities that issued them).

senses.definitionMd: In a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), a process that permits keys or key components to be unambiguously associated with their certificate sources (e.g., using digital signatures to associate public-key certificates with the certification authorities that issued them).

entries.title: Key Chords
entries.summaryMd: Specific hardware keys pressed in a particular sequence on a mobile device.

senses.definitionMd: Specific hardware keys pressed in a particular sequence on a mobile device.

entries.title: key combiner
entries.summaryMd: A function that takes multiple keys or shared secret values as input (possibly along with other information) and produces a single combined key.

senses.definitionMd: A function that takes multiple keys or shared secret values as input (possibly along with other information) and produces a single combined key.

entries.title: Key component
entries.summaryMd: One of at least two parameters that have the same security properties (e.g., randomness) as a cryptographic key; parameters are combined using an approved cryptographic function to form a plaintext cryptographic key before use.

senses.definitionMd: One of at least two parameters that have the same security properties (e.g., randomness) as a cryptographic key; parameters are combined using an approved cryptographic function to form a plaintext cryptographic key before use.

entries.title: Key-confirmation provider
entries.summaryMd: The party that provides assurance to the other party (the recipient) that the two parties have indeed established a shared secret or shared keying material.

senses.definitionMd: The party that provides assurance to the other party (the recipient) that the two parties have indeed established a shared secret or shared keying material.

entries.title: key-confirmation recipient
entries.summaryMd: The party that receives assurance from the other party (i.e., the provider) that the two parties have indeed established a shared secret key or other keying material.

senses.definitionMd: The party that receives assurance from the other party (i.e., the provider) that the two parties have indeed established a shared secret key or other keying material.

entries.title: Key custodian
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for distributing keys or key splits and/or entering them into a cryptographic module.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for distributing keys or key splits and/or entering them into a cryptographic module.

entries.title: Key de-registration
entries.summaryMd: A function in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key; the marking of a key or the information associated with it (e.g., metadata) to indicate that the key is no longer in use.

senses.definitionMd: A function in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key; the marking of a key or the information associated with it (e.g., metadata) to indicate that the key is no longer in use.

entries.title: Key derivation
entries.summaryMd: The process of deriving a key in a non-reversible manner from shared information, some of which is secret.

senses.definitionMd: The process of deriving a key in a non-reversible manner from shared information, some of which is secret.

entries.title: Key-derivation function
entries.summaryMd: As used in this Recommendation, a function used to derive secret keying material from a shared secret (or a key) and other information.

senses.definitionMd: As used in this Recommendation, a function used to derive secret keying material from a shared secret (or a key) and other information.

entries.title: Key-derivation key
entries.summaryMd: A key used as an input to a key derivation function to derive other keys.

senses.definitionMd: A key used as an input to a key derivation function to derive other keys.

entries.title: Key-derivation method
entries.summaryMd: A key-derivation function or other approved procedure for deriving keying material.

senses.definitionMd: A key-derivation function or other approved procedure for deriving keying material.

entries.title: Key-derivation procedure
entries.summaryMd: As used in this Recommendation, a multi-step process to derive secret keying material from a shared secret and other information.

senses.definitionMd: As used in this Recommendation, a multi-step process to derive secret keying material from a shared secret and other information.

entries.title: Key destruction
entries.summaryMd: To remove all traces of a cryptographic key so that it cannot be recovered by either physical or electronic means.

senses.definitionMd: To remove all traces of a cryptographic key so that it cannot be recovered by either physical or electronic means.

entries.title: Key Device Cybersecurity Requirement
entries.summaryMd: A device cybersecurity requirement that if lacking from an IoT device (in the case of a device cybersecurity capability) or manufacturer or supporting entity (in the case of a non-technical supporting capability) will result in unacceptable risk to the organization.

senses.definitionMd: A device cybersecurity requirement that if lacking from an IoT device (in the case of a device cybersecurity capability) or manufacturer or supporting entity (in the case of a non-technical supporting capability) will result in unacceptable risk to the organization.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Key Device Cybersecurity Requirement"

entries.title: key distribution
entries.summaryMd: The transport of a key and other keying material from an entity that either owns or generates the key to another entity that is intended to use the key.

senses.definitionMd: The transport of a key and other keying material from an entity that either owns or generates the key to another entity that is intended to use the key.

entries.title: key distribution center (KDC)
entries.summaryMd: COMSEC facility generating and distributing key in electronic form.

senses.definitionMd: COMSEC facility generating and distributing key in electronic form.

entries.title: Key-Encapsulation Mechanism
entries.summaryMd: A set of three cryptographic algorithms (KeyGen, Encaps, and Decaps) that can be used by two parties to establish a shared secret key over a public channel.

senses.definitionMd: A set of three cryptographic algorithms (KeyGen, Encaps, and Decaps) that can be used by two parties to establish a shared secret key over a public channel.

entries.title: key encryption key (KEK)
entries.summaryMd: A key that encrypts other key [typically traffic encryption keys (TEKs)] for transmission or storage.

senses.definitionMd: A key that encrypts other key [typically traffic encryption keys (TEKs)] for transmission or storage.

entries.title: key escrow
entries.summaryMd: The retention of the private component of the key pair associated with a subscriber’s encryption certificate to support key recovery.

senses.definitionMd: The retention of the private component of the key pair associated with a subscriber’s encryption certificate to support key recovery.

entries.title: key escrow system
entries.summaryMd: The system responsible for storing and providing a mechanism for obtaining copies of private keys associated with encryption certificates, which are necessary for the recovery of encrypted data.

senses.definitionMd: The system responsible for storing and providing a mechanism for obtaining copies of private keys associated with encryption certificates, which are necessary for the recovery of encrypted data.

entries.title: key establishment
entries.summaryMd: A procedure that results in secret keying material that is shared among different parties.

senses.definitionMd: A procedure that results in secret keying material that is shared among different parties.

entries.title: key-establishment key pair
entries.summaryMd: A public key and its corresponding private key.

senses.definitionMd: A public key and its corresponding private key.

entries.title: Key-establishment transaction
entries.summaryMd: An instance of establishing secret keying material using a key-agreement or key-transport transaction.

senses.definitionMd: An instance of establishing secret keying material using a key-agreement or key-transport transaction.

entries.title: key exchange
entries.summaryMd: Process of exchanging public keys (and other information) in order to establish secure communications.

senses.definitionMd: Process of exchanging public keys (and other information) in order to establish secure communications.

entries.title: Key expansion
entries.summaryMd: The second step in the key-derivation procedure in which a key-derivation key is used to derive secret keying material having the desired length(s). The first step in the procedure is randomness extraction.

senses.definitionMd: The second step in the key-derivation procedure in which a key-derivation key is used to derive secret keying material having the desired length(s). The first step in the procedure is randomness extraction.

entries.title: Key extraction
entries.summaryMd: See Randomness extraction.

senses.definitionMd: See Randomness extraction.

entries.title: Key format
entries.summaryMd: The data structure of a cryptographic key.

senses.definitionMd: The data structure of a cryptographic key.

entries.title: Key-generating module
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic module in which a given key is generated.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic module in which a given key is generated.

entries.title: Key generation
entries.summaryMd: The process of generating keys for cryptography.

senses.definitionMd: The process of generating keys for cryptography.

entries.title: key generation material
entries.summaryMd: Random numbers, pseudo-random numbers, and cryptographic parameters used in generating cryptographic keys.

senses.definitionMd: Random numbers, pseudo-random numbers, and cryptographic parameters used in generating cryptographic keys.

entries.title: Key information
entries.summaryMd: Information about a key that includes the keying material and associated metadata relating to the key. See Keying material and Metadata.

senses.definitionMd: Information about a key that includes the keying material and associated metadata relating to the key. See Keying material and Metadata.

entries.title: Key inventory
entries.summaryMd: Information about each key that does not include the key itself (e.g., the key owner, key type, algorithm, application and expiration date).

senses.definitionMd: Information about each key that does not include the key itself (e.g., the key owner, key type, algorithm, application and expiration date).

entries.title: Key length
entries.summaryMd: The length of a key in bits; used interchangeably with “Key size.”

senses.definitionMd: The length of a key in bits; used interchangeably with “Key size.”

entries.title: Key life cycle
entries.summaryMd: The period of time between the creation of the key and its destruction.

senses.definitionMd: The period of time between the creation of the key and its destruction.

entries.title: key list
entries.summaryMd: A printed series of key settings for a specific cryptonet. Key lists may be produced in list, pad, or printed tape format.

senses.definitionMd: A printed series of key settings for a specific cryptonet. Key lists may be produced in list, pad, or printed tape format.

entries.title: key loader
entries.summaryMd: A self-contained unit that is capable of storing at least one plaintext or encrypted cryptographic key or key component that can be transferred, upon request, into a cryptographic module.

senses.definitionMd: A self-contained unit that is capable of storing at least one plaintext or encrypted cryptographic key or key component that can be transferred, upon request, into a cryptographic module.

entries.title: key logger
entries.summaryMd: A program designed to record which keys are pressed on a computer keyboard used to obtain passwords or encryption keys and thus bypass other security measures.

senses.definitionMd: A program designed to record which keys are pressed on a computer keyboard used to obtain passwords or encryption keys and thus bypass other security measures.

entries.title: key management
entries.summaryMd: The activities involving the handling of cryptographic keys and other related security parameters (e.g. passwords) during the entire life cycle of the keys, including their generation, storage, establishment, entry and output, and destruction.

senses.definitionMd: The activities involving the handling of cryptographic keys and other related security parameters (e.g. passwords) during the entire life cycle of the keys, including their generation, storage, establishment, entry and output, and destruction.

entries.title: Key management components
entries.summaryMd: The software module applications and hardware security modules (HSMs) that are used to generate, establish, distribute, store, account for, suspend, revoke, or destroy cryptographic keys and metadata.

senses.definitionMd: The software module applications and hardware security modules (HSMs) that are used to generate, establish, distribute, store, account for, suspend, revoke, or destroy cryptographic keys and metadata.

entries.title: key management device
entries.summaryMd: A unit that provides for secure electronic distribution of encryption keys to authorized users.

senses.definitionMd: A unit that provides for secure electronic distribution of encryption keys to authorized users.

entries.title: key management entity (KME)
entries.summaryMd: Any activity/organization that performs key management related functionality and has been assigned an electronic key management system (EKMS) ID.

senses.definitionMd: Any activity/organization that performs key management related functionality and has been assigned an electronic key management system (EKMS) ID.

entries.title: Key management function
entries.summaryMd: Functions used 1) to establish cryptographic keys, certificates and the information associated with them; 2) for the accounting of all keys and certificates; 3) for key storage and recovery; 4) for revocation and replacement (as needed); and 5) for key destruction.

senses.definitionMd: Functions used 1) to establish cryptographic keys, certificates and the information associated with them; 2) for the accounting of all keys and certificates; 3) for key storage and recovery; 4) for revocation and replacement (as needed); and 5) for key destruction.

entries.title: key management infrastructure (KMI)
entries.summaryMd: A unified, scalable, interoperable, and trusted infrastructure that provides net- centric key management services to systems that rely on cryptography, serving Department of Defense (DoD) and the broader cryptographic community.

senses.definitionMd: A unified, scalable, interoperable, and trusted infrastructure that provides net- centric key management services to systems that rely on cryptography, serving Department of Defense (DoD) and the broader cryptographic community.
