entries.title: Logical Backup
entries.summaryMd: A copy of the directories and files of a logical volume.

senses.definitionMd: A copy of the directories and files of a logical volume.

entries.title: Logical Identifier
entries.summaryMd: A device identifier that is expressed logically by the device’s software. An example is a media access control (MAC) address assigned to a network interface.

senses.definitionMd: A device identifier that is expressed logically by the device’s software. An example is a media access control (MAC) address assigned to a network interface.

entries.title: Logical partitioning
entries.summaryMd: The hypervisor allowing multiple guest OSs to share the same physical resources.

senses.definitionMd: The hypervisor allowing multiple guest OSs to share the same physical resources.

entries.title: logical perimeter
entries.summaryMd: A conceptual perimeter that extends to all intended users of the system, both directly and indirectly connected, who receive output from the system without a reliable human review by an appropriate authority. The location of such a review is commonly referred to as an "air gap".

senses.definitionMd: A conceptual perimeter that extends to all intended users of the system, both directly and indirectly connected, who receive output from the system without a reliable human review by an appropriate authority. The location of such a review is commonly referred to as an "air gap".

entries.title: Logical Test
entries.summaryMd: An expression comprised of logical operators and one or more expressions to be evaluated. The individual expressions within a logical test may be fact references, check fact references, and/or other logical tests.

senses.definitionMd: An expression comprised of logical operators and one or more expressions to be evaluated. The individual expressions within a logical test may be fact references, check fact references, and/or other logical tests.

entries.title: Logical Volume
entries.summaryMd: A partition or a collection of partitions acting as a single entity that has been formatted with a filesystem.

senses.definitionMd: A partition or a collection of partitions acting as a single entity that has been formatted with a filesystem.

entries.title: login
entries.summaryMd: The establishment of an authenticated session between a person and a system. Also known as “sign in,” “log on,” or “sign on.”

senses.definitionMd: The establishment of an authenticated session between a person and a system. Also known as “sign in,” “log on,” or “sign on.”

entries.title: logistic regression
entries.summaryMd: A type of linear classifier that predicts the probability of an observation being part of a class.

senses.definitionMd: A type of linear classifier that predicts the probability of an observation being part of a class.

entries.title: Logo
entries.summaryMd: The NIST National Checklist Program logo.

senses.definitionMd: The NIST National Checklist Program logo.

entries.title: Long Runs of Ones Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the longest run of ones within the tested sequence is consistent with the longest run of ones that would be expected in a random sequence.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the longest run of ones within the tested sequence is consistent with the longest run of ones that would be expected in a random sequence.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Long Runs of Ones Test"

entries.title: long title
entries.summaryMd: The title of a COMSEC item that includes the name of the manufacturer followed by the equipment designator, a short functional description, and the model designator (e.g., Acme All Purpose Secure Radio Model APR-001).

senses.definitionMd: The title of a COMSEC item that includes the name of the manufacturer followed by the equipment designator, a short functional description, and the model designator (e.g., Acme All Purpose Secure Radio Model APR-001).

entries.title: Loop-Back Mode
entries.summaryMd: An operating system facility that allows a device to be mounted via a loopback address and viewed logically on the PC.

senses.definitionMd: An operating system facility that allows a device to be mounted via a loopback address and viewed logically on the PC.

entries.title: low‐dimensional
entries.summaryMd: A statistic composed of few numbers—e.g. a single count, or a histogram with 5 bins.

senses.definitionMd: A statistic composed of few numbers—e.g. a single count, or a histogram with 5 bins.

entries.title: low impact
entries.summaryMd: The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability that could be expected to have a limited adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the national security interests of the United States; (i.e., 1) causes a degradation in mission capability to an extent and duration that the organization is able to perform its primary functions, but the effectiveness of the functions is noticeably reduced; 2) results in minor damage to organizational assets; 3) results in minor financial loss; or 4) results in minor harm to individuals).

senses.definitionMd: The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability that could be expected to have a limited adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the national security interests of the United States; (i.e., 1) causes a degradation in mission capability to an extent and duration that the organization is able to perform its primary functions, but the effectiveness of the functions is noticeably reduced; 2) results in minor damage to organizational assets; 3) results in minor financial loss; or 4) results in minor harm to individuals).

entries.title: low-impact system
entries.summaryMd: An information system in which all three security objectives (i.e., confidentiality, integrity, and availability) are assigned a FIPS 199 potential impact value of low.

senses.definitionMd: An information system in which all three security objectives (i.e., confidentiality, integrity, and availability) are assigned a FIPS 199 potential impact value of low.

entries.title: low-power transmitter
entries.summaryMd: For the purposes of determining separation between RED equipment/lines and radio frequency (RF) transmitters, low-power is that which is less than or equal to 100 m Watt (20 dBm) effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP). Examples of low-power transmitters are wireless devices for local communications that do not need a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license, such as some IEEE 802.11X network access points, and portable (but not cellular) telephones.

senses.definitionMd: For the purposes of determining separation between RED equipment/lines and radio frequency (RF) transmitters, low-power is that which is less than or equal to 100 m Watt (20 dBm) effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP). Examples of low-power transmitters are wireless devices for local communications that do not need a Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license, such as some IEEE 802.11X network access points, and portable (but not cellular) telephones.

entries.title: low probability of detection (LPD)
entries.summaryMd: Result of measures used to hide or disguise intentional electromagnetic transmissions.

senses.definitionMd: Result of measures used to hide or disguise intentional electromagnetic transmissions.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "low probability of detection (LPD)"

entries.title: low probability of intercept (LPI)
entries.summaryMd: Result of measures used to resist attempts by adversaries to analyze the parameters of a transmission to determine if it is a signal of interest.

senses.definitionMd: Result of measures used to resist attempts by adversaries to analyze the parameters of a transmission to determine if it is a signal of interest.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "low probability of intercept (LPI)"

entries.title: low probability of positioning
entries.summaryMd: Result of measures used to resist attempts by adversaries to determine the location of a particular transmitter.

senses.definitionMd: Result of measures used to resist attempts by adversaries to determine the location of a particular transmitter.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "low probability of positioning"

entries.title: MAC algorithm
entries.summaryMd: An algorithm that computes a MAC from a message and a key.

senses.definitionMd: An algorithm that computes a MAC from a message and a key.

entries.title: MAC Chaining Value
entries.summaryMd: A 16-byte value that is an input to the CMAC function and used to detect communication errors in duplicate or missing commands.

senses.definitionMd: A 16-byte value that is an input to the CMAC function and used to detect communication errors in duplicate or missing commands.

entries.title: MAC key
entries.summaryMd: A symmetric key used as input to a security function to produce a message authentication code (MAC).

senses.definitionMd: A symmetric key used as input to a security function to produce a message authentication code (MAC).

entries.title: MAC tag
entries.summaryMd: Data obtained from the output of a MAC algorithm (possibly by truncation) that can be used by an entity to verify the integrity and the origination of the information used as input to the MAC algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: Data obtained from the output of a MAC algorithm (possibly by truncation) that can be used by an entity to verify the integrity and the origination of the information used as input to the MAC algorithm.

entries.title: MacData
entries.summaryMd: A byte string input to the MacTag computation.

senses.definitionMd: A byte string input to the MacTag computation.

entries.title: MacDataU, (or MacDataV)
entries.summaryMd: MacData associated with party U (or party V, respectively), and used to generate MacTagU (or MacTagV, respectively). Each is a byte string.

senses.definitionMd: MacData associated with party U (or party V, respectively), and used to generate MacTagU (or MacTagV, respectively). Each is a byte string.

entries.title: machine controller
entries.summaryMd: A control system/motion network that electronically synchronizes drives within a machine system instead of relying on synchronization via mechanical linkage.

senses.definitionMd: A control system/motion network that electronically synchronizes drives within a machine system instead of relying on synchronization via mechanical linkage.

entries.title: Machine Learning
entries.summaryMd: The development and use of computer systems that adapt and learn from data with the goal of improving accuracy.

senses.definitionMd: The development and use of computer systems that adapt and learn from data with the goal of improving accuracy.

entries.title: Machine-Readable
entries.summaryMd: When used with respect to data, means data in a format that can be easily processed by a computer without human intervention while ensuring no semantic meaning is lost.

senses.definitionMd: When used with respect to data, means data in a format that can be easily processed by a computer without human intervention while ensuring no semantic meaning is lost.

entries.title: machine unlearning
entries.summaryMd: A technique that involves selectively removing the influences of spe­cific training data points from a trained machine learning model, such as to remove unwanted capabilities or knowledge in a foundation model, or to enable a user to request the removal of their records from a model. Efficient approximate unlearn­ing techniques may not require retraining the ML model from scratch.

senses.definitionMd: A technique that involves selectively removing the influences of spe­cific training data points from a trained machine learning model, such as to remove unwanted capabilities or knowledge in a foundation model, or to enable a user to request the removal of their records from a model. Efficient approximate unlearn­ing techniques may not require retraining the ML model from scratch.

entries.title: MacKey
entries.summaryMd: Key used to compute the MAC; a byte string.

senses.definitionMd: Key used to compute the MAC; a byte string.

entries.title: MacKeyBits
entries.summaryMd: The bit length of MacKey such that MacKeyBits = 8 ´ MacKeyLen.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of MacKey such that MacKeyBits = 8 ´ MacKeyLen.

entries.title: MacKeyLen
entries.summaryMd: The byte length of the MacKey.

senses.definitionMd: The byte length of the MacKey.

entries.title: MacOutputBits
entries.summaryMd: The bit length of the MAC output block such that MacOutputBits = 8 ´ MacOutputLen.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the MAC output block such that MacOutputBits = 8 ´ MacOutputLen.

entries.title: MacOutputLen
entries.summaryMd: The byte length of the MAC output block.

senses.definitionMd: The byte length of the MAC output block.

entries.title: macro virus
entries.summaryMd: A virus that attaches itself to documents and uses the macro programming capabilities of the document’s application to execute and propagate.

senses.definitionMd: A virus that attaches itself to documents and uses the macro programming capabilities of the document’s application to execute and propagate.

entries.title: MacTagBits
entries.summaryMd: The bit length of the MAC tag such that MacTagBits = 8 ´ MacTagLen.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the MAC tag such that MacTagBits = 8 ´ MacTagLen.

entries.title: MacTagLen
entries.summaryMd: The byte length of MacTag.

senses.definitionMd: The byte length of MacTag.

entries.title: MacTagV, (MacTagU)
entries.summaryMd: The MacTag generated by party V (or party U, respectively). Each is a byte string.

senses.definitionMd: The MacTag generated by party V (or party U, respectively). Each is a byte string.

entries.title: magnetic remanence
entries.summaryMd: Magnetic representation of residual information remaining on a magnetic medium after the medium has been cleared.

senses.definitionMd: Magnetic representation of residual information remaining on a magnetic medium after the medium has been cleared.

entries.title: Mail Server
entries.summaryMd: A host that provides “electronic post office” facilities. It stores incoming mail for distribution to users and forwards outgoing mail. The term may refer to just the application that performs this service, which can reside on a machine with other services, but for this document the term refers to the entire host including the mail server application, the host operating system and the supporting hardware.

senses.definitionMd: A host that provides “electronic post office” facilities. It stores incoming mail for distribution to users and forwards outgoing mail. The term may refer to just the application that performs this service, which can reside on a machine with other services, but for this document the term refers to the entire host including the mail server application, the host operating system and the supporting hardware.

entries.title: Mail Server Administrator
entries.summaryMd: The mail server equivalent of a system administrator. Mail server administrators are system architects responsible for the overall design and implementation of mail servers.

senses.definitionMd: The mail server equivalent of a system administrator. Mail server administrators are system architects responsible for the overall design and implementation of mail servers.

entries.title: Mail Transfer Agent (MTA)
entries.summaryMd: A program running on a mail server that receives messages from mail user agents or other MTAs and either forwards them to another MTA or, if the recipient is on the MTA, delivers the message to the local delivery agent (LDA) for delivery to the recipient. Common MTAs include Microsoft Exchange and sendmail.

senses.definitionMd: A program running on a mail server that receives messages from mail user agents or other MTAs and either forwards them to another MTA or, if the recipient is on the MTA, delivers the message to the local delivery agent (LDA) for delivery to the recipient. Common MTAs include Microsoft Exchange and sendmail.

entries.title: Mail User Agent (MUA)
entries.summaryMd: A mail client application used by an end user to access a mail server to read, compose, and send email messages. Common MUAs include Microsoft Outlook and Mozilla Thunderbird.

senses.definitionMd: A mail client application used by an end user to access a mail server to read, compose, and send email messages. Common MUAs include Microsoft Outlook and Mozilla Thunderbird.

entries.title: maintenance
entries.summaryMd: Any act that either prevents the failure or malfunction of equipment or restores its operating capability.

senses.definitionMd: Any act that either prevents the failure or malfunction of equipment or restores its operating capability.

entries.title: maintenance key
entries.summaryMd: Key intended only for off-the-air, in-shop use. Maintenance key may not be used to protect classified or sensitive U.S. Government information. Also known as bench test key.

senses.definitionMd: Key intended only for off-the-air, in-shop use. Maintenance key may not be used to protect classified or sensitive U.S. Government information. Also known as bench test key.

entries.title: major application
entries.summaryMd: An application that requires special attention to security due to the risk and magnitude of harm resulting from the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of the information in the application. Note: All federal applications require some level of protection. Certain applications, because of the information in them, however, require special management oversight and should be treated as major. Adequate security for other applications should be provided by security of the systems in which they operate.

senses.definitionMd: An application that requires special attention to security due to the risk and magnitude of harm resulting from the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of the information in the application. Note: All federal applications require some level of protection. Certain applications, because of the information in them, however, require special management oversight and should be treated as major. Adequate security for other applications should be provided by security of the systems in which they operate.

entries.title: Major Revision
entries.summaryMd: Any increase in the version of an SCAP component’s specification or SCAP related data set that involves substantive changes that will break backwards compatibility with previous releases.

senses.definitionMd: Any increase in the version of an SCAP component’s specification or SCAP related data set that involves substantive changes that will break backwards compatibility with previous releases.

entries.title: Major version update
entries.summaryMd: A revision of a specification that breaks backward compatibility with the previous revision of the specification in numerous significant ways.

senses.definitionMd: A revision of a specification that breaks backward compatibility with the previous revision of the specification in numerous significant ways.

entries.title: majority judgment algorithm
entries.summaryMd: An inter-level judgment conflict resolution algorithm where the judgment that occurs most frequently is taken as the result. If more than one judgment occurs the greatest number of times, then the weakest such judgment is the result.

senses.definitionMd: An inter-level judgment conflict resolution algorithm where the judgment that occurs most frequently is taken as the result. If more than one judgment occurs the greatest number of times, then the weakest such judgment is the result.

entries.title: malicious cyber activity
entries.summaryMd: Activities, other than those authorized by or in accordance with U.S. law, that seek to compromise or impair the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of computers, information or communication systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by computers of information systems, or information resident thereon.

senses.definitionMd: Activities, other than those authorized by or in accordance with U.S. law, that seek to compromise or impair the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of computers, information or communication systems, networks, physical or virtual infrastructure controlled by computers of information systems, or information resident thereon.

entries.title: malware
entries.summaryMd: Hardware, firmware, or software that is intentionally included or inserted in a system for a harmful purpose.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware, firmware, or software that is intentionally included or inserted in a system for a harmful purpose.

entries.title: man-in-the-middle attack (MitM)
entries.summaryMd: A form of active wiretapping attack in which the attacker intercepts and selectively modifies communicated data to masquerade as one or more of the entities involved in a communication association.

senses.definitionMd: A form of active wiretapping attack in which the attacker intercepts and selectively modifies communicated data to masquerade as one or more of the entities involved in a communication association.

entries.title: Manage Boundaries
entries.summaryMd: An ISCM capability that addresses the following network and physical boundary areas: Physical Boundaries – Ensure that movement (of people, media, equipment, etc.) into and out of the physical facility does not compromise security. Filters – Ensure that traffic into and out of the network (and thus out of the physical facility protection) does not compromise security. Do the same for enclaves that subdivide the network. Other – Ensure that information is protected (with adequate strength) when needed to protect confidentiality and integrity, whether that information is in transit or at rest.

senses.definitionMd: An ISCM capability that addresses the following network and physical boundary areas: Physical Boundaries – Ensure that movement (of people, media, equipment, etc.) into and out of the physical facility does not compromise security. Filters – Ensure that traffic into and out of the network (and thus out of the physical facility protection) does not compromise security. Do the same for enclaves that subdivide the network. Other – Ensure that information is protected (with adequate strength) when needed to protect confidentiality and integrity, whether that information is in transit or at rest.

entries.title: Manage Credentials and Authentication
entries.summaryMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that people have the credentials and authentication methods necessary (and only those necessary) to perform their duties, while limiting access to that which is necessary.

senses.definitionMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that people have the credentials and authentication methods necessary (and only those necessary) to perform their duties, while limiting access to that which is necessary.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Manage Credentials and Authentication"

entries.title: Manage Privileges
entries.summaryMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that people have the privileges necessary (and only those necessary) to perform their duties, to limit access to that which is necessary.

senses.definitionMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that people have the privileges necessary (and only those necessary) to perform their duties, to limit access to that which is necessary.

entries.title: Manageability
entries.summaryMd: Providing the capability for granular administration of data, including alteration, deletion, and selective disclosure.

senses.definitionMd: Providing the capability for granular administration of data, including alteration, deletion, and selective disclosure.

entries.title: Managed Devices
entries.summaryMd: Personal computers, laptops, mobile devices, virtual machines, and infrastructure components require management agents, allowing information technology staff to discover, maintain, and control them. Those with broken or missing agents cannot be seen or managed by agent-based security products.

senses.definitionMd: Personal computers, laptops, mobile devices, virtual machines, and infrastructure components require management agents, allowing information technology staff to discover, maintain, and control them. Those with broken or missing agents cannot be seen or managed by agent-based security products.

entries.title: Managed Environment
entries.summaryMd: Environment comprising centrally managed IT products, everything ranging from servers and printers to desktops, laptops, smartphones, and tablets.

senses.definitionMd: Environment comprising centrally managed IT products, everything ranging from servers and printers to desktops, laptops, smartphones, and tablets.

entries.title: managed interface
entries.summaryMd: An interface within an information system that provides boundary protection capability using automated mechanisms or devices.

senses.definitionMd: An interface within an information system that provides boundary protection capability using automated mechanisms or devices.

entries.title: management client (MGC)
entries.summaryMd: A configuration of a client node that enables a key management infrastructure (KMI) external operational manager to manage KMI products and services by either 1) accessing a PRSN or 2) exercising locally-provided capabilities. A management client (MGC) consists of a client platform and an advanced key processor (AKP).

senses.definitionMd: A configuration of a client node that enables a key management infrastructure (KMI) external operational manager to manage KMI products and services by either 1) accessing a PRSN or 2) exercising locally-provided capabilities. A management client (MGC) consists of a client platform and an advanced key processor (AKP).

entries.title: management controls
entries.summaryMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that focus on the management of risk and the management of information system security.

senses.definitionMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that focus on the management of risk and the management of information system security.

entries.title: management security controls
entries.summaryMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that focus on the management of risk and the management of information systems security. Rationale: Listed for deletion in 2010 version of CNSS 4009.

senses.definitionMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that focus on the management of risk and the management of information systems security. Rationale: Listed for deletion in 2010 version of CNSS 4009.

entries.title: Management stations
entries.summaryMd: Systems with which only IT and network administrators interact

senses.definitionMd: Systems with which only IT and network administrators interact

entries.title: Manager
entries.summaryMd: An individual responsible for network resources (people, data, processing capability) who is charged with conducting business of an organization.

senses.definitionMd: An individual responsible for network resources (people, data, processing capability) who is charged with conducting business of an organization.

entries.title: mandate
entries.summaryMd: A mandatory order or requirement under statute.

senses.definitionMd: A mandatory order or requirement under statute.

entries.title: mandatory access control (MAC)
entries.summaryMd: An access control policy that is uniformly enforced across all subjects and objects within the boundary of an information system. A subject that has been granted access to information is constrained from doing any of the following: (i) passing the information to unauthorized subjects or objects; (ii) granting its privileges to other subjects; (iii) changing one or more security attributes on subjects, objects, the information system, or system components; (iv) choosing the security attributes to be associated with newly-created or modified objects; or (v) changing the rules governing access control. Organization-defined subjects may explicitly be granted organization-defined privileges (i.e., they are trusted subjects) such that they are not limited by some or all of the above constraints.

senses.definitionMd: An access control policy that is uniformly enforced across all subjects and objects within the boundary of an information system. A subject that has been granted access to information is constrained from doing any of the following: (i) passing the information to unauthorized subjects or objects; (ii) granting its privileges to other subjects; (iii) changing one or more security attributes on subjects, objects, the information system, or system components; (iv) choosing the security attributes to be associated with newly-created or modified objects; or (v) changing the rules governing access control. Organization-defined subjects may explicitly be granted organization-defined privileges (i.e., they are trusted subjects) such that they are not limited by some or all of the above constraints.

entries.title: mandatory modification (MAN)
entries.summaryMd: A change to a COMSEC end-item, which the National Security Agency (NSA) requires to be completed and reported by a specified date.

senses.definitionMd: A change to a COMSEC end-item, which the National Security Agency (NSA) requires to be completed and reported by a specified date.

entries.title: manipulated variable
entries.summaryMd: In a process that is intended to regulate some condition, a quantity or a condition that the control alters to initiate a change in the value of the regulated condition.

senses.definitionMd: In a process that is intended to regulate some condition, a quantity or a condition that the control alters to initiate a change in the value of the regulated condition.

entries.title: manipulative communications deception
entries.summaryMd: Alteration or simulation of friendly telecommunications for the purpose of deception. See communications deception and imitative communications deception. Rationale: Listed for deletion in 2010 version of CNSS 4009.

senses.definitionMd: Alteration or simulation of friendly telecommunications for the purpose of deception. See communications deception and imitative communications deception. Rationale: Listed for deletion in 2010 version of CNSS 4009.

entries.title: manual cryptosystem
entries.summaryMd: Cryptosystem in which the cryptographic processes are performed without the use of crypto-equipment or auto-manual devices.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptosystem in which the cryptographic processes are performed without the use of crypto-equipment or auto-manual devices.

entries.title: Manual key distribution
entries.summaryMd: A non-automated means of transporting cryptographic keys by physically moving a device or document containing the key or key component.

senses.definitionMd: A non-automated means of transporting cryptographic keys by physically moving a device or document containing the key or key component.

entries.title: Manual key transport
entries.summaryMd: A non-automated means of transporting cryptographic keys by physically moving a device or document containing the key or key share.

senses.definitionMd: A non-automated means of transporting cryptographic keys by physically moving a device or document containing the key or key share.

entries.title: manual remote rekeying
entries.summaryMd: Synonymous with manual remote rekeying.

senses.definitionMd: Synonymous with manual remote rekeying.

entries.title: Manufacturer Usage Description (MUD)
entries.summaryMd: A component-based architecture specified in Request for Comments (RFC) 8520 that is designed to provide a means for end devices to signal to the network what sort of access and network functionality they require to properly function.

senses.definitionMd: A component-based architecture specified in Request for Comments (RFC) 8520 that is designed to provide a means for end devices to signal to the network what sort of access and network functionality they require to properly function.

entries.title: Manufacturing Operations
entries.summaryMd: Activities concerning the facility operation, system processes, materials input/output, maintenance, supply and distribution, health, and safety, emergency response, human resources, security, information technology and other contributing measures to the manufacturing enterprise.

senses.definitionMd: Activities concerning the facility operation, system processes, materials input/output, maintenance, supply and distribution, health, and safety, emergency response, human resources, security, information technology and other contributing measures to the manufacturing enterprise.

entries.title: Maple
entries.summaryMd: An interactive computer algebra system that provides a complete mathematical environment for the manipulation and simplification of symbolic algebraic expressions, arbitrary extended precision mathematics, two- and three-dimensional graphics, and programming.

senses.definitionMd: An interactive computer algebra system that provides a complete mathematical environment for the manipulation and simplification of symbolic algebraic expressions, arbitrary extended precision mathematics, two- and three-dimensional graphics, and programming.

entries.title: Mapping
entries.summaryMd: Depiction of how data from one information source maps to data from another information source.

senses.definitionMd: Depiction of how data from one information source maps to data from another information source.

entries.title: margin
entries.summaryMd: The margin allocated during design based on assessments of uncertainty and unknowns. This margin is often consumed as the design matures.

senses.definitionMd: The margin allocated during design based on assessments of uncertainty and unknowns. This margin is often consumed as the design matures.

entries.title: Market research
entries.summaryMd: Collecting and analyzing information about capabilities within the market to satisfy agency needs.

senses.definitionMd: Collecting and analyzing information about capabilities within the market to satisfy agency needs.

entries.title: marking
entries.summaryMd: The means used to associate a set of security attributes with objects in a human-readable form, to enable organizational process-based enforcement of information security policies.

senses.definitionMd: The means used to associate a set of security attributes with objects in a human-readable form, to enable organizational process-based enforcement of information security policies.

entries.title: Markov model
entries.summaryMd: A model for a probability distribution where the probability that the ith element of a sequence has a given value depends only on the values of the previous n elements of the sequence. The model is called an nth order Markov model.

senses.definitionMd: A model for a probability distribution where the probability that the ith element of a sequence has a given value depends only on the values of the previous n elements of the sequence. The model is called an nth order Markov model.

entries.title: masking
entries.summaryMd: The process of systematically removing a field or replacing it with a value in a way that does not preserve the analytic utility of the value, such as replacing a phone number with asterisks or a randomly generated pseudonym.

senses.definitionMd: The process of systematically removing a field or replacing it with a value in a way that does not preserve the analytic utility of the value, such as replacing a phone number with asterisks or a randomly generated pseudonym.

entries.title: masquerading
entries.summaryMd: A type of threat action whereby an unauthorized entity gains access to a system or performs a malicious act by illegitimately posing as an authorized entity.

senses.definitionMd: A type of threat action whereby an unauthorized entity gains access to a system or performs a malicious act by illegitimately posing as an authorized entity.

entries.title: Master key
entries.summaryMd: See Key-derivation key.

senses.definitionMd: See Key-derivation key.

entries.title: Master Scenario Events List (MSEL)
entries.summaryMd: A chronologically sequenced outline of the simulated events and key event descriptions that participants will be asked to respond to during an exercise.

senses.definitionMd: A chronologically sequenced outline of the simulated events and key event descriptions that participants will be asked to respond to during an exercise.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Master Scenario Events List (MSEL)"

entries.title: Master Terminal Unit (MTU)
entries.summaryMd: A controller that also acts as a server that hosts the control software that communicates with lower-level control devices, such as remote terminal units (RTUs) and programmable logic controllers (PLCs), over an OT network. entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic checksum on data that uses a symmetric key to detect both accidental and intentional modifications of the data. See checksum.

entries.title: Message Authentication Code (MAC) algorithm
entries.summaryMd: A family of cryptographic functions that is parameterized by a symmetric key. Each of the functions can act on input data (called a “message”) of variable length to produce an output value of a specified length. The output value is called the MAC of the input message. An approved MAC algorithm is expected to satisfy the following property (for each of its supported security levels): It must be computationally infeasible to determine the (as yet unseen) MAC of a message without knowledge of the key, even if one has already seen the results of using that key to compute the MAC's of other (different) messages. A MAC algorithm can be used to provide data-origin authentication and data-integrity protection. In this Recommendation, a MAC algorithm is used for key confirmation; the use of MAC algorithms for key derivation is addressed in SP 800-56C.

senses.definitionMd: A family of cryptographic functions that is parameterized by a symmetric key. Each of the functions can act on input data (called a “message”) of variable length to produce an output value of a specified length. The output value is called the MAC of the input message. An approved MAC algorithm is expected to satisfy the following property (for each of its supported security levels): It must be computationally infeasible to determine the (as yet unseen) MAC of a message without knowledge of the key, even if one has already seen the results of using that key to compute the MAC's of other (different) messages. A MAC algorithm can be used to provide data-origin authentication and data-integrity protection. In this Recommendation, a MAC algorithm is used for key confirmation; the use of MAC algorithms for key derivation is addressed in SP 800-56C.

entries.title: min-entropy
entries.summaryMd: The min-entropy (in bits) of a random variable X is the largest value m having the property that each observation of X provides at least m bits of information (i.e., the min-entropy of X is the greatest lower bound for the information content of potential observations of X). The min-entropy of a random variable is a lower bound on its entropy. The precise formulation for min-entropy is −(log2 max pi) for a discrete distribution having n possible outputs with probabilities p1,…, pn. Min-entropy is often used as a worst-case measure of the unpredictability of a random variable. Also see [NIST SP 800-90B].

entries.title: mobile device
entries.summaryMd: A portable computing device that has a small form factor such that: it can easily be carried by a single individual;is designed to operate without a physical connection (e.g., wirelessly transmit or receive information);possesses local, non- removable/removable data storage; andincludes a self-contained power source.Mobile devices may also include voice communication capabilities, on-board sensors that allow the device to capture information, or built-in features that synchronize local data with remote locations. Examples include smartphones, tablets, and E-readers. Also known as a "portable computing device." Note: If the device only has storage capability and is not capable of processing or transmitting/receiving information, then it is considered a portable storage device, not a mobile device.

senses.definitionMd: A portable computing device that has a small form factor such that: it can easily be carried by a single individual;is designed to operate without a physical connection (e.g., wirelessly transmit or receive information);possesses local, non- removable/removable data storage; andincludes a self-contained power source.Mobile devices may also include voice communication capabilities, on-board sensors that allow the device to capture information, or built-in features that synchronize local data with remote locations. Examples include smartphones, tablets, and E-readers. Also known as a "portable computing device." Note: If the device only has storage capability and is not capable of processing or transmitting/receiving information, then it is considered a portable storage device, not a mobile device.

entries.title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
entries.summaryMd: The administration of mobile devices such as smartphones, tablets, computers, laptops, and desktop computers. MDM is usually implemented through a third-party product that has management features for particular vendors of mobile devices.

senses.definitionMd: The administration of mobile devices such as smartphones, tablets, computers, laptops, and desktop computers. MDM is usually implemented through a third-party product that has management features for particular vendors of mobile devices.

entries.title: Mobile Internet Key Exchange (MOBIKE)
entries.summaryMd: A form of IKE supporting the use of devices with multiple network interfaces that switch from one network to another while IPsec is in use.

senses.definitionMd: A form of IKE supporting the use of devices with multiple network interfaces that switch from one network to another while IPsec is in use.

entries.title: mobile mode
entries.summaryMd: Software programs or parts of programs obtained from remote information systems, transmitted across a network, and executed on a local information system without explicit installation or execution by the recipient.

senses.definitionMd: Software programs or parts of programs obtained from remote information systems, transmitted across a network, and executed on a local information system without explicit installation or execution by the recipient.

entries.title: Mobile Subscriber Integrated Services Digital Network (MSISDN)
entries.summaryMd: The international telephone number assigned to a cellular subscriber.

senses.definitionMd: The international telephone number assigned to a cellular subscriber.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Mobile Subscriber Integrated Services Digital Network (MSISDN)"

entries.title: mode of iteration

senses.definitionMd: A method for iterating the multiple invocations of a pseudorandom function in order to derive the keying material with a required length.

entries.summaryMd: An algorithm for the cryptographic transformation of data that features a symmetric key block cipher algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: An algorithm for the cryptographic transformation of data that features a symmetric key block cipher algorithm.

entries.title: Model
entries.summaryMd: A detailed description or scaled representation of one component of a larger system that can be created, operated, and analyzed to predict actual operational characteristics of the final produced component.

senses.definitionMd: A detailed description or scaled representation of one component of a larger system that can be created, operated, and analyzed to predict actual operational characteristics of the final produced component.

entries.title: model control
entries.summaryMd: A capability with which an attacker can control the machine learning model parameters.

senses.definitionMd: A capability with which an attacker can control the machine learning model parameters.

entries.title: model extraction
entries.summaryMd: A type of privacy attack that extracts details of the model architecture and/or parameters.

senses.definitionMd: A type of privacy attack that extracts details of the model architecture and/or parameters.

entries.title: model poisoning
entries.summaryMd: A poisoning attack which operates through model control.

senses.definitionMd: A poisoning attack which operates through model control.

entries.title: model privacy attacks
entries.summaryMd: An attack against machine learning models to extract sensitive in­formation about the model.

senses.definitionMd: An attack against machine learning models to extract sensitive in­formation about the model.

entries.title: model weight
entries.summaryMd: A numerical parameter within an AI model that helps determine the model’s outputs in response to inputs.

senses.definitionMd: A numerical parameter within an AI model that helps determine the model’s outputs in response to inputs.

entries.title: modem
entries.summaryMd: A device used to convert serial digital data from a transmitting terminal to a signal suitable for transmission over a telephone channel to reconvert the transmitted signal to serial digital data for the receiving terminal.

senses.definitionMd: A device used to convert serial digital data from a transmitting terminal to a signal suitable for transmission over a telephone channel to reconvert the transmitted signal to serial digital data for the receiving terminal.

entries.title: Moderate Impact
entries.summaryMd: The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability that could be expected to have a serious adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the national security interests of the United States; (i.e., 1) causes a significant degradation in mission capability to an extent and duration that the organization is able to perform its primary functions, but the effectiveness of the functions is significantly reduced; 2) results in significant damage to organizational assets; 3) results in significant financial loss; or 4) results in significant harm to individuals that does not involve loss of life or serious life threatening injuries.).

senses.definitionMd: The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability that could be expected to have a serious adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the national security interests of the United States; (i.e., 1) causes a significant degradation in mission capability to an extent and duration that the organization is able to perform its primary functions, but the effectiveness of the functions is significantly reduced; 2) results in significant damage to organizational assets; 3) results in significant financial loss; or 4) results in significant harm to individuals that does not involve loss of life or serious life threatening injuries.).

entries.title: moderate-impact system
entries.summaryMd: An information system in which at least one security objective (i.e., confidentiality, integrity, or availability) is assigned a FIPS 199 potential impact value of moderate, and no security objective is assigned a FIPS 199 potential impact value of high.

senses.definitionMd: An information system in which at least one security objective (i.e., confidentiality, integrity, or availability) is assigned a FIPS 199 potential impact value of moderate, and no security objective is assigned a FIPS 199 potential impact value of high.

entries.title: modern key
entries.summaryMd: A collective name for asymmetric key such as Secure Data Network system (SDNS) FIREFLY key and message signature key. It does not include the Public Key Infrastructure system or keys.

senses.definitionMd: A collective name for asymmetric key such as Secure Data Network system (SDNS) FIREFLY key and message signature key. It does not include the Public Key Infrastructure system or keys.

entries.title: Modified condition decision coverage
entries.summaryMd: This is a strong coverage criterion that is required by the US Federal Aviation Administration for Level A (catastrophic failure consequence) software; i.e., software whose failure could lead to loss of function necessary for safe operation. It requires that every condition in a decision in the program has taken on all possible outcomes at least once, and each condition has been shown to independently affect the decision outcome, and that each entry and exit point have been invoked at least once.

senses.definitionMd: This is a strong coverage criterion that is required by the US Federal Aviation Administration for Level A (catastrophic failure consequence) software; i.e., software whose failure could lead to loss of function necessary for safe operation. It requires that every condition in a decision in the program has taken on all possible outcomes at least once, and each condition has been shown to independently affect the decision outcome, and that each entry and exit point have been invoked at least once.

entries.title: Modular Contracting
entries.summaryMd: Under modular contracting, an executive agency’s need for a system is satisfied in successive acquisitions of interoperable increments. Each increment complies with common or commercially accepted standards applicable to information technology so that the increments are compatible with other increments of information technology composing the system.

senses.definitionMd: Under modular contracting, an executive agency’s need for a system is satisfied in successive acquisitions of interoperable increments. Each increment complies with common or commercially accepted standards applicable to information technology so that the increments are compatible with other increments of information technology composing the system.

entries.title: module
entries.summaryMd: See Cryptographic module.

senses.definitionMd: See Cryptographic module.

entries.title: monitoring
entries.summaryMd: Continual checking, supervising, critically observing or determining the status in order to identify change from the performance level required or expected.

senses.definitionMd: Continual checking, supervising, critically observing or determining the status in order to identify change from the performance level required or expected.

entries.title: Monobit Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in a sequence are approximately the same as would be expected for a truly random sequence.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the number of ones and zeros in a sequence are approximately the same as would be expected for a truly random sequence.

entries.title: Monte Carlo analysis
entries.summaryMd: A probabilistic sensitivity analysis used to account for uncertainty.

senses.definitionMd: A probabilistic sensitivity analysis used to account for uncertainty.

entries.title: most significant bit(s)
entries.summaryMd: The left-most bit(s) of a bit string.

senses.definitionMd: The left-most bit(s) of a bit string.

entries.title: motivated intruder test
entries.summaryMd: The ‘motivated intruder’ is taken to be a person who starts without any prior knowledge but who wishes to identify the individual from whose personal data the anonymized data have been derived. This test is meant to assess whether the motivated intruder would be successful.

senses.definitionMd: The ‘motivated intruder’ is taken to be a person who starts without any prior knowledge but who wishes to identify the individual from whose personal data the anonymized data have been derived. This test is meant to assess whether the motivated intruder would be successful.

entries.title: moving target defense
entries.summaryMd: The concept of controlling change across multiple system dimensions in order to increase uncertainty and apparent complexity for attackers, reduce their window of opportunity, and increase the costs of their probing and attack efforts.

senses.definitionMd: The concept of controlling change across multiple system dimensions in order to increase uncertainty and apparent complexity for attackers, reduce their window of opportunity, and increase the costs of their probing and attack efforts.

entries.title: Ms
entries.summaryMd: The (original) message prior to randomization.

senses.definitionMd: The (original) message prior to randomization.

entries.title: MUD-Capable
entries.summaryMd: An Internet of Things (IoT) device that can emit a MUD uniform resource locator in compliance with the MUD specification.

senses.definitionMd: An Internet of Things (IoT) device that can emit a MUD uniform resource locator in compliance with the MUD specification.

entries.title: Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED)
entries.summaryMd: A BGP attribute used on external links to indicate preferred entry or exit points (among many) for an AS.

senses.definitionMd: A BGP attribute used on external links to indicate preferred entry or exit points (among many) for an AS.

entries.title: multi-factor authentication
entries.summaryMd: The means used to confirm the identity of a user, process, or device (e.g., user password or token).

senses.definitionMd: The means used to confirm the identity of a user, process, or device (e.g., user password or token).

entries.title: multi-level cross domain solution
entries.summaryMd: A type of cross domain solution (CDS) that uses trusted security labeling to associate a classification or sensitivity level with objects and enforces a mandatory security policy over a subject's access to objects, based upon the security domain and authorization attributes.

senses.definitionMd: A type of cross domain solution (CDS) that uses trusted security labeling to associate a classification or sensitivity level with objects and enforces a mandatory security policy over a subject's access to objects, based upon the security domain and authorization attributes.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "multi-level cross domain solution"

entries.title: multi-level device
entries.summaryMd: Equipment trusted to properly maintain and separate data of different security domains.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment trusted to properly maintain and separate data of different security domains.

entries.title: Multi-level security domain
entries.summaryMd: A security domain that supports information protection at more than one impact-level.

senses.definitionMd: A security domain that supports information protection at more than one impact-level.

entries.title: multi-level security (MLS)
entries.summaryMd: Concept of processing information with different classifications and categories that simultaneously permits access by users with different security clearances and denies access to users who lack authorization.

senses.definitionMd: Concept of processing information with different classifications and categories that simultaneously permits access by users with different security clearances and denies access to users who lack authorization.

entries.title: multi-level solution
entries.summaryMd: A technical implementation of multi-level security.

senses.definitionMd: A technical implementation of multi-level security.

entries.title: multi-releasable
entries.summaryMd: A characteristic of an information domain where access control mechanisms enforce policy-based release of information to authorized users within the information domain.

senses.definitionMd: A characteristic of an information domain where access control mechanisms enforce policy-based release of information to authorized users within the information domain.

entries.title: Multi-Signature
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic signature scheme where the process of signing information (e.g., a transaction) is distributed among multiple private keys.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic signature scheme where the process of signing information (e.g., a transaction) is distributed among multiple private keys.

entries.title: Multifactor
entries.summaryMd: A characteristic of an authentication system or an authenticator that requires more than one distinct authentication factor for successful authentication. MFA can be performed using a single authenticator that provides more than one factor or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. The three authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are.

senses.definitionMd: A characteristic of an authentication system or an authenticator that requires more than one distinct authentication factor for successful authentication. MFA can be performed using a single authenticator that provides more than one factor or by a combination of authenticators that provide different factors. The three authentication factors are something you know, something you have, and something you are.

entries.title: Multifactor Authenticator
entries.summaryMd: An authenticator that provides more than one distinct authentication factor, such as a cryptographic authentication device with an integrated biometric sensor that is required to activate the device.

senses.definitionMd: An authenticator that provides more than one distinct authentication factor, such as a cryptographic authentication device with an integrated biometric sensor that is required to activate the device.

entries.title: Multimedia Messaging Service (MMS)
entries.summaryMd: An accepted standard for messaging that lets users send and receive messages formatted with text, graphics, photographs, audio, and video clips.

senses.definitionMd: An accepted standard for messaging that lets users send and receive messages formatted with text, graphics, photographs, audio, and video clips.

entries.title: multimodal models
entries.summaryMd: A model that processes and relates information from multiple sensory modalities that each represent primary human channels of communication and sensation, such as vision and touch.

senses.definitionMd: A model that processes and relates information from multiple sensory modalities that each represent primary human channels of communication and sensation, such as vision and touch.

entries.title: multipath
entries.summaryMd: The propagation phenomenon that results in signals reaching the receiving antenna by two or more paths. When two or more signals arrive simultaneously, wave interference results. The received signal fades if the wave interference is time varying or if one of the terminals is in motion.

senses.definitionMd: The propagation phenomenon that results in signals reaching the receiving antenna by two or more paths. When two or more signals arrive simultaneously, wave interference results. The received signal fades if the wave interference is time varying or if one of the terminals is in motion.

entries.title: Multiple-center group
entries.summaryMd: As used in this Recommendation, a set of two or more key centers that have agreed to work together to provide cryptographic keying services to their subscribers.

senses.definitionMd: As used in this Recommendation, a set of two or more key centers that have agreed to work together to provide cryptographic keying services to their subscribers.

entries.title: multiple security levels (MSL)
entries.summaryMd: Capability of an information system that is trusted to contain, and maintain separation between, resources (particularly stored data) of different security domains.

entries.summaryMd: A protocol that makes use of the headers in an IETF RFC 2822 message to describe the structure of rich message content.

entries.title: must
entries.summaryMd: Indicates a requirement of this recommendation that might not be testable by a CMVP testing lab.

senses.definitionMd: Indicates a requirement of this recommendation that might not be testable by a CMVP testing lab.

entries.title: mutual authentication
entries.summaryMd: The process of both entities involved in a transaction verifying each other.

senses.definitionMd: The process of both entities involved in a transaction verifying each other.

entries.title: n

entries.title: (n,k) rule
entries.summaryMd: A cell is regarded as confidential, if the n largest units contribute more than k % to the cell total, e.g., n=2 and k=85 means that a cell is defined as risky if the two largest units contribute more than 85 % to the cell total. The n and k are given by the statistical authority. In some NSOs [national statistical office] the values of n and k are confidential.

entries.title: Narrowest internal width
entries.summaryMd: The maximum amount of information from the input that can affect the output. For example, if f(x) = SHA-1(x) || 01, and x consists of a string of 1000 binary bits, then the narrowest internal width of f(x) is 160 bits (the SHA-1 output length), and the output width of f(x) is 162 bits (the 160 bits from the SHA-1 operation, concatenated by 01).

entries.title: National COMSEC Incident Reporting System (NCIRS)
entries.summaryMd: System established by the National Security Agency (NSA) as a means of ensuring that all reported incidents are evaluated so that actions can be taken to minimize any adverse impact on national security. The NCIRS is comprised of the organizations within the NSS community (NSA, heads of Department or Agency, material controlling authorities, and product resource managers) responsible for the reporting and evaluation of COMSEC incidents.

entries.title: National Information Assurance Partnership (NIAP)
entries.summaryMd: A U.S. Government initiative managed by the National Security Agency, established to promote the use of evaluated information systems products and champion the development and use of national and international standards for information technology security. The key operational component of NIAP is the Common Criteria Evaluation and Validation Scheme (CCEVS) which is the only U.S. Government- sponsored and endorsed program for conducting internationally- recognized security evaluations of COTS CS and CS-enabled information technology products. NIAP employs the CCEVS to provide government oversight or "validation" to U.S. Common Criteria (CC) evaluations to ensure correct conformance to the International Common Criteria for IT Security Evaluation (ISO/IEC Standard 15408-1:2009).

entries.summaryMd: Nationwide interconnection of communications networks, computers, databases, and consumer electronics that make vast amounts of information available to users. It includes both public and private networks, the internet, the public switched network, and cable, wireless, and satellite communications.

entries.title: national security emergency preparedness telecommunications services
entries.summaryMd: Telecommunications services that are used to maintain a state of readiness or to respond to and manage any event or crisis (local, national, or international) that causes or could cause injury or harm to the population, damage to or loss of property, or degrade or threaten the national security or emergency preparedness posture of the United States.

entries.title: national security information (NSI)
entries.summaryMd: Information that has been determined pursuant to Executive Order 12958 as amended by Executive Order 13292, or any predecessor order, or by the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and is marked to indicate its classified status.

senses.definitionMd: Information that has been determined pursuant to Executive Order 12958 as amended by Executive Order 13292, or any predecessor order, or by the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, to require protection against unauthorized disclosure and is marked to indicate its classified status.

entries.title: national security system (NSS)
entries.summaryMd: Any information system (including any telecommunications system) used or operated by an agency or by a contractor of an agency, or other organization on behalf of an agency— (i) the function, operation, or use of which involves intelligence activities; involves cryptologic activities related to national security; involves command and control of military forces; involves equipment that is an integral part of a weapon or weapons system; or is critical to the direct fulfillment of military or intelligence missions (excluding a system that is to be used for routine administrative and business applications, for example, payroll, finance, logistics, and personnel management applications); or (ii) is protected at all times by procedures established for information that have been specifically authorized under criteria established by an Executive Order or an Act of Congress to be kept classified in the interest of national defense or foreign policy.

senses.definitionMd: Any information system (including any telecommunications system) used or operated by an agency or by a contractor of an agency, or other organization on behalf of an agency— (i) the function, operation, or use of which involves intelligence activities; involves cryptologic activities related to national security; involves command and control of military forces; involves equipment that is an integral part of a weapon or weapons system; or is critical to the direct fulfillment of military or intelligence missions (excluding a system that is to be used for routine administrative and business applications, for example, payroll, finance, logistics, and personnel management applications); or (ii) is protected at all times by procedures established for information that have been specifically authorized under criteria established by an Executive Order or an Act of Congress to be kept classified in the interest of national defense or foreign policy.

entries.title: National Vulnerability Database
entries.summaryMd: The U.S. Government repository of standards-based vulnerability management data, enabling automation of vulnerability management, security measurement, and compliance (e.g., FISMA).

senses.definitionMd: The U.S. Government repository of standards-based vulnerability management data, enabling automation of vulnerability management, security measurement, and compliance (e.g., FISMA).

entries.title: natural language policy
entries.summaryMd: Statements governing management and access of enterprise objects. NLPs are human expressions that can be translated to machine-enforceable access control policies.

senses.definitionMd: Statements governing management and access of enterprise objects. NLPs are human expressions that can be translated to machine-enforceable access control policies.

entries.title: natural person
entries.summaryMd: A real-life human being, not synthetic or artificial.

senses.definitionMd: A real-life human being, not synthetic or artificial.

entries.title: navigation
entries.summaryMd: The ability to determine a current and desired position (relative or absolute) and apply corrections to course, orientation, and speed to attain a desired position. Navigation coverage requirements could be global, from sub-surface to surface and from surface to space.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to determine a current and desired position (relative or absolute) and apply corrections to course, orientation, and speed to attain a desired position. Navigation coverage requirements could be global, from sub-surface to surface and from surface to space.

entries.title: nBits

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the RSA modulus n.

entries.title: Near Field Communication (NFC)
entries.summaryMd: A form of contactless, close proximity, radio communications based on radio-frequency identification (RFID) technology.

senses.definitionMd: A form of contactless, close proximity, radio communications based on radio-frequency identification (RFID) technology.

entries.title: need-to-know

entries.title: needs assessment

senses.definitionMd: The process of identifying gaps in learning and the needs of learning activities.

entries.title: negative risk
entries.summaryMd: Any circumstance or event with the potential to adversely impact organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation through an information system via unauthorized access, destruction, disclosure, modification of information, and/or denial of service.

senses.definitionMd: Any circumstance or event with the potential to adversely impact organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation through an information system via unauthorized access, destruction, disclosure, modification of information, and/or denial of service.

entries.title: negligible
entries.summaryMd: Extremely small. Typically quantifies the probability of an undesirable event that might occur during the lifetime of a cryptosystem (including during attacks by computationally bounded adversaries).

senses.definitionMd: Extremely small. Typically quantifies the probability of an undesirable event that might occur during the lifetime of a cryptosystem (including during attacks by computationally bounded adversaries).

entries.title: neighboring datasets
entries.summaryMd: The definition of neighboring datasets is a parameter to the differential privacy framework. In many contexts, two databases are considered neighbors if they differ in the data of one individual.

senses.definitionMd: The definition of neighboring datasets is a parameter to the differential privacy framework. In many contexts, two databases are considered neighbors if they differ in the data of one individual.

entries.title: network
entries.summaryMd: Information system(s) implemented with a collection of interconnected components. Such components may include routers, hubs, cabling, telecommunications controllers, key distribution centers, and technical control devices.

senses.definitionMd: Information system(s) implemented with a collection of interconnected components. Such components may include routers, hubs, cabling, telecommunications controllers, key distribution centers, and technical control devices.

entries.title: network access
entries.summaryMd: Access to an organizational information system by a user (or a process acting on behalf of a user) communicating through a network (e.g., local area network, wide area network, Internet).

senses.definitionMd: Access to an organizational information system by a user (or a process acting on behalf of a user) communicating through a network (e.g., local area network, wide area network, Internet).

entries.title: Network Access Control (NAC)
entries.summaryMd: A feature provided by some firewalls that allows access based on a user’s credentials and the results of health checks performed on the telework client device.

entries.title: Network Address Translation (NAT)

entries.title: Network Administrator
entries.summaryMd: A person who manages a local area network (LAN) within an organization. Responsibilities include ensuring network security, installing new applications, distributing software upgrades, monitoring daily activity, enforcing licensing agreements, developing a storage management program, and providing for routine backups.

senses.definitionMd: A person who manages a local area network (LAN) within an organization. Responsibilities include ensuring network security, installing new applications, distributing software upgrades, monitoring daily activity, enforcing licensing agreements, developing a storage management program, and providing for routine backups.

entries.title: network-based intrusion detection and prevention system
entries.summaryMd: An intrusion detection and prevention system that monitors network traffic for particular network segments or devices and analyzes the network and application protocol activity to identify and stop suspicious activity.

senses.definitionMd: An intrusion detection and prevention system that monitors network traffic for particular network segments or devices and analyzes the network and application protocol activity to identify and stop suspicious activity.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "network-based intrusion detection and prevention system"

entries.title: network bootstrapping credentials
entries.summaryMd: Credentials that a device needs in order to establish communications with and be authenticated by the network onboarding component. Device bootstrapping credentials are typically installed on the device during manufacturing, and they must already be on the device before it initiates the network-layer onboarding process. The device bootstrapping credentials are authoritative credentials that are unique to the device and independent of context; they are sometimes referred to as the device birth certificate. The device bootstrapping credentials always include some sort of secret (e.g., a private or secret pre-shared key), which the device will use to authenticate itself to the network onboarding component and to establish a secure communications channel with the network onboarding component.

senses.definitionMd: Credentials that a device needs in order to establish communications with and be authenticated by the network onboarding component. Device bootstrapping credentials are typically installed on the device during manufacturing, and they must already be on the device before it initiates the network-layer onboarding process. The device bootstrapping credentials are authoritative credentials that are unique to the device and independent of context; they are sometimes referred to as the device birth certificate. The device bootstrapping credentials always include some sort of secret (e.g., a private or secret pre-shared key), which the device will use to authenticate itself to the network onboarding component and to establish a secure communications channel with the network onboarding component.

entries.title: network defense
entries.summaryMd: Programs and activities (including those governed by PPD-41), and the use of tools necessary to facilitate them, conducted on information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure by the owner or operator or with the consent of the owner or operator and, as appropriate, the user for the primary purpose of protecting (1) those information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure; or (2) data stored on, processed on, or transiting those information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure. Network Defense does not involve accessing or conducting activities on information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure without authorization from the owner or operator or exceeding access authorized by the owner or operator.

senses.definitionMd: Programs and activities (including those governed by PPD-41), and the use of tools necessary to facilitate them, conducted on information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure by the owner or operator or with the consent of the owner or operator and, as appropriate, the user for the primary purpose of protecting (1) those information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure; or (2) data stored on, processed on, or transiting those information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure. Network Defense does not involve accessing or conducting activities on information systems, networks, or physical or virtual infrastructure without authorization from the owner or operator or exceeding access authorized by the owner or operator.

entries.title: Network Discovery
entries.summaryMd: The process of discovering active and responding hosts on a network, identifying weaknesses, and learning how the network operates.

senses.definitionMd: The process of discovering active and responding hosts on a network, identifying weaknesses, and learning how the network operates.

entries.title: Network Extension
entries.summaryMd: A method of providing partial or complete network access to remote users.

senses.definitionMd: A method of providing partial or complete network access to remote users.

entries.title: network interconnection
entries.summaryMd: A physical or virtual communications link between two or more networks operated by different organizations or operated within the same organization but within different authorization boundaries.

senses.definitionMd: A physical or virtual communications link between two or more networks operated by different organizations or operated within the same organization but within different authorization boundaries.

entries.title: Network Interface
entries.summaryMd: An interface that connects the IoT device to a network.

senses.definitionMd: An interface that connects the IoT device to a network.

entries.title: Network Interface Capability
entries.summaryMd: The ability to interface with a communication network for the purpose of communicating data to or from an IoT device. A network interface capability allows a device to be connected to and use a communication network. Every IoT device has at least one network interface capability and may have more than one.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to interface with a communication network for the purpose of communicating data to or from an IoT device. A network interface capability allows a device to be connected to and use a communication network. Every IoT device has at least one network interface capability and may have more than one.

entries.title: Network Intrusion Detection System
entries.summaryMd: Software that performs packet sniffing and network traffic analysis to identify suspicious activity and record relevant information.

senses.definitionMd: Software that performs packet sniffing and network traffic analysis to identify suspicious activity and record relevant information.

entries.title: Network Layer

senses.definitionMd: Layer of the TCP/IP protocol stack that is responsible for routing packets across networks.

entries.title: network-layer onboarding

senses.definitionMd: Consists of the actions required to provide an IoT device with the network credentials (and possibly other information) it needs to connect securely to a network.

entries.title: Network Layer Security
entries.summaryMd: Protecting network communications at the layer of the IP model that is responsible for routing packets across networks.

senses.definitionMd: Protecting network communications at the layer of the IP model that is responsible for routing packets across networks.

entries.title: network map
entries.summaryMd: A representation of the internal network topologies and components down to the host/device level to include but not limited to: connection, sub-network, enclave, and host information.

senses.definitionMd: A representation of the internal network topologies and components down to the host/device level to include but not limited to: connection, sub-network, enclave, and host information.

senses.definitionMd: A process that discovers, collects, and displays the physical and logical information required to produce a network map.

entries.title: network onboarding component
