senses.definitionMd: A logical component that is authorized to act on behalf of the network to onboard devices that are authorized to connect to the network. The network onboarding component interacts with devices by using a network onboarding protocol.

entries.title: network resilience
entries.summaryMd: A computing infrastructure that provides continuous business operation (i.e., highly resistant to disruption and able to operate in a degraded mode if damaged), rapid recovery if failure does occur, and the ability to scale to meet rapid or unpredictable demands.

senses.definitionMd: A computing infrastructure that provides continuous business operation (i.e., highly resistant to disruption and able to operate in a degraded mode if damaged), rapid recovery if failure does occur, and the ability to scale to meet rapid or unpredictable demands.

entries.title: Network Sniffing
entries.summaryMd: A passive technique that monitors network communication, decodes protocols, and examines headers and payloads for information of interest. It is both a review technique and a target identification and analysis technique.

senses.definitionMd: A passive technique that monitors network communication, decodes protocols, and examines headers and payloads for information of interest. It is both a review technique and a target identification and analysis technique.

entries.title: Network Traffic
entries.summaryMd: Computer network communications that are carried over wired or wireless networks between hosts.

senses.definitionMd: Computer network communications that are carried over wired or wireless networks between hosts.

entries.title: niche cross domain solution (CDS)

The 1800 series reports the results of NCCoE demonstration projects.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the nonce.

entries.title: noise
entries.summaryMd: A convenient term for a series of random disturbances borrowed through communication engineering, from the theory of sound. In communication theory, noise results in the possibility of a signal sent, x, being different from the signal received, y, and the latter has a probability distribution conditional upon x. If the disturbances consist of impulses at random intervals, it is sometimes known as “shot noise.”

senses.definitionMd: A convenient term for a series of random disturbances borrowed through communication engineering, from the theory of sound. In communication theory, noise results in the possibility of a signal sent, x, being different from the signal received, y, and the latter has a probability distribution conditional upon x. If the disturbances consist of impulses at random intervals, it is sometimes known as “shot noise.”

senses.definitionMd: A de-identification technique that modifies a dataset by adding random values to the values of a selected attribute.

senses.definitionMd: The component of an entropy source that contains the non-deterministic, entropy-producing activity (e.g., thermal noise or hard drive seek times).

entries.title: nominal frequency
entries.summaryMd: An ideal frequency with zero uncertainty. The nominal frequency is the frequency labeled on an oscillator’s output. For this reason, it is sometimes called the nameplate frequency. For example, an oscillator whose nameplate or label reads 5 MHz has a nominal frequency of 5 MHz. The difference between the nominal frequency and the actual output frequency of the oscillator is the frequency offset.

entries.summaryMd: An RBG that always has access to an entropy source and (when working properly) produces output bitstrings that have full entropy. Often called a True Random Number (or Bit) Generator. (Contrast with a deterministic random bit generator).

entries.title: non-discretionary access control
entries.summaryMd: An access control policy that is uniformly enforced across all subjects and objects within the boundary of an information system. A subject that has been granted access to information is constrained from doing any of the following: (i) passing the information to unauthorized subjects or objects; (ii) granting its privileges to other subjects; (iii) changing one or more security attributes on subjects, objects, the information system, or system components; (iv) choosing the security attributes to be associated with newly-created or modified objects; or (v) changing the rules governing access control. Organization-defined subjects may explicitly be granted organization-defined privileges (i.e., they are trusted subjects) such that they are not limited by some or all of the above constraints.

senses.definitionMd: An access control policy that is uniformly enforced across all subjects and objects within the boundary of an information system. A subject that has been granted access to information is constrained from doing any of the following: (i) passing the information to unauthorized subjects or objects; (ii) granting its privileges to other subjects; (iii) changing one or more security attributes on subjects, objects, the information system, or system components; (iv) choosing the security attributes to be associated with newly-created or modified objects; or (v) changing the rules governing access control. Organization-defined subjects may explicitly be granted organization-defined privileges (i.e., they are trusted subjects) such that they are not limited by some or all of the above constraints.

entries.title: non-fungible token

entries.title: non-ignorable bias

senses.definitionMd: In the context of de-identification, a bias that results from the suppression or redaction of data based on the value of the suppressed data.

entries.title: non-organizational user

entries.title: Non-Owner

In the case of containment queries, the algorithm may disregard unmatched features in the larger of the objects’ two-feature sets.

entries.summaryMd: The reassignment to some subject of a storage medium (e.g., page frame, disk sector, magnetic tape) that contained one or more objects. To be securely reassigned, no residual data can be available to the new subject through standard system mechanisms. Note: Also known as “residual information protection.”

senses.definitionMd: The reassignment to some subject of a storage medium (e.g., page frame, disk sector, magnetic tape) that contained one or more objects. To be securely reassigned, no residual data can be available to the new subject through standard system mechanisms. Note: Also known as “residual information protection.”

entries.title: Obligation
entries.summaryMd: An operation specified in a policy or policy set that should be performed by the PEP in conjunction with the enforcement of an authorization decision.

senses.definitionMd: An operation specified in a policy or policy set that should be performed by the PEP in conjunction with the enforcement of an authorization decision.

entries.title: obscured data
entries.summaryMd: data that has been distorted by cryptographic or other means to hide information. It is also referred to as being masked or obfuscated.

senses.definitionMd: data that has been distorted by cryptographic or other means to hide information. It is also referred to as being masked or obfuscated.

entries.title: Observable
entries.summaryMd: An event (benign or malicious) on a network or system.

senses.definitionMd: An event (benign or malicious) on a network or system.

entries.title: observational data
entries.summaryMd: Data captured through the observation of an activity or behavior without the direct involvement of the subject.

senses.definitionMd: Data captured through the observation of an activity or behavior without the direct involvement of the subject.

entries.title: octet
entries.summaryMd: A string of eight bits.

senses.definitionMd: A string of eight bits.

entries.title: Octet Length
entries.summaryMd: The number of octets in an octet string.

senses.definitionMd: The number of octets in an octet string.

entries.title: Octet String
entries.summaryMd: An ordered sequence of octets.

senses.definitionMd: An ordered sequence of octets.

entries.title: Off-Card
entries.summaryMd: Refers to data that is not stored within the PIV Card or to a computation that is not performed by the Integrated Circuit Chip (ICC) of the PIV Card.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to data that is not stored within the PIV Card or to a computation that is not performed by the Integrated Circuit Chip (ICC) of the PIV Card.

entries.title: Off-Chain
entries.summaryMd: Refers to data that is stored or a process that is implemented and executed outside of any blockchain system.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to data that is stored or a process that is implemented and executed outside of any blockchain system.

entries.title: off-line cryptosystem
entries.summaryMd: Cryptographic system in which encryption and decryption are performed independently of the transmission and reception functions.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptographic system in which encryption and decryption are performed independently of the transmission and reception functions.

entries.title: offensive cyberspace operations (OCO)
entries.summaryMd: Missions intended to project power in and through cyberspace.

senses.definitionMd: Missions intended to project power in and through cyberspace.

entries.title: Official CPE Dictionary
entries.summaryMd: The authoritative repository of identifier names, which is hosted by NIST.

senses.definitionMd: The authoritative repository of identifier names, which is hosted by NIST.

entries.title: Official Identifier CPE Name
entries.summaryMd: Any bound representation of a CPE WFN that uniquely identifies a single product class and is contained within the Official CPE Dictionary.

senses.definitionMd: Any bound representation of a CPE WFN that uniquely identifies a single product class and is contained within the Official CPE Dictionary.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Official Identifier CPE Name"

entries.title: official information
entries.summaryMd: All information of any kind, however stored, that is in the custody and control of the Department/Agency (D/A), relates to information in the custody and control of the D/A, or was acquired by D/A employees, or former employees, as part of their official duties or because of their official status within the D/A while such individuals were employed by or served on behalf of the D/A.

senses.definitionMd: All information of any kind, however stored, that is in the custody and control of the Department/Agency (D/A), relates to information in the custody and control of the D/A, or was acquired by D/A employees, or former employees, as part of their official duties or because of their official status within the D/A while such individuals were employed by or served on behalf of the D/A.

entries.title: Offline Test
entries.summaryMd: Offline tests use previously captured images as inputs to core biometric implementations. Such tests are repeatable and can readily be scaled to very large populations and large numbers of competing products. They institute a level-playing field and produce robust estimates of the core biometric power of an algorithm. This style of testing is particularly suited to interoperability testing of a fingerprint template (see [ISOSWAP]).

senses.definitionMd: Offline tests use previously captured images as inputs to core biometric implementations. Such tests are repeatable and can readily be scaled to very large populations and large numbers of competing products. They institute a level-playing field and produce robust estimates of the core biometric power of an algorithm. This style of testing is particularly suited to interoperability testing of a fingerprint template (see [ISOSWAP]).

entries.title: Oj
entries.summaryMd: The jth output block.

senses.definitionMd: The jth output block.

entries.title: OLIR Catalog
entries.summaryMd: The Online Informative References (OLIR) Catalog, which provides information about the Informative References submitted to and accepted by NIST.

senses.definitionMd: The Online Informative References (OLIR) Catalog, which provides information about the Informative References submitted to and accepted by NIST.

entries.title: OLIR Developer
entries.summaryMd: The party that develops the entire entropy source or the noise source.

senses.definitionMd: The party that develops the entire entropy source or the noise source.

entries.title: OLIR Program
entries.summaryMd: NIST’s Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) Online Informative References Program.

senses.definitionMd: NIST’s Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) Online Informative References Program.

entries.title: OLIR Template
entries.summaryMd: A spreadsheet that contains the fields necessary for creating a well- formed Informative Reference for submission to the OLIR Program. It is available on the Cybersecurity Framework website and serves as the starting point for the Developer.

senses.definitionMd: A spreadsheet that contains the fields necessary for creating a well- formed Informative Reference for submission to the OLIR Program. It is available on the Cybersecurity Framework website and serves as the starting point for the Developer.

entries.title: On
entries.summaryMd: Block of data representing Output Block n

senses.definitionMd: Block of data representing Output Block n

entries.title: On-Access Scanning
entries.summaryMd: Configuring a security tool to perform real-time scans of each file for malware as the file is downloaded, opened, or executed.

senses.definitionMd: Configuring a security tool to perform real-time scans of each file for malware as the file is downloaded, opened, or executed.

entries.title: on behalf of (an agency)
entries.summaryMd: A situation that occurs when: (i) a non-executive branch entity uses or operates an information system or maintains or collects information for the purpose of processing, storing, or transmitting Federal information; and (ii) those activities are not incidental to providing a service or product to the government.

senses.definitionMd: A situation that occurs when: (i) a non-executive branch entity uses or operates an information system or maintains or collects information for the purpose of processing, storing, or transmitting Federal information; and (ii) those activities are not incidental to providing a service or product to the government.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "on behalf of (an agency)"

entries.title: On-Card
entries.summaryMd: Refers to data that is stored within the PIV Card or to a computation that is performed by the Integrated Circuit Chip (ICC) of the PIV Card.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to data that is stored within the PIV Card or to a computation that is performed by the Integrated Circuit Chip (ICC) of the PIV Card.

entries.title: On-Chain
entries.summaryMd: Refers to data that is stored or a process that is implemented and executed within a blockchain system.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to data that is stored or a process that is implemented and executed within a blockchain system.

entries.title: On-Demand Scanning
entries.summaryMd: Allowing users to launch security tool scans for malware on a computer as desired.

senses.definitionMd: Allowing users to launch security tool scans for malware on a computer as desired.

entries.title: On-demand self-service
entries.summaryMd: A consumer can unilaterally provision computing capabilities, such as server time and network storage, as needed automatically without requiring human interaction with each service provider.

senses.definitionMd: A consumer can unilaterally provision computing capabilities, such as server time and network storage, as needed automatically without requiring human interaction with each service provider.

entries.title: On-demand test
entries.summaryMd: A type of health test that is available to be run whenever a user or a relying component requests it.

senses.definitionMd: A type of health test that is available to be run whenever a user or a relying component requests it.

entries.title: Onboarding
entries.summaryMd: The process by which a device obtains the credentials (e.g., network SSID and password) that it needs in order to gain access to a wired or wireless network.

senses.definitionMd: The process by which a device obtains the credentials (e.g., network SSID and password) that it needs in order to gain access to a wired or wireless network.

entries.title: onboarding credentials
entries.summaryMd: The unique credentials that the IoT device requires to connect securely to the local network (e.g., network identifier, unique network password, X.509 certificate and associated private key, etc.). They may also include additional configuration information (e.g., URLs and public keys for reaching and authenticating controllers and servers) to enable the device to perform application-layer onboarding and thereby become operational at the application layer once it has securely connected to the network. In contrast to device bootstrapping credentials, which are independent of context, device onboarding credentials are locally significant.

senses.definitionMd: The unique credentials that the IoT device requires to connect securely to the local network (e.g., network identifier, unique network password, X.509 certificate and associated private key, etc.). They may also include additional configuration information (e.g., URLs and public keys for reaching and authenticating controllers and servers) to enable the device to perform application-layer onboarding and thereby become operational at the application layer once it has securely connected to the network. In contrast to device bootstrapping credentials, which are independent of context, device onboarding credentials are locally significant.

entries.title: onboarding solution
entries.summaryMd: A product/technology/service combination that an organization will deploy to onboard devices to its network. The solution usually requires the support of people and processes throughout its lifecycle in alignment with the organization's policies.

senses.definitionMd: A product/technology/service combination that an organization will deploy to onboard devices to its network. The solution usually requires the support of people and processes throughout its lifecycle in alignment with the organization's policies.

entries.title: one-part code
entries.summaryMd: Code in which plain text elements and their accompanying code groups are arranged in alphabetical, numerical, or other systematic order, so one listing serves for both encoding and decoding. One-part codes are normally small codes used to pass small volumes of low-sensitivity information.

senses.definitionMd: Code in which plain text elements and their accompanying code groups are arranged in alphabetical, numerical, or other systematic order, so one listing serves for both encoding and decoding. One-part codes are normally small codes used to pass small volumes of low-sensitivity information.

entries.title: one-source mapping
entries.summaryMd: A mapping between concepts within a single concept source.

senses.definitionMd: A mapping between concepts within a single concept source.

entries.title: one-time cryptosystem
entries.summaryMd: Cryptosystem employing key used only once.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptosystem employing key used only once.

entries.title: one-time pad (OTP)
entries.summaryMd: Manual one-time cryptosystem produced in pad form.

senses.definitionMd: Manual one-time cryptosystem produced in pad form.

entries.title: one-time tape (OTT)
entries.summaryMd: Punched paper tape used to provide key streams on a one-time basis in certain machine cryptosystems.

senses.definitionMd: Punched paper tape used to provide key streams on a one-time basis in certain machine cryptosystems.

entries.title: One-to-one
entries.summaryMd: Of or relating to biometric verification in which submitted feature data is compared with that of one, claimed, identity.

senses.definitionMd: Of or relating to biometric verification in which submitted feature data is compared with that of one, claimed, identity.

entries.title: one-way hash algorithm
entries.summaryMd: Hash algorithms which map arbitrarily long inputs into a fixed-size output such that it is very difficult (computationally infeasible) to find two different hash inputs that produce the same output. Such algorithms are an essential part of the process of producing fixed-size digital signatures that can both authenticate the signer and provide for data integrity checking (detection of input modification after signature).

senses.definitionMd: Hash algorithms which map arbitrarily long inputs into a fixed-size output such that it is very difficult (computationally infeasible) to find two different hash inputs that produce the same output. Such algorithms are an essential part of the process of producing fixed-size digital signatures that can both authenticate the signer and provide for data integrity checking (detection of input modification after signature).

entries.title: one-way transfer device
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism, usually implemented in hardware, which enforces a unidirectional data flow with varying degrees of assurance, typically referred to as a "data diode" although not exclusively implemented as such. A common example is a fiber optic isolator.

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism, usually implemented in hardware, which enforces a unidirectional data flow with varying degrees of assurance, typically referred to as a "data diode" although not exclusively implemented as such. A common example is a fiber optic isolator.

entries.title: ongoing assessment and authorization
entries.summaryMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions. Note: The terms “continuous” and “ongoing” in this context mean that security controls and organizational risks are assessed and analyzed at a frequency sufficient to support risk-based security decisions to adequately protect organization information. See organizational information security continuous monitoring and automated security monitoring.

senses.definitionMd: Maintaining ongoing awareness of information security, vulnerabilities, and threats to support organizational risk management decisions. Note: The terms “continuous” and “ongoing” in this context mean that security controls and organizational risks are assessed and analyzed at a frequency sufficient to support risk-based security decisions to adequately protect organization information. See organizational information security continuous monitoring and automated security monitoring.
