entries.title: Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP)
entries.summaryMd: An online protocol used to determine the status of a public key certificate.

senses.definitionMd: An online protocol used to determine the status of a public key certificate.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP)"

entries.title: Online Certificate Status Protocol responder
entries.summaryMd: A PKI entity that verifies the revocation status of certificates following the Online Certificate Status Protocol (specified in RFC 6960).

senses.definitionMd: A PKI entity that verifies the revocation status of certificates following the Online Certificate Status Protocol (specified in RFC 6960).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Online Certificate Status Protocol responder"

entries.title: online cryptosystem
entries.summaryMd: Cryptographic system in which encryption and decryption are performed in association with the transmitting and receiving functions.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptographic system in which encryption and decryption are performed in association with the transmitting and receiving functions.

entries.title: online service
entries.summaryMd: A service that is accessed remotely via a network, typically the internet.

senses.definitionMd: A service that is accessed remotely via a network, typically the internet.

entries.title: Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL)
entries.summaryMd: SCAP language for expressing security checks that cannot be evaluated without some human interaction or feedback.

senses.definitionMd: SCAP language for expressing security checks that cannot be evaluated without some human interaction or feedback.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL)"

entries.title: Open Pretty Good Privacy (OpenPGP)
entries.summaryMd: A protocol defined in IETF RFCs 2440 and 3156 for encrypting messages and creating certificates using public key cryptography. Most mail clients do not support OpenPGP by default; instead, third-party plug-ins can be used in conjunction with the mail clients. OpenPGP uses a “web of trust” model for key management, which relies on users for management and control, making it unsuitable for medium to large implementations.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol defined in IETF RFCs 2440 and 3156 for encrypting messages and creating certificates using public key cryptography. Most mail clients do not support OpenPGP by default; instead, third-party plug-ins can be used in conjunction with the mail clients. OpenPGP uses a “web of trust” model for key management, which relies on users for management and control, making it unsuitable for medium to large implementations.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Open Pretty Good Privacy (OpenPGP)"

entries.title: open storage
entries.summaryMd: Any storage of classified national security information outside of General Services Administration-approved storage containers. This includes classified information that is resident on information systems media and outside of an approved storage container, regardless of whether or not that media is in use (i.e., unattended operations). Open storage of classified cryptographic material and equipment must be done within an approved COMSEC facility, vault, or secure room when authorized personnel are not present.

senses.definitionMd: Any storage of classified national security information outside of General Services Administration-approved storage containers. This includes classified information that is resident on information systems media and outside of an approved storage container, regardless of whether or not that media is in use (i.e., unattended operations). Open storage of classified cryptographic material and equipment must be done within an approved COMSEC facility, vault, or secure room when authorized personnel are not present.

entries.title: Open System
entries.summaryMd: A system that allows entities from different enterprises to access information related to tags used in the system. Open systems use an inter-enterprise subsystem to share information between entities.

senses.definitionMd: A system that allows entities from different enterprises to access information related to tags used in the system. Open systems use an inter-enterprise subsystem to share information between entities.

entries.title: Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language (OVAL)
entries.summaryMd: A language for representing system configuration information, assessing machine state, and reporting assessment results.

senses.definitionMd: A language for representing system configuration information, assessing machine state, and reporting assessment results.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Open Vulnerability and Assessment Language (OVAL)"

entries.title: operating system
entries.summaryMd: The software “master control application” that runs the computer. It is the first program loaded when the computer is turned on, and its main component, the kernel, resides in memory at all times. The operating system sets the standards for all application programs (such as the Web server) that run in the computer. The applications communicate with the operating system for most user interface and file management operations.

senses.definitionMd: The software “master control application” that runs the computer. It is the first program loaded when the computer is turned on, and its main component, the kernel, resides in memory at all times. The operating system sets the standards for all application programs (such as the Web server) that run in the computer. The applications communicate with the operating system for most user interface and file management operations.

entries.title: Operating System (OS) Fingerprinting
entries.summaryMd: Analyzing characteristics of packets sent by a target, such as packet headers or listening ports, to identify the operating system in use on the target.

senses.definitionMd: Analyzing characteristics of packets sent by a target, such as packet headers or listening ports, to identify the operating system in use on the target.

entries.title: Operating system virtualization
entries.summaryMd: A virtual implementation of the operating system interface that can be used to run applications written for the same operating system.

senses.definitionMd: A virtual implementation of the operating system interface that can be used to run applications written for the same operating system.

entries.title: Operation
entries.summaryMd: the set of access modes or types permitted on objects of the system.

senses.definitionMd: the set of access modes or types permitted on objects of the system.

entries.title: operational concept
entries.summaryMd: See security concept of operations.

senses.definitionMd: See security concept of operations.

entries.title: Operational Controls
entries.summaryMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that primarily are implemented and executed by people (as opposed to systems).

senses.definitionMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that primarily are implemented and executed by people (as opposed to systems).

entries.title: operational environment
entries.summaryMd: The type of environment in which the checklist is intended to be applied. Types of operational environments are Standalone, Managed, and Custom (including Specialized Security-Limited Functionality, Legacy, and United States Government).

senses.definitionMd: The type of environment in which the checklist is intended to be applied. Types of operational environments are Standalone, Managed, and Custom (including Specialized Security-Limited Functionality, Legacy, and United States Government).

entries.title: operational key
entries.summaryMd: Key intended for use over-the-air for protection of operational information or for the production or secure electrical transmission of key streams.

senses.definitionMd: Key intended for use over-the-air for protection of operational information or for the production or secure electrical transmission of key streams.

entries.title: operational margin
entries.summaryMd: A spare amount or measure or degree allowed or given for contingencies or special situations. The allowances carried to account for uncertainties and risks.

senses.definitionMd: A spare amount or measure or degree allowed or given for contingencies or special situations. The allowances carried to account for uncertainties and risks.

entries.title: operational optimization
entries.summaryMd: Selection of those risks from the register that are most valuable based upon leadership preferences, mission objectives, stakeholder sentiment (e.g., those of customers, citizens, or shareholders), and other subjective criteria. Another optimization factor is operational and based on an iterative communications cycle of risk reporting and analytics.

senses.definitionMd: Selection of those risks from the register that are most valuable based upon leadership preferences, mission objectives, stakeholder sentiment (e.g., those of customers, citizens, or shareholders), and other subjective criteria. Another optimization factor is operational and based on an iterative communications cycle of risk reporting and analytics.

entries.title: Operational phase
entries.summaryMd: A phase in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key whereby the key is used for standard cryptographic purposes.

senses.definitionMd: A phase in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key whereby the key is used for standard cryptographic purposes.

entries.title: operational resilience
entries.summaryMd: The ability of systems to resist, absorb, and recover from or adapt to an adverse occurrence during operation that may cause harm, destruction, or loss of ability to perform mission-related functions.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of systems to resist, absorb, and recover from or adapt to an adverse occurrence during operation that may cause harm, destruction, or loss of ability to perform mission-related functions.

entries.title: Operational storage
entries.summaryMd: Storage within an FCKMS where the key can be accessed to perform cryptographic functions during normal operations.

senses.definitionMd: Storage within an FCKMS where the key can be accessed to perform cryptographic functions during normal operations.

entries.title: operational technology
entries.summaryMd: Programmable systems or devices that interact with the physical environment (or manage devices that interact with the physical environment). These systems/devices detect or cause a direct change through the monitoring and/or control of devices, processes, and events. Examples include industrial control systems, building management systems, fire control systems, and physical access control mechanisms.

senses.definitionMd: Programmable systems or devices that interact with the physical environment (or manage devices that interact with the physical environment). These systems/devices detect or cause a direct change through the monitoring and/or control of devices, processes, and events. Examples include industrial control systems, building management systems, fire control systems, and physical access control mechanisms.

entries.title: Operational Test
entries.summaryMd: Operational tests involve a deployed system and are usually conducted to measure in-the- field performance and user-system interaction effects. Such tests require the members of a human test population to transact with biometric sensors. False acceptance rates may not be measurable, depending on the controls instituted.

senses.definitionMd: Operational tests involve a deployed system and are usually conducted to measure in-the- field performance and user-system interaction effects. Such tests require the members of a human test population to transact with biometric sensors. False acceptance rates may not be measurable, depending on the controls instituted.

entries.title: operational waiver
entries.summaryMd: Authority for continued use of unmodified COMSEC end-items pending the completion of a mandatory modification.

senses.definitionMd: Authority for continued use of unmodified COMSEC end-items pending the completion of a mandatory modification.

entries.title: Operationalization
entries.summaryMd: Putting MUD implementations into operational service in a manner that is both practical and effective.

senses.definitionMd: Putting MUD implementations into operational service in a manner that is both practical and effective.

entries.title: operations code (OPCODE)
entries.summaryMd: Code composed largely of words and phrases suitable for general communications use.

senses.definitionMd: Code composed largely of words and phrases suitable for general communications use.

entries.title: operations security (OPSEC)
entries.summaryMd: Systematic and proven process by which potential adversaries can be denied information about capabilities and intentions by identifying, controlling, and protecting generally unclassified evidence of the planning and execution of sensitive activities. The process involves five steps: identification of critical information, analysis of threats, analysis of vulnerabilities, assessment of risks, and application of appropriate countermeasures.

senses.definitionMd: Systematic and proven process by which potential adversaries can be denied information about capabilities and intentions by identifying, controlling, and protecting generally unclassified evidence of the planning and execution of sensitive activities. The process involves five steps: identification of critical information, analysis of threats, analysis of vulnerabilities, assessment of risks, and application of appropriate countermeasures.

entries.title: operator
entries.summaryMd: Individual or organization that performs the operations of a system.

senses.definitionMd: Individual or organization that performs the operations of a system.

entries.title: Opportunity
entries.summaryMd: A condition that may result in a beneficial outcome.

senses.definitionMd: A condition that may result in a beneficial outcome.

entries.title: Option ROM
entries.summaryMd: Firmware that is called by the system BIOS. Option ROMs include BIOS firmware on add-on cards (e.g., video card, hard drive controller, network card) as well as modules which extend the capabilities of the system BIOS.

senses.definitionMd: Firmware that is called by the system BIOS. Option ROMs include BIOS firmware on add-on cards (e.g., video card, hard drive controller, network card) as well as modules which extend the capabilities of the system BIOS.

entries.title: optional modification
entries.summaryMd: NSA-approved modification not required for universal implementation by all holders of a COMSEC end-item. This class of modification requires all of the engineering/doctrinal control of mandatory modification but is usually not related to security, safety, TEMPEST, or reliability.

senses.definitionMd: NSA-approved modification not required for universal implementation by all holders of a COMSEC end-item. This class of modification requires all of the engineering/doctrinal control of mandatory modification but is usually not related to security, safety, TEMPEST, or reliability.

entries.title: Oracle
entries.summaryMd: A source of data from outside a blockchain that serves as input for a smart contract.

senses.definitionMd: A source of data from outside a blockchain that serves as input for a smart contract.

entries.title: Orchestration
entries.summaryMd: Defines the sequence and conditions in which one Web service invokes other Web services to realize some useful function. An orchestration is the pattern of interactions that a Web service agent must follow to achieve its goal.

senses.definitionMd: Defines the sequence and conditions in which one Web service invokes other Web services to realize some useful function. An orchestration is the pattern of interactions that a Web service agent must follow to achieve its goal.

entries.title: Orchestrator
entries.summaryMd: A tool that enables DevOps personas or automation working on their behalf to pull images from registries, deploy those images into containers, and manage the running containers. Orchestrators are also responsible for monitoring container resource consumption, job execution, and machine health across hosts.

senses.definitionMd: A tool that enables DevOps personas or automation working on their behalf to pull images from registries, deploy those images into containers, and manage the running containers. Orchestrators are also responsible for monitoring container resource consumption, job execution, and machine health across hosts.

entries.title: ordering privilege manager (OPM)
entries.summaryMd: The key management entity (KME) authorized to designate other KME as a short title assignment requester (STAR) or ordering privilege manager (OPM).

senses.definitionMd: The key management entity (KME) authorized to designate other KME as a short title assignment requester (STAR) or ordering privilege manager (OPM).

entries.title: ordinal scale
entries.summaryMd: From the Stevens Scale of Measurement, a scale that orders and ranks data without establishing a degree of variation between ranks.

senses.definitionMd: From the Stevens Scale of Measurement, a scale that orders and ranks data without establishing a degree of variation between ranks.

entries.title: organization
entries.summaryMd: A federal agency or, as appropriate, any of its operational elements.

senses.definitionMd: A federal agency or, as appropriate, any of its operational elements.

entries.title: organization-defined control parameter
entries.summaryMd: See organization-defined control parameter.

senses.definitionMd: See organization-defined control parameter.

entries.title: organization-defined parameter
entries.summaryMd: The variable part of a control or control enhancement that is instantiated by an organization during the tailoring process by either assigning an organization-defined value or selecting a value from a predefined list provided as part of the control or control enhancement.

senses.definitionMd: The variable part of a control or control enhancement that is instantiated by an organization during the tailoring process by either assigning an organization-defined value or selecting a value from a predefined list provided as part of the control or control enhancement.

entries.title: Organizational Information Security Continuous Monitoring
entries.summaryMd: Ongoing monitoring sufficient to ensure and assure effectiveness of security controls related to systems, networks, and cyberspace, by assessing security control implementation and organizational security status in accordance with organizational risk tolerance – and within a reporting structure designed to make real-time, data-driven risk management decisions.

senses.definitionMd: Ongoing monitoring sufficient to ensure and assure effectiveness of security controls related to systems, networks, and cyberspace, by assessing security control implementation and organizational security status in accordance with organizational risk tolerance – and within a reporting structure designed to make real-time, data-driven risk management decisions.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Organizational Information Security Continuous Monitoring"

entries.title: organizational registration authority (ORA)
entries.summaryMd: Entity within the public key infrastructure (PKI) that authenticates the identity and the organizational affiliation of the users.

senses.definitionMd: Entity within the public key infrastructure (PKI) that authenticates the identity and the organizational affiliation of the users.

entries.title: organizational user
entries.summaryMd: An organizational employee or an individual whom the organization deems to have equivalent status of an employee, including a contractor, guest researcher, or individual detailed from another organization. Policies and procedures for granting the equivalent status of employees to individuals may include need-to-know, relationship to the organization, and citizenship.

senses.definitionMd: An organizational employee or an individual whom the organization deems to have equivalent status of an employee, including a contractor, guest researcher, or individual detailed from another organization. Policies and procedures for granting the equivalent status of employees to individuals may include need-to-know, relationship to the organization, and citizenship.

entries.title: organizationally-tailored control baseline
entries.summaryMd: A control baseline tailored for a defined notional (type of) information system using overlays and/or system-specific control tailoring, and intended for use in selecting controls for multiple systems within one or more organizations.

senses.definitionMd: A control baseline tailored for a defined notional (type of) information system using overlays and/or system-specific control tailoring, and intended for use in selecting controls for multiple systems within one or more organizations.

entries.title: Originator
entries.summaryMd: An entity that initiates an information exchange or storage event.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that initiates an information exchange or storage event.

entries.title: Originator-usage period
entries.summaryMd: The period of time in the cryptoperiod of a key during which cryptographic protection may be applied to data using that key.

senses.definitionMd: The period of time in the cryptoperiod of a key during which cryptographic protection may be applied to data using that key.

entries.title: Orphan block
entries.summaryMd: Any block that is not in the main chain after a temporary ledger conflict.

senses.definitionMd: Any block that is not in the main chain after a temporary ledger conflict.

entries.title: oscillator
entries.summaryMd: An electronic device used to generate an oscillating signal. The oscillation is based on a periodic event that repeats at a constant rate. The device that controls this event is called a resonator. The resonator needs an energy source so it can sustain oscillation. Taken together, the energy source and resonator form an oscillator. Although many simple types of oscillators (both mechanical and electronic) exist, the two types of oscillators primarily used for time and frequency measurements are quartz oscillators and atomic oscillators.

senses.definitionMd: An electronic device used to generate an oscillating signal. The oscillation is based on a periodic event that repeats at a constant rate. The device that controls this event is called a resonator. The resonator needs an energy source so it can sustain oscillation. Taken together, the energy source and resonator form an oscillator. Although many simple types of oscillators (both mechanical and electronic) exist, the two types of oscillators primarily used for time and frequency measurements are quartz oscillators and atomic oscillators.

entries.title: other system
entries.summaryMd: A system that the system of interest interacts with in the operational environment. These systems may provide services to the system of interest (i.e., the system of interest is dependent on the other systems) or be the beneficiaries of services provided by the system of interest (i.e., other systems are dependent on the system of interest).

senses.definitionMd: A system that the system of interest interacts with in the operational environment. These systems may provide services to the system of interest (i.e., the system of interest is dependent on the other systems) or be the beneficiaries of services provided by the system of interest (i.e., other systems are dependent on the system of interest).

entries.title: OtherInput
entries.summaryMd: Other information for key derivation; a bit string.

senses.definitionMd: Other information for key derivation; a bit string.

entries.title: out-of-distribution
entries.summaryMd: Data that was collected at a different time and possibly under different conditions or in a different environment than the data collected to train the model.

senses.definitionMd: Data that was collected at a different time and possibly under different conditions or in a different environment than the data collected to train the model.

entries.title: Outage
entries.summaryMd: A period when a service or an application is not available or when equipment is not operational.

senses.definitionMd: A period when a service or an application is not available or when equipment is not operational.

entries.title: outcome
entries.summaryMd: Result of the performance (or non-performance) of a function or process(es).

senses.definitionMd: Result of the performance (or non-performance) of a function or process(es).

entries.title: outcome‐specific utility metrics
entries.summaryMd: A way of measuring the utility of data for answering a specific question or class of questions.

senses.definitionMd: A way of measuring the utility of data for answering a specific question or class of questions.

entries.title: outliers
entries.summaryMd: An observation that lies an abnormal distance from other values in a random sample from a population.

senses.definitionMd: An observation that lies an abnormal distance from other values in a random sample from a population.

entries.title: Output Block
entries.summaryMd: A data block that is an output of either the forward cipher function or the inverse cipher function of the block cipher algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: A data block that is an output of either the forward cipher function or the inverse cipher function of the block cipher algorithm.

entries.title: Output space
entries.summaryMd: The set of all possible distinct bitstrings that may be obtained as samples from a digitized noise source.

senses.definitionMd: The set of all possible distinct bitstrings that may be obtained as samples from a digitized noise source.

entries.title: outside(r) threat
entries.summaryMd: An unauthorized entity outside the security domain that has the potential to harm an information system through destruction, disclosure, modification of data, and/or denial of service.

senses.definitionMd: An unauthorized entity outside the security domain that has the potential to harm an information system through destruction, disclosure, modification of data, and/or denial of service.

entries.title: OVAL ID
entries.summaryMd: An identifier for a specific OVAL definition that conforms to the format for OVAL IDs.

senses.definitionMd: An identifier for a specific OVAL definition that conforms to the format for OVAL IDs.

entries.title: over-the-air key distribution (OTAD)
entries.summaryMd: Providing electronic key via over-the-air rekeying, over-the-air key transfer, or cooperative key generation.

senses.definitionMd: Providing electronic key via over-the-air rekeying, over-the-air key transfer, or cooperative key generation.

entries.title: over-the-air key transfer (OTAT)
entries.summaryMd: Electronically distributing key without changing traffic encryption key used on the secured communications path over which the transfer is accomplished.

senses.definitionMd: Electronically distributing key without changing traffic encryption key used on the secured communications path over which the transfer is accomplished.

entries.title: over-the-air rekeying (OTAR)
entries.summaryMd: Changing traffic encryption key or transmission security key in remote cryptographic equipment by sending new key directly to the remote cryptographic equipment over the communications path it secures.

senses.definitionMd: Changing traffic encryption key or transmission security key in remote cryptographic equipment by sending new key directly to the remote cryptographic equipment over the communications path it secures.

entries.title: overlay
entries.summaryMd: A specification of security or privacy controls, control enhancements, supplemental guidance, and other supporting information employed during the tailoring process, that is intended to complement (and further refine) security control baselines. The overlay specification may be more stringent or less stringent than the original security control baseline specification and can be applied to multiple information systems.

senses.definitionMd: A specification of security or privacy controls, control enhancements, supplemental guidance, and other supporting information employed during the tailoring process, that is intended to complement (and further refine) security control baselines. The overlay specification may be more stringent or less stringent than the original security control baseline specification and can be applied to multiple information systems.

entries.title: Overlay network
entries.summaryMd: A software-defined networking component included in most orchestrators that can be used to isolate communication between applications that share the same physical network.

senses.definitionMd: A software-defined networking component included in most orchestrators that can be used to isolate communication between applications that share the same physical network.

entries.title: overt channel
entries.summaryMd: Communications path within a computer system or network designed for the authorized transfer of data.

senses.definitionMd: Communications path within a computer system or network designed for the authorized transfer of data.

entries.title: Overt Testing
entries.summaryMd: Security testing performed with the knowledge and consent of the organization’s IT staff.

senses.definitionMd: Security testing performed with the knowledge and consent of the organization’s IT staff.

entries.title: overwrite
entries.summaryMd: Writing one or more patterns of data on top of the physical location of data stored on the media.

senses.definitionMd: Writing one or more patterns of data on top of the physical location of data stored on the media.

entries.title: overwrite procedure
entries.summaryMd: A software process that replaces data previously stored on storage media with a predetermined set of meaningless data or random patterns. Rationale: Definition is obvious based on definition of overwrite.

senses.definitionMd: A software process that replaces data previously stored on storage media with a predetermined set of meaningless data or random patterns. Rationale: Definition is obvious based on definition of overwrite.

entries.title: Owner
entries.summaryMd: A key pair owner is the entity authorized to use the private key of a key pair.

senses.definitionMd: A key pair owner is the entity authorized to use the private key of a key pair.

entries.title: p
entries.summaryMd: 3.14159… unless defined otherwise for a specific test.

senses.definitionMd: 3.14159… unless defined otherwise for a specific test.

entries.title: P#j
entries.summaryMd: The jth plaintext segment.

senses.definitionMd: The jth plaintext segment.

entries.title: P*n
entries.summaryMd: The last block of the plaintext, which may be a partial block.

senses.definitionMd: The last block of the plaintext, which may be a partial block.

entries.title: (p, q, d)
entries.summaryMd: RSA private key in the prime-factor format.

senses.definitionMd: RSA private key in the prime-factor format.

entries.title: p,q rule
entries.summaryMd: It is assumed that out of publicly available information the contribution of one individual to the cell total can be estimated to within q per cent (q=error before publication); after the publication of the statistic the value can be estimated to within p percent (p=error after publication). In the (p,q) rule the ratio p/q represents the information gain through publication. If the information gain is unacceptable, the cell is declared as confidential. The parameter values p and q are determined by the statistical authority and, thus, define the acceptable level of information gain. In some [National Statistical Organizations] the values of p and q are confidential.

senses.definitionMd: It is assumed that out of publicly available information the contribution of one individual to the cell total can be estimated to within q per cent (q=error before publication); after the publication of the statistic the value can be estimated to within p percent (p=error after publication). In the (p,q) rule the ratio p/q represents the information gain through publication. If the information gain is unacceptable, the cell is declared as confidential. The parameter values p and q are determined by the statistical authority and, thus, define the acceptable level of information gain. In some [National Statistical Organizations] the values of p and q are confidential.

entries.title: (p, t)-completeness
entries.summaryMd: For a given set of n variables, (p, t)-completeness is the proportion of the C(n, t) combinations that have configuration coverage of at least p.

senses.definitionMd: For a given set of n variables, (p, t)-completeness is the proportion of the C(n, t) combinations that have configuration coverage of at least p.

entries.title: P-value
entries.summaryMd: The probability (under the null hypothesis of randomness) that the chosen test statistic will assume values that are equal to or worse than the observed test statistic value when considering the null hypothesis. The P-valueis frequently called the “tail probability.”

senses.definitionMd: The probability (under the null hypothesis of randomness) that the chosen test statistic will assume values that are equal to or worse than the observed test statistic value when considering the null hypothesis. The P-valueis frequently called the “tail probability.”

entries.title: package management system
entries.summaryMd: An administrative tool or utility that facilitates the installation and maintenance of software on a given host, device or pool of centrally managed hosts, and the reporting of installed software attributes. May also be referred to as package manager, software manager, application manager, or app manager.

senses.definitionMd: An administrative tool or utility that facilitates the installation and maintenance of software on a given host, device or pool of centrally managed hosts, and the reporting of installed software attributes. May also be referred to as package manager, software manager, application manager, or app manager.

entries.title: package manifest
entries.summaryMd: A listing of the contents of a software package.

senses.definitionMd: A listing of the contents of a software package.

entries.title: Packet
entries.summaryMd: The logical unit of network communications produced by the transport layer.

senses.definitionMd: The logical unit of network communications produced by the transport layer.

entries.title: Packet Filter
entries.summaryMd: A routing device that provides access control functionality for host addresses and communication sessions.

senses.definitionMd: A routing device that provides access control functionality for host addresses and communication sessions.

entries.title: packet sniffer
entries.summaryMd: Software that observes and records network traffic.

senses.definitionMd: Software that observes and records network traffic.

entries.title: packet sniffer and passive wiretapping
entries.summaryMd: See packet sniffer and passive wiretapping.

senses.definitionMd: See packet sniffer and passive wiretapping.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "packet sniffer and passive wiretapping"

entries.title: padding
entries.summaryMd: A string consisting of a single “1” bit, followed by zero or more “0” bits.

senses.definitionMd: A string consisting of a single “1” bit, followed by zero or more “0” bits.

entries.title: page check
entries.summaryMd: The verification of the presence of each required page in a physical publication.

senses.definitionMd: The verification of the presence of each required page in a physical publication.

entries.title: pairing code
entries.summaryMd: An 8-digit code used to establish a relationship between the PIV Card and a device for the purpose of creating the virtual contact interface after secure messaging has been established.

senses.definitionMd: An 8-digit code used to establish a relationship between the PIV Card and a device for the purpose of creating the virtual contact interface after secure messaging has been established.

entries.title: Pairwise Pseudonymous Identifier
entries.summaryMd: A pseudonymous identifier generated by an IdP for use at a specific RP.

senses.definitionMd: A pseudonymous identifier generated by an IdP for use at a specific RP.

entries.title: Pairwise Trust
entries.summaryMd: Establishment of trust by two entities that have direct business agreements with each other.

senses.definitionMd: Establishment of trust by two entities that have direct business agreements with each other.

entries.title: parameter
entries.summaryMd: A value that is used to control the operation of a function or that is used by a function to compute one or more outputs.

senses.definitionMd: A value that is used to control the operation of a function or that is used by a function to compute one or more outputs.

entries.title: Paravirtualization
entries.summaryMd: A method for a hypervisor to offer interfaces to a guest OS that the guest OS can use instead of the normal hardware interfaces.

senses.definitionMd: A method for a hypervisor to offer interfaces to a guest OS that the guest OS can use instead of the normal hardware interfaces.

entries.title: parent assessment element
entries.summaryMd: The assessment element in a prior process step from which the current element was derived.

senses.definitionMd: The assessment element in a prior process step from which the current element was derived.

entries.title: parity
entries.summaryMd: Bit(s) used to determine whether a block of data has been altered. Rationale: Term has been replaced by the term “parity bit”.

senses.definitionMd: Bit(s) used to determine whether a block of data has been altered. Rationale: Term has been replaced by the term “parity bit”.

entries.title: parity bit
entries.summaryMd: A checksum that is computed on a block of bits by computing the binary sum of the individual bits in the block and then discarding all but the low-order bit of the sum. See checksum.

senses.definitionMd: A checksum that is computed on a block of bits by computing the binary sum of the individual bits in the block and then discarding all but the low-order bit of the sum. See checksum.

entries.title: Participant Guide
entries.summaryMd: An exercise document that typically contains the exercise’s purpose, scope, objectives, and scenario, and a copy of the IT plan being exercised

senses.definitionMd: An exercise document that typically contains the exercise’s purpose, scope, objectives, and scenario, and a copy of the IT plan being exercised

entries.title: Partition
entries.summaryMd: A logical portion of a media that functions as though it were physically separate from other logical portions of the media.

senses.definitionMd: A logical portion of a media that functions as though it were physically separate from other logical portions of the media.

entries.title: Partitioning
entries.summaryMd: Managing guest operating system access to hardware so that each guest OS can access its own resources but cannot encroach on the other guest OSs’ resources or any resources not allocated for virtualization use.

senses.definitionMd: Managing guest operating system access to hardware so that each guest OS can access its own resources but cannot encroach on the other guest OSs’ resources or any resources not allocated for virtualization use.

entries.title: party
entries.summaryMd: An individual (person), organization, device or process. Used interchangeably with “party.”

senses.definitionMd: An individual (person), organization, device or process. Used interchangeably with “party.”

entries.title: passive attack
entries.summaryMd: An attack that does not alter systems or data.

senses.definitionMd: An attack that does not alter systems or data.

entries.title: Passive Security Testing
entries.summaryMd: Security testing that does not involve any direct interaction with the targets, such as sending packets to a target.

senses.definitionMd: Security testing that does not involve any direct interaction with the targets, such as sending packets to a target.

entries.title: Passive Tag
entries.summaryMd: A tag that does not have its own power supply. Instead, it uses RF energy from the reader for power. Due to the lower power, passive tags have shorter ranges than other tags, but are generally smaller, lighter, and cheaper than other tags.

senses.definitionMd: A tag that does not have its own power supply. Instead, it uses RF energy from the reader for power. Due to the lower power, passive tags have shorter ranges than other tags, but are generally smaller, lighter, and cheaper than other tags.

entries.title: passive wiretapping
entries.summaryMd: The monitoring or recording of data that attempts only to observe a communication flow and gain knowledge of the data it contains, but does not alter or otherwise affect that flow.

senses.definitionMd: The monitoring or recording of data that attempts only to observe a communication flow and gain knowledge of the data it contains, but does not alter or otherwise affect that flow.

entries.title: Passphrase
entries.summaryMd: A passphrase is a memorized secret consisting of a sequence of words or other text that a claimant uses to authenticate their identity. A passphrase is similar to a password in usage, but is generally longer for added security.

senses.definitionMd: A passphrase is a memorized secret consisting of a sequence of words or other text that a claimant uses to authenticate their identity. A passphrase is similar to a password in usage, but is generally longer for added security.

entries.title: password
entries.summaryMd: A string of characters (letters, numbers, and other symbols) used to authenticate an identity or to verify access authorization.

senses.definitionMd: A string of characters (letters, numbers, and other symbols) used to authenticate an identity or to verify access authorization.

entries.title: Password Cracking
entries.summaryMd: The process of recovering secret passwords stored in a computer system or transmitted over a network.

senses.definitionMd: The process of recovering secret passwords stored in a computer system or transmitted over a network.

entries.title: Password Protected
entries.summaryMd: The ability to protect the contents of a file or device from being accessed until the correct password is entered.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to protect the contents of a file or device from being accessed until the correct password is entered.

entries.title: patch
entries.summaryMd: Software component that, when installed, directly modifies files or device settings related to a different software component without changing the version number or release details for the related software component.

senses.definitionMd: Software component that, when installed, directly modifies files or device settings related to a different software component without changing the version number or release details for the related software component.

entries.title: patch level
entries.summaryMd: Denotes either a patch level or a patch set. More specifically, when patches must be applied in order, the patch level is the identifier of the most recently applied patch.

senses.definitionMd: Denotes either a patch level or a patch set. More specifically, when patches must be applied in order, the patch level is the identifier of the most recently applied patch.

entries.title: patch management
entries.summaryMd: The systematic notification, identification, deployment, installation, and verification of operating system and application software code revisions. These revisions are known as patches, hot fixes, and service packs.

senses.definitionMd: The systematic notification, identification, deployment, installation, and verification of operating system and application software code revisions. These revisions are known as patches, hot fixes, and service packs.

entries.title: patch set
entries.summaryMd: When patches do not need to be applied in any particular order, the patch set includes all (and only) the applied patches.

senses.definitionMd: When patches do not need to be applied in any particular order, the patch set includes all (and only) the applied patches.

entries.title: patching
entries.summaryMd: The act of applying a change to installed software – such as firmware, operating systems, or applications – that corrects security or functionality problems or adds new capabilities.

senses.definitionMd: The act of applying a change to installed software – such as firmware, operating systems, or applications – that corrects security or functionality problems or adds new capabilities.

entries.title: Path Validation
entries.summaryMd: The process of verifying the binding between the subject identifier and subject public key in a certificate, based on the public key of a trust anchor, through the validation of a chain of certificates that begins with a certificate issued by the trust anchor and ends with the target certificate. Successful path validation provides strong evidence that the information in the target certificate is trustworthy.

senses.definitionMd: The process of verifying the binding between the subject identifier and subject public key in a certificate, based on the public key of a trust anchor, through the validation of a chain of certificates that begins with a certificate issued by the trust anchor and ends with the target certificate. Successful path validation provides strong evidence that the information in the target certificate is trustworthy.

entries.title: payload
entries.summaryMd: Consists of the information passed down from the previous layer.

senses.definitionMd: Consists of the information passed down from the previous layer.

entries.title: payload control center
entries.summaryMd: A facility that provides C2 for satellite payloads.

senses.definitionMd: A facility that provides C2 for satellite payloads.

entries.title: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
entries.summaryMd: An information security standard administered by the Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council that is for organizations that handle branded credit cards from the major card schemes.

senses.definitionMd: An information security standard administered by the Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council that is for organizations that handle branded credit cards from the major card schemes.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard"

entries.title: PCI DSS
aliases: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
Payment Card Industry Digital Security Standard
entries.summaryMd: An information security standard administered by the Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council that is for organizations that handle branded credit cards from the major card schemes.

senses.definitionMd: An information security standard administered by the Payment Card Industry Security Standards Council that is for organizations that handle branded credit cards from the major card schemes.

entries.title: pebibyte
entries.summaryMd: 250 bytes.

senses.definitionMd: 250 bytes.

entries.title: pedigree
entries.summaryMd: The validation of the composition and provenance of technologies, products, and services is referred to as the pedigree. For microelectronics, this includes material composition of components. For software this includes the composition of open source and proprietary code, including the version of the component at a given point in time. Pedigrees increase the assurance that the claims suppliers assert about the internal composition and provenance of the products, services, and technologies they provide are valid.

senses.definitionMd: The validation of the composition and provenance of technologies, products, and services is referred to as the pedigree. For microelectronics, this includes material composition of components. For software this includes the composition of open source and proprietary code, including the version of the component at a given point in time. Pedigrees increase the assurance that the claims suppliers assert about the internal composition and provenance of the products, services, and technologies they provide are valid.

entries.title: peer entity authentication
entries.summaryMd: The corroboration that a peer entity in an association is the one claimed.

senses.definitionMd: The corroboration that a peer entity in an association is the one claimed.

entries.title: peer entity authentication service
entries.summaryMd: A security service that verifies an identity claimed by or for a system entity in an association.

senses.definitionMd: A security service that verifies an identity claimed by or for a system entity in an association.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "peer entity authentication service"

entries.title: Peers
entries.summaryMd: Entities at the same tier in a CKMS hierarchy (e.g., all peers are client nodes).

senses.definitionMd: Entities at the same tier in a CKMS hierarchy (e.g., all peers are client nodes).

entries.title: Pending transaction pool
entries.summaryMd: A distributed queue where candidate transactions wait until they are added to the blockchain. Also known as memory pool, or mempool.

senses.definitionMd: A distributed queue where candidate transactions wait until they are added to the blockchain. Also known as memory pool, or mempool.

entries.title: penetration
entries.summaryMd: A security event, or a combination of multiple security events, that constitutes a security incident in which an intruder gains, or attempts to gain, access to a system or system resource without having authorization to do so.

senses.definitionMd: A security event, or a combination of multiple security events, that constitutes a security incident in which an intruder gains, or attempts to gain, access to a system or system resource without having authorization to do so.

entries.title: penetration-resistant architecture
entries.summaryMd: An architecture that uses technology and procedures to limit the opportunities for an adversary to compromise an organizational system and achieve a persistent presence in the system.

senses.definitionMd: An architecture that uses technology and procedures to limit the opportunities for an adversary to compromise an organizational system and achieve a persistent presence in the system.

entries.title: penetration testing
entries.summaryMd: A method of testing where testers target individual binary components or the application as a whole to determine whether intra or intercomponent vulnerabilities can be exploited to compromise the application, its data, or its environment resources.

senses.definitionMd: A method of testing where testers target individual binary components or the application as a whole to determine whether intra or intercomponent vulnerabilities can be exploited to compromise the application, its data, or its environment resources.

entries.title: per-call key
entries.summaryMd: Unique traffic encryption key generated automatically by certain secure telecommunications systems to secure single voice or data transmissions.

senses.definitionMd: Unique traffic encryption key generated automatically by certain secure telecommunications systems to secure single voice or data transmissions.

entries.title: Per-message secret number
entries.summaryMd: A secret random number that is generated prior to the generation of each digital signature.

senses.definitionMd: A secret random number that is generated prior to the generation of each digital signature.

entries.title: Perceived Target Value
entries.summaryMd: measures the likelihood of attack using the misuse vulnerability in an environment relative to vulnerable systems in other environments.

senses.definitionMd: measures the likelihood of attack using the misuse vulnerability in an environment relative to vulnerable systems in other environments.

entries.title: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS)
entries.summaryMd: An option that causes a new secret key to be created and shared through a new Diffie-Hellman key exchange for each IPsec SA. This provides protection against the use of compromised old keys that could be used to attack the newer derived keys still in use for integrity and confidentiality protection.

senses.definitionMd: An option that causes a new secret key to be created and shared through a new Diffie-Hellman key exchange for each IPsec SA. This provides protection against the use of compromised old keys that could be used to attack the newer derived keys still in use for integrity and confidentiality protection.

entries.title: performance reference model (PRM)
entries.summaryMd: Framework for performance measurement providing common output measurements throughout the Federal Government. It allows agencies to better manage the business of government at a strategic level by providing a means for using an agency's enterprise architecture (EA) to measure the success of information systems investments and their impact on strategic outcomes.

senses.definitionMd: Framework for performance measurement providing common output measurements throughout the Federal Government. It allows agencies to better manage the business of government at a strategic level by providing a means for using an agency's enterprise architecture (EA) to measure the success of information systems investments and their impact on strategic outcomes.

entries.title: perimeter
entries.summaryMd: 1. Encompasses all those components of the system that are to be accredited by the DAA, and excludes separately accredited systems to which the system is connected.

senses.definitionMd: 1. Encompasses all those components of the system that are to be accredited by the DAA, and excludes separately accredited systems to which the system is connected.

entries.title: Period of protection
entries.summaryMd: The period of time during which the integrity or confidentiality of a key needs to be maintained.

senses.definitionMd: The period of time during which the integrity or confidentiality of a key needs to be maintained.

entries.title: Periodic Template Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to reject sequences that show deviations from the expected number of runs of ones of a given length.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to reject sequences that show deviations from the expected number of runs of ones of a given length.

entries.title: periods processing
entries.summaryMd: A mode of system operation in which information of different sensitivities is processed at distinctly different times by the same system, with the system being properly purged or sanitized between periods.

senses.definitionMd: A mode of system operation in which information of different sensitivities is processed at distinctly different times by the same system, with the system being properly purged or sanitized between periods.

entries.title: perishable data
entries.summaryMd: Information whose value can decrease substantially during a specified time. A significant decrease in value occurs when the operational circumstances change to the extent that the information is no longer useful.

senses.definitionMd: Information whose value can decrease substantially during a specified time. A significant decrease in value occurs when the operational circumstances change to the extent that the information is no longer useful.

entries.title: Permalock
entries.summaryMd: A security feature that makes the lock status of an area of memory permanent. If the area of memory is locked and permalocked, then that area is permanently locked. If the area of memory is unlocked and permalocked, then that area is permanently unlocked.

senses.definitionMd: A security feature that makes the lock status of an area of memory permanent. If the area of memory is locked and permalocked, then that area is permanently locked. If the area of memory is unlocked and permalocked, then that area is permanently unlocked.

entries.title: permanent connection
entries.summaryMd: A perpetual communication channel. Permanent connections are most often made via a dedicated circuit.

senses.definitionMd: A perpetual communication channel. Permanent connections are most often made via a dedicated circuit.

entries.title: Permission
entries.summaryMd: Authorization to perform some action on a system.

senses.definitionMd: Authorization to perform some action on a system.

entries.title: Permissioned
entries.summaryMd: A system where every node, and every user must be granted permissions to utilize the system (generally assigned by an administrator or consortium).

senses.definitionMd: A system where every node, and every user must be granted permissions to utilize the system (generally assigned by an administrator or consortium).

entries.title: Permissionless
entries.summaryMd: A system where all users’ permissions are equal and not set by any administrator or consortium.

senses.definitionMd: A system where all users’ permissions are equal and not set by any administrator or consortium.

entries.title: Permissions
entries.summaryMd: Allowable user actions (e.g., read, write, execute).

entries.summaryMd: Poisson distributions model (some) discrete random variables. Typically, a Poisson random variable is a count of the number of rare events that occur in a certain time interval.

senses.definitionMd: Poisson distributions model (some) discrete random variables. Typically, a Poisson random variable is a count of the number of rare events that occur in a certain time interval.

entries.title: Policy
entries.summaryMd: Statements, rules or assertions that specify the correct or expected behavior of an entity. For example, an authorization policy might specify the correct access control rules for a software component.

senses.definitionMd: Statements, rules or assertions that specify the correct or expected behavior of an entity. For example, an authorization policy might specify the correct access control rules for a software component.

entries.title: policy administration point
entries.summaryMd: Provides a user interface for creating, managing, testing, and debugging digital policies and metapolicies, and storing these policies in the appropriate repository.

senses.definitionMd: Provides a user interface for creating, managing, testing, and debugging digital policies and metapolicies, and storing these policies in the appropriate repository.

entries.title: policy based access control (PBAC)
entries.summaryMd: A strategy for managing user access to one or more systems, where the business roles of users is combined with policies to determine what access privileges users of each role should have. Theoretical privileges are compared to actual privileges, and differences are automatically applied. For example, a role may be defined for a manager. Specific types of accounts on the single sign-on server, Web server, and database management system may be attached to this role. Appropriate users are then attached to this role.

senses.definitionMd: A strategy for managing user access to one or more systems, where the business roles of users is combined with policies to determine what access privileges users of each role should have. Theoretical privileges are compared to actual privileges, and differences are automatically applied. For example, a role may be defined for a manager. Specific types of accounts on the single sign-on server, Web server, and database management system may be attached to this role. Appropriate users are then attached to this role.

entries.title: policy decision point
entries.summaryMd: A system entity that makes authorization decisions for itself or for other system entities that request such decisions.

senses.definitionMd: A system entity that makes authorization decisions for itself or for other system entities that request such decisions.

entries.title: policy enforcement point
entries.summaryMd: A system entity that requests and subsequently enforces authorization decisions.

senses.definitionMd: A system entity that requests and subsequently enforces authorization decisions.

entries.title: policy information point
entries.summaryMd: Serves as the retrieval source of attributes, or the data required for policy evaluation to provide the information needed by the policy decision point to make the decisions.

senses.definitionMd: Serves as the retrieval source of attributes, or the data required for policy evaluation to provide the information needed by the policy decision point to make the decisions.

entries.title: port
entries.summaryMd: The entry or exit point from a computer for connecting communications or peripheral devices.

senses.definitionMd: The entry or exit point from a computer for connecting communications or peripheral devices.

entries.title: port scan
entries.summaryMd: A technique that sends client requests to a range of service port addresses on a host.

senses.definitionMd: A technique that sends client requests to a range of service port addresses on a host.

entries.title: Port Scanner
entries.summaryMd: A program that can remotely determine which ports on a system are open (e.g., whether systems allow connections through those ports).

senses.definitionMd: A program that can remotely determine which ports on a system are open (e.g., whether systems allow connections through those ports).

entries.title: port scanning
entries.summaryMd: Using a program to remotely determine which ports on a system are open (e.g., whether systems allow connections through those ports).

senses.definitionMd: Using a program to remotely determine which ports on a system are open (e.g., whether systems allow connections through those ports).

entries.title: portable electronic device (PED)
entries.summaryMd: Electronic devices having the capability to store, record, and/or transmit text, images/video, or audio data. Examples of such devices include, but are not limited to: pagers, laptops, cellular telephones, radios, compact disc (CD) and cassette players/recorders, portable digital assistant, audio devices, watches with input capability, and reminder recorders.

senses.definitionMd: Electronic devices having the capability to store, record, and/or transmit text, images/video, or audio data. Examples of such devices include, but are not limited to: pagers, laptops, cellular telephones, radios, compact disc (CD) and cassette players/recorders, portable digital assistant, audio devices, watches with input capability, and reminder recorders.

entries.title: portable storage device
entries.summaryMd: Portable device that can be connected to an information system (IS), computer, or network to provide data storage. These devices interface with the IS through processing chips and may load driver software, presenting a greater security risk to the IS than non-device media, such as optical discs or flash memory cards. Note: Examples include, but are not limited to: USB flash drives, external hard drives, and external solid state disk (SSD) drives. Portable Storage Devices also include memory cards that have additional functions aside from standard data storage and encrypted data storage, such as built-in Wi-Fi connectivity and global positioning system (GPS) reception. See also removable media.

senses.definitionMd: Portable device that can be connected to an information system (IS), computer, or network to provide data storage. These devices interface with the IS through processing chips and may load driver software, presenting a greater security risk to the IS than non-device media, such as optical discs or flash memory cards. Note: Examples include, but are not limited to: USB flash drives, external hard drives, and external solid state disk (SSD) drives. Portable Storage Devices also include memory cards that have additional functions aside from standard data storage and encrypted data storage, such as built-in Wi-Fi connectivity and global positioning system (GPS) reception. entries.title: Portal VPN
entries.summaryMd: A single standard SSL connection to a Web site (the portal) that allows a remote user to securely access multiple network services via a standard Web browser.

senses.definitionMd: A single standard SSL connection to a Web site (the portal) that allows a remote user to securely access multiple network services via a standard Web browser.

entries.title: positioning
entries.summaryMd: The ability to accurately and precisely determine one’s location and orientation two-dimensionally (or three-dimensionally, when required) referenced to a standard reference frame, such as the World Geodetic System 1984, WGS 84, or the International Terrestrial Reference Frame ITRF2020.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to accurately and precisely determine one’s location and orientation two-dimensionally (or three-dimensionally, when required) referenced to a standard reference frame, such as the World Geodetic System 1984, WGS 84, or the International Terrestrial Reference Frame ITRF2020.

entries.title: positive control material
entries.summaryMd: Generic term referring to any material, system, or information (e.g. a sealed authenticator system or permissive action link) that require positive control-type security monitoring.

senses.definitionMd: Generic term referring to any material, system, or information (e.g. a sealed authenticator system or permissive action link) that require positive control-type security monitoring.

entries.title: Post-Market Capability
entries.summaryMd: A cybersecurity or privacy capability an organization selects, acquires, and deploys itself; any capability that is not pre-market.

senses.definitionMd: A cybersecurity or privacy capability an organization selects, acquires, and deploys itself; any capability that is not pre-market.

entries.title: Post Office Protocol (POP)
entries.summaryMd: A mailbox access protocol defined by IETF RFC 1939. POP is one of the most commonly used mailbox access protocols.

senses.definitionMd: A mailbox access protocol defined by IETF RFC 1939. POP is one of the most commonly used mailbox access protocols.

entries.title: post‐processing invariance
entries.summaryMd: A property of differential privacy. It says that the output of a differentially private mechanism remains differentially private, even if further processing is performed on it.

senses.definitionMd: A property of differential privacy. It says that the output of a differentially private mechanism remains differentially private, even if further processing is performed on it.

entries.title: post-quantum algorithm
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic algorithm that is believed to be secure, even against adversaries who possess a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic algorithm that is believed to be secure, even against adversaries who possess a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer.

entries.title: potential impact
entries.summaryMd: The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability could be expected to have a limited adverse effect, a serious adverse effect, or a severe or catastrophic adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.

senses.definitionMd: The loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability could be expected to have a limited adverse effect, a serious adverse effect, or a severe or catastrophic adverse effect on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.

entries.title: potentially identifiable personal information
entries.summaryMd: A new category of information proposed by Robert Gellman for information that has been de-identified but can be potentially re-identified. Potentially identifiable personal information is any personal information without overt identifiers. Under Gellman’s proposal, parties that wish to exchange attempts PI2 could voluntarily subscribe to a regime that would provide for both criminal and civil penalties if the recipient of the data attempted to re-identify the data subjects.

senses.definitionMd: A new category of information proposed by Robert Gellman for information that has been de-identified but can be potentially re-identified. Potentially identifiable personal information is any personal information without overt identifiers. Under Gellman’s proposal, parties that wish to exchange attempts PI2 could voluntarily subscribe to a regime that would provide for both criminal and civil penalties if the recipient of the data attempted to re-identify the data subjects.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "potentially identifiable personal information"

entries.title: practitioner experience
entries.summaryMd: A source of ISCM assessment elements based on the experience of individuals (practitioners) with experience in designing, implementing, and operating ISCM capabilities, as well as security engineering experience.

senses.definitionMd: A source of ISCM assessment elements based on the experience of individuals (practitioners) with experience in designing, implementing, and operating ISCM capabilities, as well as security engineering experience.

entries.title: Pre-activation state
entries.summaryMd: A lifecycle state of a key in which the key has been created, but is not yet authorized for use.

senses.definitionMd: A lifecycle state of a key in which the key has been created, but is not yet authorized for use.

entries.title: Pre-Market Capability
entries.summaryMd: A cybersecurity or privacy capability built into an IoT device. Pre-market capabilities are integrated into IoT devices by the manufacturer or vendor before they are shipped to customer organizations.

senses.definitionMd: A cybersecurity or privacy capability built into an IoT device. Pre-market capabilities are integrated into IoT devices by the manufacturer or vendor before they are shipped to customer organizations.

entries.title: pre‐training
entries.summaryMd: In machine learning, a training step that trains a general‐purpose model (sometimes called a foundation model) on publicly‐available data. Pre‐training is often followed by fine‐tuning to equip the model with task‐specific information.

senses.definitionMd: In machine learning, a training step that trains a general‐purpose model (sometimes called a foundation model) on publicly‐available data. Pre‐training is often followed by fine‐tuning to equip the model with task‐specific information.

entries.title: precision
entries.summaryMd: Refers to how closely individual PNT measurements agree with each other.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to how closely individual PNT measurements agree with each other.

entries.title: precursor
entries.summaryMd: A sign that an attacker may be preparing to cause an incident. See indicator.

senses.definitionMd: A sign that an attacker may be preparing to cause an incident. See indicator.

entries.title: Predictability
entries.summaryMd: Enabling reliable assumptions by individuals, owners, and operators about data and their processing by a system, product, or service.

senses.definitionMd: Enabling reliable assumptions by individuals, owners, and operators about data and their processing by a system, product, or service.

entries.title: Predictor
entries.summaryMd: A function that predicts the next value in a sequence, based on previously observed values in the sequence.

senses.definitionMd: A function that predicts the next value in a sequence, based on previously observed values in the sequence.

entries.title: predisposing condition
entries.summaryMd: A condition that exists within an organization, a mission/business process, enterprise architecture, or information system including its environment of operation, which contributes to (i.e., increases or decreases) the likelihood that one or more threat events, once initiated, will result in undesirable consequences or adverse impact to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation.

senses.definitionMd: A condition that exists within an organization, a mission/business process, enterprise architecture, or information system including its environment of operation, which contributes to (i.e., increases or decreases) the likelihood that one or more threat events, once initiated, will result in undesirable consequences or adverse impact to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation.

entries.title: Preimage
entries.summaryMd: A message Ms that produces a given message digest when it is processed by a hash function.

senses.definitionMd: A message Ms that produces a given message digest when it is processed by a hash function.

entries.title: Preimage resistance
entries.summaryMd: An expected property of a cryptographic hash function such that, given a randomly chosen message digest, message_digest, it is computationally infeasible to find a preimage of the message_digest, See “Preimage”.

senses.definitionMd: An expected property of a cryptographic hash function such that, given a randomly chosen message digest, message_digest, it is computationally infeasible to find a preimage of the message_digest, See “Preimage”.

entries.title: Prepare for Events
entries.summaryMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that procedures and resources are in place to respond to both routine and unexpected events that can compromise security. The unexpected events include both actual attacks and contingencies (natural disasters) like fires, floods, earthquakes, etc.

senses.definitionMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that procedures and resources are in place to respond to both routine and unexpected events that can compromise security. The unexpected events include both actual attacks and contingencies (natural disasters) like fires, floods, earthquakes, etc.

entries.title: prerequisite
entries.summaryMd: A required input to an algorithm that has been established prior to the invocation of the algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: A required input to an algorithm that has been established prior to the invocation of the algorithm.

entries.title: Presentation Attack Detection (PAD)
entries.summaryMd: An automated determination of a presentation attack

senses.definitionMd: An automated determination of a presentation attack

entries.title: Presidential Directive
entries.summaryMd: A form of an executive order issued by the President of the United States with the advice and consent of the National Security Council; also known as a Presidential Decision Directive (or PDD).

senses.definitionMd: A form of an executive order issued by the President of the United States with the advice and consent of the National Security Council; also known as a Presidential Decision Directive (or PDD).

entries.title: pressure regulator
entries.summaryMd: A device used to control the pressure of a gas or liquid.

senses.definitionMd: A device used to control the pressure of a gas or liquid.

entries.title: pressure sensor
entries.summaryMd: A sensor system that produces an electrical signal related to the pressure acting on it by its surrounding medium. Pressure sensors can also use differential pressure to obtain level and flow measurements.

senses.definitionMd: A sensor system that produces an electrical signal related to the pressure acting on it by its surrounding medium. Pressure sensors can also use differential pressure to obtain level and flow measurements.

entries.title: PRF(s, x)
entries.summaryMd: A pseudorandom function with seed s and input data x.

senses.definitionMd: A pseudorandom function with seed s and input data x.

entries.title: Primary facility
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS facility that houses a primary system.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS facility that houses a primary system.

entries.title: primary services node (PRSN)
entries.summaryMd: A Key Management Infrastructure (KMI) core node that provides the users' central point of access to KMI products, services, and information.

senses.definitionMd: A Key Management Infrastructure (KMI) core node that provides the users' central point of access to KMI products, services, and information.

entries.title: Primary system
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS module that is currently active. Contrast with Backup (system).

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS module that is currently active. Contrast with Backup (system).

entries.title: Prime number
entries.summaryMd: An integer greater than 1 that has no positive integer factors other than 1 and itself.

senses.definitionMd: An integer greater than 1 that has no positive integer factors other than 1 and itself.

entries.title: Prime number generation seed
entries.summaryMd: A string of random bits that is used to begin a search for a prime number with the required characteristics.

senses.definitionMd: A string of random bits that is used to begin a search for a prime number with the required characteristics.
