entries.title: Primitive
entries.summaryMd: A low-level cryptographic algorithm that is used as a basic building block for higher-level cryptographic operations or schemes.

senses.definitionMd: A low-level cryptographic algorithm that is used as a basic building block for higher-level cryptographic operations or schemes.

entries.title: Primitive algorithm
entries.summaryMd: A low-level cryptographic algorithm (e.g., an RSA encryption operation) used as a basic building block for higher-level cryptographic algorithms or schemes (e.g., RSA key transport).

senses.definitionMd: A low-level cryptographic algorithm (e.g., an RSA encryption operation) used as a basic building block for higher-level cryptographic algorithms or schemes (e.g., RSA key transport).

entries.title: principal accrediting authority (PAA)
entries.summaryMd: Senior official with authority and responsibility for all intelligence systems within an agency.

senses.definitionMd: Senior official with authority and responsibility for all intelligence systems within an agency.

entries.title: principal authorizing official (PAO)
entries.summaryMd: A senior (federal) official or executive with the authority to oversee and establish guidance for the strategic implementation of CS and risk management within their mission areas (i.e., the warfighting mission area (WMA), business mission area (BMA), enterprise information environment mission area (EIEMA), and DoD portion of the intelligence mission area (DIMA) as defined in DoDI 8115.02).

senses.definitionMd: A senior (federal) official or executive with the authority to oversee and establish guidance for the strategic implementation of CS and risk management within their mission areas (i.e., the warfighting mission area (WMA), business mission area (BMA), enterprise information environment mission area (EIEMA), and DoD portion of the intelligence mission area (DIMA) as defined in DoDI 8115.02).

entries.title: printer
entries.summaryMd: A device that converts digital data to human-readable text on a paper medium.

senses.definitionMd: A device that converts digital data to human-readable text on a paper medium.

entries.title: privacy
entries.summaryMd: Assurance that the confidentiality of, and access to, certain information about an entity is protected.

senses.definitionMd: Assurance that the confidentiality of, and access to, certain information about an entity is protected.

entries.title: privacy architect
entries.summaryMd: Individual, group, or organization responsible for ensuring that the system privacy requirements necessary to protect individuals’ privacy are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture including reference models, segment and solution architectures, and information systems processing PII.

senses.definitionMd: Individual, group, or organization responsible for ensuring that the system privacy requirements necessary to protect individuals’ privacy are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture including reference models, segment and solution architectures, and information systems processing PII.

entries.title: privacy architecture
entries.summaryMd: An embedded, integral part of the enterprise architecture that describes the structure and behavior for an enterprise’s privacy protection processes, technical measures, personnel and organizational sub-units, showing their alignment with the enterprise’s mission and strategic plans.

senses.definitionMd: An embedded, integral part of the enterprise architecture that describes the structure and behavior for an enterprise’s privacy protection processes, technical measures, personnel and organizational sub-units, showing their alignment with the enterprise’s mission and strategic plans.

entries.title: Privacy Breach
entries.summaryMd: The loss of control, compromise, unauthorized disclosure, unauthorized acquisition, or any similar occurrence where (1) a person other than an authorized user accesses or potentially accesses data or (2) an authorized user accesses data for an other than authorized purpose.

senses.definitionMd: The loss of control, compromise, unauthorized disclosure, unauthorized acquisition, or any similar occurrence where (1) a person other than an authorized user accesses or potentially accesses data or (2) an authorized user accesses data for an other than authorized purpose.

entries.title: privacy budget
entries.summaryMd: An upper bound on allowable cumulative privacy loss across all analyses that process a single dataset.

senses.definitionMd: An upper bound on allowable cumulative privacy loss across all analyses that process a single dataset.

entries.title: Privacy Capability
entries.summaryMd: See capability.

senses.definitionMd: See capability.

entries.title: privacy compromise
entries.summaryMd: In the AML context, the unauthorized access of restricted or pro­prietary information that is part of an AI system, including information about a model’s training data, weights or architecture; or sensitive information that the model accesses such as the knowledge base of a GenAI retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) application.

senses.definitionMd: In the AML context, the unauthorized access of restricted or pro­prietary information that is part of an AI system, including information about a model’s training data, weights or architecture; or sensitive information that the model accesses such as the knowledge base of a GenAI retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) application.

entries.title: privacy continuous monitoring program
entries.summaryMd: An agency-wide program that implements the agency’s privacy continuous monitoring strategy and maintains ongoing awareness of threats and vulnerabilities that may pose privacy risks; monitors changes to information systems and environments of operation that create, collect, use, process, store, maintain, disseminate, disclose, or dispose of PII; and conducts privacy control assessments to verify the continued effectiveness of all privacy controls selected and implemented at an agency across the agency risk management tiers to ensure continued compliance with applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks.

senses.definitionMd: An agency-wide program that implements the agency’s privacy continuous monitoring strategy and maintains ongoing awareness of threats and vulnerabilities that may pose privacy risks; monitors changes to information systems and environments of operation that create, collect, use, process, store, maintain, disseminate, disclose, or dispose of PII; and conducts privacy control assessments to verify the continued effectiveness of all privacy controls selected and implemented at an agency across the agency risk management tiers to ensure continued compliance with applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks.

entries.title: privacy control
entries.summaryMd: The administrative, technical, and physical safeguards employed within an agency to ensure compliance with applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks. Note: Controls can be selected to achieve multiple objectives; those controls that are selected to achieve both security and privacy objectives require a degree of collaboration between the organization’s information security program and privacy program.

senses.definitionMd: The administrative, technical, and physical safeguards employed within an agency to ensure compliance with applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks. Note: Controls can be selected to achieve multiple objectives; those controls that are selected to achieve both security and privacy objectives require a degree of collaboration between the organization’s information security program and privacy program.

entries.title: privacy control assessment
entries.summaryMd: See Security Control Assessment.

senses.definitionMd: See Security Control Assessment.

entries.title: Privacy Control Assessor
entries.summaryMd: See Security Control Assessor.

senses.definitionMd: See Security Control Assessor.

entries.title: privacy control baseline
entries.summaryMd: A collection of controls specifically assembled or brought together by a group, organization, or community of interest to address the privacy protection needs of individuals.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of controls specifically assembled or brought together by a group, organization, or community of interest to address the privacy protection needs of individuals.

entries.title: privacy domain
entries.summaryMd: A domain that implements a privacy policy.

senses.definitionMd: A domain that implements a privacy policy.

entries.title: Privacy engineering
entries.summaryMd: A specialty discipline of systems engineering focused on achieving freedom from conditions that can create problems for individuals with unacceptable consequences that arise from the system as it processes PII.

senses.definitionMd: A specialty discipline of systems engineering focused on achieving freedom from conditions that can create problems for individuals with unacceptable consequences that arise from the system as it processes PII.

entries.title: Privacy Event
entries.summaryMd: The occurrence or potential occurrence of problematic data actions.

senses.definitionMd: The occurrence or potential occurrence of problematic data actions.

entries.title: privacy impact assessment (PIA)
entries.summaryMd: An analysis of how information is handled to ensure handling conforms to applicable legal, regulatory, and policy requirements regarding privacy; to determine the risks and effects of creating, collecting, using, processing, storing, maintaining, disseminating, disclosing, and disposing of information in identifiable form in an electronic information system; and to examine and evaluate protections and alternate processes for handling information to mitigate potential privacy concerns. A privacy impact assessment is both an analysis and a formal document detailing the process and the outcome of the analysis.

senses.definitionMd: An analysis of how information is handled to ensure handling conforms to applicable legal, regulatory, and policy requirements regarding privacy; to determine the risks and effects of creating, collecting, using, processing, storing, maintaining, disseminating, disclosing, and disposing of information in identifiable form in an electronic information system; and to examine and evaluate protections and alternate processes for handling information to mitigate potential privacy concerns. A privacy impact assessment is both an analysis and a formal document detailing the process and the outcome of the analysis.

entries.title: privacy information
entries.summaryMd: Information that describes the privacy posture of an information system or organization.

senses.definitionMd: Information that describes the privacy posture of an information system or organization.

entries.title: privacy loss
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the extent to which a data release may reveal information that is specific to an individual.

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the extent to which a data release may reveal information that is specific to an individual.

entries.title: privacy loss budget
entries.summaryMd: An upper bound on the cumulative total privacy loss for individuals.

senses.definitionMd: An upper bound on the cumulative total privacy loss for individuals.

entries.title: privacy parameter
entries.summaryMd: A parameter of a differential privacy definition that partly or wholly determines privacy loss.

senses.definitionMd: A parameter of a differential privacy definition that partly or wholly determines privacy loss.

entries.title: privacy plan
entries.summaryMd: A formal document that details the privacy controls selected for an information system or environment of operation that are in place or planned for meeting applicable privacy requirements and managing privacy risks, details how the controls have been implemented, and describes the methodologies and metrics that will be used to assess the controls.

senses.definitionMd: A formal document that details the privacy controls selected for an information system or environment of operation that are in place or planned for meeting applicable privacy requirements and managing privacy risks, details how the controls have been implemented, and describes the methodologies and metrics that will be used to assess the controls.

entries.title: privacy posture
entries.summaryMd: The privacy posture represents the status of the information systems and information resources (e.g., personnel, equipment, funds, and information technology) within an organization based on information assurance resources (e.g., people, hardware, software, policies, procedures) and the capabilities in place to comply with applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks and to react as the situation changes.

senses.definitionMd: The privacy posture represents the status of the information systems and information resources (e.g., personnel, equipment, funds, and information technology) within an organization based on information assurance resources (e.g., people, hardware, software, policies, procedures) and the capabilities in place to comply with applicable privacy requirements and manage privacy risks and to react as the situation changes.

entries.title: privacy preserving data mining
entries.summaryMd: an [extension] of traditional data mining techniques to work with … data modified to mask sensitive information

entries.title: privacy preserving data publishing

entries.title: privacy program plan

entries.title: privacy requirement
entries.summaryMd: A requirement that applies to an information system or an organization that is derived from applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, standards, regulations, procedures, and/or mission/business needs with respect to privacy. Note: The term privacy requirement can be used in a variety of contexts from high-level policy activites to low-level implementation activities in system development and engineering disciplines.

entries.title: Privacy Requirements
entries.summaryMd: Requirements of an organization, information program, or system that are derived from applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, standards, instructions, regulations, procedures, or organizational mission and business case needs with respect to privacy.

senses.definitionMd: Requirements of an organization, information program, or system that are derived from applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, standards, instructions, regulations, procedures, or organizational mission and business case needs with respect to privacy.

entries.title: Privacy Risk
entries.summaryMd: The likelihood that individuals will experience problems resulting from data processing, and the impact should they occur.

senses.definitionMd: The likelihood that individuals will experience problems resulting from data processing, and the impact should they occur.

entries.title: Privacy Risk Assessment
entries.summaryMd: A privacy risk management sub-process for identifying and evaluating specific privacy risks.

senses.definitionMd: A privacy risk management sub-process for identifying and evaluating specific privacy risks.

entries.title: Privacy Risk Assessment Methodology (PRAM)
entries.summaryMd: The PRAM is a tool that applies the risk model from NISTIR 8062 and helps organizations analyze, assess, and prioritize privacy risks to determine how to respond and select appropriate solutions. The PRAM can help drive collaboration and communication between various components of an organization, including privacy, cybersecurity, business, and IT personnel.

entries.title: Privacy Risk Management
entries.summaryMd: A cross-organizational set of processes for identifying, assessing, and responding to privacy risks.

senses.definitionMd: A cross-organizational set of processes for identifying, assessing, and responding to privacy risks.

entries.title: privacy‐utility tradeoff
entries.summaryMd: The fundamental tension between privacy and accuracy. Adding more noise increases privacy but reduces accuracy, and vice‐versa.

senses.definitionMd: The fundamental tension between privacy and accuracy. Adding more noise increases privacy but reduces accuracy, and vice‐versa.

entries.title: Private cloud
entries.summaryMd: The cloud infrastructure is provisioned for exclusive use by a single organization comprising multiple consumers (e.g., business units). It may be owned, managed, and operated by the organization, a third party, or some combination of them, and it may exist on or off premises.

senses.definitionMd: The cloud infrastructure is provisioned for exclusive use by a single organization comprising multiple consumers (e.g., business units). It may be owned, managed, and operated by the organization, a third party, or some combination of them, and it may exist on or off premises.

entries.title: private key
entries.summaryMd: The secret part of an asymmetric key pair that is typically used to digitally sign or decrypt data.

senses.definitionMd: The secret part of an asymmetric key pair that is typically used to digitally sign or decrypt data.

entries.title: Private key/private signature key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key that is used with an asymmetric (public key) cryptographic algorithm and is associated with a public key. The private key is uniquely associated with the owner and is not made public. This key is used to compute a digital signature that may be verified using the corresponding public key.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key that is used with an asymmetric (public key) cryptographic algorithm and is associated with a public key. The private key is uniquely associated with the owner and is not made public. This key is used to compute a digital signature that may be verified using the corresponding public key.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Private key/private signature key"

entries.title: privilege
entries.summaryMd: A right that, when granted to an entity, permits the entity access and/or authorization to an otherwise restricted object, state, or resource. Note: Privileges represent the authorized behavior of a subject. They are defined by an authority and embodied in policy or rules.

senses.definitionMd: A right that, when granted to an entity, permits the entity access and/or authorization to an otherwise restricted object, state, or resource. Note: Privileges represent the authorized behavior of a subject. They are defined by an authority and embodied in policy or rules.

entries.title: privilege certificate manager (PCM)
entries.summaryMd: The key management entity (KME) authorized to create the privilege certificate for another KME.

senses.definitionMd: The key management entity (KME) authorized to create the privilege certificate for another KME.

entries.title: privileged access account holder
entries.summaryMd: A user who is authorized (and therefore trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform (e.g., special access to software applications or web publishing), requires additional training, and must sign an acceptable use policy. A user with a privileged access account.

senses.definitionMd: A user who is authorized (and therefore trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform (e.g., special access to software applications or web publishing), requires additional training, and must sign an acceptable use policy. A user with a privileged access account.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "privileged access account holder"

entries.title: privileged account
entries.summaryMd: An information system account with approved authorizations of a privileged user.

senses.definitionMd: An information system account with approved authorizations of a privileged user.

entries.title: privileged command
entries.summaryMd: A human-initiated command executed on an information system involving the control, monitoring, or administration of the system including security functions and associated security-relevant information.

senses.definitionMd: A human-initiated command executed on an information system involving the control, monitoring, or administration of the system including security functions and associated security-relevant information.

entries.title: privileged network account
entries.summaryMd: A network account with elevated privileges that is typically allocated to system administrators, network administrators, DBAs, and others who are responsible for system/application control, monitoring, or administration functions.

senses.definitionMd: A network account with elevated privileges that is typically allocated to system administrators, network administrators, DBAs, and others who are responsible for system/application control, monitoring, or administration functions.

entries.title: privileged process
entries.summaryMd: A computer process that is authorized (and, therefore, trusted) to perform security- relevant functions that ordinary processes are not authorized to perform.

senses.definitionMd: A computer process that is authorized (and, therefore, trusted) to perform security- relevant functions that ordinary processes are not authorized to perform.

entries.title: privileged user
entries.summaryMd: A user that is authorized (and therefore, trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform.

senses.definitionMd: A user that is authorized (and therefore, trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform.

entries.title: PrivKeyU, PrivKeyV
entries.summaryMd: Private key of party U or V, respectively.

senses.definitionMd: Private key of party U or V, respectively.

entries.title: proactive cyber defense
entries.summaryMd: A continuous process to manage and harden devices and networks according to known best practices.

senses.definitionMd: A continuous process to manage and harden devices and networks according to known best practices.

entries.title: Probability Density Function (PDF)
entries.summaryMd: A function that provides the "local" probability distribution of a test statistic. From a finite sample size n, a probability density function will be approximated by a histogram.

senses.definitionMd: A function that provides the "local" probability distribution of a test statistic. From a finite sample size n, a probability density function will be approximated by a histogram.

entries.title: Probability Distribution
entries.summaryMd: The assignment of a probability to the possible outcomes (realizations) of a random variable.

senses.definitionMd: The assignment of a probability to the possible outcomes (realizations) of a random variable.

entries.title: Probability model
entries.summaryMd: A mathematical representation of a random phenomenon.

senses.definitionMd: A mathematical representation of a random phenomenon.

entries.title: probability of occurrence
entries.summaryMd: A weighted factor based on a subjective analysis of the probability that a given threat is capable of exploiting a given vulnerability or a set of vulnerabilities.

senses.definitionMd: A weighted factor based on a subjective analysis of the probability that a given threat is capable of exploiting a given vulnerability or a set of vulnerabilities.

entries.title: Probable prime
entries.summaryMd: An integer that is believed to be prime based on a probabilistic primality test. There should be no more than a negligible probability that the so-called probable prime is actually composite.

senses.definitionMd: An integer that is believed to be prime based on a probabilistic primality test. There should be no more than a negligible probability that the so-called probable prime is actually composite.

entries.title: Probative Data
entries.summaryMd: Information that reveals the truth of an allegation.

senses.definitionMd: Information that reveals the truth of an allegation.

entries.title: probe
entries.summaryMd: A technique that attempts to access a system to learn something about the system.

senses.definitionMd: A technique that attempts to access a system to learn something about the system.

entries.title: problem
entries.summaryMd: Difficulty, uncertainty, or otherwise realized and undesirable event, set of events, condition, or situation that requires investigation and corrective action.

senses.definitionMd: Difficulty, uncertainty, or otherwise realized and undesirable event, set of events, condition, or situation that requires investigation and corrective action.

entries.title: Problematic Data Action
entries.summaryMd: A data action that could cause an adverse effect for individuals

senses.definitionMd: A data action that could cause an adverse effect for individuals

entries.title: process
entries.summaryMd: An executing program.

senses.definitionMd: An executing program.

entries.title: process assistant
entries.summaryMd: An individual who provides support for the proofing process but does not support decision-making or risk-based evaluation (e.g., translation, transcription, or accessibility support).

senses.definitionMd: An individual who provides support for the proofing process but does not support decision-making or risk-based evaluation (e.g., translation, transcription, or accessibility support).

entries.title: process controller
entries.summaryMd: A type of computer system, typically rack-mounted, that processes sensor input, executes control algorithms, and computes actuator outputs.

senses.definitionMd: A type of computer system, typically rack-mounted, that processes sensor input, executes control algorithms, and computes actuator outputs.

entries.title: process hijacking
entries.summaryMd: A process checkpoint and migration technique that uses dynamic program re- writing techniques to add a checkpointing capability to a running program. Process hijacking makes it possible to checkpoint and migrate proprietary applications that cannot be re-linked with a checkpoint library allowing dynamic hand off of an ordinary running process to a distributed resource management system (e.g., the ability to trick or bypass the firewall allowing the server component to take over processes and gain rights for accessing the internet).

senses.definitionMd: A process checkpoint and migration technique that uses dynamic program re- writing techniques to add a checkpointing capability to a running program. Process hijacking makes it possible to checkpoint and migrate proprietary applications that cannot be re-linked with a checkpoint library allowing dynamic hand off of an ordinary running process to a distributed resource management system (e.g., the ability to trick or bypass the firewall allowing the server component to take over processes and gain rights for accessing the internet).

entries.title: process outcome
entries.summaryMd: Observable result of the successful achievement of the process purpose.

senses.definitionMd: Observable result of the successful achievement of the process purpose.

entries.title: process purpose
entries.summaryMd: High-level objective of performing the process and the likely outcomes of effective implementation of the process.

senses.definitionMd: High-level objective of performing the process and the likely outcomes of effective implementation of the process.

entries.title: process step
entries.summaryMd: A reference to one of the 6 steps in the ISCM process defined in NIST SP 800-137.

senses.definitionMd: A reference to one of the 6 steps in the ISCM process defined in NIST SP 800-137.

entries.title: processing
entries.summaryMd: Operation or set of operations performed upon PII that can include but is not limited to the collection, retention, logging, generation, transformation, use, disclosure, transfer, and disposal of PII.

senses.definitionMd: Operation or set of operations performed upon PII that can include but is not limited to the collection, retention, logging, generation, transformation, use, disclosure, transfer, and disposal of PII.

entries.title: product
entries.summaryMd: Result of a process.

senses.definitionMd: Result of a process.

entries.title: Product Category
entries.summaryMd: The main product category of the IT product (e.g., firewall, IDS, operating system, web server).

senses.definitionMd: The main product category of the IT product (e.g., firewall, IDS, operating system, web server).

entries.title: product compliant list (PCL)
entries.summaryMd: The list of information assurance (IA) and IA-enabled products evaluated and validated pursuant to the NIAP program.

senses.definitionMd: The list of information assurance (IA) and IA-enabled products evaluated and validated pursuant to the NIAP program.

entries.title: Product Component Host
entries.summaryMd: The organization, individual, and/or system that hosts the product component. Product component hosts may provide support for or supersede the need to test criteria since they are expected to implement, control, and verify the criteria.

senses.definitionMd: The organization, individual, and/or system that hosts the product component. Product component hosts may provide support for or supersede the need to test criteria since they are expected to implement, control, and verify the criteria.

entries.title: product cybersecurity capability
entries.summaryMd: Cybersecurity features or functions that computing devices provide through their own technical means (i.e., device hardware and software).

senses.definitionMd: Cybersecurity features or functions that computing devices provide through their own technical means (i.e., device hardware and software).

entries.title: Product Output
entries.summaryMd: Information produced by a product. This includes the product user interface, human-readable reports, and machine-readable reports. Unless otherwise indicated by a specific requirement, there are no constraints on the format. When this output is evaluated in a test procedure, either all or specific forms of output will be sampled as indicated by the test procedure.

senses.definitionMd: Information produced by a product. This includes the product user interface, human-readable reports, and machine-readable reports. Unless otherwise indicated by a specific requirement, there are no constraints on the format. When this output is evaluated in a test procedure, either all or specific forms of output will be sampled as indicated by the test procedure.

entries.title: product owner
entries.summaryMd: Person or organization responsible for the development, modification, operation, and/or final disposition of software or hardware used in an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Person or organization responsible for the development, modification, operation, and/or final disposition of software or hardware used in an information system.

entries.title: product source node (PSN)
entries.summaryMd: The Key Management Infrastructure core node that provides central generation of cryptographic key material.

senses.definitionMd: The Key Management Infrastructure core node that provides central generation of cryptographic key material.

entries.title: profile
entries.summaryMd: Analytic model of communications associated with an organization or activity. The model is prepared from a systematic examination of communications content and patterns, the functions they reflect, and the communications security measures applied.

senses.definitionMd: Analytic model of communications associated with an organization or activity. The model is prepared from a systematic examination of communications content and patterns, the functions they reflect, and the communications security measures applied.

entries.title: Profile augmentations
entries.summaryMd: The properties or characteristics that are recommended, but not required, by this Profile for FCKMSs.

senses.definitionMd: The properties or characteristics that are recommended, but not required, by this Profile for FCKMSs.

entries.title: Profile features
entries.summaryMd: The properties or characteristics that could be used by FCKMSs, but are not required or recommended by this Profile.

senses.definitionMd: The properties or characteristics that could be used by FCKMSs, but are not required or recommended by this Profile.

entries.title: Profile requirements
entries.summaryMd: The properties or characteristics that shall be exhibited in FCKMSs in order to conform to, or comply with, this Profile.

senses.definitionMd: The properties or characteristics that shall be exhibited in FCKMSs in order to conform to, or comply with, this Profile.

entries.title: profiling
entries.summaryMd: Measuring the characteristics of expected activity so that changes to it can be more easily identified.

senses.definitionMd: Measuring the characteristics of expected activity so that changes to it can be more easily identified.

entries.title: program manager
entries.summaryMd: Person or organization having responsibility for the development, procurement, integration, modification, operation and maintenance, and/or final disposition of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Person or organization having responsibility for the development, procurement, integration, modification, operation and maintenance, and/or final disposition of an information system.

entries.title: program metrics
entries.summaryMd: Tools designed to facilitate decision-making and improve performance and accountability through the collection, analysis, and reporting of relevant performance-related data.

senses.definitionMd: Tools designed to facilitate decision-making and improve performance and accountability through the collection, analysis, and reporting of relevant performance-related data.

entries.title: programmable logic controller
entries.summaryMd: A solid-state control system that has a user-programmable memory for storing instructions for the purpose of implementing specific functions such as I/O control, logic, timing, counting, three mode (PID) control, communication, arithmetic, and data and file processing.

senses.definitionMd: A solid-state control system that has a user-programmable memory for storing instructions for the purpose of implementing specific functions such as I/O control, logic, timing, counting, three mode (PID) control, communication, arithmetic, and data and file processing.

entries.title: project
entries.summaryMd: Endeavor with defined start and finish criteria undertaken to create a product or service in accordance with specified resources and requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Endeavor with defined start and finish criteria undertaken to create a product or service in accordance with specified resources and requirements.

entries.title: prompt extraction
entries.summaryMd: An attack that tries to divulge the system prompt or other information in the context of a large language model that would normally be hidden from a user.

senses.definitionMd: An attack that tries to divulge the system prompt or other information in the context of a large language model that would normally be hidden from a user.

entries.title: prompt injection
entries.summaryMd: An attack which exploits the concatenation of untrusted input with a prompt constructed by a higher-trust party such as the application designer.

senses.definitionMd: An attack which exploits the concatenation of untrusted input with a prompt constructed by a higher-trust party such as the application designer.

entries.title: Proof of possession (POP)
entries.summaryMd: A verification process whereby assurance is obtained that the owner of a key pair actually has the private key associated with the public key.

senses.definitionMd: A verification process whereby assurance is obtained that the owner of a key pair actually has the private key associated with the public key.

entries.title: Proof of stake consensus model
entries.summaryMd: A consensus model where the blockchain network is secured by users locking an amount of cryptocurrency into the blockchain network, a process called staking. Participants with more stake in the system are more likely to want it to succeed and to not be subverted, which gives them more weight during consensus.

senses.definitionMd: A consensus model where the blockchain network is secured by users locking an amount of cryptocurrency into the blockchain network, a process called staking. Participants with more stake in the system are more likely to want it to succeed and to not be subverted, which gives them more weight during consensus.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Proof of stake consensus model"

entries.title: Proof of work consensus model
entries.summaryMd: A consensus model where a publishing node wins the right to publish the next block by expending time, energy, and computational cycles to solve a hard-to-solve, but easy-to-verify problem (e.g., finding the nonce which, when combined with the data to be added to the block, will result in a specific output pattern).

senses.definitionMd: A consensus model where a publishing node wins the right to publish the next block by expending time, energy, and computational cycles to solve a hard-to-solve, but easy-to-verify problem (e.g., finding the nonce which, when combined with the data to be added to the block, will result in a specific output pattern).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Proof of work consensus model"

entries.title: proofing agent
entries.summaryMd: An agent of the CSP who is trained to attend identity proofing sessions and can make limited risk-based decisions, such as physically inspecting identity evidence and comparing the applicant to the identity evidence.

senses.definitionMd: An agent of the CSP who is trained to attend identity proofing sessions and can make limited risk-based decisions, such as physically inspecting identity evidence and comparing the applicant to the identity evidence.

entries.title: proper working state
entries.summaryMd: A condition in which the device or system contains no compromised internal components or data fields (e.g., data stored to memory) and from which the device or system can recognize and process valid input signals and output valid PNT solutions. An initial pre-deployment configuration is a basic example. The accuracy of the immediate PNT solution is not specified in this definition, as it will depend on the specifics of the device or system’s performance and the degradation allowed by different resilience levels.

entries.title: property inference

entries.title: property value

senses.definitionMd: Instance of a specific value together with an identifier for a data dictionary entry that defines a property.

entries.title: proprietary information (PROPIN)
entries.summaryMd: Material and information relating to or associated with a company's products, business, or activities, including but not limited to financial information; data or statements; trade secrets; product research and development; existing and future product designs and performance specifications; marketing plans or techniques; schematics; client lists; computer programs; processes; and know- how that has been clearly identified and properly marked by the company as proprietary information, trade secrets, or company confidential information. The information must have been developed by the company and not be available to the Government or to the public without restriction from another source.

senses.definitionMd: Material and information relating to or associated with a company's products, business, or activities, including but not limited to financial information; data or statements; trade secrets; product research and development; existing and future product designs and performance specifications; marketing plans or techniques; schematics; client lists; computer programs; processes; and know- how that has been clearly identified and properly marked by the company as proprietary information, trade secrets, or company confidential information. The information must have been developed by the company and not be available to the Government or to the public without restriction from another source.

entries.title: proscribed information
entries.summaryMd: Information that is classified as top secret (TS) information; communications security (COMSEC) information (excluding controlled cryptographic items when un- keyed or utilized with unclassified keys); restricted data (RD); special access program information (SAP); or sensitive compartmented information (SCI).

senses.definitionMd: Information that is classified as top secret (TS) information; communications security (COMSEC) information (excluding controlled cryptographic items when un- keyed or utilized with unclassified keys); restricted data (RD); special access program information (SAP); or sensitive compartmented information (SCI).

entries.title: Prose Checklist
entries.summaryMd: A checklist that provides a narrative descriptions of how a person can manually alter a product’s configuration.

senses.definitionMd: A checklist that provides a narrative descriptions of how a person can manually alter a product’s configuration.

entries.title: protect (CSF function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop and implement the appropriate safeguards to ensure delivery of critical infrastructure services.

senses.definitionMd: Develop and implement the appropriate safeguards to ensure delivery of critical infrastructure services.

entries.title: Protect-P (Function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop and implement appropriate data processing safeguards.

senses.definitionMd: Develop and implement appropriate data processing safeguards.

entries.title: protected distribution system (PDS)
entries.summaryMd: Wireline or fiber-optic distribution system used to transmit unencrypted classified national security information through an area of lesser classification or control. Note: "An area of lesser classification or control" refers to unencrypted classified national security information passing from, for example, an area cleared for Top Secret material to an area only cleared for Secret material or from a medium-threat area with greater physical security controls to a high- threat area with fewer physical security controls.

senses.definitionMd: Wireline or fiber-optic distribution system used to transmit unencrypted classified national security information through an area of lesser classification or control. Note: "An area of lesser classification or control" refers to unencrypted classified national security information passing from, for example, an area cleared for Top Secret material to an area only cleared for Secret material or from a medium-threat area with greater physical security controls to a high- threat area with fewer physical security controls.

entries.title: Protected Mode
entries.summaryMd: An operational mode found in x86-compatible processors with hardware support for memory protection, virtual memory, and multitasking.

senses.definitionMd: An operational mode found in x86-compatible processors with hardware support for memory protection, virtual memory, and multitasking.

entries.title: protection
entries.summaryMd: In the context of systems security engineering, a control objective that applies across all types of asset types and the corresponding consequences of loss. A system protection capability is a system control objective and a system design problem. The solution to the problem is optimized through a balanced proactive strategy and a reactive strategy that is not limited to prevention. The strategy also encompasses avoiding asset loss and consequences; detecting asset loss and consequences; minimizing (i.e., limiting, containing, restricting) asset loss and consequences; responding to asset loss and consequences; recovering from asset loss and consequences; and forecasting or predicting asset loss and consequences.

senses.definitionMd: In the context of systems security engineering, a control objective that applies across all types of asset types and the corresponding consequences of loss. A system protection capability is a system control objective and a system design problem. The solution to the problem is optimized through a balanced proactive strategy and a reactive strategy that is not limited to prevention. The strategy also encompasses avoiding asset loss and consequences; detecting asset loss and consequences; minimizing (i.e., limiting, containing, restricting) asset loss and consequences; responding to asset loss and consequences; recovering from asset loss and consequences; and forecasting or predicting asset loss and consequences.

entries.title: Protection Bits
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism commonly included in UNIX and UNIX-like systems that controls access based on bits specifying read, write, or execute permissions for a file’s (or directory’s) owner, group, or other(world).

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism commonly included in UNIX and UNIX-like systems that controls access based on bits specifying read, write, or execute permissions for a file’s (or directory’s) owner, group, or other(world).

entries.title: protection needs
entries.summaryMd: Informal statement or expression of the stakeholder security requirements focused on protecting information, systems, and services associated with mission and business functions throughout the system life cycle.

senses.definitionMd: Informal statement or expression of the stakeholder security requirements focused on protecting information, systems, and services associated with mission and business functions throughout the system life cycle.

entries.title: protection philosophy
entries.summaryMd: Informal description of the overall design of a system delineating each of the protection mechanisms employed. Combination of formal and informal techniques, appropriate to the evaluation class, used to show the mechanisms are adequate to enforce the security policy.

senses.definitionMd: Informal description of the overall design of a system delineating each of the protection mechanisms employed. Combination of formal and informal techniques, appropriate to the evaluation class, used to show the mechanisms are adequate to enforce the security policy.

entries.title: protection profile
entries.summaryMd: A minimal, baseline set of requirements targeted at mitigating well defined and described threats. Protection Profiles may be created by Technical Communities and will include:

entries.title: protective packaging
entries.summaryMd: Packaging techniques for COMSEC material that discourage penetration, reveal a penetration has occurred or was attempted, or inhibit viewing or copying of keying material prior to the time it is exposed for use.

entries.title: protocol
entries.summaryMd: A set of rules (i.e., formats and procedures) to implement and control some type of association (e.g., communication) between systems.

entries.title: protocol analyzer
entries.summaryMd: A device or software application that enables the user to analyze the performance of network data so as to ensure that the network and its associated hardware/software are operating within network specifications.

entries.title: provenance
entries.summaryMd: The chronology of the origin, development, ownership, location, and changes to a system or system component and associated data. It may also include personnel and processes used to interact with or make modifications to the system, component, or associated data.

senses.definitionMd: The chronology of the origin, development, ownership, location, and changes to a system or system component and associated data. It may also include personnel and processes used to interact with or make modifications to the system, component, or associated data.

Proxy servers are available for common Internet services; for example, a hyper text transfer protocol (HTTP) proxy used for Web access, and a simple mail transfer protocol (SMTP) proxy used for e-mail.

senses.definitionMd: A server that services the requests of its clients by forwarding those requests to other servers.

entries.title: proxy validation and verification
entries.summaryMd: Using a non-critical system with comparable properties to a critical one as a testing substitute.

senses.definitionMd: Using a non-critical system with comparable properties to a critical one as a testing substitute.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "proxy validation and verification"

entries.title: pseudonym
entries.summaryMd: A name assigned through a formal process by a federal department or agency to a federal employee for the purpose of the employee’s protection (i.e., the employee might be placed at risk if their actual name were known) or for other purposes.

senses.definitionMd: A name assigned through a formal process by a federal department or agency to a federal employee for the purpose of the employee’s protection (i.e., the employee might be placed at risk if their actual name were known) or for other purposes.

entries.title: pseudonymization
entries.summaryMd: De-identification technique that replaces an identifier (or identifiers) for a data principal with a pseudonym in order to hide the identity of that data principal.

senses.definitionMd: De-identification technique that replaces an identifier (or identifiers) for a data principal with a pseudonym in order to hide the identity of that data principal.

entries.title: Pseudorandom
entries.summaryMd: A process or data produced by a process is said to be pseudorandom when the outcome is deterministic yet also effectively random as long as the internal action of the process is hidden from observation. For cryptographic purposes, “effectively random” means “computationally indistinguishable from random within the limits of the intended security strength.”

senses.definitionMd: A process or data produced by a process is said to be pseudorandom when the outcome is deterministic yet also effectively random as long as the internal action of the process is hidden from observation. For cryptographic purposes, “effectively random” means “computationally indistinguishable from random within the limits of the intended security strength.”

entries.title: Pseudorandom function family
entries.summaryMd: An indexed family of (efficiently computable) functions, each defined for the same particular pair of input and output spaces. (For the purposes of this Recommendation, one may assume that both the index set and the output space are finite.) The indexed functions are pseudorandom in the following sense:If a function from the family is selected by choosing an index value uniformly at random, and one’s knowledge of the selected function is limited to the output values corresponding to a feasible number of (adaptively) chosen input values, then the selected function is computationally indistinguishable from a function whose outputs were fixed uniformly at random.

senses.definitionMd: An indexed family of (efficiently computable) functions, each defined for the same particular pair of input and output spaces. (For the purposes of this Recommendation, one may assume that both the index set and the output space are finite.) The indexed functions are pseudorandom in the following sense:If a function from the family is selected by choosing an index value uniformly at random, and one’s knowledge of the selected function is limited to the output values corresponding to a feasible number of (adaptively) chosen input values, then the selected function is computationally indistinguishable from a function whose outputs were fixed uniformly at random.

entries.title: Pseudorandom function (PRF)
entries.summaryMd: A function that can be used to generate output from a random seed and a data variable, such that the output is computationally indistinguishable from truly random output.

senses.definitionMd: A function that can be used to generate output from a random seed and a data variable, such that the output is computationally indistinguishable from truly random output.

entries.title: Pseudorandom key
entries.summaryMd: As used in this Recommendation, a binary string that is taken from the output of a PRF.

senses.definitionMd: As used in this Recommendation, a binary string that is taken from the output of a PRF.

entries.title: pseudorandom number generator
entries.summaryMd: A deterministic computational process that has one or more inputs called "seeds", and it outputs a sequence of values that appears to be random according to specified statistical tests. A cryptographic PRNG has the additional property that the output is unpredictable, given that the seed is not known.

senses.definitionMd: A deterministic computational process that has one or more inputs called "seeds", and it outputs a sequence of values that appears to be random according to specified statistical tests. A cryptographic PRNG has the additional property that the output is unpredictable, given that the seed is not known.

entries.title: PubKeyU, PubKeyV
entries.summaryMd: Public key of party U or V, respectively.

senses.definitionMd: Public key of party U or V, respectively.

entries.title: public
entries.summaryMd: Any entity or person who might be impacted by or need to take action for a specific vulnerability; intended to be loosely interpreted.

senses.definitionMd: Any entity or person who might be impacted by or need to take action for a specific vulnerability; intended to be loosely interpreted.

entries.title: Public and Private Key
entries.summaryMd: Public and private keys are two very large numbers that (through advanced mathematics) have a unique relationship, whereby information encrypted with one number (key) can only be decrypted with the other number (key) and vice versa. In order to leverage this characteristic for security operations, once two numbers are mathematically selected (generated), one is kept secret (private key) and the other is shared (public key). The holder of the private key can then authenticate themselves to another party who has the public key. Alternatively, a public key may be used by one party to send a confidential message to the holder of the corresponding private key. With SSH, the identity key is a private key and authorized keys are public keys.

senses.definitionMd: Public and private keys are two very large numbers that (through advanced mathematics) have a unique relationship, whereby information encrypted with one number (key) can only be decrypted with the other number (key) and vice versa. In order to leverage this characteristic for security operations, once two numbers are mathematically selected (generated), one is kept secret (private key) and the other is shared (public key). The holder of the private key can then authenticate themselves to another party who has the public key. Alternatively, a public key may be used by one party to send a confidential message to the holder of the corresponding private key. With SSH, the identity key is a private key and authorized keys are public keys.
