entries.title: Public CA
entries.summaryMd: A trusted third party that issues certificates as defined in IETF RFC 5280. A CA is considered public if its root certificate is included in browsers and other applications by the developers of those browsers and applications. The CA/Browser Forum defines the requirements public CAs must follow in their operations.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted third party that issues certificates as defined in IETF RFC 5280. A CA is considered public if its root certificate is included in browsers and other applications by the developers of those browsers and applications. The CA/Browser Forum defines the requirements public CAs must follow in their operations.

entries.title: public channel
entries.summaryMd: A communication channel between two parties. Such a channel can be observed and possibly also corrupted by third parties.

senses.definitionMd: A communication channel between two parties. Such a channel can be observed and possibly also corrupted by third parties.

entries.title: Public cloud
entries.summaryMd: The cloud infrastructure is provisioned for open use by the general public. It may be owned, managed, and operated by a business, academic, or government organization, or some combination of them. It exists on the premises of the cloud provider.

senses.definitionMd: The cloud infrastructure is provisioned for open use by the general public. It may be owned, managed, and operated by a business, academic, or government organization, or some combination of them. It exists on the premises of the cloud provider.

entries.title: public domain software
entries.summaryMd: Software not protected by copyright laws of any nation that may be freely used without permission of or payment to the creator, and that carries no warranties from or liabilities to the creator.

senses.definitionMd: Software not protected by copyright laws of any nation that may be freely used without permission of or payment to the creator, and that carries no warranties from or liabilities to the creator.

entries.title: Public Information
entries.summaryMd: The term 'public information' means any information, regardless of form or format, that an agency discloses, disseminates, or makes available to the public.

senses.definitionMd: The term 'public information' means any information, regardless of form or format, that an agency discloses, disseminates, or makes available to the public.

entries.title: public key
entries.summaryMd: The public part of an asymmetric key pair that is typically used to verify signatures or encrypt data.

senses.definitionMd: The public part of an asymmetric key pair that is typically used to verify signatures or encrypt data.

entries.title: public key certificate
entries.summaryMd: A digital document issued and digitally signed by the private key of a certification authority that binds an identifier to a cardholder through a public key. The certificate indicates that the cardholder identified in the certificate has sole control and access to the private key.

senses.definitionMd: A digital document issued and digitally signed by the private key of a certification authority that binds an identifier to a cardholder through a public key. The certificate indicates that the cardholder identified in the certificate has sole control and access to the private key.

entries.title: public key cryptography (PKC)
entries.summaryMd: Cryptography that uses two separate keys to exchange data — one to encrypt or digitally sign the data and one to decrypt the data or verify the digital signature. Also known as public-key cryptography.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptography that uses two separate keys to exchange data — one to encrypt or digitally sign the data and one to decrypt the data or verify the digital signature. Also known as public-key cryptography.

entries.title: public key enabling (PKE)
entries.summaryMd: The incorporation of the use of certificates for security services such as authentication, confidentiality, data integrity, and non- repudiation.

senses.definitionMd: The incorporation of the use of certificates for security services such as authentication, confidentiality, data integrity, and non- repudiation.

entries.title: public-key encryption scheme
entries.summaryMd: A set of three cryptographic algorithms (KeyGen, Encrypt, and Decrypt) that can be used by two parties to send secret data over a public channel. Also known as an asymmetric encryption scheme.

senses.definitionMd: A set of three cryptographic algorithms (KeyGen, Encrypt, and Decrypt) that can be used by two parties to send secret data over a public channel. Also known as an asymmetric encryption scheme.

entries.title: public key infrastructure (PKI)
entries.summaryMd: A framework that is established to issue, maintain and revoke public key certificates.

senses.definitionMd: A framework that is established to issue, maintain and revoke public key certificates.

entries.title: Public key/public signature verification key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key that is used with an asymmetric (public key) cryptographic algorithm and is associated with a private key. The public key is associated with an owner and may be made public. In the case of digital signatures, the public key is used to verify a digital signature that was signed using the corresponding private key.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key that is used with an asymmetric (public key) cryptographic algorithm and is associated with a private key. The public key is associated with an owner and may be made public. In the case of digital signatures, the public key is used to verify a digital signature that was signed using the corresponding private key.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Public key/public signature verification key"

entries.title: Public-key validation
entries.summaryMd: The procedure whereby the recipient of a public key checks that the key conforms to the arithmetic requirements for such a key in order to thwart certain types of attacks.

senses.definitionMd: The procedure whereby the recipient of a public key checks that the key conforms to the arithmetic requirements for such a key in order to thwart certain types of attacks.

entries.title: Public Reviewer
entries.summaryMd: A member of the general public who reviews a candidate checklist and sends comments to NIST.

senses.definitionMd: A member of the general public who reviews a candidate checklist and sends comments to NIST.

entries.title: public seed
entries.summaryMd: A starting value for a pseudorandom number generator. The value produced by the random number generator may be made public. The public seed is often called a "salt".

senses.definitionMd: A starting value for a pseudorandom number generator. The value produced by the random number generator may be made public. The public seed is often called a "salt".

entries.title: Publishing node
entries.summaryMd: A node that, in addition to all responsibilities required of a full node, is tasked with extending the blockchain by creating and publishing new blocks. Also known as mining node, committing node, minting node.

senses.definitionMd: A node that, in addition to all responsibilities required of a full node, is tasked with extending the blockchain by creating and publishing new blocks. Also known as mining node, committing node, minting node.

entries.title: purge
entries.summaryMd: A method of sanitization that applies physical or logical techniques that render Target Data recovery infeasible using state of the art laboratory techniques.

senses.definitionMd: A method of sanitization that applies physical or logical techniques that render Target Data recovery infeasible using state of the art laboratory techniques.

entries.title: Push-To-Talk (PTT)
entries.summaryMd: A method of communicating on half-duplex communication lines, including two-way radio, using a “walkie-talkie” button to switch from voice reception to transmit mode.

senses.definitionMd: A method of communicating on half-duplex communication lines, including two-way radio, using a “walkie-talkie” button to switch from voice reception to transmit mode.

entries.title: putative re-identifications
entries.summaryMd: Apparent re-identifications that may or may not be correct.

senses.definitionMd: Apparent re-identifications that may or may not be correct.

entries.title: q
entries.summaryMd: The octet length of the binary representation of the octet length of the payload.

senses.definitionMd: The octet length of the binary representation of the octet length of the payload.

entries.title: QEMU (Quick Emulator)
entries.summaryMd: A software module that is a component of the hypervisor platform that supports full virtualization by providing emulation of various hardware devices.

senses.definitionMd: A software module that is a component of the hypervisor platform that supports full virtualization by providing emulation of various hardware devices.

entries.title: qInv
entries.summaryMd: Inverse of q modulo p in the CRT format, i.e., q-1 mod p; an integer.

senses.definitionMd: Inverse of q modulo p in the CRT format, i.e., q-1 mod p; an integer.

entries.title: quadrant
entries.summaryMd: Short name referring to technology that provides tamper-resistant protection to cryptographic equipment.

senses.definitionMd: Short name referring to technology that provides tamper-resistant protection to cryptographic equipment.

entries.title: quadratic twist
entries.summaryMd: Certain elliptic curve related to a specified elliptic curve.

senses.definitionMd: Certain elliptic curve related to a specified elliptic curve.

entries.title: qualification
entries.summaryMd: Process of demonstrating whether an entity is capable of fulfilling specified requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Process of demonstrating whether an entity is capable of fulfilling specified requirements.

entries.title: Qualified Products List
entries.summaryMd: a list of products that have met the qualification requirements stated in the applicable specification, including appropriate product identification and test or qualification reference number, with the name and plant address of the manufacturer and distributor, as applicable.

senses.definitionMd: a list of products that have met the qualification requirements stated in the applicable specification, including appropriate product identification and test or qualification reference number, with the name and plant address of the manufacturer and distributor, as applicable.

entries.title: Qualitative Assessment
entries.summaryMd: Use of a set of methods, principles, or rules for assessing risk based on nonnumerical categories or levels.

senses.definitionMd: Use of a set of methods, principles, or rules for assessing risk based on nonnumerical categories or levels.

entries.title: Qualitative Risk Analysis
entries.summaryMd: A method for risk analysis that is based on the assignment of a descriptor such as low, medium, or high.

senses.definitionMd: A method for risk analysis that is based on the assignment of a descriptor such as low, medium, or high.

entries.title: quality
entries.summaryMd: Degree to which a set of inherent characteristics fulfils requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Degree to which a set of inherent characteristics fulfils requirements.

entries.title: quality assurance
entries.summaryMd: Part of quality management focused on providing confidence that quality requirements will be fulfilled.

senses.definitionMd: Part of quality management focused on providing confidence that quality requirements will be fulfilled.

entries.title: quality characteristic
entries.summaryMd: Inherent characteristic of a product, process, or system related to a requirement.

senses.definitionMd: Inherent characteristic of a product, process, or system related to a requirement.

entries.title: quality management
entries.summaryMd: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organization with regard to quality.

senses.definitionMd: Coordinated activities to direct and control an organization with regard to quality.

entries.title: quality property
entries.summaryMd: An emergent property of a system that includes, for example: safety, security, maintainability, resilience, reliability, availability, agility, and survivability. This property is also referred to as a systemic property across many engineering domains.

senses.definitionMd: An emergent property of a system that includes, for example: safety, security, maintainability, resilience, reliability, availability, agility, and survivability. This property is also referred to as a systemic property across many engineering domains.

entries.title: Quantitative Assessment
entries.summaryMd: Use of a set of methods, principles, or rules for assessing risks based on the use of numbers where the meanings and proportionality of values are maintained inside and outside the context of the assessment.

senses.definitionMd: Use of a set of methods, principles, or rules for assessing risks based on the use of numbers where the meanings and proportionality of values are maintained inside and outside the context of the assessment.

entries.title: Quantitative Risk Analysis
entries.summaryMd: A method for risk analysis where numerical values are assigned to both impact and likelihood based on statistical probabilities and monetarized valuation of loss or gain.

senses.definitionMd: A method for risk analysis where numerical values are assigned to both impact and likelihood based on statistical probabilities and monetarized valuation of loss or gain.

entries.title: quantum-vulnerable algorithm
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic algorithm that is believed to be secure against adversaries who possess only a classical computer but is known to be insecure against adversaries who possess a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic algorithm that is believed to be secure against adversaries who possess only a classical computer but is known to be insecure against adversaries who possess a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer.

entries.title: Quarantining
entries.summaryMd: Storing files containing malware in isolation for future disinfection or examination.

senses.definitionMd: Storing files containing malware in isolation for future disinfection or examination.

entries.title: Quasi
entries.summaryMd: A bit string representation of the octet length of P.

senses.definitionMd: A bit string representation of the octet length of P.

entries.title: quasi-identifier
entries.summaryMd: A variable that can be used to identify an individual through association with another variable.

senses.definitionMd: A variable that can be used to identify an individual through association with another variable.

entries.title: query access
entries.summaryMd: A capability with which an attacker can issue queries to a trained machine learning model and obtain predictions or generations.

senses.definitionMd: A capability with which an attacker can issue queries to a trained machine learning model and obtain predictions or generations.

entries.title: question
entries.summaryMd: The text of a question to pose, optionally accompanied by instructions to help guide a person to a response.

senses.definitionMd: The text of a question to pose, optionally accompanied by instructions to help guide a person to a response.

entries.title: questionnaire
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of questions to be used in determining a state or condition.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of questions to be used in determining a state or condition.

entries.title: Quote
entries.summaryMd: To precede printable non-alphanumeric characters (e.g., *, $, ?) with the backslash ( \) escape character in a value string. When a non-alphanumeric character is quoted in a WFN, it SHALL be processed as string data. When a non-alphanumeric character is unquoted in a WFN, it may be interpreted as a special character by CPE 2.3 specifications, including this one.

senses.definitionMd: To precede printable non-alphanumeric characters (e.g., *, $, ?) with the backslash ( \) escape character in a value string. When a non-alphanumeric character is quoted in a WFN, it SHALL be processed as string data. When a non-alphanumeric character is unquoted in a WFN, it may be interpreted as a special character by CPE 2.3 specifications, including this one.

entries.title: r
entries.summaryMd: The number of blocks in the formatted input data (N, A, P).

senses.definitionMd: The number of blocks in the formatted input data (N, A, P).

entries.title: (r, s)
entries.summaryMd: Digital signature for DSA or ECDSA.

senses.definitionMd: Digital signature for DSA or ECDSA.

entries.title: Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre
entries.summaryMd: Regional Internet Registry for Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Central Asia that allocates and registers blocks of Internet number resources to Internet service providers (ISPs) and other organizations.

senses.definitionMd: Regional Internet Registry for Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Central Asia that allocates and registers blocks of Internet number resources to Internet service providers (ISPs) and other organizations.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre"

entries.title: Random Binary Sequence
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of bits for which the probability of each bit being a “0” or “1” is ½. The value of each bit is independent of any other bit in the sequence, i.e., each bit is unpredictable.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of bits for which the probability of each bit being a “0” or “1” is ½. The value of each bit is independent of any other bit in the sequence, i.e., each bit is unpredictable.

entries.title: Random bit
entries.summaryMd: A bit for which an attacker has exactly a 50% probability of success of guessing the value of the bit as either zero or one.

senses.definitionMd: A bit for which an attacker has exactly a 50% probability of success of guessing the value of the bit as either zero or one.

entries.title: Random Bit Generator (RBG)
entries.summaryMd: A device or algorithm that can produce a sequence of bits that appear to be both statistically independent and unbiased.

senses.definitionMd: A device or algorithm that can produce a sequence of bits that appear to be both statistically independent and unbiased.

entries.title: Random Excursion Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to determine if the number of visits to a state within a random walk exceeds what one would expect for a random sequence.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to determine if the number of visits to a state within a random walk exceeds what one would expect for a random sequence.

entries.title: Random Excursion Variant Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to detect deviations from the distribution of the number of visits of a random walk to a certain state.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to detect deviations from the distribution of the number of visits of a random walk to a certain state.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Random Excursion Variant Test"

entries.title: Random Field
entries.summaryMd: In the RBG-based construction of IVs, either a direct random string or one of its successors.

senses.definitionMd: In the RBG-based construction of IVs, either a direct random string or one of its successors.

entries.title: Random nonce
entries.summaryMd: A nonce containing a random-value component that is generated anew for each nonce.

senses.definitionMd: A nonce containing a random-value component that is generated anew for each nonce.

entries.title: Random Number
entries.summaryMd: A value in a set of numbers that has an equal probability of being selected from the total population of possibilities and, in that sense, is unpredictable. A random number is an instance of an unbiased random variable, that is, the output produced by a uniformly distributed random process. Random numbers may, e.g., be obtained by converting suitable stings of random bits (see [NIST SP 800-90A], Appendix B.5 for details).

senses.definitionMd: A value in a set of numbers that has an equal probability of being selected from the total population of possibilities and, in that sense, is unpredictable. A random number is an instance of an unbiased random variable, that is, the output produced by a uniformly distributed random process. Random numbers may, e.g., be obtained by converting suitable stings of random bits (see [NIST SP 800-90A], Appendix B.5 for details).

entries.title: random number generator (RNG)
entries.summaryMd: A process that generates a random sequence of values (usually a sequence of bits) or an individual random value. Uses one or more non-deterministic bit sources and a processing function that formats the bits, and outputs an unpredictable and uniformly distributed sequence of values. Note: An RNG is also considered a randomizer.

senses.definitionMd: A process that generates a random sequence of values (usually a sequence of bits) or an individual random value. Uses one or more non-deterministic bit sources and a processing function that formats the bits, and outputs an unpredictable and uniformly distributed sequence of values. Note: An RNG is also considered a randomizer.

entries.title: random sampling
entries.summaryMd: A method of sampling where each sample has an equal chance of selection in hopes of gathering an unbiased representation.

senses.definitionMd: A method of sampling where each sample has an equal chance of selection in hopes of gathering an unbiased representation.

entries.title: Random value
entries.summaryMd: A sufficient entropy bit string.

senses.definitionMd: A sufficient entropy bit string.

entries.title: Random Variable
entries.summaryMd: Random variables differ from the usual deterministic variables (of science and engineering) in that random variables allow the systematic distributional assignment of probability values to each possible outcome.

senses.definitionMd: Random variables differ from the usual deterministic variables (of science and engineering) in that random variables allow the systematic distributional assignment of probability values to each possible outcome.

entries.title: Randomized hashing
entries.summaryMd: A technique for randomizing the input to a cryptographic hash function.

senses.definitionMd: A technique for randomizing the input to a cryptographic hash function.

entries.title: Randomized message
entries.summaryMd: A message that has been modified using a random value.

senses.definitionMd: A message that has been modified using a random value.

entries.title: randomizer
entries.summaryMd: Analog or digital source of unpredictable, unbiased, and usually independent bits. Randomizers can be used for several different functions, including key generation or to provide a starting state for a key generator.

senses.definitionMd: Analog or digital source of unpredictable, unbiased, and usually independent bits. Randomizers can be used for several different functions, including key generation or to provide a starting state for a key generator.

entries.title: Randomness extraction
entries.summaryMd: The first step in the two-step key-derivation procedure during which a key-derivation key is produced. The second step in the procedure is key expansion.

senses.definitionMd: The first step in the two-step key-derivation procedure during which a key-derivation key is produced. The second step in the procedure is key expansion.

entries.title: Randomness Source
entries.summaryMd: A component of a DRBG (which consists of a DRBG mechanism and a randomness source) that outputs bitstrings that are used as entropy input by the DRBG mechanism. The randomness source can be an entropy source or an RBG.

senses.definitionMd: A component of a DRBG (which consists of a DRBG mechanism and a randomness source) that outputs bitstrings that are used as entropy input by the DRBG mechanism. The randomness source can be an entropy source or an RBG.

entries.title: Range
entries.summaryMd: The maximum possible distance for communicating with a wireless network infrastructure or wireless client.

senses.definitionMd: The maximum possible distance for communicating with a wireless network infrastructure or wireless client.

entries.title: Rank (of a matrix)
entries.summaryMd: Refers to the rank of a matrix in linear algebra over GF(2). Having reduced a matrix into row-echelon form via elementary row operations, the number of nonzero rows, if any, are counted in order to determine the number of linearly independent rows or columns in the matrix.

senses.definitionMd: Refers to the rank of a matrix in linear algebra over GF(2). Having reduced a matrix into row-echelon form via elementary row operations, the number of nonzero rows, if any, are counted in order to determine the number of linearly independent rows or columns in the matrix.

entries.title: Rank Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to check for linear dependence among fixed length substrings of the original sequence.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to check for linear dependence among fixed length substrings of the original sequence.

entries.title: Rapid elasticity
entries.summaryMd: Capabilities can be elastically provisioned and released, in some cases automatically, to scale rapidly outward and inward commensurate with demand. To the consumer, the capabilities available for provisioning often appear to be unlimited and can be appropriated in any quantity at any time.

senses.definitionMd: Capabilities can be elastically provisioned and released, in some cases automatically, to scale rapidly outward and inward commensurate with demand. To the consumer, the capabilities available for provisioning often appear to be unlimited and can be appropriated in any quantity at any time.

entries.title: Rate
entries.summaryMd: In the sponge construction, the number of input bits processed per invocation of the underlying function.

senses.definitionMd: In the sponge construction, the number of input bits processed per invocation of the underlying function.

entries.title: ratio scale
entries.summaryMd: From the Stevens Scale of Measurement, a quantitative measurement scale with a true zero using variables that can be compared to find differences or intervals.

senses.definitionMd: From the Stevens Scale of Measurement, a quantitative measurement scale with a true zero using variables that can be compared to find differences or intervals.

entries.title: Rationale
entries.summaryMd: The explanation for why a Reference Document Element and a Focal Document Element are related within a set theory relationship mapping. This will be one of the following: syntactic, semantic, or functional.

senses.definitionMd: The explanation for why a Reference Document Element and a Focal Document Element are related within a set theory relationship mapping. This will be one of the following: syntactic, semantic, or functional.

entries.title: Raw data
entries.summaryMd: Digitized output of the noise source.

senses.definitionMd: Digitized output of the noise source.

entries.title: Rb
entries.summaryMd: The constant string for subkey generation for a cipher with block size b.

senses.definitionMd: The constant string for subkey generation for a cipher with block size b.

entries.title: RBG seed
entries.summaryMd: The input to a pseudorandom number generator. Different seeds generate different pseudorandom sequences.

senses.definitionMd: The input to a pseudorandom number generator. Different seeds generate different pseudorandom sequences.

entries.title: re-identification
entries.summaryMd: A process by which information is attributed to de-identified data in order to identify the individual to whom the de-identified data relate.

senses.definitionMd: A process by which information is attributed to de-identified data in order to identify the individual to whom the de-identified data relate.

entries.title: re-identification precision
entries.summaryMd: The ratio of correct re-identifications to the sum of correct and incorrect apparent re-identifications.

senses.definitionMd: The ratio of correct re-identifications to the sum of correct and incorrect apparent re-identifications.

entries.title: re-identification probability
entries.summaryMd: The probability that an individual’s identity will be correctly inferred by an outside party using information contained in a de-identified dataset.

senses.definitionMd: The probability that an individual’s identity will be correctly inferred by an outside party using information contained in a de-identified dataset.

entries.title: re-identification rate
entries.summaryMd: The percentage of records in a dataset that can be re-identified.

senses.definitionMd: The percentage of records in a dataset that can be re-identified.

entries.summaryMd: The likelihood that a third party can re-identify data subjects in a de-identified dataset.

entries.title: re-key (a certificate)

entries.title: Reader

senses.definitionMd: A device that can wirelessly communicate with tags. Readers can detect the presence of tags as well as send and receive data and commands from the tags.

senses.definitionMd: The act of impersonating a legitimate reader of an RFID system to read tags.

entries.summaryMd: An RF transaction in which the reader transmits a signal that is received by tags in its vicinity. The tags may be commanded to respond to the reader and continue with further transactions.

senses.definitionMd: An RF transaction in which the reader transmits a signal that is received by tags in its vicinity. The tags may be commanded to respond to the reader and continue with further transactions.

entries.title: Real Mode
entries.summaryMd: A legacy high-privilege operating mode in x86-compatible processors.

senses.definitionMd: A legacy high-privilege operating mode in x86-compatible processors.

entries.title: real time
entries.summaryMd: Pertaining to the performance of a computation during the actual time that the related physical process transpires so that the results of the computation can be used to guide the physical process.

entries.title: real time reaction
entries.summaryMd: Immediate response to a penetration attempt that is detected and diagnosed in time to prevent access.

senses.definitionMd: Immediate response to a penetration attempt that is detected and diagnosed in time to prevent access.

entries.title: reauthentication
entries.summaryMd: The process of confirming the subscriber’s continued presence and intent to be authenticated during an extended usage session.

senses.definitionMd: The process of confirming the subscriber’s continued presence and intent to be authenticated during an extended usage session.

entries.title: Receiver
entries.summaryMd: The party that receives secret keying material via a key-transport transaction. Contrast with sender.

senses.definitionMd: The party that receives secret keying material via a key-transport transaction. Contrast with sender.

entries.title: receiver operating characteristic
entries.summaryMd: A curve that plots the true positive rate versus the false positive rate for a classifier.

senses.definitionMd: A curve that plots the true positive rate versus the false positive rate for a classifier.

entries.title: recipient
entries.summaryMd: A party that either (1) receives a public key; or (2) obtains assurance from an assurance provider (e.g., assurance of the validity of a candidate public key or assurance of possession of the private key corresponding to a public key); or (3) receives key confirmation from a key-confirmation provider.

senses.definitionMd: A party that either (1) receives a public key; or (2) obtains assurance from an assurance provider (e.g., assurance of the validity of a candidate public key or assurance of possession of the private key corresponding to a public key); or (3) receives key confirmation from a key-confirmation provider.

entries.title: Recipient-usage period
entries.summaryMd: The period of time during which the protected information may be processed (e.g., decrypted).

senses.definitionMd: The period of time during which the protected information may be processed (e.g., decrypted).

entries.title: Reciprocal Agreement
entries.summaryMd: An agreement that allows two organizations to back up each other.

senses.definitionMd: An agreement that allows two organizations to back up each other.

entries.title: reciprocity
entries.summaryMd: Mutual agreement among participating organizations to accept each other’s security assessments in order to reuse information system resources and/or to accept each other’s assessed security posture in order to share information.

senses.definitionMd: Mutual agreement among participating organizations to accept each other’s security assessments in order to reuse information system resources and/or to accept each other’s assessed security posture in order to share information.

entries.title: Recommendation
entries.summaryMd: A special publication of the ITL that stipulates specific characteristics of the technology to use or the procedures to follow to achieve a common level of quality or level of interoperability.

senses.definitionMd: All books, papers, maps, photographs, machine-readable materials, or other documentary materials, regardless of physical form or characteristics, made or received by an agency of the United States Government under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations or other activities of the Government or because of the informational value of the data in them.

entries.title: records management
entries.summaryMd: The process for tagging information for records keeping requirements as mandated in the Federal Records Act and the National Archival and Records Requirements.

senses.definitionMd: The process for tagging information for records keeping requirements as mandated in the Federal Records Act and the National Archival and Records Requirements.

entries.title: recover (CSF function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop and implement the appropriate activities to maintain plans for resilience and to restore any capabilities or services that were impaired due to a cybersecurity event.

senses.definitionMd: Develop and implement the appropriate activities to maintain plans for resilience and to restore any capabilities or services that were impaired due to a cybersecurity event.

entries.title: Recovery Point Objective
entries.summaryMd: The point in time to which data must be recovered after an outage.

senses.definitionMd: The point in time to which data must be recovered after an outage.

entries.title: recovery procedures
entries.summaryMd: The actions necessary to restore a system's computational capability and data files after a system failure.

senses.definitionMd: The actions necessary to restore a system's computational capability and data files after a system failure.

entries.title: Recovery Time Objective
entries.summaryMd: The overall length of time an information system’s components can be in the recovery phase before negatively impacting the organization’s mission or mission/business processes.

senses.definitionMd: The overall length of time an information system’s components can be in the recovery phase before negatively impacting the organization’s mission or mission/business processes.

entries.title: RED/BLACK concept
entries.summaryMd: Separation of electrical and electronic circuits, components, equipment, and systems that handle classified plain text (RED) information, in electrical signal form, from those that handle unclassified (BLACK) information in the same form.

senses.definitionMd: Separation of electrical and electronic circuits, components, equipment, and systems that handle classified plain text (RED) information, in electrical signal form, from those that handle unclassified (BLACK) information in the same form.

entries.title: RED data
entries.summaryMd: Date that is not protected by encryption.

senses.definitionMd: Date that is not protected by encryption.

entries.title: RED equipment
entries.summaryMd: A term applied to equipment that processes unencrypted national security information that requires protection during electrical/electronic processing.

senses.definitionMd: A term applied to equipment that processes unencrypted national security information that requires protection during electrical/electronic processing.

entries.title: RED key
entries.summaryMd: Key that has not been encrypted in a system approved by NSA for key encryption or encrypted key in the presence of its associated key encryption key (KEK) or transfer key encryption key (TrKEK). Encrypted key in the same fill device as its associated KEK or TrKEK is considered unencrypted. (RED key is also known as unencrypted key). Such key is classified at the level of the data it is designed to protect.

senses.definitionMd: Key that has not been encrypted in a system approved by NSA for key encryption or encrypted key in the presence of its associated key encryption key (KEK) or transfer key encryption key (TrKEK). Encrypted key in the same fill device as its associated KEK or TrKEK is considered unencrypted. (RED key is also known as unencrypted key). Such key is classified at the level of the data it is designed to protect.

entries.title: RED line
entries.summaryMd: An optical fiber or a metallic wire that carries a RED signal or that originates/terminates in a RED equipment or system.

senses.definitionMd: An optical fiber or a metallic wire that carries a RED signal or that originates/terminates in a RED equipment or system.

entries.title: RED optical fiber line
entries.summaryMd: An optical fiber that carries RED signal or that originates/terminates in RED equipment or system.

senses.definitionMd: An optical fiber that carries RED signal or that originates/terminates in RED equipment or system.

entries.title: RED signal
entries.summaryMd: Any electronic emission (e.g., plain text, key, key stream, subkey stream, initial fill, or control signal) that would divulge national security information if recovered.

senses.definitionMd: Any electronic emission (e.g., plain text, key, key stream, subkey stream, initial fill, or control signal) that would divulge national security information if recovered.

entries.title: red team
entries.summaryMd: A group of people authorized and organized to emulate a potential adversary's attack or exploitation capabilities against an enterprise's security posture. The Red Team's objective is to improve enterprise CS by demonstrating the impacts of successful attacks and by demonstrating what works for the defenders (i.e., the Blue Team) in an operational environment.

senses.definitionMd: A group of people authorized and organized to emulate a potential adversary's attack or exploitation capabilities against an enterprise's security posture. The Red Team's objective is to improve enterprise CS by demonstrating the impacts of successful attacks and by demonstrating what works for the defenders (i.e., the Blue Team) in an operational environment.

entries.title: Red Team/Blue Team Approach
entries.summaryMd: A group of people authorized and organized to emulate a potential adversary’s attack or exploitation capabilities against an enterprise’s security posture. The Red Team’s objective is to improve enterprise Information Assurance by demonstrating the impacts of successful attacks and by demonstrating what works for the defenders (i.e., the Blue Team) in an operational environment. 1. The group responsible for defending an enterprise’s use of information systems by maintaining its security posture against a group of mock attackers (i.e., the Red Team). Typically the Blue Team and its supporters must defend against real or simulated attacks 1) over a significant period of time, 2) in a representative operational context (e.g., as part of an operational exercise), and 3) according to rules established and monitored with the help of a neutral group refereeing the simulation or exercise (i.e., the White Team). 2. The term Blue Team is also used for defining a group of individuals that conduct operational network vulnerability evaluations and provide mitigation techniques to customers who have a need for an independent technical review of their network security posture. The Blue Team identifies security threats and risks in the operating environment, and in cooperation with the customer, analyzes the network environment and its current state of security readiness. Based on the Blue Team findings and expertise, they provide recommendations that integrate into an overall community security solution to increase the customer's cyber security readiness posture. Often a Blue Team is employed by itself or prior to a Red Team employment to ensure that the customer's networks are as secure as possible before having the Red Team test the systems.

entries.title: red team exercise
entries.summaryMd: An exercise, reflecting real-world conditions, that is conducted as a simulated adversarial attempt to compromise organizational missions and/or business processes to provide a comprehensive assessment of the security capability of the information system and organization.

senses.definitionMd: An exercise, reflecting real-world conditions, that is conducted as a simulated adversarial attempt to compromise organizational missions and/or business processes to provide a comprehensive assessment of the security capability of the information system and organization.

entries.title: red teaming
entries.summaryMd: In the AI context, means a structured testing effort, often adopting adversarial methods, to find flaws and vulnerabilities in an AI system, including unforeseen or undesirable system behaviors or potential risks associated with the misuse of the system.

senses.definitionMd: In the AI context, means a structured testing effort, often adopting adversarial methods, to find flaws and vulnerabilities in an AI system, including unforeseen or undesirable system behaviors or potential risks associated with the misuse of the system.

entries.title: RED wireline
entries.summaryMd: A metallic wire that carries a RED signal or that originates/terminates in a RED equipment or system.

senses.definitionMd: A metallic wire that carries a RED signal or that originates/terminates in a RED equipment or system.

entries.title: redaction
entries.summaryMd: The removal of information from a document or dataset for legal or security purposes.

senses.definitionMd: The removal of information from a document or dataset for legal or security purposes.

entries.title: redundant control server
entries.summaryMd: A backup to the control server that maintains the current state of the control server at all times.

senses.definitionMd: A backup to the control server that maintains the current state of the control server at all times.

entries.title: Reference
entries.summaryMd: Relationships between elements of two documents that are recorded in a NIST IR 8278A-compliant format and shared by the OLIR Catalog. There are three types of OLIRs: concept crosswalk, set theory relationship mapping, and supportive relationship mapping.

senses.definitionMd: Relationships between elements of two documents that are recorded in a NIST IR 8278A-compliant format and shared by the OLIR Catalog. There are three types of OLIRs: concept crosswalk, set theory relationship mapping, and supportive relationship mapping.

entries.title: reference data
entries.summaryMd: Cryptographic material used in the performance of a cryptographic protocol, such as an authentication or a signing protocol. The reference data length is the maximum length of a password or PIN. For algorithms, the reference data length is the length of a key.

senses.definitionMd: Cryptographic material used in the performance of a cryptographic protocol, such as an authentication or a signing protocol. The reference data length is the maximum length of a password or PIN. For algorithms, the reference data length is the length of a key.

entries.title: Reference Document
entries.summaryMd: A cybersecurity document that is related to the Framework.

senses.definitionMd: A cybersecurity document that is related to the Framework.

entries.title: Reference Document Element
entries.summaryMd: A discrete section, sentence, phrase, or other identifiable piece of content from a Reference Document.

senses.definitionMd: A discrete section, sentence, phrase, or other identifiable piece of content from a Reference Document.

entries.title: reference monitor
entries.summaryMd: A set of design requirements on a reference validation mechanism that, as a key component of an operating system, enforces an access control policy over all subjects and objects. A reference validation mechanism is always invoked (i.e., complete mediation), tamperproof, and small enough to be subject to analysis and tests, the completeness of which can be assured (i.e., verifiable).

senses.definitionMd: A set of design requirements on a reference validation mechanism that, as a key component of an operating system, enforces an access control policy over all subjects and objects. A reference validation mechanism is always invoked (i.e., complete mediation), tamperproof, and small enough to be subject to analysis and tests, the completeness of which can be assured (i.e., verifiable).

entries.title: reference monitor concept
entries.summaryMd: An abstract model of the necessary and sufficient properties that must be achieved by any mechanism that performs an access mediation control function.

senses.definitionMd: An abstract model of the necessary and sufficient properties that must be achieved by any mechanism that performs an access mediation control function.

entries.title: reference validation mechanism
entries.summaryMd: An implementation of the reference monitor concept that validates each access to resources against a list of authorized accesses allowed.

senses.definitionMd: An implementation of the reference monitor concept that validates each access to resources against a list of authorized accesses allowed.

entries.title: Reference Version
entries.summaryMd: The version of the OLIR.

senses.definitionMd: The version of the OLIR.

entries.title: regenerative cyber defense

senses.definitionMd: The process for restoring capabilities after a successful, large scale cyberspace attack, ideally in a way that prevents future attacks of the same nature.

entries.title: register
entries.summaryMd: A set of records (paper, electronic, or a combination) maintained by a Registration Authority containing assigned names and the associated information.

senses.definitionMd: A set of records (paper, electronic, or a combination) maintained by a Registration Authority containing assigned names and the associated information.

entries.title: Registrar
entries.summaryMd: Also known as a Registration Agent, a person who performs the enrollment process.

senses.definitionMd: Also known as a Registration Agent, a person who performs the enrollment process.

entries.title: registration
entries.summaryMd: The process of making a person’s identity known to the PIV system, associating a unique identifier with that identity, and collecting and recording the person’s relevant attributes into the system. In some other NIST documents, such as [NIST SP 800-63A], identity registration is referred to as enrollment.

senses.definitionMd: The process of making a person’s identity known to the PIV system, associating a unique identifier with that identity, and collecting and recording the person’s relevant attributes into the system. In some other NIST documents, such as [NIST SP 800-63A], identity registration is referred to as enrollment.

entries.title: Registration agent
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for registering new entities and perhaps other selected information.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible for registering new entities and perhaps other selected information.

entries.title: registration authority (RA)
entries.summaryMd: An entity authorized by the certification authority system (CAS) to collect, verify, and submit information provided by potential Subscribers which is to be entered into public key certificates. The term RA refers to hardware, software, and individuals that collectively perform this function.

senses.definitionMd: An entity authorized by the certification authority system (CAS) to collect, verify, and submit information provided by potential Subscribers which is to be entered into public key certificates. entries.title: Registry
entries.summaryMd: A service that allows developers to easily store images as they are created, tag and catalog images for identification and version control to aid in discovery and reuse, and find and download images that others have created.

senses.definitionMd: A service that allows developers to easily store images as they are created, tag and catalog images for identification and version control to aid in discovery and reuse, and find and download images that others have created.

entries.title: regrader
entries.summaryMd: A trusted process explicitly authorized to re-classify and re-label data in accordance with a defined policy exception. Untrusted /Unauthorized processes are such actions by the security policy.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted process explicitly authorized to re-classify and re-label data in accordance with a defined policy exception. Untrusted /Unauthorized processes are such actions by the security policy.

entries.title: regression
entries.summaryMd: A statistical technique used to predict the value of a variable based on the relationship between explanatory variables.

senses.definitionMd: A statistical technique used to predict the value of a variable based on the relationship between explanatory variables.

entries.title: Regular Expression
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of characters (or words) that forms a search pattern, mainly for use in pattern matching with strings, or string matching.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of characters (or words) that forms a search pattern, mainly for use in pattern matching with strings, or string matching.

senses.definitionMd: A type of machine learning in which a model learns to optimize its behavior according to a reward function by interacting with and receiving feedback from an environment.

entries.title: Rekey
entries.summaryMd: A procedure in which a new cryptographic key is generated in a manner that is independent of the (old) cryptographic key that it will replace.

senses.definitionMd: A procedure in which a new cryptographic key is generated in a manner that is independent of the (old) cryptographic key that it will replace.

entries.title: Relationship
entries.summaryMd: The type of logical comparison that the Reference Document Developer asserts compared to the Focal Document within a set theory relationship mapping. This will be one of the following: subset of, intersects with, equal to, superset of, or not related to.

senses.definitionMd: The type of logical comparison that the Reference Document Developer asserts compared to the Focal Document within a set theory relationship mapping. This will be one of the following: subset of, intersects with, equal to, superset of, or not related to.

entries.title: Relationship Explanation

senses.definitionMd: A text description of the nature of the relationship between a Reference Document Element and a Focal Document Element within a supportive relationship mapping.

entries.title: Relationship Identifier
entries.summaryMd: Identifying information where the value is a relationship to another asset.

senses.definitionMd: Identifying information where the value is a relationship to another asset.

entries.title: Relationship Property
entries.summaryMd: Indicates whether the supporting concept is necessary for achieving the supported concept within a supportive relationship mapping.

senses.definitionMd: Indicates whether the supporting concept is necessary for achieving the supported concept within a supportive relationship mapping.

entries.title: relationship style
entries.summaryMd: An explicitly defined convention for characterizing relationships for a use case.

senses.definitionMd: An explicitly defined convention for characterizing relationships for a use case.

entries.title: Relationship Type
entries.summaryMd: The type of supportive relationship being specified between a Reference Document Element and a Focal Document Element within a supportive relationship mapping. This will be one of the following: supports, is supported by, identical, equivalent, contrary, or no relationship.

senses.definitionMd: The type of supportive relationship being specified between a Reference Document Element and a Focal Document Element within a supportive relationship mapping. This will be one of the following: supports, is supported by, identical, equivalent, contrary, or no relationship.

entries.title: relative error

senses.definitionMd: The absolute error divided by the unaltered query output.

entries.title: Relatively prime
entries.summaryMd: Two positive integers are relatively prime if their greatest common divisor is 1.

senses.definitionMd: Two positive integers are relatively prime if their greatest common divisor is 1.

entries.title: relay

entries.summaryMd: A collection of new and/or changed configuration items which are tested and introduced into a production environment together.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of new and/or changed configuration items which are tested and introduced into a production environment together.

entries.title: release prefix

entries.title: relying party

entries.title: remediation
entries.summaryMd: The act of mitigating a vulnerability or a threat.

senses.definitionMd: The act of mitigating a vulnerability or a threat.

entries.title: remote access

entries.title: remote diagnostics/ maintenance

entries.title: remote maintenance
entries.summaryMd: Maintenance activities conducted by individuals communicating through an external network.

senses.definitionMd: Maintenance activities conducted by individuals communicating through an external network.

entries.title: remote rekeying

senses.definitionMd: Procedure by which a distant crypto-equipment is rekeyed electrically.

entries.title: remote terminal unit
entries.summaryMd: A computer with radio interfacing used in remote situations where communications via wire is unavailable. Usually used to communicate with remote field equipment. PLCs with radio communication capabilities are also used in place of RTUs.

senses.definitionMd: A computer with radio interfacing used in remote situations where communications via wire is unavailable. Usually used to communicate with remote field equipment. PLCs with radio communication capabilities are also used in place of RTUs.

entries.title: removable media
entries.summaryMd: Portable data storage medium that can be added to or removed from a computing device or network. Note: Examples include, but are not limited to: optical discs; external/removable hard drives; external/removable solid-state disc drives; magnetic/optical tapes; flash memory devices; flash memory cards; and all other external/removable disks.

entries.title: removable media device
entries.summaryMd: Portable device that can be connected to an information system (IS), computer, or network to provide data storage. These devices interface with the IS through processing chips and may load driver software, presenting a greater security risk to the IS than non-device media, such as optical discs or flash memory cards. Note: Examples include, but are not limited to: USB flash drives, external hard drives, and external solid state disk (SSD) drives. Portable Storage Devices also include memory cards that have additional functions aside from standard data storage and encrypted data storage, such as built-in Wi-Fi connectivity and global positioning system (GPS) reception. See also removable media.

entries.title: Removable User Identity Module (R-UIM)
entries.summaryMd: A card developed for cdmaOne/CDMA2000 handsets that extends the GSM SIM card to CDMA phones and networks.

entries.title: Repeatability
entries.summaryMd: The ability to repeat an assessment in the future, in a manner that is consistent with, and hence comparable to, prior assessments.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to repeat an assessment in the future, in a manner that is consistent with, and hence comparable to, prior assessments.

entries.title: Replace
entries.summaryMd: The process of installing a new certificate and removing an existing one so that the new certificate is used in place of the existing certificate on all systems where the existing certificate is being used.

senses.definitionMd: The process of installing a new certificate and removing an existing one so that the new certificate is used in place of the existing certificate on all systems where the existing certificate is being used.

entries.title: replay attack
entries.summaryMd: An attack that involves the capture of transmitted authentication or access control information and its subsequent retransmission with the intent of producing an unauthorized effect or gaining unauthorized access.

senses.definitionMd: An attack that involves the capture of transmitted authentication or access control information and its subsequent retransmission with the intent of producing an unauthorized effect or gaining unauthorized access.

entries.title: replay resistance
entries.summaryMd: Protection against the capture of transmitted authentication or access control information and its subsequent retransmission with the intent of producing an unauthorized effect or gaining unauthorized access.

senses.definitionMd: Protection against the capture of transmitted authentication or access control information and its subsequent retransmission with the intent of producing an unauthorized effect or gaining unauthorized access.

entries.title: reporter
entries.summaryMd: Any entity that reports a vulnerability to the Government and that may be an entity outside of the Government, within the Government, or within the specific system that has the vulnerability.

senses.definitionMd: Any entity that reports a vulnerability to the Government and that may be an entity outside of the Government, within the Government, or within the specific system that has the vulnerability.

entries.title: Reporting
entries.summaryMd: The final phase of the computer and network forensic process, which involves reporting the results of the analysis; this may include describing the actions used, explaining how tools and procedures were selected, determining what other actions need to be performed (e.g., forensic examination of additional data sources, securing identified vulnerabilities, improving existing security controls), and providing recommendations for improvement to policies, guidelines, procedures, tools, and other aspects of the forensic process. The formality of the reporting step varies greatly depending on the situation.

senses.definitionMd: The final phase of the computer and network forensic process, which involves reporting the results of the analysis; this may include describing the actions used, explaining how tools and procedures were selected, determining what other actions need to be performed (e.g., forensic examination of additional data sources, securing identified vulnerabilities, improving existing security controls), and providing recommendations for improvement to policies, guidelines, procedures, tools, and other aspects of the forensic process. The formality of the reporting step varies greatly depending on the situation.

entries.title: Representational State Transfer (REST)
entries.summaryMd: A software architectural style that defines a common method for defining APIs for Web services.

senses.definitionMd: A software architectural style that defines a common method for defining APIs for Web services.

entries.title: Representative (of a key owner)
entries.summaryMd: See Sponsor (of a key).

senses.definitionMd: See Sponsor (of a key).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Representative (of a key owner)"

entries.title: Reproducibility
entries.summaryMd: The ability of different experts to produce the same results from the same data.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of different experts to produce the same results from the same data.

entries.title: Request for Comments
entries.summaryMd: A Request For Comments is a formal standards-track document developed in working groups within the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).

senses.definitionMd: A Request For Comments is a formal standards-track document developed in working groups within the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF).

entries.title: Requester
entries.summaryMd: The entity (person or organization) that wishes to make use of a provider’s Web service. It will use a requester agent to exchange messages with the provider’s provider agent. “Requester” is also used as a shorthand to refer to the requester agent acting on the requester’s behalf.

senses.definitionMd: The entity (person or organization) that wishes to make use of a provider’s Web service. It will use a requester agent to exchange messages with the provider’s provider agent. “Requester” is also used as a shorthand to refer to the requester agent acting on the requester’s behalf.

entries.title: required
entries.summaryMd: As applied to an implementation specification (see implementation specification, above), indicating an implementation specification that a covered entity must implement. All implementation specifications are either required or addressable (see “addressable” above).

senses.definitionMd: As applied to an implementation specification (see implementation specification, above), indicating an implementation specification that a covered entity must implement. All implementation specifications are either required or addressable (see “addressable” above).

entries.title: requirement
entries.summaryMd: Statement that translates or expresses a need and its associated constraints and conditions.

senses.definitionMd: Statement that translates or expresses a need and its associated constraints and conditions.

entries.title: requirements engineering
entries.summaryMd: An interdisciplinary function that mediates between the domains of the acquirer and supplier to establish and maintain the requirements to be met by the system, software, or service of interest.

senses.definitionMd: An interdisciplinary function that mediates between the domains of the acquirer and supplier to establish and maintain the requirements to be met by the system, software, or service of interest.

entries.title: reserve keying material
entries.summaryMd: Key held to satisfy unplanned needs.

senses.definitionMd: Key held to satisfy unplanned needs.

entries.title: resident alien
entries.summaryMd: A citizen of a foreign nation, legally residing in the United States on a permanent basis, who is not yet a naturalized citizen of the United States.

senses.definitionMd: A citizen of a foreign nation, legally residing in the United States on a permanent basis, who is not yet a naturalized citizen of the United States.

entries.title: residual information protection
entries.summaryMd: Ensur(ing) that any data contained in a resource is not available when the resource is de-allocated from one object and reallocated to a different object.

senses.definitionMd: Ensur(ing) that any data contained in a resource is not available when the resource is de-allocated from one object and reallocated to a different object.

entries.title: residual risk
entries.summaryMd: Portion of risk remaining after security measures have been applied.

senses.definitionMd: Portion of risk remaining after security measures have been applied.

entries.title: residue
entries.summaryMd: Data left in storage after information processing operations are complete, but before degaussing or overwriting has taken place.

senses.definitionMd: Data left in storage after information processing operations are complete, but before degaussing or overwriting has taken place.

entries.title: resilience
entries.summaryMd: The ability to maintain required capability in the face of adversity.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to maintain required capability in the face of adversity.

entries.title: Resilience Requirements
entries.summaryMd: The business-driven availability and reliability characteristics for the manufacturing system that specify recovery tolerances from disruptions and major incidents.

senses.definitionMd: The business-driven availability and reliability characteristics for the manufacturing system that specify recovery tolerances from disruptions and major incidents.

entries.title: resilient otherwise
entries.summaryMd: Security considerations applied to enable system operation despite disruption while not maintaining a secure mode, state, or transition; or only being able to provide for partial security within a given system mode, state, or transition.

senses.definitionMd: Security considerations applied to enable system operation despite disruption while not maintaining a secure mode, state, or transition; or only being able to provide for partial security within a given system mode, state, or transition.

entries.title: resolution
entries.summaryMd: The process of collecting information about an applicant to uniquely distinguish an individual within the context of the population that the CSP serves.

senses.definitionMd: The process of collecting information about an applicant to uniquely distinguish an individual within the context of the population that the CSP serves.

entries.title: Resolver
entries.summaryMd: Software that retrieves data associated with some identifier.

senses.definitionMd: Software that retrieves data associated with some identifier.

entries.title: resource
entries.summaryMd: Passive system-related entity, including bits, bytes, words, fields, devices, files, records, programs, tables, processes, programs, segments, directories, processors, and domains that contain or receive information. Access to an object (by a subject) implies access to the information it contains. Note: Sometimes referred to as "resource."

senses.definitionMd: Passive system-related entity, including bits, bytes, words, fields, devices, files, records, programs, tables, processes, programs, segments, directories, processors, and domains that contain or receive information. Access to an object (by a subject) implies access to the information it contains. Note: Sometimes referred to as "resource."

entries.title: Resource allocation
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism for limiting how much of a host’s resources a given container can consume.

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism for limiting how much of a host’s resources a given container can consume.

entries.title: resource control
entries.summaryMd: A capability in which an attacker controls one or more external resources consumed by a machine learning model at inference time, particularly for GenAI systems such as retrieval-augmented generation applications.

senses.definitionMd: A capability in which an attacker controls one or more external resources consumed by a machine learning model at inference time, particularly for GenAI systems such as retrieval-augmented generation applications.

entries.title: Resource pooling
entries.summaryMd: The provider’s computing resources are pooled to serve multiple consumers using a multi-tenant model, with different physical and virtual resources dynamically assigned and reassigned according to consumer demand. There is a sense of location independence in that the customer generally has no control or knowledge over the exact location of the provided resources but may be able to specify location at a higher level of abstraction (e.g., country, state, or datacenter). Examples of resources include storage, processing, memory, and network bandwidth.

senses.definitionMd: The provider’s computing resources are pooled to serve multiple consumers using a multi-tenant model, with different physical and virtual resources dynamically assigned and reassigned according to consumer demand. There is a sense of location independence in that the customer generally has no control or knowledge over the exact location of the provided resources but may be able to specify location at a higher level of abstraction (e.g., country, state, or datacenter). Examples of resources include storage, processing, memory, and network bandwidth.

entries.title: Resource Public Key Infrastructure
entries.summaryMd: The Resource Public Key Infrastructure is a framework aimed to secure the Internet’s routing infrastructure, in particular the routing information such as the IP address prefix and Originator mapping embedded in the BGP protocol. It provides certificates that are used to verify if the originating AS is permitted to publish the embedded IP address prefix(es).

senses.definitionMd: The Resource Public Key Infrastructure is a framework aimed to secure the Internet’s routing infrastructure, in particular the routing information such as the IP address prefix and Originator mapping embedded in the BGP protocol. It provides certificates that are used to verify if the originating AS is permitted to publish the embedded IP address prefix(es).

entries.title: respond (CSF function)
entries.summaryMd: Develop and implement the appropriate activities to take action regarding a detected cybersecurity event.

senses.definitionMd: Develop and implement the appropriate activities to take action regarding a detected cybersecurity event.

entries.title: responsibility to provide
entries.summaryMd: An information distribution approach whereby relevant essential information is made readily available and discoverable to the broadest possible pool of potential users.

senses.definitionMd: An information distribution approach whereby relevant essential information is made readily available and discoverable to the broadest possible pool of potential users.

entries.title: restoration
entries.summaryMd: The process of changing the status of a suspended (i.e., temporarily invalid) certificate to valid.

senses.definitionMd: The process of changing the status of a suspended (i.e., temporarily invalid) certificate to valid.

entries.title: restricted authenticator
entries.summaryMd: An authenticator type, class, or instantiation that has additional risk of false acceptance associated with its use and is therefore subject to additional requirements.

senses.definitionMd: An authenticator type, class, or instantiation that has additional risk of false acceptance associated with its use and is therefore subject to additional requirements.

entries.title: restricted data
entries.summaryMd: All data concerning (i) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (ii) the production of special nuclear material; or (iii) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to Section 142 [of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954].

senses.definitionMd: All data concerning (i) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (ii) the production of special nuclear material; or (iii) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to Section 142 [of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954].

entries.title: Result content
entries.summaryMd: Part or all of one or more SCAP result data streams.

senses.definitionMd: Part or all of one or more SCAP result data streams.

entries.title: results
entries.summaryMd: All data acquired from using a questionnaire, such as the answers to individual questions and the final result for the entire questionnaire.

senses.definitionMd: All data acquired from using a questionnaire, such as the answers to individual questions and the final result for the entire questionnaire.

entries.title: Retention period
entries.summaryMd: The minimum amount of time that a key or other cryptographically related information should be retained.

senses.definitionMd: The minimum amount of time that a key or other cryptographically related information should be retained.

entries.title: retirement
entries.summaryMd: Withdrawal of active support by the operation and maintenance organization, partial or total replacement by a new system, or installation of an upgraded system.

senses.definitionMd: Withdrawal of active support by the operation and maintenance organization, partial or total replacement by a new system, or installation of an upgraded system.

entries.title: retrieval-augmented generation
entries.summaryMd: A type of GenAI system in which a model is paired with a separate information retrieval system (or ”knowledge base”). Based on a user query, the RAG system identifies relevant information within the knowledge base and provides it to the GenAI model in context for the model to use in formu­lating its response. RAG systems allow the internal knowledge of a GenAI model to be modified without the need for retraining.

senses.definitionMd: A type of GenAI system in which a model is paired with a separate information retrieval system (or ”knowledge base”). Based on a user query, the RAG system identifies relevant information within the knowledge base and provides it to the GenAI model in context for the model to use in formu­lating its response. RAG systems allow the internal knowledge of a GenAI model to be modified without the need for retraining.

entries.title: Reverse Channel
entries.summaryMd: See back channel

senses.definitionMd: See back channel

entries.title: Review Status
entries.summaryMd: The status of the checklist within the internal NCP review process. Possible status options are: Candidate, Final, Archived, or Under Review. A status of "Final" signifies that NCP has reviewed the checklist and has accepted it for publication within the program.

senses.definitionMd: The status of the checklist within the internal NCP review process. Possible status options are: Candidate, Final, Archived, or Under Review. A status of "Final" signifies that NCP has reviewed the checklist and has accepted it for publication within the program.

entries.title: Review Techniques
entries.summaryMd: Passive information security testing techniques, generally conducted manually, that are used to evaluate systems, applications, networks, policies, and procedures to discover vulnerabilities. They include documentation, log, ruleset, and system configuration review; network sniffing; and file integrity checking.

senses.definitionMd: Passive information security testing techniques, generally conducted manually, that are used to evaluate systems, applications, networks, policies, and procedures to discover vulnerabilities. They include documentation, log, ruleset, and system configuration review; network sniffing; and file integrity checking.

entries.title: revocation
entries.summaryMd: The process of permanently ending the binding between a certificate and the identity asserted in the certificate from a specified time forward.

senses.definitionMd: The process of permanently ending the binding between a certificate and the identity asserted in the certificate from a specified time forward.

entries.title: Revoked key notification (RKN)
entries.summaryMd: A report (e.g., a list) of one or more keys that have been revoked and the date(s) of revocation, possibly along with the reason for their revocation. Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs) and Compromised Key Lists (CKLs) are examples of RKNs, along with Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) responses (see RFC 6960).

senses.definitionMd: See Incentive Mechanism

entries.title: RF Subsystem
entries.summaryMd: The portion of the RFID system that uses radio frequencies to perform identification and related transactions. The RF subsystem consists of two components: a reader and a tag.

senses.definitionMd: The portion of the RFID system that uses radio frequencies to perform identification and related transactions. The RF subsystem consists of two components: a reader and a tag.

entries.title: rightmost (V, a)
entries.summaryMd: The rightmost a bits of V.

senses.definitionMd: The rightmost a bits of V.

entries.title: Rijndael
entries.summaryMd: The block cipher that NIST selected as the winner of the AES competition.

senses.definitionMd: The block cipher that NIST selected as the winner of the AES competition.

entries.title: RIPE NCC
aliases: Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre
entries.summaryMd: Regional Internet Registry for Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Central Asia that allocates and registers blocks of Internet number resources to Internet service providers (ISPs) and other organizations.

senses.definitionMd: Regional Internet Registry for Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Central Asia that allocates and registers blocks of Internet number resources to Internet service providers (ISPs) and other organizations.

entries.title: risk
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the extent to which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance or event, and typically a function of: (i) the adverse impacts that would arise if the circumstance or event occurs; and (ii) the likelihood of occurrence. [Note: Information system-related security risks are those risks that arise from the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or information systems and reflect the potential adverse impacts to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation. Adverse impacts to the Nation include, for example, compromises to information systems that support critical infrastructure applications or are paramount to government continuity of operations as defined by the Department of Homeland Security.]

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the extent to which an entity is threatened by a potential circumstance or event, and typically a function of: (i) the adverse impacts that would arise if the circumstance or event occurs; and (ii) the likelihood of occurrence. [Note: Information system-related security risks are those risks that arise from the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or information systems and reflect the potential adverse impacts to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation. Adverse impacts to the Nation include, for example, compromises to information systems that support critical infrastructure applications or are paramount to government continuity of operations as defined by the Department of Homeland Security.]

entries.title: Risk Adaptive (Adaptable) Access Control
entries.summaryMd: In RAdAC, access privileges are granted based on a combination of a user’s identity, mission need, and the level of security risk that exists between the system being accessed and a user.
