RAdAC will use security metrics, such as the strength of the authentication method, the level of assurance of the session connection between the system and a user, and the physical location of a user, to make its risk determination.

senses.definitionMd: In RAdAC, access privileges are granted based on a combination of a user’s identity, mission need, and the level of security risk that exists between the system being accessed and a user. RAdAC will use security metrics, such as the strength of the authentication method, the level of assurance of the session connection between the system and a user, and the physical location of a user, to make its risk determination.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Risk Adaptive (Adaptable) Access Control"

entries.title: risk aggregation
entries.summaryMd: The combination of several risks into one risk to develop a more complete understanding of the overall risk.

senses.definitionMd: The combination of several risks into one risk to develop a more complete understanding of the overall risk.

entries.title: risk analysis
entries.summaryMd: Process to comprehend the nature of risk and to determine the level of risk.

senses.definitionMd: Process to comprehend the nature of risk and to determine the level of risk.

entries.title: Risk Appetite
entries.summaryMd: The types and amount of risk, on a broad level, [an organization] is willing to accept in its pursuit of value.

senses.definitionMd: The types and amount of risk, on a broad level, [an organization] is willing to accept in its pursuit of value.

entries.title: risk assessment
entries.summaryMd: The process of identifying risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, resulting from the operation of an information system. Part of risk management, incorporates threat and vulnerability analyses, and considers mitigations provided by security controls planned or in place. Synonymous with risk analysis.

senses.definitionMd: The process of identifying risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, resulting from the operation of an information system. Part of risk management, incorporates threat and vulnerability analyses, and considers mitigations provided by security controls planned or in place. Synonymous with risk analysis.

entries.title: Risk Assessment Methodology
entries.summaryMd: A risk assessment process, together with a risk model, assessment approach, and analysis approach.

senses.definitionMd: A risk assessment process, together with a risk model, assessment approach, and analysis approach.

entries.title: risk assessment report (RAR)
entries.summaryMd: The report which contains the results of performing a risk assessment or the formal output from the process of assessing risk.

senses.definitionMd: The report which contains the results of performing a risk assessment or the formal output from the process of assessing risk.

entries.title: risk assessor
entries.summaryMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a risk assessment.

senses.definitionMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a risk assessment.

entries.title: risk criteria
entries.summaryMd: Terms of reference against which the significance of a risk is evaluated.

senses.definitionMd: Terms of reference against which the significance of a risk is evaluated.

entries.title: Risk Detail Report
entries.summaryMd: A report listing detailed risk scenario information supporting the contents of a risk register entry including, but not limited to, risk history information, risk analysis data, and information about individual and organizational accountability.

senses.definitionMd: A report listing detailed risk scenario information supporting the contents of a risk register entry including, but not limited to, risk history information, risk analysis data, and information about individual and organizational accountability.

entries.title: risk elevation
entries.summaryMd: The process of transferring the decisions on risk response to a more senior stakeholder when the factors involved (e.g., a regulatory compliance risk) are particularly sensitive or critical. For example, enterprise risk strategy might direct that any risk with more than $1 million exposure or risks related to a particularly important business application must be managed at a more senior level.

senses.definitionMd: The process of transferring the decisions on risk response to a more senior stakeholder when the factors involved (e.g., a regulatory compliance risk) are particularly sensitive or critical. For example, enterprise risk strategy might direct that any risk with more than $1 million exposure or risks related to a particularly important business application must be managed at a more senior level.

entries.title: risk escalation
entries.summaryMd: Occurs when a particular threshold is reached, either based on a time frame or some other risk condition, thus requiring a higher level of attention. For example, a risk that has remained through more than two fiscal periods without adequate treatment might be flagged for additional scrutiny. Another condition for escalation might occur if, during risk monitoring, conditions indicate that the risk exposure rating will significantly exceed the initial estimates.

senses.definitionMd: Occurs when a particular threshold is reached, either based on a time frame or some other risk condition, thus requiring a higher level of attention. For example, a risk that has remained through more than two fiscal periods without adequate treatment might be flagged for additional scrutiny. Another condition for escalation might occur if, during risk monitoring, conditions indicate that the risk exposure rating will significantly exceed the initial estimates.

entries.title: risk evaluation
entries.summaryMd: Process of comparing the results of risk analysis with risk criteria to determine whether the risk and/or its magnitude is/are acceptable or tolerable.

senses.definitionMd: Process of comparing the results of risk analysis with risk criteria to determine whether the risk and/or its magnitude is/are acceptable or tolerable.

entries.title: risk executive (function)
entries.summaryMd: An individual or group within an organization that helps to ensure that: (i) security risk-related considerations for individual information systems, to include the authorization decisions for those systems, are viewed from an organization-wide perspective with regard to the overall strategic goals and objectives of the organization in carrying out its missions and business functions; and (ii) managing risk from individual information systems is consistent across the organization, reflects organizational risk tolerance, and is considered along with other organizational risks affecting mission/business success.

senses.definitionMd: An individual or group within an organization that helps to ensure that: (i) security risk-related considerations for individual information systems, to include the authorization decisions for those systems, are viewed from an organization-wide perspective with regard to the overall strategic goals and objectives of the organization in carrying out its missions and business functions; and (ii) managing risk from individual information systems is consistent across the organization, reflects organizational risk tolerance, and is considered along with other organizational risks affecting mission/business success.

entries.title: risk factor
entries.summaryMd: A characteristic used in a risk model as an input to determining the level of risk in a risk assessment.

senses.definitionMd: A characteristic used in a risk model as an input to determining the level of risk in a risk assessment.

entries.title: risk framing
entries.summaryMd: The set of assumptions, constraints, risk tolerances, and priorities/trade-offs that shape an organization’s approach for managing risk

senses.definitionMd: The set of assumptions, constraints, risk tolerances, and priorities/trade-offs that shape an organization’s approach for managing risk

entries.title: risk governance
entries.summaryMd: The process by which risk management evaluation, decisions, and actions are connected to enterprise strategy and objectives. Risk governance provides the transparency, responsibility, and accountability that enables managers to acceptably manage risk.

senses.definitionMd: The process by which risk management evaluation, decisions, and actions are connected to enterprise strategy and objectives. Risk governance provides the transparency, responsibility, and accountability that enables managers to acceptably manage risk.

entries.title: risk identification
entries.summaryMd: Process of finding, recognizing, and describing risks.

senses.definitionMd: Process of finding, recognizing, and describing risks.

entries.title: risk management
entries.summaryMd: The process of managing risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, or individuals resulting from the operation of an information system, and includes: (i) the conduct of a risk assessment; (ii) the implementation of a risk mitigation strategy; and (iii) employment of techniques and procedures for the continuous monitoring of the security state of the information system.

senses.definitionMd: The process of managing risks to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, or individuals resulting from the operation of an information system, and includes: (i) the conduct of a risk assessment; (ii) the implementation of a risk mitigation strategy; and (iii) employment of techniques and procedures for the continuous monitoring of the security state of the information system.

entries.title: risk management framework (RMF)
entries.summaryMd: A disciplined and structured process that integrates information security, privacy, and risk management activities into the system development life cycle (SDLC).

senses.definitionMd: A disciplined and structured process that integrates information security, privacy, and risk management activities into the system development life cycle (SDLC).

entries.title: Risk Management Framework (RMF) step
entries.summaryMd: A reference to one of the 6 steps in the Risk Management Framework process defined in SP 800-37.

senses.definitionMd: A reference to one of the 6 steps in the Risk Management Framework process defined in SP 800-37.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Risk Management Framework (RMF) step"

entries.title: risk management level
entries.summaryMd: One of three organizational levels defined in NIST SP 800-39: Level 1 (organizational level), Level 2 (mission/business process level), or Level 3(system level).

senses.definitionMd: One of three organizational levels defined in NIST SP 800-39: Level 1 (organizational level), Level 2 (mission/business process level), or Level 3(system level).

entries.title: risk management strategy
entries.summaryMd: Strategy that addresses how organizations intend to assess risk, respond to risk, and monitor risk—making explicit and transparent the risk perceptions that organizations routinely use in making both investment and operational decisions.

senses.definitionMd: Strategy that addresses how organizations intend to assess risk, respond to risk, and monitor risk—making explicit and transparent the risk perceptions that organizations routinely use in making both investment and operational decisions.

entries.title: risk mitigation
entries.summaryMd: Prioritizing, evaluating, and implementing the appropriate risk-reducing controls/countermeasures recommended from the risk management process.

senses.definitionMd: Prioritizing, evaluating, and implementing the appropriate risk-reducing controls/countermeasures recommended from the risk management process.

entries.title: risk model
entries.summaryMd: A key component of a risk assessment methodology (in addition to assessment approach and analysis approach) that defines key terms and assessable risk factors.

senses.definitionMd: A key component of a risk assessment methodology (in addition to assessment approach and analysis approach) that defines key terms and assessable risk factors.

entries.title: risk optimization
entries.summaryMd: A risk-related process to minimize negative and maximize positive consequences and their respective probabilities; risk optimization depends on risk criteria, including costs and legal requirements.

senses.definitionMd: A risk-related process to minimize negative and maximize positive consequences and their respective probabilities; risk optimization depends on risk criteria, including costs and legal requirements.

entries.title: Risk Profile
entries.summaryMd: A prioritized inventory of the most significant risks identified and assessed through the risk assessment process versus a complete inventory of risks.

senses.definitionMd: A prioritized inventory of the most significant risks identified and assessed through the risk assessment process versus a complete inventory of risks.

entries.title: Risk Register
entries.summaryMd: A repository of risk information including the data understood about risks over time.

senses.definitionMd: A repository of risk information including the data understood about risks over time.

entries.title: Risk Reserve
entries.summaryMd: A types of management reserve where funding or labor hours are set aside and employed if a risk is triggered to ensure the opportunity is realized or threat is avoided.

senses.definitionMd: A types of management reserve where funding or labor hours are set aside and employed if a risk is triggered to ensure the opportunity is realized or threat is avoided.

entries.title: risk response
entries.summaryMd: Accepting, avoiding, mitigating, sharing, or transferring risk to organizational operations (mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.

senses.definitionMd: Accepting, avoiding, mitigating, sharing, or transferring risk to organizational operations (mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.

entries.title: Risk Response Measure
entries.summaryMd: A specific action taken to respond to an identified risk.

senses.definitionMd: A specific action taken to respond to an identified risk.

entries.title: risk response plan
entries.summaryMd: A summary of potential consequence(s) of the successful exploitation of a specific vulnerability or vulnerabilities by a threat agent, as well as mitigating strategies and C-SCRM controls.

senses.definitionMd: A summary of potential consequence(s) of the successful exploitation of a specific vulnerability or vulnerabilities by a threat agent, as well as mitigating strategies and C-SCRM controls.

entries.title: risk tolerance
entries.summaryMd: The level of risk an entity is willing to assume in order to achieve a potential desired result.

senses.definitionMd: The level of risk an entity is willing to assume in order to achieve a potential desired result.

entries.title: risk treatment
entries.summaryMd: Process to modify risk.

senses.definitionMd: Process to modify risk.

entries.title: Rivest-Shamir-Adleman
entries.summaryMd: Algorithm developed by Rivest, Shamir and Adelman (allowed in FIPS 186-3 and specified in ANS X9.31 and PKCS #1).

senses.definitionMd: Algorithm developed by Rivest, Shamir and Adelman (allowed in FIPS 186-3 and specified in ANS X9.31 and PKCS #1).

entries.title: robustness
entries.summaryMd: The ability of a CS entity to operate correctly and reliably across a wide range of operational conditions, and to fail gracefully outside of that operational range.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of a CS entity to operate correctly and reliably across a wide range of operational conditions, and to fail gracefully outside of that operational range.

entries.title: Rogue Device
entries.summaryMd: An unauthorized node on a network.

senses.definitionMd: An unauthorized node on a network.

entries.title: role
entries.summaryMd: Predefined set of rules establishing the allowed interactions between a user and a system.

senses.definitionMd: Predefined set of rules establishing the allowed interactions between a user and a system.

entries.title: role-based access control (RBAC)
entries.summaryMd: Access control based on user roles (i.e., a collection of access authorizations a user receives based on an explicit or implicit assumption of a given role). Role permissions may be inherited through a role hierarchy and typically reflect the permissions needed to perform defined functions within an organization. A given role may apply to a single individual or to several individuals.

senses.definitionMd: Access control based on user roles (i.e., a collection of access authorizations a user receives based on an explicit or implicit assumption of a given role). Role permissions may be inherited through a role hierarchy and typically reflect the permissions needed to perform defined functions within an organization. A given role may apply to a single individual or to several individuals.

entries.title: Role-based authentication
entries.summaryMd: A process that provides assurance of an entity’s role by means of an authentication mechanism that verifies the role of the entity. Contrast with identity-based authentication

senses.definitionMd: A process that provides assurance of an entity’s role by means of an authentication mechanism that verifies the role of the entity. Contrast with identity-based authentication

entries.title: role-based training
entries.summaryMd: A multi-step process in the learning program that begins with defining the significant cybersecurity or privacy work roles in the organization and identifying the personnel aligned to those designated work roles. Learning materials are then assigned, acquired, or developed based on the tasks necessary to perform the work role. (See the NICE Framework for “work role.”)

senses.definitionMd: A multi-step process in the learning program that begins with defining the significant cybersecurity or privacy work roles in the organization and identifying the personnel aligned to those designated work roles. Learning materials are then assigned, acquired, or developed based on the tasks necessary to perform the work role. (See the NICE Framework for “work role.”)

entries.title: Rollup
entries.summaryMd: A scheme that enables the off-chain processing of transactions by one or more operators with on-chain state update commitments that contain “compressed” per-transaction data.

senses.definitionMd: A scheme that enables the off-chain processing of transactions by one or more operators with on-chain state update commitments that contain “compressed” per-transaction data.

entries.title: Root Cause Analysis
entries.summaryMd: A principle-based, systems approach for the identification of underlying causes associated with a particular set of risks.

senses.definitionMd: A principle-based, systems approach for the identification of underlying causes associated with a particular set of risks.

entries.title: Root Certificate
entries.summaryMd: A self-signed certificate, as defined by IETF RFC 5280, issued by a root CA. A root certificate is typically securely installed on systems so they can verify end-entity certificates they receive.

senses.definitionMd: A self-signed certificate, as defined by IETF RFC 5280, issued by a root CA. A root certificate is typically securely installed on systems so they can verify end-entity certificates they receive.

entries.title: Root Certificate Authority (CA)
entries.summaryMd: In a hierarchical public key infrastructure (PKI), the certification authority (CA) whose public key serves as the most trusted datum (i.e., the beginning of trust paths) for a security domain.

senses.definitionMd: In a hierarchical public key infrastructure (PKI), the certification authority (CA) whose public key serves as the most trusted datum (i.e., the beginning of trust paths) for a security domain.

entries.title: root user
entries.summaryMd: A user that is authorized (and therefore, trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform.

senses.definitionMd: A user that is authorized (and therefore, trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform.

entries.title: rootkit
entries.summaryMd: A set of tools used by an attacker after gaining root-level access to a host to conceal the attacker's activities on the host and permit the attacker to maintain root- level access to the host through covert means.

senses.definitionMd: A set of tools used by an attacker after gaining root-level access to a host to conceal the attacker's activities on the host and permit the attacker to maintain root- level access to the host through covert means.

entries.title: roots of trust
entries.summaryMd: Highly reliable hardware, firmware, and software components that perform specific, critical security functions. Because roots of trust are inherently trusted, they must be secure by design. Roots of trust provide a firm foundation from which to build security and trust.

senses.definitionMd: Highly reliable hardware, firmware, and software components that perform specific, critical security functions. Because roots of trust are inherently trusted, they must be secure by design. Roots of trust provide a firm foundation from which to build security and trust.

entries.title: Rotate
entries.summaryMd: The process of renewing a certificate in conjunction with a rekey, followed by the process of replacing the existing certificate with the new certificate.

senses.definitionMd: The process of renewing a certificate in conjunction with a rekey, followed by the process of replacing the existing certificate with the new certificate.

entries.title: Round
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of transformations of the state that is iterated \(Nr\)

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of transformations of the state that is iterated \(Nr\)

entries.title: Round key
entries.summaryMd: One of the \(Nr+1\)

senses.definitionMd: One of the \(Nr+1\)

entries.title: Round robin consensus model
entries.summaryMd: A consensus model for permissioned blockchain networks where nodes are pseudo-randomly selected to create blocks, but a node must wait several block-creation cycles before being chosen again to add another new block. This model ensures that no one participant creates the majority of the blocks, and it benefits from a straightforward approach, lacking cryptographic puzzles, and having low power requirements.

senses.definitionMd: A consensus model for permissioned blockchain networks where nodes are pseudo-randomly selected to create blocks, but a node must wait several block-creation cycles before being chosen again to add another new block. This model ensures that no one participant creates the majority of the blocks, and it benefits from a straightforward approach, lacking cryptographic puzzles, and having low power requirements.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Round robin consensus model"

entries.title: Route Origin Attestation
entries.summaryMd: A Route Origin Attestation is a cryptographically verifiable attestation that a given Internet prefix can be announced by an AS listed within the attestation.

senses.definitionMd: A Route Origin Attestation is a cryptographically verifiable attestation that a given Internet prefix can be announced by an AS listed within the attestation.

entries.title: router
entries.summaryMd: A computer that is a gateway between two networks at OSI layer 3 and that relays and directs data packets through that inter-network. The most common form of router operates on IP packets.

senses.definitionMd: A computer that is a gateway between two networks at OSI layer 3 and that relays and directs data packets through that inter-network. The most common form of router operates on IP packets.

entries.title: rowhammer attack
entries.summaryMd: A software-based fault-injection attack that exploits dynamic random-access memory disturbance errors via user-space applications and allows the at­tacker to infer information about certain victim secrets stored in memory cells. Mounting this attack requires the attacker to control a user-space unprivileged process that runs on the same machine as the victim’s machine learning model.

senses.definitionMd: A software-based fault-injection attack that exploits dynamic random-access memory disturbance errors via user-space applications and allows the at­tacker to infer information about certain victim secrets stored in memory cells. Mounting this attack requires the attacker to control a user-space unprivileged process that runs on the same machine as the victim’s machine learning model.

entries.title: RP subscriber account
entries.summaryMd: An account established and managed by the RP in a federated system based on the RP’s view of the subscriber account from the IdP. An RP subscriber account is associated with one or more federated identifiers and allows the subscriber to access the account through a federation transaction with the IdP.

senses.definitionMd: An account established and managed by the RP in a federated system based on the RP’s view of the subscriber account from the IdP. An RP subscriber account is associated with one or more federated identifiers and allows the subscriber to access the account through a federation transaction with the IdP.

entries.title: RPKI Validation Cache
entries.summaryMd: RPKI Validation Cache provides Validated ROA Payload (VRP) and public router keys.

senses.definitionMd: RPKI Validation Cache provides Validated ROA Payload (VRP) and public router keys.

entries.title: Rule
entries.summaryMd: An element that holds check references and may also hold remediation information.

senses.definitionMd: An element that holds check references and may also hold remediation information.

entries.title: Rule-Based Event Correlation
entries.summaryMd: Correlating events by matching multiple log entries from a single source or multiple sources based on logged values, such as timestamps, IP addresses, and event types.

senses.definitionMd: Correlating events by matching multiple log entries from a single source or multiple sources based on logged values, such as timestamps, IP addresses, and event types.

entries.title: rule-based security policy
entries.summaryMd: A security policy based on global rules imposed for all subjects. These rules usually rely on a comparison of the sensitivity of the objects being accessed and the possession of corresponding attributes by the subjects requesting access. Also known as discretionary access control (DAC).

senses.definitionMd: A security policy based on global rules imposed for all subjects. These rules usually rely on a comparison of the sensitivity of the objects being accessed and the possession of corresponding attributes by the subjects requesting access. Also known as discretionary access control (DAC).

entries.title: Rules of Engagement (ROE)
entries.summaryMd: Detailed guidelines and constraints regarding the execution of information security testing. The ROE is established before the start of a security test, and gives the test team authority to conduct defined activities without the need for additional permissions.

senses.definitionMd: Detailed guidelines and constraints regarding the execution of information security testing. The ROE is established before the start of a security test, and gives the test team authority to conduct defined activities without the need for additional permissions.

entries.title: ruleset
entries.summaryMd: A table of instructions used by a controlled interface to determine what data is allowable and how the data is handled between interconnected systems.

senses.definitionMd: A table of instructions used by a controlled interface to determine what data is allowable and how the data is handled between interconnected systems.

entries.title: Run
entries.summaryMd: An uninterrupted sequence of like bits (i.e., either all zeroes or all ones).

senses.definitionMd: An uninterrupted sequence of like bits (i.e., either all zeroes or all ones).

entries.title: Run (of output sequences)
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of identical values.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of identical values.

entries.title: Runs Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of the runs test is to determine whether the number of runs of ones and zeros of various lengths is as expected for a random sequence. In particular, this test determines whether the oscillation between such substrings is too fast or too slow.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of the runs test is to determine whether the number of runs of ones and zeros of various lengths is as expected for a random sequence. In particular, this test determines whether the oscillation between such substrings is too fast or too slow.

entries.title: runtime
entries.summaryMd: The period during which a computer program is executing.

senses.definitionMd: The period during which a computer program is executing.

entries.title: rv
entries.summaryMd: The random value that is combined with the message Ms to produce the randomized message M.

senses.definitionMd: The random value that is combined with the message Ms to produce the randomized message M.

entries.title: rv[0…b]
entries.summaryMd: For bit string rv, rv[0…b] is a substring consisting of the leftmost b+1 bit(s) of rv, where b ≥ 0.

senses.definitionMd: For bit string rv, rv[0…b] is a substring consisting of the leftmost b+1 bit(s) of rv, where b ≥ 0.

entries.title: rv_length_indicator
entries.summaryMd: A 16-bit binary representation of the length (in bits) of rv.

senses.definitionMd: A 16-bit binary representation of the length (in bits) of rv.

entries.title: S
entries.summaryMd: The desired security strength for a digital signature.

senses.definitionMd: The desired security strength for a digital signature.

entries.title: S-box
entries.summaryMd: A non-linear substitution table used in SUBBYTES() and KEYEXPANSION() to perform a one-to-one substitution of a byte value.

senses.definitionMd: A non-linear substitution table used in SUBBYTES() and KEYEXPANSION() to perform a one-to-one substitution of a byte value.

entries.title: s2
entries.summaryMd: The variance of a random variable = (standard deviation)2.

senses.definitionMd: The variance of a random variable = (standard deviation)2.

entries.title: Safe Harbor
entries.summaryMd: Within the context of de-identification, refers to the Safe Harbor method for de-identifying protected health information in accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule.

senses.definitionMd: Within the context of de-identification, refers to the Safe Harbor method for de-identifying protected health information in accordance with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Privacy Rule.

entries.title: safeguards
entries.summaryMd: Actions, devices, procedures, techniques, or other measures that reduce the vulnerability of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Actions, devices, procedures, techniques, or other measures that reduce the vulnerability of an information system.

entries.title: safety
entries.summaryMd: Freedom from conditions that can cause death, injury, occupational illness, damage to or loss of equipment or property, or damage to the environment.

senses.definitionMd: Freedom from conditions that can cause death, injury, occupational illness, damage to or loss of equipment or property, or damage to the environment.

entries.title: safety instrumented system
entries.summaryMd: A system that is composed of sensors, logic solvers, and final control elements whose purpose is to take the process to a safe state when predetermined conditions are violated. Other terms commonly used include emergency shutdown system (ESS), safety shutdown system (SSD), and safety interlock system (SIS).

senses.definitionMd: A system that is composed of sensors, logic solvers, and final control elements whose purpose is to take the process to a safe state when predetermined conditions are violated. Other terms commonly used include emergency shutdown system (ESS), safety shutdown system (SSD), and safety interlock system (SIS).

entries.title: Safety Requirements
entries.summaryMd: AC properties, business requirements, specifications of expected/unexpected system security features, or directly translation of policy values. Safety requirements can also include privilege inheritance.

senses.definitionMd: AC properties, business requirements, specifications of expected/unexpected system security features, or directly translation of policy values. Safety requirements can also include privilege inheritance.

entries.title: salt
entries.summaryMd: A bit string generated during digital signature generation using the RSA Signature Scheme with Appendix - Probabilistic Signature Scheme (RSASSA-PSS RSA).

senses.definitionMd: A bit string generated during digital signature generation using the RSA Signature Scheme with Appendix - Probabilistic Signature Scheme (RSASSA-PSS RSA).

entries.title: Sample
entries.summaryMd: An observation of the raw data output by a noise source. Common examples of output values obtained by sampling are single bits, single bytes, etc. (The term “sample” is often extended to denote a sequence of such observations; this Recommendation will refrain from that practice.)

senses.definitionMd: An observation of the raw data output by a noise source. Common examples of output values obtained by sampling are single bits, single bytes, etc. (The term “sample” is often extended to denote a sequence of such observations; this Recommendation will refrain from that practice.)

entries.title: sampling
entries.summaryMd: The process of taking samples of something for the purpose of analysis.

senses.definitionMd: The process of taking samples of something for the purpose of analysis.

entries.title: Sandbox
entries.summaryMd: A system that allows an untrusted application to run in a highly controlled environment where the application’s permissions are restricted to an essential set of computer permissions. In particular, an application in a sandbox is usually restricted from accessing the file system or the network. A widely used example of applications running inside a sandbox is a Java applet.

senses.definitionMd: A system that allows an untrusted application to run in a highly controlled environment where the application’s permissions are restricted to an essential set of computer permissions. In particular, an application in a sandbox is usually restricted from accessing the file system or the network. A widely used example of applications running inside a sandbox is a Java applet.

entries.title: sanitization
entries.summaryMd: Process to remove information from media such that information recovery is not possible. It includes removing all labels, markings, and activity logs.

senses.definitionMd: Process to remove information from media such that information recovery is not possible. It includes removing all labels, markings, and activity logs.

entries.title: sanitization method
entries.summaryMd: Actions that can be taken to sanitize media, such as clear, purge, and destroy.

senses.definitionMd: Actions that can be taken to sanitize media, such as clear, purge, and destroy.

entries.title: sanitization technique
entries.summaryMd: A technology-specific approach associated with a sanitization method that can be used to sanitize a specific type of media.

senses.definitionMd: A technology-specific approach associated with a sanitization method that can be used to sanitize a specific type of media.

entries.title: sanitize
entries.summaryMd: The removal of extraneous or potentially harmful data (e.g., malware) within a file or other information container (e.g., network protocol packet).

senses.definitionMd: The removal of extraneous or potentially harmful data (e.g., malware) within a file or other information container (e.g., network protocol packet).

entries.title: satellite
entries.summaryMd: Bus and payload combined into one operational asset.

senses.definitionMd: Bus and payload combined into one operational asset.

entries.title: Satisfaction
entries.summaryMd: Freedom from discomfort, and positive attitudes towards the use of the product.

senses.definitionMd: Freedom from discomfort, and positive attitudes towards the use of the product.

entries.title: SC 37
entries.summaryMd: The Biometrics standardization subcommittee under ISO/IEC Joint Technical Committee

senses.definitionMd: The Biometrics standardization subcommittee under ISO/IEC Joint Technical Committee

entries.title: SCADA server
entries.summaryMd: The device that acts as the master in a SCADA system.

senses.definitionMd: The device that acts as the master in a SCADA system.

entries.title: Scalability
entries.summaryMd: The ability to support more users, concurrent sessions, and throughput than a single SSL VPN device can typically handle.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to support more users, concurrent sessions, and throughput than a single SSL VPN device can typically handle.

entries.title: Scalability testing
entries.summaryMd: Testing the ability of a system to handle an increasing amount of work correctly.

senses.definitionMd: Testing the ability of a system to handle an increasing amount of work correctly.

entries.title: scanning
entries.summaryMd: Sending packets or requests to another system to gain information to be used in a subsequent attack.

senses.definitionMd: Sending packets or requests to another system to gain information to be used in a subsequent attack.

entries.title: SCAP Capability
entries.summaryMd: A specific function or functions of a product as defined below: Authenticated Configuration Scanner: the capability to audit and assess a target system to determine its compliance with a defined set of configuration requirements using target system logon privileges. Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) Option: the capability to process and present CVEs correctly and completely. Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL) Option: the capability to process and present OCIL correctly and completely.

senses.definitionMd: A specific function or functions of a product as defined below: Authenticated Configuration Scanner: the capability to audit and assess a target system to determine its compliance with a defined set of configuration requirements using target system logon privileges. Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) Option: the capability to process and present CVEs correctly and completely. Open Checklist Interactive Language (OCIL) Option: the capability to process and present OCIL correctly and completely.

entries.title: SCAP component
entries.summaryMd: A logical unit of data expressed using one or more of the SCAP component specifications.

senses.definitionMd: A logical unit of data expressed using one or more of the SCAP component specifications.

entries.title: SCAP conformant
entries.summaryMd: A product or SCAP data stream that meets the requirements of this specification.

senses.definitionMd: A product or SCAP data stream that meets the requirements of this specification.

entries.title: SCAP content
entries.summaryMd: Part or all of one or more SCAP data streams.

senses.definitionMd: Part or all of one or more SCAP data streams.

entries.title: SCAP Content Checklist
entries.summaryMd: An automated checklist that adheres to the SCAP specification in NIST SP 800-126 for documenting security settings in machine-readable standardized SCAP formats.

senses.definitionMd: An automated checklist that adheres to the SCAP specification in NIST SP 800-126 for documenting security settings in machine-readable standardized SCAP formats.

entries.title: SCAP data stream
entries.summaryMd: A specific instantiation of SCAP content.

senses.definitionMd: A specific instantiation of SCAP content.

entries.title: SCAP data stream collection
entries.summaryMd: A container for SCAP data streams and components.

senses.definitionMd: A container for SCAP data streams and components.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "SCAP data stream collection"

entries.title: SCAP result data stream
entries.summaryMd: An SCAP data stream that holds output (result) content.

senses.definitionMd: An SCAP data stream that holds output (result) content.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "SCAP result data stream"

entries.title: SCAP Revision
entries.summaryMd: A version of the SCAP specification designated by a revision number in the format nn.nn.nn, where the first nn is the major revision number, the second nn number is the minor revision number, and the final nn number is the refinement number. A specific SCAP revision will populate all three fields, even if that means using zeros to show no minor revision or refinement number has been used to date. A leading zero will be used to pad single-digit revision or refinement numbers.

senses.definitionMd: A version of the SCAP specification designated by a revision number in the format nn.nn.nn, where the first nn is the major revision number, the second nn number is the minor revision number, and the final nn number is the refinement number. A specific SCAP revision will populate all three fields, even if that means using zeros to show no minor revision or refinement number has been used to date. A leading zero will be used to pad single-digit revision or refinement numbers.

entries.title: SCAP source data stream
entries.summaryMd: An SCAP data stream that holds input (source) content.

senses.definitionMd: An SCAP data stream that holds input (source) content.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "SCAP source data stream"

entries.title: SCAP source data stream collection
entries.summaryMd: A container for SCAP data streams and components.

senses.definitionMd: A container for SCAP data streams and components.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "SCAP source data stream collection"

entries.title: SCAP use case
entries.summaryMd: A pre-defined way in which a product can use SCAP. See Section 5 for the definitions of the SCAP use cases.

senses.definitionMd: A pre-defined way in which a product can use SCAP. See Section 5 for the definitions of the SCAP use cases.

entries.title: Scatternet
entries.summaryMd: A chain of piconets created by allowing one or more Bluetooth devices to each be a slave in one piconet and act as the master for another piconet simultaneously. A scatternet allows several devices to be networked over an extended distance.

senses.definitionMd: A chain of piconets created by allowing one or more Bluetooth devices to each be a slave in one piconet and act as the master for another piconet simultaneously. A scatternet allows several devices to be networked over an extended distance.

entries.title: scavenging
entries.summaryMd: Searching through object residue to acquire data.

senses.definitionMd: Searching through object residue to acquire data.

entries.title: Scenario
entries.summaryMd: A sequential, narrative account of a hypothetical incident that provides the catalyst for the exercise and is intended to introduce situations that will inspire responses and thus allow demonstration of the exercise objectives.

senses.definitionMd: A sequential, narrative account of a hypothetical incident that provides the catalyst for the exercise and is intended to introduce situations that will inspire responses and thus allow demonstration of the exercise objectives.

entries.title: Scenario Test
entries.summaryMd: Scenario testing is intended to mimic an operational application and simultaneously institute controls on the procedures. Scenario testing requires members of a human test population to transact with biometric sensors. Scenario tests are appropriate for capturing and assessing the effects of interactions human users have with biometric sensors and interfaces.

senses.definitionMd: Scenario testing is intended to mimic an operational application and simultaneously institute controls on the procedures. Scenario testing requires members of a human test population to transact with biometric sensors. Scenario tests are appropriate for capturing and assessing the effects of interactions human users have with biometric sensors and interfaces.

entries.title: scheduled data transfer
entries.summaryMd: A connection used to transfer data on a regular, recurring basis.

senses.definitionMd: A connection used to transfer data on a regular, recurring basis.

entries.title: Scheme
entries.summaryMd: A set of unambiguously specified transformations that provide a (cryptographic) service when properly implemented and maintained. A scheme is a higher-level construct than a primitive and a lower-level construct than a protocol.

senses.definitionMd: A set of unambiguously specified transformations that provide a (cryptographic) service when properly implemented and maintained. A scheme is a higher-level construct than a primitive and a lower-level construct than a protocol.

entries.title: Scheme Owner
entries.summaryMd: Person or organization responsible for the development and maintenance of a conformity assessment system or conformity assessment scheme.

senses.definitionMd: Person or organization responsible for the development and maintenance of a conformity assessment system or conformity assessment scheme.

entries.title: scoping considerations
entries.summaryMd: A part of tailoring guidance providing organizations with specific considerations on the applicability and implementation of security controls in the security control baseline. Areas of consideration include policy/regulatory, technology, physical infrastructure, system component allocation, operational/environmental, public access, scalability, common control, and security objective.

senses.definitionMd: A part of tailoring guidance providing organizations with specific considerations on the applicability and implementation of security controls in the security control baseline. Areas of consideration include policy/regulatory, technology, physical infrastructure, system component allocation, operational/environmental, public access, scalability, common control, and security objective.

entries.title: Script
entries.summaryMd: A sequence of instructions, ranging from a simple list of operating system commands to full-blown programming language statements, which can be executed automatically by an interpreter.

senses.definitionMd: A sequence of instructions, ranging from a simple list of operating system commands to full-blown programming language statements, which can be executed automatically by an interpreter.

entries.title: Scripting Language
entries.summaryMd: A definition of the syntax and semantics for writing and interpreting scripts.

senses.definitionMd: A definition of the syntax and semantics for writing and interpreting scripts.

entries.title: seal of approval
entries.summaryMd: A single label indicating a product has met a baseline standard.

senses.definitionMd: A single label indicating a product has met a baseline standard.

entries.title: Second byte of a two-byte status word
entries.summaryMd: Second byte of a two-byte status word

senses.definitionMd: Second byte of a two-byte status word

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Second byte of a two-byte status word"

entries.title: Second preimage
entries.summaryMd: A message Ms’, that is different from a given message Ms , such that its message digest is the same as the known message digest of Ms.

senses.definitionMd: A message Ms’, that is different from a given message Ms , such that its message digest is the same as the known message digest of Ms.

entries.title: Second preimage resistance
entries.summaryMd: An expected property of a cryptographic hash function whereby it is computationally infeasible to find a second preimage of a known message digest, See “Second preimage”.

senses.definitionMd: An expected property of a cryptographic hash function whereby it is computationally infeasible to find a second preimage of a known message digest, See “Second preimage”.

entries.title: Secondary market
entries.summaryMd: An unofficial, unauthorized, or unintended distribution channel.

senses.definitionMd: An unofficial, unauthorized, or unintended distribution channel.

entries.title: secret key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key that is used with a (symmetric) cryptographic algorithm that is uniquely associated with one or more entities and is not made public. The use of the term “secret” in this context does not imply a classification level, but rather implies the need to protect the key from disclosure.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key that is used with a (symmetric) cryptographic algorithm that is uniquely associated with one or more entities and is not made public. The use of the term “secret” in this context does not imply a classification level, but rather implies the need to protect the key from disclosure.

entries.title: Secret key information
entries.summaryMd: The key information that needs to be kept secret (i.e., symmetric keys, private keys, key shares and secret metadata).

senses.definitionMd: The key information that needs to be kept secret (i.e., symmetric keys, private keys, key shares and secret metadata).

entries.title: secret key (symmetric) cryptographic algorithm
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic algorithm that uses a single key (i.e., a secret key) for both encryption and decryption.

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic algorithm that uses a single key (i.e., a secret key) for both encryption and decryption.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "secret key (symmetric) cryptographic algorithm"

entries.title: Secret keying material
entries.summaryMd: The binary data that is used to form secret keys, such as AES encryption or HMAC keys.

senses.definitionMd: The binary data that is used to form secret keys, such as AES encryption or HMAC keys.

entries.title: secret seed
entries.summaryMd: A secret value used to initialize a pseudorandom number generator.

senses.definitionMd: A secret value used to initialize a pseudorandom number generator.

entries.title: Sector
entries.summaryMd: The smallest unit that can be accessed on media.

senses.definitionMd: The smallest unit that can be accessed on media.

entries.title: secure
entries.summaryMd: To reduce the risks of intrusions and attacks as well as the effects of natural or manmade disasters on critical infrastructure by physical means or defensive cyber measures.

senses.definitionMd: To reduce the risks of intrusions and attacks as well as the effects of natural or manmade disasters on critical infrastructure by physical means or defensive cyber measures.

entries.title: Secure channel
entries.summaryMd: A path for transferring data between two entities or components that ensures confidentiality, integrity and replay protection, as well as mutual authentication between the entities or components. The secure channel may be provided using approved cryptographic, physical or procedural methods, or a combination thereof. Sometimes called a trusted channel.

senses.definitionMd: A path for transferring data between two entities or components that ensures confidentiality, integrity and replay protection, as well as mutual authentication between the entities or components. The secure channel may be provided using approved cryptographic, physical or procedural methods, or a combination thereof. Sometimes called a trusted channel.

entries.title: secure communication protocol
entries.summaryMd: A communication protocol that provides the appropriate confidentiality, authentication, and content-integrity protection.

senses.definitionMd: A communication protocol that provides the appropriate confidentiality, authentication, and content-integrity protection.

entries.title: secure communications
entries.summaryMd: Telecommunications deriving security through use of National Security Agency (NSA)-approved products and/or protected distribution systems (PDSs).

senses.definitionMd: Telecommunications deriving security through use of National Security Agency (NSA)-approved products and/or protected distribution systems (PDSs).

entries.title: secure communications interoperability protocol (SCIP) product
entries.summaryMd: National Security Agency (NSA) certified secure voice and data encryption devices that provide interoperability with both national and foreign wired and wireless products.

senses.definitionMd: National Security Agency (NSA) certified secure voice and data encryption devices that provide interoperability with both national and foreign wired and wireless products.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "secure communications interoperability protocol (SCIP) product"

entries.title: Secure Digital eXtended Capacity (SDXC)
entries.summaryMd: Supports cards up to 2 TB, compared to a limit of 32 GB for SDHC cards in the SD 2.0 specification.

senses.definitionMd: Supports cards up to 2 TB, compared to a limit of 32 GB for SDHC cards in the SD 2.0 specification.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Secure Digital eXtended Capacity (SDXC)"

entries.title: Secure Hash Algorithm
entries.summaryMd: The Secure Hash Algorithm defined in Federal Information Processing Standard 180-1.

senses.definitionMd: The Secure Hash Algorithm defined in Federal Information Processing Standard 180-1.

entries.title: Secure Hash Algorithm 256
entries.summaryMd: A hash algorithm that can be used to generate digests of messages. The digests are used to detect whether messages have been changed since the digests were generated.

senses.definitionMd: A hash algorithm that can be used to generate digests of messages. The digests are used to detect whether messages have been changed since the digests were generated.

entries.title: Secure Hash Algorithm 3
entries.summaryMd: Secure Hash Algorithm-3.

senses.definitionMd: Secure Hash Algorithm-3.

entries.title: secure hash standard
entries.summaryMd: The standard specifying hash algorithms that can be used to generate digests of messages. The digests are used to detect whether messages have been changed since the digests were generated.

senses.definitionMd: The standard specifying hash algorithms that can be used to generate digests of messages. The digests are used to detect whether messages have been changed since the digests were generated.

entries.title: Secure Messaging Key Authentication (SM-AUTH)
entries.summaryMd: An authentication mechanism where the secure messaging key and associated certificate are used for authentication.

senses.definitionMd: An authentication mechanism where the secure messaging key and associated certificate are used for authentication.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Secure Messaging Key Authentication (SM-AUTH)"

entries.title: Secure Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME)
entries.summaryMd: A set of specifications for securing electronic mail. S/MIME is based upon the widely used MIME standard and describes a protocol for adding cryptographic security services through MIME encapsulation of digitally signed and encrypted objects. The basic security services offered by S/MIME are authentication, non-repudiation of origin, message integrity, and message privacy. Optional security services include signed receipts, security labels, secure mailing lists, and an extended method of identifying the signer’s certificate(s).

senses.definitionMd: A set of specifications for securing electronic mail. S/MIME is based upon the widely used MIME standard and describes a protocol for adding cryptographic security services through MIME encapsulation of digitally signed and encrypted objects. The basic security services offered by S/MIME are authentication, non-repudiation of origin, message integrity, and message privacy. Optional security services include signed receipts, security labels, secure mailing lists, and an extended method of identifying the signer’s certificate(s).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Secure Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME)"

entries.title: Secure Sockets Layer (SSL)
entries.summaryMd: Provides privacy and data integrity between two communicating applications. It is designed to encapsulate other protocols, such as HTTP. TLS v1.0 was released in 1999, providing slight modifications to SSL 3.0.

senses.definitionMd: Provides privacy and data integrity between two communicating applications. It is designed to encapsulate other protocols, such as HTTP. TLS v1.0 was released in 1999, providing slight modifications to SSL 3.0.

entries.title: secure state
entries.summaryMd: State in which the system's data are consistent and the system continues correct enforcement of security and privacy controls.

senses.definitionMd: State in which the system's data are consistent and the system continues correct enforcement of security and privacy controls.

entries.title: Secure Transport
entries.summaryMd: Transfer of information using a transport layer protocol that provides security between applications communicating over an IP network.

senses.definitionMd: Transfer of information using a transport layer protocol that provides security between applications communicating over an IP network.

entries.title: securely resilient
entries.summaryMd: The ability of a system to preserve a secure state despite disruption, to include the system transitions between normal and degraded modes. Securely resilient is a primary objective of systems security engineering.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of a system to preserve a secure state despite disruption, to include the system transitions between normal and degraded modes. Securely resilient is a primary objective of systems security engineering.

entries.title: security
entries.summaryMd: A condition that results from the establishment and maintenance of protective measures that enable an organization to perform its mission or critical functions despite risks posed by threats to its use of systems. Protective measures may involve a combination of deterrence, avoidance, prevention, detection, recovery, and correction that should form part of the organization’s risk management approach.

senses.definitionMd: A condition that results from the establishment and maintenance of protective measures that enable an organization to perform its mission or critical functions despite risks posed by threats to its use of systems. Protective measures may involve a combination of deterrence, avoidance, prevention, detection, recovery, and correction that should form part of the organization’s risk management approach.

entries.title: security architect
entries.summaryMd: Individual, group, or organization responsible for ensuring that the information security requirements necessary to protect the organization’s core missions and business processes are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture including reference models, segment and solution architectures, and the resulting information systems supporting those missions and business processes.

senses.definitionMd: Individual, group, or organization responsible for ensuring that the information security requirements necessary to protect the organization’s core missions and business processes are adequately addressed in all aspects of enterprise architecture including reference models, segment and solution architectures, and the resulting information systems supporting those missions and business processes.

entries.title: security architecture
entries.summaryMd: A set of physical and logical security-relevant representations (i.e., views) of system architecture that conveys information about how the system is partitioned into security domains and makes use of security-relevant elements to enforce security policies within and between security domains based on how data and information must be protected. Note: The security architecture reflects security domains, the placement of security-relevant elements within the security domains, the interconnections and trust relationships between the security-relevant elements, and the behavior and interaction between the security-relevant elements. The security architecture, similar to the system architecture, may be expressed at different levels of abstraction and with different scopes.

senses.definitionMd: A set of physical and logical security-relevant representations (i.e., views) of system architecture that conveys information about how the system is partitioned into security domains and makes use of security-relevant elements to enforce security policies within and between security domains based on how data and information must be protected. Note: The security architecture reflects security domains, the placement of security-relevant elements within the security domains, the interconnections and trust relationships between the security-relevant elements, and the behavior and interaction between the security-relevant elements. The security architecture, similar to the system architecture, may be expressed at different levels of abstraction and with different scopes.

entries.title: security assertion markup language (SAML)
entries.summaryMd: A protocol consisting of XML-based request and response message formats for exchanging security information, expressed in the form of assertions about subjects, between on-line business partners.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol consisting of XML-based request and response message formats for exchanging security information, expressed in the form of assertions about subjects, between on-line business partners.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security assertion markup language (SAML)"

entries.title: security assessment
entries.summaryMd: The testing and/or evaluation of the management, operational, and technical security controls in an information system to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security requirements for the system.

senses.definitionMd: The testing and/or evaluation of the management, operational, and technical security controls in an information system to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security requirements for the system.

entries.title: security assessment report (SAR)
entries.summaryMd: Provides a disciplined and structured approach for documenting the findings of the assessor and the recommendations for correcting any identified vulnerabilities in the security controls.

senses.definitionMd: Provides a disciplined and structured approach for documenting the findings of the assessor and the recommendations for correcting any identified vulnerabilities in the security controls.

entries.title: Security Association Database (SAD)
entries.summaryMd: A list or table of all IPsec SAs, including those that are still being negotiated.

senses.definitionMd: A list or table of all IPsec SAs, including those that are still being negotiated.

entries.title: Security Association (SA)
entries.summaryMd: A relationship established between two or more entities to enable them to protect data they exchange.

senses.definitionMd: A relationship established between two or more entities to enable them to protect data they exchange.

entries.title: security attribute
entries.summaryMd: An abstraction representing the basic properties or characteristics of an entity with respect to safeguarding information; typically associated with internal data structures (e.g., records, buffers, files) within the information system which are used to enable the implementation of access control and flow control policies; reflect special dissemination, handling, or distribution instructions; or support other aspects of the information security policy.

senses.definitionMd: An abstraction representing the basic properties or characteristics of an entity with respect to safeguarding information; typically associated with internal data structures (e.g., records, buffers, files) within the information system which are used to enable the implementation of access control and flow control policies; reflect special dissemination, handling, or distribution instructions; or support other aspects of the information security policy.

entries.title: security audit
entries.summaryMd: Independent review and examination of a system’s records and activities to determine the adequacy of system controls, ensure compliance with established security policy and procedures, detect breaches in security services, and recommend any changes that are indicated for countermeasures.

senses.definitionMd: Independent review and examination of a system’s records and activities to determine the adequacy of system controls, ensure compliance with established security policy and procedures, detect breaches in security services, and recommend any changes that are indicated for countermeasures.

entries.title: Security Audit Trail
entries.summaryMd: A set of records that collectively provide documentary evidence of processing used to aid in tracing from original transactions forward to related records and reports, and/or backwards from records and reports to their component source transactions.

senses.definitionMd: A set of records that collectively provide documentary evidence of processing used to aid in tracing from original transactions forward to related records and reports, and/or backwards from records and reports to their component source transactions.

entries.title: security auditor
entries.summaryMd: A trusted role that is responsible for auditing the security of certification authority systems (CASs) and registration authorities (RAs), including reviewing, maintaining, and archiving audit logs and performing or overseeing internal audits of CASs and RAs.

senses.definitionMd: A trusted role that is responsible for auditing the security of certification authority systems (CASs) and registration authorities (RAs), including reviewing, maintaining, and archiving audit logs and performing or overseeing internal audits of CASs and RAs.

entries.title: Security Authorization
entries.summaryMd: The right or a permission that is granted to a system entity to access a system resource.

senses.definitionMd: The right or a permission that is granted to a system entity to access a system resource.

entries.title: Security Authorization Boundary
entries.summaryMd: All components of an information system to be authorized for operation by an authorizing official and excludes separately authorized systems, to which the information system is connected.

senses.definitionMd: All components of an information system to be authorized for operation by an authorizing official and excludes separately authorized systems, to which the information system is connected.

entries.title: security authorization package
entries.summaryMd: Documents the results of the security control assessment and provides the authorizing official with essential information needed to make a risk-based decision on whether to authorize operation of an information system or a designated set of common controls. Contains: (i) the security plan; (ii) the security assessment report (SAR); and (iii) the plan of action and milestones (POA&M). Note: Many departments and agencies may choose to include the risk assessment report (RAR) as part of the security authorization package. Also, many organizations use system security plan in place of the security plan.

senses.definitionMd: Documents the results of the security control assessment and provides the authorizing official with essential information needed to make a risk-based decision on whether to authorize operation of an information system or a designated set of common controls. Contains: (i) the security plan; (ii) the security assessment report (SAR); and (iii) the plan of action and milestones (POA&M). Note: Many departments and agencies may choose to include the risk assessment report (RAR) as part of the security authorization package. Also, many organizations use system security plan in place of the security plan.

entries.title: security authorization (to operate)
entries.summaryMd: See authorization to operate (ATO).

senses.definitionMd: See authorization to operate (ATO).

entries.title: Security Automation Domain
entries.summaryMd: An information security area that includes a grouping of tools, technologies, and data.

senses.definitionMd: An information security area that includes a grouping of tools, technologies, and data.

entries.title: security banner
entries.summaryMd: See security banner (also known as notice and consent banners)

senses.definitionMd: See security banner (also known as notice and consent banners)

entries.title: Security boundary
entries.summaryMd: A conceptual boundary that is used to assess the amount of entropy provided by the values output from an entropy source. The entropy assessment is performed under the assumption that any observer (including any adversary) is outside of that boundary.

senses.definitionMd: A conceptual boundary that is used to assess the amount of entropy provided by the values output from an entropy source. The entropy assessment is performed under the assumption that any observer (including any adversary) is outside of that boundary.

entries.title: Security Capability
entries.summaryMd: See capability.

senses.definitionMd: See capability.

entries.title: security categorization
entries.summaryMd: The process of determining the security category for information or an information system. Security categorization methodologies are described in CNSS Instruction 1253 for national security systems and in FIPS 199 for other than national security systems.

senses.definitionMd: The process of determining the security category for information or an information system. Security categorization methodologies are described in CNSS Instruction 1253 for national security systems and in FIPS 199 for other than national security systems.

entries.title: security category
entries.summaryMd: The characterization of information or an information system based on an assessment of the potential impact that a loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of such information or information system would have on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.

senses.definitionMd: The characterization of information or an information system based on an assessment of the potential impact that a loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of such information or information system would have on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.

entries.title: security concept of operations (Security CONOP)
entries.summaryMd: See security concept of operations.

senses.definitionMd: See security concept of operations.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security concept of operations (Security CONOP)"

entries.title: Security Configuration Management (SecCM)
entries.summaryMd: The management and control of configurations for an information system to enable security and facilitate the management of risk.

senses.definitionMd: The management and control of configurations for an information system to enable security and facilitate the management of risk.

entries.title: security content automation protocol (SCAP)
entries.summaryMd: A suite of specifications that standardize the format and nomenclature by which software flaw and security configuration information is communicated, both to machines and humans. Note: There are six individual specifications incorporated into SCAP: CVE (common vulnerabilities and exposures); CCE (common configuration enumeration); CPE (common platform enumeration); CVSS (common vulnerability scoring system); OVAL (open vulnerability assessment language); and XCCDF (eXtensible configuration checklist description format).

senses.definitionMd: A suite of specifications that standardize the format and nomenclature by which software flaw and security configuration information is communicated, both to machines and humans. Note: There are six individual specifications incorporated into SCAP: CVE (common vulnerabilities and exposures); CCE (common configuration enumeration); CPE (common platform enumeration); CVSS (common vulnerability scoring system); OVAL (open vulnerability assessment language); and XCCDF (eXtensible configuration checklist description format).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security content automation protocol (SCAP)"

entries.title: security control
entries.summaryMd: A safeguard or countermeasure prescribed for an information system or an organization designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its information and to meet a set of defined security requirements.

senses.definitionMd: A safeguard or countermeasure prescribed for an information system or an organization designed to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its information and to meet a set of defined security requirements.

entries.title: security control and privacy control
entries.summaryMd: See security control and privacy control.

senses.definitionMd: See security control and privacy control.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security control and privacy control"

entries.title: security control assessment
entries.summaryMd: The testing and/or evaluation of the management, operational, and technical security controls in an information system to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security requirements for the system.

senses.definitionMd: The testing and/or evaluation of the management, operational, and technical security controls in an information system to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting the security requirements for the system.

entries.title: security control assessor (SCA)
entries.summaryMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a security control assessment.

senses.definitionMd: The individual, group, or organization responsible for conducting a security control assessment.

entries.title: security control baseline
entries.summaryMd: The set of minimum security controls defined for a low-impact, moderate-impact, or high-impact information system.

senses.definitionMd: The set of minimum security controls defined for a low-impact, moderate-impact, or high-impact information system.

entries.title: Security Control Effectiveness
entries.summaryMd: The measure of correctness of implementation (i.e., how consistently the control implementation complies with the security plan) and how well the security plan meets organizational needs in accordance with current risk tolerance.

senses.definitionMd: The measure of correctness of implementation (i.e., how consistently the control implementation complies with the security plan) and how well the security plan meets organizational needs in accordance with current risk tolerance.

entries.title: security control enhancements
entries.summaryMd: Statement of security capability to: (i) build in additional, but related, functionality to a basic security control; and/or (ii) increase the strength of a basic control.

senses.definitionMd: Statement of security capability to: (i) build in additional, but related, functionality to a basic security control; and/or (ii) increase the strength of a basic control.

entries.title: security control inheritance
entries.summaryMd: A situation in which an information system or application receives protection from security controls (or portions of security controls) that are developed, implemented, assessed, authorized, and monitored by entities other than those responsible for the system or application; entities either internal or external to the organization where the system or application resides. See Common Control.

senses.definitionMd: A situation in which an information system or application receives protection from security controls (or portions of security controls) that are developed, implemented, assessed, authorized, and monitored by entities other than those responsible for the system or application; entities either internal or external to the organization where the system or application resides. See Common Control.

entries.title: Security Control Item
entries.summaryMd: See Security Control Item.

senses.definitionMd: See Security Control Item.

entries.title: security control provider
entries.summaryMd: An organizational official responsible for the development, implementation, assessment, and monitoring of common controls (i.e., security controls inherited by information systems). See common control provider.

senses.definitionMd: An organizational official responsible for the development, implementation, assessment, and monitoring of common controls (i.e., security controls inherited by information systems). See common control provider.

entries.title: security controls
entries.summaryMd: Actions, devices, procedures, techniques, or other measures that reduce the vulnerability of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Actions, devices, procedures, techniques, or other measures that reduce the vulnerability of an information system.

entries.title: security criteria
entries.summaryMd: Criteria related to a supplier’s ability to conform to security-relevant laws, directives, regulations, policies, or business processes; a supplier’s ability to deliver the requested product or service in satisfaction of the stated security requirements and in conformance with secure business practices; the ability of a mechanism, system element, or system to meet its security requirements; whether movement from one life cycle stage or process to another (e.g., to accept a baseline into configuration management, to accept delivery of a product or service) is acceptable in terms of security policy; how a delivered product or service is handled, distributed, and accepted; how to perform security verification and validation; or how to store system elements securely in disposal.
