senses.definitionMd: Criteria related to a supplier’s ability to conform to security-relevant laws, directives, regulations, policies, or business processes; a supplier’s ability to deliver the requested product or service in satisfaction of the stated security requirements and in conformance with secure business practices; the ability of a mechanism, system element, or system to meet its security requirements; whether movement from one life cycle stage or process to another (e.g., to accept a baseline into configuration management, to accept delivery of a product or service) is acceptable in terms of security policy; how a delivered product or service is handled, distributed, and accepted; how to perform security verification and validation; or how to store system elements securely in disposal.

entries.title: security design order of precedence
entries.summaryMd: A design approach for minimizing the design basis for loss potential and using architectural features to provide structure for implementing engineered security features and devices.

senses.definitionMd: A design approach for minimizing the design basis for loss potential and using architectural features to provide structure for implementing engineered security features and devices.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security design order of precedence"

entries.title: security domain
entries.summaryMd: A domain operating at a single security level (which includes a unique combination of classification, releasabilities, and dissemination controls) that implements a security policy and is administered by a single authority.

senses.definitionMd: A domain operating at a single security level (which includes a unique combination of classification, releasabilities, and dissemination controls) that implements a security policy and is administered by a single authority.

entries.title: security engineering
entries.summaryMd: An interdisciplinary approach and means to enable the realization of secure systems. It focuses on defining customer needs, security protection requirements, and required functionality early in the systems development lifecycle, documenting requirements, and then proceeding with design, synthesis, and system validation while considering the complete problem.

senses.definitionMd: An interdisciplinary approach and means to enable the realization of secure systems. It focuses on defining customer needs, security protection requirements, and required functionality early in the systems development lifecycle, documenting requirements, and then proceeding with design, synthesis, and system validation while considering the complete problem.

entries.title: Security Event Management Software
entries.summaryMd: Software that imports security event information from multiple data sources, normalizes the data, and correlates events among the data sources.

senses.definitionMd: Software that imports security event information from multiple data sources, normalizes the data, and correlates events among the data sources.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Security Event Management Software"

entries.title: Security Executive Agent
entries.summaryMd: Individual responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of effective, efficient, and uniform policies and procedures that govern the conduct of investigations and adjudications for eligibility to access classified information and eligibility to hold a sensitive position in the Federal Government. In accordance with Executive Order 13467 (as amended), this individual is the Director of National Intelligence (DNI)

senses.definitionMd: Individual responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of effective, efficient, and uniform policies and procedures that govern the conduct of investigations and adjudications for eligibility to access classified information and eligibility to hold a sensitive position in the Federal Government. In accordance with Executive Order 13467 (as amended), this individual is the Director of National Intelligence (DNI)

entries.title: security fault analysis (SFA)
entries.summaryMd: An assessment usually performed on information system hardware, to determine the security properties of a device when hardware fault is encountered.

senses.definitionMd: An assessment usually performed on information system hardware, to determine the security properties of a device when hardware fault is encountered.

entries.title: Security Fault Injection Test
entries.summaryMd: Involves data perturbation (i.e., alteration of the type of data the execution environment components pass to the application, or that the application’s components pass to one another). Fault injection can reveal the effects of security defects on the behavior of the components themselves and on the application as a whole.

senses.definitionMd: Involves data perturbation (i.e., alteration of the type of data the execution environment components pass to the application, or that the application’s components pass to one another). Fault injection can reveal the effects of security defects on the behavior of the components themselves and on the application as a whole.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Security Fault Injection Test"

entries.title: Security Features Users Guide
entries.summaryMd: Guide or manual explaining how the security mechanisms in a specific system work.

senses.definitionMd: Guide or manual explaining how the security mechanisms in a specific system work.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Security Features Users Guide"

entries.title: security filter
entries.summaryMd: A secure subsystem of an information system that enforces security policy on the data passing through it.

senses.definitionMd: A secure subsystem of an information system that enforces security policy on the data passing through it.

entries.title: security function
entries.summaryMd: The capability provided by the system or a system element. The capability may be expressed generally as a concept or specified precisely in requirements.

senses.definitionMd: The capability provided by the system or a system element. The capability may be expressed generally as a concept or specified precisely in requirements.

entries.title: security functionality
entries.summaryMd: The security-related features, functions, mechanisms, services, procedures, and architectures implemented within organizational information systems or the environments in which those systems operate.

senses.definitionMd: The security-related features, functions, mechanisms, services, procedures, and architectures implemented within organizational information systems or the environments in which those systems operate.

entries.title: security functions
entries.summaryMd: The hardware, software, or firmware of the system responsible for enforcing the system security policy and supporting the isolation of code and data on which the protection is based.

senses.definitionMd: The hardware, software, or firmware of the system responsible for enforcing the system security policy and supporting the isolation of code and data on which the protection is based.

entries.title: security impact analysis
entries.summaryMd: The analysis conducted by an organizational official to determine the extent to which a change to an information system has affected the security state of that system.

senses.definitionMd: The analysis conducted by an organizational official to determine the extent to which a change to an information system has affected the security state of that system.

entries.title: security incident
entries.summaryMd: An occurrence that actually or potentially jeopardizes the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system or the information the system processes, stores, or transmits or that constitutes a violation or imminent threat of violation of security policies, security procedures, or acceptable use policies.

senses.definitionMd: An occurrence that actually or potentially jeopardizes the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of an information system or the information the system processes, stores, or transmits or that constitutes a violation or imminent threat of violation of security policies, security procedures, or acceptable use policies.

entries.title: security information
entries.summaryMd: Information within the system that can potentially impact the operation of security functions or the provision of security services in a manner that could result in failure to enforce the system security policy or maintain isolation of code and data.

senses.definitionMd: Information within the system that can potentially impact the operation of security functions or the provision of security services in a manner that could result in failure to enforce the system security policy or maintain isolation of code and data.

entries.title: Security Information and Event Management
entries.summaryMd: A program that provides centralized logging capabilities for a variety of log types.

senses.definitionMd: A program that provides centralized logging capabilities for a variety of log types.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Security Information and Event Management"

entries.title: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Tool
entries.summaryMd: Application that provides the ability to gather security data from information system components and present that data as actionable information via a single interface.

senses.definitionMd: Application that provides the ability to gather security data from information system components and present that data as actionable information via a single interface.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) Tool"

entries.title: security inspection
entries.summaryMd: Examination of an information system to determine compliance with security policy, procedures, and practices.

senses.definitionMd: Examination of an information system to determine compliance with security policy, procedures, and practices.

entries.title: security kernel
entries.summaryMd: Hardware, firmware, and software elements of a trusted computing base implementing the reference monitor concept. Security kernel must mediate all accesses, be protected from modification, and be verifiable as correct.

senses.definitionMd: Hardware, firmware, and software elements of a trusted computing base implementing the reference monitor concept. Security kernel must mediate all accesses, be protected from modification, and be verifiable as correct.

entries.title: security label
entries.summaryMd: A piece of information that represents the security level of an object.

senses.definitionMd: A piece of information that represents the security level of an object.

entries.title: Security life of data
entries.summaryMd: The time period during which the security of the data needs to be protected (e.g., its confidentiality, integrity or availability).

senses.definitionMd: The time period during which the security of the data needs to be protected (e.g., its confidentiality, integrity or availability).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Security life of data"

entries.title: Security Management Dashboard
entries.summaryMd: A tool that consolidates and communicates information relevant to the organizational security posture in near real-time to security management stakeholders.

senses.definitionMd: A tool that consolidates and communicates information relevant to the organizational security posture in near real-time to security management stakeholders.

entries.title: security marking
entries.summaryMd: The means used to associate a set of security attributes with objects in a human-readable form, to enable organizational process-based enforcement of information security policies.

senses.definitionMd: The means used to associate a set of security attributes with objects in a human-readable form, to enable organizational process-based enforcement of information security policies.

entries.title: security mechanism
entries.summaryMd: A device or function designed to provide one or more security services usually rated in terms of strength of service and assurance of the design.

senses.definitionMd: A device or function designed to provide one or more security services usually rated in terms of strength of service and assurance of the design.

entries.title: security objective
entries.summaryMd: Confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

senses.definitionMd: Confidentiality, integrity, or availability.

entries.title: Security-Oriented Code Review
entries.summaryMd: A code review, or audit, investigates the coding practices used in the application. The main objective of such reviews is to discover security defects and potentially identify solutions.

senses.definitionMd: A code review, or audit, investigates the coding practices used in the application. The main objective of such reviews is to discover security defects and potentially identify solutions.

entries.title: Security Parameters Index (SPI)
entries.summaryMd: An arbitrarily chosen value that acts as a unique identifier for an IPsec connection.

senses.definitionMd: An arbitrarily chosen value that acts as a unique identifier for an IPsec connection.

entries.title: security perimeter
entries.summaryMd: All components of an information system to be accredited by an authorizing official and excludes separately accredited systems to which the information system is connected. Synonymous with the term security perimeter defined in CNSS Instruction 4009 and DCID 6/3.

senses.definitionMd: All components of an information system to be accredited by an authorizing official and excludes separately accredited systems to which the information system is connected. Synonymous with the term security perimeter defined in CNSS Instruction 4009 and DCID 6/3.

entries.title: security plan
entries.summaryMd: See System Security Plan.

senses.definitionMd: See System Security Plan.

entries.title: security policy
entries.summaryMd: The set of laws, rules, and practices that regulate how an organization manages, protects, and distributes sensitive information.

senses.definitionMd: The set of laws, rules, and practices that regulate how an organization manages, protects, and distributes sensitive information.

entries.title: Security Policy Database (SPD)
entries.summaryMd: A prioritized list of all IPsec policies.

senses.definitionMd: A prioritized list of all IPsec policies.

entries.title: security policy filter
entries.summaryMd: A hardware and/or software component that performs one or more of the following functions: content verification to ensure the data type of the submitted content; content inspection to analyze the submitted content and verify that complies with a defined policy; malicious content checker that evaluates the content for malicious code; suspicious activity checker that evaluates or executes the content in a safe manner, such as in a sandbox or detonation chamber and monitors for suspicious activity; or content sanitization, cleansing, and transformation, which modifies the submitted content to comply with a defined policy.

senses.definitionMd: A hardware and/or software component that performs one or more of the following functions: content verification to ensure the data type of the submitted content; content inspection to analyze the submitted content and verify that complies with a defined policy; malicious content checker that evaluates the content for malicious code; suspicious activity checker that evaluates or executes the content in a safe manner, such as in a sandbox or detonation chamber and monitors for suspicious activity; or content sanitization, cleansing, and transformation, which modifies the submitted content to comply with a defined policy.

entries.title: security posture
entries.summaryMd: The security status of an enterprise’s networks, information, and systems based on information security resources (e.g., people, hardware, software, policies) and capabilities in place to manage the defense of the enterprise and to react as the situation changes.

senses.definitionMd: The security status of an enterprise’s networks, information, and systems based on information security resources (e.g., people, hardware, software, policies) and capabilities in place to manage the defense of the enterprise and to react as the situation changes.

entries.title: security program plan
entries.summaryMd: Formal document that provides an overview of the security requirements for an organization-wide information security program and describes the program management security controls and common security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Formal document that provides an overview of the security requirements for an organization-wide information security program and describes the program management security controls and common security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.

entries.title: Security properties
entries.summaryMd: The security features (e.g., replay protection, or key confirmation) that a cryptographic scheme may, or may not, provide.

senses.definitionMd: The security features (e.g., replay protection, or key confirmation) that a cryptographic scheme may, or may not, provide.

entries.title: security protocol
entries.summaryMd: An abstract or concrete protocol that performs security-related functions.

senses.definitionMd: An abstract or concrete protocol that performs security-related functions.

entries.title: security range
entries.summaryMd: Highest and lowest security levels that are permitted in or on an information system, system component, subsystem, or network.

senses.definitionMd: Highest and lowest security levels that are permitted in or on an information system, system component, subsystem, or network.

entries.title: security relevance
entries.summaryMd: The term used to describe those functions or mechanisms that are relied upon, directly or indirectly, to enforce a security policy that governs confidentiality, integrity, and availability protections.

senses.definitionMd: The term used to describe those functions or mechanisms that are relied upon, directly or indirectly, to enforce a security policy that governs confidentiality, integrity, and availability protections.

entries.title: security-relevant change
entries.summaryMd: Any change to a system’s configuration, environment, information content, functionality, or users which has the potential to change the risk imposed upon its continued operations.

senses.definitionMd: Any change to a system’s configuration, environment, information content, functionality, or users which has the potential to change the risk imposed upon its continued operations.

entries.title: security-relevant information
entries.summaryMd: Information within the system that can potentially impact the operation of security functions or the provision of security services in a manner that could result in failure to enforce the system security policy or maintain isolation of code and data.

senses.definitionMd: Information within the system that can potentially impact the operation of security functions or the provision of security services in a manner that could result in failure to enforce the system security policy or maintain isolation of code and data.

entries.title: security requirement
entries.summaryMd: Requirements levied on an information system that are derived from applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, standards, instructions, regulations, or procedures, or organizational mission/business case needs to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information being processed, stored, or transmitted.

senses.definitionMd: Requirements levied on an information system that are derived from applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, standards, instructions, regulations, or procedures, or organizational mission/business case needs to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information being processed, stored, or transmitted.

entries.title: security requirements baseline
entries.summaryMd: Description of the minimum requirements necessary for an information system to maintain an acceptable level of risk.

senses.definitionMd: Description of the minimum requirements necessary for an information system to maintain an acceptable level of risk.

entries.title: security requirements guide (SRG)
entries.summaryMd: Compilation of control correlation identifiers (CCIs) grouped in more applicable, specific technology areas at various levels of technology and product specificity. Contains all requirements that have been flagged as applicable from the parent level regardless if they are selected on a Department of Defense (DoD) baseline or not.

senses.definitionMd: Compilation of control correlation identifiers (CCIs) grouped in more applicable, specific technology areas at various levels of technology and product specificity. Contains all requirements that have been flagged as applicable from the parent level regardless if they are selected on a Department of Defense (DoD) baseline or not.

entries.title: security requirements traceability matrix (SRTM)
entries.summaryMd: Matrix documenting the system's agreed upon security requirements derived from all sources, the security features' implementation details and schedule, and the resources required for assessment.

senses.definitionMd: Matrix documenting the system's agreed upon security requirements derived from all sources, the security features' implementation details and schedule, and the resources required for assessment.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security requirements traceability matrix (SRTM)"

entries.title: security risk
entries.summaryMd: The effect of uncertainty on objectives pertaining to asset loss and the associated consequences.

senses.definitionMd: The effect of uncertainty on objectives pertaining to asset loss and the associated consequences.

entries.title: security safeguards
entries.summaryMd: Protective measures and controls prescribed to meet the security requirements specified for an information system. Safeguards may include security features, management constraints, personnel security, and security of physical structures, areas, and devices.

senses.definitionMd: Protective measures and controls prescribed to meet the security requirements specified for an information system. Safeguards may include security features, management constraints, personnel security, and security of physical structures, areas, and devices.

entries.title: security service
entries.summaryMd: A capability that supports one, or many, of the security goals. Examples of security services are key management, access control, and authentication.

senses.definitionMd: A capability that supports one, or many, of the security goals. Examples of security services are key management, access control, and authentication.

entries.title: security solution
entries.summaryMd: The key design, architectural, and implementation choices made by organizations in satisfying specified security requirements for systems or system components.

senses.definitionMd: The key design, architectural, and implementation choices made by organizations in satisfying specified security requirements for systems or system components.

entries.title: security specification
entries.summaryMd: A document that specifies, in a complete, precise, verifiable manner, the requirements, design, behavior, or other characteristics of a system or component and often the procedures for determining whether these provisions have been satisfied. See specification requirement.

senses.definitionMd: A document that specifies, in a complete, precise, verifiable manner, the requirements, design, behavior, or other characteristics of a system or component and often the procedures for determining whether these provisions have been satisfied. See specification requirement.

entries.title: Security Status
entries.summaryMd: The security status of an enterprise’s networks, information, and systems based on information security resources (e.g., people, hardware, software, policies) and capabilities in place to manage the defense of the enterprise and to react as the situation changes.

senses.definitionMd: The security status of an enterprise’s networks, information, and systems based on information security resources (e.g., people, hardware, software, policies) and capabilities in place to manage the defense of the enterprise and to react as the situation changes.

entries.title: security strength
entries.summaryMd: A number associated with the amount of work (i.e., the number of operations) that is required to break a cryptographic algorithm or system.

senses.definitionMd: A number associated with the amount of work (i.e., the number of operations) that is required to break a cryptographic algorithm or system.

entries.title: security target
entries.summaryMd: Implementation-dependent statement of security needs for a specific identified target of evaluation (TOE).

senses.definitionMd: Implementation-dependent statement of security needs for a specific identified target of evaluation (TOE).

entries.title: security technical implementation guide (STIG)
entries.summaryMd: Based on Department of Defense (DoD) policy and security controls. Implementation guide geared to a specific product and version. Contains all requirements that have been flagged as applicable for the product which have been selected on a DoD baseline.

senses.definitionMd: Based on Department of Defense (DoD) policy and security controls. Implementation guide geared to a specific product and version. Contains all requirements that have been flagged as applicable for the product which have been selected on a DoD baseline.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security technical implementation guide (STIG)"

entries.title: security test and evaluation (ST&E)
entries.summaryMd: Examination and analysis of the safeguards required to protect an information system, as they have been applied in an operational environment, to determine the security posture of that system.

senses.definitionMd: Examination and analysis of the safeguards required to protect an information system, as they have been applied in an operational environment, to determine the security posture of that system.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "security test and evaluation (ST&E)"

entries.title: Security testing
entries.summaryMd: Testing that attempts to verify that an implementation protects data and maintains functionality as intended.

senses.definitionMd: Testing that attempts to verify that an implementation protects data and maintains functionality as intended.

entries.title: Seed
entries.summaryMd: A bit string used as input to a pseudorandom process.

senses.definitionMd: A bit string used as input to a pseudorandom process.

entries.title: seed key
entries.summaryMd: Initial key used to start an updating or key generation process.

senses.definitionMd: Initial key used to start an updating or key generation process.

entries.title: Seed Period
entries.summaryMd: The period of time between instantiating or reseeding a DRBG with one seed and reseeding that DRBG with another seed.

senses.definitionMd: The period of time between instantiating or reseeding a DRBG with one seed and reseeding that DRBG with another seed.

entries.title: Seedlife
entries.summaryMd: The length of the seed period.

senses.definitionMd: The length of the seed period.

entries.title: segment
entries.summaryMd: In the CFB mode, a sequence of bits whose length is a parameter that does not exceed the block size.

senses.definitionMd: In the CFB mode, a sequence of bits whose length is a parameter that does not exceed the block size.

entries.title: select (V, a, b)
entries.summaryMd: A substring of string V consisting of bit a through bit b.

senses.definitionMd: A substring of string V consisting of bit a through bit b.

entries.title: selection operation
entries.summaryMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to select a value from a list of predefined values provided as part of the control or control enhancement (e.g., selecting to either restrict an action or prohibit an action).

senses.definitionMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to select a value from a list of predefined values provided as part of the control or control enhancement (e.g., selecting to either restrict an action or prohibit an action).

entries.title: selection statement
entries.summaryMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to select a value from a list of pre-defined values provided as part of the control or control enhancement (e.g., selecting to either restrict an action or prohibit an action). See assignment and organization-defined control parameter.

senses.definitionMd: A control parameter that allows an organization to select a value from a list of pre-defined values provided as part of the control or control enhancement (e.g., selecting to either restrict an action or prohibit an action). See assignment and organization-defined control parameter.

entries.title: Self-dual Key
entries.summaryMd: A key with the property that when you encrypt twice with this key, the result is the initial input.

senses.definitionMd: A key with the property that when you encrypt twice with this key, the result is the initial input.

entries.title: self-encrypting devices / self-encrypting drives (SED)
entries.summaryMd: Data storage device with built-in cryptographic processing that may be utilized to encrypt and decrypt the stored data, occurring within the device and without dependence on a connected information system.

senses.definitionMd: Data storage device with built-in cryptographic processing that may be utilized to encrypt and decrypt the stored data, occurring within the device and without dependence on a connected information system.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "self-encrypting devices / self-encrypting drives (SED)"

entries.title: self-protection
entries.summaryMd: The protection provided by an entity to ensure its own correct behavior and function despite adversity.

senses.definitionMd: The protection provided by an entity to ensure its own correct behavior and function despite adversity.

entries.title: Self-signed certificate
entries.summaryMd: A public-key certificate whose digital signature may be verified by the public key contained within the certificate. The signature on a self-signed certificate protects the integrity of the information within the certificate but does not guarantee the authenticity of that information. The trust of self-signed certificates is based on the secure procedures used to distribute them.

senses.definitionMd: A public-key certificate whose digital signature may be verified by the public key contained within the certificate. The signature on a self-signed certificate protects the integrity of the information within the certificate but does not guarantee the authenticity of that information. The trust of self-signed certificates is based on the secure procedures used to distribute them.

entries.title: self-supervised learning
entries.summaryMd: A type of machine learning that relies on generating implicit la­bels from unstructured data rather than relying on explicit, human-created labels. Self-supervised learning tasks are constructed to allow the true labels to be automatically inferred from the training data (enabling the use of large-scale training data) and to require models to capture essential features or relationships within the data to solve them. For example, a common self-supervised learning task is providing a model with partial data with the task to accurately generate the re­mainder.

senses.definitionMd: A type of machine learning that relies on generating implicit la­bels from unstructured data rather than relying on explicit, human-created labels. Self-supervised learning tasks are constructed to allow the true labels to be automatically inferred from the training data (enabling the use of large-scale training data) and to require models to capture essential features or relationships within the data to solve them. For example, a common self-supervised learning task is providing a model with partial data with the task to accurately generate the re­mainder.

entries.title: Self testing
entries.summaryMd: Testing within a system, device or process during normal operation to detect misbehavior.

senses.definitionMd: Testing within a system, device or process during normal operation to detect misbehavior.

entries.title: Semantic matching
entries.summaryMd: uses contextual attributes of the digital object to interpret the artifact in a manner that more closely corresponds with human perceptual categories. For example, perceptual hashes allow the matching of visually similar images and are unconcerned with the low-level details of how the images are persistently stored. Semantic methods tend to provide the most specific results but also tend to be the most computationally expensive ones.

senses.definitionMd: uses contextual attributes of the digital object to interpret the artifact in a manner that more closely corresponds with human perceptual categories. For example, perceptual hashes allow the matching of visually similar images and are unconcerned with the low-level details of how the images are persistently stored. Semantic methods tend to provide the most specific results but also tend to be the most computationally expensive ones.

entries.title: semantic security
entries.summaryMd: What can be efficiently computed about some plaintexts from their ciphertexts can be computed, just as easily, in the absence of those ciphertexts.

senses.definitionMd: What can be efficiently computed about some plaintexts from their ciphertexts can be computed, just as easily, in the absence of those ciphertexts.

entries.title: Semantics
entries.summaryMd: The intended meaning of acceptable sentences of a language.

senses.definitionMd: The intended meaning of acceptable sentences of a language.

entries.title: Semantics of a language
entries.summaryMd: The meanings of all the language's acceptable sentences.

senses.definitionMd: The meanings of all the language's acceptable sentences.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Semantics of a language"

entries.title: Semi-Active Tag
entries.summaryMd: A tag that uses a battery to communicate but remains dormant until a reader sends an energizing signal. Semi-active tags have a longer range than passive tags and a longer battery life than active tags.

senses.definitionMd: A tag that uses a battery to communicate but remains dormant until a reader sends an energizing signal. Semi-active tags have a longer range than passive tags and a longer battery life than active tags.

entries.title: Semi-Passive Tag
entries.summaryMd: A passive tag that uses a battery to power on-board circuitry or sensors but not to produce back channel signals.

senses.definitionMd: A passive tag that uses a battery to power on-board circuitry or sensors but not to produce back channel signals.

entries.title: Semi-Qualitative Risk Analysis
entries.summaryMd: A method for risk analysis with qualitative categories assigned numeric values to allow for the calculation of numeric results.

senses.definitionMd: A method for risk analysis with qualitative categories assigned numeric values to allow for the calculation of numeric results.

entries.title: Semi-Quantitative Assessment
entries.summaryMd: Use of a set of methods, principles, or rules for assessing risk based on bins, scales, or representative numbers whose values and meanings are not maintained in other contexts.

senses.definitionMd: Use of a set of methods, principles, or rules for assessing risk based on bins, scales, or representative numbers whose values and meanings are not maintained in other contexts.

entries.title: semi-supervised learning
entries.summaryMd: A type of machine learning in which a small number of training samples are labeled, while the majority are unlabeled.

senses.definitionMd: A type of machine learning in which a small number of training samples are labeled, while the majority are unlabeled.

entries.title: semiblock
entries.summaryMd: Given a block cipher, a bit string whose length is half of the block size.

senses.definitionMd: Given a block cipher, a bit string whose length is half of the block size.

entries.title: semiblock string
entries.summaryMd: For a given block size, a string that can be represented as the concatenation of semiblocks.

senses.definitionMd: For a given block size, a string that can be represented as the concatenation of semiblocks.

entries.title: Sender
entries.summaryMd: The party that sends secret keying material to the receiver using a key-transport transaction. Contrast with receiver.

senses.definitionMd: The party that sends secret keying material to the receiver using a key-transport transaction. Contrast with receiver.

entries.title: senior accountable official for risk management
entries.summaryMd: The senior official, designated by the head of each agency, who has vision into all areas of the organization and is responsible for alignment of information security management processes with strategic, operational, and budgetary planning processes.

senses.definitionMd: The senior official, designated by the head of each agency, who has vision into all areas of the organization and is responsible for alignment of information security management processes with strategic, operational, and budgetary planning processes.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "senior accountable official for risk management"

entries.title: senior agency information security officer (SAISO)
entries.summaryMd: Official responsible for carrying out the Chief Information Officer responsibilities under FISMA and serving as the Chief Information Officer’s primary liaison to the agency’s authorizing officials, information system owners, and information system security officers.

senses.definitionMd: Official responsible for carrying out the Chief Information Officer responsibilities under FISMA and serving as the Chief Information Officer’s primary liaison to the agency’s authorizing officials, information system owners, and information system security officers.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "senior agency information security officer (SAISO)"

entries.title: senior agency official for privacy
entries.summaryMd: See Senior Agency Official for Privacy.

senses.definitionMd: See Senior Agency Official for Privacy.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "senior agency official for privacy"

entries.title: senior information security officer (SISO)
entries.summaryMd: Official responsible for carrying out the Chief Information Officer responsibilities under FISMA and serving as the Chief Information Officer’s primary liaison to the agency’s authorizing officials, information system owners, and information system security officers.

senses.definitionMd: Official responsible for carrying out the Chief Information Officer responsibilities under FISMA and serving as the Chief Information Officer’s primary liaison to the agency’s authorizing officials, information system owners, and information system security officers.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "senior information security officer (SISO)"

entries.title: Sensing Capability
entries.summaryMd: The ability to provide an observation of an aspect of the physical world in the form of measurement data.

senses.definitionMd: The ability to provide an observation of an aspect of the physical world in the form of measurement data.

entries.title: Sensitive
entries.summaryMd: A descriptor of information whose loss, misuse, or unauthorized access or modification could adversely affect security.

senses.definitionMd: A descriptor of information whose loss, misuse, or unauthorized access or modification could adversely affect security.

entries.title: Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF)
entries.summaryMd: An area, room, group of rooms, buildings, or installation certified and accredited as meeting Director of National Intelligence security standards for the processing, storage, and/or discussion of sensitive compartmented information (SCI).

senses.definitionMd: An area, room, group of rooms, buildings, or installation certified and accredited as meeting Director of National Intelligence security standards for the processing, storage, and/or discussion of sensitive compartmented information (SCI).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF)"

entries.title: sensitive compartmented information (SCI)
entries.summaryMd: Classified information concerning or derived from intelligence sources, methods, or analytical processes, which is required to be handled within formal access control systems established by the Director of National Intelligence.

senses.definitionMd: Classified information concerning or derived from intelligence sources, methods, or analytical processes, which is required to be handled within formal access control systems established by the Director of National Intelligence.

entries.title: sensitive information
entries.summaryMd: Information, the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of, that could adversely affect the national interest or the conduct of federal programs, or the privacy to which individuals are entitled under 5 U.S.C. Section 552a (the Privacy Act), but that has not been specifically authorized under criteria established by an Executive Order or an Act of Congress to be kept classified in the interest of national defense or foreign policy.

senses.definitionMd: Information, the loss, misuse, or unauthorized access to or modification of, that could adversely affect the national interest or the conduct of federal programs, or the privacy to which individuals are entitled under 5 U.S.C. Section 552a (the Privacy Act), but that has not been specifically authorized under criteria established by an Executive Order or an Act of Congress to be kept classified in the interest of national defense or foreign policy.

entries.title: sensitivity
entries.summaryMd: A measure of the importance assigned to information by its owner, for the purpose of denoting its need for protection.

senses.definitionMd: A measure of the importance assigned to information by its owner, for the purpose of denoting its need for protection.

entries.title: sensor
entries.summaryMd: An intrusion detection and prevention system component that monitors and analyzes network activity and may also perform prevention actions.

senses.definitionMd: An intrusion detection and prevention system component that monitors and analyzes network activity and may also perform prevention actions.

entries.title: Sentences, formal
entries.summaryMd: The entire set of sentences that can be created or recognized as being valid using the formal syntax specifications of a formal language.

senses.definitionMd: The entire set of sentences that can be created or recognized as being valid using the formal syntax specifications of a formal language.

entries.title: Separation of Concerns
entries.summaryMd: A design principle for breaking down an application into modules, layers, and encapsulations, the roles of which are independent of one another.

senses.definitionMd: A design principle for breaking down an application into modules, layers, and encapsulations, the roles of which are independent of one another.

entries.title: Separation of Duty (SOD)
entries.summaryMd: refers to the principle that no user should be given enough privileges to misuse the system on their own. For example, the person authorizing a paycheck should not also be the one who can prepare them. Separation of duties can be enforced either statically (by defining conflicting roles, i.e., roles which cannot be executed by the same user) or dynamically (by enforcing the control at access time). An example of dynamic separation of duty is the two-person rule. The first user to execute a two-person operation can be any authorized user, whereas the second user can be any authorized user different from the first [R.S. Sandhu., and P Samarati, “Access Control: Principles and Practice,” IEEE Communications Magazine 32(9), September 1994, pp. 40-48.]. There are various types of SOD, an important one is history-based SOD that regulate for example, the same subject (role) cannot access the same object for variable number of times.

senses.definitionMd: refers to the principle that no user should be given enough privileges to misuse the system on their own. For example, the person authorizing a paycheck should not also be the one who can prepare them. Separation of duties can be enforced either statically (by defining conflicting roles, i.e., roles which cannot be executed by the same user) or dynamically (by enforcing the control at access time). An example of dynamic separation of duty is the two-person rule. The first user to execute a two-person operation can be any authorized user, whereas the second user can be any authorized user different from the first [R.S. Sandhu., and P Samarati, “Access Control: Principles and Practice,” IEEE Communications Magazine 32(9), September 1994, pp. 40-48.]. There are various types of SOD, an important one is history-based SOD that regulate for example, the same subject (role) cannot access the same object for variable number of times.

entries.title: Sequence
entries.summaryMd: An ordered set of quantities.

senses.definitionMd: An ordered set of quantities.

entries.title: Serial Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the number of occurrences of m-bit overlapping patterns is approximately the same as would be expected for a random sequence.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of this test is to determine whether the number of occurrences of m-bit overlapping patterns is approximately the same as would be expected for a random sequence.

entries.title: Server
entries.summaryMd: A computer or device on a network that manages network resources. Examples include file servers (to store files), print servers (to manage one or more printers), network servers (to manage network traffic), and database servers (to process database queries).

senses.definitionMd: A computer or device on a network that manages network resources. Examples include file servers (to store files), print servers (to manage one or more printers), network servers (to manage network traffic), and database servers (to process database queries).

entries.title: service
entries.summaryMd: Performance of activities, work, or duties.

senses.definitionMd: Performance of activities, work, or duties.

entries.title: service authority
entries.summaryMd: See service authority.

senses.definitionMd: See service authority.

entries.title: Service Composition
entries.summaryMd: Aggregation of multiple small services into larger services.

senses.definitionMd: Aggregation of multiple small services into larger services.

entries.title: Service Description
entries.summaryMd: A set of documents that describe the interface to and semantics of a service.

senses.definitionMd: A set of documents that describe the interface to and semantics of a service.

entries.title: Service Interface
entries.summaryMd: The abstract boundary that a service exposes. It defines the types of messages and the message exchange patterns that are involved in interacting with the service, together with any conditions implied by those messages.

senses.definitionMd: The abstract boundary that a service exposes. It defines the types of messages and the message exchange patterns that are involved in interacting with the service, together with any conditions implied by those messages.

entries.title: service level agreement (SLA)
entries.summaryMd: Defines the specific responsibilities of the service provider and sets the customer expectations.

senses.definitionMd: Defines the specific responsibilities of the service provider and sets the customer expectations.

entries.title: Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA)
entries.summaryMd: A collection of services. These services communicate with each other. The communication can involve either simple data passing or it could involve two or more services coordinating some activity.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of services. These services communicate with each other. The communication can involve either simple data passing or it could involve two or more services coordinating some activity.

entries.title: Service Provider
entries.summaryMd: A provider of basic services or value-added services for operation of a network; generally refers to public carriers and other commercial enterprises.

senses.definitionMd: A provider of basic services or value-added services for operation of a network; generally refers to public carriers and other commercial enterprises.

entries.title: Session
entries.summaryMd: A persistent interaction between a subscriber and an end point, either a relying party or a Credential Service Provider. A session begins with an authentication event and ends with a session termination event. A session is bound by use of a session secret that the subscriber’s software (a browser, application, or operating system) can present to the relying party or the Credential Service Provider in lieu of the subscriber’s authentication credentials.

senses.definitionMd: A persistent interaction between a subscriber and an end point, either a relying party or a Credential Service Provider. A session begins with an authentication event and ends with a session termination event. A session is bound by use of a session secret that the subscriber’s software (a browser, application, or operating system) can present to the relying party or the Credential Service Provider in lieu of the subscriber’s authentication credentials.

entries.title: set point
entries.summaryMd: An input variable that sets the desired value of the controlled variable. This variable may be manually set, automatically set, or programmed.

senses.definitionMd: An input variable that sets the desired value of the controlled variable. This variable may be manually set, automatically set, or programmed.

entries.title: set theory relationship mapping
entries.summaryMd: A concept relationship style derived from the branch of mathematics known as set theory.

senses.definitionMd: A concept relationship style derived from the branch of mathematics known as set theory.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "set theory relationship mapping"

entries.title: Setting the bar
entries.summaryMd: Setting the bar means that a decision must be made as to the complexity of the material that will be developed; it applies to all three types of learning – awareness, training, and education.

senses.definitionMd: Setting the bar means that a decision must be made as to the complexity of the material that will be developed; it applies to all three types of learning – awareness, training, and education.

entries.title: shadow model
entries.summaryMd: A model that imitates the behavior of the target model. The training datasets and the truth about membership in these datasets are known for these models. Typically, the attack model is trained on the labeled inputs and outputs of the shadow model.

senses.definitionMd: A model that imitates the behavior of the target model. The training datasets and the truth about membership in these datasets are known for these models. Typically, the attack model is trained on the labeled inputs and outputs of the shadow model.

entries.title: Shadow Stack
entries.summaryMd: A parallel hardware stack that applications can utilize to store a copy of return addresses that are checked against the normal program stack on return operations.

senses.definitionMd: A parallel hardware stack that applications can utilize to store a copy of return addresses that are checked against the normal program stack on return operations.

entries.title: Shall
entries.summaryMd: Used to indicate a requirement of this standard.

senses.definitionMd: Used to indicate a requirement of this standard.

entries.title: Sharding
entries.summaryMd: A blockchain configuration and architecture that enables the processing of transactions in parallel. The blockchain’s global state is split among multiple blockchain subnetworks coordinated by a separate hub blockchain.

senses.definitionMd: A blockchain configuration and architecture that enables the processing of transactions in parallel. The blockchain’s global state is split among multiple blockchain subnetworks coordinated by a separate hub blockchain.

entries.title: shared control
entries.summaryMd: A security or privacy control that is implemented for an information system in part as a common control and in part as a system-specific control. See hybrid control.

senses.definitionMd: A security or privacy control that is implemented for an information system in part as a common control and in part as a system-specific control. See hybrid control.

entries.title: shared secret key
entries.summaryMd: A shared secret that can be used directly as a cryptographic key in symmetric-key cryptography. It does not require additional key derivation. The shared secret key must be kept private and must be destroyed when no longer needed.

senses.definitionMd: A shared secret that can be used directly as a cryptographic key in symmetric-key cryptography. It does not require additional key derivation. The shared secret key must be kept private and must be destroyed when no longer needed.

entries.title: shielded enclosure
entries.summaryMd: Room or container designed to attenuate electromagnetic radiation, acoustic signals, or emanations.

senses.definitionMd: Room or container designed to attenuate electromagnetic radiation, acoustic signals, or emanations.

entries.title: Short Message Service Chat
entries.summaryMd: a facility for exchanging messages between mobile phone users in real-time via SMS text messaging, which allows previous messages from the same conversation to be viewed.

senses.definitionMd: a facility for exchanging messages between mobile phone users in real-time via SMS text messaging, which allows previous messages from the same conversation to be viewed.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Short Message Service Chat"

entries.title: Short Message Service (SMS)
entries.summaryMd: A cellular network facility that allows users to send and receive text messages of up to 160 alphanumeric characters on their handset.

senses.definitionMd: A cellular network facility that allows users to send and receive text messages of up to 160 alphanumeric characters on their handset.

entries.title: short-term stability
entries.summaryMd: The stability of a time or frequency signal over a short measurement interval, usually an interval of 100 seconds or less in duration.

senses.definitionMd: The stability of a time or frequency signal over a short measurement interval, usually an interval of 100 seconds or less in duration.

entries.title: short title
entries.summaryMd: Identifying combination of letters and numbers assigned to certain COMSEC materials to facilitate handling, accounting, and controlling (e.g., KAM-211, KG-175). Each item of accountable COMSEC material is assigned a short title to facilitate handling, accounting and control.

senses.definitionMd: Identifying combination of letters and numbers assigned to certain COMSEC materials to facilitate handling, accounting, and controlling (e.g., KAM-211, KG-175). Each item of accountable COMSEC material is assigned a short title to facilitate handling, accounting and control.

entries.title: short title assignment requester (STAR)
entries.summaryMd: The key management entity (KME) privileged to request assignment of a new short title and generation of key against that short title.

senses.definitionMd: The key management entity (KME) privileged to request assignment of a new short title and generation of key against that short title.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "short title assignment requester (STAR)"

entries.title: Should
entries.summaryMd: Used to indicate a strong recommendation but not a requirement of this standard. Ignoring the recommendation could result in undesirable results.

senses.definitionMd: Used to indicate a strong recommendation but not a requirement of this standard. Ignoring the recommendation could result in undesirable results.

entries.title: Shrinkage
entries.summaryMd: Product loss or theft that results in declining revenue.

senses.definitionMd: Product loss or theft that results in declining revenue.

entries.title: side channel
entries.summaryMd: Allows an attacker to infer information about a secret by observing the non­functional characteristics of a program (e.g., execution time or memory) or mea­suring or exploiting the indirect coincidental effects of the system or its hardware (e.g., power consumption variation, electromagnetic emanations) while the pro­gram is executing. Most commonly, such attacks aim to exfiltrate sensitive infor­mation, including cryptographic keys.

senses.definitionMd: Allows an attacker to infer information about a secret by observing the non­functional characteristics of a program (e.g., execution time or memory) or mea­suring or exploiting the indirect coincidental effects of the system or its hardware (e.g., power consumption variation, electromagnetic emanations) while the pro­gram is executing. Most commonly, such attacks aim to exfiltrate sensitive infor­mation, including cryptographic keys.

entries.title: Side-Channel Attack
entries.summaryMd: An attack enabled by leakage of information from a physical cryptosystem. Characteristics that could be exploited in a side-channel attack include timing, power consumption, and electromagnetic and acoustic emissions.

senses.definitionMd: An attack enabled by leakage of information from a physical cryptosystem. Characteristics that could be exploited in a side-channel attack include timing, power consumption, and electromagnetic and acoustic emissions.

entries.title: Sidechain
entries.summaryMd: A blockchain with its own consensus mechanism and set of nodes that is connected to another blockchain through a two-way bridge.

senses.definitionMd: A blockchain with its own consensus mechanism and set of nodes that is connected to another blockchain through a two-way bridge.

entries.title: sig
entries.summaryMd: A digital signature of a randomized message.

senses.definitionMd: A digital signature of a randomized message.

entries.title: signaling rate
entries.summaryMd: The signaling rate of a digital signal is defined as the reciprocal of the bit width (1/bit width). The signaling rate is used to determine the frequency range of electrical isolation.

senses.definitionMd: The signaling rate of a digital signal is defined as the reciprocal of the bit width (1/bit width). The signaling rate is used to determine the frequency range of electrical isolation.

entries.title: Signatory
entries.summaryMd: The entity that generates a digital signature on data using a private key.

senses.definitionMd: The entity that generates a digital signature on data using a private key.

entries.title: signature
entries.summaryMd: A recognizable, distinguishing pattern associated with an attack, such as a binary string in a virus or a particular set of keystrokes used to gain unauthorized access to a system.

senses.definitionMd: A recognizable, distinguishing pattern associated with an attack, such as a binary string in a virus or a particular set of keystrokes used to gain unauthorized access to a system.

entries.title: signature certificate
entries.summaryMd: A public key certificate that contains a public key intended for verifying digital signatures rather than authenticating, encrypting data or performing any other cryptographic functions.

senses.definitionMd: A public key certificate that contains a public key intended for verifying digital signatures rather than authenticating, encrypting data or performing any other cryptographic functions.

entries.title: Signature generation
entries.summaryMd: The process of using a digital signature algorithm and a private key to generate a digital signature on data.

senses.definitionMd: The process of using a digital signature algorithm and a private key to generate a digital signature on data.

entries.title: Signature-in-question
entries.summaryMd: The digital signature to be verified and validated.

senses.definitionMd: The digital signature to be verified and validated.

entries.title: Signature validation
entries.summaryMd: The (mathematical) verification of the digital signature and obtaining the appropriate assurances (e.g., public key validity, private key possession, etc.).

senses.definitionMd: The (mathematical) verification of the digital signature and obtaining the appropriate assurances (e.g., public key validity, private key possession, etc.).

entries.title: Signature verification
entries.summaryMd: The process of using a digital signature algorithm and a public key to verify a digital signature on data.

senses.definitionMd: The process of using a digital signature algorithm and a public key to verify a digital signature on data.

entries.title: Signed data
entries.summaryMd: The data or message upon which a digital signature has been computed. Also, see Message.

senses.definitionMd: The data or message upon which a digital signature has been computed. Also, see Message.

entries.title: significant consequences
entries.summaryMd: Loss of life, significant responsive actions against the United States, significant damage to property, serious adverse U.S. foreign policy consequences, or serious economic impact on the United States.

senses.definitionMd: Loss of life, significant responsive actions against the United States, significant damage to property, serious adverse U.S. foreign policy consequences, or serious economic impact on the United States.

entries.title: significant cybersecurity or privacy responsibilities
entries.summaryMd: The preferred terminology herein for identifying those whose roles in the organization necessitate ongoing role-based training. These individuals have work-related responsibilities beyond those of all users and will need to participate in both general and specialized learning program activities.

senses.definitionMd: The preferred terminology herein for identifying those whose roles in the organization necessitate ongoing role-based training. These individuals have work-related responsibilities beyond those of all users and will need to participate in both general and specialized learning program activities.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "significant cybersecurity or privacy responsibilities"

entries.title: signing key
entries.summaryMd: The cryptographic key used to create a signature. In asymmetric cryptography, the signing key refers to the private key of the cryptographic key pair. In symmetric cryptography, the signing key is the symmetric key.

senses.definitionMd: The cryptographic key used to create a signature. In asymmetric cryptography, the signing key refers to the private key of the cryptographic key pair. In symmetric cryptography, the signing key is the symmetric key.

entries.title: Similarity
entries.summaryMd: The similarity of two artifacts, as measured by a particular approximate matching algorithm, is defined as an increasing monotonic function of the number of matching features contained in their respective feature sets.

senses.definitionMd: The similarity of two artifacts, as measured by a particular approximate matching algorithm, is defined as an increasing monotonic function of the number of matching features contained in their respective feature sets.

entries.title: Similarity digest
entries.summaryMd: A similarity digest is a (compressed) representation of the original data object’s feature set that is suitable for comparison with other similarity digests created by the same algorithm. In most cases, the digest is much smaller than the original artifact and the original object is not recoverable from the digest.

senses.definitionMd: A similarity digest is a (compressed) representation of the original data object’s feature set that is suitable for comparison with other similarity digests created by the same algorithm. In most cases, the digest is much smaller than the original artifact and the original object is not recoverable from the digest.

entries.title: Similarity function
entries.summaryMd: compares two similarity digests and outputs a score. The recommended approach is to assign a score s in the 0 ≤ s ≤ 1 range, where 0 indicates no similarity and 1 indicates high similarity. This score represents a normalized estimate of the number of matching features in the feature sets corresponding to the artifacts from which the similarity digests were created.

senses.definitionMd: compares two similarity digests and outputs a score. The recommended approach is to assign a score s in the 0 ≤ s ≤ 1 range, where 0 indicates no similarity and 1 indicates high similarity. This score represents a normalized estimate of the number of matching features in the feature sets corresponding to the artifacts from which the similarity digests were created.

entries.title: Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP)
entries.summaryMd: A protocol defined in an IETF internet draft specification that is used by numerous manufacturers of network equipment and software who are developing simplified means of handling certificates for large-scale implementation to everyday users, as well as referenced in other industry standards.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol defined in an IETF internet draft specification that is used by numerous manufacturers of network equipment and software who are developing simplified means of handling certificates for large-scale implementation to everyday users, as well as referenced in other industry standards.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP)"

entries.title: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)
entries.summaryMd: An MTA protocol defined by IETF RFC 2821. SMTP is the most commonly used MTA protocol.

senses.definitionMd: An MTA protocol defined by IETF RFC 2821. SMTP is the most commonly used MTA protocol.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)"

entries.title: Simple Object Access Protocol
entries.summaryMd: An XML-based protocol for exchanging structured information in a decentralized, distributed environment.

senses.definitionMd: An XML-based protocol for exchanging structured information in a decentralized, distributed environment.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Simple Object Access Protocol"

entries.title: Simple t-way combination coverage
entries.summaryMd: For a given test set for n variables, simple t-way combination coverage is the proportion of t-way combinations of n variables for which all variable-values configurations are fully covered.

senses.definitionMd: For a given test set for n variables, simple t-way combination coverage is the proportion of t-way combinations of n variables for which all variable-values configurations are fully covered.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Simple t-way combination coverage"

entries.title: Simulators
entries.summaryMd: A functional exercise staff member who simulates or represents non-participating individuals or organizations whose input or participation is necessary to the flow of the exercise.

senses.definitionMd: A functional exercise staff member who simulates or represents non-participating individuals or organizations whose input or participation is necessary to the flow of the exercise.

entries.title: single loop controller
entries.summaryMd: A controller that controls a very small process or a critical process.

senses.definitionMd: A controller that controls a very small process or a critical process.

entries.title: single point keying (SPK)
entries.summaryMd: Means of distributing key to multiple, local crypto equipment or devices from a single fill point.

senses.definitionMd: Means of distributing key to multiple, local crypto equipment or devices from a single fill point.

entries.title: Single Sign-On
entries.summaryMd: An authentication process by which one account and its authenticators are used to access multiple applications in a seamless manner, generally implemented with a federation protocol.

senses.definitionMd: An authentication process by which one account and its authenticators are used to access multiple applications in a seamless manner, generally implemented with a federation protocol.

entries.title: Singulation
entries.summaryMd: A function performed by a reader to individually identify any tags in the reader’s operating range.

senses.definitionMd: A function performed by a reader to individually identify any tags in the reader’s operating range.

entries.title: situational awareness
entries.summaryMd: Within a volume of time and space, the perception of an enterprise’s security posture and its threat environment; the comprehension/meaning of both taken together (risk); and the projection of their status into the near future.

senses.definitionMd: Within a volume of time and space, the perception of an enterprise’s security posture and its threat environment; the comprehension/meaning of both taken together (risk); and the projection of their status into the near future.

entries.title: Skill
entries.summaryMd: The capacity to perform an observable action.

senses.definitionMd: The capacity to perform an observable action.

entries.title: Skimming
entries.summaryMd: The unauthorized use of a reader to read tags without the authorization or knowledge of tag’s owner or the individual in possession of the tag.

senses.definitionMd: The unauthorized use of a reader to read tags without the authorization or knowledge of tag’s owner or the individual in possession of the tag.

entries.title: Slack Space
entries.summaryMd: The unused space in a file allocation block or memory page that may hold residual data.

senses.definitionMd: The unused space in a file allocation block or memory page that may hold residual data.

entries.title: Small business
entries.summaryMd: Small businesses are defined differently depending on the industry sector. For this publication, the definition of a small business includes for-profit, non-profit, and similar organizations with up to 500 employees. Synonymous with “Small Enterprise or Small Organization”. See the SBA website www.sba.gov for more information.

senses.definitionMd: Small businesses are defined differently depending on the industry sector. For this publication, the definition of a small business includes for-profit, non-profit, and similar organizations with up to 500 employees. Synonymous with “Small Enterprise or Small Organization”. See the SBA website www.sba.gov for more information.

entries.title: smart card
entries.summaryMd: A credit card-sized card with embedded integrated circuits that can store, process, and communicate information.

senses.definitionMd: A credit card-sized card with embedded integrated circuits that can store, process, and communicate information.

entries.title: Smart contract
entries.summaryMd: A collection of code and data (sometimes referred to as functions and state) that is deployed using cryptographically signed transactions on the blockchain network. The smart contract is executed by nodes within the blockchain network; all nodes must derive the same results for the execution, and the results of execution are recorded on the blockchain.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of code and data (sometimes referred to as functions and state) that is deployed using cryptographically signed transactions on the blockchain network. The smart contract is executed by nodes within the blockchain network; all nodes must derive the same results for the execution, and the results of execution are recorded on the blockchain.

entries.title: smart data
entries.summaryMd: Association of authority, access requirements, retention provenance and any additional information with a data object; smart data includes data provenance and data tagging.

senses.definitionMd: Association of authority, access requirements, retention provenance and any additional information with a data object; smart data includes data provenance and data tagging.

entries.title: Smart Meter
entries.summaryMd: A device that includes Metrology, Communications Module, and, optionally, HAN interface. These components are typically integrated into a single physical unit suitable for installation in a standard utility meter socket. Sub-components may or may not be integrated on the printed circuit boards contained within the Smart Meter.

senses.definitionMd: A device that includes Metrology, Communications Module, and, optionally, HAN interface. These components are typically integrated into a single physical unit suitable for installation in a standard utility meter socket. Sub-components may or may not be integrated on the printed circuit boards contained within the Smart Meter.

entries.title: SMS Chat
entries.summaryMd: A facility for exchanging messages in real-time using SMS text messaging that allows previously exchanged messages to be viewed.

senses.definitionMd: A facility for exchanging messages in real-time using SMS text messaging that allows previously exchanged messages to be viewed.

entries.title: Sn
entries.summaryMd: The nth partial sum for values Xi = {-1, +1}; i.e., the sum of the first n values of Xi.

senses.definitionMd: The nth partial sum for values Xi = {-1, +1}; i.e., the sum of the first n values of Xi.

entries.title: Snapshot
entries.summaryMd: A record of the state of a running image, generally captured as the differences between an image and the current state.

senses.definitionMd: A record of the state of a running image, generally captured as the differences between an image and the current state.

entries.title: sniffer
entries.summaryMd: See packet sniffer and passive wiretapping.

senses.definitionMd: See packet sniffer and passive wiretapping.

entries.title: SOAP Header
entries.summaryMd: A collection of zero or more blocks of information prepended to a SOAP message, each of which might be targeted at any SOAP receiver within the message path.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of zero or more blocks of information prepended to a SOAP message, each of which might be targeted at any SOAP receiver within the message path.

entries.title: SOAP Message
entries.summaryMd: The basic unit of communication between SOAP nodes.

senses.definitionMd: The basic unit of communication between SOAP nodes.

entries.title: sobs
entries.summaryMd: The observed value which is used as a statistic in the Frequency test.

senses.definitionMd: The observed value which is used as a statistic in the Frequency test.

entries.title: social engineering
entries.summaryMd: An attempt to trick someone into revealing information (e.g., a password) that can be used to attack systems or networks.

senses.definitionMd: An attempt to trick someone into revealing information (e.g., a password) that can be used to attack systems or networks.

entries.title: SOCKS Protocol
entries.summaryMd: An Internet protocol to allow client applications to form a circuit-level gateway to a network firewall via a proxy service.

senses.definitionMd: An Internet protocol to allow client applications to form a circuit-level gateway to a network firewall via a proxy service.

entries.title: Soft fork
entries.summaryMd: A change to a blockchain implementation that is backwards compatible. Non-updated nodes can continue to transact with updated nodes.

senses.definitionMd: A change to a blockchain implementation that is backwards compatible. Non-updated nodes can continue to transact with updated nodes.

entries.title: software
entries.summaryMd: Computer programs and data stored in hardware - typically in read-only memory (ROM) or programmable read-only memory (PROM) - such that the programs and data cannot be dynamically written or modified during execution of the programs.

senses.definitionMd: Computer programs and data stored in hardware - typically in read-only memory (ROM) or programmable read-only memory (PROM) - such that the programs and data cannot be dynamically written or modified during execution of the programs.

entries.title: Software as a Service (SaaS)
entries.summaryMd: The capability provided to the consumer is to use the provider’s applications running on a cloud infrastructure. The applications are accessible from various client devices through either a thin client interface, such as a web browser (e.g., web-based email), or a program interface. The consumer does not manage or control the underlying cloud infrastructure including network, servers, operating systems, storage, or even individual application capabilities, with the possible exception of limited user-specific application configuration settings.

senses.definitionMd: The capability provided to the consumer is to use the provider’s applications running on a cloud infrastructure. The applications are accessible from various client devices through either a thin client interface, such as a web browser (e.g., web-based email), or a program interface. The consumer does not manage or control the underlying cloud infrastructure including network, servers, operating systems, storage, or even individual application capabilities, with the possible exception of limited user-specific application configuration settings.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Software as a Service (SaaS)"

entries.title: Software Asset Management
entries.summaryMd: An ISCM capability that identifies unauthorized software on devices that is likely to be used by attackers as a platform from which to extend compromise of the network to be mitigated.

senses.definitionMd: An ISCM capability that identifies unauthorized software on devices that is likely to be used by attackers as a platform from which to extend compromise of the network to be mitigated.

entries.title: software assurance (SwA)
entries.summaryMd: 1. The level of confidence that software functions as intended and is free of vulnerabilities, either intentionally or unintentionally designed or inserted as part of the software throughout the lifecycle.

senses.definitionMd: 1. The level of confidence that software functions as intended and is free of vulnerabilities, either intentionally or unintentionally designed or inserted as part of the software throughout the lifecycle.

entries.title: Software Bill of Materials
entries.summaryMd: A formal record containing the details and supply chain relationships of various components used in building software. Software developers and vendors often create products by assembling existing open source and commercial software components. The SBOM enumerates these components in a product.

senses.definitionMd: A formal record containing the details and supply chain relationships of various components used in building software.
