Software developers and vendors often create products by assembling existing open source and commercial software components. The SBOM enumerates these components in a product.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Software Bill of Materials"

entries.title: Software Development Life Cycle
entries.summaryMd: A formal or informal methodology for designing, creating, and maintaining software (including code built into hardware).

senses.definitionMd: A formal or informal methodology for designing, creating, and maintaining software (including code built into hardware).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Software Development Life Cycle"

entries.title: Software Identification
entries.summaryMd: A SWID tag is an ISO 19770-2 compliant XML file describing a software product. It is typically digitally signed by the software manufacturer to verify its validity. Ideally, for purposes of software asset management, the SWID tag will contain the digests (digital fingerprints) of each software file installed or placed on the device with the product.

senses.definitionMd: A SWID tag is an ISO 19770-2 compliant XML file describing a software product. It is typically digitally signed by the software manufacturer to verify its validity. Ideally, for purposes of software asset management, the SWID tag will contain the digests (digital fingerprints) of each software file installed or placed on the device with the product.

entries.title: software identification (SWID) tag
entries.summaryMd: A set of structured data elements containing authoritative identification information about a software component.

senses.definitionMd: A set of structured data elements containing authoritative identification information about a software component.

entries.title: software product and executable file version
entries.summaryMd: A patch level versioning of the software product or digital fingerprint version of a software file.

senses.definitionMd: A patch level versioning of the software product or digital fingerprint version of a software file.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "software product and executable file version"

entries.title: software system test and evaluation process
entries.summaryMd: Process that plans, develops, and documents the qualitative/quantitative demonstration of the fulfillment of all baseline functional performance, operational, and interface requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Process that plans, develops, and documents the qualitative/quantitative demonstration of the fulfillment of all baseline functional performance, operational, and interface requirements.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "software system test and evaluation process"

entries.title: Solid-State Drive
entries.summaryMd: A storage device that uses solid-state memory to store persistent data.

senses.definitionMd: A storage device that uses solid-state memory to store persistent data.

entries.title: Source authentication
entries.summaryMd: A process that provides assurance of the source of information.

senses.definitionMd: A process that provides assurance of the source of information.

entries.title: source code control
entries.summaryMd: A capability with which an attacker controls the source code of a ma­chine learning algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: A capability with which an attacker controls the source code of a ma­chine learning algorithm.

entries.title: Source content
entries.summaryMd: Part or all of SCAP source data streams.

senses.definitionMd: Part or all of SCAP source data streams.

entries.title: Source Name
entries.summaryMd: A single WFN that a matching engine compares to a target WFN to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. (This is the X value in the CPE 2.2 matching algorithm.)

senses.definitionMd: A single WFN that a matching engine compares to a target WFN to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. (This is the X value in the CPE 2.2 matching algorithm.)

entries.title: Source of Randomness
entries.summaryMd: A component of a DRBG (which consists of a DRBG mechanism and a randomness source) that outputs bitstrings that are used as entropy input by the DRBG mechanism. The randomness source can be an entropy source or an RBG.

senses.definitionMd: A component of a DRBG (which consists of a DRBG mechanism and a randomness source) that outputs bitstrings that are used as entropy input by the DRBG mechanism. The randomness source can be an entropy source or an RBG.

entries.title: Source Restriction
entries.summaryMd: A restriction configured for an authorized key that limits the IP addresses or host names from which login using the key may take place. In some SSH implementations, source restrictions can be configured by using a "from=" restriction in an authorized keys file.

senses.definitionMd: A restriction configured for an authorized key that limits the IP addresses or host names from which login using the key may take place. In some SSH implementations, source restrictions can be configured by using a "from=" restriction in an authorized keys file.

entries.title: Source Value
entries.summaryMd: A single value that a matching engine compares to a corresponding target value to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. Source values include A-V pairs or set relation values (e.g., superset or subset).

senses.definitionMd: A single value that a matching engine compares to a corresponding target value to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. Source values include A-V pairs or set relation values (e.g., superset or subset).

entries.title: Sources Sought Notice
entries.summaryMd: A synopsis posted by a government agency that states they are seeking possible sources for a project. It is not a solicitation for work, nor is it a request for proposal.

senses.definitionMd: A synopsis posted by a government agency that states they are seeking possible sources for a project. It is not a solicitation for work, nor is it a request for proposal.

entries.title: space structures
entries.summaryMd: Any human-made assets in space, including “space debris” or “space junk” that is no longer in use for any business or mission need.

senses.definitionMd: Any human-made assets in space, including “space debris” or “space junk” that is no longer in use for any business or mission need.

entries.title: spam
entries.summaryMd: Electronic junk mail or the abuse of electronic messaging systems to indiscriminately send unsolicited bulk messages.

senses.definitionMd: Electronic junk mail or the abuse of electronic messaging systems to indiscriminately send unsolicited bulk messages.

entries.title: spear phishing
entries.summaryMd: A colloquial term that can be used to describe any highly targeted phishing attack.

senses.definitionMd: A colloquial term that can be used to describe any highly targeted phishing attack.

entries.title: special access program
entries.summaryMd: A program established for a specific class of classified information that imposes safeguarding and access requirements that exceed those normally required for information at the same classification level.

entries.title: SSH Client
entries.summaryMd: The software implementation that enables a user or an automated process to remotely access an SSH server. An SSH client is responsible for reliably performing all of the operations necessary to ensure a secure connection, including generating identity keys, prompting users to verify host keys, authenticating and establishing encrypted connections with SSH servers, prompting users for credentials, performing public key authentication, etc.

entries.title: SSH Server
entries.summaryMd: A software implementation that enables SSH access to a system from SSH clients. SSH server may be included with an operating system or appliance or may be add-on software. An SSH server is typically a complex set of software modules responsible for a broad number of tasks, including enforcing configured SSH settings, authenticating users, limiting access to certain users and groups, ensuring secure connections, interfacing with other systems (e.g., PAM and Kerberos), performing file transfers, etc.

entries.title: stability
entries.summaryMd: An inherent characteristic of an oscillator that determines how well it can produce the same frequency over a given time interval. Stability does not indicate whether the frequency is right or wrong, but only whether it stays the same. The stability of an oscillator does not necessarily change when the frequency offset changes. An oscillator can be adjusted, and its frequency moved either further away from or closer to its nominal frequency without changing its stability at all. The stability of an oscillator is usually specified by a statistic, such as the Allan deviation, that estimates the frequency fluctuations of the device over a given time interval. Some devices, such as an OCXO [Oven Controlled Crystal (Xtal) Oscillator] have good short-term stability and poor long-term stability. Other devices, such as a GPS disciplined oscillator (GPSDO), typically have poor short-term stability and good long-term stability.

Static code analyzers are designed to review bodies of source code (at the programming language level) or compiled code (at the machine language level) to identify poor coding practices. Static code analyzers provide feedback to developers during the code development phase on security flaws that might be introduced into code.

The mathematical formulation of the independence of events A and B is the probability of the occurrence of both A and B being equal to the product of the probabilities of A and B (i.e., P(A and B) = P(A)P(B)).

entries.title: Stochastic model
entries.summaryMd: A stochastic model is a mathematical description (of the relevant properties) of an entropy source using random variables. A stochastic model used for an entropy source analysis is used to support the estimation of the entropy of the digitized data and finally of the raw data. In particular, the model is intended to provide a family of distributions, which contains the true (but unknown) distribution of the noise source outputs. Moreover, the stochastic model should allow an understanding of the factors that may affect the entropy. The distribution of the entropy source needs to remain in the family of distributions, even if the quality of the digitized data goes down.

entries.summaryMd: A field in an X.509 certificate that identifies one or more fully qualified domain names, IP addresses, email addresses, URIs, or UPNs to be associated with the public key contained in a certificate.

senses.definitionMd: A field in an X.509 certificate that identifies one or more fully qualified domain names, IP addresses, email addresses, URIs, or UPNs to be associated with the public key contained in a certificate.

entries.title: Subject (in a certificate)
entries.summaryMd: The entity authorized to use the private key associated with the public key in the certificate.

senses.definitionMd: The entity authorized to use the private key associated with the public key in the certificate.

entries.title: Subkey
entries.summaryMd: A secret string that is derived from the key.

senses.definitionMd: A secret string that is derived from the key.

entries.title: Subkey Generation
entries.summaryMd: An algorithm that derives subkeys from a key.

senses.definitionMd: An algorithm that derives subkeys from a key.

entries.title: Submitter
entries.summaryMd: The party that submits the entire entropy source and output from its components for validation. The submitter can be any entity that can provide validation information as required by this Recommendation (e.g., developer, designer, vendor or any organization).

senses.definitionMd: The party that submits the entire entropy source and output from its components for validation. The submitter can be any entity that can provide validation information as required by this Recommendation (e.g., developer, designer, vendor or any organization).

entries.title: subordinate certificate authority
entries.summaryMd: In a hierarchical public key infrastructure (PKI), a certificate authority (CA) whose certificate signing key is certified by another CA, and whose activities are constrained by that other CA. See superior certification authority.

senses.definitionMd: In a hierarchical public key infrastructure (PKI), a certificate authority (CA) whose certificate signing key is certified by another CA, and whose activities are constrained by that other CA. See superior certification authority.

entries.title: subsampling
entries.summaryMd: An algorithmic strategy where the query output is computed using only a fraction of the original data, selected at random.

senses.definitionMd: An algorithmic strategy where the query output is computed using only a fraction of the original data, selected at random.

entries.title: subscriber
entries.summaryMd: An entity that has applied for and received a certificate from a Certificate Authority.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that has applied for and received a certificate from a Certificate Authority.

entries.title: subscriber account
entries.summaryMd: An account established by the CSP for each subscriber enrolled in its identity service that contains information about the subscriber and a record of any authenticators registered to the subscriber.

senses.definitionMd: An account established by the CSP for each subscriber enrolled in its identity service that contains information about the subscriber and a record of any authenticators registered to the subscriber.

entries.title: subscriber-controlled wallet
entries.summaryMd: A type of IdP that is issued attribute bundles by the CSP. The subscriber-controlled wallet that is either housed on a subscriber-controlled device (sometimes known as a digital wallet) or as a remote service (sometimes known as a cloud wallet).

senses.definitionMd: A type of IdP that is issued attribute bundles by the CSP. The subscriber-controlled wallet that is either housed on a subscriber-controlled device (sometimes known as a digital wallet) or as a remote service (sometimes known as a cloud wallet).

entries.title: Subscriber Identity Module (SIM)
entries.summaryMd: A smart card chip specialized for use in GSM equipment.

senses.definitionMd: A smart card chip specialized for use in GSM equipment.

entries.title: subsystem
entries.summaryMd: A major subdivision or component of an information system consisting of information, information technology, and personnel that performs one or more specific functions.

senses.definitionMd: A major subdivision or component of an information system consisting of information, information technology, and personnel that performs one or more specific functions.

entries.title: Successor
entries.summaryMd: In the RBG-based construction of IVs, the result of one or more applications of the appropriate incrementing function to a direct random string.

senses.definitionMd: In the RBG-based construction of IVs, the result of one or more applications of the appropriate incrementing function to a direct random string.

entries.title: Suitability and Credentialing Executive Agent
entries.summaryMd: Individual responsible for prescribing suitability standards and minimum standards of fitness for employment. With the issuance of Executive Order 13467, as amended, the Suitability and Credentialing Executive Agent is responsible for the development, implementation, and oversight of effective, efficient, and uniform policies and procedures governing the conduct of investigations and adjudications for Suitability, Fitness, and Credentialing determinations in the Federal Government. Pursuant to Sections 1103 and 1104 of Title 5, United States Code, and the Civil Service Rules, the director of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is the Suitability and Credentialing Executive Agent.

entries.title: Suite A
entries.summaryMd: A specific set of classified cryptographic algorithms used for the protection of some categories of restricted mission critical information.

senses.definitionMd: A specific set of classified cryptographic algorithms used for the protection of some categories of restricted mission critical information.

entries.title: Suite B
entries.summaryMd: A specific set of cryptographic algorithms suitable for protecting both classified and unclassified national security systems, classified national security information, and sensitive information throughout the U.S. government and to support interoperability with allies and coalition partners.

senses.definitionMd: A specific set of cryptographic algorithms suitable for protecting both classified and unclassified national security systems, classified national security information, and sensitive information throughout the U.S. government and to support interoperability with allies and coalition partners.

entries.title: Suite B compatible
entries.summaryMd: An information assurance (IA) or IA-enabled information technology (IT) product that: a. Uses National Security Agency (NSA)-approved public standards-based security protocols. If none are available with the necessary functionality, then uses a NSA-approved security protocol; b. Includes (as selectable capabilities) all of the Suite B cryptographic algorithms that are functionally supported by the NSA-approved security protocol(s); and c. Has been evaluated or validated in accordance with NSTISSP 11.

senses.definitionMd: An information assurance (IA) or IA-enabled information technology (IT) product that: a. Uses National Security Agency (NSA)-approved public standards-based security protocols. If none are available with the necessary functionality, then uses a NSA-approved security protocol; b. Includes (as selectable capabilities) all of the Suite B cryptographic algorithms that are functionally supported by the NSA-approved security protocol(s); and c. Has been evaluated or validated in accordance with NSTISSP 11.

entries.title: summation query
entries.summaryMd: A query that sums a derived quantity from each row in a dataset with a particular property.

senses.definitionMd: A query that sums a derived quantity from each row in a dataset with a particular property.

entries.title: superencryption
entries.summaryMd: 2. An encryption operation for which the plaintext input to be transformed is the ciphertext output of a previous encryption operation.

senses.definitionMd: 2. An encryption operation for which the plaintext input to be transformed is the ciphertext output of a previous encryption operation.

entries.title: superior certification authority
entries.summaryMd: In a hierarchical public key infrastructure (PKI), a certification authority (CA) who has certified the certificate signature key of another CA, and who constrains the activities of that CA. See subordinate certification authority.

senses.definitionMd: In a hierarchical public key infrastructure (PKI), a certification authority (CA) who has certified the certificate signature key of another CA, and who constrains the activities of that CA. See subordinate certification authority.

entries.title: supersession
entries.summaryMd: The scheduled or unscheduled replacement of COMSEC material with a different edition.

senses.definitionMd: The scheduled or unscheduled replacement of COMSEC material with a different edition.

entries.title: superuser
entries.summaryMd: A user that is authorized (and therefore, trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform.

senses.definitionMd: A user that is authorized (and therefore, trusted) to perform security-relevant functions that ordinary users are not authorized to perform.

entries.title: supervised learning
entries.summaryMd: A type of machine learning in which a model learns to predict explicit (often human-generated) labels or output values for data.

senses.definitionMd: A type of machine learning in which a model learns to predict explicit (often human-generated) labels or output values for data.

entries.title: supervisory control
entries.summaryMd: A term that is used to imply that the output of a controller or computer program is used as input to other controllers.

senses.definitionMd: A term that is used to imply that the output of a controller or computer program is used as input to other controllers.

entries.title: supervisory control and data acquisition
entries.summaryMd: A generic name for a computerized system that is capable of gathering and processing data and applying operational controls over long distances. Typical uses include power transmission and distribution and pipeline systems. SCADA was designed for the unique communication challenges (e.g., delays, data integrity) posed by the various media that must be used, such as phone lines, microwave, and satellite. Usually shared rather than dedicated.

senses.definitionMd: A generic name for a computerized system that is capable of gathering and processing data and applying operational controls over long distances. Typical uses include power transmission and distribution and pipeline systems. SCADA was designed for the unique communication challenges (e.g., delays, data integrity) posed by the various media that must be used, such as phone lines, microwave, and satellite. Usually shared rather than dedicated.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "supervisory control and data acquisition"

entries.title: supplemental controls
entries.summaryMd: Controls that may be added to address specific threats or attacks in addition to those controls specified in the assurance levels in these guidelines.

senses.definitionMd: Controls that may be added to address specific threats or attacks in addition to those controls specified in the assurance levels in these guidelines.

entries.title: supplier
entries.summaryMd: Organization or an individual that enters into an agreement with the acquirer for the supply of a product or service.

senses.definitionMd: Organization or an individual that enters into an agreement with the acquirer for the supply of a product or service.

entries.title: Supplier’s Declaration of Conformity
entries.summaryMd: Declaration where the conformity assessment activity is performed by the person or organization that provides the ‘object’ (such as product, process, management system, person or body) and the supplier provides written confidence of conformity.

senses.definitionMd: Declaration where the conformity assessment activity is performed by the person or organization that provides the ‘object’ (such as product, process, management system, person or body) and the supplier provides written confidence of conformity.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Supplier’s Declaration of Conformity"

entries.title: supply chain
entries.summaryMd: Linked set of resources and processes between multiple tiers of developers that begins with the sourcing of products and services and extends through the design, development, manufacturing, processing, handling, and delivery of products and services to the acquirer.

senses.definitionMd: Linked set of resources and processes between multiple tiers of developers that begins with the sourcing of products and services and extends through the design, development, manufacturing, processing, handling, and delivery of products and services to the acquirer.

entries.title: supply chain assurance
entries.summaryMd: Confidence that the supply chain will produce and deliver elements, processes, and information that function as expected.

senses.definitionMd: Confidence that the supply chain will produce and deliver elements, processes, and information that function as expected.

entries.title: supply chain attack
entries.summaryMd: Attacks that allow the adversary to utilize implants or other vulnerabilities inserted prior to installation in order to infiltrate data, or manipulate information technology hardware, software, operating systems, peripherals (information technology products) or services at any point during the life cycle.

senses.definitionMd: Attacks that allow the adversary to utilize implants or other vulnerabilities inserted prior to installation in order to infiltrate data, or manipulate information technology hardware, software, operating systems, peripherals (information technology products) or services at any point during the life cycle.

entries.title: supply chain element
entries.summaryMd: A statement about an ISCM concept that is true for a well-implemented ISCM program.

senses.definitionMd: A statement about an ISCM concept that is true for a well-implemented ISCM program.

entries.title: supply chain risk
entries.summaryMd: The risk that an adversary may sabotage, maliciously introduce unwanted function, or otherwise subvert the design, integrity, manufacturing, production, distribution, installation, operation, or maintenance of an item of supply or a system so as to surveil, deny, disrupt, or otherwise degrade the function, use, or operation of a system (Ref: The Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011).

senses.definitionMd: The risk that an adversary may sabotage, maliciously introduce unwanted function, or otherwise subvert the design, integrity, manufacturing, production, distribution, installation, operation, or maintenance of an item of supply or a system so as to surveil, deny, disrupt, or otherwise degrade the function, use, or operation of a system (Ref: The Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011).

entries.title: supply chain risk assessment
entries.summaryMd: A systematic examination of supply chain risks, likelihoods of their occurrence, and potential impacts.

senses.definitionMd: A systematic examination of supply chain risks, likelihoods of their occurrence, and potential impacts.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "supply chain risk assessment"

entries.title: supply chain risk information
entries.summaryMd: Includes, but is not limited to, information that describes or identifies: (1) Functionality of covered articles, including access to data and information system privileges; (2) Information on the user environment where a covered article is used or installed; (3) The ability of the source to produce and deliver covered articles as expected (i.e., supply chain assurance); (4) Foreign control of, or influence over, the source (e.g., foreign ownership, personal and professional ties between the source and any foreign entity, legal regime of any foreign country in which the source is headquartered or conducts operations); (5) Implications to national security, homeland security, and/or national critical functions associated with use of the covered source; (6) Vulnerability of federal systems, programs, or facilities; (7) Market alternatives to the covered source; (8) Potential impact or harm caused by the possible loss, damage, or compromise of a product, material, or service to an organization’s operations or mission; (9) Likelihood of a potential impact or harm, or the exploitability of a system; (10) Security, authenticity, and integrity of covered articles and their supply and compilation chain; (11) Capacity to mitigate risks identified; (12) Credibility of and confidence in other supply chain risk information; (13) Any other information that would factor into an analysis of the security, integrity, resilience, quality, trustworthiness, or authenticity of covered articles or sources; (14) A summary of the above information and, any other information determined to be relevant to the determination of supply chain risk.

senses.definitionMd: Includes, but is not limited to, information that describes or identifies: (1) Functionality of covered articles, including access to data and information system privileges; (2) Information on the user environment where a covered article is used or installed; (3) The ability of the source to produce and deliver covered articles as expected (i.e., supply chain assurance); (4) Foreign control of, or influence over, the source (e.g., foreign ownership, personal and professional ties between the source and any foreign entity, legal regime of any foreign country in which the source is headquartered or conducts operations); (5) Implications to national security, homeland security, and/or national critical functions associated with use of the covered source; (6) Vulnerability of federal systems, programs, or facilities; (7) Market alternatives to the covered source; (8) Potential impact or harm caused by the possible loss, damage, or compromise of a product, material, or service to an organization’s operations or mission; (9) Likelihood of a potential impact or harm, or the exploitability of a system; (10) Security, authenticity, and integrity of covered articles and their supply and compilation chain; (11) Capacity to mitigate risks identified; (12) Credibility of and confidence in other supply chain risk information; (13) Any other information that would factor into an analysis of the security, integrity, resilience, quality, trustworthiness, or authenticity of covered articles or sources; (14) A summary of the above information and, any other information determined to be relevant to the determination of supply chain risk.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "supply chain risk information"

entries.title: supply chain risk management (SCRM)
entries.summaryMd: A systematic process for managing supply chain risk by identifying susceptibilities, vulnerabilities, and threats throughout the supply chain and developing mitigation strategies to combat those threats whether presented by the supplier, the supplies product and its subcomponents, or the supply chain (e.g., initial production, packaging, handling, storage, transport, mission operation, and disposal).

senses.definitionMd: A systematic process for managing supply chain risk by identifying susceptibilities, vulnerabilities, and threats throughout the supply chain and developing mitigation strategies to combat those threats whether presented by the supplier, the supplies product and its subcomponents, or the supply chain (e.g., initial production, packaging, handling, storage, transport, mission operation, and disposal).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "supply chain risk management (SCRM)"

entries.title: Support
entries.summaryMd: To be capable of providing a service or perform a function that is required or desired; to agree with a policy or position; to fulfill requirements.

senses.definitionMd: To be capable of providing a service or perform a function that is required or desired; to agree with a policy or position; to fulfill requirements.

entries.title: Support a security strength
entries.summaryMd: A security strength of s bits is said to be supported by a particular choice of algorithm, primitive, auxiliary function, parameters (etc.) for use in the implementation of a cryptographic mechanism if that choice will not prevent the resulting implementation from attaining a security strength of at least s bits. In this Recommendation, it is assume that implementation choices are intended to support a security strenght of 112 bits or more (see [NIST SP 800-57] and [NIST SP 800-131A])

entries.title: Support Vector Machines
entries.summaryMd: Models that implement a decision function in the form of a hy­perplane that serves to separate (i.e., classify) observations that belong to one class from another based on patterns of information about those observations (i.e., features).

senses.definitionMd: Models that implement a decision function in the form of a hy­perplane that serves to separate (i.e., classify) observations that belong to one class from another based on patterns of information about those observations (i.e., features).

entries.title: Supporting Capabilities
entries.summaryMd: Capabilities that provide functionality that supports the other IoT capabilities. Examples of supporting capabilities are device management, cybersecurity, and privacy capabilities.

senses.definitionMd: Capabilities that provide functionality that supports the other IoT capabilities. Examples of supporting capabilities are device management, cybersecurity, and privacy capabilities.

entries.title: Supporting Parties
entries.summaryMd: Providers of external system services to the manufacturer through a variety of consumer-producer relationships including but not limited to: joint ventures; business partnerships; outsourcing arrangements (i.e., through contracts, interagency agreements, lines of business arrangements); licensing agreements; and/or supply chain exchanges. Supporting services include, for example, Telecommunications, engineering services, power, water, software, tech support, and security.

senses.definitionMd: Providers of external system services to the manufacturer through a variety of consumer-producer relationships including but not limited to: joint ventures; business partnerships; outsourcing arrangements (i.e., through contracts, interagency agreements, lines of business arrangements); licensing agreements; and/or supply chain exchanges. Supporting services include, for example, Telecommunications, engineering services, power, water, software, tech support, and security.

entries.title: Supporting Services
entries.summaryMd: Providers of external system services to the manufacturer through a variety of consumer-producer relationships including but not limited to: joint ventures; business partnerships; outsourcing arrangements (i.e., through contracts, interagency agreements, lines of business arrangements); licensing agreements; and/or supply chain exchanges. Supporting services include, for example, Telecommunications, engineering services, power, water, software, tech support, and security.

entries.title: supportive relationship mapping
entries.summaryMd: A concept relationship style that identifies how one concept can or does help achieve another concept.

senses.definitionMd: A concept relationship style that identifies how one concept can or does help achieve another concept.

entries.title: suppression
entries.summaryMd: One of the most commonly used ways of protecting sensitive cells in a table is via suppression. It is obvious that in a row or column with a suppressed sensitive cell, at least one additional cell must be suppressed, or the value in the sensitive cell could be calculated exactly by subtraction from the marginal total. For this reason, certain other cells must also be suppressed. These are referred to as secondary suppressions.

senses.definitionMd: One of the most commonly used ways of protecting sensitive cells in a table is via suppression. It is obvious that in a row or column with a suppressed sensitive cell, at least one additional cell must be suppressed, or the value in the sensitive cell could be calculated exactly by subtraction from the marginal total. entries.title: suppression measure
entries.summaryMd: Action, procedure, modification, or device that reduces the level of, or inhibits the generation of, compromising emanations in an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Action, procedure, modification, or device that reduces the level of, or inhibits the generation of, compromising emanations in an information system.

entries.title: Surge Protector
entries.summaryMd: A device designed to protect electrical devices from voltage spikes or dips.

senses.definitionMd: A device designed to protect electrical devices from voltage spikes or dips.

entries.title: survivability
entries.summaryMd: The ability of a system to minimize the impact of a finite-duration disturbance on value delivery (i.e., stakeholder benefit at cost), achieved through the reduction of the likelihood or magnitude of a disturbance; the satisfaction of a minimally acceptable level of value delivery during and after a disturbance; and/or a timely recovery.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of a system to minimize the impact of a finite-duration disturbance on value delivery (i.e., stakeholder benefit at cost), achieved through the reduction of the likelihood or magnitude of a disturbance; the satisfaction of a minimally acceptable level of value delivery during and after a disturbance; and/or a timely recovery.

entries.title: susceptibility
entries.summaryMd: The inability to avoid adversity.

senses.definitionMd: The inability to avoid adversity.

entries.title: Suspended state
entries.summaryMd: A lifecycle state of a key whereby the use of the key for applying cryptographic protection has been temporarily suspended.

senses.definitionMd: A lifecycle state of a key whereby the use of the key for applying cryptographic protection has been temporarily suspended.

entries.title: suspension
entries.summaryMd: The process of changing the status of a valid certificate to suspended (i.e., temporarily invalid).

senses.definitionMd: The process of changing the status of a valid certificate to suspended (i.e., temporarily invalid).

entries.title: SWID Tag
entries.summaryMd: A SWID tag is an ISO 19770-2 compliant XML file describing a software product. It is typically digitally signed by the software manufacturer to verify its validity. Ideally, for purposes of software asset management, the SWID tag will contain the digests (digital fingerprints) of each software file installed or placed on the device with the product.

senses.definitionMd: A SWID tag is an ISO 19770-2 compliant XML file describing a software product. It is typically digitally signed by the software manufacturer to verify its validity. Ideally, for purposes of software asset management, the SWID tag will contain the digests (digital fingerprints) of each software file installed or placed on the device with the product.

entries.title: Switch
entries.summaryMd: A device that channels incoming data from any of multiple input ports to the specific output port that will take the data toward its intended destination.

senses.definitionMd: A device that channels incoming data from any of multiple input ports to the specific output port that will take the data toward its intended destination.

entries.title: Sybil Attack
entries.summaryMd: A cybersecurity attack wherein an attacker creates multiple accounts and pretends to be many persons at once.

senses.definitionMd: A cybersecurity attack wherein an attacker creates multiple accounts and pretends to be many persons at once.

entries.title: syllabary
entries.summaryMd: List of individual letters, combination of letters, or syllables, with their equivalent code groups, used for spelling out words or proper names not present in the vocabulary of a code. A syllabary may also be a spelling table.

senses.definitionMd: List of individual letters, combination of letters, or syllables, with their equivalent code groups, used for spelling out words or proper names not present in the vocabulary of a code. A syllabary may also be a spelling table.

entries.title: Symbol
entries.summaryMd: The value of the noise source output (i.e., sample value).

senses.definitionMd: The value of the noise source output (i.e., sample value).

entries.title: Symmetric Card Authentication Key Authentication (SYM-CAK)
entries.summaryMd: An authentication mechanism where the PIV Card is identified using the CHUID or another data element, and then the card responds to a challenge by signing the challenge value with the symmetric card authentication key. This mechanism is deprecated.

senses.definitionMd: An authentication mechanism where the PIV Card is identified using the CHUID or another data element, and then the card responds to a challenge by signing the challenge value with the symmetric card authentication key. This mechanism is deprecated.

entries.title: Symmetric Cryptography
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic algorithm that uses the same secret key for its operation and, if applicable, for reversing the effects of the operation (e.g., an AES key for encryption and decryption).

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic algorithm that uses the same secret key for its operation and, if applicable, for reversing the effects of the operation (e.g., an AES key for encryption and decryption).

entries.title: symmetric encryption algorithm
entries.summaryMd: Encryption algorithms using the same secret key for encryption and decryption.

senses.definitionMd: Encryption algorithms using the same secret key for encryption and decryption.

entries.title: symmetric key
entries.summaryMd: A cryptographic key that is used to perform both the cryptographic operation and its inverse (e.g., to encrypt, decrypt, create a message authentication code, or verify a message authentication code).

senses.definitionMd: A cryptographic key that is used to perform both the cryptographic operation and its inverse (e.g., to encrypt, decrypt, create a message authentication code, or verify a message authentication code).

entries.title: sync fabric
entries.summaryMd: Any on-premises, cloud-based, or hybrid service used to store, transmit, or manage authentication keys generated by syncable authenticators that are not local to the user’s device.

senses.definitionMd: Any on-premises, cloud-based, or hybrid service used to store, transmit, or manage authentication keys generated by syncable authenticators that are not local to the user’s device.

entries.title: syncable authenticators
entries.summaryMd: Software or hardware cryptographic authenticators that allow authentication keys to be cloned and exported to other storage in order to sync those keys to other authenticators (i.e., devices).

senses.definitionMd: Software or hardware cryptographic authenticators that allow authentication keys to be cloned and exported to other storage in order to sync those keys to other authenticators (i.e., devices).

entries.title: synchronization
entries.summaryMd: The process of setting two or more clocks to the same time.

senses.definitionMd: The process of setting two or more clocks to the same time.

entries.title: Synchronization Protocols
entries.summaryMd: Protocols that allow users to view, modify, and transfer/update data between a cell phone and personal computer.

senses.definitionMd: Protocols that allow users to view, modify, and transfer/update data between a cell phone and personal computer.

entries.title: synchronous crypto-operation
entries.summaryMd: Method of on-line cryptographic operation in which cryptographic equipment and associated terminals have timing systems to keep them in step.

senses.definitionMd: Method of on-line cryptographic operation in which cryptographic equipment and associated terminals have timing systems to keep them in step.

entries.title: synchronous training
entries.summaryMd: Training in which instructors and learners are scheduled to participate together in a virtual or physical classroom-based learning environment.

senses.definitionMd: Training in which instructors and learners are scheduled to participate together in a virtual or physical classroom-based learning environment.

entries.title: Syntactic matching
entries.summaryMd: uses internal structures present in digital objects. For example, the structure of a TCP network packet is defined by an international standard and matching tools can make use of this structure during network packet analysis to match the source, destination or content of the packet. Syntax-sensitive similarity measurements are specific to a particular class of objects that share an encoding but require no interpretation of the content to produce meaningful results.

entries.title: Syntax

entries.title: synthetic data generation
entries.summaryMd: A process in which seed data are used to create artificial data that have some of the statistical characteristics of the seed data.

senses.definitionMd: A process in which seed data are used to create artificial data that have some of the statistical characteristics of the seed data.

entries.title: synthetic dataset
entries.summaryMd: The absolute error divided by the unaltered query output.

senses.definitionMd: The absolute error divided by the unaltered query output.

entries.title: Synthetic Identifier
entries.summaryMd: An identifier that is assigned to an asset in the context of some management domain.

senses.definitionMd: An identifier that is assigned to an asset in the context of some management domain.

entries.title: synthetic identity fraud
entries.summaryMd: The use of a combination of personal information to fabricate a person or entity to commit a dishonest act for personal or financial gain.

senses.definitionMd: The use of a combination of personal information to fabricate a person or entity to commit a dishonest act for personal or financial gain.

entries.title: syntonization
entries.summaryMd: The process of setting two or more oscillators to the same frequency.

senses.definitionMd: The process of setting two or more oscillators to the same frequency.

entries.title: Syslog
entries.summaryMd: A protocol that specifies a general log entry format and a log entry transport mechanism.

senses.definitionMd: A protocol that specifies a general log entry format and a log entry transport mechanism.

entries.title: system
entries.summaryMd: See information system.

senses.definitionMd: See information system.

entries.title: system administrator (SA)
entries.summaryMd: Individual responsible for the installation and maintenance of an information system, providing effective information system utilization, adequate security parameters, and sound implementation of established Information Assurance policy and procedures.

senses.definitionMd: Individual responsible for the installation and maintenance of an information system, providing effective information system utilization, adequate security parameters, and sound implementation of established Information Assurance policy and procedures.

entries.title: System Assurance
entries.summaryMd: The justified confidence that the system functions as intended and is free of exploitable vulnerabilities, either intentionally or unintentionally designed or inserted as part of the system at any time during the life cycle.

senses.definitionMd: The justified confidence that the system functions as intended and is free of exploitable vulnerabilities, either intentionally or unintentionally designed or inserted as part of the system at any time during the life cycle.

entries.title: System authority
entries.summaryMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible to executive-level management (e.g., the Chief Information Officer) for the overall operation and security of an FCKMS. A system authority manages all operational FCKMS roles.

senses.definitionMd: An FCKMS role that is responsible to executive-level management (e.g., the Chief Information Officer) for the overall operation and security of an FCKMS. A system authority manages all operational FCKMS roles.

entries.title: system boundary
entries.summaryMd: All components of an information system to be authorized for operation by an authorizing official and excludes separately authorized systems, to which the information system is connected.

senses.definitionMd: All components of an information system to be authorized for operation by an authorizing official and excludes separately authorized systems, to which the information system is connected.

entries.title: System Categorization
entries.summaryMd: The characterization of a manufacturing system, its components, and operations, based on an assessment of the potential impact that a loss of availability, integrity, or confidentiality would have on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.

senses.definitionMd: The characterization of a manufacturing system, its components, and operations, based on an assessment of the potential impact that a loss of availability, integrity, or confidentiality would have on organizational operations, organizational assets, or individuals.

entries.title: system component
entries.summaryMd: A discrete identifiable information technology asset that represents a building block of a system and may include hardware, software, and firmware.

senses.definitionMd: A discrete identifiable information technology asset that represents a building block of a system and may include hardware, software, and firmware.

entries.title: system context
entries.summaryMd: The specific system elements, boundaries, interconnections, interactions, and operational environment that define a system.

senses.definitionMd: The specific system elements, boundaries, interconnections, interactions, and operational environment that define a system.

entries.title: System Developer
entries.summaryMd: An individual group, or organization that develops hardware/software for distribution or sale.

senses.definitionMd: An individual group, or organization that develops hardware/software for distribution or sale.

entries.title: System Development Life Cycle (SDLC)
entries.summaryMd: The scope of activities associated with a system, encompassing the system’s initiation, development and acquisition, implementation, operation and maintenance, and ultimately its disposal.

senses.definitionMd: The scope of activities associated with a system, encompassing the system’s initiation, development and acquisition, implementation, operation and maintenance, and ultimately its disposal.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "System Development Life Cycle (SDLC)"

entries.title: system element
entries.summaryMd: See system component.

senses.definitionMd: See system component.

entries.title: System Flash Memory
entries.summaryMd: The non-volatile storage location of system BIOS, typically in electronically erasable programmable read-only memory (EEPROM) flash memory on the motherboard. While system flash memory is a technology-specific term, guidelines in this document referring to the system flash memory are intended to apply to any non-volatile storage medium containing the system BIOS.

senses.definitionMd: The non-volatile storage location of system BIOS, typically in electronically erasable programmable read-only memory (EEPROM) flash memory on the motherboard. While system flash memory is a technology-specific term, guidelines in this document referring to the system flash memory are intended to apply to any non-volatile storage medium containing the system BIOS.

entries.title: system high
entries.summaryMd: Highest security level supported by an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Highest security level supported by an information system.

entries.title: system high mode
entries.summaryMd: Information systems security mode of operation wherein each user, with direct or indirect access to the information system, its peripherals, remote terminals, or remote hosts, has all of the following: 1) valid security clearance for all information within an information system; 2) formal access approval and signed nondisclosure agreements for all the information stored and/or processed (including all compartments, sub compartments and/or special access programs); and 3) valid need-to- know for some of the information contained within the information system. Rationale: system high, along with other related terms, has been listed for deletion.

senses.definitionMd: Information systems security mode of operation wherein each user, with direct or indirect access to the information system, its peripherals, remote terminals, or remote hosts, has all of the following: 1) valid security clearance for all information within an information system; 2) formal access approval and signed nondisclosure agreements for all the information stored and/or processed (including all compartments, sub compartments and/or special access programs); and 3) valid need-to- know for some of the information contained within the information system. Rationale: system high, along with other related terms, has been listed for deletion.

entries.title: system indicator
entries.summaryMd: Symbol or group of symbols in an off-line encrypted message identifying the specific cryptosystem or key used in the encryption.

senses.definitionMd: Symbol or group of symbols in an off-line encrypted message identifying the specific cryptosystem or key used in the encryption.

entries.title: System initialization
entries.summaryMd: A function in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key; setting up and configuring a system for secure operation.

senses.definitionMd: A function in the lifecycle of a cryptographic key; setting up and configuring a system for secure operation.

entries.title: System Integrator
entries.summaryMd: Those organizations that provide customized services to the acquirer including for example, custom development, test, operations, and maintenance.

senses.definitionMd: Those organizations that provide customized services to the acquirer including for example, custom development, test, operations, and maintenance.

entries.title: system integrity
entries.summaryMd: The quality that a system has when it performs its intended function in an unimpaired manner, free from unauthorized manipulation of the system, whether intentional or accidental.

senses.definitionMd: The quality that a system has when it performs its intended function in an unimpaired manner, free from unauthorized manipulation of the system, whether intentional or accidental.

entries.title: system interconnection
entries.summaryMd: The direct connection of two or more information systems for the purpose of sharing data and other information resources.

senses.definitionMd: The direct connection of two or more information systems for the purpose of sharing data and other information resources.

entries.title: system life cycle
entries.summaryMd: Period that begins when a system is conceived and ends when the system is no longer available for use.

senses.definitionMd: Period that begins when a system is conceived and ends when the system is no longer available for use.

entries.title: system low
entries.summaryMd: Lowest security level supported by an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Lowest security level supported by an information system.

entries.title: System Management Mode (SMM)
entries.summaryMd: A high-privilege operating mode found in x86-compatible processors used for low-level system management functions. System Management Mode is only entered after the system generates a System Management Interrupt and only executes code from a segregated block of memory.

senses.definitionMd: A high-privilege operating mode found in x86-compatible processors used for low-level system management functions. System Management Mode is only entered after the system generates a System Management Interrupt and only executes code from a segregated block of memory.

entries.title: system of record
entries.summaryMd: A system of records is a group of records under the control of a Federal agency which contains a personal identifier (such as a name, date of birth, finger print, Social Security Number, and Employee Number) and one other item of personal data (such as home address, performance rating, and blood type) from which information is retrieved using a personal identifier.

senses.definitionMd: A system of records is a group of records under the control of a Federal agency which contains a personal identifier (such as a name, date of birth, finger print, Social Security Number, and Employee Number) and one other item of personal data (such as home address, performance rating, and blood type) from which information is retrieved using a personal identifier.

entries.title: system of records
entries.summaryMd: “A group of any records under the control of any agency from which information is retrieved by the name of the individual or by some identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual.”

senses.definitionMd: “A group of any records under the control of any agency from which information is retrieved by the name of the individual or by some identifying number, symbol, or other identifying particular assigned to the individual.”

entries.title: system of records notice
entries.summaryMd: The Privacy Act requires each agency to publish a notice of its systems of records in the Federal Register. This is called a System of Record Notice (SORN).

senses.definitionMd: The Privacy Act requires each agency to publish a notice of its systems of records in the Federal Register. This is called a System of Record Notice (SORN).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "system of records notice"

entries.title: system of systems
entries.summaryMd: System of interest whose system elements are themselves systems; typically, these entail large-scale interdisciplinary problems with multiple heterogeneous distributed systems.

senses.definitionMd: System of interest whose system elements are themselves systems; typically, these entail large-scale interdisciplinary problems with multiple heterogeneous distributed systems.

entries.title: system or device certificate
entries.summaryMd: The system or device whose name appears as the subject in a certificate.

senses.definitionMd: The system or device whose name appears as the subject in a certificate.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "system or device certificate"

entries.title: system owner
entries.summaryMd: Person or organization having responsibility for the development, procurement, integration, modification, operation and maintenance, and/or final disposition of an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Person or organization having responsibility for the development, procurement, integration, modification, operation and maintenance, and/or final disposition of an information system.

entries.title: system owner (or program manager)
entries.summaryMd: An organizational official responsible for the procurement, development, integration, modification, operation, maintenance, and disposal of a system.

senses.definitionMd: An organizational official responsible for the procurement, development, integration, modification, operation, maintenance, and disposal of a system.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "system owner (or program manager)"

entries.title: system privacy officer
entries.summaryMd: Individual with assigned responsibility for maintaining the appropriate operational privacy posture for a system or program.

senses.definitionMd: Individual with assigned responsibility for maintaining the appropriate operational privacy posture for a system or program.

entries.title: System privacy requirement
entries.summaryMd: System requirements that have privacy relevance. System privacy requirements define the protection capabilities provided by the system, the performance and behavioral characteristics exhibited by the system, and the evidence used to determine that the system privacy requirements have been satisfied. Note: Each system privacy requirement is expressed in a manner that makes verification possible via analysis, observation, test, inspection, measurement, or other defined and achievable means.

senses.definitionMd: System requirements that have privacy relevance. System privacy requirements define the protection capabilities provided by the system, the performance and behavioral characteristics exhibited by the system, and the evidence used to determine that the system privacy requirements have been satisfied. Note: Each system privacy requirement is expressed in a manner that makes verification possible via analysis, observation, test, inspection, measurement, or other defined and achievable means.

entries.title: system prompt
entries.summaryMd: Application-specific instructions provided in-context to a GenAI system by the model developer or application designer. System prompts are typically prepended to other input, and may be higher-trust than other forms of input.

senses.definitionMd: Application-specific instructions provided in-context to a GenAI system by the model developer or application designer. System prompts are typically prepended to other input, and may be higher-trust than other forms of input.

entries.title: system-related privacy risk
entries.summaryMd: Risk to an individual or individuals associated with the agency’s creation, collection, use, processing, storage, maintenance, dissemination, disclosure, and disposal of their PII. See risk.

senses.definitionMd: Risk to an individual or individuals associated with the agency’s creation, collection, use, processing, storage, maintenance, dissemination, disclosure, and disposal of their PII. See risk.

entries.title: system-related security risk
entries.summaryMd: Risk that arises through the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or systems and that considers impacts to the organization (including assets, mission, functions, image, or reputation), individuals, other organizations, and the Nation. See risk.

senses.definitionMd: Risk that arises through the loss of confidentiality, integrity, or availability of information or systems and that considers impacts to the organization (including assets, mission, functions, image, or reputation), individuals, other organizations, and the Nation. See risk.

entries.title: system security officer
entries.summaryMd: Individual with assigned responsibility for maintaining the appropriate operational security posture for an information system or program.

senses.definitionMd: Individual with assigned responsibility for maintaining the appropriate operational security posture for an information system or program.

entries.title: system security plan
entries.summaryMd: Formal document that provides an overview of the security requirements for an information system and describes the security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.

senses.definitionMd: Formal document that provides an overview of the security requirements for an information system and describes the security controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.

entries.title: system security requirement
entries.summaryMd: System requirement that has security relevance. System security requirements define the protection capabilities provided by the system, the performance and behavioral characteristics exhibited by the system, and the evidence used to determine that the system security requirements have been satisfied.

senses.definitionMd: System requirement that has security relevance. System security requirements define the protection capabilities provided by the system, the performance and behavioral characteristics exhibited by the system, and the evidence used to determine that the system security requirements have been satisfied.

entries.title: system service
entries.summaryMd: A capability provided by a system that facilitates information processing, storage, or transmission.

senses.definitionMd: A capability provided by a system that facilitates information processing, storage, or transmission.

entries.title: system-specific control
entries.summaryMd: A security or privacy control for an information system that is implemented at the system level and is not inherited by any other information system.

senses.definitionMd: A security or privacy control for an information system that is implemented at the system level and is not inherited by any other information system.

entries.title: system-specific security control
entries.summaryMd: A security control for an information system that has not been designated as a common security control or the portion of a hybrid control that is to be implemented within an information system.

senses.definitionMd: A security control for an information system that has not been designated as a common security control or the portion of a hybrid control that is to be implemented within an information system.

entries.title: System Test
entries.summaryMd: A test performed on a complete system to evaluate its compliance with specified requirements.

senses.definitionMd: A test performed on a complete system to evaluate its compliance with specified requirements.

entries.title: system user
entries.summaryMd: Individual, or (system) process acting on behalf of an individual, authorized to access a system.

senses.definitionMd: Individual, or (system) process acting on behalf of an individual, authorized to access a system.

entries.title: systematic stratified sampling
entries.summaryMd: A method of sampling where samples are taken at a regular interval.

senses.definitionMd: A method of sampling where samples are taken at a regular interval.

entries.title: systemic bias
entries.summaryMd: A form of bias that results from rules, processes, or norms that advantage certain social groups and disadvantages others.

senses.definitionMd: A form of bias that results from rules, processes, or norms that advantage certain social groups and disadvantages others.

entries.title: systems engineering
entries.summaryMd: An engineering discipline whose responsibility is creating and executing an interdisciplinary process to ensure that the customer and all other stakeholder needs are satisfied in a high-quality, trustworthy, cost-efficient, and schedule-compliant manner throughout a system’s entire life cycle.

senses.definitionMd: An engineering discipline whose responsibility is creating and executing an interdisciplinary process to ensure that the customer and all other stakeholder needs are satisfied in a high-quality, trustworthy, cost-efficient, and schedule-compliant manner throughout a system’s entire life cycle.

entries.title: systems privacy engineer
entries.summaryMd: Individual assigned responsibility for conducting systems privacy engineering activities.

senses.definitionMd: Individual assigned responsibility for conducting systems privacy engineering activities.

entries.title: systems privacy engineering
entries.summaryMd: Process that captures and refines privacy requirements and ensures their integration into information technology component products and information systems through purposeful privacy design or configuration.

senses.definitionMd: Process that captures and refines privacy requirements and ensures their integration into information technology component products and information systems through purposeful privacy design or configuration.

entries.title: systems security engineer
entries.summaryMd: Individual assigned responsibility for conducting systems security engineering activities.

senses.definitionMd: Individual assigned responsibility for conducting systems security engineering activities.

entries.title: systems security engineering
entries.summaryMd: Systems security engineering is a specialty engineering field strongly related to systems engineering. It applies scientific, engineering, and information assurance principles to deliver trustworthy systems that satisfy stakeholder requirements within their established risk tolerance. See also information systems security engineering (ISSE).

senses.definitionMd: Systems security engineering is a specialty engineering field strongly related to systems engineering. It applies scientific, engineering, and information assurance principles to deliver trustworthy systems that satisfy stakeholder requirements within their established risk tolerance. See also information systems security engineering (ISSE).

entries.title: systems security officer (SSO)
entries.summaryMd: See information systems security officer (ISSO).

senses.definitionMd: See information systems security officer (ISSO).

entries.title: T
entries.summaryMd: The MAC.

senses.definitionMd: The MAC.

entries.title: (t + k)-way combination coverage
entries.summaryMd: For a given test set that provides 100% t-way coverage for n variables, (t+k)-way combination coverage is the proportion of (t+k)-way combinations of n variables for which all variable-values configurations are fully covered.

senses.definitionMd: For a given test set that provides 100% t-way coverage for n variables, (t+k)-way combination coverage is the proportion of (t+k)-way combinations of n variables for which all variable-values configurations are fully covered.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "(t + k)-way combination coverage"

entries.title: T(x, l)
entries.summaryMd: Truncation of the bit string x to the leftmost l bits of x, where l ≤ the length of x in bits

senses.definitionMd: Truncation of the bit string x to the leftmost l bits of x, where l ≤ the length of x in bits

entries.title: Tabletop Exercise
entries.summaryMd: A discussion-based exercise where personnel with roles and responsibilities in a particular IT plan meet in a classroom setting or in breakout groups to validate the content of the plan by discussing their roles during an emergency and their responses to a particular emergency situation. A facilitator initiates the discussion by presenting a scenario and asking questions based on the scenario.

senses.definitionMd: A discussion-based exercise where personnel with roles and responsibilities in a particular IT plan meet in a classroom setting or in breakout groups to validate the content of the plan by discussing their roles during an emergency and their responses to a particular emergency situation. A facilitator initiates the discussion by presenting a scenario and asking questions based on the scenario.

entries.title: tabletop materials
entries.summaryMd: Materials designed for a discussion-based exercise in which personnel with roles and responsibilities in a particular IT plan meet in a classroom setting or in breakout groups to discuss their roles during an emergency and their responses to a particular emergency situation. A facilitator initiates the discussion by presenting a scenario and asking questions based on that scenario.

senses.definitionMd: Materials designed for a discussion-based exercise in which personnel with roles and responsibilities in a particular IT plan meet in a classroom setting or in breakout groups to discuss their roles during an emergency and their responses to a particular emergency situation. A facilitator initiates the discussion by presenting a scenario and asking questions based on that scenario.

entries.title: tactical data
entries.summaryMd: Information that requires protection from disclosure and modification for a limited duration as determined by the originator or information owner.

senses.definitionMd: Information that requires protection from disclosure and modification for a limited duration as determined by the originator or information owner.

entries.title: tactical edge
entries.summaryMd: The platforms, sites, and personnel (U. S. military, allied, coalition partners, first responders) operating at lethal risk in a battle space or crisis environment characterized by 1) a dependence on information systems and connectivity for survival and mission success, 2) high threats to the operational readiness of both information systems and connectivity, and 3) users are fully engaged, highly stressed, and dependent on the availability, integrity, and transparency of their information systems.

senses.definitionMd: The platforms, sites, and personnel (U. S. military, allied, coalition partners, first responders) operating at lethal risk in a battle space or crisis environment characterized by 1) a dependence on information systems and connectivity for survival and mission success, 2) high threats to the operational readiness of both information systems and connectivity, and 3) users are fully engaged, highly stressed, and dependent on the availability, integrity, and transparency of their information systems.

entries.title: Tag
entries.summaryMd: An electronic device that communicates with RFID readers. A tag can function as a beacon or it can be used to convey information such as an identifier.

senses.definitionMd: An electronic device that communicates with RFID readers. A tag can function as a beacon or it can be used to convey information such as an identifier.

entries.title: Tag Talks First
entries.summaryMd: An RF transaction in which the tag communicates its presence to a reader. The reader may then send commands to the tag.

senses.definitionMd: An RF transaction in which the tag communicates its presence to a reader. The reader may then send commands to the tag.

entries.title: tailored control baseline
entries.summaryMd: A set of controls resulting from the application of tailoring guidance to a control baseline. See tailoring.

senses.definitionMd: A set of controls resulting from the application of tailoring guidance to a control baseline. See tailoring.

entries.title: Tailored Security Control Baseline
entries.summaryMd: A set of security controls resulting from the application of tailoring guidance to the security control baseline. See Tailoring.

senses.definitionMd: A set of security controls resulting from the application of tailoring guidance to the security control baseline. See Tailoring.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Tailored Security Control Baseline"

entries.title: tailoring
entries.summaryMd: The process by which a security control baseline is modified based on: (i) the application of scoping guidance; (ii) the specification of compensating security controls, if needed; and (iii) the specification of organization-defined parameters in the security controls via explicit assignment and selection statements.

senses.definitionMd: The process by which a security control baseline is modified based on: (i) the application of scoping guidance; (ii) the specification of compensating security controls, if needed; and (iii) the specification of organization-defined parameters in the security controls via explicit assignment and selection statements.

entries.title: tailoring assessment procedures
entries.summaryMd: The process by which assessment procedures defined in SP 800-53A are adjusted or scoped to match the characteristics of a system under assessment, providing organizations with the flexibility needed to meet specific organizational requirements and avoid overly constrained assessment approaches.

senses.definitionMd: The process by which assessment procedures defined in SP 800-53A are adjusted or scoped to match the characteristics of a system under assessment, providing organizations with the flexibility needed to meet specific organizational requirements and avoid overly constrained assessment approaches.

entries.title: tainting
entries.summaryMd: The process of embedding covert capabilities in information, systems, or system components to allow organizations to be alerted to the exfiltration of information.

senses.definitionMd: The process of embedding covert capabilities in information, systems, or system components to allow organizations to be alerted to the exfiltration of information.

entries.title: Tamper evident
entries.summaryMd: A process which makes alterations to the data easily detectable.

senses.definitionMd: A process which makes alterations to the data easily detectable.

entries.title: Tamper resistant
entries.summaryMd: A process which makes alterations to the data difficult (hard to perform), costly (expensive to perform), or both.

senses.definitionMd: A process which makes alterations to the data difficult (hard to perform), costly (expensive to perform), or both.

entries.title: tampering
entries.summaryMd: An intentional but unauthorized act resulting in the modification of a system, components of systems, its intended behavior, or data.

senses.definitionMd: An intentional but unauthorized act resulting in the modification of a system, components of systems, its intended behavior, or data.

entries.title: Target
entries.summaryMd: The set of specific IT systems or applications for which a checklist has been created.

senses.definitionMd: The set of specific IT systems or applications for which a checklist has been created.

entries.title: Target Identification and Analysis Techniques
entries.summaryMd: Information security testing techniques, mostly active and generally conducted using automated tools, that are used to identify systems, ports, services, and potential vulnerabilities. Target identification and analysis techniques include network discovery, network port and service identification, vulnerability scanning, wireless scanning, and application security testing.

senses.definitionMd: Information security testing techniques, mostly active and generally conducted using automated tools, that are used to identify systems, ports, services, and potential vulnerabilities. Target identification and analysis techniques include network discovery, network port and service identification, vulnerability scanning, wireless scanning, and application security testing.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Target Identification and Analysis Techniques"

entries.title: Target Name
entries.summaryMd: A single WFN that is the target of a matching process. A matching engine compares a source WFN to a target WFN to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. In CPE 2.2 terms a target name is a single item in the list of known values (each N of K) and is equivalent to the N value in the CPE 2.2 Matching algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: A single WFN that is the target of a matching process. A matching engine compares a source WFN to a target WFN to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. In CPE 2.2 terms a target name is a single item in the list of known values (each N of K) and is equivalent to the N value in the CPE 2.2 Matching algorithm.

entries.title: target of evaluation (TOE)
entries.summaryMd: In accordance with Common Criteria, an information system, part of a system or product, and all associated documentation, that is the subject of a security evaluation.

senses.definitionMd: In accordance with Common Criteria, an information system, part of a system or product, and all associated documentation, that is the subject of a security evaluation.

entries.title: Target Operational Environment
entries.summaryMd: The IT product’s operational environment, such as Standalone, Managed, or Custom (with description, such as Specialized Security-Limited Functionality, Legacy, or United States Government). Generally only applicable for security compliance/vulnerability checklists.

senses.definitionMd: The IT product’s operational environment, such as Standalone, Managed, or Custom (with description, such as Specialized Security-Limited Functionality, Legacy, or United States Government). Generally only applicable for security compliance/vulnerability checklists.

entries.title: Target Platform
entries.summaryMd: The target operating system or application on which a vendor product will be evaluated using a platform-specific validation lab test suite. These platform-specific test suites consist of specialized SCAP content used to perform the test procedures defined in this document.

senses.definitionMd: The target operating system or application on which a vendor product will be evaluated using a platform-specific validation lab test suite. These platform-specific test suites consist of specialized SCAP content used to perform the test procedures defined in this document.

entries.title: Target Profile
entries.summaryMd: the desired outcome or ‘to be’ state of cybersecurity implementation

senses.definitionMd: the desired outcome or ‘to be’ state of cybersecurity implementation

entries.title: Target Residual Risk
