entries.summaryMd: The amount of risk that an entity prefers to assume in the pursuit of its strategy and business objectives, knowing that management will implement, or has implemented, direct or focused actions to alter the severity of the risk.

senses.definitionMd: The amount of risk that an entity prefers to assume in the pursuit of its strategy and business objectives, knowing that management will implement, or has implemented, direct or focused actions to alter the severity of the risk.

entries.title: Target Value
entries.summaryMd: A single value that is the target of a matching process. A matching engine compares a source value to a target value to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. Source values include AV pairs or set relation values (e.g., superset or subset).

senses.definitionMd: A single value that is the target of a matching process. A matching engine compares a source value to a target value to determine whether or not there is a source-to-target match. Source values include AV pairs or set relation values (e.g., superset or subset).

entries.title: Target Vulnerability Validation Techniques
entries.summaryMd: Active information security testing techniques that corroborate the existence of vulnerabilities. They include password cracking, remote access testing, penetration testing, social engineering, and physical security testing.

senses.definitionMd: Active information security testing techniques that corroborate the existence of vulnerabilities. They include password cracking, remote access testing, penetration testing, social engineering, and physical security testing.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Target Vulnerability Validation Techniques"

entries.title: targeted poisoning attack
entries.summaryMd: A poisoning attack that changes the prediction on a small num­ber of targeted samples.

senses.definitionMd: A poisoning attack that changes the prediction on a small num­ber of targeted samples.

entries.title: Targeted security strength
entries.summaryMd: The security strength that is intended to be supported by one or more implementation-related choices (such as algorithms, primitives, auxiliary functions, parameter sizes and/or actual parameters) for the purpose of instantiating a cryptographic mechanism.

senses.definitionMd: The security strength that is intended to be supported by one or more implementation-related choices (such as algorithms, primitives, auxiliary functions, parameter sizes and/or actual parameters) for the purpose of instantiating a cryptographic mechanism.

entries.title: task
entries.summaryMd: An activity that is directed toward the achievement of organizational objectives.

senses.definitionMd: An activity that is directed toward the achievement of organizational objectives.

entries.title: Taxonomy
entries.summaryMd: A scheme of classification.

senses.definitionMd: A scheme of classification.

entries.title: Team
entries.summaryMd: A number of persons associated together in work or activity. As used in this publication, a team is a group of individuals that has been assigned by an organization’s management the responsibility and capability to carry out a defined function or set of defined functions. Designations for teams as used in this publication are simply descriptive. Different organizations may have different designations for teams that carry out the functions described herein.

senses.definitionMd: A number of persons associated together in work or activity. As used in this publication, a team is a group of individuals that has been assigned by an organization’s management the responsibility and capability to carry out a defined function or set of defined functions. Designations for teams as used in this publication are simply descriptive. Different organizations may have different designations for teams that carry out the functions described herein.

entries.title: tebibyte
entries.summaryMd: 240 bytes.

senses.definitionMd: 240 bytes.

entries.title: technical community (TC)
entries.summaryMd: Government/Industry/Academia partnerships formed around major technology areas to act like a standards body for the purpose of creating and maintaining Protection Profiles.

senses.definitionMd: Government/Industry/Academia partnerships formed around major technology areas to act like a standards body for the purpose of creating and maintaining Protection Profiles.

entries.title: technical controls
entries.summaryMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that are primarily implemented and executed by the information system through mechanisms contained in the hardware, software, or firmware components of the system.

senses.definitionMd: The security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that are primarily implemented and executed by the information system through mechanisms contained in the hardware, software, or firmware components of the system.

entries.title: technical profile
entries.summaryMd: A fully conformant subset of functionality of a protocol or standard. Technical profiles are used to enhance interoperability.

senses.definitionMd: A fully conformant subset of functionality of a protocol or standard. Technical profiles are used to enhance interoperability.

entries.title: technical reference model (TRM)
entries.summaryMd: A component-driven, technical framework that categorizes the standards and technologies to support and enable the delivery of service components and capabilities.

senses.definitionMd: A component-driven, technical framework that categorizes the standards and technologies to support and enable the delivery of service components and capabilities.

entries.title: technical risk
entries.summaryMd: The risk associated with the evolution of the design and the production of the system of interest affecting the level of performance necessary to meet the stakeholder expectations and technical requirements.

senses.definitionMd: The risk associated with the evolution of the design and the production of the system of interest affecting the level of performance necessary to meet the stakeholder expectations and technical requirements.

entries.title: technical safeguards
entries.summaryMd: The technology and the policy and procedures for its use that protect electronic protected health information and control access to it.

senses.definitionMd: The technology and the policy and procedures for its use that protect electronic protected health information and control access to it.

entries.title: technical security controls
entries.summaryMd: Security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that are primarily implemented and executed by the information system through mechanisms contained in the hardware, software, or firmware components of the system.

senses.definitionMd: Security controls (i.e., safeguards or countermeasures) for an information system that are primarily implemented and executed by the information system through mechanisms contained in the hardware, software, or firmware components of the system.

entries.title: technical security material
entries.summaryMd: Equipment, components, devices, and associated documentation or other media which pertain to cryptography, or to the security of telecommunications and information systems.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment, components, devices, and associated documentation or other media which pertain to cryptography, or to the security of telecommunications and information systems.

entries.title: technical surveillance countermeasures (TSCM)
entries.summaryMd: Techniques to detect, neutralize, and exploit technical surveillance technologies and hazards that permit the unauthorized access to or removal of information.

senses.definitionMd: Techniques to detect, neutralize, and exploit technical surveillance technologies and hazards that permit the unauthorized access to or removal of information.

entries.title: technical vulnerability information
entries.summaryMd: Detailed description of a weakness to include the implementable steps (such as code) necessary to exploit that weakness.

senses.definitionMd: Detailed description of a weakness to include the implementable steps (such as code) necessary to exploit that weakness.

entries.title: technique
entries.summaryMd: See cyber resiliency technique.

senses.definitionMd: See cyber resiliency technique.

entries.title: Technology-Based Input Product
entries.summaryMd: Manufactured components used in the organization manufacturing process incorporating information technology and provided by third-parties (e.g. PLC, Sensors, Data Collection Systems, Workstations, Servers, etc).

senses.definitionMd: Manufactured components used in the organization manufacturing process incorporating information technology and provided by third-parties (e.g. PLC, Sensors, Data Collection Systems, Workstations, Servers, etc).

entries.title: telecommunications
entries.summaryMd: The term 'telecommunications' means the transmission, between or among points specified by the user, of information of the user's choosing, without change in the form or content of the information as sent and received.

senses.definitionMd: The term 'telecommunications' means the transmission, between or among points specified by the user, of information of the user's choosing, without change in the form or content of the information as sent and received.

entries.title: telecommunications security (TSEC) nomenclature
entries.summaryMd: The National Security Agency (NSA) system for identifying the type and purpose of certain items of COMSEC material.

senses.definitionMd: The National Security Agency (NSA) system for identifying the type and purpose of certain items of COMSEC material.

entries.title: telemetry
entries.summaryMd: The science of measuring a quantity or quantities, transmitting the results to a distant station, and interpreting, indicating, and/or recording the quantities measured.

senses.definitionMd: The science of measuring a quantity or quantities, transmitting the results to a distant station, and interpreting, indicating, and/or recording the quantities measured.

entries.title: TEMPEST certified equipment or system
entries.summaryMd: Equipment or systems that have been certified to meet the applicable level of NSTISSAM TEMPEST/1-92 or previous editions. Typically categorized as Level 1 for the highest containment of classified signals; Level II for the moderate containment of classified signals; and Level III for the least containment of classified signals.

senses.definitionMd: Equipment or systems that have been certified to meet the applicable level of NSTISSAM TEMPEST/1-92 or previous editions. Typically categorized as Level 1 for the highest containment of classified signals; Level II for the moderate containment of classified signals; and Level III for the least containment of classified signals.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "TEMPEST certified equipment or system"

entries.title: TEMPEST zone
entries.summaryMd: Designated area within a facility where equipment with appropriate TEMPEST characteristics (TEMPEST zone assignment) may be operated.

senses.definitionMd: Designated area within a facility where equipment with appropriate TEMPEST characteristics (TEMPEST zone assignment) may be operated.

entries.title: Template Generator
entries.summaryMd: In the PIV context a template generator is a software library providing facilities for the conversion of images conformant to FINGSTD to templates conformant to MINUSTD for storage on the PIV card.

senses.definitionMd: In the PIV context a template generator is a software library providing facilities for the conversion of images conformant to FINGSTD to templates conformant to MINUSTD for storage on the PIV card.

entries.title: Template Matcher
entries.summaryMd: In the PIV context a matcher is a software library providing for the comparison of images conformant to FINGSTD and templates conformant to MINUSTD. The output of the matcher, a similarity score, will be the basis of accept or reject decision.

senses.definitionMd: In the PIV context a matcher is a software library providing for the comparison of images conformant to FINGSTD and templates conformant to MINUSTD. The output of the matcher, a similarity score, will be the basis of accept or reject decision.

entries.title: Temporal metrics
entries.summaryMd: describe the characteristics of misuse vulnerabilities that can change over time but remain constant across user environments.

senses.definitionMd: describe the characteristics of misuse vulnerabilities that can change over time but remain constant across user environments.

entries.title: Term of Support
entries.summaryMd: The length of time for which the device will be supported by the manufacturer or supporting parties for such actions and materials as part replacements, software updates, vulnerability notices, technical support questions, etc.

senses.definitionMd: The length of time for which the device will be supported by the manufacturer or supporting parties for such actions and materials as part replacements, software updates, vulnerability notices, technical support questions, etc.

entries.title: Test
entries.summaryMd: A type of assessment method that is characterized by the process of exercising one or more assessment objects under specified conditions to compare actual with expected behavior, the results of which are used to support the determination of security control effectiveness over time.

senses.definitionMd: A type of assessment method that is characterized by the process of exercising one or more assessment objects under specified conditions to compare actual with expected behavior, the results of which are used to support the determination of security control effectiveness over time.

entries.title: test action
entries.summaryMd: The action to be performed based on the response to a particular question. Examples of test actions are asking another question or calculating a result.

senses.definitionMd: The action to be performed based on the response to a particular question. Examples of test actions are asking another question or calculating a result.

entries.title: Test Director
entries.summaryMd: A person responsible for all aspects of a test, including staffing, development, conduct, and logistics.

senses.definitionMd: A person responsible for all aspects of a test, including staffing, development, conduct, and logistics.

entries.title: Test Guide
entries.summaryMd: A document that outlines the basic steps involved in conducting a test and includes a list of the participants, a list of individuals and groups who might be affected by the test, and procedures for early termination of the test.

senses.definitionMd: A document that outlines the basic steps involved in conducting a test and includes a list of the participants, a list of individuals and groups who might be affected by the test, and procedures for early termination of the test.

entries.title: test key
entries.summaryMd: Key intended for testing of COMSEC equipment or systems. If intended for off-the-air, in-shop use, such key is called maintenance key.

senses.definitionMd: Key intended for testing of COMSEC equipment or systems. If intended for off-the-air, in-shop use, such key is called maintenance key.

entries.title: Test Plan
entries.summaryMd: A document that outlines the specific steps that will be performed for a particular test, including the required logistical items and expected outcome or response for each step.

senses.definitionMd: A document that outlines the specific steps that will be performed for a particular test, including the required logistical items and expected outcome or response for each step.

entries.title: Test Tools
entries.summaryMd: are a means of testing to confirm that an IT product, process, or service conforms to the requirements of a standard or standards. Examples of test tools are executable test code or reference data.

senses.definitionMd: are a means of testing to confirm that an IT product, process, or service conforms to the requirements of a standard or standards. Examples of test tools are executable test code or reference data.

entries.title: Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Event
entries.summaryMd: An event used to support the maintenance of an IT plan by allowing organizations to identify problems related to an IT plan and implement solutions before an adverse situation occurs.

senses.definitionMd: An event used to support the maintenance of an IT plan by allowing organizations to identify problems related to an IT plan and implement solutions before an adverse situation occurs.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Event"

entries.title: Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Plan
entries.summaryMd: A plan that outlines the steps to be taken to ensure that personnel are trained in their IT plan roles and responsibilities, IT plans are exercised to validate their viability, and IT components or systems are tested to validate their operability in the context of an IT plan.

senses.definitionMd: A plan that outlines the steps to be taken to ensure that personnel are trained in their IT plan roles and responsibilities, IT plans are exercised to validate their viability, and IT components or systems are tested to validate their operability in the context of an IT plan.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Plan"

entries.title: Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Policy
entries.summaryMd: A policy that outlines an organization’s internal and external requirements associated with training personnel, exercising IT plans, and testing IT components and systems.

senses.definitionMd: A policy that outlines an organization’s internal and external requirements associated with training personnel, exercising IT plans, and testing IT components and systems.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Policy"

entries.title: Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Program
entries.summaryMd: A means for ensuring that personnel are trained in their IT plan roles and responsibilities; IT plans are exercised to validate their viability; and IT components or systems are tested to validate their operability.

senses.definitionMd: A means for ensuring that personnel are trained in their IT plan roles and responsibilities; IT plans are exercised to validate their viability; and IT components or systems are tested to validate their operability.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Program"

entries.title: Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Program Coordinator
entries.summaryMd: A person who is responsible for developing a TT&E plan and coordinating TT&E events.

senses.definitionMd: A person who is responsible for developing a TT&E plan and coordinating TT&E events.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Test, Training, and Exercise (TT&E) Program Coordinator"

entries.title: Testing
entries.summaryMd: Determination of one or more characteristics of an object of conformity assessment, according to a procedure.

senses.definitionMd: Determination of one or more characteristics of an object of conformity assessment, according to a procedure.

entries.title: testing data control
entries.summaryMd: A capability with which an attacker controls the testing data input to the machine learning model.

senses.definitionMd: A capability with which an attacker controls the testing data input to the machine learning model.

entries.title: Testing laboratory
entries.summaryMd: An accredited cryptographic security testing laboratory.

senses.definitionMd: An accredited cryptographic security testing laboratory.

entries.title: TestResult
entries.summaryMd: The container for XCCDF results. May be the root node of an XCCDF results document.

senses.definitionMd: The container for XCCDF results. May be the root node of an XCCDF results document.

entries.title: Third-party Providers
entries.summaryMd: Service providers, integrators, vendors, telecommunications, and infrastructure support that are external to the organization that operates the manufacturing system.

senses.definitionMd: Service providers, integrators, vendors, telecommunications, and infrastructure support that are external to the organization that operates the manufacturing system.

entries.title: Third-Party Relationships
entries.summaryMd: relationships with external entities. External entities may include, for example, service providers, vendors, supply-side partners, demand-side partners, alliances, consortiums, and investors, and may include both contractual and non-contractual parties.

senses.definitionMd: relationships with external entities. External entities may include, for example, service providers, vendors, supply-side partners, demand-side partners, alliances, consortiums, and investors, and may include both contractual and non-contractual parties.

entries.title: Third-party testing
entries.summaryMd: Independent testing by an organization that was not involved in the design and implementation of the object being tested (e.g., a system or device) and is not intended as the eventual user of that object.

senses.definitionMd: Independent testing by an organization that was not involved in the design and implementation of the object being tested (e.g., a system or device) and is not intended as the eventual user of that object.

entries.title: Thread
entries.summaryMd: A defined group of instructions executing apart from other similarly defined groups, but sharing memory and resources of the process to which they belong.

senses.definitionMd: A defined group of instructions executing apart from other similarly defined groups, but sharing memory and resources of the process to which they belong.

entries.title: threat
entries.summaryMd: Any circumstance or event with the potential to adversely impact organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, or individuals through an information system via unauthorized access, destruction, disclosure, modification of information, and/or denial of service. Also, the potential for a threat-source to successfully exploit a particular information system vulnerability.

senses.definitionMd: Any circumstance or event with the potential to adversely impact organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, or individuals through an information system via unauthorized access, destruction, disclosure, modification of information, and/or denial of service. Also, the potential for a threat-source to successfully exploit a particular information system vulnerability.

entries.title: threat actor
entries.summaryMd: An individual or a group posing a threat.

senses.definitionMd: An individual or a group posing a threat.

entries.title: threat analysis
entries.summaryMd: Process of formally evaluating the degree of threat to an information system or enterprise and describing the nature of the threat.

senses.definitionMd: Process of formally evaluating the degree of threat to an information system or enterprise and describing the nature of the threat.

entries.title: Threat Assessment/Analysis
entries.summaryMd: Process of formally evaluating the degree of threat to an information system or enterprise and describing the nature of the threat.

senses.definitionMd: Process of formally evaluating the degree of threat to an information system or enterprise and describing the nature of the threat.

entries.title: threat event
entries.summaryMd: An event or situation that has the potential for causing undesirable consequences or impact.

senses.definitionMd: An event or situation that has the potential for causing undesirable consequences or impact.

entries.title: threat event outcome
entries.summaryMd: The effect a threat acting upon a vulnerability has on the confidentiality, integrity, and/or availability of the organization’s operations, assets, or individuals.

senses.definitionMd: The effect a threat acting upon a vulnerability has on the confidentiality, integrity, and/or availability of the organization’s operations, assets, or individuals.

entries.title: threat information
entries.summaryMd: Analytical insights into trends, technologies, or tactics of an adversarial nature affecting information systems security.

senses.definitionMd: Analytical insights into trends, technologies, or tactics of an adversarial nature affecting information systems security.

entries.title: threat intelligence
entries.summaryMd: Threat information that has been aggregated, transformed, analyzed, interpreted, or enriched to provide the necessary context for decision-making processes.

senses.definitionMd: Threat information that has been aggregated, transformed, analyzed, interpreted, or enriched to provide the necessary context for decision-making processes.

entries.title: Threat Intelligence Report
entries.summaryMd: A prose document that describes TTPs, actors, types of systems and information being targeted, and other threat-related information.

senses.definitionMd: A prose document that describes TTPs, actors, types of systems and information being targeted, and other threat-related information.

entries.title: threat modeling
entries.summaryMd: A form of risk assessment that models aspects of the attack and defense sides of a logical entity, such as a piece of data, an application, a host, a system, or an environment.

senses.definitionMd: A form of risk assessment that models aspects of the attack and defense sides of a logical entity, such as a piece of data, an application, a host, a system, or an environment.

entries.title: threat monitoring
entries.summaryMd: Analysis, assessment, and review of audit trails and other information collected for the purpose of searching out system events that may constitute violations of system security.

senses.definitionMd: Analysis, assessment, and review of audit trails and other information collected for the purpose of searching out system events that may constitute violations of system security.

entries.title: threat scenario
entries.summaryMd: A set of discrete threat events, associated with a specific threat source or multiple threat sources, partially ordered in time.

senses.definitionMd: A set of discrete threat events, associated with a specific threat source or multiple threat sources, partially ordered in time.

entries.title: Threat Shifting
entries.summaryMd: The response of actors to perceived safeguards and/or countermeasures (i.e., security controls), in which actors change some characteristic of their intent/targeting in order to avoid and/or overcome those safeguards/countermeasures.

senses.definitionMd: The response of actors to perceived safeguards and/or countermeasures (i.e., security controls), in which actors change some characteristic of their intent/targeting in order to avoid and/or overcome those safeguards/countermeasures.

entries.title: Threat Signaling
entries.summaryMd: Real-time signaling of DDoS-related telemetry and threat-handling requests and data between elements concerned with DDoS attack detection, classification, trace back, and mitigation.

senses.definitionMd: Real-time signaling of DDoS-related telemetry and threat-handling requests and data between elements concerned with DDoS attack detection, classification, trace back, and mitigation.

entries.title: threat source
entries.summaryMd: The intent and method targeted at the intentional exploitation of a vulnerability or a situation and method that may accidentally trigger a vulnerability. Synonymous with Threat Agent.

senses.definitionMd: The intent and method targeted at the intentional exploitation of a vulnerability or a situation and method that may accidentally trigger a vulnerability. Synonymous with Threat Agent.

entries.title: threshold rule
entries.summaryMd: Usually, with the threshold rule, a cell in a table of frequencies is defined to be sensitive if the number of respondents is less than some specified number. Some agencies require at least five respondents in a cell, others require three. When thresholds are not respected, an agency may restructure tables and combine categories or use cell suppression, rounding or the confidentiality edit, or provide other additional protection in order to satisfy the rule.

senses.definitionMd: Usually, with the threshold rule, a cell in a table of frequencies is defined to be sensitive if the number of respondents is less than some specified number. Some agencies require at least five respondents in a cell, others require three. When thresholds are not respected, an agency may restructure tables and combine categories or use cell suppression, rounding or the confidentiality edit, or provide other additional protection in order to satisfy the rule.

entries.title: Thresholds
entries.summaryMd: Values used to establish concrete decision points and operational control limits to trigger management action and response escalation.

senses.definitionMd: Values used to establish concrete decision points and operational control limits to trigger management action and response escalation.

entries.title: Tier 0 (central facility) (COMSEC)
entries.summaryMd: The composite facility approved, managed, and operated under National Security Agency (NSA) oversight that includes: a. National COMSEC Material Generation and Production facilities for physical and electronic keys, both traditional and modern. b. Central Office of Record (COR) services for NSA, contractor, and select Civil Agency accounts. c. National Distribution Authority (NDA) for U.S. accounts worldwide. d. National Registration Authority for all non-military accounts on U.S. systems. e. National Credential Manager for all electronic key management system (EKMS) accounts on U.S. systems. f. EKMS Defense Courier Service (DCS) data administrator.

senses.definitionMd: The composite facility approved, managed, and operated under National Security Agency (NSA) oversight that includes: a. National COMSEC Material Generation and Production facilities for physical and electronic keys, both traditional and modern. b. Central Office of Record (COR) services for NSA, contractor, and select Civil Agency accounts. c. National Distribution Authority (NDA) for U.S. accounts worldwide. d. National Registration Authority for all non-military accounts on U.S. systems. e. National Credential Manager for all electronic key management system (EKMS) accounts on U.S. systems. f. EKMS Defense Courier Service (DCS) data administrator.

entries.title: Tier 1/common tier 1 (CT1) (COMSEC)
entries.summaryMd: The composite of the electronic key management system (EKMS) Common Tier 1 (CT1) systems that is a tool used by the military service central offices of record (CORs) to support their accounts and by the Civil Agency CORs requesting CT1 support. The CT1 also provides generation and distribution of many types of traditional keying material for large nets. The CT1 consists of two Primary Tier 1 sites, one Extension Tier 1 site, and other Physical Material Handling Segments (PMHS) at several service sites providing the following services: a. Common military traditional electronic keying material generation and distribution facilities. b. Common keying material ordering interface for all types of keying material required by military accounts. c. Registration Authority for U.S. military accounts. d. Ordering Privilege Manager for U.S. military accounts. e. Management for the military’s COMSEC vaults, depots, and logistics system facilities.

senses.definitionMd: The composite of the electronic key management system (EKMS) Common Tier 1 (CT1) systems that is a tool used by the military service central offices of record (CORs) to support their accounts and by the Civil Agency CORs requesting CT1 support. The CT1 also provides generation and distribution of many types of traditional keying material for large nets. The CT1 consists of two Primary Tier 1 sites, one Extension Tier 1 site, and other Physical Material Handling Segments (PMHS) at several service sites providing the following services: a. Common military traditional electronic keying material generation and distribution facilities. b. Common keying material ordering interface for all types of keying material required by military accounts. c. Registration Authority for U.S. military accounts. d. Ordering Privilege Manager for U.S. military accounts. e. Management for the military’s COMSEC vaults, depots, and logistics system facilities.

entries.title: Tier 2 (COMSEC)
entries.summaryMd: The layer of the electronic key management system (EKMS) comprising COMSEC accounts and subaccounts managing keying material and other COMSEC material. Automated EKMS Tier 2s consist of a Service- or Agency-provided Local Management Device (LMD) running the Local COMSEC Management Software (LCMS), a Key Processor (KP), and a secure terminal equipment (STE) or other secure communication device(s).

senses.definitionMd: The layer of the electronic key management system (EKMS) comprising COMSEC accounts and subaccounts managing keying material and other COMSEC material. Automated EKMS Tier 2s consist of a Service- or Agency-provided Local Management Device (LMD) running the Local COMSEC Management Software (LCMS), a Key Processor (KP), and a secure terminal equipment (STE) or other secure communication device(s).

entries.title: Tier 3 (COMSEC)
entries.summaryMd: The lowest tier or layer of electronic key management system (EKMS) architecture comprising hand-receipt holders who use an electronic fill device (e.g., the Data Transfer Device (DTD), Secure DTD2000 System (SDS), Simple Key Loader (SKL)) and all other means to issue key to End Cryptographic Units (ECUs). Tier 3 elements receive keying material from Tier 2 activities by means of electronic fill devices or in canisters (for physical keying material).

senses.definitionMd: The lowest tier or layer of electronic key management system (EKMS) architecture comprising hand-receipt holders who use an electronic fill device (e.g., the Data Transfer Device (DTD), Secure DTD2000 System (SDS), Simple Key Loader (SKL)) and all other means to issue key to End Cryptographic Units (ECUs). Tier 3 elements receive keying material from Tier 2 activities by means of electronic fill devices or in canisters (for physical keying material).

entries.title: Tier I Checklist
entries.summaryMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that is prose-based, such as narrative descriptions of how a person can manually alter a product’s configuration.

senses.definitionMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that is prose-based, such as narrative descriptions of how a person can manually alter a product’s configuration.

entries.title: Tier II Checklist
entries.summaryMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that documents the recommended security settings in a machine-readable but non-standard format, such as a proprietary format or a product-specific configuration script.

senses.definitionMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that documents the recommended security settings in a machine-readable but non-standard format, such as a proprietary format or a product-specific configuration script.

entries.title: Tier III Checklist
entries.summaryMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that uses SCAP to document the recommended security settings in machine-readable standardized SCAP formats that meet the definition of “SCAP Expressed” specified in NIST SP 800-126. SCAP Validated products should be able to process Tier III checklists.

senses.definitionMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that uses SCAP to document the recommended security settings in machine-readable standardized SCAP formats that meet the definition of “SCAP Expressed” specified in NIST SP 800-126. SCAP Validated products should be able to process Tier III checklists.

entries.title: Tier IV Checklist
entries.summaryMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that is considered production-ready and has been validated by NIST or a NIST-recognized authoritative entity to ensure, to the maximum extent possible, interoperability with SCAP-validated products. Tier IV checklists also demonstrate the ability to map low-level security settings (for example, standardized identifiers for individual security configuration issues) to high -level security requirements as represented in various security frameworks (e.g., SP 800-53 controls for FISMA), and the mappings have been vetted with the appropriate authority.

senses.definitionMd: A checklist in the National Checklist Repository that is considered production-ready and has been validated by NIST or a NIST-recognized authoritative entity to ensure, to the maximum extent possible, interoperability with SCAP-validated products. Tier IV checklists also demonstrate the ability to map low-level security settings (for example, standardized identifiers for individual security configuration issues) to high -level security requirements as represented in various security frameworks (e.g., SP 800-53 controls for FISMA), and the mappings have been vetted with the appropriate authority.

entries.title: tiered label
entries.summaryMd: Indicates the degree to which a product has satisfied a specific standard, sometimes based on attaining increasing levels of performance against specified criteria. Tiers or grades are often represented by colors (e.g., red-yellow-green), numbers of icons (e.g., stars or security shields), or other appropriate metaphors (e.g., precious metals: gold-silver-bronze).

senses.definitionMd: Indicates the degree to which a product has satisfied a specific standard, sometimes based on attaining increasing levels of performance against specified criteria. Tiers or grades are often represented by colors (e.g., red-yellow-green), numbers of icons (e.g., stars or security shields), or other appropriate metaphors (e.g., precious metals: gold-silver-bronze).

entries.title: time bomb
entries.summaryMd: Resident computer program that triggers an unauthorized act at a predefined time.

senses.definitionMd: Resident computer program that triggers an unauthorized act at a predefined time.

entries.title: time-compliance date
entries.summaryMd: Date by which a mandatory modification to a COMSEC end-item must be incorporated if the item is to remain approved for operational use.

senses.definitionMd: Date by which a mandatory modification to a COMSEC end-item must be incorporated if the item is to remain approved for operational use.

entries.title: time-dependent password
entries.summaryMd: Password that is valid only at a certain time of day or during a specified interval of time.

senses.definitionMd: Password that is valid only at a certain time of day or during a specified interval of time.

entries.title: time interval
entries.summaryMd: The elapsed time between two events. In time and frequency metrology, time interval is usually measured in small fractions of a second, such as milliseconds, microseconds, or nanoseconds. Higher resolution time interval measurements are often made with a time interval counter.

senses.definitionMd: The elapsed time between two events. In time and frequency metrology, time interval is usually measured in small fractions of a second, such as milliseconds, microseconds, or nanoseconds. Higher resolution time interval measurements are often made with a time interval counter.

entries.title: time scale
entries.summaryMd: An agreed upon system for keeping time. All time scales use a frequency source to define the length of the second, which is the standard unit of time interval. Seconds are then counted to measure longer units of time interval, such as minutes, hours, or days. Modern time scales, such as UTC, define the second based on an atomic property of the cesium atom, and thus standard seconds are produced by cesium oscillators. Earlier time scales (including earlier versions of Universal Time) were based on astronomical observations that measured the frequency of the Earth’s rotation.

senses.definitionMd: An agreed upon system for keeping time. All time scales use a frequency source to define the length of the second, which is the standard unit of time interval. Seconds are then counted to measure longer units of time interval, such as minutes, hours, or days. Modern time scales, such as UTC, define the second based on an atomic property of the cesium atom, and thus standard seconds are produced by cesium oscillators. Earlier time scales (including earlier versions of Universal Time) were based on astronomical observations that measured the frequency of the Earth’s rotation.

entries.title: time series analysis
entries.summaryMd: The analysis of an ordered sequence of values of a variable at equally spaced time intervals.

senses.definitionMd: The analysis of an ordered sequence of values of a variable at equally spaced time intervals.

entries.title: Timestamp
entries.summaryMd: A token or packet of information that is used to provide assurance of timeliness; the timestamp contains timestamped data, including a time, and a signature generated by a Trusted Timestamp Authority (TTA).

senses.definitionMd: A token or packet of information that is used to provide assurance of timeliness; the timestamp contains timestamped data, including a time, and a signature generated by a Trusted Timestamp Authority (TTA).

entries.title: Timestamp Packet
entries.summaryMd: A unit of information that is transmitted by a TTA that contains timestamped_data and a timestamp_signature.

senses.definitionMd: A unit of information that is transmitted by a TTA that contains timestamped_data and a timestamp_signature.

entries.title: timestamp_signatureTTA
entries.summaryMd: A digital signature that is generated using a TTA’s private signature key.

senses.definitionMd: A digital signature that is generated using a TTA’s private signature key.

entries.title: timestamp_time
entries.summaryMd: The time provided in a timestamp.

senses.definitionMd: The time provided in a timestamp.

entries.title: timestamped_data
entries.summaryMd: The data on which a digital signature is generated by a TTA.

senses.definitionMd: The data on which a digital signature is generated by a TTA.

entries.title: Tj
entries.summaryMd: The jth counter block.

senses.definitionMd: The jth counter block.

entries.title: Tlen
entries.summaryMd: The bit length of the MAC.

senses.definitionMd: The bit length of the MAC.

entries.title: TMacTagBits(X)
entries.summaryMd: A truncation function that outputs the most significant (i.e., leftmost) MacTagBits bits of the input string, X, when the bit length of X is greater than MacTagBits; otherwise, the function outputs X. For example, T2(1011) = 10, T3(1011) = 101, and T4(1011) = 1011.

senses.definitionMd: A truncation function that outputs the most significant (i.e., leftmost) MacTagBits bits of the input string, X, when the bit length of X is greater than MacTagBits; otherwise, the function outputs X. For example, T2(1011) = 10, T3(1011) = 101, and T4(1011) = 1011.

entries.title: token
entries.summaryMd: Something the cardholder possesses and controls (e.g., PIV Card or derived PIV credential) that is used to authenticate the cardholder’s identity.

senses.definitionMd: Something the cardholder possesses and controls (e.g., PIV Card or derived PIV credential) that is used to authenticate the cardholder’s identity.

entries.title: Token Factory Contract
entries.summaryMd: A smart contract that defines and issues a token.

senses.definitionMd: A smart contract that defines and issues a token.

entries.title: Tool Configuration
entries.summaryMd: A recommendation for setting up and using tools that support the automated collection, exchange, processing, analysis, and use of threat information.

senses.definitionMd: A recommendation for setting up and using tools that support the automated collection, exchange, processing, analysis, and use of threat information.

entries.title: traceability
entries.summaryMd: Discernible association among two or more logical entities, such as requirements, system elements, verifications, or tasks.

senses.definitionMd: Discernible association among two or more logical entities, such as requirements, system elements, verifications, or tasks.

entries.title: traceability matrix
entries.summaryMd: A matrix that records the relationship between two or more products of the development process (e.g., a matrix that records the relationship between the requirements and the design of a given software component).

senses.definitionMd: A matrix that records the relationship between two or more products of the development process (e.g., a matrix that records the relationship between the requirements and the design of a given software component).

entries.title: traceability, metrological
entries.summaryMd: Property of a measurement result whereby the result can be related to a reference through a documented, unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty.

senses.definitionMd: Property of a measurement result whereby the result can be related to a reference through a documented, unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty.

entries.title: Traceable
entries.summaryMd: Information that is sufficient to make a determination about a specific aspect of an individual's activities or status.

senses.definitionMd: Information that is sufficient to make a determination about a specific aspect of an individual's activities or status.

entries.title: trade-off
entries.summaryMd: Decision-making actions that select from various requirements and alternative solutions on the basis of net benefit to the stakeholders.

senses.definitionMd: Decision-making actions that select from various requirements and alternative solutions on the basis of net benefit to the stakeholders.

entries.title: trade-off analysis
entries.summaryMd: Determining the effect of decreasing one or more key factors and simultaneously increasing one or more other key factors in a decision, design, or project.

senses.definitionMd: Determining the effect of decreasing one or more key factors and simultaneously increasing one or more other key factors in a decision, design, or project.

entries.title: tradecraft identity
entries.summaryMd: An identity used for the purpose of work-related interactions that may or may not be synonymous with an individual’s true identity.

senses.definitionMd: An identity used for the purpose of work-related interactions that may or may not be synonymous with an individual’s true identity.

entries.title: traditional key
entries.summaryMd: Term used to reference symmetric key wherein both ends of a link or all parties in a cryptonet have the same exact key. 256-bit advanced encryption standard (AES), high assurance internet protocol encryptor (HAIPE) pre-placed, and authenticated pre-placed key are examples of traditional key.

senses.definitionMd: Term used to reference symmetric key wherein both ends of a link or all parties in a cryptonet have the same exact key. 256-bit advanced encryption standard (AES), high assurance internet protocol encryptor (HAIPE) pre-placed, and authenticated pre-placed key are examples of traditional key.

entries.title: traffic encryption key (TEK)
entries.summaryMd: Key used to encrypt plain text or to superencrypt previously encrypted text and/or to decrypt cipher text.

senses.definitionMd: Key used to encrypt plain text or to superencrypt previously encrypted text and/or to decrypt cipher text.

entries.title: Traffic Filter
entries.summaryMd: An entry in an access control list that is installed on the router or switch to enforce access controls on the network.

senses.definitionMd: An entry in an access control list that is installed on the router or switch to enforce access controls on the network.

entries.title: Traffic Flow Confidentiality (TFC) Padding
entries.summaryMd: Dummy data added to real data in order to obfuscate the length and frequency of information sent over IPsec.

senses.definitionMd: Dummy data added to real data in order to obfuscate the length and frequency of information sent over IPsec.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Traffic Flow Confidentiality (TFC) Padding"

entries.title: traffic flow security (TFS)
entries.summaryMd: Techniques to counter Traffic Analysis.

senses.definitionMd: Techniques to counter Traffic Analysis.

entries.title: traffic padding
entries.summaryMd: The generation of spurious instances of communication, spurious data units, and/or spurious data within data units. Note: May be used to disguise the amount of real data units being sent.

senses.definitionMd: The generation of spurious instances of communication, spurious data units, and/or spurious data within data units. Note: May be used to disguise the amount of real data units being sent.

entries.title: Training
entries.summaryMd: The ‘Training’ level of the learning continuum strives to produce relevant and needed security skills and competencies by practitioners of functional specialties other than IT security (e.g., management, systems design and development, acquisition, auditing).

senses.definitionMd: The ‘Training’ level of the learning continuum strives to produce relevant and needed security skills and competencies by practitioners of functional specialties other than IT security (e.g., management, systems design and development, acquisition, auditing).

entries.title: training data control
entries.summaryMd: A capability in which an attacker controls some or all of the training data of a machine learning model.

senses.definitionMd: A capability in which an attacker controls some or all of the training data of a machine learning model.

entries.title: training data extraction
entries.summaryMd: The ability of an attacker to extract the training data of a genera­tive model by prompting the model with specific inputs.

senses.definitionMd: The ability of an attacker to extract the training data of a genera­tive model by prompting the model with specific inputs.

entries.title: training key
entries.summaryMd: Key intended for use for over-the-air or off-the-air training.

senses.definitionMd: Key intended for use for over-the-air or off-the-air training.

entries.title: training stage
entries.summaryMd: The stage of a machine learning pipeline in which a model learns parameters that minimize its error against an objective function based on training data.

senses.definitionMd: The stage of a machine learning pipeline in which a model learns parameters that minimize its error against an objective function based on training data.

entries.title: tranquility
entries.summaryMd: Property whereby the security level of an object cannot change while the object is being processed by an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Property whereby the security level of an object cannot change while the object is being processed by an information system.

entries.title: Transaction
entries.summaryMd: A discrete event between a user and a system that supports a business or programmatic purpose. A government digital system may have multiple categories or types of transactions, which may require separate analysis within the overall digital identity risk assessment.

senses.definitionMd: A discrete event between a user and a system that supports a business or programmatic purpose. A government digital system may have multiple categories or types of transactions, which may require separate analysis within the overall digital identity risk assessment.

entries.title: Transaction fee
entries.summaryMd: An amount of cryptocurrency charged to process a blockchain transaction. Given to publishing nodes to include the transaction within a block.

senses.definitionMd: An amount of cryptocurrency charged to process a blockchain transaction. Given to publishing nodes to include the transaction within a block.

entries.title: transdisciplinary
entries.summaryMd: Creating a unity of intellectual frameworks beyond the disciplinary perspectives.

senses.definitionMd: Creating a unity of intellectual frameworks beyond the disciplinary perspectives.

entries.title: Transducer Capabilities
entries.summaryMd: Capabilities that provide the ability for computing devices to interact directly with physical entities of interest. The two types of transducer capabilities are sensing and actuating.

senses.definitionMd: Capabilities that provide the ability for computing devices to interact directly with physical entities of interest. The two types of transducer capabilities are sensing and actuating.

entries.title: transfer cross domain solution
entries.summaryMd: A type of cross domain solution (CDS) that facilitates the movement of data between information systems operating in different security domains.

senses.definitionMd: A type of cross domain solution (CDS) that facilitates the movement of data between information systems operating in different security domains.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "transfer cross domain solution"

entries.title: transfer key encryption key (TrKEK)
entries.summaryMd: A key used to move key from a Key Processor to a data transfer device (DTD)/secure DTD2000 system (SDS)/simple key loader (SKL).

senses.definitionMd: A key used to move key from a Key Processor to a data transfer device (DTD)/secure DTD2000 system (SDS)/simple key loader (SKL).

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "transfer key encryption key (TrKEK)"

entries.title: transfer of accountability
entries.summaryMd: The process of transferring accountability for COMSEC material from the COMSEC account of the shipping organization to the COMSEC account of the receiving organization.

senses.definitionMd: The process of transferring accountability for COMSEC material from the COMSEC account of the shipping organization to the COMSEC account of the receiving organization.

entries.title: transformation
entries.summaryMd: The conversion of one state or format into another state or format.

senses.definitionMd: The conversion of one state or format into another state or format.

entries.title: Transforming Application
entries.summaryMd: An application that transforms a CBEFF Basic Data Structure from one Patron Format into another Patron Format. This can include processing of the content of the BDB, but need not. CBEFF defines rules for migrat­ ing the values in Standard Biometric Header fields.

senses.definitionMd: An application that transforms a CBEFF Basic Data Structure from one Patron Format into another Patron Format. This can include processing of the content of the BDB, but need not. CBEFF defines rules for migrat­ ing the values in Standard Biometric Header fields.

entries.title: transmission
entries.summaryMd: The state that exists when information is being electronically sent from one location to one or more other locations.

senses.definitionMd: The state that exists when information is being electronically sent from one location to one or more other locations.

entries.title: Transmission Control Protocol
entries.summaryMd: TCP is one of the main protocols in TCP/IP networks. Whereas the IP protocol deals only with packets, TCP enables two hosts to establish a connection and exchange streams of data. TCP guarantees the delivery of data and also guarantees that packets will be delivered in the same order in which they were sent.

senses.definitionMd: TCP is one of the main protocols in TCP/IP networks. Whereas the IP protocol deals only with packets, TCP enables two hosts to establish a connection and exchange streams of data. TCP guarantees the delivery of data and also guarantees that packets will be delivered in the same order in which they were sent.

entries.title: transmission security
entries.summaryMd: Measures (security controls) applied to transmissions in order to prevent interception, disruption of reception, communications deception, and/or derivation of intelligence by analysis of transmission characteristics such as signal parameters or message externals. Note: TRANSEC is that field of COMSEC which deals with the security of communication transmissions, rather than that of the information being communicated.

senses.definitionMd: Measures (security controls) applied to transmissions in order to prevent interception, disruption of reception, communications deception, and/or derivation of intelligence by analysis of transmission characteristics such as signal parameters or message externals. Note: TRANSEC is that field of COMSEC which deals with the security of communication transmissions, rather than that of the information being communicated.

entries.title: transparency
entries.summaryMd: Amount of information that can be gathered about a supplier, product, or service and how far through the supply chain this information can be obtained.

senses.definitionMd: Amount of information that can be gathered about a supplier, product, or service and how far through the supply chain this information can be obtained.

entries.title: Transponder
entries.summaryMd: An electronic device that communicates with RFID readers. A tag can function as a beacon or it can be used to convey information such as an identifier.

senses.definitionMd: An electronic device that communicates with RFID readers. A tag can function as a beacon or it can be used to convey information such as an identifier.

entries.title: Transport Layer
entries.summaryMd: Layer of the TCP/IP protocol stack that is responsible for reliable connection-oriented or connectionless end-to-end communications.

senses.definitionMd: Layer of the TCP/IP protocol stack that is responsible for reliable connection-oriented or connectionless end-to-end communications.

entries.title: Transport Layer Security (TLS)
entries.summaryMd: Provides privacy and data integrity between two communicating applications. It is designed to encapsulate other protocols, such as HTTP. TLS v1.0 was released in 1999, providing slight modifications to SSL 3.0.

senses.definitionMd: Provides privacy and data integrity between two communicating applications. It is designed to encapsulate other protocols, such as HTTP. TLS v1.0 was released in 1999, providing slight modifications to SSL 3.0.

entries.title: Transport Mode
entries.summaryMd: An IPsec mode that does not create an additional IP header for each protected packet.

senses.definitionMd: An IPsec mode that does not create an additional IP header for each protected packet.

entries.title: trap door
entries.summaryMd: 1. A means of reading cryptographically protected information by the use of private knowledge of weaknesses in the cryptographic algorithm used to protect the data. See backdoor.

senses.definitionMd: 1. A means of reading cryptographically protected information by the use of private knowledge of weaknesses in the cryptographic algorithm used to protect the data. See backdoor.

entries.title: trigger
entries.summaryMd: 1) A set of logic statements to be applied to a data stream that produces an alert when an anomalous incident or behavior occurs

senses.definitionMd: 1) A set of logic statements to be applied to a data stream that produces an alert when an anomalous incident or behavior occurs

entries.title: Triple Data Encryption Algorithm
entries.summaryMd: The algorithm specified in FIPS PUB 46-3 –1999, Data Encryption Algorithm.

senses.definitionMd: The algorithm specified in FIPS PUB 46-3 –1999, Data Encryption Algorithm.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Triple Data Encryption Algorithm"

entries.title: Triple Data Encryption Standard
entries.summaryMd: An implementation of the data encryption standard (DES) algorithm that uses three passes of the DES algorithm instead of one as used in ordinary DES applications. Triple DES provides much stronger encryption than ordinary DES but it is less secure than advanced encryption standard (AES). Rationale: The terminology has been changed by NIST.

senses.definitionMd: An implementation of the data encryption standard (DES) algorithm that uses three passes of the DES algorithm instead of one as used in ordinary DES applications. Triple DES provides much stronger encryption than ordinary DES but it is less secure than advanced encryption standard (AES). Rationale: The terminology has been changed by NIST.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Triple Data Encryption Standard"

entries.title: trojan
entries.summaryMd: In the machine learning context, a malicious modification to a model that is difficult to detect, may appear harmless, but that can alter the intended function of the system upon a signal from an attacker to cause a malicious behavior desired by the attacker. For Trojan attacks to be effective, the trigger must be rare in the normal operating environment so that it does not affect the normal effectiveness of the AI and raise the suspicions of users. In the machine learning context, trojan may be used interchangeably with backdoor pattern.

senses.definitionMd: In the machine learning context, a malicious modification to a model that is difficult to detect, may appear harmless, but that can alter the intended function of the system upon a signal from an attacker to cause a malicious behavior desired by the attacker. For Trojan attacks to be effective, the trigger must be rare in the normal operating environment so that it does not affect the normal effectiveness of the AI and raise the suspicions of users. In the machine learning context, trojan may be used interchangeably with backdoor pattern.

entries.title: Trojan horse
entries.summaryMd: A computer program that appears to have a useful function, but also has a hidden and potentially malicious function that evades security mechanisms, sometimes by exploiting legitimate authorizations of a system entity that invokes the program.

senses.definitionMd: A computer program that appears to have a useful function, but also has a hidden and potentially malicious function that evades security mechanisms, sometimes by exploiting legitimate authorizations of a system entity that invokes the program.

entries.title: truncation
entries.summaryMd: A process that shortens an input bitstring, preserving only a sub-string of a specified length.

senses.definitionMd: A process that shortens an input bitstring, preserving only a sub-string of a specified length.

entries.title: trust
entries.summaryMd: The willingness to take actions expecting beneficial outcomes, based on assertions by other parties.

senses.definitionMd: The willingness to take actions expecting beneficial outcomes, based on assertions by other parties.

entries.title: trust agreement
entries.summaryMd: A set of conditions under which a CSP, IdP, and RP are allowed to participate in a federation transaction to establish an authentication session between the subscriber and the RP.

senses.definitionMd: A set of conditions under which a CSP, IdP, and RP are allowed to participate in a federation transaction to establish an authentication session between the subscriber and the RP.

entries.title: trust anchor
entries.summaryMd: A CA with one or more trusted certificates containing public keys that exist at the base of a tree of trust or as the strongest link in a chain of trust and upon which a Public Key Infrastructure is constructed. “Trust anchor” also refers to the certificate of this CA.

senses.definitionMd: A CA with one or more trusted certificates containing public keys that exist at the base of a tree of trust or as the strongest link in a chain of trust and upon which a Public Key Infrastructure is constructed. “Trust anchor” also refers to the certificate of this CA.

entries.title: trust assumption
entries.summaryMd: An assumption that characterizes how one expects a specific party to behave when given access to sensitive data.

senses.definitionMd: An assumption that characterizes how one expects a specific party to behave when given access to sensitive data.

entries.title: Trust Framework
entries.summaryMd: The “rules” underpinning federated identity management, typically consisting of: system, legal, conformance, and recognition.

senses.definitionMd: The “rules” underpinning federated identity management, typically consisting of: system, legal, conformance, and recognition.

entries.title: Trust Framework Operators
entries.summaryMd: The entity responsible for the governance and administration of an identity federation.

senses.definitionMd: The entity responsible for the governance and administration of an identity federation.

entries.title: Trust Framework Providers
entries.summaryMd: The entity responsible for the governance and administration of an identity federation.

senses.definitionMd: The entity responsible for the governance and administration of an identity federation.

entries.title: trust list
entries.summaryMd: Collection of trusted certificates used by Relying Parties to authenticate other certificates.

senses.definitionMd: Collection of trusted certificates used by Relying Parties to authenticate other certificates.

entries.title: Trust Management
entries.summaryMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that untrustworthy persons are prevented from being trusted with network access (to prevent insider attacks).

senses.definitionMd: An ISCM capability that ensures that untrustworthy persons are prevented from being trusted with network access (to prevent insider attacks).

entries.title: trust model
entries.summaryMd: A collection of assumptions that characterize the trustworthiness of each component in a system.

senses.definitionMd: A collection of assumptions that characterize the trustworthiness of each component in a system.

entries.title: Trust Protection Platform
entries.summaryMd: The Venafi Machine Identity Protection platform used in the example implementation described in this practice guide.

senses.definitionMd: The Venafi Machine Identity Protection platform used in the example implementation described in this practice guide.

entries.title: trust relationship
entries.summaryMd: Policies that govern how entities in differing domains honor each other’s authorizations. An authority may be completely trusted—for example, any statement from the authority will be accepted as a basis for action—or there may be limited trust, in which case only statements in a specific range are accepted.

senses.definitionMd: Policies that govern how entities in differing domains honor each other’s authorizations. An authority may be completely trusted—for example, any statement from the authority will be accepted as a basis for action—or there may be limited trust, in which case only statements in a specific range are accepted.

entries.title: Trusted
entries.summaryMd: An element that another element relies upon to fulfill critical requirements on its behalf.

senses.definitionMd: An element that another element relies upon to fulfill critical requirements on its behalf.

entries.title: trusted agent (TA)
entries.summaryMd: 1. An individual explicitly aligned with one or more registration authority (RA) officers who has been delegated the authority to perform a portion of the RA functions. A trusted agent (TA) does not have privileged access to certification authority system (CAS) components to authorize certificate issuance, certificate revocation, or key recovery.

senses.definitionMd: 1. An individual explicitly aligned with one or more registration authority (RA) officers who has been delegated the authority to perform a portion of the RA functions. A trusted agent (TA) does not have privileged access to certification authority system (CAS) components to authorize certificate issuance, certificate revocation, or key recovery.

entries.title: Trusted association
entries.summaryMd: Assurance of the integrity of an asserted relationship between items of information that may be provided by cryptographic or non-cryptographic (e.g., physical) means. Also see Binding.

senses.definitionMd: Assurance of the integrity of an asserted relationship between items of information that may be provided by cryptographic or non-cryptographic (e.g., physical) means. Also see Binding.

entries.title: Trusted boot
entries.summaryMd: A system boot where aspects of the hardware and firmware are measured and compared against known good values to verify their integrity and thus their trustworthiness.

senses.definitionMd: A system boot where aspects of the hardware and firmware are measured and compared against known good values to verify their integrity and thus their trustworthiness.

entries.title: trusted certificate
entries.summaryMd: A certificate that is trusted by the relying party on the basis of secure and authenticated delivery. The public keys included in trusted certificates are used to start certification paths. Also known as a “trust anchor.”

senses.definitionMd: A certificate that is trusted by the relying party on the basis of secure and authenticated delivery. The public keys included in trusted certificates are used to start certification paths. Also known as a “trust anchor.”

entries.title: trusted channel
entries.summaryMd: A protected communication link established between the cryptographic module and a sender or receiver (including another cryptographic module) to securely communicate and verify the validity of plaintext CSPs, keys, authentication data, and other sensitive data. Also called a secure channel.

senses.definitionMd: A protected communication link established between the cryptographic module and a sender or receiver (including another cryptographic module) to securely communicate and verify the validity of plaintext CSPs, keys, authentication data, and other sensitive data. Also called a secure channel.

entries.title: Trusted compute pool
entries.summaryMd: A physical or logical grouping of computing hardware in a data center that is tagged with specific and varying security policies. Within a trusted compute pool, the access and execution of applications and workloads are monitored, controlled, audited, etc.

senses.definitionMd: A physical or logical grouping of computing hardware in a data center that is tagged with specific and varying security policies. Within a trusted compute pool, the access and execution of applications and workloads are monitored, controlled, audited, etc.

entries.title: trusted computer system
entries.summaryMd: A system that has the necessary security functions and assurance that the security policy will be enforced and that can process a range of information sensitivities (i.e. classified, controlled unclassified information (CUI), or unclassified public information) simultaneously.

senses.definitionMd: A system that has the necessary security functions and assurance that the security policy will be enforced and that can process a range of information sensitivities (i.e. classified, controlled unclassified information (CUI), or unclassified public information) simultaneously.

entries.title: trusted computing base (TCB)
entries.summaryMd: Totality of protection mechanisms within a computer system, including hardware, firmware, and software, the combination responsible for enforcing a security policy.

senses.definitionMd: Totality of protection mechanisms within a computer system, including hardware, firmware, and software, the combination responsible for enforcing a security policy.

entries.title: trusted data recipient
entries.summaryMd: an entity that has limited access to the data that it receives as a result of being bound by some administrative control such as a law, regulation, or data use agreement

senses.definitionMd: an entity that has limited access to the data that it receives as a result of being bound by some administrative control such as a law, regulation, or data use agreement

entries.title: Trusted Execution Environment
entries.summaryMd: An area or enclave protected by a system processor.

senses.definitionMd: An area or enclave protected by a system processor.

entries.title: trusted foundry
entries.summaryMd: Facility that produces integrated circuits with a higher level of integrity assurance.

senses.definitionMd: Facility that produces integrated circuits with a higher level of integrity assurance.

entries.title: trusted network-layer onboarding
entries.summaryMd: A network-layer onboarding process that: provides each device with unique network credentials, provides the device and the network an opportunity to mutually authenticate, is performed over an encrypted channel (to protect network credential confidentiality), does not provide anyone with access to the network credentials, and can be performed repeatedly throughout the device lifecycle (to enable network credentials to be replaced).

senses.definitionMd: A network-layer onboarding process that: provides each device with unique network credentials, provides the device and the network an opportunity to mutually authenticate, is performed over an encrypted channel (to protect network credential confidentiality), does not provide anyone with access to the network credentials, and can be performed repeatedly throughout the device lifecycle (to enable network credentials to be replaced).

entries.title: trusted operating system
entries.summaryMd: An operating system in which there exists a level of confidence (based on rigorous analysis and testing) that the security principals and mechanisms (e.g., separation, isolation, least privilege, discretionary and non-discretionary access control, trusted path, authentication, and security policy enforcement) are correctly implemented and operate as intended even in the presence of adversarial activity.

senses.definitionMd: An operating system in which there exists a level of confidence (based on rigorous analysis and testing) that the security principals and mechanisms (e.g., separation, isolation, least privilege, discretionary and non-discretionary access control, trusted path, authentication, and security policy enforcement) are correctly implemented and operate as intended even in the presence of adversarial activity.

entries.title: Trusted Party
entries.summaryMd: A party that is trusted by its clients to generate cryptographic keys.

senses.definitionMd: A party that is trusted by its clients to generate cryptographic keys.

entries.title: trusted path
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism by which a user (through an input device) can communicate directly with the security functions of the information system with the necessary confidence to support the system security policy. This mechanism can only be activated by the user or the security functions of the information system and cannot be imitated by untrusted software.

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism by which a user (through an input device) can communicate directly with the security functions of the information system with the necessary confidence to support the system security policy. This mechanism can only be activated by the user or the security functions of the information system and cannot be imitated by untrusted software.

entries.title: Trusted Platform Module (TPM)
entries.summaryMd: A tamper-resistant integrated circuit built into some computer motherboards that can perform cryptographic operations (including key generation) and protect small amounts of sensitive information, such as passwords and cryptographic keys.

senses.definitionMd: A tamper-resistant integrated circuit built into some computer motherboards that can perform cryptographic operations (including key generation) and protect small amounts of sensitive information, such as passwords and cryptographic keys.

entries.title: trusted pool
entries.summaryMd: A physical or logical grouping of computing hardware in a data center that is tagged with specific and varying security policies. Within a trusted compute pool, the access and execution of applications and workloads are monitored, controlled, audited, etc.

senses.definitionMd: A physical or logical grouping of computing hardware in a data center that is tagged with specific and varying security policies. Within a trusted compute pool, the access and execution of applications and workloads are monitored, controlled, audited, etc.

entries.title: trusted process
entries.summaryMd: Process that has been tested and verified to operate only as intended.

senses.definitionMd: Process that has been tested and verified to operate only as intended.

entries.title: trusted recovery
entries.summaryMd: Ability to ensure recovery without compromise after a system failure.

senses.definitionMd: Ability to ensure recovery without compromise after a system failure.

entries.title: trusted referee
entries.summaryMd: An agent of the CSP who is trained to make risk-based decisions regarding an applicant’s identity proofing case when that applicant is unable to meet the expected requirements of a defined IAL proofing process.

senses.definitionMd: An agent of the CSP who is trained to make risk-based decisions regarding an applicant’s identity proofing case when that applicant is unable to meet the expected requirements of a defined IAL proofing process.

entries.title: Trusted Third Party
entries.summaryMd: An entity other than the key pair owner and verifier that is trusted by the owner or the verifier or both. Sometimes shortened to “trusted party.”

senses.definitionMd: An entity other than the key pair owner and verifier that is trusted by the owner or the verifier or both. Sometimes shortened to “trusted party.”

entries.title: trusted timestamp
entries.summaryMd: A digitally signed assertion by a trusted authority that a specific digital object existed at a particular time.

senses.definitionMd: A digitally signed assertion by a trusted authority that a specific digital object existed at a particular time.

entries.title: Trusted Timestamp Authority (TTA)
entries.summaryMd: An entity that is trusted to provide accurate time information.

senses.definitionMd: An entity that is trusted to provide accurate time information.

entries.title: trustworthiness
entries.summaryMd: The attribute of a person or enterprise that provides confidence to others of the qualifications, capabilities, and reliability of that entity to perform specific tasks and fulfill assigned responsibilities.

senses.definitionMd: The attribute of a person or enterprise that provides confidence to others of the qualifications, capabilities, and reliability of that entity to perform specific tasks and fulfill assigned responsibilities.

entries.title: trustworthiness (system)
entries.summaryMd: The degree to which an information system (including the information technology components that are used to build the system) can be expected to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information being processed, stored, or transmitted by the system across the full range of threats and individuals’ privacy.

senses.definitionMd: The degree to which an information system (including the information technology components that are used to build the system) can be expected to preserve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the information being processed, stored, or transmitted by the system across the full range of threats and individuals’ privacy.

entries.title: trustworthy information system
