entries.summaryMd: An information system that is believed to be capable of operating within defined levels of risk despite the environmental disruptions, human errors, structural failures, and purposeful attacks that are expected to occur in its environment of operation.

senses.definitionMd: An information system that is believed to be capable of operating within defined levels of risk despite the environmental disruptions, human errors, structural failures, and purposeful attacks that are expected to occur in its environment of operation.

entries.title: TTA_supplied_info
entries.summaryMd: Additional information that is included in the timestamped_data by a TTA during the generation of a timestamp_signature.

senses.definitionMd: Additional information that is included in the timestamped_data by a TTA during the generation of a timestamp_signature.

entries.title: Tunnel Mode
entries.summaryMd: An IPsec mode that creates an additional outer IP header for each protected packet.

senses.definitionMd: An IPsec mode that creates an additional outer IP header for each protected packet.

entries.title: Tunnel VPN
entries.summaryMd: An SSL connection that allows a remote user to securely access a wide variety of protocols and applications, through a tunnel that is running under SSL, via a Web browser, generally augmented by a client application or plug-in..

senses.definitionMd: An SSL connection that allows a remote user to securely access a wide variety of protocols and applications, through a tunnel that is running under SSL, via a Web browser, generally augmented by a client application or plug-in..

entries.title: tunneling
entries.summaryMd: Technology enabling one network to send its data via another network’s connections. Tunneling works by encapsulating a network protocol within packets carried by the second network.

senses.definitionMd: Technology enabling one network to send its data via another network’s connections. Tunneling works by encapsulating a network protocol within packets carried by the second network.

entries.title: Tuple Density
entries.summaryMd: Sum of t and the fraction of the covered (t+1)-tuples out of all possible (t+1)-tuples.

senses.definitionMd: Sum of t and the fraction of the covered (t+1)-tuples out of all possible (t+1)-tuples.

entries.title: Turing complete
entries.summaryMd: A system (computer system, programming language, etc.) that can be used for any algorithm, regardless of complexity, to find a solution.

senses.definitionMd: A system (computer system, programming language, etc.) that can be used for any algorithm, regardless of complexity, to find a solution.

entries.title: Two-Factor Authentication
entries.summaryMd: Proof of the possession of a physical or software token in combination with some memorized secret knowledge.

senses.definitionMd: Proof of the possession of a physical or software token in combination with some memorized secret knowledge.

entries.title: two-person control
entries.summaryMd: The continuous surveillance and control of material at all times by a minimum of two authorized individuals, each capable of detecting incorrect or unauthorized procedures with respect to the task being performed and each familiar with established security requirements.

senses.definitionMd: The continuous surveillance and control of material at all times by a minimum of two authorized individuals, each capable of detecting incorrect or unauthorized procedures with respect to the task being performed and each familiar with established security requirements.

entries.title: two-person integrity
entries.summaryMd: The system of storage and handling designed to prohibit individual access to certain COMSEC keying material by requiring the presence of at least two authorized persons, each capable of detecting incorrect or unauthorized security procedures with respect to the task being performed. Note: Two-Person Control refers to the handling of Nuclear Command and Control COMSEC material while Two-Person Integrity refers only to the handling of COMSEC keying material.

senses.definitionMd: The system of storage and handling designed to prohibit individual access to certain COMSEC keying material by requiring the presence of at least two authorized persons, each capable of detecting incorrect or unauthorized security procedures with respect to the task being performed. Note: Two-Person Control refers to the handling of Nuclear Command and Control COMSEC material while Two-Person Integrity refers only to the handling of COMSEC keying material.

entries.title: type accreditation
entries.summaryMd: A form of accreditation that is used to authorize multiple instances of a major application or general support system for operation at approved locations with the same type of computing environment. In situations where a major application or general support system is installed at multiple locations, a type accreditation will satisfy Certification and Accreditation (C&A) requirements only if the application or system consists of a common set of tested and approved hardware, software, and firmware. See type authorization.

senses.definitionMd: A form of accreditation that is used to authorize multiple instances of a major application or general support system for operation at approved locations with the same type of computing environment. In situations where a major application or general support system is installed at multiple locations, a type accreditation will satisfy Certification and Accreditation (C&A) requirements only if the application or system consists of a common set of tested and approved hardware, software, and firmware. See type authorization.

entries.title: type authorization
entries.summaryMd: An official authorization decision to employ identical copies of an information system or subsystem (including hardware, software, firmware, and/or applications) in specified environments of operation.

senses.definitionMd: An official authorization decision to employ identical copies of an information system or subsystem (including hardware, software, firmware, and/or applications) in specified environments of operation.

entries.title: type certification
entries.summaryMd: The certification acceptance of replica information systems based on the comprehensive evaluation of the technical and non-technical security features of an information system and other safeguards, made as part of and in support of the formal approval process, to establish the extent to which a particular design and implementation meet a specified set of security requirements.

senses.definitionMd: The certification acceptance of replica information systems based on the comprehensive evaluation of the technical and non-technical security features of an information system and other safeguards, made as part of and in support of the formal approval process, to establish the extent to which a particular design and implementation meet a specified set of security requirements.

entries.title: Type I error
entries.summaryMd: Incorrectly rejection of a true null hypothesis.

senses.definitionMd: Incorrectly rejection of a true null hypothesis.

entries.title: u
entries.summaryMd: The number of bits in the last plaintext or ciphertext block.

senses.definitionMd: The number of bits in the last plaintext or ciphertext block.

entries.title: U.S.-controlled facility
entries.summaryMd: A base or building, access to which is physically controlled by U.S. citizens or resident aliens who are authorized U.S. Government or U.S. Government contractor employees.

senses.definitionMd: A base or building, access to which is physically controlled by U.S. citizens or resident aliens who are authorized U.S. Government or U.S. Government contractor employees.

entries.title: U.S.-controlled space
entries.summaryMd: A space (e.g., room or floor) within a facility other than a U.S.-controlled facility, access to which is physically controlled by U.S. citizens or resident aliens who are authorized U.S. Government or U.S. Government contractor employees. Keys or combinations to locks controlling entrance to the U.S.-controlled space must be under the exclusive control of U.S. citizens or resident aliens who are U.S. Government or U.S. Government contractor employees.

senses.definitionMd: A space (e.g., room or floor) within a facility other than a U.S.-controlled facility, access to which is physically controlled by U.S. citizens or resident aliens who are authorized U.S. Government or U.S. Government contractor employees. Keys or combinations to locks controlling entrance to the U.S.-controlled space must be under the exclusive control of U.S. citizens or resident aliens who are U.S. Government or U.S. Government contractor employees.

entries.title: U.S. national interests
entries.summaryMd: Matters of vital interest to the United States to include national security, public safety, national economic security, the safe and reliable functioning of “critical infrastructure”, and the availability of “key resources”.

senses.definitionMd: Matters of vital interest to the United States to include national security, public safety, national economic security, the safe and reliable functioning of “critical infrastructure”, and the availability of “key resources”.

entries.title: U.S. person
entries.summaryMd: U.S. person means a person (as defined in 22 CFR 120.14) who is a lawful permanent resident as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1101(a) (20) or who is a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a) (3). It also means any corporation, business association, partnership, society, trust, or any other entity, organization or group that is incorporated to do business in the United States. It also includes any governmental (federal, state or local) entity. It does not include any foreign person as defined in 22 CFR 120.16.

senses.definitionMd: U.S. person means a person (as defined in 22 CFR 120.14) who is a lawful permanent resident as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1101(a) (20) or who is a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a) (3). It also means any corporation, business association, partnership, society, trust, or any other entity, organization or group that is incorporated to do business in the United States. It also includes any governmental (federal, state or local) entity. It does not include any foreign person as defined in 22 CFR 120.16.

entries.title: umbilical cord
entries.summaryMd: The cable that connects the space vehicle to the launch pad during pre-launch to monitor the vehicle health and is disconnected or cut when the vehicle launches; enables the exchange of data with ground launch mission systems.

senses.definitionMd: The cable that connects the space vehicle to the launch pad during pre-launch to monitor the vehicle health and is disconnected or cut when the vehicle launches; enables the exchange of data with ground launch mission systems.

entries.title: UMTS Subscriber Identity Module (USIM)
entries.summaryMd: A module similar to the SIM in GSM/GPRS networks, but with additional capabilities suited to 3G networks.

senses.definitionMd: A module similar to the SIM in GSM/GPRS networks, but with additional capabilities suited to 3G networks.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "UMTS Subscriber Identity Module (USIM)"

entries.title: unattended
entries.summaryMd: A facility is unattended when there is no human presence. Use of roaming guards and/or an intrusion detection system is not enough to consider a facility attended. Having a trusted individual sitting at the entrance to a vault does make the vault attended.

senses.definitionMd: A facility is unattended when there is no human presence. Use of roaming guards and/or an intrusion detection system is not enough to consider a facility attended. Having a trusted individual sitting at the entrance to a vault does make the vault attended.

entries.title: unauthorized access
entries.summaryMd: Any access that violates the stated security policy.

senses.definitionMd: Any access that violates the stated security policy.

entries.title: unauthorized disclosure
entries.summaryMd: An event involving the exposure of information to entities not authorized access to the information.

senses.definitionMd: An event involving the exposure of information to entities not authorized access to the information.

entries.title: Unbiased
entries.summaryMd: A value that is chosen from a sample space is said to be unbiased if all potential values have the same probability of being chosen. Contrast with biased.

senses.definitionMd: A value that is chosen from a sample space is said to be unbiased if all potential values have the same probability of being chosen. Contrast with biased.

entries.title: Unbind
entries.summaryMd: To deterministically transform a binding into its logical-form construct.

senses.definitionMd: To deterministically transform a binding into its logical-form construct.

entries.title: unbounded differential privacy
entries.summaryMd: A unit of privacy variant that calls two datasets D1 and D2 neighbors if it is possible to construct D2 from D1 by adding or removing one person’s data. Under unbounded differential privacy, neighboring datasets have different sizes.

senses.definitionMd: A unit of privacy variant that calls two datasets D1 and D2 neighbors if it is possible to construct D2 from D1 by adding or removing one person’s data. Under unbounded differential privacy, neighboring datasets have different sizes.

entries.title: unclassified
entries.summaryMd: Information that does not require safeguarding or dissemination controls pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13556 (Controlled Unclassified Information) and has not been determined to require protection against unauthorized disclosure pursuant to E.O. 13526 (Classified National Security Information), or any predecessor or successor Order, or the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended. See controlled unclassified information (CUI), and classified national security information.

senses.definitionMd: Information that does not require safeguarding or dissemination controls pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13556 (Controlled Unclassified Information) and has not been determined to require protection against unauthorized disclosure pursuant to E.O. 13526 (Classified National Security Information), or any predecessor or successor Order, or the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended. See controlled unclassified information (CUI), and classified national security information.

entries.title: unencrypted key
entries.summaryMd: Key that has not been encrypted in a system approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) for key encryption or encrypted key in the presence of its associated key encryption key (KEK) or transfer key encryption key (TrKEK). Encrypted key in the same fill device as its associated KEK or TrKEK is considered unencrypted. (Unencrypted key is also known as RED key).

senses.definitionMd: Key that has not been encrypted in a system approved by the National Security Agency (NSA) for key encryption or encrypted key in the presence of its associated key encryption key (KEK) or transfer key encryption key (TrKEK). Encrypted key in the same fill device as its associated KEK or TrKEK is considered unencrypted. (Unencrypted key is also known as RED key).

entries.title: unidirectional gateway
entries.summaryMd: Unidirectional gateways are a combination of hardware and software. The hardware permits data to flow from one network to another but is physically unable to send any information at all back to the source network. The software replicates databases and emulates protocol servers and devices.

senses.definitionMd: Unidirectional gateways are a combination of hardware and software. The hardware permits data to flow from one network to another but is physically unable to send any information at all back to the source network. The software replicates databases and emulates protocol servers and devices.

entries.title: Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI)
entries.summaryMd: A possible replacement for the conventional BIOS that is becoming widely deployed in new x86-based computer systems. The UEFI specifications were preceded by the EFI specifications.

senses.definitionMd: A possible replacement for the conventional BIOS that is becoming widely deployed in new x86-based computer systems. The UEFI specifications were preceded by the EFI specifications.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Unified Extensible Firmware Interface (UEFI)"

entries.title: Uniform Resource Identifier
entries.summaryMd: A compact sequence of characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource available on the Internet. The syntax used for URIs is defined in.

senses.definitionMd: A compact sequence of characters that identifies an abstract or physical resource available on the Internet. The syntax used for URIs is defined in.

entries.title: Uniform Resource Locator
entries.summaryMd: A reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it. A typical URL could have the form http://www.example.com/index.html, which indicates a protocol (http), a host name (www.example.com), and a file name (index.html). Also sometimes referred to as a web address.

senses.definitionMd: A reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it. A typical URL could have the form http://www.example.com/index.html, which indicates a protocol (http), a host name (www.example.com), and a file name (index.html). Also sometimes referred to as a web address.

entries.title: Uninstantiate
entries.summaryMd: The termination of a DRBG instantiation.

senses.definitionMd: The termination of a DRBG instantiation.

entries.title: Uninterruptible Power Supply
entries.summaryMd: A device with an internal battery that allows connected devices to run for at least a short time when the primary power source is lost.

senses.definitionMd: A device with an internal battery that allows connected devices to run for at least a short time when the primary power source is lost.

entries.title: unit of privacy
entries.summaryMd: The choice of definition for neighboring datasets.

senses.definitionMd: The choice of definition for neighboring datasets.

entries.title: United States Government Configuration Baseline (USGCB)
entries.summaryMd: The United States Government Configuration Baseline (USGCB) provides security configuration baselines for Information Technology products widely deployed across the federal agencies. The USGCB baseline evolved from the federal Desktop Core Configuration mandate. The USGCB is a Federal government-wide initiative that provides guidance to agencies on what should be done to improve and maintain an effective configuration settings focusing primarily on security.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "United States Government Configuration Baseline (USGCB)"

entries.title: United States Government Environment
entries.summaryMd: A Custom environment that contains federal government systems to be secured according to prescribed configurations as mandated by policy.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "United States Government Environment"

entries.title: Universal Description, Discovery, and Integration (UDDI)
entries.summaryMd: An XML-based lookup service for locating Web services in an Internet Topology. UDDI provides a platform-independent way of describing and discovering Web services and Web service providers. The UDDI data structures provide a framework for the description of basic service information, and an extensible mechanism to specify detailed service access information using any standard description language.

UDDI provides a platform-independent way of describing and discovering Web services and Web service providers. The UDDI data structures provide a framework for the description of basic service information, and an extensible mechanism to specify detailed service access information using any standard description language.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Universal Description, Discovery, and Integration (UDDI)"

entries.title: Universal Integrated Circuit Card
entries.summaryMd: An integrated circuit card that securely stores the international mobile subscriber identity (IMSI) and the related cryptographic key used to identify and authenticate subscribers on mobile devices. A UICC may be referred to as a: SIM, USIM, RUIM or CSIM, and is used interchangeably with those terms.

A UICC may be referred to as a: SIM, USIM, RUIM or CSIM, and is used interchangeably with those terms.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Universal Integrated Circuit Card"

entries.title: Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS)
entries.summaryMd: A third-generation (3G) mobile phone technology standardized by the 3GPP as the successor to GSM.

senses.definitionMd: A third-generation (3G) mobile phone technology standardized by the 3GPP as the successor to GSM.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Universal Mobile Telecommunications System (UMTS)"

entries.title: Universal Serial Bus (USB)
entries.summaryMd: A hardware interface for low-speed peripherals such as the keyboard, mouse, joystick, scanner, printer, and telephony devices.

senses.definitionMd: A hardware interface for low-speed peripherals such as the keyboard, mouse, joystick, scanner, printer, and telephony devices.

entries.title: Universal Statistical Test
entries.summaryMd: The purpose of the test is to detect whether or not the sequence can be significantly compressed without loss of information. A compressible sequence is considered to be non­ random.

senses.definitionMd: The purpose of the test is to detect whether or not the sequence can be significantly compressed without loss of information. A compressible sequence is considered to be non­ random.

entries.title: unkeyed
entries.summaryMd: COMSEC equipment containing no key or containing key that has been protected from unauthorized use by removing the cryptographic ignition key (CIK) or deactivating the personal identification number (PIN).

senses.definitionMd: COMSEC equipment containing no key or containing key that has been protected from unauthorized use by removing the cryptographic ignition key (CIK) or deactivating the personal identification number (PIN).

entries.title: Unmanaged Device
entries.summaryMd: A device inside the assessment boundary that is either unauthorized or, if authorized, not assigned to a person to administer.

senses.definitionMd: A device inside the assessment boundary that is either unauthorized or, if authorized, not assigned to a person to administer.

entries.title: Unpredictable
entries.summaryMd: In the context of random bit generation, an output bit is unpredictable if an adversary has only a negligible advantage (that is, essentially not much better than chance) in predicting it correctly.

senses.definitionMd: In the context of random bit generation, an output bit is unpredictable if an adversary has only a negligible advantage (that is, essentially not much better than chance) in predicting it correctly.

entries.title: unstructured data
entries.summaryMd: Data formats that often lack explicit structure that relates data to individuals, such as text, pictures, audio, and video.

senses.definitionMd: Data formats that often lack explicit structure that relates data to individuals, such as text, pictures, audio, and video.

entries.title: unsupervised learning
entries.summaryMd: A type of machine learning in which a model learns based on pat­terns in unlabeled data, such as learning a function to cluster or group data points.

senses.definitionMd: A type of machine learning in which a model learns based on pat­terns in unlabeled data, such as learning a function to cluster or group data points.

entries.title: untrusted party
entries.summaryMd: A party that cannot be expected to keep sensitive data safe or refrain from disclosing it to others.

senses.definitionMd: A party that cannot be expected to keep sensitive data safe or refrain from disclosing it to others.

entries.title: untrusted process
entries.summaryMd: Process that has not been evaluated or examined for correctness and adherence to the security policy. It may include incorrect or malicious code that attempts to circumvent the security mechanisms.

senses.definitionMd: Process that has not been evaluated or examined for correctness and adherence to the security policy. It may include incorrect or malicious code that attempts to circumvent the security mechanisms.

entries.title: unwrapping function
entries.summaryMd: The inverse of the wrapping function.

senses.definitionMd: The inverse of the wrapping function.

entries.title: UOCAVA Systems
entries.summaryMd: Information technology systems which support various aspects of the UOCAVA voting process?

senses.definitionMd: Information technology systems which support various aspects of the UOCAVA voting process?

entries.title: Update
entries.summaryMd: A patch, upgrade, or other modification to code that corrects security and/or functionality problems in software.

senses.definitionMd: A patch, upgrade, or other modification to code that corrects security and/or functionality problems in software.

entries.title: update (a certificate)
entries.summaryMd: 2. The process of creating a new certificate with a new serial number that differs in one or more fields from the old certificate. The new certificate may have the same or different subject public key.

entries.title: update (a key)
entries.summaryMd: Automatic or manual cryptographic process that irreversibly modifies the state of a COMSEC key, equipment, device, or system.

senses.definitionMd: Automatic or manual cryptographic process that irreversibly modifies the state of a COMSEC key, equipment, device, or system.

entries.title: Update Server
entries.summaryMd: A server that provides patches and other software updates to IoT devices.

senses.definitionMd: A server that provides patches and other software updates to IoT devices.

entries.title: Upgrade Management System
entries.summaryMd: The hardware and software used to communicate and manage the Upgrade Process. The Upgrade Management System may be included in the Network Management System.

senses.definitionMd: The hardware and software used to communicate and manage the Upgrade Process. The Upgrade Management System may be included in the Network Management System.

entries.title: Upgrading
entries.summaryMd: An authorized increase in the level of protection to be provided to specified information, e.g., from a Low impact-level to a Moderate impact-level.

senses.definitionMd: An authorized increase in the level of protection to be provided to specified information, e.g., from a Low impact-level to a Moderate impact-level.

entries.title: uplink
entries.summaryMd: Communication that originates from the ground to the satellite.

senses.definitionMd: Communication that originates from the ground to the satellite.

entries.title: Usability
entries.summaryMd: The extent to which a product can be used by specified users to achieve specified goals with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction in a specified context of use.

senses.definitionMd: The extent to which a product can be used by specified users to achieve specified goals with effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction in a specified context of use.

entries.title: user
entries.summaryMd: Individual or (system) process authorized to access an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Individual or (system) process authorized to access an information system.

entries.title: user activity monitoring
entries.summaryMd: The technical capability to observe and record the actions and activities of an individual, at any time, on any device accessing U.S. Government information in order to detect insider threat and to support authorized investigations.

senses.definitionMd: The technical capability to observe and record the actions and activities of an individual, at any time, on any device accessing U.S. Government information in order to detect insider threat and to support authorized investigations.

entries.title: user agreement
entries.summaryMd: A user-based agreement that is similar to rules of behavior. It specifies user responsibilities when exchanging information or accessing information or systems that contain the exchanged information. Also known as access agreement or acceptable use agreement.

senses.definitionMd: A user-based agreement that is similar to rules of behavior. It specifies user responsibilities when exchanging information or accessing information or systems that contain the exchanged information. Also known as access agreement or acceptable use agreement.

entries.title: user ID
entries.summaryMd: Unique symbol or character string used by an information system to identify a specific user.

senses.definitionMd: Unique symbol or character string used by an information system to identify a specific user.

entries.title: User interface
entries.summaryMd: The physical or logical means by which users interact with a system, device or process.

senses.definitionMd: The physical or logical means by which users interact with a system, device or process.

entries.title: User Key
entries.summaryMd: A key that is used for granting access to a user account via the SSH protocol (as opposed to a host key, which does not grant access to anything but serves to authenticate a host). entries.title: user‐level privacy

senses.definitionMd: A unit of privacy that defines neighboring databases as those that differ in one user’s data.

entries.title: User Principal Name
entries.summaryMd: In Windows Active Directory, this is the name of a system user in email address format, i.e., a concatenation of username, the “@” symbol, and domain name.

entries.title: user representative (risk management)
entries.summaryMd: The person that defines the system’s operational and functional requirements, and who is responsible for ensuring that user operational interests are met throughout the systems authorization process.

senses.definitionMd: The person that defines the system’s operational and functional requirements, and who is responsible for ensuring that user operational interests are met throughout the systems authorization process.

entries.title: user_supplied_info
entries.summaryMd: Additional information that is provided by an entity when requesting a timestamp from a TTA.

entries.title: utility
entries.summaryMd: The degree to which a dataset or statistic is useful for a specific purpose.

entries.title: V

entries.title: Valid Data Element
entries.summaryMd: A payload, an associated data string, or a nonce that satisfies the restrictions of the formatting function.

senses.definitionMd: A payload, an associated data string, or a nonce that satisfies the restrictions of the formatting function.

entries.title: valid length
entries.summaryMd: A length for a plaintext or ciphertext input that is allowed for an implementation of the authenticated-encryption function or the authenticated-decryption function.

entries.title: Validated ROA Payload
entries.summaryMd: Validated ROA Payload contains {prefix, max length, origin AS} information from an X.509 validated ROA.

entries.title: validation
entries.summaryMd: Confirmation (through the provision of strong, sound, objective evidence) that requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled (e.g., a trustworthy credential has been presented, or data or information has been formatted in accordance with a defined set of rules, or a specific process has demonstrated that an entity under consideration meets, in all respects, its defined attributes or requirements).

senses.definitionMd: Confirmation (through the provision of strong, sound, objective evidence) that requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled (e.g., a trustworthy credential has been presented, or data or information has been formatted in accordance with a defined set of rules, or a specific process has demonstrated that an entity under consideration meets, in all respects, its defined attributes or requirements).

entries.title: Validity period
entries.summaryMd: The period of time during which a certificate is intended to be valid; the period of time between the start date and time and end date and time in a certificate.

senses.definitionMd: The period of time during which a certificate is intended to be valid; the period of time between the start date and time and end date and time in a certificate.

entries.title: Value
entries.summaryMd: A named data value that can be substituted into other items’ properties or into checks.

senses.definitionMd: A named data value that can be substituted into other items’ properties or into checks.

entries.title: Value String
entries.summaryMd: A value assigned to an attribute of a WFN. It must be a non-empty contiguous string of bytes encoded using printable Unicode Transformation Format-8 (UTF-8) characters with hexadecimal values between x00 and x7F.

senses.definitionMd: A value assigned to an attribute of a WFN. It must be a non-empty contiguous string of bytes encoded using printable Unicode Transformation Format-8 (UTF-8) characters with hexadecimal values between x00 and x7F.

entries.title: valve
entries.summaryMd: An in-line device in a fluid-flow system that can interrupt flow, regulate the rate of flow, or divert flow to another branch of the system.

senses.definitionMd: An in-line device in a fluid-flow system that can interrupt flow, regulate the rate of flow, or divert flow to another branch of the system.

entries.title: \(\varepsilon\)
entries.summaryMd: A positive constant that is assumed to be no greater than \(2^{-32}\)

senses.definitionMd: A positive constant that is assumed to be no greater than \(2^{-32}\)

entries.title: variable
entries.summaryMd: A logical entity that holds a single value.

senses.definitionMd: A logical entity that holds a single value.

entries.title: Variable-value configuration
entries.summaryMd: For a set of t variables, a variable-value configuration is a set of t valid values, one for each of the variables.

senses.definitionMd: For a set of t variables, a variable-value configuration is a set of t valid values, one for each of the variables.

entries.title: Variable-value configuration coverage
entries.summaryMd: For a given combination of t variables, variable-value configuration coverage is the proportion of variable-value configurations that are covered by at least one test case in a test set.

senses.definitionMd: For a given combination of t variables, variable-value configuration coverage is the proportion of variable-value configurations that are covered by at least one test case in a test set.

entries.title: variant
entries.summaryMd: One of two or more code symbols having the same plain text equivalent.

senses.definitionMd: One of two or more code symbols having the same plain text equivalent.

entries.title: vehicle
entries.summaryMd: Space operational items that include the launching items used to place the satellite, bus, and/or payload into orbit.

senses.definitionMd: Space operational items that include the launching items used to place the satellite, bus, and/or payload into orbit.

entries.title: Vendor
entries.summaryMd: A commercial supplier of software or hardware.

senses.definitionMd: A commercial supplier of software or hardware.

entries.title: verification
entries.summaryMd: The process of confirming or denying that a claimed identity is correct by comparing the credentials of a person requesting access with those previously proven and associated with the PIV Card or a derived PIV credential associated with the identity being claimed.

senses.definitionMd: The process of confirming or denying that a claimed identity is correct by comparing the credentials of a person requesting access with those previously proven and associated with the PIV Card or a derived PIV credential associated with the identity being claimed.

entries.title: verification key
entries.summaryMd: The cryptographic key used to verify a signature. In asymmetric cryptography, the verification key refers to the public key of the cryptographic key pair. In symmetric cryptography, the verification key is the symmetric key.

senses.definitionMd: The cryptographic key used to verify a signature. In asymmetric cryptography, the verification key refers to the public key of the cryptographic key pair. In symmetric cryptography, the verification key is the symmetric key.

entries.title: verification model
entries.summaryMd: The synthetic data user is provided with statistics that measure the similarity of the synthetic data result to the same output computed from the confidential data.

senses.definitionMd: The synthetic data user is provided with statistics that measure the similarity of the synthetic data result to the same output computed from the confidential data.

entries.title: verifier
entries.summaryMd: The entity that verifies the authenticity of a digital signature using the public key.

senses.definitionMd: The entity that verifies the authenticity of a digital signature using the public key.

entries.title: Verifier Impersonation
entries.summaryMd: A technique for attempting to acquire sensitive data, such as bank account numbers, through a fraudulent solicitation in email or on a web site, in which the perpetrator masquerades as a legitimate business or reputable person.

senses.definitionMd: A technique for attempting to acquire sensitive data, such as bank account numbers, through a fraudulent solicitation in email or on a web site, in which the perpetrator masquerades as a legitimate business or reputable person.

entries.title: Version Scanning
entries.summaryMd: The process of identifying the service application and application version currently in use.

senses.definitionMd: The process of identifying the service application and application version currently in use.

entries.title: view
entries.summaryMd: Representation of a whole system from the perspective of a related set of concerns.

senses.definitionMd: Representation of a whole system from the perspective of a related set of concerns.

entries.title: viewpoint
entries.summaryMd: Specification of the conventions for constructing and using a view.

senses.definitionMd: Specification of the conventions for constructing and using a view.

entries.title: virtual-led
entries.summaryMd: When instruction occurs in a virtual or simulated environment and is presented or facilitated by an instructor in real time.

senses.definitionMd: When instruction occurs in a virtual or simulated environment and is presented or facilitated by an instructor in real time.

entries.title: Virtual Local Area Network
entries.summaryMd: A broadcast domain that is partitioned and isolated within a network at the data link layer. A single physical local area network (LAN) can be logically partitioned into multiple, independent VLANs; a group of devices on one or more physical LANs can be configured to communicate within the same VLAN, as if they were attached to the same physical LAN.

senses.definitionMd: A broadcast domain that is partitioned and isolated within a network at the data link layer. A single physical local area network (LAN) can be logically partitioned into multiple, independent VLANs; a group of devices on one or more physical LANs can be configured to communicate within the same VLAN, as if they were attached to the same physical LAN.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Virtual Local Area Network"

entries.title: Virtual machine monitor (VMM)
entries.summaryMd: See “hypervisor”.

senses.definitionMd: See “hypervisor”.

entries.title: Virtual Machine (VM)
entries.summaryMd: A simulated environment created by virtualization.

senses.definitionMd: A simulated environment created by virtualization.

entries.title: virtual private network (VPN)
entries.summaryMd: Protected information system link utilizing tunneling, security controls, and endpoint address translation giving the impression of a dedicated line.

senses.definitionMd: Protected information system link utilizing tunneling, security controls, and endpoint address translation giving the impression of a dedicated line.

entries.title: Virtualization
entries.summaryMd: The simulation of the software and/or hardware upon which other software runs.

senses.definitionMd: The simulation of the software and/or hardware upon which other software runs.

entries.title: Virtualized Host
entries.summaryMd: The physical host on which the virtualization software such as the Hypervisor is installed. Usually, the virtualized host will contain a special hardware platform that assists virtualization - specifically Instruction Set and Memory virtualization.

senses.definitionMd: The physical host on which the virtualization software such as the Hypervisor is installed. Usually, the virtualized host will contain a special hardware platform that assists virtualization - specifically Instruction Set and Memory virtualization.

entries.title: virus
entries.summaryMd: A computer program that can copy itself and infect a computer without permission or knowledge of the user. A virus might corrupt or delete data on a computer, use e-mail programs to spread itself to other computers, or even erase everything on a hard disk. See malicious code.

senses.definitionMd: A computer program that can copy itself and infect a computer without permission or knowledge of the user. A virus might corrupt or delete data on a computer, use e-mail programs to spread itself to other computers, or even erase everything on a hard disk. See malicious code.

entries.title: Visibility
entries.summaryMd: Amount of information that can be gathered about a supplier, product, or service and how far through the supply chain this information can be obtained.

senses.definitionMd: Amount of information that can be gathered about a supplier, product, or service and how far through the supply chain this information can be obtained.

entries.title: Vn
entries.summaryMd: The expected number of runs that would occur in a sequence of length n under an assumption of randomness See Sections 2.3 and 3.3.

senses.definitionMd: The expected number of runs that would occur in a sequence of length n under an assumption of randomness See Sections 2.3 and 3.3.

entries.title: Vn(obs)
entries.summaryMd: The observed number of runs in a sequence of length n. See Sections 2.3 and 3.3.

senses.definitionMd: The observed number of runs in a sequence of length n. See Sections 2.3 and 3.3.

entries.title: voice over internet protocol (VoIP)
entries.summaryMd: A term used to describe the transmission of packetized voice using the internet protocol (IP) and consists of both signaling and media protocols.

senses.definitionMd: A term used to describe the transmission of packetized voice using the internet protocol (IP) and consists of both signaling and media protocols.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "voice over internet protocol (VoIP)"

entries.title: Volatile Data
entries.summaryMd: Data on a live system that is lost after a computer is powered down.

senses.definitionMd: Data on a live system that is lost after a computer is powered down.

entries.title: Volatile Memory
entries.summaryMd: Memory that loses its content when power is turned off or lost.

senses.definitionMd: Memory that loses its content when power is turned off or lost.

entries.title: vulnerability
entries.summaryMd: Weakness in an information system, system security procedures, internal controls, or implementation that could be exploited or triggered by a threat source.

senses.definitionMd: Weakness in an information system, system security procedures, internal controls, or implementation that could be exploited or triggered by a threat source.

entries.title: vulnerability advisory report
entries.summaryMd: Publication by a technology developer and/or provider to customers or the general public that describes a vulnerability with a focus on remediation and mitigation.

senses.definitionMd: Publication by a technology developer and/or provider to customers or the general public that describes a vulnerability with a focus on remediation and mitigation.

entries.title: vulnerability analysis
entries.summaryMd: Formal description and evaluation of the vulnerabilities in an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Formal description and evaluation of the vulnerabilities in an information system.

entries.title: vulnerability assessment
entries.summaryMd: Formal description and evaluation of the vulnerabilities in an information system.

senses.definitionMd: Formal description and evaluation of the vulnerabilities in an information system.

entries.title: Vulnerability Disclosure Program Office
entries.summaryMd: The entity with which an agency coordinates internally to resolve reported vulnerabilities.

senses.definitionMd: The entity with which an agency coordinates internally to resolve reported vulnerabilities.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Vulnerability Disclosure Program Office"

entries.title: Vulnerability Management
entries.summaryMd: An ISCM capability that identifies vulnerabilities [Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs)] on devices that are likely to be used by attackers to compromise a device and use it as a platform from which to extend compromise to the network.

senses.definitionMd: An ISCM capability that identifies vulnerabilities [Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs)] on devices that are likely to be used by attackers to compromise a device and use it as a platform from which to extend compromise to the network.

entries.title: vulnerability report
entries.summaryMd: Notification received by a technology developer and/or provider from a vulnerability reporter, which may include a description of what product or service is affected, how the potential vulnerability can be identified, demonstrated, or reproduced, and what type of functional impact the vulnerability allows.

senses.definitionMd: Notification received by a technology developer and/or provider from a vulnerability reporter, which may include a description of what product or service is affected, how the potential vulnerability can be identified, demonstrated, or reproduced, and what type of functional impact the vulnerability allows.

entries.title: vulnerability scanner
entries.summaryMd: (As used in this volume) A network tool (hardware and/or software) that scans network devices to identify generally known and organization specific CVEs. It may do this based on a wide range of signature strategies.

senses.definitionMd: (As used in this volume) A network tool (hardware and/or software) that scans network devices to identify generally known and organization specific CVEs. It may do this based on a wide range of signature strategies.

entries.title: Vulnerability Scanning
entries.summaryMd: A technique used to identify hosts/host attributes and associated vulnerabilities.

senses.definitionMd: A technique used to identify hosts/host attributes and associated vulnerabilities.

entries.title: w
entries.summaryMd: In XMSS, the length of a Winternitz chain. A single Winternitz chain uses log2(w) bits from the hash or checksum.

senses.definitionMd: In XMSS, the length of a Winternitz chain. A single Winternitz chain uses log2(w) bits from the hash or checksum.

entries.title: Wallet
entries.summaryMd: Software used to store and manage asymmetric-keys and addresses used for transactions.

senses.definitionMd: Software used to store and manage asymmetric-keys and addresses used for transactions.

entries.title: wander
entries.summaryMd: The long-term variations—random walk frequency noise—of the significant instants of a digital signal from their ideal position in time (where long-term implies that these variations are of frequency less than 10 Hz).

senses.definitionMd: The long-term variations—random walk frequency noise—of the significant instants of a digital signal from their ideal position in time (where long-term implies that these variations are of frequency less than 10 Hz).

entries.title: WAP identity module
entries.summaryMd: a security module implemented in the SIM that provides a trusted environment for using WAP related applications and services on a mobile device via a WAP gateway.

senses.definitionMd: a security module implemented in the SIM that provides a trusted environment for using WAP related applications and services on a mobile device via a WAP gateway.

entries.title: warm site
entries.summaryMd: An environmentally conditioned work space that is partially equipped with information systems and telecommunications equipment to support relocated operations in the event of a significant disruption.

senses.definitionMd: An environmentally conditioned work space that is partially equipped with information systems and telecommunications equipment to support relocated operations in the event of a significant disruption.

entries.title: warning banner
entries.summaryMd: The opening screen that informs users of the implications of accessing a computer resource (e.g., consent to monitor). A security banner. System use notification.

senses.definitionMd: The opening screen that informs users of the implications of accessing a computer resource (e.g., consent to monitor). A security banner. System use notification.

entries.title: Watering Hole
entries.summaryMd: Watering hole attacks involve attackers compromising one or more legitimate Web sites with malware in an attempt to target and infect visitors to those sites.

senses.definitionMd: Watering hole attacks involve attackers compromising one or more legitimate Web sites with malware in an attempt to target and infect visitors to those sites.

entries.title: watering hole attack
entries.summaryMd: In a watering hole attack, the attacker compromises a site likely to be visited by a particular target group, rather than attacking the target group directly.

senses.definitionMd: In a watering hole attack, the attacker compromises a site likely to be visited by a particular target group, rather than attacking the target group directly.

entries.title: weakest judgment algorithm
entries.summaryMd: An inter-level judgment conflict resolution algorithm where the weakest judgment is taken as the result.

senses.definitionMd: An inter-level judgment conflict resolution algorithm where the weakest judgment is taken as the result.

entries.title: weakness
entries.summaryMd: Defect or characteristic that may lead to undesirable behavior.

senses.definitionMd: Defect or characteristic that may lead to undesirable behavior.

entries.title: Weapons System
entries.summaryMd: A 'weapons system' is a combination of one or more weapons with all related equipment, materials, services, personnel, and means of delivery and deployment (if applicable) required for self- sufficiency.

senses.definitionMd: A 'weapons system' is a combination of one or more weapons with all related equipment, materials, services, personnel, and means of delivery and deployment (if applicable) required for self- sufficiency.

entries.title: web-based training
entries.summaryMd: An internet-based session that allows learners to study independently and at their own pace with video, audio, and/or interactive techniques (e.g., drag-and-drop or fill in the blank). Built-in testing and accountability features can gauge performance.

senses.definitionMd: An internet-based session that allows learners to study independently and at their own pace with video, audio, and/or interactive techniques (e.g., drag-and-drop or fill in the blank). Built-in testing and accountability features can gauge performance.

entries.title: Web Browser
entries.summaryMd: Client software used to view Web content.

senses.definitionMd: Client software used to view Web content.

entries.title: web bug
entries.summaryMd: Malicious code, invisible to a user, placed on web sites in such a way that it allows third parties to track use of web servers and collect information about the user, including internet protocol (IP) address, host name, browser type and version, operating system name and version, and web browser cookie.

senses.definitionMd: Malicious code, invisible to a user, placed on web sites in such a way that it allows third parties to track use of web servers and collect information about the user, including internet protocol (IP) address, host name, browser type and version, operating system name and version, and web browser cookie.

entries.title: Web Portal
entries.summaryMd: Provides a single point of entry into the SOA for requester entities, enabling them to access Web services transparently from any device at virtually any location.

senses.definitionMd: Provides a single point of entry into the SOA for requester entities, enabling them to access Web services transparently from any device at virtually any location.

entries.title: Web Server
entries.summaryMd: A computer that provides World Wide Web (WWW) services on the Internet. It includes the hardware, operating system, Web server software, and Web site content (Web pages). If the Web server is used internally and not by the public, it may be known as an “intranet server.”

senses.definitionMd: A computer that provides World Wide Web (WWW) services on the Internet. It includes the hardware, operating system, Web server software, and Web site content (Web pages). If the Web server is used internally and not by the public, it may be known as an “intranet server.”

entries.title: Web Server Administrator
entries.summaryMd: The Web server equivalent of a system administrator. Web server administrators are system architects responsible for the overall design, implementation, and maintenance of Web servers. They may or may not be responsible for Web content, which is traditionally the responsibility of the Webmaster.

senses.definitionMd: The Web server equivalent of a system administrator. Web server administrators are system architects responsible for the overall design, implementation, and maintenance of Web servers. They may or may not be responsible for Web content, which is traditionally the responsibility of the Webmaster.

entries.title: Web Service
entries.summaryMd: A software component or system designed to support interoperable machine- or application- oriented interaction over a network. A Web service has an interface described in a machine-processable format (specifically WSDL). Other systems interact with the Web service in a manner prescribed by its description using SOAP messages, typically conveyed using HTTP with an XML serialization in conjunction with other Web-related standards.

senses.definitionMd: A software component or system designed to support interoperable machine- or application- oriented interaction over a network. A Web service has an interface described in a machine-processable format (specifically WSDL). Other systems interact with the Web service in a manner prescribed by its description using SOAP messages, typically conveyed using HTTP with an XML serialization in conjunction with other Web-related standards.

entries.title: Web Service Interoperability (WS-I) Basic Profile
entries.summaryMd: A set of standards and clarifications to standards that vendors must follow for basic interoperability with SOAP products.

senses.definitionMd: A set of standards and clarifications to standards that vendors must follow for basic interoperability with SOAP products.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Web Service Interoperability (WS-I) Basic Profile"

entries.title: Web Services Description Language (WSDL)
entries.summaryMd: An XML format for describing network services as a set of endpoints operating on messages containing either document- oriented or procedure-oriented information. WSDL complements the UDDI standard by providing a uniform way of describing the abstract interface and protocol bindings and deployment details of arbitrary network services.

senses.definitionMd: An XML format for describing network services as a set of endpoints operating on messages containing either document- oriented or procedure-oriented information. WSDL complements the UDDI standard by providing a uniform way of describing the abstract interface and protocol bindings and deployment details of arbitrary network services.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Web Services Description Language (WSDL)"

entries.title: Web Services Security (WS -Security)
entries.summaryMd: A mechanism for incorporating security information into SOAP messages. WS-Security uses binary tokens for authentication, digital signatures for integrity, and content-level encryption for confidentiality.

senses.definitionMd: A mechanism for incorporating security information into SOAP messages. WS-Security uses binary tokens for authentication, digital signatures for integrity, and content-level encryption for confidentiality.

entries.title: Web3
entries.summaryMd: Web3 is a restructuring of the internet that places ownership and operation into the hands of users themselves, thus changing the structure from organization-centric to user-centric.Web3 proposes several changes to the existing web architecture:Users own their data and are responsible for their data, data security, and data privacy.Decentralized and distributed systems are used, and users can host and run applications.Applications and organizations request data directly from users.Users can supply applications and organizations with actual data or verifiable credentials/verifiable presentations of their data or choose to deny applications and organizations access to their data.Applications and organizations may offer incentives for users to provide data.Data can be tokenized and transferred directly between users.Application execution and transaction fees are paid for with web-native currencies (e.g., cryptocurrencies).Users who execute application logic and maintain the state of systems can receive payment in web-native currencies (e.g., cryptocurrencies).

senses.definitionMd: Web3 is a restructuring of the internet that places ownership and operation into the hands of users themselves, thus changing the structure from organization-centric to user-centric.Web3 proposes several changes to the existing web architecture:Users own their data and are responsible for their data, data security, and data privacy.Decentralized and distributed systems are used, and users can host and run applications.Applications and organizations request data directly from users.Users can supply applications and organizations with actual data or verifiable credentials/verifiable presentations of their data or choose to deny applications and organizations access to their data.Applications and organizations may offer incentives for users to provide data.Data can be tokenized and transferred directly between users.Application execution and transaction fees are paid for with web-native currencies (e.g., cryptocurrencies).Users who execute application logic and maintain the state of systems can receive payment in web-native currencies (e.g., cryptocurrencies).

entries.title: Webmaster
entries.summaryMd: A person responsible for the implementation of a Web site. Webmasters must be proficient in HTML and one or more scripting and interface languages, such as JavaScript and Perl. They may or may not be responsible for the underlying server, which is traditionally the responsibility of the Web administrator (see above).

senses.definitionMd: A person responsible for the implementation of a Web site. Webmasters must be proficient in HTML and one or more scripting and interface languages, such as JavaScript and Perl. They may or may not be responsible for the underlying server, which is traditionally the responsibility of the Web administrator (see above).

entries.title: Website
entries.summaryMd: A set of related web pages that are prepared and maintained as a collection in support of a single purpose.

senses.definitionMd: A set of related web pages that are prepared and maintained as a collection in support of a single purpose.

entries.title: Well-formed
entries.summaryMd: An SCAP-conformant data stream or stream component.

senses.definitionMd: An SCAP-conformant data stream or stream component.

entries.title: Well-Formed CPE Name
entries.summaryMd: A logical construct that constitutes an unordered list of A-V pairs that collectively describe or identify one or more operating systems, software applications, or hardware devices. Unordered means that there is no prescribed order in which A-V pairs should be listed, and there is no specified relationship (hierarchical, set-theoretic, or otherwise) among attributes. WFNs must satisfy the criteria specified in the CPE Naming specification [CPE23-N:5.2]. For a full description and usage constraints on WFN logical attribute values, see Section 5 of the CPE Naming specification [CPE23-N:5].

senses.definitionMd: A logical construct that constitutes an unordered list of A-V pairs that collectively describe or identify one or more operating systems, software applications, or hardware devices. Unordered means that there is no prescribed order in which A-V pairs should be listed, and there is no specified relationship (hierarchical, set-theoretic, or otherwise) among attributes. entries.title: WGS 84
entries.summaryMd: An Earth-centered, Earth-fixed terrestrial reference system and geodetic datum. WGS 84 is based on a consistent set of constants and model parameters that describe the Earth’s size, shape, gravity, and geomagnetic fields. WGS 84 is the standard U.S. Department of Defense definition of a global reference system for geospatial information and is the reference system for GPS. It is consistent with the International Terrestrial Reference System (ITRS).

senses.definitionMd: An Earth-centered, Earth-fixed terrestrial reference system and geodetic datum. WGS 84 is based on a consistent set of constants and model parameters that describe the Earth’s size, shape, gravity, and geomagnetic fields. WGS 84 is the standard U.S. Department of Defense definition of a global reference system for geospatial information and is the reference system for GPS. It is consistent with the International Terrestrial Reference System (ITRS).

entries.title: whaling
entries.summaryMd: A specific kind of phishing that targets high-ranking members of organizations.

senses.definitionMd: A specific kind of phishing that targets high-ranking members of organizations.

entries.title: White Box Testing
entries.summaryMd: A test methodology that assumes explicit and substantial knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as white box testing.

senses.definitionMd: A test methodology that assumes explicit and substantial knowledge of the internal structure and implementation detail of the assessment object. Also known as white box testing.

entries.title: White Team
entries.summaryMd: 1. The group responsible for refereeing an engagement between a Red Team of mock attackers and a Blue Team of actual defenders of their enterprise’s use of information systems. In an exercise, the White Team acts as the judges, enforces the rules of the exercise, observes the exercise, scores teams, resolves any problems that may arise, handles all requests for information or questions, and ensures that the competition runs fairly and does not cause operational problems for the defender's mission. The White Team helps to establish the rules of engagement, the metrics for assessing results and the procedures for providing operational security for the engagement. The White Team normally has responsibility for deriving lessons-learned, conducting the post engagement assessment, and promulgating results.

entries.title: whitelist
entries.summaryMd: A list of discrete entities, such as hosts or applications that are known to be benign and are approved for use within an organization and/or information system. Also known as “clean word list”.

senses.definitionMd: A list of discrete entities, such as hosts or applications that are known to be benign and are approved for use within an organization and/or information system. Also known as “clean word list”.

entries.title: whitelisting
entries.summaryMd: An implementation of a default deny all or allow by exception policy across an enterprise environment, and a clear, concise, timely process for adding exceptions when required for mission accomplishments.

senses.definitionMd: An implementation of a default deny all or allow by exception policy across an enterprise environment, and a clear, concise, timely process for adding exceptions when required for mission accomplishments.

entries.title: wide area network
entries.summaryMd: A physical or logical network that provides data communications to a larger number of independent users than are typically served by a local area network (LAN) and that is usually spread over a larger geographic area than that of a LAN.

senses.definitionMd: A physical or logical network that provides data communications to a larger number of independent users than are typically served by a local area network (LAN) and that is usually spread over a larger geographic area than that of a LAN.

entries.title: Wiping
entries.summaryMd: Overwriting media or portions of media with random or constant values to hinder the collection of data.

senses.definitionMd: Overwriting media or portions of media with random or constant values to hinder the collection of data.

entries.title: wireless access point (WAP)
entries.summaryMd: A device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network using wi-fi, or related standards.

senses.definitionMd: A device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network using wi-fi, or related standards.

entries.title: wireless application protocol (WAP)
entries.summaryMd: A standard that defines the way in which Internet communications and other advanced services are provided on wireless mobile devices.

senses.definitionMd: A standard that defines the way in which Internet communications and other advanced services are provided on wireless mobile devices.

entries.title: wireless device
entries.summaryMd: Any device that can connect to an OT network via radio or infrared waves, usually to collect or monitor data but also to modify control set points in some cases.

senses.definitionMd: Any device that can connect to an OT network via radio or infrared waves, usually to collect or monitor data but also to modify control set points in some cases.

entries.title: Wireless Fidelity (WiFi)
entries.summaryMd: A term describing a wireless local area network that observes the IEEE 802.11 protocol.

senses.definitionMd: A term describing a wireless local area network that observes the IEEE 802.11 protocol.

entries.title: wireless intrusion detection system (WIDS)
entries.summaryMd: A commercial wireless technology that assists designated personnel with the monitoring of specific parts of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum to identify unauthorized wireless transmissions and/or activities.

senses.definitionMd: A commercial wireless technology that assists designated personnel with the monitoring of specific parts of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum to identify unauthorized wireless transmissions and/or activities.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "wireless intrusion detection system (WIDS)"

entries.title: Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN)
entries.summaryMd: A group of wireless access points and associated infrastructure within a limited geographic area, such as an office building or building campus, that is capable of radio communications. WLANs are usually implemented as extensions of existing wired LANs to provide enhanced user mobility.

senses.definitionMd: A group of wireless access points and associated infrastructure within a limited geographic area, such as an office building or building campus, that is capable of radio communications. WLANs are usually implemented as extensions of existing wired LANs to provide enhanced user mobility.

citation.citationText: NIST CSRC Glossary, "Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN)"

entries.title: Wireless Markup Language
entries.summaryMd: a stripped down version of HTML to allow mobile devices to access Web sites and pages that have been converted from HTML to the more basic text format supported.

entries.title: World Geodetic System 1984
entries.summaryMd: An Earth-centered, Earth-fixed terrestrial reference system and geodetic datum. WGS 84 is based on a consistent set of constants and model parameters that describe the Earth’s size, shape, gravity, and geomagnetic fields. WGS 84 is the standard U.S. Department of Defense definition of a global reference system for geospatial information and is the reference system for GPS. It is consistent with the International Terrestrial Reference System (ITRS).
